This is an indirect glorification of Krsna, because it is He who empowers the devotees with the astounding potency to immediately purify others, “whereas the Ganges can sanctify only after prolonged use.” Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments that even seeing the Ganges can purify one, but by simply remembering a devotee he becomes sanctified; thus a devotee is superior to the Ganges.

Srila Sridhara Svami comments: Although formerly the Ganges River was considered the foremost of all holy places, the holy place of the glorification of Sri Krsna, who appeared in the Yadu dynasty, makes the Ganges appear insignificant.

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on text 15 in Krsna-sandarbha, anuccheda 67: yat in this text means “of Sri Krsna” and pada-samsrayah means “those who have taken shelter of the lotus feet”; in the word prasamayanah, рта means prakasta (special), and sama refers to bhagavad-nistha-buddhita, “intelligence fixed on the Supreme Lord.”

That one should continually meditate on Lord Krsna is confirmed by Krsna’s words in Bhagavatam 11.19.36: “Absorbing the intelligence in Me constitutes mental equilibrium.” Because Suta Gosvami and the other great sages at Naimisaranya have taken full shelter of Krsna and are attracted to hearing of His pastimes, simply by one’s offering them a little direct service, one may become at once purified from all the sinful contamination of material existence.

Srila Narottama Dasa sings of the purifying potency of the great Vaisnava in Prarthana (Song 45, verses 2-3):

*jahara darsane saba papa dure jay*  
*emona doyala prabhu keba kotha pay*  
*gangara parasa hoile pascate paban*  
*darsane pabitra кого—ei tomara gun*

**Where does anyone find such a merciful personality by whose mere audience all sins go far away? After bathing in the waters of the sacred Ganges many times, one becomes purified, but just by the sight of you, the fallen souls become purified. This is your great power.**

In his purport to Bhagavatam [1.1.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.16), Srila Prabhupada offers this practical direction:

**The age of Kali is the most condemned age due to its quarrelsome features. Kali-yuga is so saturated with vicious habits that there is a great fight at the slightest misunderstanding. Those who are engaged in the pure devotional service of the Lord, who are without any desire for self-aggrandizement and who are freed from the effects of fruitive actions and dry philosophical speculations are capable of getting out of the estrangements of this complicated age. The leaders of the people are very much anxious to live in peace and friendship, but they have no information of the simple method of hearing the glories of the Lord. On the contrary, such leaders are opposed to the propagation of the glories of the Lord. In other words, the foolish leaders want to completely deny the existence of the Lord. In the name of secular state, such leaders are enacting various plans every year. But by the insurmountable intricacies of the material nature of the Lord, all these plans for progress are being constantly frustrated. They have no eyes to see that their attempts at peace and friendship are failing. But here is the hint to get over the hurdle. If we want actual peace, we must open the road to understanding of the Supreme Lord Krsna and glorify Him for His virtuous activities as they are depicted in the pages of Srimad-Bhagavatam.**

## Texts 17-18: Questions Four and Five

Saunaka Rsi continues: “His transcendental acts are magnificent and gracious, and great learned sages like Narada sing of them. Please, therefore, speak to us, who are eager to hear about the adventures He performs in His various incarnations. О wise Suta, please narrate to us the transcendental pastimes of the Supreme Godhead’s multi-incarnations. Such auspicious adventures and pastimes of the Lord, the supreme controller, are performed by His internal powers.” (Bhag. [1.1.17-18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.17))

In essence, Saunaka Rsi asks: Which adventures does the Lord perform in His various incarnations? While analyzing Saunaka Rsi’s question, Srila Jiva Gosvami explains that Saunaka is specifically referring to the Lord’s pastimes of universal creation. The answer to this question, he explains, will be presented in Bhagavatam [1.2.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.30): “In the beginning of the material creation, that Absolute Personality of Godhead \[Vasudeva\], in His transcendental position, created the energies of cause and effect by His own internal energy.” Understood in this way, the question deals with Krsna’s creation and maintenance of the material worlds through His purusa-avatdras, Maha-Visnu, Garbhodakasayi Visnu, and Karanodakasayi Visnu. These topics are outlined in Bhagavatam [1.2.30-33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.30) and extensively discussed in the Second and Third Cantos.

About the sages’ words, What are the adventures of the different incarnations of the Lord? spoken in text 18, Srila Jiva Gosvami comments that the verse beginning athdkhyahi (18) is requesting avatdra-kathah, narrations concerning the Lord’s descents into this world, and that the Bhagavatam's First Canto, third chapter answers this question. In Krsna-sandarbha, anuccheda 70, Srila Jiva Gosvami comments that the word avatdra refers to the purusa-avatdras, guna-avatdras (controllers of the material modes), and hla-avatdras (pastime incarnations), and that these avatdras are hareh, which refers to Their being sri-krsndya, of Krsna. The Lord’s pastimes as avatdras include His creation of the material universes, the removal of the earth’s burden, and many other pastimes. Eager to hear of the Lord’s adventures, the sages at Naimisaranya thus appeal to Suta Gosvami.

## Texts 19-23: Question Six

Saunaka continues to glorify hearing about Krsna: “We never tire of hearing the transcendental pastimes of the Personality of Godhead, who is glorified by hymns and prayers. Those who have developed a taste for transcendental relationships with Him relish hearing of His pastimes at every moment. Lord Sri Krsna, the Personality of Godhead, along with Balarama, played like a human being, and so masked He performed many superhuman acts.” (Bhag. [1.1.19-20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.19))

Sridhara Svami comments on text 20 that although the sages were finding the sacrifice tiring, they still wanted to hear more and more about Krsna. Their taste for such katha was insatiable. They were so eager to hear that although they had already asked to hear about Krsna in text 17, they asked again. The word uttama-sloka in text 19 also means “He whose glories dispel tamas, ignorance,” so it is expected that hearing about Krsna would allow the sages to feel relief.

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments that the two verses beginning vayam (Bhag. [1.1.19-20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.19)) paraphrase the question spoken in the verse beginning siita jandsi (Bhag. [1.1.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.12) and question three): For what purpose did the Personality of Godhead appear in the womb of Devaki as the son of Vasudeva?” Srila Sridhara Svami explains that the sages

at Naimisaranya spoke this verse to encourage Suta Gosvami to describe Krsna’s transcendental pastimes. Thus the word atimartyani in text 20 means “superhuman acts, such as lifting Govardhana Hill, which can never be performed by ordinary human beings. The sages know that Kali-yuga has begun, so they wish to hear about the Lord and His activities. They accept hearing from Sri Suta Gosvami as a great fortune awarded to them by Krsna’s grace.”

Text 22 states: “We think that we have met Your Goodness by the will of providence, just so that we may accept you as captain of the ship for those who desire to cross the difficult ocean of Kali, which deteriorates all the good qualities of a human being.”Mayavadis also sometimes read the Bhagavatam, but because they impose their impersonal understanding on the Bhagavatam’s glorification of the Supreme Person, their study proves useless. When both speaker and hearer are qualified, however, as were Suta Gosvami and the Naimisaranya sages, speaking and hearing the Bhagavatam is immensely beneficial. An advanced hearer will experience an ever-fresh and ever-new taste even by repeatedly hearing the Srimad-Bhagavatam. The Bhagavatam is of a different caliber than mundane literature, which is by nature dead. Srila Prabhupada emphasizes the importance of hearing the Bhagavatam in his purports to texts 21 and 22:

**By the example of these sages one should learn that regular hearing and recitation of the Bhagavatam is the only way for selfrealization. Other attempts are simply a waste of time, for they do not give any tangible results. Lord Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu preached this system of Bhagavata-dharma, and He recommended that all those who were bom in India should take the responsibility of broadcasting the messages of Lord Sri Krsna, primarily the message of Bhagavad-gita. And when one is well established in the teachings of Bhagavad-gita, he can take up the study of Srimad-Bhagavatam for further enlightenment in self-realization. (Bhag.** [**1.1.21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.21)**, purport)**

**Learned men . . . must be cautious of this age, and if they at all want to cross over the dangerous ocean of Kali, they must follow the footsteps of the sages of Naimisaranya and accept Sri Suta Gosvami or his bona fide representative as the captain of the ship. The ship is the message of Lord Sri Krsna in the shape of Bhagavad' gita or the Srimad-Bhagavatam. (Bhag.** [**1.1.22**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.22)**, purport)**

The glories of hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam are the glories of hearing about Krsna. By hearing about Krsna, one crosses the ocean of Kali-yuga, which deteriorates people’s good qualities, namely, austerity, compassion, charity, and humility. The sages were submissive and not materially motivated, and when they understood their fortune in hearing from a devotee as powerful as Suta Gosvami, who could guide them beyond the dangerous ocean of Kali-yuga, they thanked the Lord.

The chapter’s final text (23) contains Saunaka Rsi’s sixth question: “Since Sri Krsna, the Absolute Truth, the master of all mystic powers, has departed for His own abode, please tell us to whom the religious principles have now gone for shelter.” Suta Gosvami will answer this question in Bhagavatam [1.3.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/3.43) and clearly illuminate the Bhagavatam as the great shelter from Kali-yuga.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, at the end of his commentary on Bhagavatam [1.1.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.23) (where he lists Saunaka Rsi’s six questions), states: “We can infer that the Srimad-Bhagavatam, along with additional connected discussions (prasangas), constitutes the answers to these questions.”

## Summary of the Six Questions Asked by Saunaka Rsi and the Sages of Naimisaranya

QUESTION ONE: “Please ... explain to us, in an easily understandable way, what you have ascertained to be the absolute and ultimate good for the people in general.” (Bhag. [1.1.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.9))  
ANSWER: Bhagavatam [1.2.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.6)

QUESTION TWO: “There are many varieties of scriptures... Therefore, О sage, please select the essence of all these scriptures and explain it for the good of all living beings, that by such instruction their hearts may be fully satisfied.” (Bhag. [1.1.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.11))  
ANSWER: Bhagavatam [1.2.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.7)

QUESTION THREE: О Suta Gosvami, “You know for what purpose the Personality of Godhead appeared in the womb of Devaki as the son of Vasudeva.” (Bhag. [1.1.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.12))  
REPHRASED: “Why did the Personality of Godhead appear in Devaki’s womb as the son of Vasudeva?” \[Implied: the desire to hear about Krsna and His pastimes.\]  
ANSWER: Bhagavatam [1.2.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.34) and the Tenth Canto

QUESTION FOUR: “\[The Lord’s\] transcendental acts are magnificent and gracious, and great learned sages like Narada sing of them. Please, therefore, speak to us, who are eager to hear about the adventures He performs in His various incarnations.” (Bhag. [1.1.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.17))  
\[Question Four, according to Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, is an inquiry into the pastimes of the Lord’s incarnations.\] ANSWER: The incarnations are discussed in the third chapter of the First Canto and throughout the Bhagavatam.  
\[According to Jiva Gosvami, this question asks about the activities of the Lord specifically in relation to His creation of the world. It is thus asking about the activities of the Lord’s three purusa-avataras.\] ANSWER: Bhagavatam [1.2.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.30)

QUESTION FIVE: “O wise Suta, please narrate to us the transcendental pastimes of the Supreme Godhead’s multi-incarnations. Such auspicious adventures and pastimes of the Lord, the supreme controller, are performed by His internal powers.” (Bhag. [1.1.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.18)) REPHRASED: “What are the Lord’s different incarnations?”  
ANSWER: Srila Jiva Gosvami says that Bhagavatam [1.1.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.18) asks about avatdra-kathah, narrations concerning the Lord’s descents, and that the third chapter of the First Canto answers this question.

QUESTION SIX: “Since Sri Krsna, the Absolute Truth, the master of all mystic powers, has departed for His own abode, please tell us to whom the religious principles have now gone for shelter?” (Bhag. [1.1.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.23))  
ANSWER: Bhagavatam [1.3.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/3.43)  
\[Again, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti, in his commentary on Bhagavatam [1.1.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.23) (where he lists Saunaka Rsi’s six questions), says: “We can infer that the Srimad-Bhagavatam, along with additional connected discussions (prasangas), constitutes the answers to these questions.”\]

## Dialogue Two - Divinity and Divine Service

## Chapter 2 - Suta Gosvami Begins Answering the Sages’ Questions

## Texts 1-5: Suta Gosvami’s Reply Begins with Obeisances

Before beginning his reply to Saunaka Rsi’s questions, Suta Gosvami first offers obeisances to Sukadeva Gosvami, his spiritual master, from whom he heard the Srimad-Bhagavatam. He glorifies him: “Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto that great sage \[Sukadeva Gosvami\] who can enter the hearts of all. When he went away to take up the renounced order of life \[sannyasa\], leaving home without undergoing reformation by the sacred thread or the ceremonies observed by the higher castes, his father, Vyasadeva, fearing separation from him, cried out, ‘O my son!’ Indeed, only the trees, which were absorbed in the same feelings of separation, echoed in response to the begrieved father.” (Bhag. [1.2.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.2))

Sukadeva (a liberated Vaisnava, according to Prabhupada’s purport) was already Brahman realized and thus did not need the sacred thread initiation, which admits one to the study of the Vedas. As Sukadeva Gosvami was walking away to renounce the world, Vyasa was calling after him but heard only the trees echo in reply. Jiva Gosvami indicates in his commentary on Bhagavatam [1.2.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.2) that the reply was actually Krsna Himself sounding through the trees. Sri Jiva adds that the trees, which were feeling the same depth of separation from Sukadeva as Vyasadeva was feeling, loved Sukadeva for his purity.

Vyasadeva was deeply disappointed. He had wished to teach his son the Srimad-Bhagavatam. To entice him to return, Vyasa ordered some of his disciples to recite texts from the Bhagavatam whenever they went into the forest. Sukadeva Gosvami happened to hear those disciples, and as Vyasadeva hoped, he became attracted to their recitations and did return to his father’s hermitage to learn the Srimad-Bhagavatam, a fact mentioned in Bhagavatam [1.7.8-11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/7.8).

Suta Gosvami continues: “Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto him \[Suka\], the spiritual master of all sages, the son of Vyasadeva, who, out of his great compassion for those gross materialists who struggle to cross over the darkest regions of material existence, spoke this most confidential supplement to the cream of Vedic knowledge, after having personally assimilated it by experience.” (Bhag. [1.2.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.3))

Prabhupada comments on this text as follows: “In this prayer, Srila Suta Gosvami practically summarizes the complete introduction of Srimad-Bhagavatam. Srimad-Bhagavatam is the natural supplementary commentary on the Vedanta-sutras. The Vedanta-sutras, or the Brahma-sutras, were compiled by Vyasadeva with a view to presenting just the cream of Vedic knowledge. Srimad-Bhagavatam is the natural commentary on this cream. Srila Sukadeva Gosvami was a thoroughly realized master on the Vedanta-sutra, and consequently he also personally realized the commentary, Srimad-Bhagavatam. And just to show his boundless mercy upon bewildered materialistic men who want to cross completely over nescience, he recited for the first time this confidential knowledge. . . . Srimad-Bhagavatam is the one unrivaled commentary on Vedanta-sutra.”

Srila Prabhupada explained this point further in a conversation: “. . . Vedanta-sutra begins when one is inquisitive to understand the Absolute Truth. . . . And the first question is brahma-jijnasa, inquiry about Brahman. So Brahman is described in a nutshell. Brahman means ‘the origin of everything’: janmady asya yatah. ... So the whole Vedanta is a description of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. But because in this Kali-yuga people will not be able to study Vedanta nicely on account of a lack of education, Vyasadeva personally wrote a commentary on the Vedanta. . . . That commentary is Srimad-Bhagavatam. Bhasyam brahma-sutranam. The Srimad-Bhagavatam is the real commentary on the Vedanta-sutra, written by the author himself under the instruction of Narada, his spiritual master. And Srimad-Bhagavatam also begins with the same aphorism, janmady asya yatah . . . So, actually, the Vedanta-sutra is explained by the author of the Vedanta in Srimad-Bhagavatam.” (Answering questions submitted by Bhavan’s Journal, Vrndavana, June 28, 1976)

Sukadeva Gosvami was considered the topmost sage, capable of instructing all other sages, specifically because he had advanced from his Brahman-realized position to pure devotional service, after which he compassionately spoke the Srimad-Bhagavatam for the benefit of all, including those Srila Prabhupada mentions in his purport to Bhagavatam [1.2.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.3):

**There is no point in arguing that a materialistic man can be happy. No materialistic creature—be he the great Brahma or an insignificant ant—can be happy. Everyone tries to make a permanent plan for happiness, but everyone is baffled by the laws of material nature. Therefore the materialistic world is called the darkest region of God’s creation. Yet the unhappy materialists can get out of it simply by desiring to get out. Unfortunately they are so foolish that they do not want to escape. Therefore they are compared to the camel who relishes thorny twigs because he likes the taste of the twigs mixed with blood. He does not realize that it is his own blood and that his tongue is being cut by the thorns. Similarly, to the materialist his own blood is as sweet as honey, and although he is always harassed by his own material creations, he does not wish to escape. Such materialists are called karmis. Out of hundreds of thousands of karmis, only a few may feel tired of material engagement and desire to get out of the labyrinth. Such intelligent persons are called jnanis. The Vedanta-sutra is directed to such jnanis. But Srila Vyasadeva, being the incarnation of the Supreme Lord, could foresee the misuse of the Vedanta-sutra by unscrupulous men, and, therefore, he personally supplemented the Vedanta-surra with the Bhagavata Purana. It is clearly said that this Bhagavatam is the original commentary on the Brahma-sutras. Srila Vyasadeva also instructed the Bhagavatam to his own son, Srila Sukadeva Gosvami, who was already at the liberated stage of transcendence. Srila Sukadeva realized it personally and then explained it. By the mercy of Srila Sukadeva, the Bhagavata-vedanta-sutra is available for all those sincere souls who want to get out of material existence.**

Srila Suta Gosvami now continues offering obeisances because, as a humble Vaisnava, he feels unqualified to speak without obtaining the blessings of superior persons: “Before reciting this Srimad-Bhagavatam, which is the very means of conquest, one should offer respectful obeisances unto the Personality of Godhead, Narayana, unto Nara-narayana Rsi, the supermost human being, unto mother Sarasvati, the goddess of learning, and unto Srila Vyasadeva, the author.” (Bhag. [1.2.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.4))

Suta has thus begun to recite Bhagavatam by first offering respects to Nara-narayana Rsi and to Sarasvati. The Bhagavatam ([12.4.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/4.41)) tells us that Nara-Narayana spoke Srimad-Bhagavatam to Narada Muni, who then repeated it to Vyasa. Vyasa later spoke it to Sarasvati, the goddess of learning. In text 5 Suta offers respects to the sages at Naimisaranya, for their questions have given him the opportunity to speak about Krsna. All beings—birds, beasts, businessmen—begin their day by asking questions. They inquire steadily until they fall asleep at night. But only questions and answers about Krsna can actually satisfy the soul. Suta Gosvami therefore says that because Saunaka Rsi’s questions relate to Krsna (krsna-samprasno), they are glorious. Srila Jiva Gosvami notes in Krsna-sandarbha, anuccheda 73, that in Bhagavatam [1.2.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.5) Suta describes the questions as excellent because they are auspicious for the world (loka-mangalam) and capable of completely satisfying the self (yendtmd suprasidati). Additionally, he comments that as this text mentions krsna-samprasna, in his answers that follow, adhoksaja (text 6), vasudeva (text 7), and satvatam-pati (text 14) all refer to Krsna.

## Texts 6-7: Suta Gosvami Answers Saunaka Rsi’s First and Second Questions

In Bhagavatam [1.2.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.6), Suta Gosvami finally addresses Saunaka Rsi’s first question: “What have you ascertained to be the absolute and ultimate good for all people?” (This question is found in Bhagavatam [1.1.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.9).)

*sa vai pumsarii pare dharmo yato bhaktir adhoksaje ahaituky apratihata yayatma suprasidati*

**The supreme occupation \[dharma\] for all humanity is that by which men can attain to loving devotional service unto the transcendent Lord. Such devotional service must be unmotivated and uninterrupted to completely satisfy the self.**

By performing param dharma, the topmost activity of pure devo-tional service to Krsna, everyone will become self-satisfied. If we wish to fully satisfy our hearts, however, our service must be continuously performed with no motivation other than to please Krsna. Thus a pure devotee places pleasing Krsna at the center of his life. Even processes that develop the realization that “I am not my body but an eternal soul” are rejected.

Srila Prabhupada discusses pure devotion in his purport to Bhagavatam [1.2.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.6): “The relation is one of the servant and the served. It is transcendental and is completely distinct from our experience in material existence. This relation of servant and the served is the most congenial form of intimacy. One can realize it as devotional service progresses. Everyone should engage himself in that transcendental loving service of the Lord, even in the present conditional state of material existence. That will gradually give one the clue to actual life and please him to complete satisfaction.”

People desire intimacy, but because they are self-centered, which ultimately places them in the position of exploiter, their attempts to find intimacy on the physical, emotional, or intellectual levels actually push true intimacy away. On the other hand, serving Krsna, as Suta Gosvami indicates, feels true because it is deeply pleasing to the soul.

Kapila Muni describes the result of practicing pure devotional service in Bhagavatam [3.29.11-12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.11): “The manifestation of unadulterated devotional service is exhibited when one’s mind is at once attracted to hearing the transcendental name and qualities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is residing in everyone’s heart. Just as the water of the Ganges flows naturally down towards the ocean, such devotional ecstasy, uninterrupted by any material condition, flows towards the Supreme Lord.”

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to these texts describes pure devotional service in terms similar to how it is described in Bhagavatam [1.2.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.6): “The word ahaituki means ‘without reason.’ A pure devotee does not render loving service to the Personality of Godhead for any cause or for any benefit, material or spiritual. This is the first symptom of unalloyed devotion. Anyabhildsitd'SHnyam: he has no desire to fulfill by rendering devotional service. Such devotional service is meant for the purusottama, the Supreme Personality, and not for anyone else. ... A pure devotee must engage in the service of the Lord twenty-four hours a day, without cessation; his life is so molded that at every minute and every second he engages in some sort of devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. . . . The devotee has no interest but to fulfill the transcendental desire of the Supreme Lord. Such spontaneous service unto the Supreme Lord is transcendental and is never contaminated by the material modes of nature. These are the symptoms of pure devotional service, which is free from all contamination of material nature.”

Next, in text 7, Suta Gosvami answers Saunaka Rsi’s second question (from Bhagavatam [1.1.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.11)): What is the essential recommendation of all sastras?

*vasudeve bhagavati*  
*bhakti-yogah prayojitah*  
*janayaty asu vairagyah*  
*jnanam ca yad ahaitukam*

**By rendering devotional service unto the Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, one immediately acquires causeless knowledge and detachment from the world.**

Suta Gosvami’s answer is this: In essence, the sastras’ message is to perform bhakti-yoga in relationship with Sri Krsna. No process other than bhakti is required. One may think, “I will take to bhakti after I realize that I am not my body but a spirit soul.” Suta Gosvami’s response, however, is clear: By performing devotional service, knowledge and detachment—the fruits of other spiritual practices—manifest automatically. The jnana mentioned in this text does not refer to the knowledge that leads to the impersonalists’ sayujya liberation (merging into the existence of the body of the Lord). Rather, it refers to knowledge of the sweetness of the Lord’s attributes. Such knowledge leads one to become firmly attached to Krsna and detached from all else.

*bhaktih paresanubhavo viraktir*  
*anyatra caisa trika eka-kalah*  
*prapadyamanasya yathasnatah syus*  
*tustih pustih ksud-apayo 'nu-ghasam*

**Devotion, direct experience of the Supreme Lord, and detachment from other things—these three occur simultaneously for one who has taken shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in the same way that pleasure, nourishment and relief from hunger come simultaneously and increasingly, with each bite, for a person engaged in eating. (Bhag.** [**11.2.42**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.42)**)**

And in Bhagavatam [5.18.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/18.12):

**All the demigods and their exalted qualities, such as religion, knowledge and renunciation, become manifest in the body of one who has developed unalloyed devotion for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vasudeva.**

As every leaf is nourished when we water the root of a tree, so while bhakti gives Krsna pleasure, each soul performing bhakti naturally also becomes satisfied. Therefore the recommendation to serve Krsna with devotion is the essence of sastric teachings. In his purport to Bhagavatam [1.2.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.7), Srila Prabhupada comments that bhakti, “being the supermost occupation of the living being, leads him out of material sense enjoyment. That is the sign of a pure devotee. . . . one who is a pure devotee has all other good qualities, namely knowledge, detachment, etc., but one who has only knowledge or detachment is not necessarily well acquainted with the principles of the bhakti cult. Bhakti is the supermost occupation of the human being.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments that when one attains some level of devotion, his hearing about Krsna and desire to perform other acts that increase bhakti (such as chanting the holy name) tend to increase as a matter of course. The word asu, “very soon,” indicates that as soon as one hears the Srimad-Bhagavatam, he begins to experience the effects mentioned in text 7.

## Texts 8-15: Only Bhakti Is to Be Gained Through the Performance of One’s Work

Suta Gosvami now adds emphasis to his assertion of the importance of bhakti: “The occupational activities a man performs according to his own position are only so much useless labor if they do not provoke attraction for the message of the Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [1.2.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.8)) Here, Suta Gosvami speaks the same truth he spoke in Bhagavatam [1.2.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.6), but in negative terms: If one performs his duties properly but fails to attain attraction to krsna-katha, or hearing and speaking about Krsna, he will have acted uselessly.

Srila Jiva Gosvami says about this text that love for hearing and speaking krsna-katha is glorified above all other forms of bhakti. Although many people believe that it is necessary to cultivate knowledge and detachment in order to come to bhakti, these are not direct forms of bhakti and are actually subservient to it. Rather than bhakti being dependent on jndna and karma, success in jndna and karma depends on the development of bhakti. Bhakti itself is independent. Ultimately, although people seek pleasure by trying to satisfy the body (by karma) or mind (through jndna), both attempts lead only to final dissatisfaction, because they neglect the needs of the soul. The self is satisfied only by the culture of bhakti, Srila Prabupada explains in his purport, “because other occupational duties.. . cannot give liberation to the soul.”

Srila Prabhupada writes: “The need of the spirit soul is that he wants to get out of the limited sphere of material bondage and fulfill his desire for complete freedom. He wants to get out of the covered walls of the greater universe. He wants to see the free light and the spirit. That complete freedom is achieved when he meets the complete spirit, the Personality of Godhead. There is a dormant affection for God within everyone; spiritual existence is manifested through the gross body and mind in the form of perverted affection for gross and subtle matter. Therefore we have to engage ourselves in occupational engagements that will evoke our divine consciousness. This is possible only by hearing and chanting the divine activities of the Supreme Lord, and any occupational activity which does not help one to achieve attachment for hearing and chanting the transcendental message of Godhead is said herein to be simply a waste of time.”

Srila Sridhara Svami comments on text 8 that even if one properly engages in religion, his worship is useless if it does not evoke love for Krsna. Why? Because love for God is the only permanent result; all other results are temporary.

Still, one may ask: It’s wonderful to think that the goal of my work is loving Krsna, but practically speaking, isn’t the first objective of my work to provide an income to ensure the security and comfort of me and my family? Suta Gosvami’s response is a definite no. Text 9 states: Great sages conclude that the main purpose of occupational duties is to gain ultimate liberation from material life (apavargasya), not material gain. And gains that do arise from one’s engagement in this ultimate occupational service should never be used to increase sense pleasure.

People might consider themselves religious, but Suta Gosvami defines the standard: our dharma is meant to give Krsna pleasure. Religion is meant to carry one out of this world, not to facilitate our enjoyment. Bhakti, pure devotional service, is the true standard of religion. By the power of pure bhakti, Krsna Himself can be brought under control.

Devotees—those who perform bhakti—are categorized in three classes: kanistha (neophyte), madhyama (intermediate), anduttama (topmost). A kanistha devotee has material desires and approaches Krsna to fulfill them. He respects the temple deity but is indifferent toward the Lord’s devotees. The madhyama devotee genuinely wants to serve the Lord. Thus he builds friendships with those of a similar mentality. In addition, he shows compassion toward neophytes and avoids atheists. An uttama devotee sees nothing but the Lord. He sees everything as situated in the Lord and coming from Him. A first-class devotee is perfect in all respects.

Life’s duties should lead us to pure bhakti. Karma, jnana, yoga, and the lower levels of bhakti cannot satisfy the soul. When we honestly act to please Krsna, Krsna will be satisfied. When Krsna is satisfied, we will be fully satisfied.

What then should we desire while living in the material world? Suta continues in text 10: “One should desire only a healthy life, or self-preservation, since a human being is meant for inquiry about the Absolute Truth. Nothing else should be the goal of one’s works.” This means that one should desire only enough wealth to maintain one’s life. People’s needs differ, but one’s heart’s desire should be fixed on knowing the Absolute Truth. In his purport to text 10, Srila Prabhupada mentions: “Seekers of the Absolute Truth are never allured by unnecessary engagements in sense gratification because the serious students seeking the Absolute Truth are always overwhelmed with the work of researching the Truth.” All levels of devotees should be wary of thoughts that allow them to desire a percentage of the results of their work for themselves. Of course, it is difficult to inhibit our subtle tendencies. The most powerful way to work toward such selfcontrol is to increase our desire to attain the Absolute Truth.

What is the Absolute Truth? Suta Gosvami now defines it in text 11:

*vadanti tat tattva-vidas*  
*tattvam yaj jnanam advayam*  
*brahmeti paramatmeti*  
*bhagavan iti sabdyate*

**Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth call this nondual substance Brahman, Paramatma or Bhagavan.**

The Absolute Truth is the one, nondual substance comprising the totality of existence. Individuals perceive this substance differently according to how they approach it, but there is only one Absolute Truth. Approaching the Absolute Truth through jndna reveals it as Brahman, an undifferentiated oneness. Approaching it through yoga causes one to see Paramatma, the Supersoul. A bhakta, a lover of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, will, by Krsna’s grace, see the Absolute Truth as Bhagavan Sri Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

Srila Jiva Gosvami defines bhagavan in his Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 2. Quoting the Visnu Purana ([5.6.73-75](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vp/5.6.73)), he explains that the word bhagavan may be understood by defining its syllables. Bha means “bharta, the maintainer and nourisher of the devotees,” and ga means “gamayayita, the leader of the devotees, or the original creator of the devotees’ good qualities.” Va stands for the verb vas, “to reside”; because all material elements and all living entities reside in the Supreme Lord and because He resides in the hearts of all conditioned souls, He is addressed by the syllable va.

Bhaga also means “opulence.” According to Visnu Purana ([6.5.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vp/6.5.47)), the six types of opulence are wealth, strength, fame, beauty, knowledge, and renunciation. The suffix vat, which means “he who possesses,” becomes van when grammatically adjusted. Thus Krsna is known as Bhagavan because He possesses all opulences in full as well as the qualities bha, ga, and va.

Srila Prabhupada explains the various perspectives on the Absolute Truth in his purport to text 11: “. . . Brahman, Paramatma and Bhagavan are qualitatively one and the same. The same substance is realized as impersonal Brahman by the students of the Upanisads, as localized Paramatma by the Hiranyagarbhas or the yogis, and as Bhagavan by the devotees. In other words, Bhagavan, or the Personality of Godhead, is the last word in the Absolute Truth. Paramatma is the partial representation of the Personality of Godhead, and impersonal Brahman is the glowing effulgence of the Personality of Godhead, as the sun rays are to the sun-god. Less intelligent students of either of the above schools sometimes argue in favor of their own respective realization, but those who are perfect seers of the Absolute Truth know well that the above three features of the one Absolute Truth are different perspective views seen from different angles of vision.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on this text in many sections of the Sat-sandarbhas. In Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 6, he asks, “What is the Absolute Truth?” He replies that this is explained in text 11. By using the word advayam, “not divided into parts,” and by showing that the three aspects of the Supreme are nondifferent, the Lord’s nature as the master of potencies is accepted.

In Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 3, Sri Jiva explains that the Supreme is manifest in three features: Brahman, Paramatma, and Bhagavan. The Bhagavan feature is the complete manifestation of the Supreme, and the other two features are partial revelations of the Lord’s actual nature.

Further, in anuccheda 94, he concludes that among the Lord’s three features, Bhagavan is the Lord’s original, primal nature. Sri Jiva substantiates his statement by quoting the Moksa'dharma: “The great sages who seek the truth with thorough philosophical analysis have concluded that the Supreme Truth is Lord Narayana, known as Hari, who is the master of Yogamaya.” The Narayana Upanisad adds confirmation: “Narayana is the Supreme Brahman. Narayana is the ultimate truth.” This point is again confirmed by the following passage from the sruti'Sastra, cited by Sripada Ramanujacarya: “The one Supreme Personality of Godhead is Lord Narayana. He is transcendental, self-manifest, and sinless. The earth is His body. The soul is His body. The unmanifest pradhana is His body. The imperishable Brahman is His body. He is the Supersoul present in all creatures.” In this way, Sri Jiva concludes, many scriptural passages confirm that the Bhagavan feature of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the ultimate aspect of the Absolute Truth.

How can we realize the Absolute Truth in full? Suta Gosvami makes the method clear: “The seriously inquisitive student or sage, well equipped with knowledge and detachment, realizes that Absolute Truth by rendering devotional service in terms of what he has heard from the Vedanta-sruti. . . . \[T\]he highest perfection one can achieve by discharging the duties prescribed for one’s own occupation ... is to please the Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [1.2.12-13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.12))

Srila Prabhupada asserts this point: “Devotional service, which is based on the foreground of full knowledge combined with detachment from material association and which is fixed by the aural reception of the Vedanta-sruti, is the only perfect method by which the seriously inquisitive student can realize the Absolute Truth.” (Bhag. [1.2.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.12), purport)

We should be seriously inquisitive and carefully study sastra with the sole desire to know the truth. Although we may already be blessed with knowledge and detachment, the essence of our approach should be devotional. Everyone’s aim, regardless of external situation, “must be to please the supreme authority of the Personality of Godhead.”

Srila Sridhara Svami comments on Bhagavatam [1.2.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.12) that this text impresses on the reader’s mind that the tattvam mentioned in Bhagavatam [1.2.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.11) can be realized through unswerving devotional service. None of the three aspects of the Absolute—Brahman, Paramatma, and Bhagavan—can be realized without practicing bhakti.

Additionally, in Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 6, Srila Jiva Gosvami cites Srila Sridhara Svami’s statement that the knowers of the Absolute Truth say that wealth, artha, is not for sense enjoyment; its purpose is only to preserve one’s life. The purpose of life is not to attain wealth or the heavenly planets, therefore, but to know the Absolute Truth.

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on Bhagavatam [1.2.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.12) that the ultimate result of attraction to krsna-katha is devotion to Krsna. By that devotion, we will see Krsna Himself. On Bhagavatam [1.2.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.13) he comments that this devotion is rare, invaluable, and obtained by practices performed solely to please Krsna. Srila Sridhara Svami comments on Bhagavatam [1.2.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.13) that devotion to Krsna is the true effect of religion.

Accepting the preeminence of bhakti, how should we act? Suta now further describes how to attain perfection: “Therefore, with one-pointed attention, one should constantly hear about, glorify, remember and worship the Personality of Godhead, who is the protector of the devotees.” (Bhag. [1.2.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.14))

All activities should be centered on Krsna. Just imagine how quickly our lives would become sublime if we were able to practice, with one-pointed attention, all our hearing, chanting, remembering, and service, offering them only for Krsna’s pleasure. Srila Prabhupada wanted ISKCON to facilitate conditioned souls throughout the world to come to that standard.

Srila Sridhara Svami comments on Bhagavatam [1.2.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.14) that religion without devotion is toil. Srila Jiva Gosvami defines bhakti as the desire to regularly hear the name and glories of the Lord.

In Srila Prabhupada’s purport to Bhagavatam [1.2.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.14), he explains why Krsna should be the object of everyone’s glorification: “Any man from any social status becomes a well-known man in human society within a very short time if he is simply glorified truly or falsely in the daily newspapers. Sometimes political leaders of a particular party are also advertised by newspaper propaganda, and by such a method of glorification an insignificant man becomes an important man—within no time. But such propaganda by false glorification of an unqualified person cannot bring about any good, either for the particular man or for the society. There may be some temporary reactions to such propaganda, but there are no permanent effects. Therefore such activities are a waste of time. The actual object of glorification is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has created everything manifested before us. . . . The tendency to glorify others or hear others must be turned to the real object of glorification—the Supreme Being. And that will bring happiness.” Krsna is powerful; all others are insignificant by comparison and thus unworthy of our glorification.

But, one may wonder, how can I remove the karmic reactions that bind me to the world and cause me to value things other than Krsna? Suta replies in Bhagavatam [1.2.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.15): “\[I\]ntelligent men cut through the binding knots of reactionary work \[karma\] by remembering the Personality of Godhead. Therefore, who will not pay attention to His message?”

Our karma—as well as our tendencies that spring from that karma —is bom of actions performed in this and previous lives. Karma is thus compared to a tangle of knots that bind us to this world. The sharp sword of remembering Krsna slashes through these knots and thus cuts through our material existence. Knowing this as the result of remembering Krsna, an intelligent person naturally attempts to practice such remembrance.

People are affected by ads, trading their money for products and services. Everyone becomes attracted to objects and activities by hearing about their capacity to deliver enjoyment or remove difficulty. Hearing about Krsna’s power and beauty can similarly attract us to Him. Jiva Gosvami comments (text 15) that meditation on Krsna is compared to a sword and that the soul’s contacts with material elements that produce false ego and generate material bodies are cut by this sword. Similarly, Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes that granthimibandhanam refers to the cessation of that which generates ego. Thus the cycle of living out acts predestined by our past and present births also ceases.

After hearing the glories of krsna-katha from trusted saints, what person would consciously avoid hearing about or remembering Krsna? Prabhupada comments on Bhagavatam [1.2.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.15): “Therefore, any sensible man who is above the average man with a poor fund of knowledge must constantly remember the Personality of Godhead by hearing about Him, by glorifying Him, by remembering Him and by worshiping Him always, without cessation. That is the perfect way of devotional service. The Gosvamis of Vrndavana, who were authorized by Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu to preach the bhakti cult, rigidly followed this rule and made immense literatures of transcendental science for our benefit.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami, who also comments on this text, asks, “Who will not hear about Krsna, who saves mankind from the greatest misery?” All people, according to their positions, can focus the mind on Krsna. In this regard, Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu defines misfortune (durdaivam) in the second verse of His Siksastakam as having no attraction to the mercy that Krsna is giving us: although Krsna kindly offers everyone His holy names, we fail to achieve attachment to them because of offenses.

Chanting Krsna’s names can easily focus the mind on Krsna. Krsna invested His holy name with all His potencies, and, unlike Vedic mantras, there are no restrictions in chanting those names. Still, we do not become attached to hearing and chanting about Krsna. That is true misfortune. In his Bhajana-rahasya, Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura lists four causes of this misfortune:

- **tattva-bhrama:** philosophical misunderstandings based on illusion about our identity, illusion about the Supreme Lord, illusion about sadhana- and prema-bhakti, and illusion about subjects unfavorable to Krsna consciousness;
- **aparadha:** offenses toward the Lord’s name, form, devotees, and other living entities;
- **asat-trsna:** “thirst for the temporary,” or desires for material objects, heavenly comforts, mystic powers, and impersonal liberation;
- **hrdaya-daurbalyam:** “weakness of heart,” or deceit, faultfinding, envy, desire for fame and attachment to objects unrelated to Krsna.

Still, we may honestly ask, What can I do? As easy and important as the process may be, I simply have not acquired the taste either for chanting or hearing krsna-katha. Srila Suta Gosvami will answer this question and another of Saunaka Rsi’s inquiries in the following texts.

## Texts 16-21: Bhakti Progresses

**О twice-born sages, by serving those devotees who are completely freed from all vice, great service is done. By such service, one gains affinity for hearing the messages of Vasudeva. (Bhag.** [**1.2.16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.16)**)**

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to Bhagavatam [1.2.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.16) addresses this point directly: “The servants of God come to propagate God consciousness, and intelligent people should cooperate with them in every respect. By serving the servant of God, one can please God more than by directly serving the Lord. The Lord is more pleased when He sees that His servants are properly respected because such servants risk everything for the service of the Lord and so are very dear to the Lord. The Lord declares in the Bhagavad-gita (18.69) that no one is dearer to Him than one who risks everything to preach His glory. By serving the servants of the Lord, one gradually gets the quality of such servants, and thus one becomes qualified to hear the glories of God. The eagerness to hear about God is the first qualification of a devotee eligible for entering the kingdom of God.”

Srila Sridhara Svami’s comment on text 16 responds to the question, I lack a taste for hearing, so what should I do? He says that visiting places of pilgrimage and serving the mahatmas residing there will gradually purify us and evoke our spiritual desires. Jiva Gosvami comments that holy people frequent holy places; meeting them, taking their association, and feeling their potency will awaken our desire to gain knowledge about the Supreme by hearing krsna-katha from them. Further spiritual taste is generated from this initial desire to hear krsna' katha.

Practically speaking, devotees are moving holy places. Yudhisthira Maharaja told Vidura: “My lord, devotees like your good self are verily holy places personified. Because you carry the Personality of Godhead within your heart, you turn all places into places of pilgrimage.” (Bhag. [1.13.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/13.10))

Bhagavatam [10.87.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/87.35) further describes the exalted qualities of devotees and the effects of serving them: “Sages free from false pride live on this earth by frequenting the sacred pilgrimage sites and those places where the Supreme Lord displayed His pastimes. Because such devotees keep Your lotus feet within their hearts, the water that washes their feet destroys all sins. Anyone who even once turns his mind toward You, the ever-blissful Soul of all existence, no longer dedicates himself to serving family life at home, which simply robs a man of his good qualities.”

Srila Sridhara Svami comments on this text: The rsis who have been characterized in the statements so far made are free from false ego because Your lotus feet are in their hearts. Thus they are such that the water that has washed their feet destroys sins.

He continues: Alternatively, those who possess vast pious credit, symptomized by their worship of the Supreme Lord, are all gurus in the sense that they are great, as are the holy pilgrimage sites where such saints are found. No longer do they worship those homes that steal the essential qualities, headed by discrimination, steadfastness, sobriety, tolerance, and peacefulness, of men. Nor do they continue to pay regard to the contemptible happiness found in such homes. Those who even once give their minds to You are no longer attached to home and so on, what to speak of those who possess the pious credit of pure devotional service.

Srila Sridhara Svami prays: “My dear Lord, when will I give up all sense gratification and engage incessantly in meditating on You? And when I take up my residence in the hermitages of saintly devotees free from false pride, then I will become fully immersed in the inundation of nectar pouring from lotus mouths as they chant sacred narrations about You. And then, О Lord Narahari, I will never again have to take a material body.” (quoted in the purport to Bhag. [10.87.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/87.35))

In Bhagavadgita [13.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/13.26), Krsna Himself describes why preachers, who allow others to hear about Him, are so dear to Him: “There are those who, although not conversant in spiritual knowledge, begin to worship the Supreme Person upon hearing about Him from others. Because of their tendency to hear from authorities, they also transcend the path of birth and death.” In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada notes that most people in modem society are innocent: “This verse is particularly applicable to modem society because in modem society there is practically no education in spiritual matters. Some of the people may appear to be atheistic or agnostic or philosophical, but actually there is no knowledge of philosophy. As for the common man, if he is a good soul, then there is a chance for advancement by hearing. This hearing process is very important. Lord Caitanya, who preached Krsna consciousness in the modem world, gave great stress to hearing because if the common man simply hears from authoritative sources he can progress, especially, according to Lord Caitanya, if he hears the transcendental vibration Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare.”

Krsna is pleased with those who serve preachers, His dearmost devotees. Preachers are dear to Krsna because they renounce their own convenience to tell others of their eternal relationship with Krsna. It is natural that serving such selfless devotees pleases Krsna.

The ability to please Krsna by preaching is not limited, of course, to those who have taken sannyasa and travel worldwide. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu ordered:

*ydre dekha, tare kaha ‘krsna’-upadesa*  
*amara ajndya guru hana tara’ ei desa*

**Instruct everyone to follow the orders of Lord Sri Krsna as they are given in Bhagavad-gita and Srimad- Bhagavatam. In this way become a spiritual master and try to liberate everyone in this land. (Cc. Madhya** [**7.128**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/7.128)**)**

In his purport, Prabhupada states, “This is the sublime mission of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. . . . The Krsna consciousness movement is trying to elevate human society to the perfection of life by pursuing the method described by Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu in His advice to the brahmana Kurma. That is, one should stay at home, chant the Hare Krsna mantra and preach the instructions of Krsna as given in Bhagavad-gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam.”

Preachers in ISKCON should think of themselves as insignificant servants of Srila Prabhupada and his mission to establish Krsna consciousness in the world. If they feel their insignificance, they will be able to pray that Srila Prabhupada preach through them, or that in one of any number of ways they may assist Srila Prabhupada and his mission. Such a service mood will award them a taste for hearing krsna-katha.

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on Bhagavatam [1.2.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.16) in Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 11. He states that this text also means that by seeing, touching, conversing with, and in other ways serving the great souls who travel to or permanently reside in holy places, one develops faith in those great souls. He explains that one will then naturally wonder about the taste these great souls experience when they speak about the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and this will encourage one to hear about Him in order to understand it. In this way, the desire to hear about the Lord is bom, and by hearing about Krsna one will become attracted to Him. Thus by hearing from great souls, one attains the goal of life.

## The Progression in Bhagavatam 1.2.16-21 Described by Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura

**Texts 16-17**

For his commentary on Bhagavatam [1.2.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.21), Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura composed a verse that lists fourteen stages of spiritual development indicated by texts 16-21, and his commentaries on those six texts include specific words or phrases that define each stage. He derives five stages from text 16 alone (although he derives the first two stages from the same term in the text):

**1) satam krpa**—the mercy of devotees. The phrase mahat-sevaya, he explains, means “by service to the devotees”: “This indicates that the opportunity to serve the devotees arises from their causeless mercy. Therefore, mercy is the first step.”

**2) mahat-seva**—service to devotees is the second stage.

**3) sraddha**—faith. The word sraddadhanasya, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains, means “for a man in whom faith has developed by serving devotees.”

**4) gurupadasrayah**—seeking shelter at the feet of a guru. Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, quoting the Amara-kosa dictionary, says that in the line punya'tirtha'nisevanat, “ttrtha also means guru.” A man in whom faith has developed must seek shelter at the feet of a guru.

**5) bhajanesu sprha**—eagerness to worship. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that susruhoh means that a person who becomes eager to hear by taking shelter at the feet of a guru will eventually develop taste.

After serving devotees, we begin to desire to hear about Krsna. What happens next?

**Sri Krsna, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Supersoul in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted. (Bhag.** [**1.2.17**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.17)**)**

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to this text describes how Krsna helps those who are eager to hear krsna-katha: “The Lord is reciprocally respondent to His devotees. When He sees that a devotee is completely sincere in getting admittance to the transcendental service of the Lord and has thus become eager to hear about Him, the Lord acts from within the devotee in such a way that the devotee may easily go back to Him. The Lord is more anxious to take us back into His kingdom than we can desire. Most of us do not desire at all to go back to Godhead. Only a very few men want to go back to Godhead. But anyone who desires to go back to Godhead, Sri Krsna helps in all respects.”

Krsna is supremely virtuous, and hearing about Him creates virtue in us. Krsna is suhrt, our dearmost friend, well-wisher, and benefactor. He removes abhadrani, inauspiciousness, from the hearts of those eager to hear about Him. Such abhadrani is also called anartha. Specific anarthas cause unsteady devotional service. In the second “Shower” of Mddhurya'kddambini, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura defines six anarthas that initially cause unsteadiness:

**(a) utsaha-mayi**: enthusiasm indicating pride. Pride in personal devotional achievements causes beginning devotees to immaturely think that they, unlike others, have already mastered everything.

**(b) ghana-tarala**: moving unsteadily between diligence and negligence. Such a devotee chants his rounds one day; the next day he’s too busy. One day he reads scripture; the next, he’s too sleepy.

**(c) vyudha-vikalpa**: flickering determination. “Should I remain a householder or become renounced?” “Should I enjoy my youth and thereby fulfill my tendency for sense gratification, or should I practice renunciation now?” Those suffering from vyudha-vikalpa will offer quotations from sastra that confirm each choice.

**(d) visaya-sangara**: an ongoing struggle with sense pleasure. Seeing themselves being carried away by waves of material enjoyment, devotees firmly resolve: “From now on, I'll take shelter of Krsna’s holy name.” They then try to renounce everything and to simply chant, but their practice is intermittent and they are loxcedby xbeb wmvaiuKAo    bavtvtuouuccd.

**(e) niyamaksama**: inability to improve devotional practices. “From today on I will chant sixty-four rounds.” “From today on, I will see the deities three times a day.” “From today on, I will read a chapter of Bhagavad-gita daily.” Despite such good intentions and even vows, these devotees cannot increase or improve their practices.

**(f) taranga-rangini**: delighting in the material facilities that bhakti produces. The engaging nature of bhakti attracts position, followers, and wealth. Devotees become enamored by these small waves (taranga) in the ocean of bhakti.

One’s devotional service becomes steady when these six obstacles are removed.

Although these anarthas are difficult to take away, Krsna can easily remove them. In his purport to Bhagavatam [1.2.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.17), Srila Prabhupada explains that material desires, especially desires for women and wealth, are extremely difficult to remove from the heart. “But when one is helped by the Lord Himself, the whole proess becomes as easy as anything by the divine grace of the Lord. To become restless in the contact of women and wealth is not an astonishment, because every living being is associated with such things from remote time, practically immemorial, and it takes time to recover from this foreign nature. But if one is engaged in hearing the glories of the Lord, gradually he realizes his real position. By the grace of God such a devotee gets sufficient strength to defend himself from the state of disturbances, and gradually all disturbing elements are eliminated from his mind.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura next explains that Bhagavatam [1.2.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.17) contains just one stage, bhajanesu sprha—eagerness to worship—which was already mentioned as the fifth stage in connection with the previous text. In text 17, that stage is indicated by the lines smvatam sva-katham krsnah punya-sravana-kirtanah. From the desire to hear follows the practices of hearing, chanting, and then remembering. So much therefore depends on our eagerness to hear and chant.

What occurs after we become eager to hear, which begins the clearing of material desires from the heart?

**By regular attendance in classes on the Bhagavatam and by rendering of service to the pure devotee, all that is troublesome to the heart is almost completely destroyed, and loving service unto the Personality of Godhead, who is praised with transcendental songs, is established as an irrevocable fact. Bhagavatam** [**1.2.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.18)

By hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam and serving devotees, all inauspiciousness (abhadresu) is almost completely (prdyesu) destroyed (nasta).

One therefore becomes fixed in devotional service (bhaktir bhavati naisthiki). Srila Prabhupada’s purport to Bhagavatam [1.2.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.18) speaks of the Bhagavatam as the remedy for inauspiciousness: “Here is the remedy for eliminating all inauspicious things within the heart which are considered to be obstacles in the path of self-realization. The remedy is the association of the Bhagavatas. There are two types of Bhag' avatas, namely the book Bhagavata and the devotee Bhagavata. Both the Bhagavatas are competent remedies, and both of them or either of them can be good enough to eliminate the obstacles. A devotee Bhag' avata is as good as the book Bhagavata because the devotee Bhagavata leads his life in terms of the book Bhagavata and the book Bhagavata is full of information about the Personality of Godhead and His pure devotees, who are also Bhagavatas. Bhagavata book and person are identical.”

Prabhupada continues to glorify the potency of Vaisnava association, by which one may become a great devotee, as did Narada simply by association with these two Bhagavatas. “These are the miraculous effects of the association of Bhagavatas.... The more progress is made in devotional service under the guidance of the Bhagavatas, the more one becomes fixed in the transcendental loving service of the Lord. The messages of the book Bhagavata, therefore, have to be received from the devotee Bhagavata, and the combination of these two Bhag' avatas will help the neophyte devotee to make progress on and on.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that Bhagavatam [1.2.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.18) indicates three stages:

**6) bhaktih—bhakti**. The phrase bhaktir bhavati naisthiki contains the word bhakti, devotional service. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura makes no comment on the word bhakti.

**7) anarthapagamam**—disappearance of obstacles. The phrase nasta' prayesv abhadresu means that inauspicious things, including the namaparadhas, are almost completely destroyed.

**8) tatha nistha**—then steadiness is achieved. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that contained in the phrase bhaktir bhavati naisthiki is the word naisthiki, which means nistha.

What occurs after a devotee reaches nistha, steadiness?

**As soon as irrevocable loving service is established in the heart, the effects of nature’s modes of passion and ignorance, such as lust, desire and hankering, disappear from the heart. Then the devotee is established in goodness, and he becomes completely happy. Bhagavatam** [**1.2.19**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.19)

In the depths of Krsna consciousness, in which all material desires are destroyed, the heart plunges into pure goodness (suddha-sattva). At that time, the heart is qualified to receive the Lord’s direct audience, or darsana. Although the modes of nature may to some extent still be acting on devotees of this caliber, the modes are unable to actually influence them. Srila Prabhupada explains these effects of bhakti at this stage in his purport to Bhagavatam [1.2.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.19): “The soul’s activity becomes adulterated in contact with matter, and as such the diseased activities are expressed in the form of lust, desire, hankering, inactivity, foolishness and sleep. The effect of devotional service becomes manifest by complete elimination of these effects of passion and ignorance. The devotee is fixed at once in the mode of goodness, and he makes further progress to rise to the position of vasudeva, or the state of unmixed sattva, or suddha-sattva. Only in this suddha-sattva state can one always see Krsna eye to eye by dint of pure affection for the Lord.”

Bhagavatam [11.2.53](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.53) describes the purity of love of such an advanced devotee: “The lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are sought even by the greatest of demigods, such as Brahma and Siva, who have all accepted the Supreme Personality of Godhead as their life and soul. A pure devotee of the Lord can never forget those lotus feet in any circumstance. He will not give up his shelter at the lotus feet of the Lord for a single moment—indeed, not even for half a moment—even in exchange for the benediction of ruling and enjoying the opulence of the entire universe. Such a devotee of the Lord is to be considered the best of the Vaisnavas.”

Text 19 indicates that it is difficult to advance under the grip of passion and ignorance. From passion (rajas) comes distraction (viksepa), and from ignorance (tamos) sleepiness (lay a). Adayah means “and more” negative qualities, such as anger, greed, envy, and illusion. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura notes that text 19 indicates two stages in the progression of bhakti—ruci and asakti:

**9) ruci**—taste. He defines “the heart is not pierced by sense objects” by saying that one develops distaste (arucya) for sense objects. Thus one arrives at actual spiritual taste, ruci. Although the word ruci was also mentioned in Bhagavatam 1.2.16 (vasudeva-katha-rucih), Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura treated it only as a remote result of gurupadasraya (taking shelter of a guru) and bhajanesu sprha (eagerness to worship).

**10) atha asakti**—then firm attachment. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that in the phrase sthitam sattve prasidati, sthitam, “fixed,” means asaktam, or firmly attached.

One unaffected by rajas and tamas will easily get a taste, ruci, from spiritual practice. Yet even in the stage of ruci, one’s mind may wander. However, we can drag the mind back under our control by the strength of our intelligence.

The next stage, asakti (attachment) is different. If the mind does wander, the strength of our attraction to Krsna automatically pulls it back. Thus text 19 states that when (tada) the effects of passion and ignorance (rajas'tamo^bhdvah)—lust, greed, and so on (kamadobhadayas ca ye)—no longer affect us (ceta etair anaviddham), we will become situated in goodness (sthitam sattve) and feel fully happy (prasidati).

What does a progressive soul experience after asakti?

**Thus established in the mode of unalloyed goodness, the man whose mind has been enlivened by contact with devotional serv' ice to the Lord gains positive scientific knowledge of the Personality of Godhead in the stage of liberation from all material association. Bhagavatam** [**1.2.20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.20)

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to this text explains the qualifications necessary for us to actually know the Supreme Personality of Godhead: “As soon as one understands that he has nothing to do with matter, he at once ceases his material hankerings and becomes enlivened as a spiritual being. This attainment of success is possible when one is above the modes of passion and ignorance, or, in other words, when one is actually a brahmana by qualification. A brahmana is the symbol of sattva-guna, or the mode of goodness. . . . One has to surpass the brahminical stage and reach the vasudeva stage \[transcendental to the modes\] to understand the Personality of Godhead Krsna.

The science of the Personality of Godhead is the subject matter for study by the postgraduate students in the spiritual line. Foolish men, or men with a poor fund of knowledge, do not understand the Supreme Lord, and they interpret Krsna according to their respective whims. The fact is, however, that one cannot understand the science of the Personality of Godhead unless one is freed from the contamination of the material modes, even up to the stage of a brahmana. When a qualified brahmana factually becomes a Vaisnava, in the enlivened state of liberation he can know what is actually the Personality of Godhead.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami also comments on text 20 in Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 15: As previously described (evam), by engaging in devotional service one becomes enlivened (prasanna-manasah) and liberated from association (muktasangasya) with lust and other vices. In this way pure, positive (suddha-sattva) knowledge (vijnanam) is manifest (jayate), whereby the Lord appears in and (without the process of meditation) outside the heart.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura lists these four stages of bhakti indicated in text 20:

**11) ratih**—fondness. This is indicated by the phrase evam prasanna~ manasah. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura shows that prasanna' manasah, “of one whose mind is satisfied,” means utpanna-rateh, “of one whose fondness has arisen.”

**12) prema**—devotional love. About the phrase bhagavad'bhakti-yogatah, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes that engaging in devotion to Bhagavan, bhagavati bhakti-yogah, is prema, “devotional love.”

**13) atha darsanam**—then vision, audience. About the phrase bhagavat-tattva-vijnanam, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that vijnanam means “experience,” anubhavah. Thus realization follows prema, and refers to experiencing Krsna’s form, pastimes, greatness, sweetness, and qualities,.

**14) harer madhuryanubhava**—direct experience of Hari’s sweetness. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura notes that bhagavat'tattva~ vijnanam occurs after one experiences Lord Hari directly.

Commenting on Bhagavatam [1.2.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.21), Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura will note that words in that text again refer to stage 13.

**Thus the knot in the heart is pierced, and all misgivings are cut to pieces. The chain of fruitive actions is terminated when one sees the self as master. Bhagavatam** [**1.2.21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.21)

This text describes liberation and reiterates effects already described. The Visnu Purana ([6.5.59](https://vedarama.com/en/books/vp/6.5.59)) notes that this stage of devotional service, wherein one attains the Supreme Lord, is the actual cure for suffering: “This is the medicine that fills the taker with transcendental bliss.”

Prabhupada’s purport to Bhagavatam [1.2.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.21) describes the piercing of “the knot in the heart,” which awards liberation: “This knot is called ahankara, and it falsely obliges a living being to become identified with matter. As soon as this knot is loosened . . . One sees his master and fully engages himself in the transcendental loving service of the Lord, making a full termination of the chain of fruitive action.”

And who is the devotee’s liberator and master? The Personality of Godhead takes charge of illuminating the heart of a devotee engaged in His service in transcendental love, as the Lord Himself explains (Bg. [10.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.11)). Lord Siva explains how we can attain this exalted qualification in his prayer to Lord Aniruddha (Bhag. [4.24.59](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.59)): “The devotee whose heart has been completely cleansed by the process of devotional service and who is favored by Bhaktidevi \[the personification of devotional service\] does not become bewildered by the external energy, which is just like a dark well. Being completely cleansed of all material contamination in this way, a devotee is able to understand very happily Your name, fame, form, activities, etc.”

Yet having a sinless heart is not the sole cause of directly seeing Krsna. Our pure heart must also be filled with devotional longing to see the Lord. That longing is the root from which seeing the Supreme Personality of Godhead grows. By such yearning, we attain all perfection. “Pure devotional service in Krsna consciousness cannot be had even by pious activity in hundreds and thousands of lives. It can be attained only by paying one price—that is, intense greed to obtain it. If it is available somewhere, one must purchase it without delay.” (spoken by Ramananda Raya in Cc. Madhya [8.70](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/8.70))

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on text 21 that seeing the Lord increases our eagerness to serve Him. That eagerness powerfully overrules our feeling of being disqualified for this service. In Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 16, Sri Jiva notes that this text describes the results obtained when the independent and supremely blissful Lord directly appears. He explains that the phrase “knot in the heart” (hrdaya-granthih) refers to misidentification with false ego. The phrase “all misgivings are cut to pieces” (sarva-samsayah ksiyante) means that by our engaging in devotional activities, the Lord can be seen directly. At that time all doubts are destroyed. By our hearing about the Lord, all theories opposing devotional service are cut to pieces, and by our meditating on the Lord, all meditations opposing devotional service are devastated. When the Lord personally appears, the devotee’s disqualifications are shredded. The word ksiyante means “completely destroyed.” “Simply by the Lord’s desire, even the slightest trace of these disqualifications no longer remains.”

In Priti-sandarbha, anuccheda 1, Srila Jiva Gosvami mentions that Sukadeva Gosvami described liberation in Bhagavatam [12.4.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/4.34) with words similar to those found in Bhagavatam [1.2.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.20): “When the illusory false ego that binds the soul has been cut off with the sword of discriminating knowledge and one has developed realization of Lord Acyuta, the Supreme Soul, this is called the ultimate annihilation of material existence.” Srila Jiva explains that the state described here, wherein the soul sees the infallible Supreme Personality of Godhead, is called liberation. He also notes that these words mean that although the soul may still reside in the world of birth and death, he may nevertheless see his original spiritual form directly. This means that the soul’s misidentification with the external material body (anyatha-rupam) has been destroyed.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments that the words drsta evatmanisvare in Bhagavatam [1.2.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/12.21) refer to the thirteenth stage of bhakti: seeing the Lord directly. As mentioned before, at the end of his commentary on text 21, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura presents a verse that contains fourteen steps, a progression ending with direct experience of Lord Hari’s sweetness. These stages—along with the relationships between the stages and the words and phrases in Bhagavatam [1.2.16-21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.16)—have already been analyzed. A summary follows:

1. satam krpa—the mercy of devotees (Bhag. 1.2.16)
2. mahat'seva—service to devotees (Bhag. 1.2.16)
3. sraddha—faith (Bhag. 1.2.16)
4. gurupaddsrayah—seeking shelter at the guru’s feet (Bhag. 1.2.16)
5. bhajanesu sprha.—eagerness to worship Krsna (Bhag. 1.2.16-17)
6. bhaktih—bhakti (Bhag. 1.2.18)
7. anarthapagamah—disappearance of obstacles (Bhag. 1.2.18)
8. tatha nistha—then steadiness (Bhag. 1.2.18)
9. rucih—taste (Bhag. 1.2.19)
10. atha asakti—then firm attachment (Bhag. 1.2.19)
11. ratih—fondness (Bhag. 1.2.20)
12. prema—devotional love (Bhag. 1.2.20)
13. atha darsanam—then vision, audience (Bhag. 1.2.20-21)
14. harer madhuryanubhava—direct experience of Hari’s sweetness (Bhag. 1.2.20)

What can we conclude?

## Texts 22-29: The Conclusion is that Hari, Vasudeva, Lord Krsna, is the Absolute Truth, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and Only He Should be Served

Suta Gosvami, presenting the conclusion to texts 16-21, continues: “Certainly, therefore, since time immemorial, all transcendentalists have been rendering devotional service to Lord Krsna, the Personality of Godhead, with great delight, because such devotional service is enlivening to the self.” Bhagavatam [1.2.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.22)

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to this text notes that Vasudeva is mentioned in this text as the object of the transcendentalists’ worship. This Vasudeva refers to Sri Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead: “Lord Sri Krsna is the svayarh-rupa Personality of Godhead, and all other forms of Godhead, beginning from Sri Baladeva, Sankarsana, Vasudeva, Aniruddha, Pradyumna and Narayana and extending to the purusa-avataras, guna-avataras, lila-avataras, yuga^avataras and many other thousands of manifestations of the Personality of Godhead, are Lord Sri Krsna’s plenary portions and integrated parts.” (Bhag. [1.2.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.22), purport)

In Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 17, Srila Jiva Gosvami’s comment on this text explains that the words atma-prasadanim mean “purification of heart,” which is not all that occurs when we perform devotional service. Devotional service, as Bhagavatam [1.2.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.22) explains, is performed with “great delight” (paramay a muda).
