[1.19.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/19.33)) In your presence our sins are immediately vanquished. О saint! О great mystic! Without having been directly inspired by Lord Krsna, how could you have voluntarily appeared here?

In his purport to text 36 Srila Prabhupada’s speaks of the benefit an inquiring soul may achieve from an inspired spiritual master:

**The great sage Sukadeva Gosvami was certainly inspired by Lord Krsna to appear voluntarily before Maharaja Pariksit, the great devotee of the Lord, just to give him the teachings of Srimad-Bhagavatam. One can achieve the nucleus of the devotional service of the Lord by the mercy of the spiritual master and the Personality of Godhead. The spiritual master is the manifested representative of the Lord to help one achieve ultimate success. One who is not authorized by the Lord cannot become a spiritual master. Srila Sukadeva Gosvami is an authorized spiritual master, and thus he was inspired by the Lord to appear before Maharaja Parik-sit and instruct him in the teachings of Srimad-Bhagavatam. One can achieve the ultimate success of going back to Godhead if he is favored by the Lord’s sending His true representative. As soon as a true representative of the Lord is met by a devotee of the Lord, the devotee is assured a guarantee for going back to Godhead just after leaving the present body. This, however, depends on the sincerity of the devotee himself. The Lord is seated in the heart of all living beings, and thus he knows very well the movements of all individual persons. As soon as the Lord finds that a particular soul is very eager to go back to Godhead, the Lord at once sends His bona fide representative. The sincere devotee is thus assured by the Lord of going back to Godhead. The conclusion is that to get the assistance and help of a bona fide spiritual master means to receive the direct help of the Lord Himself.**

Maharaja Pariksit continued: “You are the spiritual master of great saints and devotees. I am therefore begging you to show the way of perfection for all persons, and especially for one who is about to die. Please let me know what a man should hear, chant, remember and worship, and also what he should not do. Please explain all this to me.” (Bhag. [1.19.37-38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/19.37))

Srila Prabhupada describes the proper mood with which one should inquire from a spiritual master in his purport to text 37: “Unless one is perfectly anxious to inquire about the way of perfection, there is no necessity of approaching a spiritual master. . . . Maharaja Pariksit is the right type of disciple because he puts forward questions vital to the interest of all men, particularly for the dying men. The question put forward by Maharaja Pariksit is the basic principle of the complete thesis of Srimad-Bhagavatam.’’

Maharaja Pariksit stated: О powerful brahmana, I have heard it said that you hardly stay in the houses of men long enough to milk a cow, yet inspired by Sri Krsna, you have mercifully come before me as I near the time of my death.

Commenting on Maharaja Pariksit’s sentiment, Srila Sridhara Svami rephrases it: It is rare to see you (Sukadeva Gosvami), what to speak of hear from you.

After hearing Maharaja Pariksit’s sweet words, powerful Sukadeva Gosvami, son of Vyasadeva, began his reply.

Although Maharaja Pariksit has accepted his fate as Krsna’s mercy and has even attained the great sage Sukadeva Gosvami’s association, it is tempting to consider how Maharaja Pariksit cheated Kali by containing him in places that didn’t exist in his kingdom. One could question whether the king’s plan was actually effective, as Maharaja Pariksit was cursed because of Kali’s influence. If Kali had been killed rather than simply restricted, the world would have continued to flourish under the king’s benign rule. Did Pariksit Maharaja make a mistake?

Actually, Maharaja Pariksit acted wonderfully. By the action of unstoppable time in Krsna’s universal management system, ages with different qualities cycle naturally; Kali-yuga must occur. Yet Maharaja Pariksit couldn’t allow Kali to act in his kingdom. The necessary progression of Kali-yuga and a powerful, effective monarch are contradictory. They cannot exist side by side.

Bhagavatam [12.2.12-16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/2.12) and [12.3.24-44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/3.24) describe Kali’s horrendous symptoms. One wonders why the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the all-good supreme controller, demands that Kali-yuga have its day. Just after the above Bhagavatam texts, however, in Bhagavatam [12.3.45-50](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/3.45), Sukadeva Gosvami instructs the king how to receive death. In texts 51-52, Sukadeva describes Kali-yuga’s supreme benefit. “My dear King, although Kali-yuga is an ocean of faults, there is still one good quality about this age: Simply by chanting the Hare Krsna mahd-mantra, one can become free from material bondage and be promoted to the transcendental kingdom. Whatever result was obtained in Satya-yuga by meditating on Visnu, in Treta-yuga by performing sacrifices, and in Dvapara-yuga by serving the Lord’s lotus feet can be obtained in Kali-yuga simply by chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra.”But couldn’t Krsna, who is an ocean of kindness, offer the benefit of Kali-yuga without allowing so much suffering and misery? This question has been answered in various scriptures by various acaryas, including Srila Sridhara Svami and Srila Jiva Gosvami. The following is from the Bhaktivedanta Book Trust’s commentary on Bhagavatam [11.5.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.37):

**In the Skanda Purana, as well as in other Puranas, there is the following statement: mahd-bhagavata nityam kalau kurvanti lartanam. “During Kali-yuga the great devotees of the Lord always engage in kirtana, chanting the Lord’s holy names.” It is the nature of the Supreme Personality of Godhead to be merciful, and He is especially merciful to those who, in a helpless condition, take complete shelter of His lotus feet. One can immediately take shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord by chanting His holy names. According to Sridhara Svami, even in previous ages such as Satya-yuga it was not possible for the living entities to achieve the perfection that is available in Kali-yuga. Srila Jiva Gosvami has explained this as follows. In former ages such as Satya-yuga human beings were perfectly qualified and easily performed even the most difficult spiritual processes, meditating for many thousands of years practically without eating or sleeping. Thus, although in any age one who completely takes shelter of the Lord’s holy name gets all perfection, the highly qualified inhabitants of Satya-yuga do not consider that merely moving the tongue and lips, chanting the Lord’s holy name, is a complete process and that the Lord’s holy name is the only shelter within the universe. They are more attracted to the difficult and elaborate yoga system of meditation, complete with sophisticated sitting postures, painstaking control of the breath and deep, extended meditations in trance on the Personality of Godhead within the heart. In Satya-yuga sinful life is practically unheard of, and therefore people are not afflicted with the terrible reactions seen in Kali-yuga, such as world war, famine, plague, drought, insanity, etc. Although in Satya-yuga people always worship the Personality of Godhead as the ultimate goal of life and meticulously follow His laws, called dharma, they do not feel themselves to be in a helpless condition, and thus they do not always experience intense love for the Lord.**

**However, in Kali-yuga living conditions are so unbearable, modem governments are so obnoxious, our bodies are so ridden by physical and mental disease, and even self-preservation is so troublesome, that the conditioned souls intensely cry out the holy name of Krsna begging for relief from the onslaught of this age.**

Srila Prabhupada said that in Kali-yuga, “the mental diseases of the present generation are more acute than bodily diseases.” Everyone is continuously disturbed. Devotees, therefore, seeking to escape Kali’s inconsistencies and torture, can chant the Hare Krsna maha-mantra, calling out to Krsna with full hearts. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu has therefore bestowed His blessings by saying, param vijayate sri'krsna'sankirtanam: “All glories to Sri Krsna sankirtana!” May the holy names of Krsna be victorious throughout the world! May the glorious message of Srimad-Bhagavatam spoken by Sukadeva Gosvami to Maharaja Pariksit, by Suta Gosvami to Saunaka Rsi and the sages of Naimisaranya, and by Srila Prabhupada to the fallen souls of Kali-yuga completely purify all hearers! And as the final texts (Bhag. [12.13.22-23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/13.22)) in Srimad-Bhagavatam state: “O Lord of lords, О master, please grant us pure devotional service at Your lotus feet, life after life. I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Lord, Hari, the congregational chanting of whose holy names destroys all sinful reactions, and the offering of obeisances unto whom relieves all material suffering.”

## CANTO TWO

## Dialogue One - The Path of Perfection For Those About to Die

## Chapter 1 - The First Step in God Realization

## Texts 1-15: The Sage Immediately Answers the King’s Question

Maharaja Pariksit, soon to pass from this world, requested Sukadeva Gosvami to explain clearly what he should do during his remaining days. Before Sukadeva’s reply begins, however, auspiciousness is invoked: otn namo bhagavate vasudevaya, “O my Lord, the allpervading Personality of Godhead, I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.” (Bhag. 2.1, Invocation)

The goal of Srimad-Bhagavatam is to awaken the hearer to his or her loving relationship with Krsna. Although Krsna is all-pervading, He is nevertheless a person. This understanding is impossible to grasp with our finite intelligence. It is natural to wonder how a person with specific characteristics and form can be unlimited. To understand the Supreme Lord’s personal form, one must hear Srimad-Bhagavatam from His devotee. Even a great Bhagavatam scholar not in the devotional line will be forced in his studies, by the Lord’s illusory energy, to reach an incorrect or only partially correct conclusion. Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, will remain covered and unavailable to such a person, because the Lord reveals His nature only to those who serve Him with devotion—His devotees.

If one doesn’t truly accept the Absolute Truth as a person, then one will be unable to have a loving relationship with Him. Loving relationships are possible only between persons. When impersonalists perform bhakti, as some Mayavadis do, they can practice only a shadow of true devotional service. This is because they are not really attempting to please the Lord; they don’t even accept Him as a person. Rather, their “bhakti" is based on their attempt to lose their individuality—to become one with Krsna’s brahmajyoti. Such “service” is not a devotional offering but an offering based on selfish motivation. This means that while serving the Lord’s deity form, impersonalists use the service they perform as a vehicle to become the Deity. The devotees’ service, on the other hand, is far different; pure devotees offer unmotivated service simply to give Krsna pleasure.

The Second Canto begins with Sukadeva Gosvami complimenting Maharaja Pariksit on the depth of his question. Actually, as Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to the invocation, the king’s question has hinted that “worship of Lord Krsna is the ultimate function of every living entity.” Sukadeva therefore welcomed the idea and replied: “My dear King, your question is glorious because it is very beneficial to all kinds of people. The answer to this question is the prime subject matter for hearing, and it is approved by all transcendentalists.” (Bhag. [2.1.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.1))These words are the first Sukadeva Gosvami speaks in Srimad-Bhagavatam. He has appeared by Krsna’s will exactly at the appropriate moment. Maharaja Pariksit has just asked the sages on the bank of the Ganges about his duty during the fearful time immediately before death. Most people facing the same circumstance remain fearful and choose to take shelter of illusion and forgetfulness. Maharaja Pariksit, however, faced reality and remained sober. Srila Prabhupada summarized these events in a lecture given in Melbourne on June 26, 1974:

**Pariksit Maharaja was going to die within seven days, for he was cursed by a brahmana boy. The King was in the forest, engaged in hunting, and when he became tired he went to the cottage of a sage and asked him for water. But the sage was absorbed in meditation and could not hear him. Pariksit Maharaja, being thirsty, became angry. He took a dead snake and wrapped it around the neck of the meditating sage. This news was spread, and his son, who was only twelve years old, heard that his father was insulted. Immediately he cursed that a snake would bite the King in seven days. After his meditation was over, the father was very sorry that such a great king has been cursed. He was very, very sorry, but what could be done? The brahmana boy’s curse must be effective.**

**In those days brahmanas, even by caste, were very, very strong in spiritual strength. When Pariksit Maharaja was informed that he was to die within seven days, he accepted the curse: “Yes, I was wrong to insult the sage.” Otherwise, he could counteract. He was also powerful. But he did not counteract. This is the history.**

**Pariksit Maharaja immediately left his kingdom, family, and children, and went to the bank of the Ganges and sat down, prepared for his imminent death... Because the emperor of the world was going to die, the news spread. And all big, big men, great saintly persons, even demigods, they also came to see him.**

**And he was asking everyone, “What is my duty?” Pariksit Maharaja was a devotee of Lord Krsna from the beginning of his life. He inquired, “Whether I shall absorb my mind in Krsna consciousness?” The sages that had gathered gave different advice: “Maharaja, do this at the time of death,” “Do that,” “Do this.” There were many big persons and so many opinions that he was perplexed. But he was a devotee of Krsna from the beginning of his life, and thus he inquired, “Whether it is better to absorb the mind in Krsna consciousness?” This was his question.**

**This is answered all over the Srimad-Bhagavatam, but specifically in the first two chapters and the beginning of the third chapter of the Second Canto. Sukadeva Gosvami is going to speak of it in a gradual, progressive way. At that time Sukadeva Gosvami arrived.**

**Sukadeva Gosvami was young boy, but he was a parama-hamsa, and he was received in that big assembly as a great personality of knowledge. Everyone stood up.**

**He was such a great personality. He was given a nice seat, as is the custom, and then he advised Maharaja Pariksit as to “What is my duty?” Because Maharaja Pariksit was a devotee, he wanted to hear about Krsna. But he was confirming with Sukadeva that he was right in thinking in that way.**

**So in answer to this question, Sukadeva Gosvami replied, variydn esa te prasnah krto loka-hitam nrpa: “My dear King, your inquiry is very glorious because on account of this question, whatever I shall reply ...” He knew that the question was about Krsna, and the reply will be the Srimad-Bhagavatam.**

The word loka-hitam used in the opening text indicates that Maharaja Pariksit asked a question that will benefit all people. Srila Jiva Gosvami explains that the word variyan (“glorious”) Srila Sukadeva Gosvami used in his reply indicates that this question is the greatest of questions. Srila Prabhupada amplifies the glory of this question in his purport to the first text: “Lord Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu said that the highest perfection of life is to achieve the transcendental loving service of Krsna. Because questions and answers about Krsna elevate one to that transcendental position, the questions of Maharaja Pariksit about Krsna philosophy are greatly glorified. Maharaja Pariksit wanted to absorb his mind completely in Krsna, and such absorption can be effected simply by hearing about the uncommon activities of Krsna. . . . It is very auspicious, therefore, to hear always about Krsna. So Maharaja Pariksit requested Sukadeva Gosvami to narrate the activities of Krsna so that he could engage his mind in Krsna. The activities of Krsna are nondifferent from Krsna Himself. As long as one is engaged in hearing such transcendental activities of Krsna, he remains aloof from the conditional life of material existence. The topics of Lord Krsna are so auspicious that they purify the speaker, the hearer and the inquirer.”

Hearing is like pouring sound into the funnel of the ear. As a bottle will fill when one pours liquid into it, so the mind will fill and become absorbed in the subject of one’s hearing. But do people choose to hear about things other than Krsna at the time of death? Obviously they do. Therefore, Sukadeva states, criticizing those interested only in the temporary: “Those persons who are materially engrossed, being blind to the knowledge of ultimate truth, have many subject matters for hearing in human society, О Emperor.” (Bhag. [2.1.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.2))

The word grha mentioned in Bhagavatam [2.1.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.2) means “house.” The term grhastha is used when a householder uses his time and asrama to help himself advance spiritually. Household life is considered an asrama when it is used for spiritual progress. When a householder is materialistic, however, the suffix medhi, “envious,” is affixed to grha to show that his values are quite different from those of the grhastha.

“Blind” grhamedhis may be inclined to hear about politics, sports, and the weather; they watch movies, listen to the radio, and spend long hours surfing the internet but seem unable to find time to hear about Krsna. Although life is meant for spiritual advancement—and hearing about Krsna is recommended as the primary means of advancement— few are interested.

Grhamedhis absorb their minds in their households, envy their neighbors, and spend their nights in sex and sleep and their days in making money for their families. Why does Sukadeva criticize them so strongly? Sukadeva Gosvami continues: They do not know the Absolute Truth, nor are they interested in inquiring about it. Rather, the life and attachments of such persons are focused only on the ephemeral. They become absorbed in and feel sheltered by the support offered by fallible soldiers—their bodies, children, and wives. They invest their hopes in these soldiers. Although sufficiently experienced, they attempt only material improvement and refrain from acknowledging their inevitable destruction. It is as if such persons are blind to reality. Srila Prabhupada makes several strong statements in his purport to Bhagavatam [2.1.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.4):

**This material world is called the world of death. .. . Although he is sufficiently experienced in the matter by dint of past experience and previous examples of his deceased predecessors, he does not see that the so-called fighting soldiers like the children, relatives, society members and countrymen are all fallible in the great struggle. One should examine the fact that his father or his father’s father has already died, and that he himself is therefore also sure to die, and similarly, his children, who are the would-be fathers of their children, will also die in due course. No one will survive in this struggle with material nature. . . . The great ocean of material nature is tossing with the waves of time, and the so-called living conditions are something like foaming bubbles, which appear before us as bodily self, wife, children, society, countrymen, etc. Due to a lack of knowledge of self, we become victimized by the force of ignorance and thus spoil the valuable energy of human life in a vain search after permanent living conditions, which are impossible in this material world. Our friends, relatives and so-called wives and children are not only fallible, but also bewildered by the outward glamor of material existence. As such, they cannot save us. Still we think that we are safe within the orbit of family, society or country.**

Srila Prabhupada spoke on this topic many times, such as in this Boston lecture on December 22, 1969: “So does it mean to become a family man is bad? No. It does not mean. But be grhastha, not grhamedhi. Grhamedhi means they simply want to decorate their apartment and children and wife. That is the goal of their life. That is all. They have no other business. Apasyatam—blind to the value of life. Whereas the grhastha, he is not blind. He is simply looking how to become successful in Krsna conscious. So those who are blind of the point of selfrealization, such householders, they have got many subject matter of hearing in the newspapers. Srotavyadini rajendra nrnarh sand sahasrasah. Sahasrasah means thousands of subject matters. Such householders make their aim of life to decorate their apartments. That’s all. Work whole day and night, and have good dress, good apartment. They think this is success.”

Srila Prabhupada continues:

Now, what is their mode of life? How do they live? Sukadeva Gosvami will next explain that to Pariksit Maharaja. Nidraya hriy-ate naktam vyavayena ca va vayah: At night they are wasting their duration of life either by sleeping or by sex life. This is their business at night. Then, at daytime, what is their business? At daytime, diva cdrthehaya rajan kutumba'bharanena vat In daytime, they are always busy: “Where is money? Where is money? Where is money? Where is money?” Arthe means money. Dhaya, hankering after money. Then, after they get money? As soon as there is money, there is immediately a program how to spend it for their family. Kutumba'bharanena va. Kutumba means family, relatives. You see? They will spend thousands of dollars for family and relatives. But if you ask some dollars for Krsna consciousness they are not interested. So for these persons there are varieties of material news. . . . Their life is wasted both day and night. At night . . . either sleeping or going to the nightclub or dancing club— sex life, that’s all. Not that these things are new. These are old things. People were previously addicted to all these things too. Human nature is always like that. Yet, they are thinking, “These are modem days.” What do you mean by “modem days”? Nothing has changed. “Putting old wine in new bottle.” That’s all.

Srila Jiva Gosvami writes that texts 2-4 describe the common people who neglect hearing about Krsna. Indirectly, Sukadeva Gosvami is trying to push devotees away from these activities and mentalities. Text 5, on the other hand, tells devotees how they should act and where they should seek shelter. Srila Sridhara Svami comments that after describing what should not be done, Sukadeva Gosvami will now describe the proper object of hearing.

Sukadeva Gosvami instructs Maharaja Pariksit on how to become free from these troublesome and illusory activities: “O descendant of King Bharata, one who desires to be free from all miseries must hear about, glorify and also remember the Personality of Godhead, who is the Supersoul, the controller and the savior from all miseries.” (Bhag, [2.1.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.5))

Srila Sridhara Svami comments: By using the word sarvatma, the speaker says that the Lord is most dear to everyone. By the word isvara, “the supreme controller,” Sukadeva is saying that the Lord’s will cannot be thwarted. By using the word harih, “He who takes away,” Sukadeva is saying that the Lord removes the bondage of repeated material existence. The phrase abhayam icchata indicates those who desire liberation.

In his purport to this text, Prabhupada expands the advice Sukadeva Gosvami has offered the king: One “should first of all hear about the Lord. When one has perfectly and scrutinizingly heard, one must glorify His acts and deeds, and thus it will become possible to remember constantly the transcendental nature of the Lord. Hearing about and glorifying the Lord are identical with the transcendental nature of the Lord, and by so doing, one will be always in the association of the Lord. This brings freedom from all sorts of fear.”

It is important to keep in mind the special relevance of this instruction to Maharaja Pariksit, for the king will soon meet death. As Sukadeva Gosvami advises the king: Thus somehow or another, one should remember the Lord at life’s end. That is the highest perfection. “In other words,” Srila Prabhupada writes in his purport to text 6, “life should be molded in such a manner that one is able to progressively remember the Personality of Godhead in every step of life.”

While commenting on text 6, Srila Sridhara Svami defines etdvan as “the highest goal of life.” That highest goal is presented in the words narayana'Smrtih, “to remember the Personality of Godhead at life’s end.” Neither Sankhya nor yoga nor any spiritual path other than devotional service can bring one to this highest goal. “To remember the Supreme Personality of Godhead at the end of life is therefore the highest attainment. No one has the power to sufficiently glorify this attainment. That is this text’s meaning.”

The best way to remember Krsna at the end of life is to chant His names, as the Visnudutas state in Bhagavatam [6.2.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/2.13): “At the time of death, this Ajamila helplessly and very loudly chanted the holy name of the Lord, Narayana. That chanting alone has already freed him from the reactions of all sinful life. Therefore, О servants of Yamaraja, do not try to take him to your master for punishment in hellish conditions.” Hearing and chanting are not really separate endeavors. Thus hearing about Krsna is not a lesser activity condescendingly recommended for a materialistic king suffering from diminished spiritual capacity. Rather, associating with Krsna by remembering Him, especially during the final moments of life, is the highest goal. Describing Krsna’s glories is the practice not only of kings but of sages. Indeed, Sukadeva Gosvami continues, the sages who have purified their consciousness to the topmost degree “take pleasure in describing the glories of the Lord.” (Bhag. [2.1.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.7))

Sukadeva Gosvami offers himself as an example of a liberated sage who was attracted to hearing about Krsna from the Bhagavatam: At the end of the Dvapara-yuga, I myself studied this great Srimad-Bhagavatam from my father, Srila Dvaipayana Vyasadeva. I was already situated perfectly in transcendence, yet was still attracted by the Bhagavatam’s descriptions of the Lord’s pastimes. Because of your sincere devotion to Lord Krsna, I shall now recite to you the same Bhagavatam I myself heard. “One who gives full attention and respect to hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam achieves unflinching faith in the Supreme Lord, the giver of salvation.” (Bhag. [2.1.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.10))

In his purport, Srila Prabhupada describes the factors required to attain the described success: “Both the spiritual master and the disciple must be bona fide. In this case, the spiritual master, Sukadeva Gosvami, is ready to recite exactly what he has learned from his great father, Srila Vyasadeva, and the disciple, Maharaja Pariksit, is a great devotee of Lord Krsna. A devotee of Lord Krsna is he who believes sincerely that by becoming a devotee of the Lord one becomes folly equipped with everything spiritual. This teaching is imparted by the Lord Himself in the pages of the Bhagavad-gita, in which it is clearly described that the Lord (Sri Krsna) is everything, and that to surrender unto Him solely and wholly makes one the most perfectly pious man. This unflinching faith in Lord Krsna prepares one to become a student of Srimad-Bhagavatam, and one who hears Srimad-Bhagavatam from a devotee like Sukadeva Gosvami is sure to attain salvation at the end, as Maharaja Pariksit did.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments that text 10 describes the Bhaga' vatam’s glories. He adds that in the next text, Srila Sukadeva Gosvami will instruct the king about the Bhagavatam’s main subject: chanting the holy name.

Thus Sukadeva Gosvami both assures and encourages Maharaja Pariksit: “O King, constant chanting of the holy name of the Lord after the ways of the great authorities is the doubtless and fearless way of success for all, including those who are free from all material desires, those who are desirous of all material enjoyment, and also those who are self-satisfied by dint of transcendental knowledge.” (Bhag. [2.1.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.11))

In his commentary on text 11, Sridhara Svami states that nothing is more beneficial than chanting the Lord’s holy names. Jiva Gosvami adds a condition: “But one must avoid the offenses against the holy name if one is to attain the ultimate result.”

It may be fortunate to be able to chant at the time of death, but wouldn’t it have been more fortunate for the king to have reigned for many more years? Isn’t it a misfortune for the king to have to leave this world? In response, Sukadeva Gosvami defines fortune and misfortune in terms of elevation of consciousness. What is the value of living a long wasted life in which one learns nothing? “Better a moment of full consciousness, because that gives one a start in searching after his supreme interest.” (Bhag. [2.1.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.12)) The king’s fortune is not defined as the power to rule the world for any number of years. Rather, Sukadeva encourages a life lived fully—with full consciousness of one’s own supreme interest—even if that life lasted only a moment.

Are the king’s days sufficient to develop the required knowledge, detachment, and devotion to achieve the spiritual goal? After all, he has only seven remaining days. To inspire Maharaja Pariksit’s confidence, Sukadeva offers an example of a king who attained Krsna’s shelter in even less time: “The saintly King Khatvanga, after being informed that the duration of his life would be only a moment more, at once freed himself from all material activities and took shelter of the supreme safety, the Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [2.1.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.13)) Srila Sridhara Svami adds that Khatvanga Maharaja came to earth at the time of death because he did not wish to be enamored by heaven. Sukadeva Gosvami concludes that King Pariksit can easily prepare himself for his next life in the seven days he has left. “At the last stage of one’s life, one should be bold enough not to be afraid of death. But one must cut off all attachment to the material body and everything pertaining to it and all desires thereof.” (Bhag. [2.1.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.15))

Srila Prabhupada expresses Sukadeva’s thoughts still further in his purport to text 14: “Indirectly, the Gosvami told Maharaja Pariksit that be should take shelter of the sound representation of the Lord for the seven days still remaining in the duration of his life and thus get himself liberated. In other words, everyone can best prepare himself for the next life simply by hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam, as it was recited by Sukadeva Gosvami to Maharaja Pariksit.”

One’s desires at the time of death attract one’s next body. Clearly, the best use of the remaining days of anyone’s life is to prepare for the next life. Srila Prabhupada explains, “(O\]ne has only to change the aspiration during the course of this present body, and for this there is need of training in the current duration of human life. This training can be begun at any stage of life, or even a few seconds before death, but the usual procedure is for one to get the training from very early life. . . . One cannot, therefore, stop desiring, but the subject matter for desires can be changed. So one must develop the desires for returning back home, back to Godhead, and automatically the desires for material gain, material honor and material popularity will diminish in proportion to the development of devotional service. A living being is meant for service activities, and his desires are centered around such a service attitude. Beginning from the top executive head of the state down to the insignificant pauper in the street, all are rendering some sort of service to others. The perfection of such a service attitude is only attained simply by transferring the desire of service from matter to spirit, or from Satan to God.” (Bhag. [2.1.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.15), purport)

## Texts 16—21: Preparing for a Better Next Life— Leaving Home in Renunciation

How should we prepare for death? Sukadeva suggests we first learn to become detached from the temporary. Toward this end he instructs: “One should leave home and practice self-control. In a sacred place he should bathe regularly and sit down in a lonely place duly sanctified.” (Bhag. [2.1.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.16)) In his purport, Srila Prabhupada explains why renunciation is important: “To prepare oneself for the better next life, one must get out of one’s so-called home. . . . Modem civilization is based on family comforts, the highest standard of amenities, and therefore after retirement everyone expects to live a very comfortable life in a well-furnished home decorated with fine ladies and children, without any desire to get out of such a comfortable home. High government officers and ministers stick to their prize posts until death, and they neither dream nor desire to get out of homely comforts. Bound by such hallucinations, materialistic men prepare various plans for a still more comfortable life, but suddenly cruel death comes without mercy and takes away the great planmaker against his desire, forcing him to give up the present body for another body. Such a planmaker is thus forced to accept another body in one of the 8,400,000 species of life according to the fruits of the work he has performed.”

“Therefore,” Srila Prabhupada explains, “to live apart from family life means to become self-controlled in regard to all sense desires, especially sex desires. The method is that one should have a duly sanctified sitting place made of straw, deerskin and carpet, and thus sitting on it one should chant the holy name of the Lord without offense, as prescribed above. The whole process is to drag the mind from material engagements and fix it on the lotus feet of the Lord. This simple process alone will help one advance to the highest stage of spiritual success.”

And then? After sitting in the above manner, one should continuously remember the transcendental seed mantra от. Thus the materially absorbed mind should be brought under control. “This is the way,” Srila Prabhupada writes in his purport to text 17, “of changing the habit of the mind. The mind is not to be killed. Mind or desire cannot be stopped, but to develop a desire to function for spiritual realization, the quality of engagement by the mind has to be changed. The mind is the pivot of the active sense organs, and as such if the quality of thinking, feeling and willing is changed, naturally the quality of actions by the instrumental senses will also change.... The devotees directly fix their minds on the Person of the Absolute Truth. But one who is unable to accommodate such personal features of the Absolute is disciplined in impersonality to train the mind to make further progress.”

What steps should a practitioner take? “Gradually, as the mind becomes progressively spiritualized, withdraw it from sense activities, and by intelligence the senses will be controlled. The mind too absorbed in material activities can be engaged in the service of the Personality of Godhead and become fixed in full transcendental consciousness.” (Bhag. [2.1.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.18))

Srila Prabhupada reiterates the goal: “. . . Sukadeva Gosvami recommends the next step of assured policy, namely to fix one’s mind in the service of the Personality of Godhead. Lord Sri Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, also recommends this direct process in the Bhagavad-gita ([6.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/6.47)). Thus, the mind being spiritually cleansed, one should at once engage himself in the transcendental loving service of the Lord by the different devotional activities of hearing, chanting, etc. If performed under proper guidance, that is the surest path of progress, even for the disturbed mind.”

Srila Sridhara Svami explains that Sukadeva Gosvami is describing pratyahara, sense restraint and internal meditation, according to the astanga-yoga system.

Sukadeva continues: “Thereafter, you should meditate upon the limbs of Visnu, one after another, without being deviated from the conception of the complete body. Thus the mind becomes free from all sense objects. There should be no other thing to be thought upon. Because the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Visnu, is the Ultimate Truth, the mind becomes completely reconciled in Him only.” (Bhag. [2.1.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.19)) On the path to full God realization, one can check the mind from materialism by first training it to see everything as Visnu according to a pantheistic view. Gradually, one moves from that vision to understanding everything in its spiritual relationship with Visnu. Srila Prabhupada refers to this progression as the progression from immature to mature pantheism. In his purport to text 20, he explains the value of both degrees of pantheism: “To acquire such a qualification of God realization in the personal feature, the neophyte impersonalist is given a chance to realize the relation of the Lord in everything by the philosophy of pantheism. Pantheism in its higher status does not permit the student to form an impersonal conception of the Absolute Truth, but it extends the conception of the Absolute Truth into the field of the so-called material energy. Everything created by the material energy can be dovetailed with the Absolute by an attitude of service, which is the essential part of living energy. The pure devotee of the Lord knows the art of converting everything into its spiritual existence by this service attitude, and only in that devotional way can the theory of pantheism be perfected.”

And in the purport to Bhagavatam [2.1.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.21): “Pantheism, or the system of feeling the presence of the Almighty everywhere, is a sort of training of the mind to become accustomed to the devotional conception, and it is this devotional attitude of the mystic that makes possible the successful termination of such mystic attempts.”

What is the goal of these graduated modes of thought? Sukadeva Gosvami further advises Pariksit Maharaja: “O King, by this system of remembrance and by being fixed in the habit of seeing the all-good personal conception of the Lord, one can very soon attain devotional service to the Lord, under His direct shelter.” (Bhag. [2.1.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.21))

Referring to text 19, Srila Sridhara Svami explains that confining the mind to one place is called dhyana. This is the goal. In his comment on text 20 he adds that passion and ignorance destroy meditation. Thus one should purify the mind from the debilitating effects of passion and ignorance by fixing it on Visnu.

In his purport to text 19, Srila Prabhupada recommends that instead of meditating on the Lord’s virat-тйра or on omkara, one should meditate on the Lord’s deity form in the temple. Such meditation is more effective. After all, Srila Prabhupada explains, the above text indicates “that the Visnu form is the ultimate goal of meditation, and as such it is better to concentrate upon the forms of Visnu than on impersonal отката. The latter process is also more difficult than the former.”

## Texts 22-39: The Lord’s Universal Form: Applying the Mind for Purification

Fortunate King Pariksit inquired further: Please instruct me in the details of the process that removes the dirty things from the mind. These dirty things, Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 22, are “the root cause of all troubles” for the living entity. These dirty things are the “concocted desires” for pleasure that the jiva has “accumulated during the long prison life in the material world.” But instead of these desires providing peace of mind, Srila Prabhupada states, they “create new problems and thus bind him to the cycle of repeated birth and death.” How can these desires be removed from the heart and mind? Only by associating with the Supreme Lord. Those who can perceive only matter and are “unable to pin their faith on the personal feature of the Absolute are given a chance to associate with His virat-rupa, or the cosmic impersonal feature of the Lord. The cosmic impersonal feature of the Lord is a feature of His unlimited potencies. Since the potent and potencies are identical, even the conception of His impersonal cosmic feature helps the conditioned soul to associate with the Lord indirectly and thus gradually rise to the stage of personal contact.”

In the following texts (23-39), Sukadeva Gosvami will describe a purifying process based on pantheism through which such persons can see the Lord while viewing the material world. (Srila Jiva Gosvami tells us that Maharaja Pariksit is asking this question for others’ benefit, because he himself already has a personal relationship with the Lord.)

Sukadeva Gosvami then describes where one should focus the mind: Through yogic practices one first should control his mind and senses. Then, with his intelligence, one should apply his “mind to the gross potencies of the Lord \[called the virat-rupa\]. This gigantic manifestation of the phenomenal material world as a whole is the personal body of the Absolute Truth, wherein the universal resultant past, present and future of material time is experienced.’’ (Bhag. [2.1.23-24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.23)) Sukadeva’s idea is to present a practical first step to spiritual advancement. An essentially materialistic person is recommended to adjust the conceptual lens though which he views matter, for he cannot yet perceive spirit. Thus “by a different conception” he may “realize the potency of the Lord. As soon as the potencies are understood to be instrumental manifestations of the transcendence, one automatically advances to the next step, and gradually the stage of full realization becomes possible for him.” (Bhag. [2.1.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.23), purport)

In his next purport, Srila Prabhupada explains the wisdom of perceiving everything in the universe as part of Krsna’s universal form (virat-rupa). Materialists “do not accept any evidential proof from the revealed scriptures, nor do they recognize the authority of the great acaryas. They want to see with their own eyes at once. Therefore they can see the gigantic body of the Lord as virat, which will answer their challenge, and since they are accustomed to paying homage to superior material strength like that of the tiger, elephant and lightning, they can offer respect to the virat-rupa. . . . This is a favor of the all-merciful Lord to the atheists and the gross materialists.” (Bhag. [2.1.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.24), purport)

Sukadeva continues to describe the Lord’s virat-rupa: “The gigantic universal form of the Personality of Godhead, within the body of the universal shell, which is covered by sevenfold material elements, is the subject for the virat conception. Persons who have realized it have studied that the planets known as Patala constitute the bottoms of the feet of the universal Lord, and the heels and the toes are the Rasatala planets. The ankles are the Mahatala planets, and His shanks constitute the Talatala planets. The knees of the universal form are the planetary system of the name Sutala, and the two thighs are the Vitala and Atala planetary systems. The hips are Mahitala, and outer space is the depression of His navel.” (Bhag. [2.1.25-27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.25))

Sukadeva continues: The Lord’s chest is the sun and moon, and above that, in the heavenly realm, are His neck, mouth, and forehead, which are the Mahar, Janas, and Tapas planets. The topmost planetary system, Satyaloka, is His head. His arms are the demigods headed by Indra, the ten directions are His ears, physical sound is His sense of hearing, and the two Asvini-kumaras are His two nostrils. Material fragrance is His sense of smell, and His mouth is the blazing fire. Outer space constitutes His eye pits, and the eyeball is the sun as the power of seeing. Day and night are His eyelids, and in the movements of His eyebrows, Brahma and similar personalities reside. The director of water, Varuna, is His palate, and the juice or essence of everything is His tongue. Yama, god of death, who punishes sinners, is His jaws and teeth. The art of affection is also His teeth, and the most alluring illusory material energy is His smile.

The great ocean of material creation is but the casting of His glance. Modesty is the upper portion of His lips, hankering is His chin, religion is His breast, and irreligion His back. The ocean is His waist, and the hills and mountains His bones. The rivers are the veins of His gigantic body, the trees His hairs, and the omnipotent air His breath. The passing ages are His movements, and the water-carrying clouds are the hairs on His head. The terminations of days and nights are His dress, and the supreme cause of material creation is His intelligence. The moon, the reservoir of all changes, is His mind. Rudradeva is His ego. The horse, mule, camel, and elephant are His nails, and wild animals and all quadrupeds are situated in the area of His belt. Birds are His masterful artistic sense. The celestial species represent His musical rhythm, and the demoniac soldiers His wonderful prowess. The brahmanas are the virdt'purusa’s face, the ksatriyas His arms, the vaisyas His thighs, and the stidras are under the protection of His feet.Srila Prabhupada’s purports to Bhagavatam [2.1.25-37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.25) offer a number of points for our consideration:

**In the Eleventh Chapter of the Bhagavad-gita, the Personality of Godhead, Lord Krsna, manifested His viraprupa just to convince the less intelligent class of men, who cannot conceive of the Lord as appearing just like a human being, that He factually has the potency of His claim to be the Supreme Absolute Person without any rival or superior. . . . The virat-тйра was particularly exhibited by the Lord just to give lessons to such foolish men, so that one can accept a person as the incarnation of Godhead only if such a person is able to exhibit such a virat-riipa as Lord Krsna did. The materialistic person may concentrate his mind upon the virat or gigantic form of the Lord in his own interest and as recommended by Sukadeva Gosvami, but he must be on his guard not to be misled by pretenders who claim to be the identical person as Lord Krsna but are not able to act like Him or exhibit the virat-rupa comprehending the whole of the universe. (Bhag.** [**2.1.25**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.25)**, purport)**

**The conception of the universal form of the Lord gives a chance to the materialist to think of the Supreme Lord, but the materialist must know for certain that his visualization of the world in a spirit of lording over it is not God realization. The materialistic view of exploitation of the material resources is occasioned by the illusion of the external energy of the Lord, and as such, if anyone wants to realize the Supreme Truth by conceiving of the universal form of the Lord, he must cultivate the service attitude. Unless the service attitude is revived, the conception of virat realization will have very little effect on the seer. (Bhag.** [**2.1.26**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.26)**)**

**To common sense the description in this verse appears to be somewhat contradictory because sometimes the sun has been described as the eyeball and sometimes as the outer space sphere. But there is no room for common sense in the injunctions of the sastras. We must accept the description of the sastras and concentrate more on the form of the virat-rupa than on common sense. Common sense is always imperfect, whereas the description in the sastras is always perfect and complete. If there is any incongruity, it is due to our imperfection and not the sastras’. That is the method of approaching Vedic wisdom. (Bhag.** [**2.1.30**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.30)**, purport)**

**According to Vedic assertion, this material creation is the result of the Lord’s casting a glance over the material energy, which is described herein as the most alluring illusory energy. The conditioned souls who are allured by such materialism should know that the material temporary creation is simply an imitation of the real' ity and that those who are captivated by such alluring glances of the Lord are put under the direction of the controller of sinners called Yamaraja. The Lord smiles affectionately, displaying His teeth. The intelligent person who can grasp these truths about the Lord becomes a soul fully surrendered unto Him. (Bhag.** [**2.1.31**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.31)**, purport)**

**The aesthetic sense of the Lord is manifested in the artistic, colorful creation of varieties of birds like the peacock, parrot and cuckoo. The celestial species of human beings, like the Gandharvas and Vidyadharas, can sing wonderfully and can entice even the minds of the heavenly demigods. Their musical rhythm represents the musical sense of the Lord. How then can He be impersonal? His musical taste, artistic sense and standard intelligence, which is never fallible, are different signs of His supreme personality. (Bhag.** [**2.1.36**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.36)**, purport)**

**None of the living beings is away from the Lord’s gigantic body. Each and every one has a particular duty in relation to the supreme body. Disruption in the matter of discharging the specific duty assigned to each and every living being is the cause of disharmony between one living being and another, but when the relation is reestablished in relation with the Supreme Lord, there is complete unity between all living beings, even up to the limit of the wild animals and human society. Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu displayed this living unity in the jungle of Madhya Pradesa, where even the tigers, elephants and many other ferocious animals perfectly cooperated in glorifying the Supreme Lord. That is the way to peace and amity all over the world.” (Bhag.** [**2.1.36**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.36)**, purport)**

Sukadeva Gosvami concludes his description of the universal form (texts 38-39) by explaining that one should fix the mind on the Lord by seeing everything in the universe as connected to Him: “I have thus explained to you the gross material gigantic conception of the Personality of Godhead. One who seriously desires liberation concentrates his mind on this form of the Lord, because there is nothing more than this in the material world.” (Bhag. [2.1.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.38))

Srila Prabhupada summarizes Sukadeva Gosvami’s description in his purport: “None of the materialistic thoughtful men can go beyond this conception of the gigantic form. The minds of the materialistic men are flickering and constantly changing from one aspect to another. Therefore, one is advised to think of the Lord by thinking of any part of His gigantic body, and by one’s intelligence only one can think of Him in any manifestation of the material world—the forest, the hill, the ocean, the man, the animal, the demigod, the bird, the beast or anything else. Each and every item of the material manifestation entails a part of the body of the gigantic form, and thus the flickering mind can be fixed in the Lord only and nothing else. This process of concentrating on the different bodily parts of the Lord will gradually diminish the demoniac challenge of godlessness and bring about gradual development of devotional service to the Lord.”

In his comment on text 26, Srila Sridhara Svami states that the Supreme Lord should be worshiped while thinking no difference exists between His virat-rupa and Himself. Thus materialists can worship the Supreme Lord. On text 38 he writes that those desiring salvation can concentrate the mind on this great being by using the intellect.

Since one’s existence—and even one’s power to see—rests on the Lord, one is completely dependent on Him. Sukadeva Gosvami concludes: “One should concentrate his mind upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who alone distributes Himself in so many manifestations just as ordinary persons create thousands of manifestations in dreams. One must concentrate the mind on Him, the only all-blissful Absolute Truth. Otherwise one will be misled and will cause his own degradation.” (Bhag. [2.1.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.39)) Seeing that everything in existence depends on the Lord, one should avoid other allurements and focus the mind only on Him. Srila Sridhara Svami, commenting on text 39, writes that this verse means one should concentrate the mind on the Lord (tarn, eva satyam bhajeta), who alone distributes Himself in so many manifestations (sarva-dhi-vrtty-anubhuta-sarvah). One should not be attached to anyone or anything else (na anyatra sajjet), because that attachment (yatah) causes one to fall (atma'patah) into the material world of repeated birth and death.

Although Sukadeva has recommended that one focus the mind on a vision of the Lord based on pantheism, and although his instructions are only pointing to a first step in God realization, still his conclusion is based on sah, “He,” the first word in Bhagavatam [2.1.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.39), referring to the Supreme Person. “The conclusion,” Srila Prabhupada states in his purport to text 39, is “that one should unhesitatingly become a worshiper of Lord Krsna, or, for that matter, His plenary expansion

Narayana, and none else.... He is always in His transcendental posi-tion, but essentially He is everything, and nothing is apart from Him. As a part of Him, one should therefore concentrate on Him only, without deviation; otherwise one is sure to be overcome by the potencies of the material creation, one after another.”

In his commentary on this text, Srila Jiva Gosvami states that after describing the process of fixing the mind on the virat-rupa, the author again brings us to the point of devotion to the Lord. He also points out that the words nanyatra sajjed remind us not to become attached to anything other than the Lord. Although concentrating the mind on the Lord’s virat-rupa results in concentration on the Lord, the devotee should nonetheless not become mentally attached to concentrating on the virat-rupa. Rather, he should devote himself to Lord Narayana.

## Chapter 2 - The Lord of the Heart

## Texts 1-14: Meditating on the Lord in the Heart

Sukadeva Gosvami next cites a previous authority to verify the potency of meditating on the Lord’s universal form: Formerly, Lord Brahma attained the ability to re-create the universe by meditating on the Lord’s virat-rupa. Thus through his meditation on the Lord he became reinstated in his actual identity. Every soul is a servant of Krsna; that is the soul’s identity. Prabhupada states: “The conditioned soul, even in the position of a Brahma, forgets this by the influence of the illusory, material energy generated out of false egoism. One can counteract such false egoism by invoking God consciousness. Liberation means getting out of the slumber of forgetfulness and becoming situated in the real loving service of the Lord, as exemplified in the case of Brahma.” (Bhag. [2.2.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.1), purport)

Sukadeva then tells Maharaja Pariksit to become fully renounced in his final days and to meditate on the Lord: Don’t dream of meaningless happiness, such as enjoyment in heavenly kingdoms, for no tangible happiness exists in such places, even though the Vedas support the attainment of these delights.

Srila Sridhara Svami informs us that Sukadeva Gosvami speaks text 2 to encourage renunciation despite Vedic encouragement to attain the higher material planets. In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada explains why heavenly pleasure leaves the eternal soul dissatisfied: “The real happiness is in the kingdom of God, where no one has to undergo the pangs of material existence. Therefore, the Vedic ways of fruitive activities for the living entities are misleading. One thinks of a superior way of life in this country or that, or on this planet or another, but nowhere in the material world can he fulfill his real desire of life, namely eternal life, full intelligence and complete bliss. Indirectly, Srila Sukadeva Gosvami affirms that Maharaja Pariksit, in the last stage of life, should not desire to transfer himself to the so-called heavenly planets, but should prepare himself for going back home, back to Godhead. None of the material planets, nor the amenities available there for living conditions, is everlasting; therefore one must have a factual reluctance to enjoy such temporary happiness as they afford.”

Sukadeva further instructs the king: Do not waste your life-energy chasing material enjoyment. Endeavor only to obtain the minimum requirements to maintain your body while you are in this world. Working for more than this is useless labor.

Srila Prabhupada explains the “fixed-in-mind,” renounced mood of a transcendentalist: “The fruitive worker aspires after a big fortune in the matter of wealth, woman and worldly adoration, but those who are fixed in perfect reality are not at all interested in such false things. For them it is all a waste of time. Since every second of human life is important, an enlightened man should be very careful to utilize time very cautiously. One second of human life wasted in the vain research of planning for happiness in the material world can never be replaced, even if one spends millions of coins of gold. Therefore, the transcendentalist desiring freedom from the clutches of maya, or the illusory activities of life, is warned herewith not to be captivated by the external features of fruitive actors. Human life is never meant for sense gratification, but for self-realization. . . . Even if there is difficulty in plain living and high thinking he will not budge an inch from his stark determination.” (Bhag. [2.2.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.3), purport)

But can one acquire one’s needs—food, shelter, and clothing— without a sustained material effort? Sukadeva Gosvami describes the simplest way to maintain existence without jobs, credit cards, or commuting: rely on nature’s basic gifts. “When there are ample earthly flats to lie on, what is the necessity of cots and beds? When one can use his own arms, what is the necessity of a pillow? When one can use the palms of his hands, what is the necessity of varieties of utensils? When there is ample covering, or the skins of trees, what is the necessity of clothing? Are there no torn clothes lying on thecommon road? Do the trees, which exist for maintaining others, no longer give alms in charity? Do the rivers, being dried up, no longer supply water to the thirsty?” (Bhag. [2.2.4-5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.4))

In this day and age, only the rarest soul may possess both the capacity and facility to live such a carefree and simple existence. Rivers are now polluted, few trees bear fruit, and governments arrest the homeless as vagrants. Yet the principle of living simply to support higher thinking remains ideal. At least, as Srila Prabhupada points out in his purport to text 4, “The necessities of life for the protection and comfort of the body must not be unnecessarily increased.” Why? “The idea given by Srila Sukadeva Gosvami is that the reserve energy of human life, which is far superior to that of animals, should simply he utilized for self-realization. Advancement of human civilization must be towards the goal of establishing our lost relationship with God, which is not possible in any form of life other than the human.”

Sukadeva Gosvami continues: With the principle of dependence on Krsna at the center of their surrender, why then do learned sages spoil their spiritual lives by going “to flatter those who are intoxicated by hard-earned wealth?” (Bhag. [2.2.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.5)) Renunciants may beg to maintain their simple existence, but they should also contribute spiritual instruction to ensure that society maintains its perspective. Therefore, Srila Prabhupada suggests, “The first duty of a person in the renounced order of life is to contribute some literary work for the benefit of the human being in order to give him realized direction toward self-realization.” (Bhag. [2.2.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.5), purport)

One should not become a renunciant, a person with a legitimate right to beg, unless one is surrendered to Krsna’s guardianship. Srila Prabhupada adds: “When a man becomes a mendicant willfully or by circumstances, he must be of firm faith and conviction that the Supreme Lord is the maintainer of all living beings everywhere in the universe. Why, then, would He neglect the maintenance of a surrendered soul who is cent percent engaged in the service of the Lord? A common master looks to the necessities of his servant, so how much more would the all-powerful, all-opulent Supreme Lord look after the necessities of life for a fully surrendered soul.”

Taking shelter of the temporary has been disallowed. Then what should those fixed in renunciation do? Sukadeva Gosvami’s instructions now move toward the positive. He has already recommended thinking of the Lord’s virat-rupa. Now he will lead Maharaja Pariksit one step higher in renunciation. The king does not need to go anywhere. He tells the king that the Supersoul resides in his heart. Render service to Him. He is substance, not illusion; He is almighty and the ultimate goal of life. By worshiping Him, one can end his material existence.

One should worship the Supersoul and love Him as naturally as one loves oneself. That type of service pleases the soul. Srila Sridhara Svami comments on text 6: “What then should be done? Lord Hari should be served.” The word evarn (thus) here means “thus being renounced.” Thus being renounced, one should serve the Lord (tam bhajeta).

Srila Prabhupada sweetly directs the reader in his purport to text 6: “Actually we are hankering after Him as the child seeks the mother. And to search out the Supreme Personality of Godhead, we need not go anywhere else, because the Lord is within our hearts.” As each living entity is a spiritual being, the material realm, regardless of how extravagantly it is organized, cannot afford him shelter any more than land can shelter a fish. The soul’s true shelter is the Supersoul, and worshiping Him addresses the existential problem that caused his material existence. Narottama dasa Thakura therefore states: “The struggle to travel to various holy pilgrimage places is simply the mind’s mistake, because to make spiritual advancement all one needs is the lotus feet of Lord Govinda. Abandoning pride and envy, and with firm faith in your heart, always worship Lord Govinda without deviation.” (Prema-bhakti-сandrika, Song 2, Verse 5)

Does the Lord’s being both all-pervasive and within the heart of every living entity eliminate the need for temples? Srila Prabhupada continues: “This does not suggest, however, that we should not go to the places of worship, namely the temples, churches and mosques. Such holy places of worship are also occupied by the Lord because the Lord is omnipresent. For the common man these holy places are centers of learning about the science of God.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami’s comment on text 6 in his Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 2, cites Srila Sridhara Svami: “Then what should a person do \[who has understood that his endeavor should not be simply for material comforts\]? Rather, it is Lord Hari \[and not this body\] who is worthy of our service. This verse is spoken to emphasize this point.”

Sukadeva continues: Who but foolish and gross materialists would neglect thinking of transcendence to immerse themselves in impermanent matter? Just see how the mass of people are suffering due to the resultant reactions of their materialistic thoughts and deeds!

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 7 indicates that Sukadeva Gosvami has now carried his recommendation higher than contemplation of the impersonal virat-rupa; now he has suggested meditation on the Supersoul. Of course, both forms of contemplation are superior to materialism, which invariably ends in suffering. Yet despite the universality of material suffering, people tend to sheep-walk down the path of material enjoyment, the path followed by all sufferers. Such persons imagine that others are somehow attaining the pleasure that has eluded them, and they tend to overlook the universality of death as well as its usual prior conditions of old age and sickness. And of course, they don’t look at all the other assorted miseries it is possible to suffer, a few being poverty, hospitalization, lawsuits, family quarrels, suicide, debt, and office or factory employment. Srila Prabhupada explains: “Intelligent persons who can see properly may look into the general conditions of the living entities who are wandering in the cycle of the 8,400,000 species of life, as well as in different classes of human beings. . .. No one is happy in this material world, and all of them are either class A, В or C prisoners suffering because of their own deeds. The Lord is impartial to all circumstances of the sufferings of the living entities, but to one who takes shelter at His lotus feet, the Lord gives proper protection, and He takes such a living entity back home, back to Himself.”

How can one visualize the Supersoul, whose expansion is the virat' rupa, who is untouched by material existence, and who lives in the heart of every living entity? Sukadeva Gosvami explains that He can be thought of as “measuring only eight inches” and as residing in the heart in a four-armed form carrying a club, disc, conch, and lotus. “His mouth expresses His happiness. His eyes spread like the petals of a lotus, and His garments, yellowish like the saffron of a kadamha flower, are bedecked with valuable jewels. His ornaments are all made of gold and are set with jewels.... On His chest is the kaustubha jewel, engraved with a beautiful calf, and there are other jewels on His shoulders. His complete torso and body are garlanded with fresh flowers.... His leglets, His bangles, His oiled hair, curling with a bluish tint, and His beautiful smiling face are all very pleasing.” (Bhag. [2.2.9-11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.9)) To attain the benedictions the Lord naturally offers, one should neglect the impersonal to meditate on the Lord’s transcendental form. Meditation on the Lord is the essence of bhaktiyoga, and it automatically bestows on a devotee both detachment and knowledge.

But without pure consciousness one will not be able to focus the mind on the Supersoul, for mental impurities will inevitably draw one back to contemplation on matter. Therefore purifying the mind becomes the goal of years of difficult yoga practice. Srila Prabhupada describes that the practice of bhakti-yoga progresses to anartha-nivrtti, the removal of impurities in the heart. Of the heart’s impurities, Srila Prabhupada explains, “The grossest type of anartha which binds the conditioned soul in material existence is sex desire ... bhakti-yoga leads to gradual evaporation of the sex desire, which is summarized in three headings, namely profit, adoration and distinction. All conditioned souls are mad after these different forms of sex desire, and one shall see for himself how much he has been freed from such material hankerings based primarily on the sex desire. As a person feels his hunger satisfied after eating each morsel of foodstuff, he must similarly be able to see the degree to which he has been freed from sex desire.” (Bhag. [2.2.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.12), purport)

How should one begin meditation on the Supersoul? Srila Sukadeva Gosvami’s instructions are clear: begin at the Lord’s lotus feet and progress gradually to His smiling face. “The more the mind becomes fixed upon the different parts of the limbs, one after another, the more the intelligence becomes purified.” (Bhag. [2.2.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.13)) Srila Prabhupada again defines purification as becoming free of sex desire: “So purification means getting free gradually from sex desire, and this is attained by meditation on the person of the Lord as described herein, beginning from the feet. One should not try to go upwards artificially without seeing for himself how much he has been released from the sex desire. The smiling face of the Lord is the Tenth Canto of Srimad-Bhagavatam, and there are many upstarts who at once try to begin with the Tenth Canto and especially with the five chapters which delineate the rasa-lila of the Lord. This is certainly improper. ... Sri Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura clearly defines the import of purification as cessation from sex indulgence.” (Bhag. [2.2.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.12), purport)

Similarly, in his purport to text 13, he writes: “According to the Bhagavata school, the Lord’s rasa dancing is the smiling face of the Lord. Since it is recommended in this verse that one should gradually progress from the lotus feet up to the smiling face, we shall not jump at once to understand the Lord’s pastimes in the rasa dance. It is better to practice concentrating our attention by offering flowers and tulasi to the lotus feet of the Lord. In this way, we gradually become purified by the arcana process. We dress the Lord, bathe Him, etc., and all these transcendental activities help us purify our existence. When we reach the higher standard of purification, if we see the smiling face of the Lord or hear the rasa dance pastimes of the Lord, then we can relish His activities.”

Sukadeva continues his instructions on meditation: Unless one develops a sense of loving service to the Supreme Lord, one should remember or meditate on the Lord’s universal form at the end of his prescribed duties. In his purport to text 14, Srila Prabhupada again places meditation on the virat-rupa in perspective: “Some way or other, one must try to reestablish one’s forgotten relation with the Lord if one at all desires to gain real happiness in life, and to reclaim his natural unfettered condition. For the less intelligent beginners, meditation on the impersonal feature, the virat-rupa, or universal form of the Lord, will gradually qualify one to rise to personal contact. One is advised herewith to meditate upon the virat-rupa specified in the previous chapters in order to understand how the different planets, seas, mountains, rivers, birds, beasts, human beings, demigods and all that we can conceive are but different parts and limbs of the Lord’s virat form. This sort of thinking is also a type of meditation on the Absolute Truth, and as soon as such meditation begins, one develops one’s godly qualities, and the whole world appears to be a happy and peaceful residence for all the people of the world. Without such meditation on God, either personal or impersonal, all good qualities of the human being become covered with misconceptions regarding his constitutional position, and without such advanced knowledge, the whole world becomes a hell for the human being.”

## Texts 15-21: Leaving One’s Body through Yoga

Next Sukadeva Gosvami instructs how a yoga practitioner may leave his body to attain the supreme destination. The yogi’s specific concern should be neither the time nor the place of death but his concentration on the Supreme. The yogi should sit without disturbance and control his senses by his mind. Gradually, by withdrawing the mind from the external world, he should situate it through pure intelligence in the Supersoul and attain full self-satisfaction through being seen by the Lord. Srila Prabhupada explains this stage in his purport to text 16: “When the living entity is directly seen by the Lord, the Lord dictates to him to act according to His desire, and when the living entity follows Him perfectly, the living entity ceases to discharge any other duty for his illusory satisfaction. In his pure unalloyed state, the living being attains the stage of full bliss, labdhopasanti, and ceases all material hankerings.” One thus perfected merges his mind into his soul through his intelligence. Thus his intelligence, mind, and soul have one objective: full harmony with Krsna’s desires.

The purpose of yoga practice, then, is to control the body and pacify the mind and senses. Facilitating materialistic activities is not the purpose of yoga practice. A controlled mind can be aligned through the intelligence with service to Krsna’s desire. That transcendental consciousness awards one the satisfaction for which one hankers. Therefore, Sukadeva Gosvami describes the state of fully harmonious consciousness first in the negative—by describing what it is not: “In that transcendental state of labdhopasanti, there is no supremacy of devastating time, which controls even the celestial demigods who are empowered to rule over mundane creatures. (And what to speak of the demigods themselves?) Nor is there the mode of material goodness, nor passion, nor ignorance, nor even the false ego, nor the material Causal Ocean, nor the material nature.” (Bhag. [2.2.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.17))

A perfected yogi is unwilling to deviate even for a moment from the taste he derives from worshiping Krsna, yet less mature spiritual practitioners face dangers. In Prema^bhakd-candrikd, Srila Narottama dasa Thakura describes the predicament of the imperfect soul: “The insubordinate senses are like enemies that live in the body. Tell the ear to hear and it may rebel, refusing to hear. Tell the mind to understand a particular point, or become firm in a certain way, and it may very well disobey.” (Song 2, verse 8) A karma-yogi faces the danger of becoming attached to the fruits of his work; a jnana-yogi faces the danger of thinking himself one in every way with the Lord. An astariga-yogi faces the danger of becoming enamored by his own mystic power. In Bhagavatam [11.15.33-34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/15.33) Krsna Himself concludes His discussion on yogic perfections by glorifying devotional service alone: “Learned experts in devotional service state that the mystic perfections of yoga that I have mentioned are actually impediments and are a waste of time for one who is practicing the supreme yoga, by which one achieves all perfection in life directly from Me. Whatever mystic perfections can be achieved by good birth, herbs, austerities and mantras can all be achieved by devotional service to Me; indeed, one cannot achieve the actual perfection of yoga by any other means.”

Srila Prabhupada describes that the state of freedom from false ego described in text 17 is transcendental, and that impersonalists, whose aim is to end individuality by merging with Brahman, may also possess it. In his purports to texts 18 and 19, however, he stresses that so-called impersonalist saints who maintain gross material desires are not tran-scendentalists. “All these nondevotees and debauchees are, according to Visvanatha Cakravarti, duratmas, or crooked souls in the dress of mahatmas, or great souls.” (Bhag. [2.2.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.18), purport)

Sukadeva Gosvami then states that the yogi should extinguish his material desires by the strength of his realization and begin to give up his material body. He should block the anus with the heel of his foot, and through his yogic practice, control his life-air by his intelligence. He should then progressively move his life-air from the lowest cakra (muladhara-cakra) through the cakra below the navel (svadhisthana-cakra) to the abdomen (mani-puraka-cakra), and upward from there through the heart cakra (anahata-cakra), palate (visuddhi-cakra), eyebrows (ajha-cakra), and finally cerebral pit (brahma-randhra).

After pushing the life-air up between his eyebrows, the yogi should block “the seven outlets of the life-air” and remain determined to go back to Godhead. “If he is completely free from all desires for material enjoyment, he should then reach the cerebral hole and give up his material connections, having gone to the Supreme.” (Bhag. [2.2.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.21))

Leaving the body by bursting through the cerebral hole “is the sure sign of a great devotee’s leaving the material connection,” Srila Prabhupada states in his purport to Bhagavatam [2.2.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.21). He also states that such complete “material detachment is possible to attain when one is acquainted with the supreme association of life,” and that “only one who has his aim fixed upon that spiritual world and personal association with the Godhead can give up his material connections even while living in the material world.”

## Texts 22-31: The Yogi Transfers Himself Beyond the Universe to the Spiritual World

Yogis who desire improved enjoyment or mystic power, however, and those who, like tourists, are inquisitive about life on other planets are immature. When such yogis quit their bodies, they take with them the “materially molded” mind and subtle senses, both of which are filled with material desires. Such souls cannot travel outside the realm of matter. Srila Prabhupada contrasts such yogis with devotees:

**As inquisitive persons tour all over the world to gain direct local experience, the less intelligent transcendentalist similarly desires to have some experience of those planets about which he has heard so many wonderful things. The yogi can, however, easily fulfill his desire by going there with the present materialistic mind and senses. The prime inclination of the materialistic mind is to lord it over the material world, and all the siddhis mentioned above are features of domination over the world. The devotees of the Lord are not ambitious to dominate a false and temporary phenomenon. On the contrary, a devotee wants to be dominated by the supreme predominator, the Lord. A desire to serve the Lord, the supreme predominator, is spiritual or transcendental, and one has to attain this purification of the mind and the senses to get admission into the spiritual kingdom. With the materialistic mind one can reach the best planet in the universe, but no one can enter into the kingdom of God. (Bhag.** [**2.2.22**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.22)**, purport)**

Clearly, to escape the material world and return to the spiritual world by the intricate and indirect method of astanga'yoga is extremely difficult. Nevertheless, the process, if followed, will transfer a yogi, by the demigods’ power, upward.
