Those yogis who are pure transcendentalists, however, are not restricted in their movements and can surpass the material world and journey to the spiritual realm. Still, even these yogis walk a gradual path. First, the transcendentalist yogi goes to the Vaisvanara planet to be purified. This planet is filled with fire. By the time he arrives, of course, he has already relinquished his gross, physical body. His challenge on this planet is to purify his subtle body, his mind, his intelligence, and ultimately his false ego. After that, he must travel along and eventually over the Milky Way (Sisumara) to the exalted Maharloka and remain there until the end of Brahma’s long life. As Brahma’s life is ending, the yogi perceives the fire emanating from Ananta Sesa’s mouth and sees the planets being burned to ashes. He then leaves on an airship for Satyaloka (Brahmaloka), the highest and most subtle planet of the universe.

Although the Bhagavatam’s description may not fit with contemporary science’s perception of reality, in his purport to text 26 Srila Prabhupada argues in favor of accepting the Vedic presentation: “The Srimad-Bhagavatam gives us many clues about other planets far, far away from us which modem planes and spacecraft cannot reach, even by imaginary speeds. ... In the creation of the Lord there are many wonderful things we can see with our own eyes every day and night, but we are unable to reach them equipped by modem materialistic science. We should not, therefore, depend on the fragmentary authority of materialistic science for knowing things beyond the range of scientific purview. For a common man, both modem science and Vedic wisdom are simply to be accepted because none of the statements either of modem science or of Vedic literature can be verified by him. The alternative for a common man is to believe either of them or both of them. The Vedic way of understanding, however, is more authentic because it has been accepted by the acaryas, who are not only faithful and learned men, but are also liberated souls without any of the flaws of conditioned souls. The modem scientists, however, are conditioned souls liable to so many errors and mistakes; therefore the safe side is to accept the authentic version of Vedic literatures, like Srimad-Bhagavatam, which is accepted unanimously by the great acaryas.”

After showing the consistency between Vedic statements, the conclusions presented in the Bhagavatam, and the words of the acaryas, the learned authorities on scripture, Srila Prabhupada again argues that one should accept the Bhagavatam’s authoritative statements: “So there is no difference between the versions of all the authorities. The truth is eternal, and as such there cannot be any new opinion about the truth. That is the way of knowing the knowledge contained in the Vedas. It is not a thing to be understood by one’s erudite scholarship or by the fashionable interpretations of mundane scholars. There is nothing to be added and nothing to be subtracted, because the truth is the truth. One has to accept, after all, some authority. The modem scientists are also authorities for the common man for some scientific truths. The common man follows the version of the scientist. This means that the common man follows the authority. The Vedic knowledge is also received in that way. The common man cannot argue about what is beyond the sky or beyond the universe; he must accept the versions of the Vedas as they are understood by the authorized disciplic succession.” (Bhag. [2.2.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.32), purport)

Again, the purpose of yoga is to purify the mind. As long as the mind remains illusioned, falsely placing itself at the center of existence, the soul must remain in the material world. Instead, one should supplant illusion with reality. What is reality? The mood of devotional service to Krsna, the soul’s natural consciousness. Yoga practices are meant to purify the materialistic mind of its tendency to grasp at its own pleasure.

Materialists carry the heavy baggage of material desires. That baggage is often unpleasant and contains unlimited desires along with the positive and negative voices of parents, teachers, and friends: “You are the greatest! Achieve! Succeed!” Or, “You’ll never be able to accomplish anything! You’re the worst!” The mind reacts to and is controlled by this conditioned pushing toward and against aspects of matter. Indeed, in Bhagavad-gita ([7.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.27)) Krsna blames attraction and aversion for binding us to the material world: “O scion of Bharata, О conqueror of the foe, all living entities are bom into delusion, bewildered by dualities arisen from desire and hate.”

The solution Sukadeva Gosvami and all transcendentalists recommend is to rid oneself of material desire. When a transcendentalist yogi decides to leave this world, he knows he has to purify his mind, and in this chapter of the Bhagavatam, Sukadeva has described how to do so according to the processes of yoga. Wishing to leave the material world behind while remaining attached to gross material happiness is a contradiction. Still, material enjoyment has subtle gradations, and those wishing to enjoy matter to its fullest will seek more esoteric experiences. The degree of subtlety one achieves in his understanding of material enjoyment will dictate the level of pleasure he can obtain from an activity. Both a pig and a gourmet enjoy eating, but is their enjoyment on the same level? Does the dog that howls happily at the moon experience the same pleasure as a human relishing classical music?

If one wishes to enter the spiritual realm, however, he must understand that it is not the senses that give one pleasure but the soul, symptomized by consciousness, that experiences life. The quality of one’s sense perception is determined by the nature of the coverings over consciousness. The grosser the coverings the less sensual refinement one has; the subtler the coverings, the more refined one’s sensual experience. The more refined one’s senses, the higher one’s capacity to feel pleasure.

Ultimately, the soul—free from all coverings and experiencing its true, unadulterated consciousness as Krsna’s servant—is the true connoisseur of pleasure. The pleasure in the spiritual realm consists of realization of this full, unadulterated consciousness.

As one’s consciousness becomes finer, one begins to experience peace, then happiness. The yogic process of transference to the higher planets in the universe means being transferred through ever more subtle levels of existence. Each higher planet on the yogis’ journey requires further degrees of purification and thus awards deeper peace and more subtle forms of happiness. When the yogi approaches the Sisumara, in which the polestar is located, he is nearing the limits of the universe.

Practically speaking, one who measures happiness in terms of palatial properties, speedy cars, and sexual pleasure is unable to imagine, what to speak of experience, the happiness available on the higher material planets. The topmost of these material planets is Satyaloka, which affords its inhabitants inestimable life durations. There, existence is so refined that there are no traces of pain. In those topmost material planets, the transcendentalist yogis live in subtle forms, with their subtle material bodies functioning similarly to the physical bodies we have on this planet. The only anxiety they feel is compassion, because they can perceive the miseries, struggles, and disappointments of those restricted by the lower realms.

Although it is tempting to become enamored by higher material planets, one should know that such planets are still far from the spiritual world. The most refined yogis desire to depart from the realm of matter altogether, penetrating the various universal coverings. If they are successful, they leave these elements behind one after another until they reach the ethereal covering.

Sukadeva Gosvami continues his description of the yogi who possesses only transcendental desires: When he attains Satyaloka, the yogi’s existence is rarefied. He becomes further exalted and purified and then surpasses the subtle universal coverings one by one until he attains the realm of false ego. At that stage, he neutralizes the lower modes of material nature and reaches egoism in goodness. Finally leaving that behind, he comes to the spiritual platform of pure selfrealization. “Only the purified soul can attain the perfection of associating with the Personality of Godhead in complete bliss and satisfaction in his constitutional state. Whoever is able to renovate such devotional perfection is never again attracted by this material world, and he never returns.” (Bhag. 2.2.31)

Practically speaking, it is impossible to successfully accomplish these gradual steps of purification in the modem age through yogic processes. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu therefore recommends chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra as an alternative, simple, and effective method. “Ultimately,” Srila Prabhupada states in his purport to text 30, “there is no difference in the result.... Lord Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu recommends that the devotee sow the seed of bhakti-yoga in his heart and nurture it by the watering of hearing and chanting the holy name, fame, etc., of the Lord. The simple process of offenselessly chanting and hearing the holy name of the Lord will gradually promote one very soon to the stage of emancipation.”

Merging with the Lord’s Brahman effulgence is not the supreme goal of yoga. The level of existence experienced in such a state, although free from even subtle material traces and thus offering incredible pleasure, is nevertheless far from the ultimate destination. It takes more than purification to reach the spiritual realm of the Vaikuntha planets. It requires devotion, bhakti. Srila Prabhupada clarifies the goal of yoga: “We should specially note in this verse the description of gatim bhaga-vatim. To become merged in the rays of the Parabrahman, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, as desired by the brahmavadi impersonalist, is not bhagavatim perfection. The bhagavatas never accept merging in the impersonal rays of the Lord, but always aspire after personal association with the Supreme Lord in one of the Vaikuntha spiritual planets in the spiritual sky.” (Bhag. [2.2.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.31), purport)

The devotional creeper (bhakti-lata) Prabhupada mentions in his purport to text 30 (and which Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu describes in Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya [19.151-62](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.151)) must be both protected and nourished. One protects it by avoiding offenses and nourishes it by hearing and chanting about Krsna. By caring for one’s bhakti-lata, one can gradually attain liberation, and beyond that, residence in the fully spiritual Vaikuntha planets. Yet above all these attainments, Srila Prabhupada points out, “is Krsnaloka, or Goloka Vrndavana, wherein the growing creeper enters and takes repose at the lotus feet of Lord Sri Krsna, the original Personality of Godhead. When one reaches the lotus feet of Lord Krsna at Goloka Vrndavana, the watering process of hearing and reading, as also chanting of the holy name in the pure devotional stage, fructifies, and the fruits grown there in the form of love of God are tangibly tasted by the devotee, even though he is here in this material world. The ripe fruits of love of God are relished only by the devotees constantly engaged in the watering process as described above. . . . The highest perfection of life is to enjoy life constantly in the association of the Lord, and one who can relish this does not aspire after any temporary enjoyment of the material world via other media.” (Bhag. [2.2.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.30), purport)

## Texts 32-37: Sukadeva Gosvami’s Conclusion: All Methods Lead to Bhakti

After having described virat-rupa meditation and the yogic methods to attain the spiritual realm, Sukadeva Gosvami now offers Maharaja Pariksit his actual instruction: Everything I have described is according to the Vedas and is eternal truth. Lord Krsna Himself explained the same to Brahma when He was satisfied with Brahma’s worship. “For those who are wandering in the material universe, there is no more auspicious means of deliverance than what is aimed at in the direct devotional service of Lord Krsna.” (Bhag. [2.2.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.33))

In Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 28, Srila Jiva Gosvami explains the sequence leading to Sukadeva’s direct glorification of hearing and chanting (Bhag. [2.2.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.33)) as follows: After describing the method of knowledge that leads to immediate liberation (Bhag. [2.2.15-21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.15)), and yoga (Bhag. [2.2.22-23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.22))—which then leads to gradual liberation—and after explaining the superiority of the form of devotional service in which one offers the fruits of his work to the Lord (karma-misra-bhakti), Sukadeva Gosvami now declares that “For those who are wandering in the material universe, there is no means of deliverance more auspicious than the direct devotional service of Lord Krsna.” “Direct devotional service” specifically means hearing and chanting about Krsna’s glories. In other words, Sukadeva is glorifying the process of hearing and chanting about Krsna.

Srila Sridhara Svami comments as follows on the same text: For persons traversing the cycle of birth and death, there are many paths to salvation, such as penance and yoga, but the only true path is that which is mentioned in this verse.

By referring to a great authority, Lord Brahma, Sukadeva Gosvami now reaffirms his instruction to engage directly in devotional service: “The great personality Brahma, with great attention and concentration of the mind, studied the Vedas three times, and after scrutin-izingly examining them, he ascertained that attraction for the Supreme Personality of Godhead Sri Krsna is the highest perfection of religion.” (Bhag. [2.2.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.34))

Srila Prabhupada’s lengthy purport to the next text (“The Personality of Godhead Lord Sri Krsna is in every living being along with the individual soul. And this fact is perceived and hypothesized in our acts of seeing and taking help from the intelligence”) demonstrates how we can deduce—use “reason and perception” to find— the presence of the Supersoul in everyone’s heart. Here’s a brief summary:

1. One can perceive oneself as existing. From there, with a little intelligence, one can understand that one is different from the body. That is, that he is the seer and that his existence is separate from everything else, which is seen.
2. The seer does not see or move independently. Both sight and movement are dependent on the various forms of energy combined in nature. For example, one’s ability to see depends on both one’s senses (eyes) and the presence of light (an energy of nature). Similarly, one’s five perceptual senses, five working senses, and three subtle senses (mind, intelligence, and ego) provide only the mechanics that make both perception and movement possible. They do not in themselves provide the experiences one perceives.
3. Those experiences—the things one sees—are “nothing but the products of the inexhaustible permutations and combinations of the forms taken by natural energy.” One’s ability to see is therefore subject to the conditions imposed on him by nature.
4. That which is seen (matter) is unconscious. That which sees (spirit) is always conscious. Matter is ever-changing; spirit is immutable.
5. The seer experiences his material conditioning in the form of dissatisfaction with the limitations matter imposes.
6. Nothing material “has ever developed the power of seeing or moving in any part of the world. Therefore it is definite that matter and spirit are two different identities ...” One can thus conclude that the seer is spiritual and the seen is matter. Spirit and matter are distinct from one another.
7. Every living entity uses his intelligence. That he directs himself by the instructions of his intelligence, or that he may reject those instructions, implies that he is different from that intelligence. His dependence on and accepting direction from his intelligence also indicates that his intelligence is superior to him. “Intelligence gives one direction like some higher authority, and the living being cannot see or move or eat or do anything without the use of intelligence.”
8. One can also perceive that not only he but every entity possesses and is directed by at least some intelligence. As there are vast gradations of intelligence among living entities, and as no one living entity possesses the totality of intelligence, one can understand that the sum of intelligence is greater than the intelligence possessed by any one entity. As that sum of all intelligence apportions gradations of intelligence, which direct the unlimited and all-pervading entities as “a higher authority,” the presence of a most intelligent, highest authority can be assumed. That entity, who apportions intelligence and is residing within and instructing every individual living being, is known as the Superself or Supersoul.
9. One then naturally wishes to know what causes the Supersoul to apportion different amounts of intelligence to the various living entities. All conditioned living entities identify with the body they possess. One’s actions, and desires are based on this identification. According to the body and desires one possesses, “the superior principle of Superself is guiding and supplying us according to our desire.” Thus the Supersoul, the source of intelligence, awards either contracted or expanded intelligence depending on the body. The body is awarded according to previous desires and dictates how one will enjoy matter. The grosser the desires, the more contracted the intelligence the Supersoul awards.
10. All living entities face a choice: Should one orient himself toward ignorance, the bodily concept of existence, or toward knowledge, the spiritual concept of existence?
11. If one chooses the spiritual conception, he can move toward that understanding by surrendering to the Supersoul. Then, rather than one’s desires being dictated and limited by the body he inhabits, his desires will be centered on the Lord’s desire. The Lord will then award him the appropriate, corresponding intelligence.
12. “So far as common sense is concerned, we come to the conclusion that there are three identities, namely matter, spirit and Superspirit. Now if we go to the Bhagavad-gita, or the Vedic intelligence, we can further understand that all three identities, namely matter, individual spirit, and the Superspirit, are all dependent on the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” One may wonder why the Supersoul is dependent on the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is because the Supersoul is only a partial representation (urnsa) of the Lord. We learn this from sastra. But the perception that the supreme entity must possess more characteristics than that of supplying intelligence to the soul is also common sense.
13. “Realization of the Superself by the individual self is the beginning of self-realization, and by the progress of such self-realiztion one is able to realize the Supreme Personality of Godhead by intelligence, by the help of authorized scriptures, and, principally, by the grace of the Lord.” The Lord can award one a vast amount of intelligence and spiritual realization or none at all. If one wishes to attain the greatest amount of both, he should hope to inspire the Lord to become inclined to award him the greatest amount of grace. Bhakti, surrender to the Lord in loving devotion, is the method the Lord Himself recommends to those wishing to accomplish this end.

Srila Jiva Gosvami states that text 35 describes how logic is used to understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In Paramatmd' sandarbha, anuccheda 109, he comments: Here the words drastd'laksitah mean that the individual spirit soul is the first seer. One may then ask, “What enables him to see?” The answer is given in the words drsyair buddhy'ddibhih: he sees with the help of his intelligence. Without the presence of the seer, the act of seeing the visible material world will not occur. Therefore it is due to the seer, who sees with the help of his intelligence and similar tools, that seeing occurs.

Then the Lord is described as the Supersoul in the hearts of all seers, Jiva Gosvami says. That is the meaning of the words bhagavdn sarva'bhutesu laksitah svatmana harih. One can understand that the Supersoul is present because the living entities are clearly not independent in their actions or encounters with pleasure and pain, and because they cannot act without external help. Thus one can understand both by logic and intelligence that the Supersoul must exist. Here the word “atmand" means “by the eyes.” By giving him eyes, the Supersoul enables the individual soul to see, by giving him ears, He enables him to hear, by giving him a mind, He enables him to think, and by giving him intelligence, He enables him to understand. This is confirmed by the Vallabha'Sruti: srtir asrtih, “\[By the Supersoul’s will\] all things are set into motion and are also made motionless.”

Also, Srila Jiva Gosvami continues, by seeing that the Supersoul has entered all living beings, one can understand that these “Supersouls” are all expansions or parts of a great person. In this way, one can infer that the Supreme Personality of Godhead exists. That the Supersoul is a partial expansion of the Supreme Lord is confirmed by the Lord Himself in these words (Bg. [10.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.42)): “But what need is there, Arjuna, for all this detailed knowledge? With a single fragment of Myself I pervade and support this entire universe.”

Desiring that Maharaja Pariksit now take full shelter of Krsna, Sukadeva Gosvami concludes: “O King, it is therefore essential that every human being hear about, glorify and remember the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead, always and everywhere. Those who drink through aural reception, fully filled with the nectarean message of Lord Krsna, the beloved of the devotees, purify the polluted aim of life known as material enjoyment and thus go back to Godhead, to the lotus feet of Him \[the Personality of Godhead\].” (Bhag. [2.2.36-37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.36)) Maharaja Pariksit has no time to follow a lengthy, intricate yoga practice. He even lacks the time to read all the Vedic scriptures. Sukadeva Gosvami has therefore reiterated what he said in Bhagavatam [2.1.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.5): Always and everywhere hear about and glorify Krsna. You will become purified even without having practiced renunciation or yoga—and you will go to Krsna. Again, these words address Maharaja Pariksit’s inquiry in Bhagavatam [1.19.37-38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/19.37): How can one who is about to die attain perfection?

Hearing krsna-katha, words spoken about or by Krsna, removes a conditioned soul’s deepest fears. At the end of the Uddhava-gita, Sri Uddhava says: “I offer my obeisances to that Supreme Personality of Godhead, the original and greatest of all beings, Lord Sri Krsna. He is the author of the Vedas, and just to destroy His devotees’ fear of material existence, like a bee He has collected this nectarean essence of all knowledge and self-realization. Thus He has awarded to His many devotees this nectar from the ocean of bliss, and by His mercy they have drunk it.” (Bhag. [11.29.49](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/29.49))

Srila Prabhupada’s purports to these final verses of the Second Canto’s second chapter again emphasize the importance of hearing about Krsna even while practicing the other potent processes of bhakti-yoga: “But out of all the nine different methods, the first one, namely hearing, is the most important function in the process of bhakti-yoga. Without hearing sufficiently and properly, no one can make any progress by any of the methods of practice. ... If human society gives itself to the process of hearing the Vedic literature, it will not become a victim to the impious sounds vibrated by impious men who degrade the standards of the total society. Hearing is solidified by the process of chanting. One who has perfectly heard from the perfect source becomes convinced about the all-pervading Personality of Godhead and thus becomes enthusiastic in glorifying the Lord. . . . The Lord is the master of all time and all space, and therefore the Lord’s holy name must be heard, glorified and remembered everywhere in the world. That will bring about the desired peace and prosperity so eagerly awaited by the people of the world.” (Bhag. [2.2.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.36), purport)

And from the purport to text 37, the last in the chapter: “Life is never made comfortable by artificial needs, but by plain living and high thinking. The highest perfectional thinking for human society is suggested here by Sukadeva Gosvami, namely, sufficiently hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam. For men in this age of Kali, when they have lost the perfect vision of life, this Srimad-Bhagavatam is the torchlight by which to see the real path. Srila Jiva Gosvami Prabhupada has commented on the kathamrtam mentioned in this verse and has indicated Srimad-Bhagavatam to be the nectarean message of the Personality of Godhead. By sufficient hearing of Srimad-Bhagavatam, the polluted aim of life, namely lording it over matter, will subside, and the people in general in all parts of the world will be able to live a peaceful life of knowledge and bliss. . . . And by the constant hearing of the messages of the Bhagavad-gita, and later of Srimad-Bhagavatam, one is assured herein by Srila Sukadeva Gosvami that he will reach the Personality of Godhead and render Him transcendental loving service in the spiritual planet of the name Goloka Vrndavana, which resembles a huge lotus flower.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments in Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 30: How does attraction for the Supreme Personality of Godhead develop? This is explained in the following question and answer (Bhag. [1.19.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/19.38)): “Please let me know what a man should hear, chant, remember and worship, and also what he should not do. Please explain all this to me.” This question is answered in the words of Bhagavatam [2.2.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.36) (“O King, it is therefore essential that every human being hear about, glorify and remember the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead, always and everywhere”). In that verse, the word ca, “and,” hints at the other nine principle angas of devotional service, beginning with serving the Lord’s feet. The result obtained by engaging in devotional activities, beginning with hearing about the Lord, is described in the next verse, text 37.

In the same anuccheda, Srila Jiva comments on Bhagavatam [2.2.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.37): The word punanti, “purify,” indirectly indicates that the previously described path of meditating on the Lord’s universal form is unable to award the purification required to actually obtain the Lord’s lotus feet. Because devotional service itself brings great purification, one should engage only in devotional service.

Later (anuccheda 86), Sri Jiva explains that text 37 allows one to see that hearing narrations about the Supreme Lord’s transcendental pastimes is the final, highest recommendation of the scriptures: “Although I have spoken about many paths, this is what is actually recommended.”

He also explains that Bhagavatam [12.4.40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/4.40) confirms this point as Sukadeva Gosvami’s conclusive instruction to Maharaja Pariksit: “For a person who is suffering in the fire of countless miseries and who desires to cross the insurmountable ocean of material existence, there is no suitable boat except that of cultivating devotion to the transcendental taste for the narrations of the Supreme Personality of Godhead’s pastimes.”

Srila Sridhara Svami comments on this same text: The words na anyah plavah confirm that there is no other boat.

Then Sri Jiva explains that in response to the king’s question (Bhag. [1.19.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/19.38)), Sukadeva Gosvami teaches the king meditation on and glorification of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Sri Jiva adds that Sukadeva also specifically answers Maharaja Pariksit in Bhagavatam [12.3.49—51](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/3.49): “Therefore, О King, endeavor with all your might to fix the Supreme Lord Kesava within your heart. Maintain this concentration upon the Lord, and at the time of death you will certainly attain the supreme destination. My dear King, the Personality of Godhead is the ultimate controller. He is the Supreme Soul and the supreme shelter of all beings. When those who are about to die meditate on Him, He reveals to them their own eternal spiritual identity. My dear King, although Kali-yuga is an ocean of faults, there is still one good quality about this age: Simply by chanting the Hare Krsna ma/ia-mantra, one can become free from material bondage and be promoted to the transcendental kingdom.”

## Chapter 3 - Pure Devotional Service—The Change in Heart

## Texts 1-12: Worshiping Krsna: The Ultimate Path

Srila Sukadeva Gosvami has already answered Maharaja Pariksit’s questions (Bhag. [1.19.37-38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/19.37)) about “the way of perfection for all persons,” especially those about to die, and has instructed him about what “a man should hear, chant, remember and worship, and also what he should not do.” He has also now defined an intelligent person (Bhag. [2.2.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.35)) as one able to perceive the Supersoul. Such a person, as Srila Prabhupada concluded in his purport, surrenders to the Lord in the heart. Maharaja Pariksit now proves that he himself is intelligent and “thoughtful” (Srila Prabhupada’s word in his purport to Bhagavatam [2.3.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.1)) by deciding that he wishes to hear about Krsna at the point of his death: “A manisinam \[thoughtful\] person, like Maharaja Pariksit, must therefore take to the lotus feet of Lord Krsna and fully engage himself in devotional service, hearing, chanting, etc., of the holy name and pastimes of the Lord, which are all hari-kathamrta. This action is especially recommended when one is preparing for death.”

But, as Srila Prabhupada also states, “Not all human beings are intelligent, so the importance of human life is not always understood.” People in general tend to be more interested in satisfying the desires they have developed based on the bodily concept. They thus neglect eternal good for the temporary. How should such people act so that their desires can be fulfilled? Certainly those who live for the temporary as if they will always be young are not rare. In time, however, such persons find themselves aged, in pain, and cynical. To their astonishment, their capacity to work and enjoy life has vanished. Of course, had they been thoughtful, this inevitability would have been obvious from the beginning, and clinging to those things that could not be kept would have appeared foolish.

Yet despite hearing this, many of us find we still have material desires. Can one satisfy one’s desires without neglecting the unavoidable approach of his own death? In Vedic culture, as in the present, people tried to ignore the obvious—birth, disease, old age, and death—in the attempt to fulfill their material desires. In Vedic culture, however, people were taught to fulfill their desires by worshiping a superior, a demigod. In other words, they satisfied themselves only after submitting to a higher power. The dominant mood in the West is to barely acknowledge superiors. Few people supplicate themselves voluntarily. Rather, Western culture instructs them to trust their fate only to their own powers and abilities. This degrades people because attempts to fulfill one’s desires (which are bom of passion) independently lead to ignorance (Bg. [3.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/3.37)). The Vedic system, however, uplifts and purifies people, because even as they attempt to fulfill their desires, they are forced to face their own ultimate insignificance and dependence.

Gathering in all hearers possessing material desires, Sukadeva Gosvami now presents a list of desires and the appropriate demigod to worship to attain them. “One who desires to be absorbed in the impersonal brahmajyoti effulgence should worship the master of the Vedas \[Lord Brahma or Brhaspati, the learned priest\], one who desires powerful sex should worship the heavenly King, Indra, and one who desires good progeny should worship the great progenitors called the Prajapatis. One who desires good fortune should worship Durgadevi, the superintendent of the material world. One desiring to be very powerful should worship fire, and one who aspires only after money should worship the Vasus. . . . One who desires domination over a kingdom or an empire should worship the Manus. One who desires victory over an enemy should worship the demons, and one who desires sense gratification should worship the moon.” (Bhag. [2.3.2-7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.2), [9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.9))

Despite this, in his purport to texts 2-7 Srila Prabhupada criticizes those who have material desires. Aspirations for wife, wealth, beauty, and fame pale, even appear foolish, when one is confronted by death. Every material body is doomed to die. Those who are thoughtful should not, therefore, endeavor for something temporary. Sukadeva Gosvami is not suggesting that Maharaja Pariksit—or any intelligent person—worship the demigods, but he is pointing out that for those who have material desires, demigod worship is recommended by the Vedic system.

After explaining that the perfection of both jnanic and yogic practice is devotional service, Sukadeva Gosvami explains the practices of those who would rather satisfy their material desires.

After completing his list, however, Sukadeva Gosvami will instruct Maharaja Pariksit on a still higher level: “A person who has broader intelligence, whether he be full of all material desire, without any material desire, or desiring liberation, must by all means worship the supreme whole, the Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [2.3.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.10)) This is Sukadeva’s conclusion. The sage has earlier recommended renunciation and viewing everything as part of the universal form (jndna). He has also recommended meditation on the Supersoul (yoga), and now demigod worship (karma) for the satisfaction of material desires. But his final and definitive instruction is that everyone —regardless of their desires or level of advancement—should worship Krsna, because devotional service to Krsna, bhakti-yoga, is the ultimate goal of karma, jnana, and yoga. In addition, he wants people to understand that they must perform at least some bhakti-yoga if they wish to succeed on other paths. At the same time, bhakti-yoga is independent; it does not require the assistance of karma or jnana for its own success. Therefore, as Srila Prabhupada points out in his purport to this text, bhakti-yoga “is especially stressed here as the means of all perfection.”Prabhupada then explains the nature of bhakti-yoga:

**. . . Jiva Gosvami has explained this desirelessness as bhajaniya-parama-purusa-sukha-matra-sva-sukhawam in his Sandarbha. This means that one should feel happy only by experiencing the happiness of the Supreme Lord. This intuition of the living being is sometimes manifested even during the conditioned stage of a living being in the material world, and such intuition is expressed in the manner of altruism, philanthropy, socialism, communism, etc., by the undeveloped minds of less intelligent persons. In the mundane field such an outlook of doing good to others in the form of society, community, family, country or humanity is a partial manifestation of the same original feeling in which a pure living entity feels happiness by the happiness of the Supreme Lord. Such superb feelings were exhibited by. the damsels of Vrajabhumi for the happiness of the Lord. The gopis loved the Lord without any return, and this is the perfect exhibition of the akamah spirit. Kama spirit, or the desire for one’s own satisfaction, is fully exhibited in the material world, whereas the spirit of akamah is fully exhibited in the spiritual world.**

**.. . Influenced by the kama spirit, Arjuna declined to fight in the Kuruksetra battlefield because he wanted to save his relatives for his own satisfaction. But being a pure devotee, he agreed to fight on the instruction of the Lord because he came to his senses and realized that satisfaction of the Lord at the cost of his own satisfaction was his prime duty. Thus he became akdma.**

**... Therefore a person with a broader outlook can see that the ultimate authority is the Lord, even for material benefits. Under the circumstances, one with a broader outlook, even with the desire for material enjoyment or for liberation, should take to the worship of the Lord directly. And everyone, whether an akdma or sakama or moksa-kama, should worship the Lord with great expedience. This implies that bhakti-yoga may be perfectly administered without any mixture of karma and jnana. As the unmixed sun ray is very forceful and is therefore called tivra, similarly unmixed bhakti-yoga of hearing, chanting, etc., may be performed by one and all regardless of inner motive.**

Commenting on text 10, Srila Sridhara Svami interprets purusa as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, not the Supersoul, because that Supreme Person is worshiped by advanced souls desiring liberation, souls becoming fit to enter the spiritual planets beyond the jurisdiction of the Supersoul.

In his commentary, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura gives a sweet explanation of the word akamah: “Of letters I am the letter A,” Krsna states in Bhagavad-gita [10.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.33). When that “A” is added to kamah, desire, the result is the desire to please Krsna. This is the only way to become free of material desire. If we lack the desire to please Krsna, we will be sarva-kamah, filled with material desire.

Sukadeva Gosvami will now begin his conclusion to this set of instructions by pointing those interested in satisfying their desires (kama) toward Krsna’s devotional service. First he addresses those with material desires by saying that those intent on worshiping demigods “can attain the highest perfectional benediction, which is spontaneous attraction unflinchingly fixed upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead, only by the association of the pure devotee of the Lord.” (Bhag. [2.3.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.11)) Srila Sridhara Svami states: Sukadeva Gosvami explains how the previously described worshipers of the many demigods can attain devotional service. The worshipers (yajatam) of Indra and the other demigods, in the course of their demigod worship (iha), can, by associating with (sangatah) devotees of the Lord (bhagavata), attain unflinching (acalah) devotion (bhavah) to the Lord (bhagavati). In this way they attain (udayah) the supreme goal of life (nihsreyasa). All other things are insignificant in comparison to that attainment.

Despite the plans one may have for happiness, Srila Prabhupada points out in his purport to text 11, the actual problems of life—birth, death, old age, and disease—remain unresolved. Bhakti both resolves these problems and allows one to become blissful as he serves Krsna. Paralleling Sridhara Svamt’s comments, Srila Prabhupada explains how one can attain bhakti: “Only by the grace of the divine personalities, the pure devotees of the Lord, can one achieve pure devotion, which is the highest perfection of human life. Only a pure devotee of the Lord can show one the right way of progressive life.”

Sukadeva Gosvami next directs his words to those desiring knowledge: “Transcendental knowledge in relation with the Supreme Lord Hari is knowledge resulting in the complete suspension of the waves and whirlpools of the material modes. Such knowledge is selfsatisfying due to its being free from material attachment, and being transcendental it is approved by authorities. Who could fail to be attracted?” (Bhag. [2.3.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.12))

Srila Prabhupada discusses the wonderful characteristics of pure devotees in his purport to text 12: “The complete functional activities of a pure devotee are always engaged in the service of the Lord, and thus the pure devotees exchange feelings of ecstasy between themselves and relish transcendental bliss. This transcendental bliss is experienced even in the stage of devotional practice (sadhana-avasthd), if properly undertaken under the guidance of a bona fide spiritual master. And in the mature stage the developed transcendental feeling culminates in realization of the particular relationship with the Lord by which a living entity is originally constituted (up to the relationship of conjugal love with the Lord, which is estimated to be the highest transcendental bliss).”

Pure devotees are connected with Krsna’s internal energy through their full serving mood. Thus they experience true happiness. The desires possessed by materialists, on the other hand, resemble a whirlpool. The selfishness of the materialist sucks him ever under, and satisfaction, real pleasure, and true relationships forever elude him. If one wants to renounce the whirlpool of desires to which one is clinging, one needs to experience the sweetness of Krsna consciousness.

## Texts 13-25: Saunaka Rsi’s Eagerness to Hear Krsna-katha

After hearing Suta Gosvami’s account of Sukadeva Gosvami’s instructions to Maharaja Pariksit, Saunaka Rsi inquired: “The son of Vyasadeva, Srila Sukadeva Gosvami, was a highly learned sage and was able to describe things in a poetic manner. What did Maharaja Pariksit again inquire from him after hearing all that he had said?’’ (Bhag. [2.3.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.13)) Saunaka Rsi then expressed his enthusiasm for krsna-katha, but added that “the discussion of the Lord Hari should certainly be discussed in the assembly of devotees.” (Bhag. [2.3.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.14))

Why is this important? Because hearing about Krsna from nondevotees will plant false and mundane concepts about Krsna in the heart. Only devotees know Krsna properly. Saunaka Rsi, however, knew that both the king and the sage were exalted devotees, and that the krsna-katha between them would therefore be potent. With full confidence in Suta Gosvami’s qualification to accurately convey the dialogue, Saunaka expressed his eagerness to hear further. He knew that by hearing from Suta, he and the sages of Naimisaranya would be able to experience Krsna, for Krsna Himself is present wherever devotees speak and hear about Him purely.

In a 1973 lecture in Bombay, Srila Prabhupada also noted the potency of discussing krsna-katha among devotees: “Krsna’s place, Goloka Vrndavana—that is spread everywhere. How does that Goloka Vrndavana become spread? As soon as there is devotee. Yes. Tatra tisthdmi narada yatra gayanti mad'bhaktdh. Krsna says, naharh tisthami vaikunthe na ca yoginam hrdayesu: ‘I do not stay in Vaikunthaloka or within the heart of the yogis.’ Tatra tisthami narada yatra gayanti mad' bhaktah: ‘I stay where My devotees are chanting about Me, about My glories.’ This is the process. Immediately.”

Appreciating the depth of Maharaja Pariksit’s devotion, the Rsi then commented on how the king, even as a child, worshiped deities of Krsna in his play. In Krsna-sandarbha, anuccheda 49, Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on text 15 by describing Maharaja Pariksit’s devotional childhood: In this verse, Saunaka Rsi’s explains that as a child Maharaja Pariksit would hear descriptions of Lord Krsna’s childhood pastimes in Vrndavana (balakrid) and would become absorbed in love (premdvesa). In that mood full of love for Lord Krsna, Prince Pariksit would act out the Lord’s pastimes as his childhood play.

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 15 makes similar points: “The life history of many such devotees is almost the same because there is always symmetry between the early lives of all great devotees of the Lord. According to Jiva Gosvami, Maharaja Pariksit must have heard about the childhood pastimes of Lord Krsna at Vrndavana, for he used to imitate the pastimes with his young playmates. According to Sridhara Svami, Maharaja Pariksit used to imitate the worship of the family Deity by elderly members. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti also confirms the viewpoint of Jiva Gosvami. So accepting either of them, Maharaja Pariksit was naturally inclined to Lord Krsna from his very childhood. He might have imitated either of the above-mentioned activities, and all of them establish his great devotion from his very childhood, a symptom of a maha-bhagavata.”

Additionally, in his purport to text 15, Srila Prabhupada writes about the significance of gathering impressions of Krsna during childhood. In this regard he discusses his own Vaisnava childhood, in which his natural and ecstatic inclination to serve Krsna became manifest: “Our father encouraged us in all respects to observe all functions such as the Ratha-yatra and Dola-yatra ceremonies, and he used to spend money liberally for distributing prasada to us children and our friends. Our spiritual master, who also took his birth in a Vaisnava family, got all inspirations from his great Vaisnava father, Thakura Bhaktivinoda. That is the way of all lucky Vaisnava families.”

Krsna had left the earth by the time Maharaja Pariksit reached adulthood, yet the king was nevertheless fortunate because he grew up hearing the pastimes that the Lord had so recently displayed. Similarly, since Srila Prabhupada has so recently left this world, talks about him are still prevalent, especially among those who had the fortune to have been with him personally. Therefore this is also a fortunate time, for soon there will be no one left who had the direct association of Srila Prabhupada, that personality empowered both by Sri Guru and Sri Gauranga to fulfill the prophecy that the holy name be spread throughout the world.

Not only was Maharaja Pariksit a great devotee from birth, but Sukadeva Gosvami, the speaker of the Bhagavatam, was a powerful devotee, full in transcendental knowledge. The depth of his ecstatic devotion will be shown when Pariksit Maharaja inquires from him about the events following Krsna’s killing of Aghasura: “Suta Gosvami said: О Saunaka, greatest of saints and devotees, when Maharaja Pariksit inquired from Sukadeva Gosvami in this way, Sukadeva Gosvami, immediately remembering subject matters about Krsna within the core of his heart, externally lost contact with the actions of his senses. Thereafter, with great difficulty, he revived his external sensory perception and began to speak to Maharaja Pariksit about krsna-katha.” (Bhag. [10.12.44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/12.44)) Thus Saunaka Rsi concludes that because both hearer and speaker were great devotees, on meeting, the topics they discussed must have been centered on Lord Krsna.

Srila Prabhupada discusses the potency of glorifying Krsna among pure devotees in his purport to text 16: “Only in the association of such devotees are the transcendental glories of Lord Krsna properly discussed. It is said by the Lord that His topics are all full of spiritual significance, and once one properly hears about Him in the association of the satam, certainly one senses the great potency and so automatically attains to the devotional stage of life.” As both were actual devotees, the purpose of their discussion, as Srila Prabhupada explains further in his purport, was “only for the glorification of the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna.”

That krsna-katha will be discussed in the association of devotees has increased Saunaka Rsi’s enthusiasm. His eagerness inspires him to criticize, in the remaining texts of this chapter, those who neglect krsna-katha, because hearing krsna-katha affords one the chance to attain the spiritual world. Saunaka Rsi’s heart cracks to see people acting frantically but misusing their human lives. He decries hearing other topics, because hearing krsna-katha carries one toward eternal life, whereas hearing other kathd simply calls death closer. His criticism is therefore an indirect glorification of krsna-katha: “Both by rising and by setting, the sun decreases the duration of life of everyone, except one who utilizes the time by discussing topics of the allgood Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [2.3.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.17)) The days and nights of one’s life run like sand through an hourglass. In the hearts of devotees who hear about Krsna blossoms the desire to forget maya and awaken their relationship with Krsna. By hearing, they become both attracted and attached to Krsna’s name, form, qualities, and pastimes.

In a lecture on this text, Srila Prabhupada once said, “If we pass our time simply by reading and talking about Krsna, then the sun will not be able to take away our life. This is the secret. If you want to become immortal, then you always be engaged in krsna-katha. Always, twenty-four hours, always think of Krsna. This is Krsna consciousness.” (June 12, 1972, Los Angeles)

Although each passing day does decrease a devotee’s lifespan, such decrease moves him closer to eternal life. The nondevotees, however, move closer only to death. Only hearing about Krsna can distinguish human beings from animals and life from death. Saunaka Rsi continues his criticism of the nondevotees: “Do the trees not live? Do the bellows of the blacksmith not breathe? All around us, do the beasts not eat and discharge semen?” (Bhag. [2.3.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.18)) Hearing about Krsna is the only purpose of human life. Those who do not do so are no better than animals.

Certainly someone may choose to argue this point. Many people have good qualities, and others praise them for their deeds. Should these leaders of society—especially those who have achieved acclaim in the world—be condemned as animals? Saunaka Rsi’s opinion is clear: “Men who are like dogs, hogs, camels and asses praise those men who never listen to the transcendental pastimes of Lord Sri Krsna, the deliverer from evils.” (Bhag. [2.3.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.19)) Srila Jiva Gosvami agrees in Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 35: If among these persons someone is great or powerful, he is still only a big animal. Srila Prabhupada shares their opinion: “Our business is a very thankless task. We say any man who is not a devotee, he is rascal. ... It is a very harsh word, but we have to use it. As soon as we see that he is not a devotee of Krsna, then he’s a rascal. How do we say? He is not my enemy, but we have to say because it is stated by Krsna. If we are really Krsna conscious, then our business is to repeat the words of Krsna. That’s all.”

And: “It is said that a person without God consciousness, Krsna consciousness, he is no better than these dogs and hogs. That’s all. This is our conclusion. We don’t give any formal respect. Of course, we have to give because we are in this world. But at heart we cannot give respect to a person who has not any sense of Krsna consciousness. We cannot give. Because who is going to give any respect to the dogs and hogs? Sva-vid-varahostra-kharaih, samstutah purusah pasuh. Therefore Jiva Gosvami has commented on this verse ... If somebody says that ‘this Mr. Such-and-such, this Dr. Such-and-such, he is respected by so many people, and you are saying that he’s a rascal? What is this?’ So Jiva Gosvami says that ‘This man, who is respected, but he is respected by whom? He is respected by this class of men: dogs, hogs, camel and asses. So he is a big pasuh.” (Lecture on Bg. [1.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/1.20), July 17, 1973, London)

From another lecture on a similar topic: “Sva-vid-varahostra-kharaih, samstutah purusah pasuh. A leader means voted by some hogs, by some dogs, by some camels, and by some asses. This is the position of the society. Suppose there are many dogs in this Los Angeles city . .. So if they are called for votes, ‘Now we are taking vote for this, for this,’ what is the value of that election? Is there any value? So actually we are collecting votes from dogs, hogs, camels and asses.” (Lecture, September 15, 1972, Los Angeles)

Although both Saunaka Rsi’s and Srila Prabhupada’s words are strong, even harsh as Prabhupada himself said, it is difficult to disagree with them when one examines the current world situation. Who but an animal would engage in such cruel and indiscriminate violence as abortion, terrorism, economic exploitation, the manufacture of nuclear, biological, and chemical weaponry, and the mass slaughter of innocent, dependent, and helpless cows and other creatures? Each of the specific animals to which Saunaka compares such persons—dogs, hogs, camels, and asses—has its specific qualities. Dogs must beg for scraps of food from their masters. Similarly, as Prabhupada states in his purport to text 19: “Modem university education practically prepares one to acquire a doggish mentality with which to accept the service of a greater master. After finishing a so-called education, the so-called educated persons move like dogs from door to door with applications for some service, and mostly they are driven away, informed of no vacancy.”

Hogs are condemned for their indiscriminate eating: “Human beings are expected to accept the remnants of food offered to Lord Sri Krsna, and the Lord accepts foodstuff from the categories of leaves, flowers, fruits, etc. (Bg. [9.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.26)). As prescribed by Vedic scriptures, no animal food is offered to the Lord. Therefore, a human being is meant to eat a particular type of food. He should not imitate the animals to derive so-called vitamin values. Therefore, a person who has no discrimination in regard to eating is compared to a hog.”

Camels are condemned for relishing the taste of their own blood. “The central point of attraction for material enjoyment is sex life. To enjoy sex life is to suck one’s own blood, and there is not much more to be explained in this connection. The camel also sucks its own blood while chewing thorny twigs. The thorns the camel eats cut the tongue of the camel, and so blood begins to flow within the camel’s mouth. The thorns, mixed with fresh blood, create a taste for the foolish camel, and so he enjoys the thorn-eating business with false pleasure. Similarly, the great business magnates, industrialists who work very hard to earn money by different ways and questionable means, eat the thorny results of their actions mixed with their own blood.”

Asses are famed for their foolishness. “The ass is an animal who is celebrated as the greatest fool, even amongst the animals. The ass works very hard and carries burdens of the maximum weight without making profit for itself. . . . And the special qualification of the ass is that it is very much accustomed to being kicked by the opposite sex. When the ass begs for sexual intercourse, he is kicked by the fair sex, yet he still follows the female for such sexual pleasure. A henpecked man is compared, therefore, to the ass. . . . The laborers in great factories and workshops are also engaged in such burdensome work, and after working hard during the day, the poor laborer has to be again kicked by the fair sex, not only for sex enjoyment but also for so many household affairs.”

Saunaka Rsi has already criticized those who don’t hear krsna-katha; now in texts 20-24 he will condemn the limbs and other bodily parts of those who do not serve Krsna. “One who has not listened to the messages about the prowess and marvelous acts of the Personality of Godhead and has not sung or chanted loudly the worthy songs about the Lord is to be considered to possess earholes like the holes of snakes and a tongue like the tongue of a frog.” (Bhag. [2.3.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.20)) If a snake were to enter the holes of our ears, it would fill them with poison. Frogs croak continually, but their message is useless and only informs snakes where to find their next meal.

Srila Prabhupada’s comment suggests how one can help people who do not hear krsna-katha: “If the ear is not engaged in the service of the Lord by hearing about Him from Bhagavad-gita or Srimad-Bhagavatam, certainly the holes of the ear will be filled with some rubbish. Therefore the messages of Bhagavad-gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam should be preached all over the world very loudly. That is the duty of a pure devotee who has actually heard about them from the perfect sources.” (Bhag. [2.3.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.20), purport)Prabhupada explained the same point in a lecture on Bhagavatam 2.3.20 given in Los Angeles on June 16, 1972:

**When you walk on the paddy field, you will find so many holes. Have you got experience? There are so many holes. Even on the beach, you will find so many holes. But especially in the agricultural field there are holes, because rats and mice come to eat and they make a hole to live. And the snakes take advantage. They enter the hole and eat the rat and mouse and live peacefully.**

**When these ear holes are not receptive to the message of Krsna, they are not being utilized properly. Similarly, you have a tongue, but if you cannot chant Hare Krsna, it is just like the tongue of the frog. The frogs use their tongue very nicely. They sing ka-ka-kan, ka-ka-kan, ka-ka-kan. \[laughter\] Yes. But what is the result of their singing? In the darkness, the snake understands, “Here is a frog,” and it comes and immediately eats.**

**In a previous verse we have learned that the sun’s business is to gradually take away the lifespan of one who does not hear about Krsna. This is the same. As the frog is calling his death, the snake says: “Please come here, I am here.” Similarly, these persons who are talking all nonsense without krsna-katha, they are inviting Yamaraja, the lord of death, “Please come soon. I am here. I am here.” This is the position.**

Saunaka Rsi continues his condemnation of materialists: The bodily decorations and the wealth of those who do not engage in Krsna’s service are worse than useless, because as these persons are drowning, these things weigh them down. “The upper portion of the body, though crowned with a silk turban, is only a heavy burden if not bowed down before the Personality of Godhead who can award mukti \[freedom\]. And the hands, though decorated with glittering bangles, are like those of a dead man if not engaged in the service of the Personality of Godhead Hari.” (Bhag. [2.3.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.21))

Even a turban-wearing king and his bangled wife should bow before the Lord and offer Him service, acknowledging themselves as His subordinates and servants. One’s position in the material world is fragile, and one should humbly admit his insignificance by bowing his head before the Lord. Prabhupada states this strongly: “A drowning man with a heavy weight on his head is sure to go down more swiftly than those who have no heavy weight. A foolish, puffed-up man defies the science of God and says that God has no meaning for him, but when he is in the grip of God’s law and is caught by some disease like cerebral thrombosis, that godless man sinks into the ocean of nescience by the weight of his material acquisition. Advancement of material science without God consciousness is a heavy load on the head of human society, and so one must take heed of this great warning.” (Bhag. [2.3.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.21), purport)

Saunaka continues: The eyes of those who do not see the Lord’s deity are as useful as the eyes on peacock feathers. The legs that are not used to carry them to holy places are no better than tree trunks. Such eyes and legs are useless, because they do not fulfill the purpose for which they were created. Similarly, the “person who has not at any time received the dust of the feet of the Lord’s pure devotee upon his head is certainly a dead body. And the person who has never experienced the aroma of the tulasi leaves from the lotus feet of the Lord is also a dead body, although breathing.” (Bhag. [2.3.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.23))

Seeing a beautiful person causes one’s heart to melt a little. Imagine, then, how soft one’s heart can become on seeing Krsna, the reservoir of all beauty. The soul has a natural attraction to beauty, because it is naturally attracted to Krsna. One should turn oneself to Krsna. The beautiful eye on a peacock feather has no practical use. Similarly, the eyes of those who neglect seeing the Lord offer no true benefit and unfailingly leave them attracted to material beauty, the shadow of Krsna. The eyes of those who see Krsna’s beauty can truly see.

In his purport to text 22, Srila Prabhupada writes: “Only attention engaged in the service of the Lord, especially in decorating the temple, accompanied by musical kirtana and spiritual instructions from scriptures, can save the common man from the hellish cinema attractions and rubbish sex-songs broadcast everywhere by radios. If one is unable to maintain a temple at home, he should go to another’s temple where all the above performances are regularly executed. Visiting the temple of a devotee and looking at the profusely decorated forms of the Lord well dressed in a well-decorated, sanctified temple naturally infuse the mundane mind with spiritual inspiration. People should visit holy places like Vrndavana where such temples and worship of the Deity are specifically maintained. . . . One who does not move in that way is as good as a standing tree condemned by the Lord not to move. The moving tendency of the human being is misused by visiting places for sightseeing. The best purpose of such traveling tendencies could be fulfilled by visiting the holy places established by great acaryas and thereby not being misled by the atheistic propaganda of moneymaking men who have no knowledge of spiritual matters.”

Later, Maharaja Pariksit will himself speak of the positive use of the body: “Actual speech is that which describes the qualities of the Lord, real hands are those that work for Him, a true mind is that which always remembers Him dwelling within everything moving and nonmoving, and actual ears are those that listen to sanctifying topics about Him. An actual head is one that bows down to the Lord in His manifestations among the moving and nonmoving creatures, real eyes are those that see only the Lord, and actual limbs are those which regularly honor the water that has bathed the Lord’s feet or those of His devotees.” (Bhag. [10.80.3-4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/80.3))

Srila Prabhupada resonates with a similar mood in his purport to Bhagavatam [2.3.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.23): “. . . Lord Sri Krsna is the property of His pure unconditional devotees, and as such only the devotees can deliver Krsna to another devotee; Krsna is never obtainable directly. Lord Caitanya therefore designated Himself as gopi-bhartuh pada-kamalayor dasa-dasanudasah, or ‘the most obedient servant of the servants of the Lord, who maintains the gopi damsels at Vrndavana.’”

Prabhupada goes on to say that pure devotees never approach the Lord directly. Rather, they try to please the servant of the Lord’s servants. In this way, the Lord becomes pleased. Only then can the devotees relish the taste of the tulasi leaves stuck to His lotus feet. In the Brahma'Samhitd it is said that the Lord can never be found by becoming a great scholar of Vedic literature. Instead, He is easily approached through His pure devotees. In Vrndavana, all the pure devotees pray for Srimati Radharani’s mercy, because She is the Lord’s pleasure potency. “Srimati Radharani is the tenderhearted feminine counterpart of the supreme whole, resembling the perfectional stage of the worldly feminine nature.” Therefore, Her mercy is readily available for sincere devotees. Once She recommends a devotee to Lord Krsna, the Lord immediately accepts that devotee into His association. The conclusion is that we should be more serious about seeking the devotee’s mercy than the Lord’s direct mercy, and by the good will of the devotees, our natural attraction for the Lord’s service will be revived.

Now those who have thus far escaped Saunaka’s condemnation will be humbled: “Certainly that heart is steel-framed which, in spite of one’s chanting the holy name of the Lord with concentration, does not change when ecstasy takes place, tears fill the eyes and the hairs stand on end.” (Bhag. [2.3.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.24)) Prabhupada’s purport to this text drives the point deep by defining the mature stage of Visnu worship. We call this stage pure devotional service, which requires a change of heart. “The whole process of spiritual culture is aimed at changing the heart of the living being in the matter of his eternal relation with the Supreme Lord as subordinate servant, which is his eternal constitutional position. ... It is expected that by discharging regulated devotional service one must manifest the change of heart. If there is no such change, the heart must be considered steel-framed, for it is not melted even when there is chanting of the holy name of the Lord. We must always remember that hearing and chanting are the basic principles of discharging devotional duties, and if they are properly performed there will follow the reactional ecstasy with signs of tears in the eyes and standing of the hairs on the body. ... If the reaction does not take place, even after continuous hearing and chanting of the Lord’s holy name, it may be considered to be due to offenses only.”

Prabhupada spoke more on this topic in a lecture given on text 24 in Los Angeles (June 22, 1972): “If we chant this Hare Krsna mantra without offense, observing the regulative principles and numerical strength—sankhya-purvaka-nama-gana-natibhih . . . The Gosvamis in Vrndavana used to chant keeping in numerical strength. They were all liberated persons. Still, for teaching us they also used to chant keeping a numerical strength. Haridasa Thakura, he used to chant Hare Krsna mantra keeping a numerical strength—300,000 times. So our prescription is only 25,000, not 100,000. So it is not very difficult; it takes utmost two hours. We can find time. Out of twenty-four hours, that chanting will take two hours. We can find out time. So if we actually follow the rules and regulations and chant Hare Krsna mantra, then these symptoms will come. Netrejalam gatra^ruhesu harsah. When this comes then you know that ‘I am coming to perfection.’ And if it is not coming, then it is to be understood the heart is steel-framed. Stone. If we keep our heart stone or steel-framed, then it cannot be melted. These symptoms mean that the heart is melting or changing.”  
Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura also comments on this important text.

**This verse should be interpreted in the following way: The heart is condemned if it is not transformed even when there are external signs of ecstasy, such as tears. The true signs of the transformed heart have been given elsewhere: forbearance, not wasting time, detachment, freedom from false prestige, fixed hope, supreme eagerness, a taste for always singing the holy name, attachment to describing the Lord’s transcendental qualities, and affection for the places where the Lord resides—His temples or dhama. The external symptoms are common, whereas the internal signs are extraordinary.**

**This, then, is the meaning: When nonenvious devotees, who are on the highest levels of qualification, chant the holy name, they experience the name’s sweetness. This results in an internal transformation symptomized by forbearance and the other internal signs on the one hand, and tears and the other external signs on the other.**

**Those on the lowest levels of qualification, the neophytes, are usually filled with envy. Because of their offenses they may chant the holy name, but they never experience its sweetness or achieve the internal proof of such experience (forbearance, etc.). Thus although they may make a show of the external signs, crying tears, etc., their hearts have not really changed.**

**Saunaka’s criticism—“their hearts must be made of stone”— applies to these envious and offensive neophytes. Through association with more advanced devotees, the anarthas of such neophytes will be destroyed and they will rise through the stages of devotion from steadfastness, taste, and attachment to bhava. At bhava, the heart will truly soften and this criticism will no longer apply.**

**Those who develop the inner symptoms but remain hardhearted are beyond cure.**

Having enthusiastically condemned the materialists, Saunaka Rsi again requests Suta Gosvami to further narrate what Srila Sukadeva Gosvami spoke to Maharaja Pariksit. Sridhara Svami summarizes the contents of the first three chapters of the Second Canto in his prefaces to those chapters: The first chapter describes meditation on the Lord’s universal form by engaging in devotional activities, beginning with hearing and chanting about the Lord. The second chapter describes abandoning meditation on the Lord’s universal form and accepting instead meditation on Lord Visnu, who is the witness of everything and the master of all. The third chapter describes the superiority of service to Lord Visnu, which is performed with great devotion, and which consists of many activities beginning with hearing about the Lord.

## Dialogue Two - The Lord’s Relationship with the Material World

## Chapter 4 - The Process of Creation

## Texts 1-10: Maharaja Pariksit Inquires Further from Srila Sukadeva Gosvami

After hearing Sukadeva Gosvami’s conclusive instruction to always focus his mind on Krsna, Maharaja Pariksit, who was already an exalted devotee, faithfully concentrated his mind on the Lord. Constant remembrance of Krsna is both the goal and the method to attain the goal. As Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to Bhagavatam [2.4.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.1), “The whole Vedic adventure is to draw one’s attention entirely unto the lotus feet of Lord Krsna without any diversion ...”

In Krsna-sandarbha, anuccheda 53, Jiva Gosvami cites Bhagavatam [10.1.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/1.15) (“O Your majesty, best of all saintly kings, because you are greatly attracted to topics of Vasudeva, it is certain that your intelligence is firmly fixed in spiritual understanding, which is the only true goal for humanity. Because that attraction is unceasing, it is certainly sublime”). That the king was able to faithfully concentrate on Krsna shows that he had already succeeded in attaining the goal of life, steady (naisthiki) attachment (rati) to the topics (kathayam) that were fixed on the form (sthayi) of Vasudeva’s son (vasudeva nandanasya). Maharaja Pariksit’s mind was already chaste (satim) and pure, for it manifested devotional, prayerful intelligence (mati). He was parama-rasa-vidagdha, completely expert in relishing rasa. His purity will manifest in the words he speaks in Bhagavatam [2.8.2-3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.2): “Narrations concerning the Lord, who possesses wonderful potencies, are certainly auspicious for living beings in all planets. О greatly fortunate Sukadeva Gosvami, please continue narrating Srimad-Bhagavatam so that I can place my mind upon the Supreme Soul, Lord Krsna, and, being completely freed from material qualities, thus relinquish this body.”

Continuing, Suta Gosvami states that the king’s attraction to Krsna has allowed him to renounce affection for everything else, including his body, treasury, family, and kingdom. Maharaja Pariksit, “rapt in thought of Lord Krsna, knowing well of his imminent death, renounced all sorts of fruitive activities, namely acts of religion, economic development and sense gratification, and thus fixed himself firmly in his natural love for Krsna . . .” (Bhag. [2.4.3—4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.3)) How complete was Maharaja Pariksit’s dependence on Krsna!

In his purport to text 2 Srila Prabhupada explains the need for detachment as well as how to attain it: “Attachment for household paraphernalia and for Lord Krsna go poorly together. One attachment is the path of darkness, and the other attachment is the path of light. Where there is light, there is no darkness, and where there is darkness, there is no light. But an expert devotee can turn everything to the path of light by an attitude of service to the Lord, and the best example here is the Pandavas. Maharaja Yudhisthira and householders like him can turn everything to light by dovetailing so-called material assets in the service of the Lord, but one who is not trained or is unable to turn everything to the service of the Lord (nirbandhah krsna' sambandhe) must give up all material connections before he can be fit to hear and chant the glories of the Lord, or in other words, one who has seriously heard Srimad-Bhagavatam for even one day, like Maharaja Pariksit, from a fit personality like Sukadeva Gosvami, may be able to lose all affinity for material things.”One can become truly detached from matter when one becomes fully attracted to Krsna. Only then will the world’s “glories” pale. How different from the people of today was Maharaja Pariksit’s mood as he faced death. Srila Prabhupada mocked the mood of the contemporary people in a lecture he gave on Bhagavatam [2.4.3—4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.3) in Los Angeles on June 27, 1972:

**One who is actually intelligent, he should know that he will die. But the karmi, the rascal, he knows also that he will die—at least, he theoretically accepts—but he wants to enjoy to the fullest extent, as long as death has not yet come. That is the present condition of the society. He knows that he will die. “So, so long my senses are there, let me gratify.” Now, yesterday, when I went to the bank, there was a cinema signboard. What is that?**

**Karandhara: Is there sex after death?**

**Prabhupada: Yes. \[laughter\] You see? Because this material life means sex. So, they are seeking sex after death also, \[laughter\] “Is there sex after death?” they’re inquiring. If there is sex after death, then they are not fearful of death, \[laughter\] There is a story that one man was drinking. So, drinking in India is a great sin. His friend advised that “You are drinking. You’ll go to hell.” So he said, “Oh, my father also drinks.” So he said, “Your father also will go to hell.” “Oh, my brother also drinks.” “Oh, he also will go to hell.” In this way, he continued to say, “My father, my brother, my sister, my this, my that...” And he was replying, “Yes, they will also go to hell.” “Oh, then hell is heaven. Because we’re all drinking here and drinking there. So what is hell? That is heaven.” Similarly this signboard is like that. “If sex is there after death, then that is not death. That is life.” \[laughter\] You see? So actually, you have got sex after death. Because you’ll get into another body. Now you are having sex as human being in very nice apartment or on the street, on the beach, as you like. In the next life also, as cats and dogs, you will have sex life.**

Another example is the six Gosvamis of Vrndavana, who were able to consider material pleasure insignificant because they were so captivated by Krsna. When pleasing Krsna becomes one’s desire, attraction to the pleasures based on the false sense of self—body, spouse, wealth, and possessions—dims. Yet matter in and of itself does not cause illusion, nor does renunciation of matter award attraction to Krsna. Rather, matter, being Krsna’s energy, should be used in Krsna’s service. One may maintain a healthy aversion toward using matter for one’s own petty pleasures, but one should not be averse to matter itself; one should be willing to use Krsna’s energies in His service. If one is pure and sincere in that endeavor, he will become free from illusion, not more entangled in it.

Maharaja Pariksit’s situation—being cursed to die—was only the immediate push behind his complete renunciation. Actually, Krsna arranged both the curse and the king’s renunciation for the king’s benefit. As Srila Prabhupada describes: “Pariksit Maharaja, simply by

hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam, got salvation. So this superficial awkward position—he lost his life, lost his kingdom, he had to leave his wife and children and everything—don’t take it that ‘By Krsna consciousness, he became bereft of all assets.’ No. He was going to be rewarded very highly, going back to home, back to Godhead.” (Lecture, June 25, 1972, Los Angeles)

Maharaja Pariksit was fully surrendered to Krsna. Therefore, he accepted the difficult circumstances as his Lord’s mercy, and while living through those circumstances resolutely engaged in the Lord’s service. Accepting whatever happens to us as Krsna’s mercy, regardless of the form that mercy takes, while sincerely attempting to serve Krsna through those circumstances, is true dependence on Krsna and true Krsna consciousness.

Suta Gosvami next relates Maharaja Pariksit’s reply to Sukadeva Gosvami: “O learned brahmana, you know everything because you are without material contamination. Therefore whatever you have spoken to me appears perfectly right. Your speeches are gradually destroying the darkness of my ignorance, for you are narrating the topics of the Lord.” (Bhag. [2.4.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.5)) Srila Jiva Gosvami notes that Maharaja Pariksit has asserted that his ignorance is being shattered by Sukadeva Gosvami’s words. In this way, the king recognizes the sage’s potency. Wishing to increase his mental focus on Krsna, Maharaja Pariksit inquires about how, by His personal energies, the Lord creates the phenomenal universes, which are inconceivable even to the great demigods. The king continues: The Lord’s activities are wonderful, but I wish to know how He uses His inconceivable potencies in creation. Does He utilize His energies and expansions to maintain and destroy the universes? Does He act directly through the modes of material nature?

In his purport to text 6, Srila Prabhupada criticizes the idea that the universe was not created but appeared by chance: “The common man also knows that the creation is made by some creator and is not created automatically. We have no experience in the practical world that a thing is created automatically. . . . An inexperienced boy may be struck with wonder by seeing the impersonal actions of electronics or many other wonderful things conducted by electrical energy, but an experienced man knows that behind the action is a living man who creates such energy.
