Similarly the so-called scholars and philosophers of the world may, by mental speculation, present so many utopian theories about the impersonal creation of the universe, but an intelligent devotee of the Lord, by studying the Bhagavad' gita, can know that behind the creation is the hand of the Supreme Lord, just as in the generating electrical powerhouse there is the resident engineer.”

Maharaja Pariksit, himself a learned devotee, inquires still further from Sukadeva Gosvami, who was both his spiritual master and a great transcendental authority, about the unfathomable Lord Krsna: “Kindly clear up all these doubtful inquiries, because you are not only vastly learned in the Vedic literatures and self-realized in transcendence, but are also a great devotee of the Lord and are therefore as good as the Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [2.4.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.10))

Srila Prabhupada also explains the importance of learning about Krsna’s greatness as the creator of the material world before one speaks about His transcendental pastimes in Vrndavana (Bhag. [2.4.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.6), purport). Sukadeva thus first describes the Supreme Lord and His power so that later, when he describes Krsna’s Vrndavana pastimes, no one will mistake them for something mundane, although they appear to parallel human activities. In addition, Kali-yuga’s influence has made it fashionable to name oneself God and for the ignorant to accept such claims. To clarify what it means to be God—the one who creates, maintains, and destroys the entire universe with only a fragment of His power—Sukadeva Gosvami will now describe simply a fragment of Krsna’s inconceivable potency.

Srila Prabhupada continues this theme in his purport to text 10: “The Lord’s pastimes in the internal potency are displayed in His activities in Vrndavana, but His external potential works are directed in His features of Karanarnavasayi Visnu, Garbhodakasayi Visnu and Ksirodakasayi Visnu. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti offers his good counsel to the interested Vaisnavas when he says that they should not be interested in hearing only about the Lord’s activities (like rasa-lila), but must be keenly interested in His pastimes in His features of the purusd' vataras in connection with srsri-tattva, creational functions, following the examples of Maharaja Pariksit, the ideal disciple, and Sukadeva Gosvami, the ideal spiritual master.”

## Texts 11-18: Sukadeva Gosvami Offers his Obeisances to the Lord with Eight Prayers

Before beginning his reply, Sukadeva Gosvami humbly remembers the Lord, the creator, who reciprocates with everyone’s desires. As a great devotee, Sukadeva humbly accepts that he has no ability to independently answer the king’s questions. He therefore remembers the Lord, the master of his senses, and prays for the ability to properly reply.

In his purport to text 11 Srila Prabhupada details a pure devotee’s mood as he remembers the Lord: “The devotees of the Lord, while delivering speeches and describing the transcendental attributes of the Lord, do not think that they can do anything independently. They think that they can speak only what they are induced to speak by the Supreme Lord, the master of the senses.... No one is free to act freely and independently, and as such, one should always seek the permission of the Lord to act or eat or speak, and by the blessing of the Lord everything done by a devotee is beyond the principles of the four defects typical of the conditioned soul.” How does the inconceivably powerful Lord deal reciprocally with His countless servitors? Srila Prabhupada answers this question in his purport to text 13: “Just like a kind father, either in His favor upon the devotees or His punishment of the demons, He is ever kind to everyone because He is the complete existence for all individual existence.”

Appreciating the ever-kind yet all-powerful Lord, Srila Suka-deva Gosvami continues to offer prayers: “Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead who, for the creation of the material world, accepts the three modes of nature. He is the complete whole residing within the body of everyone, and His ways are inconceivable. I again offer my respectful obeisances unto the form of complete existence and transcendence, who is the liberator of the pious devotees from all distresses and the destroyer of the further advances in atheistic temperament of the nondevoteedemons. For the transcendentalists who are situated in the topmost spiritual perfection, He grants their specific destinations. Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto He who is the associate of the members of the Yadu dynasty and who is always a problem for the nondevotees. He is the supreme enjoyer of both the material and spiritual worlds, yet He enjoys His own abode in the spiritual sky. There is no one equal to Him because His transcendental opulence is immeasurable.” (Bhag. [2.4.12-14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.12))

Krsna’s main activity, however, is not reciprocating with the desires and needs of His innumerable parts and parcels. Rather, He is the supremely independent enjoyer. The actions He enacts for His own pleasure, which have nothing to do with the innumerable desires of the independent living entities, occur in the spiritual world, a realm to which nondevotees have no access.

Srila Sridhara Svami comments on text 14, which, along with text 13, seems to indicate Krsna’s partiality—Krsna appears to reward His devotees and chastise the demons. Srila Sridhara Svami indicates that Krsna’s partiality is not a defect. Rather, because of Krsna’s acintya-sakti, inconceivable power and opulence, His partiality is only apparent. His actions are always impartial and beneficial for everyone.

By quoting Bhismadeva (Bhag. [1.9.21-22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/9.21)) in his Paramatma' sandarbha, anuccheda 93, Srila Jiva Gosvami offers an example to show the Lord’s ability to maintain the contradictory stances of universal impartiality and partiality toward His devotees: Bhisma prays: “Being the Absolute Personality of Godhead, He is present in everyone’s heart. He is equally kind to everyone, and He is free from the false ego of differentiation. Therefore whatever He does is free from material inebriety. He is equibalanced. Yet despite His being equally kind to everyone, He has graciously come before me while I am ending my life, for I am His unflinching servitor.”

Wishing to inspire his hearers with the faith that will assist them in taking shelter of the Lord, Sukadeva Gosvami now speaks more on Krsna’s inconceivable potencies: “Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the all-auspicious Lord Sri Krsna, about whom glorification, remembrances, audience, prayers, hearing and worship can at once cleanse the effects of all sins of the performer. Let me offer my respectful obeisances again and again unto the all-auspicious Lord Sri Krsna. The highly intellectual, simply by surrendering unto His lotus feet, are relieved of all attachments to present and future existences and without difficulty progress toward spiritual existence.” (Bhag. [2.4.15-16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.15))

In his purport to text 15, Srila Prabhupada writes: “The sublime form of religious performances to free oneself from all reactions of sins is suggested herein by the greatest authority, Sri Sukadeva Gosvami.”

What is that “sublime form of religious performance”? Srila Prabhupada explains: “The devotees need not be disappointed in the physical absence of the Lord, though they may think of not being associated with Him. The devotional process of chanting, hearing, remembering, etc., (either all or some of them, or even one of them) can give us the desired result of associating with the Lord by discharging the transcendental loving service of the Lord in the above manner. Even the very sound of the holy name of Lord Krsna or Rama can at once surcharge the atmosphere spiritually. We must know definitely that the Lord is present wherever such pure transcendental service is performed, and thus the performer of offenseless kirtanam has positive association with the Lord. Similarly, remembrance and prayers also can give us the desired result if they are properly done under expert guidance.”

In his purport to text 16, Srila Prabhupada sweetly paraphrases the essence of Krsna’s words in the eighteenth chapter of Bhagavad-gita ([64-66](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.64)): “My dear Arjuna, you are very dear to Me, and therefore only for your good I will disclose the most secret part of My instructions. It is simply this: become a pure devotee of Mine and give yourself unto Me only, and I promise you full spiritual existence, by which you may gain the eternal right of transcendental loving service unto Me. Just give up all other ways of religiosity and exclusively surrender unto Me and believe that I will protect you from your sinful acts, and I shall deliver you. Do not worry any more.”

This purport is full of the description of a life enriched by surrender to Krsna: “Such a devotional life is full of kirtanam, smaranam, iksanam, etc., as mentioned in the previous verse. One must therefore adopt this simple way of devotional life in order to attain the highest perfection available in any category of the human form of life in any part of the world.”

Srila Sridhara Svami states that texts 15-16 remind one of the glories of faithful devotion. Srila Jiva Gosvami comments that text 15 shows us that one can both remember the Lord’s glories and benefit from that remembrance even in the Lord’s absence. The word yat is singular, and shows that repeating the Lord’s glories on even one occasion is sufficient to remove one’s sins. Referring to text 16, Jiva Gosvami writes that this text enjoins all people to seek refuge in the Supreme Lord.

In text 17, Sukadeva Gosvami glorifies the power of bhakti-yoga: Neither sages, nor those who give charity, nor workers, nor mystics or philosophers, nor followers of Vedic principles can achieve any fruitful result without His service. Such pious souls must practice devotional service if they wish to obtain the fruits of their pious acts. But how should the sinful become purified? Srila Jiva Gosvami concludes: All men should seek refuge in the Lord. Sukadeva Gosvami’s conclusion is the same: “Kirata, Huna, Andhra, Pulinda, Pulkasa, Abhira, Sumbha, Yavana, members of the Khasa races and even others addicted to sinful acts can be purified by taking shelter of the devotees of the Lord, due to His being the supreme power. I beg to offer my respectful obeisances unto Him.” (Bhag. [2.4.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.18)) According to Srila Sridhara Svami, this text also glorifies faithful devotion, while Srila Jiva Gosvami states that this text asserts that devotion is so powerful that even a sinful practitioner will become purified.

One may wonder how such a thing is possible. Sridhara Svami writes that the Lord is prabhavisnave, powerful Visnu. He is so powerful that He can do anything. Prabhupada is grave in his purport to text 18, as he refers both to the method devotees must follow and the responsibility each devotee has to become purified, remain pure, and preach:

**And from the version of Srila Sukadeva Gosvami it appears that instead of running a godless civilization in the present context of the world situation, if the leadership of world affairs is entrusted to the devotees of the Lord, for which a worldwide organization under the name and style of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness has already been started, then by the grace of the Almighty Lord there can be a thorough change of heart in human beings all over the world because the devotees of the Lord are able authorities to effect such a change by purifying the dust-wom minds of the people in general.... As Sukadeva Gosvami began his prayer by discussing the word yat-kirtanam, so also Lord Caitanya recommended that simply by glorifying the Lord’s holy name, a tremendous change of heart can take place by which the complete misunderstanding between the human nations created by politicians can at once be extinguished. And after the extinction of the fire of misunderstanding, other profits will follow.... Anyone from any part of the world who becomes well conversant in the science of Krsna becomes a pure devotee and a spiritual master for the general mass of people and may reclaim them by purification of heart. Though a person be even the most sinful man, he can at once be purified by systematic contact with a pure Vaisnava. A Vaisnava, therefore, can accept a bona fide disciple from any part of the world without any consideration of caste and creed and promote him by regulative principles to the status of a pure Vaisnava who is transcendental to brahminical culture. ... So by the order of Lord Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, the cult of Srimad-Bhagavatam or the Bhagavad-gita can be preached all over the world, reclaiming all persons willing to accept the transcendental cult.**

## Texts 19-25: Sukadeva Gosvami’s Request for the Lord’s Mercy

Sukadeva Gosvami has offered his obeisances to the Lord who can purify everyone. Now, with feelings laden with love, before addressing Maharaja Pariksit’s questions he glorifies Krsna as the Supersoul and the Lord of all self-realized souls. Krsna is the Lord of all opulence, sacrifice, and intelligence, and the leader of all living entities. “May that Supreme Absolute be pleased with me.”

Krsna reciprocates with all living entities according to their desires, but what ultimate award can the Lord give? And what qualification is required to achieve it? Srila Prabhupada comments on the phrase gata-vyalikaih., “by those who are above pretensions.” The word “pretension” comes from the same root as “pretend.” Pretentious devotees perform worship, but only to reap personal benefit—to overcome enemies, become famous, gain wealth, or become liberated. This isn’t true worship because the motive underlying the glorification is selfish gain. Most people consider attaining such gain the purpose behind religion. Although Krsna reciprocates with everyone according to his desire (including those who desire material results), pretentious, motivated service does not inspire Him to award the worshiper His full blessings. By contrast, pure devotees wish only to please Krsna by their worship.

In his purport to text 19, Srila Prabhupada speaks of the sincerity of service devotees require if they are to rise above pretension and come to know Krsna. The pure devotee’s worship is indeed sincere. Srila Prabhupada further describes such devotees’ moods: “They want only to serve the Lord because the Lord is great and as living entities they are eternally subordinate parts and parcels of the Lord. This perfect realization of the self by the devotee helps him to become desireless, to desire nothing for his personal self, and thus the devotees are called niskami, without any desire. A living entity, by his constitutional position, cannot be void of all desires (the bhukti-kami, mukti-kami and siddhi-kami all desire something for personal satisfaction), but the niskami devotees of the Lord desire everything for the satisfaction of the Lord. They are completely dependent on the orders of the Lord and are always ready to discharge their duty for the satisfaction of the Lord.”

Srila Sridhara Svami states that Sukadeva Gosvami is praying for the mercy of the one Lord by first remembering the Lord and the various worshipers who worship Him on different levels according to their realizations.What is the process of knowing the dhiyam pad, the powerful and merciful Lord, the powerful controller, master, and awarder of intelligence and transcendental knowledge? “It is the Personality of Godhead Sri Krsna who gives liberation. By thinking of His lotus feet at every second, following in the footsteps of authorities, the devotee in trance can see the Absolute Truth.” (Bhag. [2.4.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.21)) By His mercy, which one attains by practicing bhakti-yoga, that Lord will be pleased and bestow His grace. It is through this grace that one can come to know Him. Srila Prabhupada describes the potent process of Krsna consciousness in his purport to this text:

**The mystic yogis, after a strenuous effort to control the senses, may be situated in a trance of yoga just to have a vision of the Supersoul within everyone, but the pure devotee, simply by remembering the Lord’s lotus feet at every second, at once becomes established in real trance because by such realization his mind and intelligence are completely cleansed of the diseases of material enjoyment. The pure devotee thinks himself fallen into the ocean of birth and death and incessantly prays to the Lord to lift him up. He only aspires to become a speck of transcendental dust at the lotus feet of the Lord. The pure devotee, by the grace of the Lord, absolutely loses all attraction for material enjoyment, and to keep free from contamination he always thinks of the lotus feet of the Lord. . . .**

**This humbleness of the pure devotee, who is one hundred percent engaged in His service, puts the devotee of the Lord in a trance by which to realize everything, because to the sincere devotee of the Lord, the Lord reveals Himself, as stated in the Bhagavad-gita (**[**10.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.10)**). The Lord, being the Lord of intelligence in everyone (even in the nondevotee), favors His devotee with proper intelligence so that automatically the pure devotee is enlightened with the factual truth about the Lord and His different energies.**

Again praying that the Lord may be pleased with him, Sukadeva Gosvami requests the same Lord who inspired knowledge within Brahma’s heart, the Supersoul of everything, to empower his words. Ultimately, Sukadeva’s prayers are meant to benefit others. Prabhupada’s purports to this section confirm Sukadeva Gosvami’s attitude before beginning to preach: “Sukadeva Gosvami is praying to the Lord by dint of being inspired from within by the Lord so that he could rightly explain the facts and figures of creation as inquired by Maharaja Pariksit.” (Bhag. [2.4.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.22), purport)

And from his purport to text 23: “As a fully dependent devotee, Sukadeva Gosvami (unlike a mundane man who is proud of his own capability) invokes the pleasure of the Personality of Godhead so that his statements may be successful and be appreciated by the hearers. The devotee always thinks of himself as instrumental for anything successfully carried out, and he declines to take credit for anything done by himself. The godless atheist wants to take all credit for activities, not knowing that even a blade of grass cannot move without the sanction of the Supreme Spirit, the Personality of Godhead. Sukadeva Gosvami therefore wants to move by the direction of the Supreme Lord, who inspired Brahma to speak the Vedic wisdom. . . . Sukadeva prays for the mercy of the Lord, not only for being helped personally in presenting the truth, but also for helping others to whom he would like to speak.”

Devotees don’t view themselves as “the doer,” nor do they desire credit for whatever they have accomplished. Rather, they desire to act as Krsna’s instruments, and they pray to be effectively used by Him like tools in the hands of an expert carpenter. Thus Sukadeva Gosvami’s prayers express his desire that the Lord be pleased to use him to answer Maharaja Pariksit’s questions. Sukadeva then begs for his spiritual master’s blessings, because he wishes to respond to Maharaja Pariksit based on what he has heard in disciplic succession. “I offer my respectful obeisances unto Srila Vyasadeva, the incarnation of Vasudeva who compiled the Vedic scriptures. The pure devotees drink up the nec-tarean transcendental knowledge dropping from the lotuslike mouth of the Lord.” (Bhag. [2.4.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/4.24))

Thus Sukadeva Gosvami, after having prayed for blessings, begins his reply to Pariksit Maharaja’s questions by relating a conversation between Brahma and Narada. Sukadeva begins: The first-born, Lord Brahma, answered these same questions after his son, Narada Muni, had inquired from him.

## Chapter 5 - The Cause of All Causes

## Texts 1-8: Sri Narada Muni Inquires from Lord Brahma

Sukadeva Gosvami tells the story of how Narada Muni inquired from his father, Lord Brahma. Narada began by offering his obeisances to Lord Brahma, who served not only as his father but as his guru. Then he respectfully inquired about the nature of the individual soul and the Supersoul. “My dear father, please describe factually the symptoms of this manifest world. What is its background? How is it created? How is it conserved? And under whose control is all this being done?” (Bhag. [2.5.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.2)) These are essential questions. In the following text, Narada inquires further: Who creates and controls the manifest world?

Clearly, the creation has not occurred by chance. Is it within anyone’s experience that something well-organized has organized itself by chance? Scientists don’t leave the construction of their homes to chance, nor their cooking, nor their salaries. No one trusts random selection—chance—to be an effective organizational system. If the effect is structured and organized, the cause must also possess the characteristics of structure and organization, for the effect follows from the cause. The universe was designed and created by a Supreme Cause. Is it logical to assume that that effect contains more than its cause? If one man gave another man money and was the source of the second man’s wealth, it is understood that the second man’s wealth (the effect) does not contain more than the first man’s gift (the cause).

The laws that organize the universe are strict. For example, without exception every living being dies, trees point unfailingly toward the sun, and water flows downwards. That these natural laws are universally enforced means that the enforcer must be powerful. But not only are universal laws strictly enforced, the universe requires complex orchestration. The seasons change regularly, the winds blow, and water—first evaporated and then transported through the sky in clouds —returns to the earth as rain. Blood circulates, food is digested, air enters the lungs, and diseases are warded off to maintain life. Who can count the unlimited number of often complex, contradictory, and interdependent laws that must be interwoven to maintain efficiency and function in the world? Could this have been achieved without the help of an inconceivably great intelligence? Having at least these two characteristics—power and intelligence—the creator cannot be impersonal, because impersonal entails being devoid of qualities and characteristics. Who, then, asks Narada, has masterminded this incredible creation?

Srila Prabhupada argues that effects, such as the world, necessarily imply a cause: “The inquiries by Narada Muni on the basis of factual cause and effect appear very reasonable. The atheists, however, put forward many self-made theories without any touch of cause and effect. The manifested world, as well as the spirit soul, is still unexplained by the godless atheists through the medium of experimental knowledge, although they have put forward many theories manufactured by their fertile brains. Contrary to such mental speculative theories of creation, however, Narada Muni wanted to know all the facts of creation in truth, and not by theories.... Transcendental knowledge regarding the soul and the Supersoul includes knowledge of the phenomenal world and the basis of its creation. In the phenomenal world three things are factually observed by any intelligent man: the living beings, the manifest world, and the ultimate control over them. The intelligent man can see that neither the living entity nor the phenomenal world are creations of chance. The symmetry of creation and its regulative actions and reactions suggests the plan of an intelligent brain behind them, and by genuine inquiry one may find out the ultimate cause with the help of one who knows them factually.” (Bhag. [2.5.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.2), purport)It is important to note that to properly understand the answers to his questions, Narada Muni seeks answers from an authority, “one who knows them factually.” In a lecture given in Hyderabad on November 30, 1972, Srila Prabhupada describes such inquiry as the Vedic method to acquire knowledge of anything beyond our perception:

**Things beyond our perception we should not simply try to understand by logic and argument. It is a useless waste of time, because nobody can decide on theory. The modem so-called scientists also write like that: “Perhaps,” “It may be,” like that. “It may be millions of years.” “It may be.” What is the value of saying “It may be”? Say definitely. That they cannot do. All the scientists’ theories are “Perhaps” and “Maybe.” “Perchance, if it comes to be true.” So such kind of argument has no value. Therefore our sastra says acintyah khalu ye bhavah: beyond your . . . sense perception, don’t try to understand it by argument and logic.**

**Then how to know it? Know it from the person who knows it. That is knowledge. Just like we are trying to get knowledge about the soul, not by experiment but we are trying to understand from the words of Krsna. Krsna is the authority. So He says, in the beginning: dehino ’smin yatha dehe kaumaram yauvanarh jara. Krsna says, and we can think over it and ponder over it. Then we come to conclusion. And the other process, Vedic process, is:**

***yasya deve para bhaktir***  
***yatha deve tatha gurau***  
***tasyaite kathita hy arthah***  
***prakasante mahatmanah***

**Our process is descending process. We are not trying to understand by the ascending process. Inductive or deductive. We accept the statements of the Vedas. .. . According to our Vedic system, sruti~ pramana, if it is statement, the statement is there in the sruti, in the Vedas, then we accept.**

Sri Narada Muni continues to inquire from Brahma: You know all truths past, present, and future as intimately as a person knows a walnut in his hand. Where does your knowledge come from? Who is your protector? Do you work under someone, or did you alone create all entities by your personal energy? Srila Prabhupada expands on Narada Muni’s words in his purport to text 6: “In human society the human being is considered to be the superior living being, and amongst the human beings there are also different varieties: good, bad, equal, etc. But Narada Muni took for granted that none of them has any source of generation besides his father, Brahmaji.”

Narada continues: Does your knowledge have a source? Do you create independently, like a spider spinning a web and then later winding it up? Are you like the sun, who is self-sufficient in illuminating everything but which requires no illumination itself? Are you the Supreme, He who can act independently with no external help? How are you creating, and why? “Yet we are moved to wonder about the existence of someone more powerful than you when we think of your great austerities in perfect discipline, although your good self is so powerful in the matter of creation.” (Bhag. [2.5.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.7))

Narada is wondering why Brahma, whom he is addressing as supreme, would perform austerities, because this implies the existence of a superior whom Brahma is trying to please. He then wonders who has invested Brahma with his power to create. “My dear father . . . may all that I have inquired from you be kindly instructed to me so that 1 may be able to understand it as your student.” (Bhag. [2.5.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.8))

Srila Prabhupada restates Narada Muni’s question in his purport to text 7: “Narada Muni thought of Brahmaji as the Supreme Person, but when he saw Brahmaji engaged in the process of transcendental realization, doubts arose in him. So he wanted to be clearly informed.” Srila Sridhara Svami, in commenting on texts 7-8, also paraphrases Narada Muni’s thoughts: Although you are independent and powerful, I see you performing austerities to please another. Thus I am confused. Please enlighten me, to the extent I have the capacity to understand, as to the answers to my questions.

## Texts 9-17: Lord Brahma Describes the Greatness of the Supreme Lord

Brahma, the supreme manager of the universe, is the proper person to ask about the universe’s ultimate creator. The replies Brahma offers his student will be strictly in accord with the knowledge he received directly from the Supreme Personality of Godhead. After hearing from Lord Brahma, Narada will repeat this knowledge to Vyasadeva, who will in turn instruct his son Sukadeva Gosvami. Suta Gosvami, who is now speaking to the sages at Naimisaranya, heard this same knowledge from Sukadeva when Sukadeva presented it to Maharaja Pariksit. This system of transmitting knowledge is called guru-parampara, disciplic succession.

Hearing Narada’s questions, Lord Brahma begins his reply. His first words are of thanks: “My dear boy Narada, being merciful to all (including me) you have asked all these questions because I have been inspired to see into the prowess of the Almighty Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [2.5.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.9))

Srila Sridhara Svami states that in text 9, Brahma praises Narada’s questions because they give him the opportunity to glorify the Supreme Lord. Srila Prabhupada explains Brahma’s mood in a similar way in his purport to this text: “Brahmaji, being so questioned by Naradaji, congratulated him, for it is usual for the devotees to become very enthusiastic whenever they are questioned concerning the Almighty Personality of Godhead. That is the sign of a pure devotee of the Lord. Such discourses on the transcendental activities of the Lord purify the atmosphere in which such discussions are held, and the devotees thus become enlivened while answering such questions. It is purifying both for the questioners and for one who answers the questions. The pure devotees are not only satisfied by knowing everything about the Lord, but are also eager to broadcast the information to others, for they want to see that the glories of the Lord are known to everyone. Thus the devotee feels satisfied when such an opportunity is offered to him. This is the basic principle of missionary activities.”

First Brahma describes his own position in relation to the Supreme Lord: You have seen my acts in the creation of the universe, so you are naturally assuming that I am the supreme creator. Actually, I am only empowered by the Lord’s potency of passion to enact the universal creation. Unless people are aware of the Personality of Godhead, who is the ultimate truth beyond me, they are sure to become illusioned when they observe my powerful activities.

In his purport to text 10, Srila Prabhupada explains that Narada Muni, already a liberated soul, was nevertheless mistaken about the Supreme Lord’s identity. His bewilderment, Srila Prabhupada explains, was Krsna’s will “so that other, nonliberated persons may realize the real truth and knowledge of the Lord.” In essence, Narada’s reply indicates that a living entity, even one as great as Brahma, can never be the all-knowing God.

Brahma is indeed the creator, but only the secondary creator. His creation rests on everything the Lord has already created. Lord Brahma’s answers to Narada’s questions thus define God in terms of His unlimited potency. As Prabhupada states in his purport: “The Lord is always the Lord, and a common living being can never be equal to Him.”

Srila Prabhupada compares scientists who attempt to contain the Supreme in their limited conceptual potency to frogs in wells: “‘The frog in the well’ logic illustrates that a frog residing in the atmosphere and boundary of a well cannot imagine the length and breadth of the gigantic ocean. Such a frog, when informed of the gigantic length and breadth of the ocean, first of all does not believe that there is such an ocean, and if someone assures him that factually there is such a thing, the frog then begins to measure it by imagination by means of pumping its belly as far as possible, with the result that the tiny abdomen of the frog bursts and the poor frog dies without any experience of the actual ocean. Similarly, the material scientists also want to challenge the inconceivable potency of the Lord by measuring Him with their froglike brains and their scientific achievements, but at the end they simply die unsuccessfully, like the frog.”

Lord Brahma continues, explaining his position as secondary creator and delineating his creation as based on the Lord’s. Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 11 compares Brahma’s role in the creation to that of a gardener: “One should not expect the Lord to create like a blacksmith with a hammer and other instruments. The Lord creates by His potencies. He has His multifarious potencies (parasya saktir vividhaiva sruyate). Just as the small seed of a banyan fruit has the potency to create a big banyan tree, the Lord disseminates all varieties of seeds by His potential brahmajyoti (sva-rocisa), and the seeds are made to develop by the watering process of persons like Brahma. Brahma cannot create the seeds, but he can manifest the seed into a tree, just as a gardener helps plants and orchards to grow by the watering process.... Thus the ultimate cause of creation is the Lord.”

What limits our vision to the superficial? What influences one person to mistakenly see another as the Lord and creator? In answering these questions, Brahma offers prayers to the Lord, the primary creator: “I offer my obeisances and meditate upon Lord Krsna \[Vasudeva\], the Personality of Godhead, whose invincible potency influences them \[the less intelligent class of men\] to call me the supreme controller.” (Bhag. [2.5.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.12))

In text 2, Narada had asked about the symptoms that characterize the world, and now Brahma begins his answer: “The illusory energy of the Lord cannot take precedence, being ashamed of her position, but those who are bewildered by her always talk nonsense, being absorbed in thoughts of ‘It is Г and ‘It is mine.”’ (Bhag. [2.5.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.13)) What is this world’s primary characteristic? That the conditioned souls within it think like fools and speak nonsense! These two characteristics are caused by mayas influence, and maya is the Lord’s illusory energy. Those under maya’s influence mistakenly think and speak about “I” and “mine”—who they think they are and what they think is theirs. Clearly nothing in the realm of matter belongs to anyone. One comes into this world with nothing, with hardly even a body, and the body, along with everything else one imagines one has acquired, is left behind at death. The fact that one cannot take anything with him but is forced to leave it all behind indicates that nothing was ever his in the first place.

Under illusion’s influence, however, one tends to identify the ob-jects with which one comes into contact as one’s own. One then invests his consciousness in them, calling them “mine.” The power illusion has over each living entity increases with the increase of the soul’s desire to enjoy whatever he considers his own in the world of matter. Although all souls are naturally eternal, conscious, and blissful, those qualities are covered when the soul contacts the material energy in a spirit of enjoyment.

Embracing matter is like embracing a prostitute. The prostitute of maya allures the soul with inappropriate desires and induces him to forget his spiritual identity. Infused with the desires to find pleasure in matter, he identifies his body with his self and speaks as if his “possessions” were his to enjoy.

Maya, illusion, powerful as it is, can influence the tiny living entities but can never cover the Lord. The Bhagavatam ([2.7.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.47)) states, maya paraity abhimukhe ca vilajjamana: illusion flees from the Lord out of shame. Because maya is unable to stand in Krsna’s presence, those who keep themselves in Krsna’s presence can also keep maya at a distance. Thus to prevent oneself from falling into illusion and to cure the illusion one has, one should always remain under the soothing rays of Krsna’s mercy. Srila Krsnadasa Kaviraja describes this mercy in Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya [22.31-34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.31), as follows:

**Krsna is compared to sunshine, and maya is compared to darkness. Wherever there is sunshine, there cannot be darkness. As soon as one takes to Krsna consciousness, the darkness of illusion (the influence of the external energy) will immediately vanish. The external illusory energy of Krsna, known as maya, is always ashamed to stand in front of Krsna, just as darkness is ashamed to remain before the sunshine. However, that maya bewilders unfortunate people who have no intelligence. Thus they simply boast that this material world is theirs and that they are its enjoyers. One is immediately freed from the clutches of maya if he seriously and sincerely says, “My dear Lord Krsna, although I have forgotten You for so many long years in the material world, today I am surrendering unto You. I am Your sincere and serious servant. Please engage me in Your service.” \[Lord Rama says:\] “It is My vow that if one only once seriously surrenders unto Me, saying ‘My dear Lord, from this day I am Yours,’ and prays to Me for courage, I shall immediately award courage to that person, and he will always remain safe from that time on.”**

What knowledge will free one from the illusory perception of “I” and “mine”? Lord Brahma continues: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, and their interactions, which are set up by time, as well as the living entity’s material sense of identity, are all part of Lord Narayana’s external energy. They have no value if perceived as separate from Him. In his comment on this text (14), Srila Sridhara Svami states that Brahma has now answered one of Narada’s questions (from text 7) by explaining that it is the Lord who is above him as the supreme creator. Now Brahma explains that nothing can exist beyond the Lord. Srila Sridhara Svami adds that Lord Narayana, as the source of all scriptures, is omniscient, and Srila Jiva Gosvami explains that the demigods are worshipable as part of Lord Narayana’s universal body.

Thus Lord Brahma continues to describe the Lord, who is beyond him: The Vedic literature, the sacrifices they recommend, and the demigods are all meant to know and please Him. The planets are created for His pleasure. All meditation, mysticism, and austerities are meant to achieve Lord Narayana. “Culture of transcendental knowledge is for getting a glimpse of Narayana, and ultimately salvation is entering the kingdom of Narayana.” (Bhag. [2.5.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.16))

Srila Sridhara Svami explains that the question “How and why is Brahma creating?” will be answered by Brahma in the following text (17): “Inspired by Him only, I discover what is already created by Him \[Narayana\] under His vision as the all-pervading Supersoul, and I also am created by Him only.” Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 17 describes devotees, such as Lord Brahma, who act under the Lord’s inspiration and according to His desire:

**The Lord inspires the individual soul to create what is already created by the Lord, and by the good will of the Lord a discoverer of something in the world is accredited as the discoverer. It is said that Columbus discovered the Western Hemisphere, but actually the tract of land was not created by Columbus. The vast tract of land was already there by the omnipotency of the Supreme Lord, and Columbus, by dint of his past service unto the Lord, was blessed with the credit of discovering America. Similarly, no one can create anything without the sanction of the Lord, since everyone sees according to his ability. This ability is also awarded by the Lord according to one’s willingness to render service unto the Lord. One must therefore be voluntarily willing to render service unto the Lord, and thus the Lord will empower the doer in proportion to his surrender unto the lotus feet of the Lord. Lord Brahma is a great devotee of the Lord; therefore he has been empowered or inspired by the Lord to create such a universe as the one manifested before us. . . . Devotees like Brahma and Arjuna do not do anything on their own account, but as fully surrendered souls they always await indications from the Lord; therefore they attempt to do something which appears very wonderful to ordinary vision. One of the Lord’s names is Urukrama, or one whose actions are very wonderful and are beyond the imagination of the living being, so the actions of His devotees sometimes appear very wonderful due to the direction of the Lord.**

As Srila Prabhupada has explained, our conception of reality and our pleasures and accomplishments are direct gifts from Krsna and are awarded according to our purity. Both the pig and the gourmet desire to enjoy themselves through eating, and Krsna, as the Supersoul, reciprocates with each by awarding them—according to their individual piety—specific mentalities and suitable bodies. Therefore, persons will view an item differently and ascribe it value based on their various minds and bodies. That is, one will either see something as adorable or abominable according to his particular mentality. A mother will view her child’s corpse differently than a vulture would view it. The object is one, the child’s corpse, but Krsna has awarded each being a vision according to both desire and piety.

Srila Prabhupada continues: “In the Vedic writings such as the Katha Upanisad, the Lord is described as the sarva-bhuta-antaratma, or the Personality of Godhead who resides in everyone’s body and who directs everything for one who is a soul surrendered unto Him. Those who are not surrendered souls are put under the care of the material nature (bhramayan sarva'bhutani yantrarudhani mayayd); therefore, they are allowed to do things on their own account and suffer the consequences themselves.” Rather than remaining under the care of the material nature, devotees depend on the superior strength and vision of Krsna. An example can be offered to aid our understanding. A young boy tries to lift a heavy weight. His father assists the boy’s attempt, and his adult strength makes him the actual lifter. Similarly, a devotee’s attempt to please Krsna, like the attempt of a child to lift a weight, inspires Krsna to complete the task. Thus the ultimate doer is Krsna. Because devotees desire to please Krsna, acting only for His pleasure, they can accomplish wonders.

## Texts 18-33: Lord Brahma Describes the Creation

In texts 18-21, Lord Brahma describes the Lord’s activities as the prime mover of creation. In doing so, he first reveals the difference between the Lord (text 18) and the living entity (text 19): “The Supreme Lord is pure spiritual form, transcendental to all material qualities, yet for the sake of the creation of the material world and its maintenance and annihilation, He accepts through His external energy the material modes of nature called goodness, passion and ignorance.” (Bhag. [2.5.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.18)) Once activated, these modes manifest as matter (dravya), knowledge (jnana), and activities (kriya). The modes place the living entity, who is actually transcendental and eternal, under the conditions of cause and effect and make him responsible for his actions. The living entities’ actions are controlled, yet each remains responsible for his actions and their result due to his sense that he is the doer and that he can enjoy through his actions. This sense of false ego and doership allows maya, illusion, to bind the soul.

Illusion is so powerful that one is completely unaware that he is controlled. A young man may see a young woman and become enthralled by her beauty. Or perhaps he becomes absorbed in a new car. “Just imagine,” he thinks, “how wonderful it would be to drive that bright red car.” Maya has colored the young man’s vision and provided an illusory conception of the actual object. A glitter or glow almost seems to emanate from whomever or whatever attracts us. In time, however, the glow fades and the object assumes its true nature; it appears ordinary.

Again, what causes illusion is the living entity’s false sense of being the enjoyer, the doer. When he no longer wishes to enjoy matter, maya can no longer color his vision. Those who impulsively buy expensive cars, computers, or homes may chase the glitter and obtain a short-lived thrill, but then, as the illusion fades, they find themselves dealing with a mundane object rather than what they imagined they had purchased. The cause of the bewilderment? Both the living entity’s inappropriate enjoying spirit and Krsna’s illusory potency.

Srila Prabhupada further delineates the problem: “Factually, the living entities are not meant to be so conditioned by material energy, but due to their being affected by the false sense of lording it over the material energy, they come under the influence of such potency and thus become conditioned by the three modes of material nature. This external energy of the Lord covers up the pure knowledge of the living entity’s eternally existing with Him, but the covering is so constant that it appears that the conditioned soul is eternally ignorant. Such is the wonderful action of maya, or external energy manifested as if materially produced. . . . These are the material manifestations of cause and effect and the sense of responsibility of the conditioned actors. They are, after all, manifestations of the conditioned state, and the human being’s freedom from such a conditioned state is the highest perfectional attainment.” (Bhag. [2.5.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.19), purport)

Some attractions are foundational. The attraction between the male form and the female form is one such illusion. If one were to remove the thin layer of skin and analyze the truth beneath the surface, one would see only unattractive bones, blood, and organs. When that same form is covered, shaped, empowered by maya, and fueled by a spirit of enjoyment, however, one finds oneself attracted to it. When one passionately embraces such a form, he is in fact embracing maya, not a particular body. Indeed, the living entity’s attempt to enjoy matter is an attempt to achieve happiness by embracing illusion. Krsna’s maya forever covers, bewilders, and limits the consciousness of conditioned living entities. Brahma continues by describing the living entity’s plight as vastly different from the Lord’s position: “O Brahmana Narada, the Superseer, the transcendent Lord, is beyond the perception of the material senses of the living entities because of the above-mentioned three modes of nature. But He is the controller of everyone, including me.” (Bhag. [2.5.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.20))

Sridhara Svami states in his comment on this text that Narayana subdues illusion. Since He controls it, He can dispel it as the sun dispels morning fog. Thus by His potencies He creates the material manifestation and repeatedly places the living entities in it along with time (kalam), their karma, and their particular natures (svabhavam).

After describing the Creator’s supreme position, Brahma then summarizes (until the end of the chapter) how Krsna creates through His expansions and potencies (described in Bhag. [2.5.22-33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.22) ). Brahma explains: The first plenary expansion related directly to the material world is the first purusa-avatara, Karanadakasayi Visnu. In a comer of the spiritual sky (brahmajyoti) a “cloud” appears by Krsna’s will. That cloud is at first called pradhana and is later known as the mahat-tattva.

Prabhupada would at times refer to the “cloud” of the pradhana as the “water of the mahat-tattva,” or the causal ocean (Karana-jala), because this primal substance is the ingredient cause of everything in the material world. Prabhupada writes in his purport to Bhagavatam [2.5.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.33): “In a comer of the spiritual sky of brahmajyoti a spiritual cloud sometimes appears, and the covered portion is called the mahat-tattva. The Lord then, by His plenary portion as Maha-Visnu, lies down within the water of the mahat-tattva, and the water is called the Causal Ocean (Karana-jala). While Maha-Visnu sleeps within the Causal Ocean, innumerable universes are generated along with His breathing. These universes are floating, and they are scattered all over the Causal Ocean.”

Thus Karanadakasayi Visnu lies on the “waters” of the Causal Ocean and generates seedling universes with each breath. These universes are scattered as they float on the water, and remain until the great Visnu again inhales. Next, while lying within the pradhana (Causal Ocean), Karanadakasayi Visnu glances from a great distance at the pradhana, which begins to transform. It then comes to be known as the mahat-tattva. Due to the agitation caused by His glance (which contains time, the living entities, and their karma), false ego is produced and manifests in each of the three modes, goodness, passion, and ignorance. Gradually those forms of false ego transform further. The evolution of the universe continues by His potencies: matter evolves through His dravya-sakti, creative actions through His kriya-sakti, and the intelligence that guides materialistic activities through His jnana-sakti.

From false ego in the mode of ignorance, sky (ether) is generated along with the sense object sound. The air element is generated from sky along with its quality of touch. From air comes fire along with the sense object shape, and water is generated from fire along with taste. From water comes the element earth and the sense object fragrance. Each element contains within it all the sense objects previously generated.

False ego in the mode of goodness generates mind along with the demigods who control the directions. False ego in the mode of passion generates intelligence, prana (the life force), the five knowledgeacquiring senses (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin), and the five working senses (voice, legs, hands, anus, and genitals).

Within the scheme of universal creation, under the direction and through the energy of the Supersoul, these newly created parts are soon assembled into bodies according to what is deserved and appropriate for each conditioned soul. In an automobile factory, under the direction of a chief engineer, parts are designed, created, and assembled. After assembly, they await their new owners. According to their ability to pay, customers can then purchase the particular car they desire and enjoy whatever luxuries it may provide.

Similarly, according to what a living entity desires and deserves, bodies are assembled for specific souls under the supervision of maya. In his purport to text 32 Prabhupada compares souls in the material universes to children playing under a servant’s supervision: “Just as a father gives some playthings to the crying child to satisfy him, the whole material creation is made possible by the will of the Lord to allow the bewildered living entities to lord it over things as they desire, although under the control of the agent of the Lord. The living entities are exactly like small children playing the material field under the control of the maidservant of the Lord (nature). They accept the maya, or the maidservant, as all in all and thus wrongly conceive the Supreme Truth to be feminine (goddess Durga, etc.). The foolish, childlike materialists cannot reach beyond the conception of the maidservant, material nature, but the intelligent grown-up sons of the Lord know well that all the acts of material nature are controlled by the Lord, just as a maidservant is under the control of the master, the father of the undeveloped children.”

Krsna’s will and potency are continually required to further the creation; at no time can it proceed under its own power. Thus by the Lord’s grace, the creation is eventually completed and the embodied souls are able to engage in further conditioned activities.

## Texts 34-42: The Lord Enters Each Universe

Lord Brahma continues his explanation: The universes remain for thousands of years in the Causal Ocean. Then, by His desire, Lord Karanadakasayi Visnu further expands Himself into each universe. That expanded form of the Lord is known as Garbhodakasayi Visnu. To enter the heart of each living entity and each atom in existence, the Lord again expands Himself and becomes known as Ksirodakasayi Visnu. In this form, the Lord resides on the milk ocean present in each universe. This Lord, as the Supersoul and life of everything material and spiritual in existence, causes the universal form, the virat-rupa, to come into existence.

Prabhupada opens his purport to text 34 by saying that in this text, the Lord is called jiva because He is the leader of all other living entities, who are jivas. It is also interesting to note that Suka-deva Gosvami has earlier advised (Canto Two, Chapter One) those unable to accept the Lord’s transcendental form to conceive of Him in His expansion of the material energy, the virat-rupa. In text 36, Sukadeva has termed this method kalpayana, imaginary, because it more or less conceptualizes the Supreme as matter. Although materialists may derive benefit from thinking of the Lord in this way, this conception nevertheless limits the Lord, as if He were nothing more than the totality of matter. The Lord’s actual form can never be material, and therefore in his purports throughout the Second Canto, Prabhupada occasionally refers to the Lord’s universal form as imagination: “The virat universal form of the Lord is an imagination for the material world. It has nothing to do with the spiritual world, or the kingdom of God.” (Bhag. [2.5.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.39), purport)

Nor, as Srila Prabhupada explains, is the Lord’s real form ultimately formless: “So the universal form of the Lord is the secondary imagination of the impersonal form of the Lord, but the primary form of the Lord is Syamasundara, with two hands, playing on His eternal flute.” (Bhag. [2.6.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.17), purport)

However, we cannot say that the Lord’s universal form is fully imaginary, as if it did not exist. Bhagavatam [3.6.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/6.8) states: “The gigantic universal form of the Supreme Lord is the first incarnation and plenary portion of the Supersoul.” While commenting on Krsna’s disappearance from the world in his purport to Bhagavatam [3.4.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/4.29), Srila Prabhupada writes: “. . . He has His universal form, as manifested before Arjuna on the Battlefield of Kuruksetra. Here in this verse the word sphitam is also used, which indicates that He left His gigantic universal form called the virat-rupa, not His primeval, eternal form, because there is hardly any possibility of His changing His form of sat-cit-ananda.”

And in his purport to Bhagavatam [3.6.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/6.4) Srila Prabhupada makes the universal form’s position clear: “The virat-rupa or visva'tupa, the gigantic universal form of the Lord, which is very much appreciated by the impersonalist, is not an eternal form of the Lord. It is manifested by the supreme will of the Lord after the ingredients of material creation. . . . The virat-rupa is not, therefore, an eternal form of the Lord exhibited in the spiritual sky; it is a material manifestation of the Lord. The arcd'Vigraha, or the worshipable Deity in the temple, is a similar manifestation of the Lord for the neophytes. But in spite of their material touch, such forms of the Lord as the virat and area are all nondifferent from His eternal form as Lord Krsna.”

Krsna’s universal form serves the creation almost as a blueprint, positioning everything in the material world in its proper functional position. Thus Brahma continues to describe the universal form to Narada Muni: “The brahmanas represent His mouth, the ksatriyas His arms, the vaisyas His thighs, and the sudras are born of His legs.” (Bhag. [2.5.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.37)) The lower planetary systems are situated on His legs, the middle planetary systems on His navel, and the higher systems on His chest. The topmost planets are situated on the universal form’s head. Beyond this great form of the Lord, however, are the spiritual planets, which are the Lord’s abodes and which are eternal.

Sridhara Svami’s comments on Bhagavatam [2.5.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.39) confirm that the words brahmalokah sanatanah refer not to the Brahmaloka in the material world but to the Lord’s eternal abode in the spiritual world: In this verse the word brahmaloka refers to the eternal (sanatoria) Vaikuntha planets. Here the word brahmaloka does not refer to a planet in the created material universe. Rather it means “spiritual” (brahma) “planet” (loka).

Lord Brahma continues: Although people divide the planetary systems differently, the Lord’s universal form is filled with varieties of planetary systems. Thus everything in the material creation can be seen in relationship to the universal form.

## Chapter 6 - Purusa-sukta Confirmed

## Texts 1-22: The Lord, the Supreme Controller, is Himself Beyond the Virat-purusa

Narada Muni had asked Lord Brahma about the actual identity of the Supreme Lord and creator. Brahma thus described the sequence of creation, beginning with Karanadakasayi Visnu and Garbhodakasayi Visnu, which led to the manifestation of the universal form, the virat-rupa, also known as the universal person, the virat-purusa. Now continuing his response, Brahma recites his own prayers, which will support the conclusion of the Rg Veda’s purusa-sukta prayers, for Brahma’s words, like the texts of the purusa-sukta, ultimately glorify that person (Garbhodakasayi Visnu) who is the source of Lord Brahma and the universal form.

Brahma’s prayers begin by denoting the universal form as the source of everything in the world: The universal form’s mouth generates voice as well as its controlling demigod, fire (agni). The universal form’s tongue produces food as well as the source of the tasty delicacies meant for sacrificial offerings. His skin is the source of Vedic hymns. His nostrils generate our breathing, and His breathing produces fragrances. His eyes, which glitter and illuminate, generate forms, and His ears generate both the sky and sound. His skin generates touch, His bodily hair causes vegetation, specifically trees meant for sacrificial use, and His polished nails generate electricity. Clouds rest on the hair of His head. The arms of the universal form produce powerful demigods and leaders for the mass of people.

In his purport to Bhagavatam [2.6.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.6), Srila Prabhupada presses those who are powerful, the “leaders for the mass of people,” to attain peace of mind through devotional humility: “A sane person must know for certain that a living being, however powerful he may be, is neither absolute nor independent. All living beings must accept the origin of their specific power as mentioned in this verse. And if they act accordingly, then simply by discharging their respective occupational duties they can achieve the highest perfection of life, namely eternal life, complete knowledge and inexhaustible blessings. As long as the powerful men of the world do not accept the origin of their respective powers, namely the Personality of Godhead, the actions of maya (illusion) will continue to act. . . . The intelligent class of men, therefore, must admit the Lord as the ultimate source of all energies and thus pay tribute to the Lord for His good blessings. Simply by accepting the Lord as the supreme proprietor of everything, since He is actually so, one can achieve the highest perfection of life. Whatever a person may be in the estimation of the social order of things, if a person tries to reciprocate a feeling of love towards the Supreme Personality of Godhead and is satisfied with the blessings of the Lord, he will at once feel the highest peace of mind for which he is hankering life after life. Peace of mind, or in other words the healthy state of mind, can be achieved only when the mind is situated in the transcendental loving service of the Lord.”

Thus in this and subsequent texts Brahma points out that the qualities and abilities of all living entities are dependent on the universal form—and ultimately on the Lord. For example, one may draw on the potency of a medicinal herb to cure a disease, but it is the Lord’s universal form that supplies the herb with its medicinal potency. One’s ability to see depends on sunlight or electricity, which in turn depends on the universal form. One’s ability to see therefore depends on the Lord. Pride in one’s achievements or qualities is ludicrous, because whatever one has is dependent on another.

Lord Brahma continues: The Lord’s lotus feet serve as protection from all fear. In his purport to text 7 Srila Prabhupada offers brief but practical advice on how to achieve fearlessness: “For absolute protection from all sorts of fear, as well as for all our needs of life, we must take shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord, not only in this planet but also in all the upper, lower and heavenly planets. This absolute dependence on the lotus feet of the Lord is called pure devotional service, and it is directly hinted at within this passage.”

О Narada, Brahma continues, the Lord’s genitals cause the pleasure that counteracts the distressful encumbrances of begetting children. “The back of the Lord is the place for all kinds of frustration and ignorance, as well as for immorality. From His veins flow the great rivers and rivulets, and on His bones are stacked the great mountains.” (Bhag. [2.6.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.10)) His impersonal feature is the abode of great oceans, and in His belly rests all living entities during the period of universal annihilation. From His consciousness stem religious principles, truth, and transcendental knowledge.

The emphasis of Brahma’s words now shifts: All living beings, including myself, Lord Siva, you (Narada), and all living entities bom before and after you, as well as all the phenomenal manifestations such as stars, planets, lightning, and thunder, as well as all other varieties of living entities, rest in the Lord’s universal form, and have always done so in the past, do so in the present, and will continue to do so in the future. That transcendental Lord is “eternally existing in a form not exceeding nine inches. The sun illuminates both internally and externally by expanding its radiation; similarly, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by expanding His universal form, maintains everything in the creation both internally and externally.” (Bhag. [2.6.16-17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.16)) Srila Sridhara Svami comments that texts 14-16 show that the universe is not separate from the Supreme Person. These texts, he explains, contain what the Purusa'sukta confirms.

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to texts 13-16 underscores those texts’ philosophical implications: “Everything rests on the potency of Lord Sri Krsna, and still the Lord is different from and transcendental to all such identities. In the Vedic Purusa'sukta of the Rg mantra, this is also confirmed. This philosophical truth of simultaneous oneness and difference was propounded by Lord Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, and it is known as acintya-bhedahheda-tattva.”

This is Lord Brahma’s answer to Narada’s question about the identity of the universe’s ultimate creator, for in response he glorifies the source of the vastly powerful virat-purusa, the Supersoul who resides in everyone’s heart: He is the controller of immortality and fearlessness, and He is transcendental to death and the fruitive reactions that affect everyone in this material world. “O Narada, О brahmana, it is therefore difficult to measure the glories of the Supreme Person.” (Bhag. [2.6.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.18)) He is the supreme reservoir of all opulences in the world of matter. He causes deathlessness, fearlessness, and freedom from the anxieties of old age and disease for those residing in His kingdom. That “spiritual world, which consists of three fourths of the Lord’s energy, is situated beyond this material world, and it is especially meant for those who will never be reborn. Others, who are attached to family life and who do not strictly follow celibacy vows, must live within the three material worlds.” (Bhag. [2.6.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.20)) By His energies the Lord controls both the material and the spiritual worlds in all situations. He is the ultimate master of both ignorance and true knowledge. From Him have come all universes as well as the universal form and everything manifest from it.

“Yet He is aloof from such material manifestations, like the sun, which is separate from its rays and heat.” (Bhag. [2.6.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.22))

In his comment on text 21, Srila Jiva Gosvami states that in the material world, the Lord’s illusory energy (maya) dominates, whereas in the spiritual world the Lord’s internal energy (yogctrndyd) is in control.

Material existence causes fear, but the Lord awards His devotees the bliss of an anxiety-free life in the spiritual world. Srila Prabhupada’s purports to the above texts point readers to the Lord’s eternal service in the spiritual world. Here are a few relevant sections from his purport to text 18.

The material world is insignificant:

**In one of the universes, in which we are now living, the number of planets cannot be counted by human energy, and so how can we think of the sum total in all the universes, which are compared to a bucketful of mustard seeds?**

The spiritual world is greater and more wonderful than the world of matter:

**And the planets in the spiritual sky are at least three times the number of those in the material sky. . . . The conception of spiritual bliss (brahmananda) is fully present in those planets. Each of them is eternal, indestructible and free from all kinds of inebrieties experienced in the material world. Each of them is self-illuminating and more powerfully dazzling than (if we can imagine) the total sunshine of millions of mundane suns.**

The Lord’s devotees reside in the spiritual world. They are eternal and full of bliss:

**The inhabitants of those planets are liberated from birth, death, old age and diseases and have full knowledge of everything; they are all godly and free from all sorts of material hankerings. They have nothing to do there except to render transcendental loving service to the Supreme Lord Narayana, who is the predominating Deity of such Vaikuntha planets. . . . The Lord and His eternal servitors in the transcendental kingdom all have eternal forms which are auspicious, infallible, spiritual and eternally youthful. In other words, there is no birth, death, old age and disease. That eternal land is full of transcendental enjoyment and full of beauty and bliss.**

The following excerpts are from the purport to text 20.

To attain the spiritual world, we must become free from sex life:

**The highest benefit that can be awarded to a human being is to train him to be detached from sex life, particularly because it is only due to sex indulgence that the conditioned life of material existence continues birth after birth. Human civilization in which there is no control of sex life is a fourth-class civilization because in such an atmosphere there is no liberation of the soul encaged in the material body. Birth, death, old age and disease are related to the material body, and they have nothing to do with the spirit soul. But as long as the bodily attachment for sensual enjoyment is encouraged, the individual spirit soul is forced to continue the repetition of birth and death on account of the material body, which is compared to garments subjected to the law of deterioration.**

We should strictly follow the devotional principles regarding sex:

**The householders and persons who have deliberately broken the vow of celibacy cannot enter into the kingdom of deathlessness. The pious householders or the fallen yogis or the fallen transcen-dentalists can be promoted to the higher planets within the material world (one fourth of the energy of the Lord), but they will fail to enter into the kingdom of deathlessness. Abrhad'Vratas are those who have broken the vow of celibacy. The vanaprasthas, or those retired from family life, and the sannyasis, or the renounced persons, cannot break the vow of celibacy if they want success in the process.**

Lord Caitanya was strict in regard to celibacy:

**Lord Caitanya was very strict in advising His followers in this matter of celibacy. One of His personal attendants, Chota Hari-dasa, was severely punished by Lord Caitanya because of his failure to observe the vow of celibacy. For a transcendentalist, therefore, who at all wants to be promoted to the kingdom beyond material miseries, it is worse than suicide to deliberately indulge in sex life, especially in the renounced order of life. Sex life in the renounced order of life is the most perverted form of religious life, and such a misguided person can only be saved if, by chance, he meets a pure devotee.**

## Texts 23-33: Performing Sacrifice by Using the Creation in the Lord’s Service

Lord Brahma continues: After I was bom from the lotus flower growing from Lord Visnu’s abdomen, I wished to perform a sacrifice, but I saw only darkness. I felt perplexed. From in my heart I felt the inspiration to undergo austerity and to thereby acquire the needed sacrificial ingredients. But as the Lord is everything, what did I possess that could be sacrificed? By the Lord’s grace, I understood how to proceed and was thus able to obtain all the required ingredients from the bodily limbs of the Lord’s universal form.

Sacrifice is defined as surrendering or offering something of value for the sake of something or someone else. Sacrifice is the point of life; remaining selfish leaves one feeling unfulfilled and subject to the world’s condemnation. Those who sacrifice their lives for the welfare of others are universally honored. Still, one sees that it is the desire to take and exploit rather than to serve and sacrifice that dominates the times. Because of this, people feel loveless, lonely, dissatisfied, and impoverished in spirit.

Brahma’s inspiration to perform sacrifice was natural, and so was his dilemma. He saw clearly that nothing belonged to him. What then could he offer? He was dependent on the Lord to provide the ingredients for his sacrifice. Srila Prabhupada draws a parallel between Brahma’s predicament and our own in his purport to text 23: “While the impersonalist wrongly concludes that he is the Lord himself, the personalist, out of a great gratitude, worships the Lord in devotional service, knowing perfectly well that nothing is different from the Lord. The devotee therefore endeavors to apply everything in the service of the Lord because he knows that everything is the property of the Lord and that no one can claim anything as one’s own. This perfect conception of oneness helps the worshiper in being engaged in His loving service, whereas the impersonalist, being falsely puffed up, remains a nondevotee forever, without being recognized by the Lord.”

Srila Sridhara Svami instructs that texts 23-27 should be read together. Srila Jiva Gosvami suggests that the situation described by Lord Brahma took place before the creation, because the elements required for sacrifice didn’t yet exist. For sacrifice, Brahma thought, I require flowers, leaves, straw, an altar, and the proper time. I also require utensils, grains, ghee, honey, gold, earth, water, and each of the four Vedas along with qualified priests to recite them. Hymns must be sung and the names of demigods invoked.

After describing the components of sacrifice, Lord Brahma now explains to Narada the true purpose of sacrifice: After arranging all the necessary ingredients, he says, the priest invoked the names of the demigods and gradually, the ultimate goal, Visnu, was achieved. “Thus I created the ingredients and paraphernalia for offering sacrifice out of the parts of the body of the Supreme Lord, the enjoyer of the sacrifice, and I performed the sacrifice to satisfy the Lord.” (Bhag. [2.6.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.28))

Although it may superficially appear that the goal of Vedic sacrifice is to appease particular demigods, Lord Brahma clearly states that the actual goal is to please Krsna. Srila Prabhupada states: “Brahma, the original living being within the material world, taught us the way of sacrifice. The word ‘sacrifice’ suggests dedication of one’s own interests for satisfaction of a second person. That is the way of all activities. Every man is engaged in sacrificing his interests for others, either in the form of family, society, community, country or the entire human society. But perfection of such sacrifices is attained when they are performed for the sake of the Supreme Person, the Lord. Because the Lord is the proprietor of everything, because the Lord is the friend of all living creatures, and because He is the maintainer of the performer of sacrifice, as well as the supplier of the ingredients of sacrifices, it is He only and no one else who should be satisfied by all sacrifices. ... If men at all want peace in the world, they must practice sacrifice in the interest of the supreme proprietor and friend of all.” (Bhag. [2.6.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.28), purport)Why should one try to please Krsna through sacrifice? In a lecture given in Columbus, Ohio on May 9, 1969, Srila Prabhupada states that sacrifice and service to Krsna are natural for every honest soul:

**Don’t you see how God is supplying all the necessities of birds, beasts, and everyone? Ours also. We don’t acknowledge. Because we are “civilized,” ... we do not acknowledge. The birds, beasts also do not acknowledge, but because they are birds and beasts. So we are just becoming like birds and beasts, denying the existence of God, denying the authority of God.**

**We are taking advantage. If Krsna does not supply you this sunlight, you will die. He does not charge anything. But because you are human being, you should try to repay: “Oh, Krsna is giving us so much facilities. Let me render some service unto Him.” This is Krsna consciousness. It acknowledges, “O God, You are so kind. You are giving so many things. So I have collected this fruit. It is Your fruit, I know. Still, please accept.” This makes you a great devotee.**

Brahma tells Narada that after he performed the sacrifice and created the universe, Narada’s “nine brothers, who are the masters of living creatures, performed the sacrifice with proper rituals to satisfy both the manifested and nonmanifested personalities.” (Bhag. [2.6.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.29)) Afterwards, all others performed sacrifices with the aim of pleasing the Supreme Lord. Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 29 describes that the “manifested” personalities we are meant to please are the demigods, and the “nonmanifested” personality is the Lord Himself. “In this age of Kali the manifested demigods are also not to be seen, for space travel has completely stopped. So both the powerful demigods and the Supreme Personality of Godhead are nonmanifested to the covered eyes of the modem man. Modem men want to see everything with their eyes, although they are not sufficiently qualified. Consequently, they disbelieve in the existence of the demigods or of the Supreme God. They should see through the pages of authentic scriptures and should not simply believe their unqualified eyes. Even in these days, God can also be seen by qualified eyes tinged with the ointment of love of God.”

Brahma thus concludes his response to Narada’s question as to the identity of the ultimate universal power: “All the material manifestations of the universes are therefore situated in His powerful material energies, which He accepts self-sufficiently, although He is eternally without affinity for the material modes. By His will, I create, Lord Siva destroys, and He Himself, in His eternal form as the Personality of Godhead, maintains everything. He is the powerful controller of these three energies. My dear son, whatever you inquired from me I have thus explained unto you, and you must know for certain that whatever there is (either as cause or as effect, both in the material and spiritual worlds) is dependent on the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [2.6.31-33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.31))

Brahma, the most intelligent person, has thus explained the Lord’s position to Narada Muni. Srila Prabhupada restates Brahma’s instructions succinctly in his purport to text 31: “The material energy thus works under the supreme spell of His Lordship, although He is always transcendental to all such material activities. . . . He is not required to do anything personally, but everything in the material world is carried out by His wishes and direction; therefore, the entire material manifestation is situated in Narayana, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

The three functions of creation, maintenance, and destruction continue through the Lord’s material energies, and although He is aloof, He alone remains forever the all-powerful, supreme controller. No impersonal conception looms above Him. The Lord does everything through His different energies. Therefore He is called tri-sakti-dhrk, the controller of three energies (Bhag. [2.6.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.32)). In text 32, Brahma summarizes his reply to Narada about the identity of the soul of the universe: There is no truth above Him, and He is ultimately a person. The Supreme Personality of Godhead alone maintains both the material and spiritual universes. Everything in existence depends on Him, Krsna, the cause of all causes.

Srila Jiva Gosvami explains that text 32 confirms that both Brahma and Siva are subordinate to Visnu, the Supreme Lord. In Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 36, Sri Jiva Gosvami states that text 32 confirms Krsna’s performance of the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the material universes. He adds that this verse also teaches us that Lord Visnu is a direct manifestation of the Personality of Godhead and is thus essentially nondifferent from Sri Krsna’s transcendental form. That same Visnu is, therefore, different from Brahma and Siva, who are not direct manifestations of the Personality of Godhead but are of a different category.

In Krsna-sandarbha, anuccheda 43, Jiva Gosvami adds: We may note that the word purusa in the verse means “by Sri Krsna, the original Supreme Personality of Godhead.” This is confirmed in Brahma-samhita [5.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/39): krsnah svayam samabhavat paramah pumdn yah—Sri Krsna, the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, personally appeared as the various avataras.
