Lord Brahma described the Lord’s universal form in this and the previous chapter, and his descriptions have naturally ended with his glorification of the Lord. In Bhagavatam [6.16.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/16.25), Narada Muni repeats what he has learned from Brahma to Maharaja Citraketu and again teaches that the Lord is glorified by the prayers in the Purusa'sukta: “O transcendental Lord, who are situated in the topmost planet of the spiritual world, Your two lotus feet are always massaged by a multitude of the best devotees with their lotus-bud hands. You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, complete in six opulences. You are the supreme person mentioned in the Purusa'sukta prayers. You are the most perfect, self-realized master of all mystic power. Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto You.” Thus those who worship the Lord’s universal form ultimately worship Visnu, the soul and source of the universal form.

## Texts 34-38: Lord Brahma Glorifies Taking Shelter of the Lord

Lord Brahma next reveals the cause behind his own great power: “O Narada, because I have caught hold of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, with great zeal, whatever I say has never proved to have been false. Nor is the progress of my mind ever deterred. Nor are my senses ever degraded by temporary attachment to matter.” (Bhag. [2.6.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.34))

Srila Prabhupada tells of the power of devotion in his purport to this text: “The devotee’s senses, being engaged in the service of the Lord, never go astray under the attraction of false material enjoyment. The plans of the devotee never go in vain, and all this is due to the faithful attachment of the devotee for the service of the Lord. This is the standard of perfection and liberation. Anyone, beginning from Brahmaji down to the human being, is at once put on the path of liberation simply by his attachment in great earnestness for the Supreme Lord, Sri Krsna, the primeval Lord.”

Srila Prabhupada concludes: “Anyone, therefore, who is earnestly serious in heart and soul about being in intimate touch with the Personality of Godhead in the relationship of transcendental loving service will always be infallible in words and action. The reason is that the Supreme Lord is Absolute Truth, and anything earnestly dovetailed with the Absolute Truth attains the same transcendental quality. On the other hand, any amount of mental speculation on the strength of material science and knowledge without any bona fide touch with the Absolute Truth is sure to be a mundane untruth and failure, simply due to not being in touch with the Absolute Truth. Such godless, unfaithful words and actions, however materially enriched, are never to be trusted. That is the purport of this important verse. A grain of devotion is more valuable than tons of faithlessness.”

In his comment on text 34, Srila Jiva Gosvami states that the Supreme Being manifests Himself to those who possess unflinching devotion. In his comment on text 35, he underscores that the Lord does not manifest Himself to anyone, regardless of that person’s qualification, unless that person possesses devotion. Brahma was greatly qualified, but he understood how insignificant he was in comparison to the Lord: “Although I am known as the great Brahma, perfect in the disciplic succession of Vedic wisdom, and although I have undergone all austerities and am an expert in mystic powers and selfrealization, and although I am recognized as such by the great forefathers of the living entities, who offer me respectful obeisances, still I cannot understand Him, the Lord, the very source of my birth.” (Bhag. [2.6.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.35))

Brahma is able to know the Lord to some extent, but his method of acquiring knowledge does not rely on his own greatness. In his purport to text 35, Srila Prabhupada explains: “Brahmaji could understand the Lord to a little extent only when he was trying to serve Him by the eagerness of his heart (hrdautkanthyavata), which is the devotional service mood. . . . No one can know the Personality of Godhead in full, but at least to a certain extent one can know the Absolute Truth, the Personality of Godhead, by self-surrender and a devotional attitude, and by nothing else. In the Brahma'Samhita also, it is said, vedesu durlabham, or simply by study of Vedanta one can hardly find out the existence of the Personality of Godhead, but the Lord is adurlabham atma-bhaktau, very easily available to His devotee.”

What should one do when one realizes his fallibility and insignificance? Brahma continues: “Therefore it is best for me to surrender unto His feet, which alone can deliver one from the miseries of repeated birth and death. Such surrender is all-auspicious and allows one to perceive all happiness. Even the sky cannot estimate the limits of its own expansion. So what can others do when the Lord Himself is unable to estimate His own limits?” (Bhag. [2.6.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.36))

Srila Prabhupada’s powerful purport to Bhagavatam [2.6.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.36) criticizes those scientists who accept as reality only what their material intelligence and senses can perceive. To reciprocate with the mentality of these materialists, Krsna offers them only perceptions of His material energy. Srila Prabhupada underscores the inevitability of surrender for every soul: “The living entity, by his constitutional position, is not independent. He must surrender, either unto the Lord or unto material nature. Material nature is also not independent of the Lord, since the Lord Himself has claimed material nature as mama maya, or ‘My energy’ (Bg. [7.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.14)), and as me bhinna prakrtir astadha, or ‘My separated energy in eight divisions’ (Bg. [7.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.4)). . . . And the living entities, being superior energy to matter, have choice and discrimination either to surrender unto the Lord or to surrender unto material nature. By surrendering unto the Lord, one is happy and liberated, but by surrendering unto material nature the living entity suffers. So the end of all suffering means surrendering unto the Lord because the surrendering process itself is bhava'cchidam (liberation from all material miseries), svasty-ayanam (perception of all happiness), and sumangalam (the source of everything auspicious).”

In noting the Lord’s greatness, Brahma amazes us by stating that the Lord Himself is unable to know Himself fully or even to know the extent of His own happiness. In his purport, Srila Prabhupada discusses whether this “limitation” is truly a limitation, explaining that the Lord can actually measure His own happiness, but nevertheless, His happiness is ever-increasing. “So the happiness derived from the Lord may be measured by the Lord, but the happiness increases again, and the Lord measures it again, and then again the happiness increases more and more, and the Lord measures it more and more, and as such there is eternally a competition between increment and measurement, so much so that the competition is never stopped, but goes on unlimitedly ad infinitum.”

No one in existence—this is not only Brahma’s shortcoming— can fathom the Lord, the material world, or even the Lord’s plan: “Since neither Lord Siva nor you nor I could ascertain the limits of spiritual happiness, how can other demigods know it? And because all of us are bewildered by the illusory external energy of the Supreme Lord, we can see only this manifested cosmos according to our individual ability.” (Bhag. [2.6.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.37)) Srila Jiva Gosvami comments that here Brahma is describing his personal limitation: No one by his own power can know the Lord.

As Krsna, who is the all-knowing, is the only person who can perceive reality fully, all others see only according to their limited capacities. Naturally, the capacity of some souls exceeds that of others. In his purport to text 37, Srila Prabhupada traces the practical implications of this point: “Brahma, Narada and Lord Siva know about the Lord to a considerable extent, and therefore one should follow the instructions of these great personalities instead of being satisfied with a tiny brain and its playful discoveries such as spacecraft and similar products of science. As the mother is the only authority to identify the father of a child, so the mother Vedas, presented by the recognized authority such as Brahma, Narada or Siva, is the only authority to inform us about the Absolute Truth.”

Therefore, Lord Brahma concludes: “Let us offer our respectful obeisances unto that Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose incarnations and activities are chanted by us for glorification, though He can hardly be fully known as He is.” (Bhag. [2.6.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.38))

The unlimited Lord cannot be fully understood by any person by any means, but, as Lord Brahma has concluded, one should nevertheless surrender unto Him, offer Him obeisances, and glorify Him. Proportionate to one’s purity and surrender, and according to His own will, Krsna allows His devotees to know Him. Srila Prabhupada emphasizes these same points in his purport to text 38: “No one can know the Lord by any puffed-up material process of challenge, but the humble devotee can please the Lord by his earnest devotional activities. Thus the Lord reveals Himself proportionately before the devotee. Lord Brahma therefore offers his respectful obeisances as a bona fide spiritual master and advises us to follow the process of sravana and kirtana. . . . The conclusion is that one cannot know the Supreme Personality of Godhead fully by any method, but He can be seen and felt partially by the devotional service process of hearing, chanting, etc.”

## Texts 39-46: The Lord’s Incarnations

Narada Muni previously inquired from Lord Brahma (Bhag. [2.5.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.2)) about the creator and maintainer of the material world. Brahma’s reply allowed Narada to glimpse the Lord’s unfathomable power, and his conclusion assured Narada that an individual soul’s personal power, however great it may be, is insufficient to know God. In this way, Brahma directed Narada away from himself so that he would glorify and offer obeisances to the cause of all causes, the all-powerful person, the Supreme Lord: tasmai bhagavate namah. (Bhag. [2.6.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.38)). Text 39, Srila Sridhara Svami explains, begins Brahma’s description of the Lord’s deeds, especially as the first purusa-avatdra. He also comments as follows on the first line of the text, saying that here the activities of the avataras are briefly described. The phrase sa esa adyah refers to the primeval God, who as a purusa-avatara creates, maintains, and annihilates the material worlds.

Brahma continues his reply to Narada’s questions: That unborn Supreme Lord expands Himself into His unborn, plenary portion, Maha-Visnu, or Karanadakasayi Visnu, who then creates this manifest cosmos. The creation takes place in Him, and the material substance and manifestations, having come from Him, are therefore nondiffer-ent from Him. He maintains the entire creation for some time and then absorbs everything into Himself again. The Lord has no material tinge and is all-pervading and unrivaled. He can be known only when one is free of all material hankering. The Lord’s first incarnation, the first of the three purusa-avataras, is thus the source and substance of creation, yet He is separate and aloof from it. All that will ever exist in the material creation is various displays of His inconceivable personal energies. Attempts to understand Him by one’s own abilities and logical arguments, all of which will ultimately prove indefensible, only distort one’s perception of the Lord and further hide Him from one’s sight.

In his purport to texts 40-41, Srila Prabhupada shows how these texts attack impersonalist philosophy, which claims that all living entities are directly the Supreme Lord, although they have currently fallen into the illusion of forgetfulness. This slant on theism appears illogical, for the Lord, different from the jiva, has no tendency toward contamination or sin. Can common sense direct one to conclude that an all-powerful and ever-satisfied Supreme Lord, on whom all existence rests, who is the controller of His own illusory potencies, can fall into a degraded, miserable condition of life? Since Lord Brahma has again and again described the Lord’s unrivalled qualities, can the Lord be ultimately impersonal, devoid of qualities and characteristics? Casting aside the speculative method of understanding the Absolute Truth, Srila Prabhupada establishes in his purport the appropriate method for knowing Krsna: “Only the prasantas, or the unalloyed devotees of the Lord, can know Him to a greater extent. The reason is that the devotees have no demands in their lives but to be obedient servants of the Lord, while all others, namely the empiric philosophers, the mystics and the fruitive workers, all basically have some demand, and as such they cannot be pacified.”

Srila Sridhara Svami states that this text (42) and the subsequent texts of this chapter describe the chief components the Lord brings into being as He creates the material world in cycles. Srila Jiva Gosvami writes that it had been previously stated that the Lord manifested everything. Text 42, he says, offers more detail of that creation.

Lord Brahma continues: “Karanarnavasayi Visnu is the first incarnation of the Supreme Lord, and He is the master of eternal time, space, cause and effects, mind, the elements, the material ego, the modes of nature, the senses, the universal form of the Lord, Garbhodakasayi Visnu, and the sum total of all living beings, both moving and nonmoving.” (Bhag. [2.6.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.42)) The demigods and all other beings, both good and evil, “may appear to be the specific truth and the form of the Lord, but actually they are not so. They are only a fragment of the transcendental potency of the Lord.” (Bhag. [2.6.45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.45))

No powerful or opulent being, including Lord Brahma, is independent of the Lord. Everything in the creation rests on Him. Thus He alone is worshipable. Srila Prabhupada speaks of the merciful purpose behind the creation: “The material creation is but a temporary exhibition of the material energy of the Almighty God. This material manifestation is necessary to give a chance to the conditioned souls who are unwilling to associate with the Lord in the relationship of loving transcendental service. Such unwilling conditioned souls are not allowed to enter into the liberated life of spiritual existence because at heart they are not willing to serve. Instead, they want to enjoy themselves as imitation Gods. The living entities are constitutionally eternal servitors of the Lord, but some of them, because of misusing their independence, do not wish to serve; therefore they are allowed to enjoy the material nature, which is called maya, or illusion.... So the temporary creation of the material manifestation is an exhibition of the material energy of the Lord, and to manage the whole show the Supreme Lord incarnates Himself as the Karanarnavasayi Visnu just as a magistrate is deputed by the government to manage affairs temporarily.” (Bhag. [2.6.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.42), purport)

Thus by creating the material world, Krsna offers all souls an immense opportunity to change their self-conception from “I am meant to enjoy” to “I am meant to serve Krsna.” In addition to these “deputed” magisterial deeds of creation, the Lord personally displays His attractive pastimes in the material universes. When the Lord descends to reveal pastimes, we call these incarnations lild-avataras. According to the Bhagavatam, the lila-avataras are as numerous as the “waves of a river.” Lord Brahma’s concluding words in Chapter Six glorify hearing of the activities of these lila-avataras: “O Narada, now I shall state, one after another, the transcendental incarnations of the Lord known as lila-avataras. Hearing of their activities counteracts all foul matters accumulated in the ear. These pastimes are pleasing to hear and are to be relished. Therefore they are in my heart.” (Bhag. [2.6.46](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.46))

In his comment on this text, Srila Sridhara Svami explains that this text introduces the upcoming descriptions of the Lord’s incarnations as they descend into the material world. In his purport, Srila Prabhupada stresses the importance of hearing about the Lord:

**As it was said in the beginning of Srimad-Bhagavatam (**[**1.5.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/5.8)**), one cannot be fully satisfied by hearing unless and until one is given a chance to hear of the transcendental activities of the Lord. So Brahmaji is also trying, in this verse, to stress the importance of narrating the transcendental pastimes of the Lord as He comes and manifests Himself here on the surface of the material planets. Every living entity has a tendency to hear pleasing messages, and as such almost every one of us is inclined to hear news and talks broadcast by the radio stations. But the difficulty is that no one is satisfied at heart by hearing all those messages. The cause of such dissatisfaction is the incompatibility of the message with the innermost stratum of the living soul. This transcendental literature is especially prepared by Srila Vyasadeva to give the utmost satisfaction to the people in general by narration of the activities of the Lord, as instructed by Sri Narada Muni to Srila Vyasadeva. ... Srimad-Bhagavatam is the history of such activities of the Lord, and people who take interest in hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam clear their hearts of accumulated mundane filth. There are a thousand and one rash literatures on the market, but one who has taken interest in the Srimad-Bhagavatam loses all interest in such filthy literatures. Sri Brahmaji is thus attempting to narrate the principal incarnations of the Lord so that they may be drunk by Narada as transcendental nectar.**

## Chapter 7 - Scheduled Incarnations with Specific Functions

## Texts 1-25: Lord Brahma Describes Twenty Lila-avataras

This Bhagavatam chapter lists the three purusa-avataras as well as a number of lila-avataras and Their missions. It cannot list all the lila-avataras because innumerable incarnations of the Lord descend into each universe to perform wondrous pastimes. Details about the Lord’s many incarnations, such as each avatara’s father’s name or the village in which He takes birth, are recorded in sastra to protect the population from cheaters who try to pose themselves as God.

Sukadeva Gosvami continues his narration by explaining that Brahma spoke first to Narada about Lord Varaha, the Lord’s boar form who lifted the earth from the water-filled portion of the universe.

Interestingly, the Lord appeared from Brahma’s nostril. This is incredible to consider, but a simple feat for Him to perform, because by definition He is already present everywhere in each universe. After His appearance, Varahadeva grew, and through His beauty and pastimes attracted the watching sages, who, struck with wonder, offered Him Vedic prayers. The purified sages clearly declared that the Lord is always pure and transcendental regardless of the form in which He appears. This understanding is prepartory to appreciating Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose activties Brahma (in Bhag. [2.7.26-35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.26)) and Sukadeva (in Canto Ten) will describe. Indeed, Krsna’s activities, many of which appear humanlike (and this is especially true of His Vrndavana pastimes), are more easily misunderstood and thought of as mundane than the pastimes of Varahadeva, the unfathomably powerful gigantic boar who performed the incredible feat of lifting the earth and replacing it in its orbit.

Without understanding the Lord’s unlimited potency, and even with an inability to perform the same wonderful activities, foolish men may claim themselves God. Varahadeva, whom Srila Prabhupada describes in His purport to Bhagavatam [2.7.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.1), is far different from these “cheap incarnations”: “The Lord, as maintainer of the whole creation of the material world, therefore assumed the gigantic form of a boar with a proportionate snout and picked up the earth from within the water of Garbhodaka. Sri Jayadeva Gosvami, the great Vaisnava poet, sang as follows ... ‘O Kesava! О Supreme Lord who have assumed the form of a boar! О Lord! The planet earth rested on Your tusks, and it appeared like the moon engraved with spots.’... The modem creators of the many cheap incarnations may take note of the factual incarnation of God as the gigantic boar with a suitable snout to carry the planet earth.”

Brahma then tells Narada of the Lord’s other incarnations one after another—Suyajna, Kapila, Dattatreya (Datta, the son of Atri), the four Kumaras (Sanaka, Sanat-kumara, Sanandana, and Sanatana), the twin forms of Narayana and Nara, Prsnigarbha (the name of the Lord who appeared before Dhruva Maharaja), Maharaja Prthu, Rsabhadeva, Hayagriva, Matsya (the fish incarnation), Kurma (the tortoise incarnation), Nrsimhadeva (the half-man, half-lion incarnation), the savior of Gajendra (Hari), Vamanadeva, Hamsavatara, Manu, Dhanvantari, Parasurama, and Lord Ramacandra.

Srila Sridhara Svami mentions that the Suyajha incarnation created demigods and removed the world’s distress. About Vamanadeva he writes that the Lord took everything Bali Maharaja possessed (described in Canto Eight, chapters Fifteen through Twenty-three) on the pretext of begging. We would call a beggar greedy who took away all of a person’s wealth, especially if that included the person’s glory, but although Vamanadeva did temporarily take everything from Bali Maharaja, later He awarded Bali rulership over his own realm, and Vamanadeva Himself agreed to become his servant and doorman.

The Lord incarnated as Sri Rama to show that one should not try to enjoy the Lord’s energies the way Ravana attempted to enjoy Mother Sita. His energy is meant only for His service. Regardless what power one possesses, one’s pride will be vanquished unless he uses what he possesses to render the Lord service.In his purports to the first twenty-five verses of the chapter, Srila Prabhupada expands the information the texts offer about the Lord’s numerous appearances. In addition, he offers important instructions. I have mined ten gems from these purports:

**“The antiseptic potency of devotional service to the Lord is so great that it can neutralize the material infection even in the present life of a devotee. A devotee does not need to wait for his next birth for complete liberation.” (Bhag.** [**2.7.3**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.3)**, purport)**

**“A serious personality can thus achieve the highest perfection of meeting the Lord and attain his objective simply by being guided by a pure devotee, who automatically approaches by dint of one’s serious determination to meet the Lord by all means.” (Bhag.** [**2.7.8**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.8)**, purport)**

**“The whole process of yoga, under whatever heading it may be, is to control the unbridled material senses and thus prepare oneself for self-realization. . . . The simple method of hearing from the right source, Srimad-Bhagavatam, will lead one to the highest perfectional stage of yoga.” (Bhag.** [**2.7.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.10)**, purport)**

**“So we cannot deny the existence of the ocean of milk as stated in Srimad-Bhagavatam unless and until we have experimentally seen all the planets hovering in space. Since such an experiment is not possible, naturally we have to accept the statement of Srimad-Bhagavatam as it is because it is so accepted by spiritual leaders like Sridhara Svami, Jiva Gosvami, Visvanatha Cakravarti and others. The Vedic process is to follow in the footsteps of great authorities, and that is the only process for knowing that which is beyond our imagination.” (Bhag.** [**2.7.13**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.13)**, purport)**

**“Therefore a pure devotee is given first preference because of his full dependence, whereas the person who denies the existence of the Lord and declares himself the Lord is called asura, and as such he is given protection by the strength of limited power subject to the sanction of the Lord. Since the Lord is superior to everyone, His perfection is also superior. No one can imagine it.” (Bhag.** [**2.7.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.15)**, purport)**

**“People go to places of pilgrimage in order to be delivered from the reactions of unknown sinful acts. But one can be freed from all sinful reactions simply by remembering His holy name. The Lord is therefore as good as the holy places of pilgrimage. One can be free from all sinful reactions after reaching a place of pilgrimage, but one can have the same benefit at home or at any place simply by chanting the holy name of the Lord. For a pure devotee, there is no need to go to the holy place of pilgrimage. He can be delivered from all sinful acts simply by remembering the Lord in earnestness.” (Bhag.** [**2.7.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.15)**, purport)**

**“The Lord descends on this earth and acts like others in connection with the activities of the world just to create subject matters for hearing about Him; otherwise the Lord has nothing to do in this world, nor has He any obligation to do anything. He comes out of His own causeless mercy and acts as He desires. The Vedas and Puranas are full of descriptions of His different activities so that people in general may naturally be eager to hear and read something about His activities.” (Bhag.** [**2.7.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.15)**, purport)**

**“When the Lord snatches away one’s hard-earned material possessions and favors one with His personal transcendental service for eternal life, bliss and knowledge, such taking away by the Lord should be considered a special favor upon such a pure devotee.” (Bhag.** [**2.7.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.18)**, purport)**

**“The sane man knows that all material possessions are temporary and that the best use of such possessions is to engage them in the service of the Lord so that the Lord may be pleased with him and award him a permanent place in His param dhama.” (Bhag.** [**2.7.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.18)**, purport)**

**“To know exactly the permanency of spiritual existence, one must voluntarily practice possessing less or only the minimum to maintain one’s material existence without difficulty. One should not create artificial needs. That will help one be satisfied with the minimum.” (Bhag.** [**2.7.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.18)**, purport)**

Prabhupada also spoke about Krsna’s incarnations in a lecture given in Vrndavana on November 13, 1972:

**So the Supreme Personality of Godhead, lilavatara, incarnates in many forms, not only in the human society, but in the demigod society, or lower than human society, the animal society also, tree society. Because as we have forgotten our relationship with Krsna, He’s always anxious to get us back to home, back to Godhead. He has got ananta-rupa, unlimited forms. Advaitam acyutam anadim. But all those forms are in essence one. ... So at the present moment, the whole civilization is a set of rascals only. That’s all. There is no education. They do not know. And because they do not know, Krsna comes. Just to make these rascals, to inform that “I am,” Krsna says, “I am,” aham adir hi devanam. Aham sarvasya pra-bhavo mattah sarvam pravartate. Sarva-dharman parityajya mam ekam saranam vraja. Man-mana bhava mad-bhakto mad-yaji. Canvassing. Canvassing, “My dear sons, why you are rotting in this material world? Please come. You are My beloved son. I cannot tolerate that you are suffering.” This is Krsna’s business. He’s more kind. He’s more anxious to get us back. Therefore He comes personally. ... So Krsna is always anxious to give us enlightenment, that “This is not your life. Why are you rotting in this material world? Come back.”**

## Texts 26-38: The Advent of Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and the Advent of Vyasadeva, Buddha, and Kalki

Lord Brahma states: “When the world is overburdened by the fighting strength of kings who have no faith in God, the Lord, just to diminish the distress of the world, descends with His plenary portion. The Lord comes in His original form, with beautiful black hair. And just to expand His transcendental glories, He acts extraordinarily. No one can properly estimate how great He is.” (Bhag. [2.7.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.26)) To demonstrate that He was the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Krsna killed Putana when He was still on His mother’s lap and performed other wonderful pastimes while still a boy. He chastised the Kaliya serpent, saved His cowherd friends from a forest fire, and showed His mother that all the universes were in His mouth. He lifted Govardhana Hill, despite Indra’s anger, He danced with the gopis, and He killed many demons, like Sarikhacuda and others, either directly or indirectly through His brother Balarama or His friend Arjuna. Brahma concludes that no one but the Supreme Lord can act in such a superhuman way.

In his commentary on text 29, Srila Sridhara Svami states that Krsna performs karma-divyam, superhuman acts, to inspire our faith. Thus Krsna incarnates along with Balarama to demonstrate His wonderful pastimes. No one can estimate His greatness. His body is transcendental, and He comes not exactly to diminish the earth’s burden but to exhibit His transcendental activities. These activities create subjects for His pure devotees to discuss, because their only pleasure in life is to chant His glories.

In Krsna-sandarbha, anuccheda 63, Srila Jiva Gosvami comments as follows on texts 26 and 27: Now let us consider Lord Brahma’s statement from Bhagavatam [2.7.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.26). In this text, Brahma says, “The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is superior to everyone, including the allpervading Supersoul, and who cannot be perfectly understood by me or anyone else, will appear in this material world and perform many transcendental activities to lessen the earth’s burden.” Someone may raise the following doubt: If Sri Krsna is the original Personality of Godhead, superior even to the purusa incarnations, why does He descend to the material world to perform such an insignificant act as removing the earth’s burden?

To this Sri Jiva replies that Krsna did not descend for such an insignificant act. He could have removed the earth’s burden through His incarnations or simply by His desire. Lessening the earth’s burden does not require the Lord’s personal appearance. Rather, Sri Krsna appears to manifest His pastimes, which are filled with transcendental sweetness. He comes to delight the devotees, for the Lord’s lotus feet are dearer to them than life itself. He comes to shower transcendental sweetness on the world.

Some of these transcendental pastimes are described in text 27. Jiva Gosvami adds that if the Lord had not wished to charm and delight His devotees, He would not have personally performed beautiful activities while still a small child. This is the real reason He performed these pastimes, for it enables devotees to meditate on them.

Lord Brahma completes his description of the avataras by speaking briefly of Vyasadeva, Buddha, and Kalki. About Vyasadeva Brahma states: “The Lord Himself in His incarnation as the son of Satya-vati \[Vyasadeva\] will consider his compilation of the Vedic literature to be very difficult for the less intelligent persons with short life, and thus He will divide the tree of Vedic knowledge into different branches, according to the circumstances of the particular age.” (Bhag. [2.7.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.36)) In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada describes Vyasadeva’s greatest gift: “Herein Brahma mentions the future compilation of Srimad-Bhagavatam for the short-lived persons of the Kali age. As explained in the First Canto, the less intelligent persons of the age of Kali would be not only short-lived, but also perplexed with so many problems of life due to the awkward situation of the godless human society.... But the Lord, as the compassionate father of all living beings, imparts unto them the vast Vedic knowledge in short treatises like the Bhagavad-gita and, for the graduates, the Srimad-Bhagavatam.”

Commenting on this section of Srimad-Bhagavatam, Srila Sridhara Svami says that by the time Brahma and Narada had this conversation, some of the incarnations mentioned, such as Varahadeva, had already appeared, some were current, such as Dhanvantari and Parasurama, and some were yet to come, such as Ramacandra and Kalki.

## Texts 39-50: No Cause Exists Beyond Lord Hari

In speaking further about the ultimate cause of the universe, Lord Brahma says that things required at the beginning of creation (penance and the Prajapatis), during universal maintenance (demigods and kings), and at the time of universal destruction (when irreligion and atheists prevail) are a manifestation of the supremely powerful Lord’s energy. “Who can describe completely the prowess of Visnu? Even the scientist, who might have counted the particles of the atoms of the universe, cannot do so. . . . Neither I nor all the sages born before you know fully the omnipotent Personality of Godhead. So what can others, who are born after us, know about Him? Even the first incarnation of the Lord, namely Sesa, has not been able to reach the limit of such knowledge, although He is describing the qualities of the Lord with ten hundred faces.” (Bhag. [2.7.40—41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.40))

To inspire surrender to Krsna, Srila Prabhupada notes the unfathomable extent of Krsna’s energy in his purport to text 40: “The highest scientific advancement of the material scientists is atomic energy. But the material scientist is not able to have an estimation of the particles of atoms contained in the whole universe. But even if one is able to count such atomic particles or is able to roll up the sky like one’s bedding, even then one is unable to estimate the extent of the prowess and energy of the Supreme Lord.”

Sridhara Svami states that text 40 assures us that no one can completely describe what Brahma has described in brief. Brahma himself, what to speak of others, cannot even know the extent of the Supreme Lord’s illusory maya potency. Even Sesa, with his “ten hundred faces,” cannot describe the Lord’s glories. Sridhara Svami then asks: If no one can know the Supreme Lord’s incredible prowess, then how can His glories be described? He answers this question by saying that the Lord’s glories can be described when the Lord gives His grace to a person who sincerely and completely takes refuge at His feet.

In text 42, Brahma explains how the Lord may be known despite the fact that He is limitless: “Anyone who is specifically favored by the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead, due to unalloyed surrender unto the service of the Lord, can overcome the insurmountable ocean of illusion and can understand the Lord. But those who are attached to this body, which is meant to be eaten at the end by dogs and jackals, cannot do so.” Pure devotees can know the Lord’s glories in the sense that they understand both His personal greatness and the greatness of His diverse energies. Materialists, attached to bodies that will inevitably perish, remain covered by illusion and ignorance. Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 42 applies opposing qualities—an awareness of Krsna’s greatness and attachment to the body—as the criteria by which to judge the worth of a civilization: “Unless, therefore, one is saved from the wrong conception of the body and the soul, there is no knowledge of Godhead, and unless there is knowledge of God, all advancement of material civilization, however dazzling, should be considered a failure.”

Brahma has expressed to Narada his knowledge of the Lord as well as how he acquired that knowledge. Far from this knowledge being offered exclusively to Brahma, the most intelligent person in the creation, both knowledge of the unlimited Lord and knowledge of how to obtain that information have been liberally presented to everyone. Brahma states: “O Narada, although the potencies of the Lord are unknowable and immeasurable, still, because we are all surrendered souls, we know how He acts through yogamaya potencies. And, similarly, the potencies of the Lord are also known to the all-powerful Siva, the great king of the atheist family, namely Prahlada ...” and he goes on to list a number of devotees (in Bhag. [2.7.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.43)). “Surrendered souls, even from groups leading sinful lives, such as women, the laborer class, the mountaineers and the Siberians, or even the birds and beasts, can also know about the science of Godhead and become liberated from the clutches of the illusory energy by surrendering unto the pure devotees of the Lord and by following in their footsteps in devotional service.” (Bhag. [2.7.46](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.46))

In his commentary on text 46, Srila Sridhara Svami explains that Sukadeva Gosvami has listed quite a few names here to illustrate that many souls have come to know Krsna by His grace and by surrendering to Him in service. Indeed, anyone who becomes attached to Krsna can know the science of God.

In his commentaries on texts 23 and 47, written in Paramdtmd-sandarbha, anuccheda 90, Srila Jiva Gosvami writes that the Lord’s external potency, maya, is like a reflection; it does not touch the Supreme Lord directly. He then offers these two texts, 23 and 47, as illustrations of this point. In Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 171, he comments on text 46 that the only qualification to practice devotional service is faith. One does not need to practice renunciation. If somehow or other (yadrcchaya) someone associates with devotees, he will attain the Lord’s mercy and his life will become auspicious.

In his purport to Bhagavatam [2.7.43-45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.43), Srila Prabhupada writes: “The Lord is knowable only by one who is a surrendered soul. Herein Brahmaji, the greatest of all material living beings, acknowledges this truth. Therefore, the fruitless spoiling of energy by pursuing the path of experimental knowledge must be given up. One should gain knowledge by surrendering unto the Lord and by acknowledging the authority of the persons mentioned herein. The Lord is unlimited and, by the grace of the yogamaya, helps the surrendered soul to know Him proportionately with the advance of one’s surrender.” Srila Prabhupada’s wonderful purport to text 46 reveals that surrender is the essence of devotional life:

**The Personality of Godhead may not be present before one’s eyes, but if one is sincere in wanting such guidance the Lord will send a bona fide person who can guide one properly back home, back to Godhead. There is no need of material qualifications for making progress on the path of spiritual realization. In the material world, when one accepts some particular type of service, he is required to possess some particular type of qualification also. Without this one is unfit for such service. But in the devotional service of the Lord the only qualification required is surrender. Surrendering oneself is in one’s own hand. If one likes, he can surrender immediately, without delay, and that begins his spiritual life.**

While discussing surrender, Brahma offers a description of pure Krsna consciousness, in which one can realize the Absolute Brahman, who is only blissful and devoid of grief. That Supreme Lord is uncontaminated and is the ultimate cause. The illusory energy cannot stand before Him. In the transcendental state of consciousness in which one realizes Him, “there is no need of artificial control of the mind, mental speculation or meditation, as performed by the jnanis and yogis. One gives up such processes, as the heavenly king, Indra, forgoes the trouble to dig a well.” (Bhag. [2.7.48](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.48)) It is the Lord who awards reactions to the living entities for everything they have done both material and spiritual. He is thus the ultimate benefactor. Therefore everyone should worship Him to achieve their desired goals.

Srila Sridhara Svami comments on text 48 that nothing remains undone for the accomplished sages who have fixed their minds on the glorious Lord. Srila Jiva Gosvami comments that yoga and jfidna are abandoned for devotion to the Lord, who is the refuge of all knowledge. One requires no process but devotion. Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 48 speaks of devotional service as the perfection of life: “A poor man in want of water digs a well and undertakes the trouble of digging. Similarly, those who are poor in transcendental realization speculate on the mind or meditate by controlling the senses. But they do not know that such control of the senses and achievement of spiritual perfection are simultaneously made possible as soon as one is factually engaged in the transcendental loving service of the Supreme Person, the Personality of Godhead. It is for this reason that the great liberated souls also desire to be associated in hearing and chanting the activities of the Lord. The example of Indra is very appropriate in this connection. King Indra of heaven is the controlling deity or demigod for arranging clouds and supplying rains in the universe, and as such he does not have to take the trouble to dig a well for his personal water supply. For him, digging a well for a water supply is simply ludicrous. Similarly, those who are factually engaged in the loving service of the Lord have attained the ultimate goal of life, and for them there is no need of mental speculation to find out the true nature of God or His activities.”

To answer whether the soul retains its individuality after becoming situated in transcendence and its material karma is destroyed, Lord Brahma states: “Every individual living entity is unborn, and therefore even after the annihilation of the material elementary body, the living entity exists, exactly like the air within the body.” (Bhag. [2.7.49](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.49)) Underneath the coverings of good and bad karma, the individual eternal soul remains. With his karma removed, the pure devotee lives forever with Krsna.

“My dear son, I have now explained in brief the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is creator of the manifested worlds. Without Him, Hari, the Lord, there are no other causes of the phenomenal and noumenal existences.” (Bhag. [2.7.50](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.50))

Srila Sridhara Svami states that this text concludes the purport of the previous three chapters (Canto Two, chapters Five through Seven). Nothing is beyond Hari. But, Srila Sridhara Svami asks, if He is nondifferent from His creation and His creation is always changing, does that mean that He also changes? No, no change is possible in Him, because Lord Hari, although the creator of the material world, is nevertheless separate from His energy (the material world). Srila Prabhupada confirms this truth in his own purport to text 50 when he explains the sublime philosophy of acintya'bheddbheda-tattva taught by Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu: “Brahmaji explained to Naradadeva that this temporary world is the work of the external potency of the Lord and that the conditioned souls struggling here for existence are the marginal potency of the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead. There is no cause for all these phenomenal activities but Him, Hari, the Supreme Lord, who is the primeval cause of all causes. This does not mean, however, that the Lord Himself is distributed impersonally. He is aloof from all these interactions of the external and marginal potencies. In the Bhagavad-gita ([9.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.4)) it is confirmed that by His potencies alone He is present everywhere and anywhere. Everything that is manifested rests on His potency only, but He, as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is always aloof from everything. The potency and the potent are simultaneously one and different from one another.”

In addition, Srila Prabhupada explains why we should not fault the Lord for creating a miserable material world and then placing the living entities there: “One should not deprecate the Supreme Lord for the creation of this miserable world, just as one should not blame the king for creating a prisonhouse in the government. The prisonhouse is a necessary institution of the governmental establishment for those who are disobedient to the laws of the government. Similarly, this material world, full of miseries, is a temporary creation of the Lord for those who have forgotten Him and are trying to lord it over the false manifestation. He, however, is always anxious to get the fallen souls back home, back to Godhead, and for this He has given so many chances to the conditioned souls via the authoritative scriptures, His representatives, and personal incarnations also. Since He has no direct attachment to this material world, He is not to be blamed for its creation.” (Bhag. [2.7.50](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.50), purport)

## Texts 51 -53: Lord Brahma’s Request to Narada Muni

After giving Narada Muni knowledge, Brahma, Narada’s father and guru, gives him service: “O Narada, this science of God, Srimad-Bhagavatam, was spoken to me in summary by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and it was spoken as the accumulation of His diverse potencies. Please expand this science yourself.” (Bhag. [2.7.51](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.51)) Brahma indicates that he has already heard the Bhagavatam in its nutshell form directly from the Lord. After hearing it, he spoke it to Narada Muni, who in turn ordered Srila Vyasadeva to further expand it. In this fashion, the Bhagavatam’s pure message has reached us through the linked chain of disciplic teachers and not, as Srila Prabhupada states in his purport to text 51, “from the professional Bhagavatam reciters who earn their livelihood by gratifying the senses of the audience.”

Brahma then tells Narada the motive behind his order: “Please describe the science of Godhead with determination and in a manner by which it will be quite possible for the human being to develop transcendental devotional service unto the Personality of Godhead Hari, the Supersoul of every living being and the summum bonum source of all energies. The Lord’s activities in association with His different energies should be described, appreciated and heard in accordance with the teachings of the Supreme Lord. If this is done regularly with devotion and respect, one is sure to get out of the illusory energy of the Lord.” (Bhag. [2.7.52-53](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.52))

Humanity’s need in this sinful age of Kali is clear: People are blind to their relationship with God; they require true vision. Srila Prabhupada explains the Bhagavatam’s gift to humanity in his purport to text 52: ” . . . Srimad-Bhagavatam is so scientifically presented that any sincere student of this great science will be able to understand the science of God simply by reading it with attention or simply by regularly hearing it from the bona fide speaker. Everyone is hankering after happiness in life, but in this age the members of human society, blind as they are, do not have the proper vision that the Personality of Godhead is the reservoir of all happiness because He is the ultimate source of everything (janmddy asya yatah). Happiness in complete perfection without hindrance can be achieved only by our devotional relationship with Him. And it is only by His association that we can get free of distressful material existence. Even those who are after the enjoyment of this material world can also take shelter of the great science of Srimad-Bhagavatam, and they will be successful at the end. Narada is therefore requested or ordered by his spiritual master to present this science with determination and in good plan.”The Srimad-Bhagavatam is an incarnation of Krsna, and one will become enlightened and free from all distress simply by hearing it from proper sources in the proper order from beginning to end. Srila Prabhupada guides one how to hear the Bhagavatam in his final purport to this chapter:

**Those who are not completely free from the clutches of the Lord’s external energy should devoutly hear regularly about the activities of the Lord in relation with the external energy. They should not foolishly jump up to the activities of the internal energy, falsely attracted by the Lord’s internal potential activities like His rasadila. The cheap reciters of the Bhagavatam are very much enthusiastic about the Lord’s internal potential activities, and the pseudo-devotees, absorbed in material sense enjoyment, falsely jump to the stage of liberated souls and thus fall down deeply into the clutches of external energy.**

**Some of them think that to hear about the pastimes of the Lord means to hear about His activities with the gopis or about His pastimes like lifting the Govardhana Hill, and they have nothing to do with the Lord’s plenary expansions as the purusavataras and Their pastimes of the creation, maintenance or annihilation of the material worlds. But a pure devotee knows that there is no difference between the pastimes of the Lord, either in rasadila or in creation, maintenance or destruction of the material world. Rather, the descriptions of such activities of the Lord as the purusa' vataras are specifically meant for persons who are in the clutches of the external energy. Topics like the rasadila are meant for the liberated souls and not for the conditioned souls. The conditioned souls, therefore, must hear with appreciation and devotion the Lord’s pastimes in relationship with the external energy, and such acts are as good as the hearing of rasa-lild in the liberated stage. A conditioned soul should not imitate the activities of liberated souls. Lord Sri Caitanya never indulged in hearing the rdsaAila with ordinary men.**

**In the Srimad-Bhagavatam, the science of God, the first nine cantos prepare the ground for hearing the Tenth Canto. This will be further explained in the last chapter of this Canto. In the Third Canto it will be more explicit. A pure devotee of the Lord, there-fore, must begin reading or hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam from the very beginning, and not from the Tenth Canto. (Bhag.** [**2.7.53**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.53)**, purport)**

## Dialogue Three - The Lord Instructs Brahma

## Chapter 1 - Questions by King Pariksit

## Texts 1-6: Maharaja Pariksit Glorifies Srimad-Bhagavatam

Lord Brahma conclusively answered Narada Muni’s question about the Supreme Controller’s identity: “Without Him, Hari, the Lord, there are no other causes of the phenomenal and noumenal existences.” (Bhag. [2.7.50](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.50)) Brahma then revealed that the Lord had previously briefly instructed him about the science of God. Brahma wanted Narada to make the science of God available for the purification of humanity and therefore added: “Please expand this science yourself.”

Hearing this, Maharaja Pariksit asks Sukadeva: How did Narada Muni explain this science, which describes the Lord and His energies? To whom did he explain it? I wish to know, for narrations concerning the Lord, who possesses wonderful potencies, are certainly auspicious for living beings in all planets. Please narrate to me the auspicious Srimad-Bhagavatam so I can fix my mind on Lord Krsna, the Supreme Soul. Then, being completely free of material qualities, I will relinquish my body.

The Bhagavatam makes it clear in texts 2 and 3 of the Second Canto’s eighth chapter that Maharaja Pariksit poses so many questions in order to elicit descriptions of Krsna and pure devotional service. Nothing else interests the King; he simply wants to focus his mind on the Lord as he leaves this world.

Srila Prabhupada expands Sukadeva Gosvami’s description of the potency of hearing the Bhagavatam in his purport to text 2: “Srimad-Bhagavatam is certainly a very dear scripture for all the devotees of the Lord, but it is auspicious even for the nondevotees also because it explains that even the nondevotees hovering under the spell of material energy can be delivered from such clutches if they hear the narration of the Srimad-Bhagavatarn with devotion and attention from the right source representing the Lord by disciplic succession.” In his purport to text 3 he states: “To be fully engaged in hearing the transcendental narration described in the text of Srimad-Bhagavatam means to constantly associate with the Supreme Soul, Sri Krsna. And to constantly associate with the Supreme Lord Krsna means to be liberated from the qualities of matter. Lord Krsna is like the sun, and material contamination is like darkness. As the presence of the sun dissipates darkness, constant engagement in the association of the Lord Sri Krsna frees one from the contamination of the material qualities. . . . Maharaja Pariksit was destined to give up his body at the end of seven days, and thus he decided to continue remembering the Lord by His association with the topics of Srimad-Bhagavatam, and thus to quit his body in full consciousness of the presence of the Lord Sri Krsna, the Supreme Soul.”

Maharaja Pariksit glorifies the Bhagavatam in texts 4-6: “Persons who hear Srimad-Bhagavatam regularly and are always taking the matter very seriously will have the Personality of Godhead Sri Krsna manifested in their hearts within a short time. The sound incarnation of Lord Krsna, the Supreme Soul \[i.e., Srimud-Bhagavatam\], enters into the heart of a self-realized devotee, sits on the lotus flower of his loving relationship, and thus cleanses the dust of material association, such as lust, anger and hankering. Thus it acts like autumnal rains upon pools of muddy water. A pure devotee of the Lord whose heart has once been cleansed by the process of devotional service never relinquishes the lotus feet of Lord Krsna, for they fully satisfy him, as a traveler is satisfied at home after a troubled journey.”

In his commentary on text 4, Sridhara Svami explains that one who hears about the Supreme Lord with devotion need not exert himself to attain the Lord’s grace. In his purport to text 5 Prabhupada speaks of a pure devotee’s power not only to cleanse his own heart but to deliver the entire world from mdya’s clutches. How can one attain such purity? Prabhupada writes: “By sincere efforts to hear Srimad-Bhagavatam one realizes his constitutional relationship with the Lord in the transcendental humor of servitude, friendship, paternal affection or conjugal love, and by such self-realization one becomes situated at once in the transcendental loving service of the Lord. Not only were all the pure devotees like Narada self-realized souls, but they were engaged in preaching work automatically by spiritual impetus, and thus they delivered many poor souls entangled in the material modes. They became so powerful because they sincerely followed the Bhagavatam principles by regular hearing and worshiping. By such actions the accumulated material lusts, etc., become cleansed by the personal endeavor of the Lord within the heart. The Lord is always within the heart of the living being, but He becomes manifested by one’s devotional service.”

A pure soul accepts with a devotional spirit even the difficulties he encounters while preaching the Bhagavatam's message. Those difficulties ultimately make him glorious, because they highlight the selflessness of his devotion: “\[D\]ifficulties are very gladly suffered by the devotees in preaching because in such activities, although apparently very severe, the devotees of the Lord feel transcendental pleasure because the Lord is satisfied. Prahlada Maharaja suffered greatly, but still he never forgot the lotus feet of the Lord. This is because a pure devotee of the Lord is so purified in his heart that he cannot leave the shelter of Lord Krsna in any circumstances. There is no self-interest in such service.” (Bhag. [2.8.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.6), purport)

Just a year before leaving this world, Prabhupada spoke strongly about how one should view difficulties:

**Just like Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s teaching—yugayitam nimesena caksusa pravasayitam sunyayitam jagat-sarvam. We have got practical experience. If somebody’s beloved has died, he sees everything as zero. Nothing is appealing to him. Similarly, if we have developed our love for Krsna and if we do not see Krsna, that is sunyayitam jagat'Sarvam govinda-virahena me. But a devotee and ordinary person are different. If an ordinary person wants to see something and he cannot, he becomes angry because that is ката. A devotee says that “Krsna, although the whole world is vacant because I cannot see You, still I cannot change my mind to love You.” One side sunyayitam jagat-sarvam, the other side, aslisya va padaratam pinastu mam marma-hatam karotu va adarsanam. “You break my heart by not allowing me to see You. Still You are my beloved, worshipable Lord.” That is the difference. There is no disappointment. Disappointment is there, but although he may have broken heart, still he wants to love Krsna. That is pure love. Not that “I have been disappointed, my heart is broken; therefore I give up Krsna.” No. Still Krsna is good. That is pure love. (Lecture, November 27, 1976, Vrndavana)**

## Texts 7-23: Maharaja Pariksit Inquires Further

Maharaja Pariksit has listened carefully to Sukadeva Gosvami’s words. Now thinking deeply, the king inquires further: How does the soul, who is transcendental, acquire a material body? Is this accidental or due to some cause? If the Lord assumes a gigantic body as He did as Garbhodakasayi Visnu, what is the difference between His body and the bodies of common living entities? Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on text 7 that Maharaja Pariksit is inquiring about the differences between how the law of cause and effect works on the Lord’s body and on the bodies of ordinary jivas. On one level, the depth of Maharaja Pariksit’s questions reveals his probing mind and his eagerness to understand both the Absolute Truth and the processes by which the Absolute Truth works in the material and spiritual worlds. On another level, Maharaja Pariksit’s questions reveal how intensely interested he is in hearing about Krsna. His many questions spring from keen desire. This reveals the glorious nature of a spiritually inquisitive mind.

The King continues: Is Brahma’s body, which is bom directly from the Lord’s body, of the same quality as the Lord’s body? Please explain the Supersoul in everyone’s heart. Where are the planets and the universal governors positioned in the virat-rupa? Please also explain how much time passes between creation and annihilation, the nature of time itself, and the life spans of the demigods and humans on the various planets. Please explain how the different modes of nature act on living beings. How are the planets and their inhabitants created, maintained, and annihilated? How are they recreated after entering the Lord’s body at the time of destruction? Please describe the universe’s extent and measurement, the character of great souls, and the distinguishing characteristics of each of the varnasrama orders. How long does each age last? What activities does each of the Lord’s incarnations perform? What religious principles should the distressed follow? Kindly describe the elementary principles of creation and how to acquire mystic powers. What is the ultimate realization of great mystics? How does a perfect mystic become detached from his subtle (astral) body? What knowledge do the Vedas actually teach? What are the advantages and disadvantages of practicing bhakti-yoga! How

do infidels appear in this world? How do unconditioned living entities exist? The Lord enjoys His pastimes in the world by His internal potency, yet He renounces those pastimes when He departs. Although He witnesses everything, He remains aloof. Please explain this also.In his purports to the above texts, Srila Prabhupada both glorifies devotional service to Krsna and instructs his readers. I have included seven of his most powerful instructions from this section below:

**The spiritual master must also be well versed and learned so that he may be able to answer all these inquiries from the devotees. Thus one who is not well versed in the authorized scriptures and not able to answer all such relevant inquiries should not pose as a spiritual master for the matter of material gain. It is illegal to become a spiritual master if one is unable to deliver the disciple. (Bhag.** [**2.8.7**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.7)**, purport)**

**Those who are of the opinion that the devotees of the Lord are satisfied with mere sentiments can find in the inquiries of Maharaja Pariksit good lessons as to how inquisitive a pure devotee is to know things in their true perfection. (Bhag.** [**2.8.16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.16)**, purport)**

**The Lord descends by His internal energy without any obligation to the laws of material nature, and thus His activities are also uncommon. The specific activities of the Lord are mentioned, and one should know that the activities of the Lord and the Lord Himself are identical due to being on the absolute plane. Thus to hear the activities of the Lord means to associate with the Lord directly, and association with the Lord directly means purification from material contamination. (Bhag.** [**2.8.17**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.17)**, purport)**

**People following the principles of devotional service to the Lord can never be put into difficulty, and thus there cannot be any question of apad'dharma, or religion in distress. As will be explained in this book by the greatest authority, Srila Sukadeva Gosvami, there is no religion save and except the devotional service of the Lord, though this may be presented in different forms. (Bhag.** [**2.8.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.18)**, purport)**

**At the time of Draupadi’s precarious position, when she was attacked by the Kurus who wanted to see her naked in the open assembly of the royal order, the Lord saved her from being stripped by supplying an unlimited length of sari to cover her. And Draupadi knew nothing of mystic powers. Therefore the devotees are also yogesvaras by the unlimited power of the Lord, just as a child is powerful by the strength of the parents. They do not try to protect themselves by any artificial means, but are saved by the mercy of the parents. (Bhag.** [**2.8.20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.20)**, purport)**

**Living the conditional life is just like plying a boat in the middle of the ocean. One is completely at the mercy of the ocean, and at every moment there is every chance of being drowned in the ocean by slight agitation. If the atmosphere is all right, the boat can ply very easily, undoubtedly, but if there is some storm, fog, wind or cloud, there is every possibility of being drowned in the ocean. No one can control the whims of the ocean, however one may be materially well equipped. One who has crossed the oceans by ship may have sufficient experience of such dependence upon the mercy of the ocean. But one can ply over the ocean of material existence by the grace of the Lord very easily, without any fear of storm or fog. It all depends on the will of the Lord; no one can help if there is some unfortunate danger in the state of conditional life. The devotees of the Lord, however, cross the ocean of material existence without anxiety because a pure devotee is always protected by the Lord (Bg.** [**9.13**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.13)**). The Lord gives special attention to His devotees in their activities within material, conditional life (Bg.** [**9.29**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.29)**). Therefore everyone should take shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord and be a pure devotee of the Lord by all means. (Bhag.** [**2.8.21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.21)**, purport)**

**The favorable conditions for discharging devotional service are that one should be very enthusiastic in serving the Lord. The Lord in His form of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu wanted the cult of devotional service to the Lord to be preached all over the world, in every nook and comer, and therefore a pure devotee’s duty is to discharge this order as far as possible. Every devotee should be very enthusiastic, not only in performing his daily rituals of devotional service, but in trying to preach the cult peacefully by following in the footsteps of Lord Caitanya. If he is not superficially successful in such an attempt, he should not be deterred from the discharge of his duty. Success or failure has no meaning for a pure devotee because he is a soldier in the field. Preaching the cult of devotional service is something like declaring war against materialistic life. (Bhag.** [**2.8.21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.21)**, purport)**

## Texts 24-26: Maharaja Pariksit’s Humble Request, and Sukadeva Gosvami Begins His Reply

The king asks: О great sage, representative of the Lord, please answer all my inquiries. Since I am a soul surrendered unto you, please impart full knowledge unto me. О learned brahmana, because of my drinking the nectar of the message of the infallible Personality of Godhead, which is flowing down from the ocean of your speeches, I do not feel any exhaustion even though I am fasting.

In relation to this text (26), Sridhara Svami asks how it was possible for Maharaja Pariksit to hear about Krsna with such concentration even though he was fasting and no doubt disturbed by the curse. This verse answers the question: It was possible for him to concentrate because pibato ’cyuta-piyusa, he was drinking the nectar of the infallible Lord’s messages. Sukadeva Gosvami is pleased to hear Maharaja Pariksit’s questions because they prompt him to glorify Krsna. He therefore answers Pariksit systematically, although not in the same order the questions were asked. “And,” as Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 29, “he answered all of them without exception.”

Sukadeva Gosvami begins by telling Maharaja Pariksit that the science of God was first spoken by Lord Krsna to Lord Brahma just after Brahma’s birth. This is the same science that Brahma asked Narada Muni to expand on in Bhagavatam [2.7.51](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.51).

## Chapter 9 - Answers by Citing the Lord’s Version

## Texts 1-3: The Relationship Between the Eternal Soul and his Material Body

Sukadeva Gosvami responds first to the question Maharaja Pariksit asked (Bhag. [2.8.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.7)) about the pure soul’s acquisition of a material body: Does he acquire it accidentally or by some cause? Sukadeva explains the illusory relationship between body and soul: “O King, unless one is influenced by the energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, there is no meaning to the relationship of the pure soul in pure consciousness with the material body. That relationship is just like a dreamer’s seeing his own body working.” (Bhag. [2.9.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.1)) The living entity truly has no relationship with his material body, and thus the questions of “how” and “when” never arise. Under maya’s influence, the living entity wishes to rule and exploit Krsna’s material energy and is therefore offered a dreamlike facility—a material body in the material world. Both body and material energy are reflections of spiritual reality. This is similar to how a child crying for the moon is handed a mirror by which he can catch the moon’s reflection. The living entity dreams of “I and mine.” Ultimately, when the living entity becomes purified, he reawakens to his natural position as a lover of Krsna.

Srila Prabhupada takes the discussion further in his purport to this text: “Now the next question automatically made will be why the Lord influences the living entity to such consciousness and forgetfulness. The answer is that the Lord clearly wishes that every living entity be in his pure consciousness as a part and parcel of the Lord and thus be engaged in the loving service of the Lord as he is constitutionally made; but because the living entity is partially independent also, he may not be willing to serve the Lord, but may try to become as independent as the Lord is. All the nondevotee living entities are desirous of becoming equally as powerful as the Lord, although they are not fit to become so. The living entities are illusioned by the will of the Lord because they wanted to become like Him. Like a person who thinks of becoming a king without possessing the necessary qualification, when the living entity desires to become the Lord Himself, he is put in a condition of dreaming that he is a king. Therefore the first sinful will of the living entity is to become the Lord, and the consequent will of the Lord is that the living entity forget his factual life and thus dream of the land of utopia where he may become one like the Lord.”Srila Prabhupada also spoke on this text in 1972 in Tokyo, Japan:

**Svapna-drastur ivanjasa. The very exact example is given, svapna~ drastuh. Just like a man seeing in a dream: “Oh, there is tiger, tiger, tiger, tiger! Save me!” He is crying. Another man is viewing him, thinking, “Where is the tiger? Why you are crying?” But in the dream he is actually feeling: “The tiger has attacked me.” Therefore this example is given, na ghrtetartha-sambandhah. There cannot be any meaning of this relationship except that it is like a man dreaming, and in that dream he creates a fearful situation.**

**Actually there is no cause of fear. There is no tiger. That situation is created within a dream. Similarly we have created this material world and its activities. People are identifying that “Oh, I am the manager. I am the factory owner. I am this, I am that. We have got his politics. We have to defeat such competitors.” All these are created exactly like that, svapna-drastur ivanjasa, just like a man is creating his particular situation simply by dream. That’s all.**

**When somebody asks you that “When has the living entity come in contact with material nature?” So the answer is that he has not come in contact. He is thinking that he is in contact due to the influence of the external energy. Just like the same example: A man is dreaming; there is no contact with a tiger. Actually he has no contact with that. Similarly, actually we are not fallen. We cannot be fallen. Try to understand. It is a very important point. We have simply created a situation. Rather, we have not created a situation, but Krsna has given us a situation. Because we wanted to imitate Krsna, so Krsna has given an opportunity: “All right. Imitate. You want to be imitation king on the stage. So feel like this. Play like this. Do like this. People will applaud. ‘Oh, a very nice king, very nice.’”**

**So everyone in this material world, they are playing some part. They wanted, “I want to be prime minister.” “All right.” “I want to become very big business magnate.” “I want to be leader.” “I want to be a philosopher.” “I want to be a scientist.” So all this nonsense, they are trying to play—Krsna is giving him the opportunity: “All right.” But it is a nonsense, all nonsense. Simply dreaming. Next moment when the dream is gone, everything is finished. No more tiger, no more jungle. Everything is finished. Similarly, so long this body is continuing, I am thinking, “I am a responsible leader, I am this, I am that.” But as soon as this body is finished, all these are gone. It is just like dream. Actually we are not fallen. Therefore, because we are not fallen, at any moment we can revive our Krsna consciousness. As soon as we understand, “I have nothing to do with this. I am simply Krsna’s servant. Eternal servant. That’s all,” immediately he becomes liberated.**

**Sometimes we do that. When the fearful dreaming becomes too much intolerable, we break the dream. We break the dream when it becomes intolerable. Similarly, we can break this material connection at any moment as soon as we come to the point of Krsna consciousness. “Oh, Krsna is my eternal master. I am His servant.” That’s all. This is the way. Actually we are not fallen. There cannot be any fallen. The same example: Actually there is no tiger; it is dreaming. Similarly, our fallen condition is also dreaming. We are not fallen. We can simply give up that illusory condition at any moment. At any moment. So if you study all these verses very nicely, you get all this knowledge quickly.**

Sukadeva Gosvami continues, for he wishes to explain the eternal soul’s fate after it has been cast into the Lord’s illusory energy to fulfill his “utopian” dream of overlordship: “The illusioned living entity appears in so many forms offered by the external energy of the Lord. While enjoying in the modes of material nature, the encaged living entity misconceives, thinking in terms of ‘Г and ‘mine.’” (Bhag. [2.9.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.2)) The illusioned living entity appears in one physical form after another, each offered by the Lord’s external energy. While attempting to gain pleasure from the body, the living entity, trapped by the modes of nature, misconstrues the body as the self and everything the body contacts as his own, meant only for his self-centered pleasure.

What happens when an entrapped soul is somehow freed from illusion’s grip? “As soon as the living entity becomes situated in his constitutional glory and begins to enjoy the transcendence beyond time and material energy, he at once gives up the two misconceptions of life \[I and mine\] and thus becomes fully manifested as the pure self.” (Bhag. [2.9.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.3))

Sridhara Svami states that this text shows that the living entity can renounce illusion and attain the ultimate bliss by practicing devotion. Srila Prabhupada’s purports to texts 2 and 3 expand on this idea: “The living entity creates his own body by his personal desires, and the external energy of the Lord supplies him the exact form by which he can enjoy his desires to the fullest extent. The tiger wanted to enjoy the blood of another animal, and therefore, by the grace of the Lord, the material energy supplied him the body of the tiger with facilities for enjoying blood from another animal. Similarly, a living entity desiring to get the body of a demigod in a higher planet can also get it by the grace of the Lord. And if he is intelligent enough, he can desire to get a spiritual body to enjoy the company of the Lord, and he will get it. So the minute freedom of the living entity can be fully utilized, and the Lord is so kind that He will award the living entity the same type of body he desires.” (Bhag. [2.9.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.2), purport)

Srila Prabhupada defines the false concept of “mine” as animalistic. He says we can perceive this consciousness “even in the category of cats and dogs, who fight with one another with the same misconception . . .” (Bhag. [2.9.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.3), purport) He then defines the misconceived understanding of “I” as a full identification of ourselves as the Supreme: “I am” or “It is all I am.” About this misconception Srila Prabhupada states: “The misconception of ‘I am the Lord,’ or ‘I am the Supreme,’ is more dangerous than the misconception of ‘mine.’” Earlier in the purport he states, “But the real significance of T can be realized only when one is situated in the consciousness of ‘I am the eternal servitor of the Lord.’ This is pure consciousness, and the whole Vedic literatures teach us this conception of life.” (Bhag. [2.9.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.3), purport)

How can we become free of such misconceptions and again situated in our constitutionally glorious position? Prabhupada continues:

**So the science of bhakti-yoga, of worshiping the Lord, glorifying the Lord, hearing the Srimad-Bhagavatam from the right sources (not from the professional man but from a person who is Bhag-avatam in life) and being always in the association of pure devotees, should be adopted in earnestness. One should not be misled by misconceptions of “I” and “mine.” . . . The perfect process is to accept Lord Vasudeva as the Supreme in everything, and the best perfection in culturing knowledge is to surrender unto Him because He is the source of everything. Only in that conception can one get rid of the misconception of I and mine. Both Bhagavad-gita and the Srimad-Bhagavatam confirm it. Srila Vyasadeva has specifically contributed to the illusioned living entities the science of God and the process of bhakti-yoga in his great literature Srimad-Bhagavatam, and the conditioned soul should fully take advantage of this great science.**

## Texts 4-18: The Lord Reveals Vaikuntha to Brahma

In Bhagavatam [2.8.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.8), Maharaja Pariksit asked about the difference between the Lord and the jiva. Srila Sridhara Svami restates the question in his commentary on this text: In the eighth chapter of this Canto, Maharaja Pariksit asked, “If the Supreme Lord has a material body, then how is it that the devotees become liberated simply by serving and worshiping the Supreme Lord’s material body?” Maharaja Pariksit also asked if there was any difference between the Lord’s body and the bodies of conditioned souls. Sri Jiva replies in Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 46: This question is answered in Bhagavatam [2.9.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.4). In this verse, the phrase atma-tattva-visuddhy-artham means that the Lord purifies the conditioned souls and bestows on them transcendental knowledge. From this we may conclude (and here, Jiva Gosvami cites Sridhara Svami’s commentary) that the external form of the conditioned living entity is a manifestation of the Supreme Lord’s material illusory potency. The Lord’s form, on the other hand, is not manifest by the material potency but by the Lord’s own spiritual potency known as yogamaya. Because the Supreme Lord’s form is spiritual in nature, the devotees attain liberation by worshiping that form.

In answer to Maharaja Pariksit’s question, Sukadeva will now speak about dtma-tattva, the science of God and the living entity, Paramatma and jivatma. Suta Gosvami will also continue the instructions he began in Bhagavatam [2.8.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.28), where he stated, “The science of the Personality of Godhead \[the Bhagavatam\] was spoken first by the Lord Himself to Brahma when he was first bom.” Suta narrates Sukadeva Gosvami’s words to Maharaja Pariksit as follows: “O King, the Personality of Godhead, being very much pleased with Lord Brahma because of his nondeceptive penance in bhakti-yoga, presented His eternal and transcendental form before Brahma. And that is the objective goal for purifying the conditioned soul.” (Bhag. [2.9.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.4))
