Because the Lord appeared before Brahma, Srila Prabhupada writes in his purport, Brahma lost all misconceptions about both Paramatma and jivatma: “The wrong conception of the jivatma is to identify the material body with the pure soul, and the wrong conception of Paramatma is to think Him on an equal level with the living entity.... Srila Sukadeva Gosvami therefore says that for purification of both wrong conceptions, the Lord presented His eternal form before Brahmaji, being fully satisfied by Brahma’s nondeceptive vow of discharging bhakti-yoga. . . . Brahma was then told by the Lord the gist of Srimad-Bhagavatam in four original verses.” Srila Sridhara Svami comments that this text indicates that Brahma gained his spiritual knowledge by the Lord’s grace.

Now as a prelude to describing the Lord’s transcendental abode, Sukadeva Gosvami continues: “Lord Brahma, the first spiritual master, supreme in the universe, could not trace out the source of his lotus seat, and while thinking of creating the material world, he could not understand the proper direction for such creative work, nor could he find out the process for such creation.” (Bhag. [2.9.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.5)) Lord Brahma found himself unable to understand how to do the work he had been assigned. He then heard two vibrated syllables, ta pa, which, when joined, denoted penance and austerity, the wealth of those in the renounced order.

“When he heard the sound, he tried to find the speaker, searching on all sides. But when he was unable to find anyone besides himself, he thought it wise to sit down on his lotus seat firmly and give his attention to the execution of penance, as he was instructed.” (Bhag. [2.9.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.7))

Brahma could not find a speaker because at that time, he was the only created being. What else could he do but follow the instruction of those two syllables? Because his vision was pure, he correctly surmised that the Supreme Lord Himself was instructing him. Brahma, greatest of ascetics, then controlled his mind and senses and underwent a thousand celestial years of austerity. He thus satisfied the Personality of Godhead. The Lord then appeared to Brahma and revealed His personal abode, Vaikuntha, which is beyond illusion and is adored by all self-realized persons.

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 6 offers more detail: “When Lord Brahma was perplexed about how to construct the material manifestations in the universe and went down within the water to find out the means and the source of his lotus seat, he heard the word tapa vibrated twice. Taking the path of tapa is the second birth of the desiring disciple. . . . Thus Brahma was initiated by the Krsna mantra, by Lord Krsna Himself, and thus he became a Vaisnava, or a devotee of the Lord, before he was able to construct the huge universe. It is stated in the Brahmasariihita that Lord Brahma was initiated into the eighteen-letter Krsna mantra, which is generally accepted by all the devotees of Lord Krsna.”

In his purport to text 8 Srila Prabhupada describes the reason why Brahma was successful: “One should be qualified enough to discern such transcendental potency, and either by discriminating or by fortunate chance if one is able to receive the transcendental sound from the bona fide spiritual master, his path of liberation is guaranteed. The disciple, however, must be ready to execute the order of the bona fide spiritual master as Lord Brahma executed the instruction of his spiritual master, the Lord Himself. Following the order of the bona fide spiritual master is the only duty of the disciple, and this completely faithful execution of the order of the bona fide spiritual master is the secret of success.”

Prabhupada notes in his purport to text 9 that because Brahma was able to see Vaikuntha, it is obvious that his penance was performed as bhakti-yoga. “Otherwise, there was no chance that Vaikuntha or sva-lokam, the Lord’s personal abodes, would become visible to Brahma)!.”

Sukadeva Gosvami will now describe the spiritual world. His descriptions will begin negatively. That is, he will describe what Vaikuntha is not, and how, therefore, its qualities, of which we have no direct experience, contrast with the qualities of the material realm. In this way, the known world can aid our understanding of the spiritual world: “In that personal abode of the Lord, the material modes of ignorance and passion do not prevail, nor is there any of their influence in goodness. There is no predominance of the influence of time, so what to speak of the illusory, external energy; it cannot enter that region. Without discrimination, both the demigods and the demons worship the Lord as devotees.” (Bhag. [2.9.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.10)) Although as one reads these descriptions he should contemplate the superiority of the spiritual realm, while one is in the material mayic realm, he should know that he is actually unable to fathom the spiritual world. In Bhagavat' sandarbha, anuccheda 10, Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on the pure goodness (sattva) in Vaikuntha.

The material mode of goodness, which is invariably mixed with the lower modes of passion and ignorance, does not exist in Vaikunthaloka. Only the spiritual mode of goodness, known as suddha'sattva, which is completely free from the touch of the illusory energy, maya, exists in the spiritual realm.

How, then, can a conditioned soul limited by the illusory energy know of the spiritual realm except by hearing realized descriptions of it? Srila Jiva states further that in text 10, the phrase na yatra maya (“there is no predominance of the external illusory energy”) is like an ax cutting at the root of the conception that the material modes or material time have influence in Vaikuntha. The phrase kim utapare (“what to speak of’) reinforces the statement made in this verse: In Vaikunthaloka, the material energy has no influence.

Sri Jiva then poses a possible objection to this statement: The three modes of material nature have no influence in Vaikuntha, but those modes are the origin of variety. Wouldn’t it be logical, therefore, to assume that there is no variety in Vaikuntha? Sri Jiva writes: Because someone may raise this objection, Srila Sukadeva Gosvami goes on to describe the varieties present in the Lord’s transcendental potency known as suddhasattva that prevail in the Vaikuntha planets. This description begins with the word hareh, “of the Personality of Godhead,” in text 10.

Next, Sukadeva Gosvami provides a positive description of the spiritual world. He has already explained that there are no misery-causing elements in the spiritual world. For example, time, the great destroyer, has no effect at all in Vaikuntha. He now tells us that the inhabitants of Vaikuntha have complexions as blue as the sky. Their eyes resemble lotus flowers, and their clothes are brilliant yellow. They are youthful, have four hands, and are decorated with pearl necklaces. All are effulgent, some like coral and others like diamonds. “The Vaikuntha planets are also surrounded by various airplanes, all glowing and brilliantly situated. These airplanes belong to the great mahatmas or devotees of the Lord. The ladies are as beautiful as lightning because of their celestial complexions, and all these combined together appear just like the sky decorated with both clouds and lightning.” (Bhag. [2.9.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.13)) The goddess of fortune lovingly serves the Lord’s lotus feet while singing His glories.

In Vaikuntha, Lord Brahma saw the Supreme Personality of Godhead leaning favorably toward His loving servitors. His smiling face was an enchanting reddish hue. He wore earrings, a helmet, possessed four hands, and His chest was marked with the lines of the goddess of fortune. Surrounded by His different energies, He sat on His throne as He enjoyed His own abode.

The Lord’s leaning favorably toward His devotees is further described in Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya [24.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/24.42):

*aisvarya-madhurya-karunye svarupa-purnata*  
*bhakta-vatsalya, atma-paryanta vadanyata*

**Krsna’s transcendental qualities of opulence, sweetness and mercy are perfect and full. As far as Krsna’s affectionate leaning toward His devotees is concerned, He is so magnanimous that He can give Himself to His devotees.**

Srila Prabhupada’s purports to these Bhagavatam texts describe both Vaikuntha and the Lord of Vaikuntha. Here is a sampling:

**The whole Vaikuntha existence proclaims that everyone there is a follower of the Lord. The Lord is the chief leader there, without any competition for leadership, and the people in general are all followers of the Lord. (Bhag.** [**2.9.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.10)**, purport)**

**There are some inhabitants who have attained the liberation of sdrupya, or possessing bodily features like those of the Personality of Godhead. (Bhag.** [**2.9.12**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.12)**, purport)**

**So also when we see the Lord we see Him with His different energies, associates, confidential servitors, etc. So the Supreme Lord, who is the leader of all living entities, the Lord of all devotee sects, the Lord of all opulences, the Lord of sacrifices and the enjoyer of everything in His entire creation, is not only the Supreme Person, but also is always surrounded by His immediate associates, all engaged in their loving transcendental service to Him. (Bhag.** [**2.9.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.15)**, purport)**

About the Lord of Vaikuntha Himself: “The Supreme Lord, by His own potency, is unlimitedly more powerful than any yogi, He is unlimitedly more learned than any jnani, He is unlimitedly richer than any wealthy person, He is unlimitedly more beautiful than any beautiful living being, and He is unlimitedly more charitable than any philanthropist. He is above all; no one is equal to or greater than Him. Nor can anyone reach His level of perfection in any of the above powers by any amount of penance or yogic demonstrations. The yogis are dependent on His mercy. Out of His immensely charitable disposition He can award some temporary powers to the yogis because of the yogi’s hankering after them, but to His unalloyed devotees, who do not want anything from the Lord save and except His transcendental service, the Lord is so pleased that He gives Himself in exchange for unalloyed service.” (Bhag. [2.9.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.17), purport)

Srila Jiva Gosvami shows in his commentary on text 18 that the Lord is all-powerful because He is not dependent on anyone in any way; no one can have more opulence or power than He has.Srila Prabhupada describes the path Brahma took that brought him to perfection and suggests we follow a similar path:

**Following in the footsteps of Lord Brahma, any person, even up to this day, can attain the same perfection by following the path of the paramahamsa as recommended herein. Lord Caitanya also approved of this method of self-realization for men in this age. One should first, with all conviction, believe in the Personality of Godhead Sri Krsna, and without making efforts to realize Him by speculative philosophy, one should prefer to hear about Him from the Srimad Bhagavad-gita and later from the text of the Srimad-Bhagavatam. One should hear such discourses from a person Bhagavatam and not from the professional man, or from the karmi, jnani or yogi. That is the secret of learning the science. One does not need to be in the renounced order of life; he can remain in his present condition of life, but he must search out the association of a bona fide devotee of the Lord and hear from him the transcendental message of the Lord with faith and conviction. That is the path of the paramahamsa recommended herein. Amongst various holy names of the Lord, He is also called ajita, or one who can never be conquered by anyone else. Yet He can be conquered by the paramahamsa path, as practically realized and shown by the great spiritual master Lord Brahma. Lord Brahma has personally recommended this paramahamsa-panthah in his own words as follows:**

***jnane prayasam udapasya namanta eva***  
***jivanti san-mukharitam bhavadiya-vartam***  
***sthane sthitah sruti-gatam tanu-vah-manobhir***  
***ye prayaso ’jita jito ’py asi tais tri-lokyam***

**Lord Brahma said, “O my Lord Krsna, a devotee who abandons the path of empiric philosophical speculation aimed at merging in the existence of the Supreme and engages himself in hearing Your glories and activities from a bona fide sadhu, or saint, and who lives an honest life in the occupational engagement of his social life, can conquer Your sympathy and mercy even though You are ajita, or unconquerable.” (Bhag.** [**10.14.3**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.3)**) That is the path of the paramahamsas, which was personally followed by Lord Brahma and later recommended by him for attaining perfect success in life. (Bhag.** [**2.9.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.18)**, purport)**

And as Srila Prabhupada states in his purport to text 19: “Anyone, however, preaching the mission of the Lord in the line of the Brahma-sampradaya is always dear to the Lord, and the Lord, being satisfied with such a preacher of the authorized bhakti cult, shakes hands with him in great satisfaction.”

## Texts 19-30: The Lord Expresses His Pleasure to Brahma, and Brahma. Inquires from the Lord

Lord Brahma was overwhelmed with joy, and his eyes filled with tears of love as he bowed before his Lord. The Lord saw Brahma present before Him and accepted him as worthy to create on His behalf. Satisfied with Brahma, the beautiful Personality of Godhead shook his hand and, smiling slightly, said: О Brahma, I am pleased with the long penances you executed to please me. I know you desire to create the universe for My pleasure, and I wish you all fortune. О Brahma, you may ask from Me, the giver of all benediction, all that you desire. You may know that the ultimate benediction, as the result of all penances, is to realize Me. You have achieved the highest perfection of perceiving My abode, because you have maintained a submissive attitude while performing severe penance according to My order.

In texts 19-24, the Lord explains that one can achieve Him by penance performed in proper consciousness. To perform penance means to accept hardship in order to achieve a future goal. Penance is usually reserved for atonement, and it is performed to right a wrong one has committed. That type of penance may be performed to remove the reaction to a sinful act or to induce an offended person to forgive. When one performs such penance, however, one’s personal interests remain central. Brahma’s concept of penance was different. He performed penance to gain the power to create the material world for Krsna’s pleasure. For Brahma, Krsna’s pleasure was central, and he did not consider as important the difficulties he underwent to secure Krsna’s pleasure. Thus his penance was devotional. Devotional penance like Brahma performed is Krsna’s heart and soul. “Anything, at any cost, to please Krsna” is the motto of those who perform this type of penance. To surrender on such a high level requires purity, and Brahma’s attitude and purity evoked Krsna’s mercy on him.

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on the Lord’s shaking Brahma’s hand (text 19) in Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 10 as follows: One may raise the following objection: “Brahma is merely the creator of the material universes and is insignificant in comparison to the Personality of Godhead, the greatest of the great. I do not think it is possible for Brahma to have a direct relationship with the Supreme Lord.” He then responds to this doubt: In text 19, Sukadeva Gosvami described the Supreme Lord’s intense love for His devotees.

Why was Brahma able to see the Lord’s abode? Srila Sridhara Svami states in his commentary on text 22 that it was by the Lord’s grace, not on the strength of Brahma’s austerities.

Srila Prabhupada explains that the perfection Brahma achieved is available to all: “The highest perfectional stage of life is to know the Lord by actual perception, by the grace of the Lord. This can be attained by everyone who is willing to discharge the act of devotional service to the Lord as enjoined in the revealed scriptures that are standard and accepted by the bona fide acaryas, spiritual masters ... In Bhagavad-gita the Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, asks that one always be mindful of Him, always be His devotee, always worship Him only, and always bow down before the Lord. And by doing so one is sure to go back home, back to Godhead, without any doubt. In other places also the same order is there, that one give up all other engagements and fully surrender unto the Lord without hesitation. And the Lord will give such a devotee all protection. These are the secrets of attaining the highest perfectional stage. Lord Brahma exactly followed these principles without any superiority complex, and thus he attained the highest perfectional stage of experiencing the abode of the Lord and the Lord Himself with all His paraphernalia.” (Bhag. [2.9.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.22), purport)

The Lord continues to speak to Brahma: “O sinless Brahma, you may know from Me that it was I who first ordered you to undergo penance when you were perplexed in your duty. Such penance is My heart and soul, and therefore penance and I are nondifferent.” (Bhag. [2.9.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.23)) It was Krsna who first vibrated the syllables ta and pa and thus ordered Brahma to undergo penance when he was perplexed. The Lord creates the cosmos by penance and maintains and withdraws it by the same energy. “Therefore the potential power is penance only.” (Bhag. [2.9.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.24)) Ultimately, as it was in Brahma’s case, the penance to which the Lord is referring is action performed for His pleasure—devotional service.

Srila Prabhupada addresses the need to perform penance while practicing devotional service: “In executing penance, one must be determined to return home, back to Godhead, and must decide to undergo all types of tribulations for that end. Even for material prosperity, name and fame, one has to undergo severe types of penance, otherwise no one can become an important fig ure in this material world. Why, then, are there severe types of penance for the perfection of devotional service? An easygoing life and attainment of perfection in transcendental realization cannot go together. The Lord is more clever than any living entity; therefore He wants to see how painstaking the devotee is in devotional service. The order is received from the Lord, either directly or through the bona fide spiritual master, and to execute that order, however painstaking, is the severe type of penance. One who follows the principle rigidly is sure to achieve success in attaining the Lord’s mercy.” (Bhag. [2.9.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.24), purport)

Lord Brahma replies to the Lord by asking several questions: “O Personality of Godhead, You are situated in every living entity’s heart as the supreme director, and therefore You are aware of all endeavors by Your superior intelligence, without any hindrance whatsoever. In spite of that, my Lord, I am praying to You to kindly fulfill my desire. May I please be informed how, in spite of Your transcendental form, You assume the mundane form, although You have no such form at all. \[This is the first question.\] And \[please inform me\] how You, by Your own Self, manifest different energies for annihilation, generation, acceptance and maintenance by combination and permutation. \[This is the second question.\]” (Bhag. [2.9.25-27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.25)) That is, how does God manifest various energies and combine and transform them for universal creation, maintenance, and annihilation? Brahrna wants the Lord to explain these points philosophically, and states that the Lord possesses infallible determination. The Lord, he says, is playing like a spider that covers itself by its own web, its own potency.

Brahma’s third question states: “Please tell me so that I may be taught in the matter by the instruction of the Personality of Godhead and may thus act instrumentally to generate living entities, without being conditioned by such activities.” (Bhag. [2.9.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.29)) Brahma wants to create not of his own accord but as an instrument of the Lord’s will. In this way he can successfully complete his service of creating the universe and the living entities without becoming contaminated by the idea that he himself is “the doer.”

“O my Lord, the unborn,” Brahma begins his fourth question, “You have shaken hands with me just as a friend does with a friend \[as if equal in position\]. I shall be engaged in the creation of different types of living entities, and 1 shall be occupied in Your service. I shall have no perturbation, but I pray that all this may not give rise to pride, as if I were the Supreme.” (Bhag. [2.9.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.30))

In summary, Brahma asks the Lord about His inconceivable relationship with His energies. As Srila Prabhupada notes in his purport to text 27: “In other words, there is nothing but the Lord, and still the Lord is different from all such manifestive activities.” Srila Prabhupada also states in his purport to the following verse (text 28): “The exact example is the spider and spider’s web. The web is created by the spider, and it is maintained by the spider, and as soon as the spider likes, the whole thing is wound up within the spider. The spider is covered within the web. If an insignificant spider is so powerful as to act according to its will, why can’t the Supreme Being act by His supreme will in the creation, maintenance and destruction of the cosmic manifestations? By the grace of the Lord, a devotee like Brahma, or one in his chain of disciplic succession, can understand the almighty Personality of Godhead eternally engaged in His transcendental pastimes in the region of different energies.”

In his purport to text 30, Srila Prabhupada underscores a second issue that Brahma addresses, one that is relevant to all who attempt to perform devotional service for the Lord’s pleasure: “Devotees of the Lord are engaged in the specific duty offered by the Lord, and such duties are successfully carried out without hindrance because they are ordained by the Lord. The credit of success goes not to the doer but to the Lord. But persons with a poor fund of knowledge take the credit of success into their own accounts and give nothing to the credit of the Lord. That is the symptom of the nondevotee class of men.”

## Texts 31-37: The Lord’s Replies to Brahma (Including the Catuh-sloki Bhagavatam, Texts 33-36)

The Personality of Godhead then describes the knowledge He plans to reveal to Brahma:

*jnanam parama-guhyam me*  
*yad vijnana-samanvitam*  
*sarahasyam tad-angam ca*  
*grhana gaditam maya*

**Knowledge about Me as described in the scriptures is very confidential, and it has to be realized in conjunction with devotional service. The necessary paraphernalia for that process is being explained by Me. You may take it up carefully. (Bhag.** [**2.9.31**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.31)**)**

In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada summarizes Brahma’s four questions and introduces the four seed verses of the Bhagavatam the Lord is about to speak:

**Lord Brahma is the topmost devotee of the Lord within the universe, and therefore the Personality of Godhead replied to his four principal inquiries in four important statements, which are known as the original Bhagavatam in four verses. These were Brahma’s questions: (1) What are the forms of the Lord both in matter and in transcendence? (2) How are the different energies of the Lord working? (3) How does the Lord play with His different energies? (4) How may Brahma be instructed to discharge the duty entrusted to Him? The prelude to the answers is this verse under discussion, wherein the Lord informs Brahma that knowledge of Him, the Supreme Absolute Truth, as it is stated in the revealed scriptures, is very subtle and cannot be understood unless one is self-realized by the grace of the Lord. The Lord says that Brahma may take the answers as He explains them. This means that transcendental knowledge of the absolute Supreme Being can be known if it is made known by the Lord Himself.**

Srila Jiva Gosvami (Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 95) paraphrases text 31 as follows: In this verse the Lord says, “Please accept this transcendental Vedic knowledge that I, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, am speaking to you. Others do not possess this knowledge.” The words parama-guhyam here mean, “This knowledge is most confidential—more confidential than the knowledge of impersonal Brahman.” That this is so is confirmed in the following words from Bhagavatam [6.14.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/14.5): “O great sage, among many millions who are liberated and per feet in knowledge of liberation, one may be a devotee of Lord Narayana, or Krsna. Such devotees, who are fully peaceful, are extremely rare.” In addition, as Sri Jiva explains in the same Sandarbha and anuccheda, the Lord has hinted in this text at the four topics He will present to Brahma in Bhagavatam [2.9.33-36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.33), the Srimad-Bhagavatam’s four seed verses. These verses are known as the catuh'sloki Bhagavatam. His four “hints” follow:

1. Jnana, knowledge, means to know the Lord’s personal form, which is far more confidential than realization of the Lord’s impersonal feature. Srila Prabhupada has explained this in his purport to text 31: “The mental speculators can reach up to the standard of impersonal Brahman realization, but, factually, complete knowledge of transcendence is beyond the knowledge of impersonal Brahman. Thus it is called the supreme confidential wisdom.” This topic will be explained in the first of the Bhagavatam’s seed texts, text 33.
2. Vijnana, realization of this subtle science, occurs by the Lord’s grace. Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 31 that “the Lord informs Brahma that knowledge of Him, the Supreme Absolute Truth, as it is stated in the revealed scriptures, is very subtle and cannot be understood unless one is self-realized by the grace of the Lord.” This is because the Lord’s form, qualities, and activities are spiritual and beyond mdyd’s realm. In addition, because He is the Absolute Truth, anything that appears as if it is separate from Him is only an illusion, maya. In order to teach this truth and the understanding that we are dependent on His mercy, the Lord speaks the second of the Bhagavatam’s seed texts, text 34.
3. Sarahasyam refers to rahasya, secret, confidential, or mysterious. The most secret, confidential, and mysterious goal is prema-bhakti. “Raha' syam means devotional service,” Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 31. “This mystery is love of Godhead.” The Lord will explain this in the third of the Bhagavatam’s four seed verses, text 35.
4. Tad-angam, the necessary paraphernalia or means by which one may attain the confidential goal is sadhana'bhakti. As Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 31: “Therein lies the main qualification for knowing the mystery of the Personality of Godhead. And to attain the stage of transcendental love of Godhead, regulative
5. principles of devotional service must be followed. The regulative principles are called vidhi'bhakti, or the devotional service of the Lord, and they can be practiced by a neophyte with his present senses. Such regulative principles are mainly based on hearing and chanting of the glories of the Lord.” This topic will be explained in the fourth of the Bhagavatam's seed texts, text 36.

In the Caitanya-caritamrta, Srila Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami (Madhya [25.131](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/25.131)) places these four verses into categories of sambandha (jnana and vijnana, Bhagavatam [2.9.33—4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.33), discussed in Madhya [25.110-19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/25.110)), abhidheya (tad'angam, Bhagavatam [2.9.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.36), discussed in Madhya [25.120-23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/25.120)) andprayojana (sarahasyam, Bhagavatam [2.9.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.35), discussed in Madhya [25.124-27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/25.124)). Kaviraja Gosvami also includes texts [2.9.31-36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.31) in his Caitanya-caritamrta, Adi [1.51-56](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/1.51). Srila Prabhupada comments extensively in his purports to those sections.

Srila Prabhupada summarizes all four texts as follows in his purport to the last catuh-sloki text (Adi [1.56](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/1.56)):

**From this and the preceding three verses of Caitanya-caritamrta, which have been selected from the Srimad-Bhagavatam, the missionary activities of Lord Caitanya can be understood. Srimad-Bhagavatam has 18,000 verses, which are summarized in the four verses beginning with aham evasam evagre (53) and concluding with yat syat sarvatra sarvada (56). In the first of these verses (53) the transcendental nature of Lord Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is explained. The second verse (54) further explains that the Lord is detached from the workings of the material energy, maya. The living entities, although parts and parcels of Lord Krsna, are prone to be controlled by the external energy; therefore, although they are spiritual, in the material world they are encased in bodies of material energy. The eternal relationship of the living entities with the Supreme Lord is explained in that verse. The next verse (55) instructs that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by His inconceivable energies, is simultaneously one with and different from the living entities and the material energy. This knowledge is called acintya'bhedabheda'tattva. When an individual living entity surrenders to the Supreme Lord, Krsna, he can then develop natural transcendental love for Him. This surrendering process should be the primary concern of a human being. In the next verse (56) it is said that a conditioned soul must ultimately approach a bona fide spiritual master and try to understand perfectly the material and spiritual worlds and his own existential position. Here the words anvaya-vyatirekabhyam, “directly and indirectly,” suggest that one must learn the process of devotional service in its two aspects: one must directly execute the process of devotional service and indirectly avoid the impediments to progress.”**

Be blessed! the Lord tells Brahma. By My causeless mercy may you practically realize everything about Me—My eternal form, qualities, and the transcendental nature of My existence and activities! Thus in text 32 the Lord blesses Brahma so that all knowledge (jnana) and realization (vijnana) will awaken in him. The secret of realizing these is, as Srila Prabhupada states in his purport, to attain the Lord’s causeless mercy. “The Lord discloses His form even to the extent of measurement, to His pure devotees...”

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments as follows on text 32 in Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 96: And so, for the manifestation of the two objectives to be achieved, namely, practical realization and the confidential essence, the Lord gives a benediction: “All of Me—My actual eternal form and transcendental existence, color, qualities, and activities—let it all be awakened in you by factual realization and by My causeless mercy.” Thus the Lord says, “May My essence and extent, characteristics, visible forms (such as My form with dark blue complexion and My form with four arms), qualities (such as My concern for My devotees), pastimes, and factual, realized knowledge about Me—may you gain all of these by My favor.” Here the blessing for realization is obvious, and there is also a blessing in connection with the rahasya, the most secret, confidential essence, because the supreme blissful direct perception of these matters necessarily gives rise to pure love.

**Bhagavatam** [**2.9.33**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.33)**, Catuh-sloki Seed Verse One**

*aham evasam evagre*  
*nanyad yat sad-asat param*  
*pascad aham yad etac ca*  
*yo ’vasisyeta so ’smy aham*

**Brahma, it is I, the Personality of Godhead, who was existing before the creation, when there was nothing but Myself. Nor was there the material nature, the cause of this creation. That which you see now is also I, the Personality of Godhead, and after annihilation what remains will also be I, the Personality of Godhead.**

Although the Lord of Vaikuntha, Bhagavan, is the original source of all, He is nevertheless a person. This text clearly emphasizes His personal nature, for in it the Lord, who is speaking, uses the word aham, “I,” three times. “Aham means ‘I’; therefore the speaker who is saying aham, ‘1,’ must have His own personality,” Srila Prabhupada insists in his purport to this text as it is cited in Caitanya-caritamrta Adi [1.53](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/1.53). Prabhupada’s lengthy purport to this text appearing as Bhagavatam [2.9.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.33) also asserts this point: “We should note very carefully that the Personality of Godhead is addressing Lord Brahma and specifying with great emphasis Himself, pointing out that it is He, the Personality of Godhead, who existed before the creation, it is He only who maintains the creation, and it is He only who remains after the annihilation of the creation.”

Nor does the Lord’s existence mean that He exists alone. When one exclaims, “The king is coming!” no one expects the king to arrive alone. As the king’s arrival implies the arrival of his entire retinue, the Lord’s existence prior to the material creation implies the existence of the Vaikuntha planets and His devotees who dwell there eternally.

Srila Sridhara Svami mentions that text 33 describes the extent of the Lord’s existence. He has neither beginning nor end; He is everything. Therefore He has no equal.For our edification, Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami expands Bhagavatam [2.9.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.33) into six verses as Caitanya-caritamrta Madhya [25.110-15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/25.110):

**“Before the creation of the cosmic manifestation,” the Lord said, “I existed, and the total material energy, material nature and the living entities all existed in Me. After creating the cosmic manifestation, I entered into it. Whatever you see in the cosmic manifestation is but an expansion of My energy. When the whole universe dissolves, I remain full in Myself, and everything that was manifested is again preserved in Me. Prior to the cosmic manifestation, only I exist, and no phenomena exist, either gross, subtle or primordial. After creation, only I exist in everything, and after annihilation, only I remain eternally."**

**In the verse beginning “aham eva,” the word “aham” is expressed three times. In the beginning there are the words “a/iam eva." In the second line there are the words “pascad aham." At the end are the words “so ’smy aham." This “aham" indicates the Supreme Person. By the repetition of “aham," the transcendental personality who is complete with six opulences is confirmed.**

**Impersonalists do not accept the personal feature of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Personality of Godhead is stressed in this verse in order to impress upon them the necessity of accepting Him. Therefore the word “aham" is mentioned three times. To stress something important, one repeats it three times.**

Here is a nine-point summary of Prabhupada’s purport to text 33:

1. Nothing exists beyond the “I” mentioned in this verse. That “I” is the Absolute Truth, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Lord of Vaikuntha, not the “all-is-formless-Brahman” of the impersonalists.
2. Yet a second “I” exists as the individual souls, nondifferent from the Lord, who are one in quality with the creator yet are the created. Both are individuals. The difference between these I’s is their quantity, not their quality. That is, one is the predominator I and the other is the predominated I. Both I’s, the predominator and the predominated, are persons. Brahma is seeing the predominator I, the Lord, face to face. That predominator is the source of all, and He exists before, during, and after the material creation.
3. Srila Prabhupada quotes from sastra to demonstrate that the Lord, as a person, exists eternally and transcendentally as the original source of creation.
4. Along with the Lord, the spiritual world, the eternal Vaikuntha planets, exists in transcendental variegatedness.
5. Prabhupada offers quotations from Srimad-Bhagavatam and other sastras to assert the eternal existence of the Personality of Godhead.
6. The Lord exists personally, but works through His energies, just as a king lives and acts through his government, his energies. Even though the king may not be seen in every government office, he is nevertheless the source of all government power.
7. Srila Prabhupada presents sastric evidence to demonstrate that Krsna existed prior to the purusa-avataras.
8. The Lord is impersonal through His energies in the material world, but He is ultimately personal. One mainly sees the Lord’s impersonal form with one’s material senses. In that way, it can be said that the Lord’s impersonal aspect is the “immediate cause” and the personal form the “cause of all causes, or the remote cause.”
9. Both features of the Lord—His personal form and His impersonal formlessness—do exist. Yet realization of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, not of the impersonal Brahman, is the goal, for Krsna is the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the root cause of all.

Thus the Lord has offered Brahma true knowledge of Himself as the Absolute Truth, the source of all, including the impersonal Brahman, of the individual souls, and of the entirety of the material creation. Srila Sridhara Svami comments on this text that this verse describes the extent of the Lord’s existence. The Lord has no beginning or end. He is everything and has no equal.

**Bhagavatam** [**2.9.34**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.34)**, Catuh'Sloki Seed Verse Two**

Nothing is separate from the Lord, and the Lord describes the action of His illusory maya potency in text 34, which is the second seed verse:

*rte ’rtham yat pratiyeta*  
*na pratiyeta catmani*  
*tad vidyad atmano mayam*  
*yathabhaso yatha tamah*

**О Brahma, whatever appears to be of any value, if it is without relation to Me, has no reality. Know it as My illusory energy, that reflection which appears to be in darkness.**

Once one has assimilated the Lord’s position as He described it in text 33, one can understand that nothing is separate from Him. Thus He is known as the Absolute Truth. In his purport to text 34, as cited in Caitanya-caritamrta Adi [1.54](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/1.54), Srila Prabhupada clarifies the difference between absolute and relative truths: “Since it is difficult to understand the distinction between the absolute and relative truths, an analogy can be given for clarification. The Absolute Truth can be compared to the sun, which is appreciated in terms of two relative truths: reflection and darkness. Darkness is the absence of sunshine, and a reflection is a projection of sunlight into darkness. Neither darkness nor reflection has an independent existence. Darkness comes when the sunshine is blocked. For example, if one stands facing the sun, his back will be in darkness. Since darkness stands in the absence of the sun, it is therefore relative to the sun. The spiritual world is compared to the real sunshine, and the material world is compared to the dark regions where the sun is not visible.”

That which appears to be separate or independent appears as such only due to the Lord’s illusory energy, maya, which is also supported by and rests in Him. Yet the Lord Himself, as well as His qualities, pastimes, and associates, are fully transcendental, beyond maya’s realm. Those in maya’s grip, however, will perceive the Lord as if He too were within maya. Conversely, those who are free from maya can perceive Krsna as an entity separate from maya. It is impossible for those suffering from material illusion to know and love the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore, one should give up illusion.

Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami expands Bhagavatam [2.9.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.34) into four verses, setting them as Madhya [25.116-19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/25.116) in his Caitanya-caritamrta:

**Actual spiritual knowledge and its practical application are considered in all these sound vibrations \[of the words from Bhagavatam** [**2.9.33**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.33)**, or Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya** [**25.110—115**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/25.110)**\]. Although the external energy comes from Me, I am different from it. Sometimes a reflection of the sun is experienced in place of the sun, but its illumination is never possible independent of the sun. When one is transcendentally situated, he can perceive Me. This perception is the basis of one’s relationship with the Supreme Lord. Now let Me further explain this subject matter. What appears to be truth without Me is certainly My illusory energy, for nothing can exist without Me. It is like a reflection of a real light in the shadows, for in the light there are neither shadows nor reflections.**

Knowing the above vijnana, truths of science or realized knowledge, is the subject of the second seed verse. Below is a ten-point outline of Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 34:

1. Srila Prabhupada’s first paragraph summarizes the first two seed verses.
2. The material world is always changing but is not false, for it rests on the Lord. One’s tendency to accept something that changes as eternal is an illusion caused by maya. The material world should be accepted as a reflection of actual reality, as reflected light shining in the darkness.
3. Mayas last two traps are when living entities think themselves the Lord or imagine that the Lord is formless. Under all circumstances, both the Lord and the living entity possess form.
4. The Vedanta-sutra confirms that everything comes from and is connected to the Lord.
5. As nothing is truly separate from the Lord, the living entities are dependent on Him.
6. Only those dazzled by mayas glare deny the Lord’s existence.
7. A sane man takes enlightenment from the disciplic succession beginning with Brahma, who was personally instructed by the Lord. A sane man thus knows the Lord’s position as the source, maintainer, and annihilator of all that is and becomes the Lord’s pure servant.
8. The living entities are also of the Lord, although they are not themselves God. “The superior energy of the Lord cannot be as good as the Lord, although there is very little difference between the energy and the possessor of the energy, or the fire and the heat.”
9. The material energy is like darkness. The Lord is light and the living entities are like the reflection of light in darkness. No one can become freed from darkness “by the reflected light of the common man; one has to receive the light from the original light itself.” One should take shelter of the Lord’s light in the form of Bhagavad-gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam.
10. All living entities are bom in darkness; light, the mercy of the Lord, is required for them to attain the ability to see: “Therefore the action of different energies of the Lord, or the Personality of God head Himself, can be realized by the light manifested by the causeless mercy of the Lord. The impersonalists say that God cannot be seen. God can be seen by the light of God and not by man-made speculations. Here this light is specifically mentioned as vidyat, which is an order by the Lord to Brahma. This direct order of the Lord is a manifestation of His internal energy, and this particular energy is the means of seeing the Lord face to face. Not only Brahma but anyone who may be graced by the Lord to see such merciful direct internal energy can also realize the Personality of Godhead without any mental speculation.”

Srila Sridhara Svami has commented that this verse describes darkness, the Lord’s power of illusion.

**Bhagavatam** [**2.9.35**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.35)**, Catuh-sloki Seed Verse Three**

*yatha mahanti bhutani*  
*bhutesuccavacesv anu*  
*pravistany apravistani*  
*tatha tesu na tesv aham*

**О Brahma, please know that the universal elements enter into the cosmos and at the same time do not enter into the cosmos; similarly, I Myself also exist within everything created, and at the same time I am outside of everything.**

This verse, which hints at prema-bhakti, indirectly describes the rahasyam, the Bhagavatam’s great secret. In Bhagavatam [11.21.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/21.35), Sri Krsna tells Uddhava that the Vedas reveal truth in an esoteric, indirect fashion, and that He Himself is pleased by this mode of description. Thus Krsna has also spoken to Brahma the highest truth, but He has spoken it indirectly.

In Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 95, Srila Jiva Gosvami describes how this verse speaks of prema-bhakti: Without pure love, one cannot actually give up maya. Krsna then explains the confidentiality of that pure love: “The universal elements enter into the cosmos and at the same time do not enter into the cosmos; similarly, I Myself also exist within everything created, and at the same time I am outside of everything.” As the principal elements of creation simultaneously remain outside created beings and still appear to have entered and are present in them, so also I, even though I have not entered this universe, being situated in Vaikuntha, appear to have entered and am present in the hearts of surrendered persons. Here the confidential essence is hinted at: pure loving devotion, which brings the Supreme Soul under control and causes Him to enter (and be active in) a soul’s heart. So, the Lord says, I am manifest to My devotees inside (in the activity of their minds) and outside (in the activity of their senses) due to their possessing the rahasya. This confidential essence (rahasya) is self-luminating prema-bhakti, which is composed of pure ecstasy. Because of their possessing this, My devotees perform no other activity. Thus Sri Brahma has said, “O Narada, because I have caught hold of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, with great zeal, whatever I say has never proved to have been false. Nor is the progress of my mind ever deterred. Nor are my senses ever degraded by temporary attachment to matter.”

There might be contention against this explanation according to some other interpretation of the four-verse Bhagavatam, Sri Jiva says, but the actual purport of the verses is only found in this explanation.

Srila Prabhupada quotes Brahma-samhita ([37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/37)) in his purport to show that Krsna stays in the spiritual world: “I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who resides in His own realm, Goloka, with Radha, who resembles His own spiritual figure and who embodies His ecstatic potency (hladini). Their companions are Her confidantes, who embody extensions of Her bodily form and who are imbued and permeated with ever-blissful spiritual rasa.” He then quotes Brahma-samhitd (38) to explain how Krsna enters the devotees’ hearts: “I worship the primeval Lord, Govinda, who is always seen by the devotees whose eyes are anointed with the pulp of love. He is seen in His eternal form of Syamasundara, situated within the heart of the devotees.” These two verses form the purport to Bhagavatam [2.9.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.35).

Srila Jiva Gosvami continues his discussion of this text in the same anuccheda: What is called rahasya, the greatest secret and most confidential essence—prema-bhakti—is the most rare thing. Ordinary matters of this world are meant to cover and divert the eyes of evil and uninterested people from this. It is like a cintamani gem hidden in a box. Thus the Personality of Godhead has said, “The Vedic seers deal in esoteric terms, and I also am pleased by such confidential descriptions.” Something is kept esoteric when it is a precious item, scarcely available and not to be given away. This has been described in many statements, such as “He sometimes bestows liberation, but hardly ever pure devotion.” The Personality of Godhead Himself has also said this in His own words to His best devotees, Arjuna and Uddhava, in such statements as “because you are My very dear friend, I am speaking to you My supreme instruction, the most confidential knowledge of all. Hear this from Me, for it is for your benefit.”

Below is a six-point summary of Prabhupada’s purport to text 35:

1. The elements exist outside the cosmos and are used in the universe to construct all things. Similarly, the Lord exists both inside and outside everything. This is the Lord’s acintya-sakti. Like the elements, He is both within and without.
2. The Lord abides in the universe through His plenary expansion, the Supersoul. This is described in Brahma-samhita [5.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/35) and [5.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/37).
3. Because the impersonalists have no devotion, they cannot understand the mystery of how the Lord is both all-pervading and simultaneously playing His flute in Goloka Vrndavana. Srila Prabhupada adds: “This vision is the real mystery of spiritual knowledge, as stated by the Lord in the beginning (sarahasyam tad'angam cd). This mystery is the most confidential part of the knowledge of the Supreme, and it is impossible for the mental speculators to discover by dint of intellectual gymnastics.” This is the secret mentioned previously: the Lord can only be known by loving devtional service: premanjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena (Bs. [5.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/38)).
4. As the elements are both outside and within the universe, those possessing bhakti have the Lord’s pastimes and names—which are nondifferent from Him—“televised” in their hearts, even though His pastimes also occur “outside,” in Vaikuntha or Goloka Vrndavana.
5. That the Lord is all-pervading does not mean that He cannot have a personal form, but that form can only be seen by those who possess prema-bhakti, love for Krsna. Krsna rarely bestows prema on anyone. Srila Prabhupada states: “Thus love of Godhead, developed in the heart of the devotee, is a great mystery. Brahmaji previously told Narada that the desires of Brahmaji are never unfulfilled because he is always absorbed in the transcendental loving service of the Lord; nor has he any desire in his heart save and except the transcendental service of the Lord. That is the beauty and mystery of the process of bhakti-yoga. As the Lord’s desire is infallible because He is acyuta, similarly the desires of the devotees in the transcendental service of the Lord are also acyuta, infallible.” Thus devotional service is the most mysterious of spiritual practices.
6. Wonderful and mysterious bhakti-yoga may be received and understood only through the chain of disciplic succession. As Srila Prabhupada states to conclude his purport: “If one is fortunate enough to have received the knowledge in the transcendental disciplic succession, surely he will have the chance to understand the mystery of the Lord and that of the Srimad-Bhagavatam, the sound incarnation of the Lord.”

Krsna clearly reciprocates with everyone. He allows the materialists to view the world and perceive a field of pleasurable opportunities. An impersonalist, by Krsna’s grace, perceives Brahman everywhere; a yogi sees the Supersoul. But only to those whose eyes are smeared with the ointment of love does Krsna reveal Himself continuously.

Srila Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami expands on text 35 as follows in Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya [25.124-27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/25.124):

**Supreme affection for Me is called love of Godhead, and that is the ultimate goal of life. Let Me explain by a practical example the natural characteristics of such love. The five material elements are existing inside and outside of every living entity. Similarly, I, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, am manifest within the heart of the devotee as well as outside his body. As the material elements enter the bodies of all living beings and yet remain outside them all, I exist within all material creations and yet am not within them. A highly elevated devotee can bind Me, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in his heart by love. Wherever he looks, he sees Me and nothing else.**

Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami then offers three texts from the Bhagavatam to further describe such love for Krsna: “Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who destroys everything inauspicious for His devotees, does not leave the hearts of His devotees even if they remember Him and chant about Him inattentively. This is because the rope of love always binds the Lord within the devotees’ hearts. Such devotees should be accepted as most elevated.” (Bhag. [11.2.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.55))

“A person advanced in devotional service sees within everything the soul of souls, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna. Consequently he always sees the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead as the cause of all causes and understands that all things are situated in Him.” (Bhag. [11.2.45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/2.45))

“All the gopis assembled to chant the transcendental qualities of Krsna very loudly, and they began to wander from one forest to another like madwomen. They began to inquire about the Lord, who is situated in all living entities, internally and externally. Indeed, they even asked all the plants and vegetables about Him, the Supreme Person.” (Bhag. [10.30.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/30.4))

Srila Prabhupada also writes on text 35 in his purport to Caitanya' caritamrta Adi [1.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/1.55): “Because of his development of transcendental attachment for the Supreme Lord, a surrendered soul feels the presence of his beloved everywhere, and all his senses are engaged in the loving service of the Lord. His eyes are engaged in seeing the beautiful couple Sri Radha and Krsna sitting on a decorated throne beneath a desire tree in the transcendental land of Vrndavana. His nose is engaged in smelling the spiritual aroma of the lotus feet of the Lord. Similarly, his ears are engaged in hearing messages from Vaikuntha, and his hands embrace the lotus feet of the Lord and His associates. Thus the Lord is manifested to a pure devotee from within and without. This is one of the mysteries of the devotional relationship in which a devotee and the Lord are bound by a tie of spontaneous love. To achieve this love should be the goal of life for every living being.”

Using the Bhagavatam’s Tenth Canto as his main reference for his Krsna-sandarbha commentary, anucchedas 154-70, Srila Jiva Gosvami wonderfully describes the exalted stage of prema-bhakti that the Vraja gopis possess. By virtue of their powerful love for Krsna, they remain constantly in Krsna’s association. Interestingly, in anuccheda 155 he offers a quotation from Bhagavatam [10.47.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.29) to express the sarahasya meaning of the third of the catuhAloki Bhagavatam verses. Here is anuccheda 156:

Superficially describing the all-pervading Supersoul, Lord Krsna actually described the gopis’ constant meditation on Him and their uninterrupted svarasiki perception of Him through strong feelings of separation in the following Srimad-Bhagavatam verse ([10.47.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.29)): “My dear gopis, just as the five material elements of earth, water, fire, air and ether are all-pervading in this material world and present in the bodies of all living entities, in the same way I am always present within you. I reside in your minds, senses, and your life-breath, for I have taken shelter in all these places.”

Sri Krsna’s statement, Jiva Gosvami explains, can be interpreted in the following way: The material elements are causes of one another. That is, ether is the cause of air, air of fire, fire of water, and water of earth. Each element’s cause is situated in its effect. That is, ether is situated in air, air in fire, fire in water, and water in earth. One can understand from this that Krsna, who is the cause of everything, is therefore situated in everything, because as a general rule, causes are always situated in their effects. Krsna continues: “Even though we have been externally separated, I still always remain within you. Thus I am eternally situated in all of you, although I am not externally perceived as such. In which way am I within you? ‘I am the refuge of the minds of all of you, who are my only life. Were I not with you, because of separation from Me for even a moment your minds, etc., would be unable to exist.’ Or, in answer to the expected question, “In which form are You situated in us?” Krsna answers, “Only in that form that is two-handed, dark-complexioned, and that plays the flute. In that form, I am the refuge of all of your minds.”

In anuccheda 155, Srila Jiva Gosvami states: Although the gopis seemed to be separated from Krsna in His prakata-lila (manifest pastimes), they were always thinking of Him and thus perceived His presence directly in His aprakata-lila (unmanifest pastimes). Being situated in the stage of svarasiki realization, the gopis saw Sri Krsna constantly: “In all of My manifestations, your being separated from Me actually doesn’t take place. While separation does occur in My manifest pastimes (prakata-lila), union with Me simultaneously exists in My unmanifest pastimes (aprakata-lila)."

And: “At that time, during separation, the union of the gopis with Me is within My unmanifest pastimes in Vrndavana.” Thus although Krsna sometimes does go elsewhere (in Vrndavana, Mathura, and Dvaraka) with His associates in His manifest pastimes, His prakata-lila, His statement in Bhagavatam [10.47.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.29) is nevertheless quite accurate: “It is not possible for you to be separated from Me.” Thus it is explained that this state of being always united with Krsna through love is the highest secret, but it is herein explained only in an indirect and obscure manner, similar to the manner in which brahma-juana is indirectly explained by the device of describing something else.

In anuccheda 158-59, Srila Jiva Gosvami discusses that even in the prakata'lila, after His departure from Vraja, the gopis remain in contact with Krsna in their minds. In anuccheda 161-64, he continues the discussion: Sri Krsna expects the following argument from the gopis: “Well, instead of considering us as being greatly afflicted by separation from You and thus You, due to Your compassionate heart, teaching us how to attain You, why don’t you personally come in such a way that You are visible before us? We consider Your ‘compassion’ simply cheating!”

Considering that the gopis might think like this, Lord Krsna speaks the following words (Bhag. [10.47.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.34)): “My dear gopis, although you were accustomed to love Me from the beginning of your lives, in order to increase your superexcellent love for Me, I have purposely separated Myself from you. I have done this so that you may meditate upon Me constantly.”

In this verse Sri Krsna says to the gopis: “Although you are all full of love for Me and always eager to see Me (bhavatinam dasarh priyah), I have now separated Myself from your company (yad dure varte) in order that you may constantly meditate on Me (manasah sannikarsartham). In this way you may always see Me in your minds, just as you formerly always saw Me with your eyes.”

Lord Krsna continues His explanation in the next verse (Bhag. [10.47.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.35)): “When a woman’s beloved is away, she thinks of him meditatively and he is present before her. In fact, she is more conscious of him than when he was actually present. In the same way, you have become more conscious of Me in this condition of separation than when I was directly present before you.”

In the next verse (Bhag. [10.47.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.36)), Lord Krsna describes the result the gopis attain by their constant meditation on Him: “My dear gopis, because you constantly think of Me without thinking of anything else, and because you never forget Me, You will quickly attain Me.”

In anuccheda 164, Srila Jiva Gosvami quotes Bhagavatam [10.47.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.37) and [10.82.44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/82.44), then paraphrases their essence: I am completely submissive to the pure love of My devotees, and thus every day I leave the city of the Yadus and come to Vrajabhumi, continually revealing My form to the residents there. I do this according to My repeated promise to return to Vrndavana. Anuccheda 165 continues: The gopis were able to understand the description of Sri Krsna’s aprakata presence among them and became satisfied to understand that they were not actually separated from Him. Sukadeva Gosvami describes their satisfaction in Bhagavatam [10.47.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/47.38): “After hearing the message written by their dear-most Krsna, the gopis became pleased and satisfied. Remembering that message, they spoke the following words to Uddhava.” Jiva Gosvami adds: Remembering Lord Krsna’s instructions, the gopis were able to directly see Lord Krsna’s aprakata form and pastimes and become relieved of their strong feelings of separation. They became very pleased (pritah).

**Bhagavatam** [**2.9.36**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.36)**, Catuh-sloki Seed Verse Four**

After having described the most wonderful and confidential of truths—that the Lord is always present amid the prema'bhaktas who love Him fully—and after the hearer’s desire to achieve that mysterious state of consciousness has increased, a question naturally and eagerly arises: How do we achieve prema-bhakti; The Supreme Personality of Godhead teaches the method in the next verse (Bhag. [2.9.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.36)):

*etavad eva jijnasyam*  
*tattva-jijnasunatmanah*  
*anvaya-vyatirekabhayam*  
*yat syat sarvatra sarvada*

**A person who is searching after the Supreme Absolute Truth, the Personality of Godhead, must certainly search for it up to this, in all circumstances, in all space and time, and both directly and indirectly.**

This is tad-angam, both the means of searching and the process of attainment. Tad-angam refers to sadhana-bhakti, which is based on the nine processes mentioned in Bhagavatam [7.5.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/5.23), beginning with sravanam kirtanam visnoh smaranam. Srila Jiva Gosvami has confirmed this in Bhagavatsandarbha, anuccheda 95, by briefly describing that rahasya refers to the advanced stage of love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead (prema-bhakti) and that tad'angam refers to devotional service in practice (sadhana-bhakti). Those seriously desiring to obtain the most confidential goal described in Bhagavatam [2.9.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.35) must be one-pointed in their determination. They must always be searching, examining all places and all circumstances for prema-bhakti. They should inquire about this and nothing else from their spiritual masters.

Srila Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami has expanded this one text into four in Caitanya-cantdmrta, Madhya [25.120-23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/25.120):

**Now please hear from Me about the process of devotional service, which is applicable in any country, for any person, at all times and in all circumstances. As far as religious principles are concerned, there is a consideration of the person, the country, the time and the circumstance. In devotional service, however, there are no such considerations. Devotional service is transcendental to all such considerations. It is therefore the duty of every man—in every country, in every circumstance and at all times—to approach a bona fide spiritual master, question him about devotional service and listen to him explain the process. A person interested in transcendental knowledge must therefore always directly and indirectly inquire about it to know about the all-pervading truth.**

In his purport to this text as it is cited in the Caitanya-caritamrta, Adi [1.56](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/1.56), Srila Prabhupada writes: “When one develops pure love for the Lord, he derives an ocean of transcendental happiness from the association of the Personality of Godhead. To qualify oneself to reach this stage of life is the highest perfection.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments in his Bhagavatsandarbha, anuccheda 95: In response to the question, “How can this confidential essence, the rahasya, become revealed?” the Lord teaches the discipline for achieving it, which is also the confidential essence in the sense that it is the means for achieving, step by step, everything up to and including that secret essence: “A person who is searching after the Supreme Absolute Truth, the Personality of Godhead, must certainly search for it up to this, in all circumstances, in all space and time, and both directly and indirectly.” One who desires to understand the truth of the self (of Me, the Personality of Godhead), who wants to experience the confidential essence as it actually is, should inquire only into this (and should learn it at the lotus feet of his divine spiritual master).

On what should that inquiry be based? That which alone is found always and everywhere, both positively and negatively, by both injunctions and prohibitions. For example, in the beginning (Bhag. [2.2.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.33)) the search is stated in the negative as a prohibition: “For those who are wandering in the material universe there is no auspicious means of deliverance other than what is aimed at in the direct devotional service of Lord Krsna.” In the conclusion (Bhag. [2.2.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.36)) it is stated positively as an injunction: “O King, it is therefore essential that every human being hear about, glorify and remember the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead, always and everywhere.”

Actions to be done (anvaya) and those to be avoided (vyatireka) are described in Bhagavatam [2.2.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/2.36): one should hear about, glorify and remember Krsna, and this should be done, as stated in Bhagavatam [2.9.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.36), “in all circumstances, all space and time.” Thus the Supreme Personality of Godhead teaches about jnana, vijndna, rahasyam, and tad-angam in these four verses (Bhag. [2.9.33-36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.33)).I have outlined Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 36 in twelve points:

**1. Srila Prabhupada states: “To unfold the mystery of bhakti-yoga, as it is explained in the previous verse, is the ultimate stage of all inquiries or the highest objective for the inquisitive.” Every person at all times and places should inquire and progress until they come to the point of love for Krsna.**

**2. People do not understand either the process of bhakti or its goal, Visnu or Krsna, because they are entangled in the material world and interested only in sense gratification, especially sex.**

**3. We should inquire about the Absolute Truth through disciplic succession. Srila Prabhupada states: “Although everyone is free to consult the revealed scriptures in this connection, one still requires the guidance of a bona fide spiritual master, and that is the direction in this verse.” Bewildered by maya, people cannot see the truth even when it is presented in sdstras such as Bhagavad-gita. This is because they lack a bona fide guru’s guidance. The truths imparted here are also imparted in the Bhagavad-gita.**

**4. The purpose of varnasrama is to organize society in such a way that everyone serves the Lord. The advancements of contemporary society are nullified, considered only “decorations on a dead body,” because neither the citizens nor the leaders know the goal of life or how to achieve it.**

**5. The ultimate goal of life is to attain love for Krsna. Failing to acquire that by practicing bhakti-yoga, one continues in the cycle of birth and death because matter overwhelms the mind. To become free, one must absorb the mind in Vasudeva.**

**6. Everyone therefore has the right to take to devotional service and attain the highest goal, and everyone should do so under proper guidance. Sincerity is the only qualification.**

**7. There is no obstacle to performing devotional service. Krsna can be served with even the most common ingredients. Srila Prabhupada offers many sastric quotations that directly (anvaya) indicate that the Lord should be served in all cases and at all times.**

**8. The Lord should be worshiped with devotion in all stages of life, even in childhood, and in all places.**

**9. The conclusion of Srimad-Bhagavatam, presented by Sukadeva Gosvami to Maharaja Pariksit, is that everyone “should chant the holy name of the Lord fearlessly to achieve the desired success in their pursuits.” (Bhag.** [**2.1.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/1.11)**)**

**10. Through further quotations, Srila Prabhupada demonstrates that sastra also indirectly (vyatirek) indicates that everyone should take to bhakti-yoga.**

**11. The final conclusion is that we should always hear, chant, and proclaim the Lord’s glories. We should not adopt any other method of advancement. “The best and guaranteed path of progress is therefore engagement in bhakti-yoga, pure devotional service.”**

**12.    Impersonalists are unable to access either the goal or the process to attain it. “The whole matter is explained by the Lord Himself, and one who has no approach to the Lord in His personal feature can rarely understand the purport of Srimad-Bhagavatam without being taught by the bhagavatas in the disciplic succession.”**

Having concluded His four-text summary of the Bhagavatam, the Lord now addresses the fear Brahma has expressed in texts 29 and 30: “Please tell me so that 1 may be taught in the matter by the instruction of the Personality of Godhead and may thus act instrumentally to generate living entities, without being conditioned by such activities.... I shall be engaged in the creation of different types of living entities, and I shall be occupied in Your service. I shall have no perturbation, but I pray that all this may not give rise to pride, as if I were the Supreme.” The Lord concludes: “O Brahma, just follow this conclusion by fixed concentration of mind, and no pride will disturb you, neither in the partial nor in the final devastation.” (Bhag. [2.9.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.37))

In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada points out that despite the Lord thrice using the word “aham” in text 33, impersonalists screw out an impersonal meaning from the catuh'sloki texts. To learn properly, therefore, one should “approach a bona fide guru who is the representative of the Lord following the parampara system.” By following his instructions, one can become completely satisfied by being fully engaged in Krsna’s service. As Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport, the Lord bestows His mercy on those devotees who are constantly engaged in His transcendental loving service (priti'purvakam) and He gives direct instructions “so that \[they\] may make accurate progress on the path . .. back to Godhead.”It is interesting to note that although it appears from many of this chapter’s texts that Narayana, the Lord of Vaikuntha, is speaking, Srila Prabhupada states: “As in the Bhagavad-gita, Tenth Chapter, the Personality of Godhead, Lord Krsna, has summarized the whole text in four verses, namely, aham sarvasya prabhavah, etc., so the complete Srimad-Bhagavatam has also been summarized in four verses, as aham evasam evagre, etc. Thus the secret purpose of the most important Bhagavatite conclusion has been explained by the original speaker of the Srimad-Bhagavatam, who was also the original speaker of the Bhagavad-gita, the Personality of Godhead, Lord Sri Krsna.” Later in that purport he states:

**In the Gopala-tapani Upanisad (sruti) it is said, gopa-veso me purusah purastad avirbabhuva: the Lord appeared before Brahma as a cowboy, that is, as the original Personality of Godhead, Lord Sri Krsna, Govinda, who is later described by Brahmaji in his Brahma-samhita (**[**5.29**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/29)**):**

***cintamani-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-vrksa-***  
***laksavrtesu surabhir abhipalayantam***  
***laksmi-sahasra-sata-sambhrama-sevyamanam***  
***govindam adi-purusam tarn aham bhajami***

**Brahmaji desires to worship the original personality of Godhead, Lord Sri Krsna, who resides in the topmost Vaikuntha planet, known as Goloka Vrndavana, where He is in the habit of keeping surabhi cows as a cowboy and where He is served by hundreds and thousands of goddesses of fortune (the gopis) with love and respect.**

**Therefore Lord Sri Krsna is the original form of the Supreme Lord (krsnas tu bhagavdn svayam). This is also clear from this instruction. The Supreme Personality of Godhead is Lord Krsna, and not directly Narayana or the purusa-avatdras, which are subsequent manifestations. Therefore Srimad-Bhagavatam means consciousness of the Supreme Personality of Godhead Lord Sri Krsna, and Srimad-Bhagavatam is the sound representation of the Lord as much as the Bhagavad-gita is. Thus the conclusion is that Srimad-Bhagavatam is the science of the Lord in which the Lord and His abode are perfectly realized.**

That Lord Krsna, not Narayana, spoke these catuh-sloki to Brahma is supported by Srila Jiva Gosvami in Krsna-sandarbha, anuccheda 64: In the following verse from Gopala-tapani Upanisad (1.29), Lord Krsna is described as the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the original teacher of Vedic knowledge: “It was Krsna, who in the beginning instructed Brahma in Vedic knowledge and who disseminated Vedic knowledge in the past. Those who aspire to become liberated surrender to Him, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who grants transcendental knowledge to His devotees.” At the beginning of a certain kalpa, Lord Krsna revealed to Brahma His original form as a cowherd boy and His original abode, the best of Vaikuntha planets. This is confirmed in the following verse from the Gopala-tapani Upanisad (1.27-28): “Brahma replied: ‘I continually glorified the Lord and meditated upon Him for millions of years, and at last I was able to understand the transcendental form of the Lord as Sri Krsna, who appeared before me in the dress of a cowherd boy.’”

## Texts 38-46: The Lord Departs and Brahma Recreates the Universe As it was Previously

Krsna disappeared as soon as He had completed His instructions to Brahma. With hands folded in respect, Brahma then began to recreate the universe as it was before. Returning to the original storyline, we will now see how Brahma, by replying to Narada Muni’s inquiries, taught him the Srimad-Bhagavatam, which contains ten characteristics and which the Lord spoke in four seed texts.

Srila Prabhupada explains that although “the Srimad-Bhagavatam was spoken in four verses, it had ten characteristics, which will be explained in the next chapter. . . . The ten characteristics . . . require so many verses just to explain them properly.” (Bhag. [2.9.44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.44), purport) Prabhupada also comments on the ten characteristics in his purport to text 46: “The ten divisions of Srimad-Bhagavatam, as explained by the great speaker Srila Sukadeva Gosvami, are the limitation of all questions, and intelligent persons will derive all intellectual benefits from them by proper utilization.”

Sukadeva Gosvami continues his narration to Maharaja Pariksit: “In succession, О King,” after hearing the Bhagavatam from Lord Brahma, “the great sage Narada instructed Srimad-Bhagavatam unto the unlimitedly powerful Vyasadeva, who meditated in devotional service upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Absolute Truth, on the bank of the River Sarasvati.” (Bhag. [2.9.45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.45))

Sukadeva Gosvami has finished responding to Maharaja Pariksit’s question about the pure soul’s acquisition of a material body (answered in Bhag. [2.9.1-3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.1)), the difference between the Lord and the jiva (answered in Bhag. [2.9.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.4)), and about atma-tattva, the science of God, the living entity, the jivdtma, and the Paramatma (this topic began with Suta Gosvami’s words in Bhag. [2.8.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/8.28) and was continued when Sukadeva spoke Bhagavatam [2.9.4-39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.4)).

Sukadeva Gosvami then tells Maharaja Pariksit that he will also answer his other questions in detail as he further explains the four texts spoken by the Lord to Brahma.

At this point, the reader may recall that in Chapter Eight, Maharaja Pariksit asked Sukadeva Gosvami a number of questions. Sukadeva began to respond to those questions, and in due course, repeated the narration about how Brahma heard the entire Bhagavatam in four seed texts and then asked Narada Muni to expand on them. Narada will begin to do that, and, as Sukadeva Gosvami has just told Maharaja Pariksit, with the retelling of that expanded Srimad-Bhagavatam, all the other questions he asked in Chapter Eight will be answered. Therefore, the next chapter, the final chapter of the Second Canto, which includes an explanation of the Bhagavatam’s ten subjects, is entitled, “Bhagavatam Is the Answer to All Questions.” And as Srila Prabhupada states, this knowledge is the “limitation of all questions.”

## Chapter 10 - Bhagavatam Is the Answer to All Questions

## Texts 1-9: The Bhagavatam’s Ten Subjects

In one text (Bhag. [2.10.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/10.1)) Srila Sukadeva Gosvami lists the ten subject matters of Srimad-Bhagavatam: the creation of the universe (sargah), subcreation (visargah), planetary systems (sthanam), the Lord’s protection (posanam), the creative impetus (utayah), the change of Manus (manvantara), the science of God (isa-anukathah), returning home, back to Godhead (nirodhah), liberation (muktir), and the sum-mum bonum, the cause of all causes (dsrayah). “To isolate the transcendence of the summum bonum, the symptoms of the rest are described sometimes by Vedic inference, sometimes by direct explanation, and sometimes by summary explanations given by the great sages.” (Bhag. [2.10.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/10.2))

Sukadeva then presents a brief explanation of each of these ten topics in texts 3-9: Lord Maha-Visnu’s creation of the sixteen elements (earth, water, fire, air, sky, the five sense objects, the five sense organs, and the mind), which are the elementary universal ingredients, is called the primary creation, sarga.
