He did not ask directly about Krsna, however, but about the proper use of human life, the Creator and His process of creation, the Lord’s incarnations, and the world’s inhabitants and rulers. Then he revealed his heart: “O Maitreya, О friend of the distressed, the glories of the Supreme Lord can alone do good for people all over the world. Therefore, just as bees collect honey from flowers, kindly describe the essence of all topics—the topics of the Lord.” (Bhag. [3.5.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.15))

Although Vidura’s inquiries fell below the level of his devotion, he requested Maitreya to make his replies in relation to Krsna because krsna-katha is potent. Still, readers of the Bhagavatam may wonder why Vidura asked such indirect and apparently ordinary questions. Srila Prabhupada responds to this query in two of his purports:

**Vidura asked Maitreya some common questions, which was not originally his intention. Uddhava asked Vidura to approach Maitreya Muni and inquire into all the truths concerning the Lord, His name, fame, quality, form, pastimes, entourage, etc., and thus when Vidura approached Maitreya, he should have asked only about the Lord. But out of natural humility he did not immediately ask about the Lord, but inquired into a subject which would be of great importance to the common man. A common man cannot understand the Lord. He must first know the real position of his life under the influence of the illusory energy. (Bhag.** [**3.5.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.2)**, purport)**

And from the purport to Bhagavatam [3.5.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.16):

**Vidura was undoubtedly very eager to hear about Lord Krsna in particular, but he was overwhelmed because Lord Krsna had just passed away from the visible world. He therefore wanted to hear about Him in His purusa incarnations, which He manifests with full potencies for the creation and maintenance of the cosmic world. The activities of the purusa incarnations are but an extension of the activities of the Lord. This hint was given by Vidura to Maitreya because Maitreya could not decide which part of the activities of Lord Krsna should be chanted.**

After asking his questions, Vidura glorified the potency of krsna' katha. He explained that he had already heard both higher and lower topics—topics not directly discussing Krsna—from Vyasadeva and was satiated with them. “They have not satisfied me with the nectar of topics about Krsna. Who in human society can be satisfied without hearing sufficient talk of the Lord, whose lotus feet are the sum total of all places of pilgrimage and who is worshiped by great sages and devotees? Such topics can cut off one’s bondage to family affection simply by entering the holes of one’s ears.” (Bhag. [3.5.10-11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.10))

Vidura goes on to say that the motive behind Vyasadeva’s presentation of the Mahabharata, which is full of mundane topics, was to engage people in hearing krsna-katha. And one who becomes anxious to constantly hear krsna'kathd, Vidura says, gradually increases his indifference toward all other things. “Such constant remembrance of the lotus feet of Lord Krsna by the devotee who has achieved transcendental bliss vanquishes all his miseries without delay.” (Bhag. [3.5.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.13))

Srila Prabhupada further describes the potency of krsna-katha in a number of purports in this section:

**Vidura wanted to hear of everything from Maitreya, and so he inquired from him, but he desired that all the topics be in relationship with Krsna. As fire is never satisfied in its consumption of firewood, so a pure devotee of the Lord never hears enough about Krsna. Historical events and other narrations concerning social and political incidents all become transcendental as soon as they are in relationship with Krsna. That is the way to transform mundane things into spiritual identity. The whole world can be transformed into Vaikuntha if all worldly activities are dovetailed with krsna-katha. There are two important krsna-kathas current in the world—Bhagavad-gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam. Bhagavadgita is krsna-katha because it is spoken by Krsna, whereas Snmud-Bhagavatam is krsna-katha because it narrates about Krsna. Lord Caitanya advised all His disciples to preach krsna-katha all over the world without discrimination because the transcendental value of krsna-katha can purify one and all from material contamination. (Bhag.** [**3.5.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.10)**, purport)**

From Prabhupada’s purport to text 11:

**Krsna'katha is so powerful that simply by entering into a person’s ear it can at once give deliverance from the bondage of family affection. . . . Krsna'katha is the only remedy for all people of the world because it can situate one in pure consciousness of the self and liberate one from material bondage. To preach krsna-katha all over the world, as recommended by Lord Caitanya, is the greatest missionary activity, and all sensible men and women of the world may join in this great movement started by Lord Caitanya.**

From the purport to text 13:

**We must certainly know that on the absolute plane krsna-katha and Krsna are one and the same. The Lord is the Absolute Truth, and therefore His name, form, quality, etc., which are all understood to be krsna-katha, are nondifferent from Him. Bhagavad-gita, being spoken by the Lord, is as good as the Lord Himself. When a sincere devotee reads Bhagavad-gita, this is as good as seeing the Lord face to face in his personal presence . . . The pure devotee of the Lord enjoys life by constantly remembering the lotus feet of the Lord by hearing krsna-katha. For such a devotee there is no such thing as material existence, and the much advertised bliss of brahmananda is like a fig for the devotee who is in the midst of the transcendental ocean of bliss.**

Vidura ends by first expressing compassion and then a desire: Only the sinful are averse to hearing krsna-katha! I pity them, because their lives are spoiled by eternal time. In the meantime, they entangle themselves in rituals, philosophical speculation, and the imaginary goals of life. “O Maitreya, О friend of the distressed, the glories of the Supreme Lord can alone do good for people all over the world. Therefore, just as bees collect honey from flowers, kindly describe the essence of all topics—the topics of the Lord.” (Bhag. [3.5.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.15)) Please, Vidura asks further, kindly speak about the Lord’s superhuman and transcendental activities by which He incarnates to manifest and maintain the creation.

## Texts 17-38: Maitreya Describes How the Creation Begins

Maitreya Muni honored Vidura, appreciating that his questions blessed him with the opportunity to speak about Krsna. Maitreya also praised Vidura’s full absorption in Krsna consciousness and then began to describe the pastimes of the purusa-avatdras, “by which the Personality of Godhead extends His transcendental self for the creation, maintenance and dissolution of the cosmic world as they occur, one after another.” (Bhag. [3.5.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.22))

Maitreya Muni states: “The Personality of Godhead, the master of all living entities, existed prior to the creation as one without a second.” (Bhag. [3.5.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.23)) In Bhagavatam [3.4.13-20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/4.13), Uddhava requests Krsna to explain the catuh-sloki Bhagavatam He had spoken to Brahma “in days of yore.” Later, Vidura requests Uddhava to explain those same texts to him. Uddhava, however, suggests that it would be better for Vidura to hear from Maitreya instead (Bhag. [3.4.24-26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/4.24)). Now, as also explained in the first of the original catuh-sloki Bhagavatam texts (Bhag. [2.9.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.33)), Maitreya explains that only the Lord existed prior to the universal creation. “It is by His will only that creation is made possible and again everything merges in Him. This Supreme Self is symptomized by different names.” (Bhag. [3.5.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.23))

The Lord as Karanadakasayi Visnu existed alone and prior to the material creation. It was He who impregnated the material nature by His glance. Prior to receiving that glance, the material nature is called pradhana (the primal element, which is the “via medium between pure spirit and material existence” and “the junction of matter and spirit wherefrom the false ego of the living entity is generated” \[Bhag. [3.5.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.28), purport\]). It is “pure goodness with the slight addition of the material mode of passion” (Bhag. [3.5.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.27), purport), and is composed of the three modes of nature in an unmanifest and undifferentiated state.

By His glance, the Lord injects the living entities into the pradhana (Bhag. [3.5.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.26)). Immediately following that injection, pradhana develops into the mahat-tattva, which then incrementally manifests everything required for material creation. Impelled by the Lord’s potency, the mahat-tattva develops further. False ego—the illusory consciousness on which the material creation is based—next manifests in goodness, passion, and ignorance. Thus the creation evolves from subtle to gross. Unlike a watch that is created, assembled, wound, and finally left to its own workings by the watchmaker, each stage of development requires the Lord’s personal glance. Maitreya reveals this to Vidura: “O gentle one, of all the physical elements, beginning from the sky down to the earth, all the inferior and superior qualities are due only to the final touch of the glance of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [3.5.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.37))

When false ego combined with goodness to generate demigods, these controllers of the phenomenal world noted that the created elements were stagnant and unsynthesized and that the evolution of the universe had ceased. At this point in creation, the demigods are inspired to perform their entrusted creative services but find themselves unable to do so. They need direction from their master, and thus they seek His shelter.

Prabhupada describes the mixed position of the demigods in his purport to text 51: “The demigods are amongst the conditioned souls who have developed this pure consciousness of service to the Lord but who at the same time continue to desire to lord it over the material energy. Such mixed consciousness puts a conditioned soul in the position of managing the affairs of this creation. The demigods are entrusted leaders of the conditioned souls. As some of the old prisoners in government jails are entrusted with some responsible work of prison management, so the demigods are improved conditioned souls acting as representatives of the Lord in the material creation. Such demigods are devotees of the Lord in the material world, and when completely free from all material desire to lord it over the material energy they become pure devotees and have no desire but to serve the Lord.”

## Texts 39-51: The Prayers of the Demigods

## Texts 39-43: The Glorious Shelter of the Lord’s Lotus Feet

The demigods’ prayers in this section are both sweet and fascinating. The demigods begin by glorifying the Lord and taking shelter at His lotus feet: As an umbrella gives shelter from both the scorching sun and the pounding rain, Krsna’s lotus feet offer shelter to those overwhelmed by material miseries. It is impossible to avoid misery in this world. Still, although devotees who have achieved the Lord’s shelter also experience material existence, their experience does not parallel that of nondevotees. Devotees see Krsna’s mercy in everything that occurs and therefore experience in every event, pleasurable or miserable, the gentle touch of Krsna’s hand.

The demigods continue: Your lotus feet are the shelter of all places of pilgrimage, including those on the bank of the Ganges. Ganges water is most sacred and purifying, for it has touched Your lotus feet. Thus those who take shelter of the Ganges, which delivers us from sinful reactions, are actually taking shelter of Your lotus feet. The “wings of the Vedas” are meant to carry us to those lotus feet, and the great sages who take shelter of such holy texts are like swans sheltering in a lotus flower. Srila Prabhupada eloquently writes: “The paramaharhsas are compared to royal swans who make their nests on the petals of the lotus flower. The Lord’s transcendental bodily parts are always compared to the lotus flower because in the material world the lotus flower is the last word in beauty. The most beautiful thing in the world is the Vedas, or Bhagavad-gita, because therein knowledge is imparted by the Personality of Godhead Himself. The paramahamsa makes his nest in the lotuslike face of the Lord and always seeks shelter at His lotus feet, which are reached by the wings of Vedic wisdom. Since the Lord is the original source of all emanations, intelligent persons, enlightened by Vedic knowledge, seek the shelter of the Lord, just as birds who leave the nest again search out the nest to take complete rest.” (Bhag. [3.5.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.41), purport)

The demigods further glorify the potency of the Lord’s lotus feet in the next text: “Simply by hearing about Your lotus feet with eagerness and devotion and by meditating upon them within the heart, one at once becomes enlightened with knowledge, and on the strength of detachment one becomes pacified. We must therefore take shelter of the sanctuary of Your lotus feet.” (Bhag. [3.5.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.42))

Srila Prabhupada expands on this wonderful text in his purport: “The miracles of meditating on the lotus feet of the Lord with eagerness and devotion are so great that no other process can compare to it. The minds of materialistic persons are so disturbed that it is almost impossible for them to search after the Supreme Truth by personal regulative endeavors. But even such materialistic men, with a little eagerness for hearing about the transcendental name, fame, qualities, etc., can surpass all other methods of attaining knowledge and detachment.”

The demigods next describe the fortune of achieving the Lord’s shelter: “O Lord, You assume incarnations for the creation, maintenance and dissolution of the cosmic manifestation, and therefore we all take shelter of Your lotus feet because they always award remembrance and courage to Your devotees.” (Bhag. [3.5.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.43))

## Texts 44-47: Those Who Attain the Shelter of the Lord’s Lotus Feet and Those who Do Not

The demigods then describe two kinds of unfortunates who are unable to realize Krsna’s shelter. First, they name the materialist: “O Lord, persons who are entangled by undesirable eagerness for the temporary body and kinsmen, and who are bound by thoughts of ‘mine’ and ‘I,’ are unable to see Your lotus feet, although Your lotus feet are situated within their own bodies. But let us take shelter of Your lotus feet. О great Supreme Lord, offensive persons whose internal vision has been too affected by external materialistic activities cannot see Your lotus feet, but they are seen by Your pure devotees, whose one and only aim is to transcendentally enjoy Your activities.” (Bhag. [3.5.44—45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.44))

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 44 explains how the first type of unfortunate persons, those attached to and entangled by material consciousness, can become fortunate: “But even a person perpetually condemned to the miseries of material existence can get relief from bondage if he simply agrees to hear only krsna-katha. In this age of Kali, the process of hearing krsna-katha is the most effective means to gain release from unwanted family affection and thus find permanent freedom in life. The age of Kali is full of sinful reactions, and people are more and more addicted to the qualities of this age, but simply by hearing and chanting of krsna-katha one is sure to go back to Godhead. Therefore, people should be trained to hear only krsna-katha— by all means—in order to get relief from all miseries.”

Prabhupada’s wonderful purport to text 45 describes the liberality of devotees, for devotees bestow their kindness on all those who are unfortunate, both materialists and offenders: “The Lord’s devotees continue to bestow the blessings of devotion upon all such offenders without hesitation. That is the nature of devotees.” Jiva Gosvami comments similarly in his Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 179. There he writes that many persons do not see the Lord’s lotus feet because their internal vision is too affected by external materialistic activities. Jiva then states that great souls give mercy to those who do not commit offenses. Simply by the association of these great souls, he explains, materialistic persons also become saints. Because great souls are independent, they may also offer mercy to offenders and thus transform them into devotees. Such a transformation cannot occur without a great soul’s mercy. The power of the association of saintly persons to award Krsna consciousness is also stated in Bhagavatam [10.51.53](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/51.53): “When the material life of a wandering soul has ceased, О Acyuta, he may attain the association of Your devotees. And when he associates with them, there awakens in him devotion unto You, who are the goal of the devotees and the Lord of all causes and their effects.” And in Bhagavatam [10.10.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/10.41): “When one is face to face with the sun, there is no longer darkness for one’s eyes. Similarly, when one is face to face with a sadhu, a devotee, who is fully determined and surrendered to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one will no longer be subject to material bondage.”

The demigods continue: “O Lord, persons who, because of their serious attitude, attain the stage of enlightened devotional service achieve the complete meaning of renunciation and knowledge and attain the Vaikunthaloka in the spiritual sky simply by drinking the nectar of Your topics.” (Bhag. [3.5.46](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.46)) But there are also jnanis and yogis who conquer the modes of nature through their own knowledge and renunciation. By practicing devotional service, Vaisnavas achieve greater results than yogis, even if their devotional practices do not include the painful methods jnanis and yogis undertake.

Why do the demigods consider the practices of jnanis and yogis painful? After all, aren’t they too transcendentalists? Although jnanis and yogis are transcendentalists, they nevertheless possess material senses. They will be pushed to act with their senses because the soul in the body is ever active. Unlike the process used by devotees to transcend matter, the yogis and jnanis try to make themselves (and their senses) inactive to focus on renunciation and meditation. This is not effective. Even in their hearing of sastra they prefer the ponderous philosophy of Vedanta-sutra. But they often become bored with such philosophy, and eventually take to hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam.

Gradually, unavoidably, desire for activity is bom from the unnatural state of inactivity. Their minds and senses demand pleasure. But jnana and yoga demand their practitioners to focus on the negative— on renunciation and on everything an aspirant must not do. This is painful for those desiring activity and pleasure.

Fearing that the activities of bhakti will entangle them in karma, they do not allow themselves to use their senses in Krsna’s service. Thus their position as transcendentalists becomes precarious, and their unengaged senses tend to drag them down.

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 47 raises and responds to a similar point: “One may suggest that there is sufficient labor for the devotees also in the matter of discharging devotional service. But that labor is compensated by the enhancement of transcendental pleasure. The devotees derive more transcendental pleasure while engaged continuously in the service of the Lord than when they have no such engagement. In the family combination of a man and a woman there is much labor and responsibility for both of them, yet when they are single they feel more trouble for want of their united activities.”

## Texts 48-51: The Demigods Pray for Service

After glorifying the unparalleled shelter of Krsna’s lotus feet, synonymous with devotional service, and after calling those who have not attained that shelter unfortunate, the demigods shift their prayers to a request: О Lord, although we wish to serve You, we have been unable to act for Your transcendental pleasure because we have been conditioned by the three modes of nature. Please enlighten us so that we and all other living entities can offer sacrifice. Thus we can “maintain ourselves without disturbance and can easily accumulate the necessities of life both for You and for ourselves.” (Bhag. [3.5.49](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.49))

The demigods near their conclusion by saying that Krsna is the original person, the founder of all the devas, the oldest and unchanged. “O Lord, You have no source or superior. You have impregnated the external energy with the semen of the total living entities, yet You are unborn.” (Bhag. [3.5.50](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.50)) The demigods ask how to act in concert to assist Krsna in manifesting the creation, and they beg Him to bestow His potency upon them so that they will have the power to help Him.

Toward which of the Lord’s purposes are the demigods inspired to offer their assistance? Srila Prabhupada responds: “The Lord creates this material world and impregnates the material energy with the living entities who will act in the material world. All these actions have a divine plan behind them. The plan is to give the conditioned souls who so desire a chance to enjoy sense gratification. But there is another plan behind the creation: to help the living entities realize that they are created for the transcendental sense gratification of the Lord and not for their individual sense gratification. This is the constitutional position of the living entities.” (Bhag. [3.5.51](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.51), purport)

## Chapter 6 - Creation of the Universal Form

## Texts 1-10: The Lord’s Response to the Demigods

The Lord heard the demigods’ request for guidance so that the creation, now suspended, could resume. The suspension of the creation demonstrates the full dependence at each step of all things, not on the demigods’ potency or the strength of others, but on the Lord.

As Srila Prabhupada points out in his purport to Bhagavatam [3.6.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/6.1): “There is nothing wanting in the creation of the Lord; all the potencies are there in a dormant state. But unless they are combined by the will of the Lord, nothing can progress. The suspended progressive work of creation can only be revived by the direction of the Lord.” In response to the demigods’ prayers, Maitreya Muni explains to Vidura that the supremely powerful Karanadakasayi Visnu entered the material potency, the mahat-tattva, as Garbhodakasayi Visnu, along with His time potency. Simultaneous with the Lord’s entrance, the universal elements were set into motion, and the living entities who had been injected into the material nature awakened and began to act according to their previous natures and desires. The Lord, then, by His will, manifested His gigantic universal form, the visva-rupa. This was His response to the demigods’ prayers.

The visva-rupa is like a blueprint of the universe. As a material manifestation of the Lord, it cannot strictly be called His form because His form is ever spiritual and never material. Nevertheless, the Lord pervades and is nondifferent from the entire material creation. The subtle material form by which the Lord pervades the universe while displaying everything in the universe is called His universal form.

The universal form appears from Garbhodakasayi Visnu and is an aspect of Ksirodakasayi Visnu, the third of the purusa-avatar as. Ksirodakasayi Visnu both enters the heart of each living entity and pervades every atom in the universe. Thus the gross manifestation of the universe rests directly on the Lord’s universal form, which is considered the Lord’s first descent into the material realm. Just as a soul encaged in matter possesses both a subtle and a gross body, with the gross body based on the subtle (Bg. [15.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/15.9)), so the Supersoul possesses a subtle body (the universal form) and a gross manifestation of it (the universe). As the gross and subtle bodies ultimately rest on the soul, so both the subtle and gross features of the universe ultimately rest on Krsna’s presence as the Supersoul.

In Srimad-Bhagavatam, Canto Three, chapters One through Three, Vidura and Uddhava have directly described Krsna’s humanlike pastimes. Now to insure that readers receive an accurate understanding of Krsna’s identity, the Bhagavatam offers a glimpse of the Lord’s unlimited power. Prabhupada’s purport to text 4 further describes that Krsna manifests an insignificant aspect of Himself in order to allow the creation to continue: “The virat-rupa or visva-rupa, the gigantic universal form of the Lord, which is very much appreciated by the impersonalist, is not an eternal form of the Lord. It is manifested by the supreme will of the Lord after the ingredients of material creation. Lord Krsna exhibited this virat or visva-rupa to Arjuna just to convince the impersonalists that He is the original Personality of Godhead. Krsna exhibited the virapritpa; it is not that Krsna was exhibited by the virat-rupa. The virat-rupa is not, therefore, an eternal form of the Lord exhibited in the spiritual sky; it is a material manifestation of the Lord. The arca'vigraha, or the worshipable Deity in the temple, is a similar manifestation of the Lord for the neophytes. But in spite of their material touch, such forms of the Lord as the virat and area are all nondifferent from His eternal form as Lord Krsna.”

## Texts 11-34: The Demigods Enter the Universal Form

Guided by the universal form, the demigods, the directors of material affairs, entered their allocated realms in the visva-rupa. They were then able to dutifully serve the Lord by providing the necessary sensory functions in the universe, such as smelling, hearing, etc. Furthermore, from the universal form, the various planetary systems (Bhag. [3.6.28-29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/6.28)), organized according to the qualities of the material modes (Bhag. [3.6.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/6.28)), appeared, along with the powers and prototypes of the varnasrama system (Bhag. [3.6.29-34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/6.29)).

## Texts 35-40: Maitreya Comments on the Greatness of the Lord’s Universal Form

Maitreya Muni then frankly expresses his inability to know the full extent of the universal form: “O Vidura, who can estimate or measure the transcendental time, work and potency of the gigantic form manifested by the internal potency of the Supreme Personality of Godhead?” (Bhag. [3.6.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/6.35)) How then can we know Him, even in His feature as the universal form? Srila Prabhupada writes: “The best path is to become a cool-headed, submissive devotee of the Lord, try to hear about the Lord from the bona fide spiritual master, and thus serve the Lord in transcendental loving service ...”

Despite his inability to measure the breadth of the universal form, Maitreya Muni has still repeated what he has heard about the universal form with confidence because he has remained chaste to what he has heard in disciplic succession. Then Maitreya again underlines the importance of krsna-katha: “The highest perfectional gain of humanity is to engage in discussions of the activities and glories of the Pious Actor. Such activities are so nicely arranged in writing by the greatly learned sages that the actual purpose of the ear is served just by being near them.” (Bhag. [3.6.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/6.37))

Srila Prabhupada explains the potency of this literature: “These transcendental activities of the Lord are so arranged in writing by the great sages that simply by hearing of those narrations one becomes perfectly self-realized, and the proper use of the ear and the tongue is also achieved. Srimad-Bhagavatam is one of such great literatures, and the highest perfectional state of life is attained simply by hearing and reciting its contents.” (Bhag. [3.6.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/6.37), purport)

Indeed, Maitreya explains, even after years of meditation, Lord Brahma ascertained that the Lord’s glories are inconceivable and unlimited, because even the Lord Himself cannot find the limit of His own potencies! “Words, mind and ego, with their respective controlling demigods, have failed to achieve success in knowing the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore, we simply have to offer our respectful obeisances unto Him as a matter of sanity.” (Bhag. [3.6.40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/6.40))

We cannot know Krsna, the ultimate creator, simply by viewing His creation, just as we can’t know a farmer’s name, family, or fortunes simply by studying his wheat crop or the bread baked from it. If we want to know the details of a farmer’s life, we must develop an affectionate relationship with him. Only then will the farmer reveal his personal details. Similarly, only bhakti, a relationship of affection for and service to Krsna, will induce the Lord to reveal intimate details about Himself. Krsna states this: bhaktya mam abhijanati—“One can understand Me as I am, as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, only by devotional service.” Ultimately, it is impossible even for devotees to know Krsna in full. Yet devotees still try to know their “unknowable” Lord. Srila Prabhupada measures the devotees’ attempt against that of materialists in his purport to text 40:

**The froggish calculator may raise the objection that if the Absolute is unknowable even by the controlling deities of speech, mind and ego, namely the Vedas, Brahma, Rudra and all the demigods headed by Brhaspati, then why should the devotees be so interested in this unknown object? The answer is that the transcendental ecstasy enjoyed by the devotees in delineating the pastimes of the Lord is certainly unknown to nondevotees and mental speculators. . . . The devotees can at least know that the Absolute Truth is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Visnu, as the Vedic hymns confirm: от tad visnoh paramam padam soda pasyanti surayah . . . With devotion \[Maitreya Muni\] offers his sincere surrender, narnah, to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, bhagavate. One has to follow in the footsteps of great sages and devotees like Maitreya and Vidura, Maharaja Pariksit and Sukadeva Gosvami, and engage in the transcendental devotional service of the Lord if one would know His ultimate feature, which is above Brahman and Paramatma.**

## Chapter 7 - Further Inquiries by Vidura

## Texts 1-17: Vidura Inquires Further, and Maitreya Replies

**Question One (Texts 2-3), and Maitreya’s Reply (Text 9)**

After hearing Maitreya speak of the universal creation, ending with his description of the universal form, and after hearing him reverentially offer his respects to the Lord, the possessor of unlimited potencies, Vidura poses three questions about the Lord’s relationship with His material creation. Vidura has understood that the Lord is the creator and is simultaneously self-satisfied and detached. He wants to know, therefore, whether the Lord possesses desires that motivate Him to interact with the material energy. If so, does He become entangled by the material energy as the living entities do?

Maitreya states that the idea of the Lord being overcome by His own illusory energy is a contradiction; it goes against logic. The Lord’s material energy, by definition, necessarily remains under His control, just as the prison in a kingdom remains always subject to the king’s power. In his purport to Bhagavatam [3.7.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/7.9), Srila Prabhupada explains how the Lord is free from the influence of His own material energy:

**Srila Jiva Gosvami and Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, however, offer a very nice example in explanation. They say that although the sun is all light, the clouds, darkness and snowfall are all part and parcel of the sun. Without the sun there is no possibility of the sky’s being overcast with clouds or darkness, nor can there be snowfall on the earth. Although life is sustained by the sun, life is also disturbed by darkness and snowfall produced by the sun. But it is also a fact that the sun itself is never overcome by darkness, clouds or snowfall; the sun is far, far away from such disturbances. Only those who have a poor fund of knowledge say that the sun is covered by a cloud or by darkness. Similarly, the Supreme Brahman, or the Parabrahman, the Personality of Godhead, is always unaffected by the influence of the material energy, although it is one of His energies (parasya saktir vividhaiva sruyate).**

By contrast, Prabhupada also describes the effect the material energy has on the Lord’s part and parcel living entities: “The conditioned living entity, bewildered by the illusory energy, considers himself a part of the material creation due to forgetfulness of his spiritual identity, and thus he becomes entangled in material activities life after life. This material world is not for the purpose of the Lord Himself, but is for the conditioned souls who wanted to be controllers due to misuse of their God-gifted minute independence. Thus the conditioned souls are subjected to repeated birth and death.” (Bhag. [3.7.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/7.4), purport)

**Question Two (Texts 4-5), Question Three (Text 6), and Maitreya’s Replies (Texts 8-14)**

Vidura next asks how the living entity, who is spiritual and pure by constitution (as well as fully conscious of past, present, and future), becomes covered by ignorance. How can an eternal soul, who can become neither contaminated nor impure, be unable to remember his identity? He also asks about the relationship between the Supersoul and the living entities: With the Supersoul in the heart as a constant companion, how can a living entity’s activities continuously result in misfortune and misery?

Maitreya first distinguishes between the Lord’s position and that of the living entity (Bhag. [3.7.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/7.9)). While responding to Vidura’s second and third questions, Maitreya characterizes the living entity, who is eternally part and parcel of the Lord, as always pure—just as the Lord is always pure—but infinitesimal. Due to its minute size, the soul can be placed under mayd’s influence and, in a dreaming, illusory state, forget its actual nature. Covered by forgetfulness and suffering illusion, the soul experiences misery despite its unbreakable relationship with the Lord. This can be compared to the moon appearing to quiver when its reflection is viewed on water. As the moon does not actually quiver, so the soul does not actually suffer. The soul’s “quivering” is caused by maya, which forces us to misconceive our own identity, seeing ourselves as if we were in the reflection of the material energy.

The great sage Maitreya then offers the cure for suffering: devotional service. Devotional service awakens one to truth and reinstates one in his actual position as the Lord’s servant: “Simply by chanting and hearing of the transcendental name, form, etc., of the Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, one can achieve the cessation of unlimited miserable conditions. Therefore what to speak of those who have attained attraction for serving the flavor of the dust of the Lord’s lotus feet?” (Bhag. [3.7.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/7.14))

Prabhupada describes two stages of devotional service in his purport to this text: “The two stages of executing devotional service are, first, the stage of practicing devotional service with our present senses under the regulations of the recognized scriptures and, second, attaining sincere attachment for serving the particles of the dust of the lotus feet of the Lord. The first stage is called sadhana^bhakti, or devotional service for the neophyte, which is rendered under the direction of a pure devotee, and the second stage is called raga-bhakti, in which the mature devotee automatically takes to the various services of the Lord out of sincere attachment. ... By practicing sadhana-bhakti one may gradually rise to the point of rdga-bhakti, and by performing raga-bhakti in loving transcendental service one can even control the Supreme Powerful Lord.” In his purport to text 12, Srila Prabhupada describes a necessary element in the awakening from illusion to attain the Lord’s loving service: “Lord Vasudeva is pleased by devotional service only, and thus His mercy is realized by association with pure devotees of the Lord. Pure devotees of the Lord are transcendental to all material desires, including the desire for the results of fruitive activities and philosophical speculation. If one wants to acquire the mercy of the Lord, he has to associate with pure devotees. Such association alone can, by degrees, release one from the quivering elements.”

Vidura concludes somewhat sarcastically that happiness visits only liberated souls and fools, because liberated souls have awakened from the dream and fools are like animals who remain enamored by it, unaware of their misery despite approaching death: “Both the lowest of fools and he who is transcendental to all intelligence enjoy happiness, whereas persons between them suffer the material pangs.” (Bhag. [3.7.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/7.17))

## Texts 18-22: Vidura’s Acceptance of Maitreya's Words

Vidura thanks Maitreya Muni for his answers and realizes that he should turn his attention from the dreamlike material world. “I am confident,” he says, “that by serving your feet it will be possible for me to give up the false idea. By serving the feet of the spiritual master, one is enabled to develop transcendental ecstasy in the service of the Personality of Godhead, who is the unchangeable enemy of the Madhu demon and whose service vanquishes one’s material distresses.” (Bhag. [3.7.18-19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/7.18)) The opportunity to offer service to someone fully engaged in the Lord’s service is extremely rare. By stating this, Vidura venerates both Maitreya and his own good fortune in having obtained Maitreya’s association.

Desiring to hear more about creation, Vidura inquires further about what he has heard.

## Texts 23-38: Vidura Questions Maitreya Muni Further

In the sixteen texts, 23-38, Vidura asks Maitreya approximately forty questions, one nestled inside another, and begs the muni to answer them along with any pertinent questions he has somehow neglected to ask. Maitreya’s responses, which scrutinize the creation, its organization, the lineages of procreators, the creation’s inhabitants and their activities, time, and the Lord’s incarnations, will take us to the end of the Fourth Canto.

## Chapter 8 - Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu

## Texts 1-9: Maitreya Begins his Answers

Maitreya praises Vidura’s inquiries because answering them will expand the Lord’s glories. Therefore he decides to speak Bhagavata Purana, which was originally spoken by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, because hearing the Bhagavatam can solve all of humanity’s problems.

Prabhupada glorifies hearing the Bhagavatam in his purport to Bhagavatam [3.8.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/8.2): “The sage Maitreya proposed to speak on Srimad-Bhagavatam because it was especially compiled, and traditionally comes down in the disciplic succession, for the solution of all the problems of human society. Only one who is fortunate can have the opportunity to hear Srimad-Bhagavatam in the association of pure devotees of the Lord. ... If one comes in contact with the book Bhagavatam as well as with the devotee bhagavata, who knows what the Bhagavatam is, then such a fortunate man gets out of the material entanglement. Therefore Maitreya Muni, out of compassion for the suffering men in the world, proposes to speak on the Srimad-Bhagavatam first and last.”

Maitreya first relates his own history of hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam from his guru, Parasara Muni. Parasara had heard the Bhagavatam from Sankhyayana Muni, who had heard it from Sanat-kumara, who had heard it from Lord Sahkarsana, Anantadeva, the divine many-hooded serpent living in the depths of the Garbhodaka Ocean.

## Texts 10-21: The Creation Continues—Brahma’s Birth and Meditation

Maitreya then continues his description of creation (from where he left off at the end of Chapter Six). Garbhodakasayi Visnu appeared as if asleep, resting alone on Ananta Sesa in the waters that had previ-ously devastated the universe. At that time, both the material energy and the living entities (wrapped in their subtle bodies) were wound up within Him.

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on the conditioned souls’ birth in matter. He cites Bhagavatam [10.87.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/87.31), and then states: When the material world is finally destroyed, the individual souls, as well as their dormant material desires, enter the Supreme Personality of Godhead. When the material world is again created, these souls become attracted to the various transformations of matter and, their material desires aroused, again take birth in material bodies.

Rebellious souls averse to the Lord are bom in material bodies. When the body is bom, the bewildered soul inhabiting it also thinks himself bom; he considers his existence as having begun at that point. Prabhupada describes the conditioned soul’s unfortunate mentality after having taken his birth: “The fruitive workers are described in Bhagavad-gita as mudhas, or foolish. Such foolish living entities are very enthusiastic to work for some temporary benefit within perpetual bondage. One thinks himself very clever throughout his life if he is able to leave behind him a great asset of wealth for his children, and to achieve this temporary benefit he takes the risk of all sinful activities, without knowledge that such activities will keep him perpetually bound by the shackles of material bondage.” (Bhag. [3.8.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/8.12), purport)

Maitreya Muni next explains that after one thousand yuga cycles of lying inside Garbhodakasayi Visnu’s body, the living entities, under the influence of time, prepare to emerge and again begin fruitively motivated action. While the Lord was lying down, a subtle form containing all the living entities’ karma suddenly pierced His abdomen. By His supreme will, that energy took on the shape of a lotus stem and gradually grew into a bud. The lotus, which was the virat-rupa, the Lord’s gigantic subtle universal form, had been amalgamated in the Lord at the time of the previous universal dissolution. As it grew, it illuminated everything and dried up the vast waters of devastation. The Lord then expanded Himself as Ksirodakasayi Visnu, the Supersoul of all living entities, and entered into the lotus. It was on that lotus that Lord Brahma took birth.

Commenting on Lord Brahma’s genesis as described in text 15, Jiva Gosvami writes (Paramdtmd-sandarbha, anuccheda 8): “To create the material world, Lord Visnu, by His inconceivable potency, entered the lotus flower and personally (svayam) became Brahma. Then as a potter fashions pots and other things from clay, He fashioned the material universe from the various material ingredients.”

Srila Prabhupada’s comments on text 15 further explain the lotus: “This lotus flower is the universal virat form, or the gigantic form of the Lord in the material world. It becomes amalgamated in the Personality of Godhead Visnu, in His abdomen, at the time of dissolution, and it becomes manifest at the time of creation. ... In this form is the sum total of all the fruitive activities of the living entities conditioned by material nature, and the first of them, namely Brahma, or the controller of the universe, is generated from this lotus flower.”

Sitting on the whorl of the lotus, Brahma, who possessed the desire to create but not the ability, could neither understand his surroundings, the lotus on which he sat, nor his own self. Seeking understanding, he entered into the water through the stem of the lotus and tried to discover his source. Searching deeper into the lotus, Brahma perceived the Lord’s cakra, the devastating time factor. Becoming fearful, he returned to the lotus.

Neither Brahma nor the total past, present, or future scientists can fully understand the complexity of creation. Srila Prabhupada’s comment to text 17 is authoritative and to the point: “No one . . . can know the mystery of the creation and cosmic manifestation simply by mental speculation. The human being is so limited in his capacity that without the help of the Supreme he can hardly understand the mystery of the will of the Lord in terms of creation, continuance and destruction.”

Trying again to understand, but by a different method, Brahma sat with focused intelligence and meditated on the Supreme Lord, the ultimate cause of everything. Brahma’s meditation ultimately brought him success, because he renounced his own attempt to understand and instead surrendered himself in devotional service.

Srila Prabhupada comments on text 19: “By dint of one’s personal endeavor one may go nearer to the Lord, but without the Lord’s mercy one cannot reach the ultimate point. Such understanding of the Lord is possible only by devotional service, as confirmed in Bhagavad-gita ([18.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.55)): bhaktya mam abhijanati yavan yas casmi tattvatah.”

Two purports later he writes: “To cease from personal sense endeavors and to concentrate on the supreme cause is a sign of selfsurrender, and when self-surrender is present, that is a sure sign of devotional service. Each and every living entity needs to engage in devotional service to the Lord if he wishes to understand the ultimate cause of his existence.” (Bhag. [3.8.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/8.21), purport)

On text 22 he writes: “One has to wait for the mercy of the Lord before one can either render service unto Him or know Him as He is.”

## Texts 22-33: Brahma Performs Austerities and Sees the Lord

In due course the self-bom Brahma, having engaged in meditation for one hundred years, developed the intelligence to automatically see in his own heart that person he had been unable to see despite great endeavor. Brahma saw the illustrious and beautiful Lord, who was lying like a mountain of green coral on Sesa-naga. He was helmeted, bejeweled, and fantastically beautiful with His decorations of tulasi leaves and flower garlands. Pleased with Brahma, the merciful Lord smiled and raised His lotus feet, which offer pure devotional service. Brahma thus concluded that the Lord he was seeing was Hari, the Personality of Godhead, who is protected by His own Sudarsana cakra.

Srila Prabhupada describes this scene further in his purport to text 26: “According to the Gopala-tapani Upanisad, the Lord showed one of the many thousands of petals of His lotus feet. It is said: brahmano ’sav anavaratam me dhyatah stutah parardhante so 'budhyata gopa-veso me purastat avirbabhuva. . . . Lord Brahma could understand the transcendental form of the Lord as Sri Krsna, in the dress of a cowherd boy, and thus he recorded his experience in the Brahma-samhitd in the famous prayer, govindam adi-purusarh tarn aham bhajami."

By the Lord’s grace, Brahma simultaneously saw and knew his own source as well as the immediate cause of creation, the navel of Visnu, from which the lotus flower on which he sat had grown. Brahma immediately understood the waters and winds that had caused devastation as well as the vast universal sky. Empowered by Krsna’s creative potency (mode of passion) and desiring to create, Brahma began to pray.

## Chapter 9 - Brahma’s Prayers for Creative Energy

## Texts 1-5: Part One, True Fortune Means Accepting the Shelter of the Lord’s Lotus Feet

Lord Brahma says: О my Lord, today, after many, many years of practicing penance, I have attained true fortune: I have come to see and know You, the ultimate object of knowledge. No one and nothing is superior to You. Your form is nonmaterial and is composed of Your spiritual, internal potency, as are the forms of all Your incarnations. These incarnations, who descend by Your mercy, are equally auspicious. We are meant to meditate on them. Those who are destined for hell neglect Your personal form and speculate on matter instead.

In his purport to Bhagavatam [3.9.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.1), Prabhupada powerfully states why the living entities fail to know Krsna: “The Lord has employed His wonderful material energy in manifesting many wonderful distractions in the material world, and the conditioned souls, illusioned by the same energy, are thus unable to know the supreme cause. The most stalwart scientists and philosophers, therefore, cannot be accepted as wonderful. They only appear wonderful because they are instruments in the hands of the illusory energy of the Lord. Under illusion, the general mass of people deny the existence of the Supreme Lord and accept the foolish products of illusory energy as supreme.”

Brahma continues: I attempted to understand my source and couldn’t, but by Your mercy I now see it clearly. I am bom from the lotus flower grown from Your navel, and although I tend to become covered by maya and therefore become proud of my physical strength, You are the actual cause of the cosmic manifestation and are completely untouched by maya or matter. I surrender unto You. Matter does not even touch the rays emanating from Your transcendental body. Those who meditate on Your lotus feet through the Vedic mantras accept devotional service to You, and You never separate Yourself from the lotus of their hearts.

In his purport to text 5, Srila Prabhupada explains the importance of the Lord’s lotus feet: “For the pure devotee of the Lord there is nothing beyond the lotus feet of the Lord, and the Lord knows that such devotees do not wish anything more than that. The word tu specifically establishes this fact. The Lord also does not wish to be separated from the lotus hearts of those pure devotees. That is the transcendental relationship between the pure devotees and the Personality of Godhead. Because the Lord does not wish to separate Himself from the hearts of such pure devotees, it is understood that they are specifically dearer than the impersonalists.”

In Bhagavata sandarbha, anuccheda 50, just before citing and commenting on texts 2-4 of this chapter, Jiva Gosvami states that one should consider the Lord’s form fully spiritual because it is eternal, all-powerful, all-pervading, the shelter of everything, transcendental to all gross and subtle forms of material energy, manifest in the hearts of all conditioned souls, manifest only by His own wish, and clearly described in all Vedic literature. It is that form that the supreme philosopher, Lord Brahma, has described in texts 2-4.

Sridhara Svami points out a possible objection: Isn’t it true that you, Brahma, have not actually seen the transcendental Supreme Godhead (saguna brahman)? You may have seen some form, but the form you saw was composed of the three modes of material nature. It is not at all transcendental, for the transcendental Supreme Godhead is devoid of all form and qualities.

He then responds to his own objection: Thinking someone might argue like this, Brahma states in text 2 that the form he sees is eternally free from material contamination (avabodha--rasodayena sasvan~ nivrtta'tamasah) and has advented voluntarily to show the devotees mercy (sad'anugrahaya adau grhitam). This incarnation is the origin of the other incarnations (avatara'Sataika'bijam), who are all situated on the platform of transcendental goodness. “I, the raja-guna-avatara, am born from the lotus flower grown from that Lord’s navel (yan-ndbhi'padma'bhavanad aham avirasam).”

Sridhara Svami continues: In the second of these texts (Bhag. [3.9.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.3)), Brahma states: “O my Lord (parama), I do not see (na pasyami) a form superior (param) to Your present form (bhavatah svarupam), which is composed of eternal bliss and knowledge. In your impersonal Brahman effulgence in the spiritual sky (ananda-matram), there is no occasional change (avikalpam), and no deterioration of Your internal potency (aviddha-varcah). I surrender unto You (asrito ’smi) because whereas I am proud of my material body and senses (bhutendriyatmaka-modus), You are the ultimate object of worship. You are the cause of the cosmic manifestation (visva-srjam) and are therefore different from the universe (avisvan). Moreover, You are the cause of the created beings’ senses.”Sridhara Svami then states that Lord Brahma speaks the third text (Bhag. [3.9.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.4)) thinking that someone might consider that the Supreme Lord’s form had been manifest—that is, that it is not eternal:

**This present form, or any transcendental form expanded by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, is equally auspicious for all the universes (bhuvana-mangala). Since You have manifest this eternal personal form on whom we, Your devotees, meditate (upasakanam mangalaya dhyane darsitam), I offer my respectful obeisances unto You (tubby am bhagavate ’nuvidhema). It would not be appropriate for You to show a materially conditioned form to us, whose minds are absorbed in the path of the unmanifest (avyakta-vartma). I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.**

**At this point Krsna Himself may object: “If this is true, why then do some decline to worship Me?” To answer this doubt, Lord Brahma explains that the Lord’s personal form is neglected (yo ’nadrto) by those who accept faulty, atheistic philosophy (asat-prasangaih).**

Jiva Gosvami, who offered these quotations from Sridhara Svami in Bhagavat-sandarbha, explains that because Brahma is the spiritual master of the greatest philosophers, he never accepts any viewpoint opposed to what he has expressed in these texts. The impersonalists and atheists, however, do not accept his statements.

Sri Jiva adds that the Supreme Person’s transcendental form is clearly established by all authorities, yet the atheists reject the direct experience of learned devotees and insist that God does not exist. On the other hand, the devotees, who are qualified to properly understand the Supreme Lord’s form, are described in text 5 of this section. There, Brahma uses the word tu, “but,” to contrast the Lord’s devotees with the previously described nondevotees: “O Lord, the devotees have faith in the existence of Your transcendental form because they accept the Vedic revelation as the highest source of knowledge. They smell the aroma of Your lotus feet, which is carried by the air of Vedic sound (sruti-vata-nitam) through the holes of their ears, and they accept devotional service to Your lotus feet (bhaktya grhita-caranah).

## Texts 6-10: Part Two, Those Unable to Accept the Shelter of the Lord’s Feet

Hearing of the singular focus required to understand the Lord, we may ask how one involved in family life can possibly serve only the Lord’s feet and think always of His name, fame, and qualities. To this Brahma replies that pure devotees, even those with families, are free of the anxieties that naturally surround family affairs because they have surrendered proprietorship of their homes to the Lord. In his book Saranagati, Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura also sings of surrendering one’s family, home, possessions, and self to Krsna: “Mind, body, family, and whatever else may be mine, I have surrendered at Your lotus feet, О youthful son of Nanda! In good fortune or in bad, in life or in death, all my difficulties have disappeared by accepting those feet of Yours as my only shelter. Slay me or protect me as You wish, for You have full authority over Your eternal servant. If it is Your wish that I be bom again, then may I take birth in the home of Your devotee. May I be bom again even as a worm, as long as I remain Your devotee. I have no desire to be bom as a Brahma averse to You. I yearn for the company of that devotee who is completely devoid of all desire for worldly enjoyment or liberation. Father, mother, lover, son, Lord, preceptor, and husband—You are everything to me. Bhaktivinoda says, ‘“О Капа, please hear me! О Lord of Radha, You are my life and soul!”’

Srila Prabhupada acknowledges the difficulties that come with household life, but points to Brahma’s words in text 6 as the solution: “A pure devotee of the Lord never thinks of himself as the proprietor of his home. He surrenders everything unto the supreme control of the Lord, and thus he has no fear for maintaining his family or protecting the interests of his family. Because of this surrender, he no longer has any attraction for wealth. Even if there is attraction for wealth, it is not for sense enjoyment, but for the service of the Lord. . . . Thus the acquisition of wealth by a devotee is not a source of anxieties, as is the case for a worldly man. And because a pure devotee accepts everything in the sense of serving the Lord, the poisonous teeth of accumulation of wealth are extracted. If a snake has its poison removed and bites a man, there is no fatal effect. Similarly, wealth accumulated in the cause of the Lord has no poisonous teeth, and the effect is not fatal. A pure devotee is never entangled in material worldly affairs even though he may remain in the world like an ordinary man.”

Brahma continues, stating that it is those who do not chant and hear about the Lord who are truly unfortunate. These people are overwhelmed by sensual desires and are entangled and controlled by illusion. It becomes impossible for them to overcome the perplexing miseries of life. “I take pity on them, and I am very much aggrieved for them.” (Bhag. [3.9.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.8))

Factually, Brahma states, these material miseries do not affect the soul because only those under maya’s influence—who feel themselves independent of the Lord and who wish to view their bodies as the vehicle to achieve sense pleasure—experience misery. Thus everyone in maya’s kingdom is frustrated and troubled. Everyone—even the great sage—who neglects the cure and does not take shelter of hearing krsna-katha continues to revolve in the painful cycle of birth and death.

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 10 vividly describes the painful life of Kali-yuga materialists: “Most of them engage during the daytime in hard physical labor; their senses are engaged very extensively in troublesome duties in the gigantic plants of heavy industrial enterprise. The owners of such factories are engaged in finding a market for their industrial products, and the laborers are engaged in extensive production involving huge mechanical arrangements. ‘Factory’ is another name for hell. At night, hellishly engaged persons take advantage of wine and women to satisfy their tired senses, but they are not even able to have sound sleep because their various mental speculative plans constantly interrupt their sleep. Because they suffer from insomnia sometimes they feel sleepy in the morning for lack of sufficient rest. By the arrangement of supernatural power, even the great scientists and thinkers of the world suffer frustration of their various plans and thus rot in the material world birth after birth.”

## Texts 11-13: Part Three, The Lord's Reciprocation

How wonderfully the Lord reciprocates with those who hear about Him! Brahma explains: “O my Lord, Your devotees can see You through the ears by the process of bona fide hearing, and thus their hearts become cleansed, and You take Your seat there. You are so merciful to Your devotees that You manifest Yourself in the particular eternal form of transcendence in which they always think of You.” (Bhag. [3.9.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.11))Once a devotee’s heart is cleansed by hearing, the Lord mercifully sits in that pure heart in the exact eternal form in which His devotee has always thought of Him. Srila Prabhupada describes Krsna’s subordination to His devotee in his purport to this text: the Lord appears before His devotee because of the devotee’s intense desire to serve a specific form.

**The sruteksita path is to hear from bona fide devotees who are conversant with Vedic wisdom, free from mundane sentiment. By this bona fide hearing process, the neophyte devotee becomes cleansed of all material rubbish, and thus he becomes attached to one of the many transcendental forms of the Lord, as described in the Vedas.**

**This attachment of the devotee to a particular form of the Lord is due to natural inclination. Each and every living entity is originally attached to a particular type of transcendental service because he is eternally the servitor of the Lord. Lord Caitanya says that the living entity is eternally a servitor of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna. Therefore, every living entity has a particular type of service relationship with the Lord, eternally. This particular attachment is invoked by practice of regulative devotional service to the Lord, and thus the devotee becomes attached to the eternal form of the Lord, exactly like one who is already eternally attached. This attachment for a particular form of the Lord is called svarupa-siddhi. The Lord sits on the lotus heart of the devotee in the eternal form the pure devotee desires, and thus the Lord does not part from the devotee...**

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments on text 11:

**The devotees, however, even without knowledge, cross over the ocean of birth and death. From this verse it is clear that by devotion these devotees make even You subservient.**

**It can also be explained: bhakti-yoga paribhavita, inspired only by bhakti-yoga, the Lord in all respects (pari) reveals Himself to those who approach Him with fixed devotion. Thus it is understood that the means of evoking the Lord’s manifestation is only bhakti-yoga.**

**Due to their devotion, You come onto the lotus of their hearts, and having come, You stay. That You do not go away has already been stated in Bhagavatam** [**3.9.5**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.5)**: napaisi natha, “You are never separated from the lotus of their hearts.”**

**The path to reach You is first heard from the guru’s mouth and then seen and perceived directly. By that same path (hearing from one’s guru) You enter into the lotus of their hearts. This implies that among all the paths, the devotees \[who have heard from the guru’s mouth\] perfectly ascertain the exact way of practicing sadhana-bhakti. The further implication is that if someone has a desire to attain the Lord, he should also seek to thoroughly ascertain the path.**

**Moreover, if even without hearing Your devotee fixes his mind on a particular form of Yours in meditation, You then manifest that exact form.” So says the revered Sridhara Svami.**

**Or else it means: Those practicing devotees, by their intelligence, meditate on a certain form according to their particular mood and You manifest that exact body for them, which is their siddha-deha, their body of perfection, making them obtain it in all its splendor. Oh, how submissive to Your devotees You are! This is the purport.**

Brahma then offers his obeisances to He who remains in everyone’s heart and is satisfied neither by those who worship the demigods, those who perform pious Vedic rituals or austerities, nor those who worship His impersonal feature. Rather, Brahma says that those who offer the fruits of their Vedic rituals, penances, or service to the Lord for His satisfaction never lose.

## Texts 14-19: Part Four, Obeisances to the Lord

Brahma, the most respectable person, then offers obeisances to the Supreme Transcendence and Enjoyer, who creates, maintains, and dissolves the cosmos: “Let me take shelter of the lotus feet of Him whose incarnations, qualities and activities are mysterious imitations of worldly affairs. One who invokes His transcendental names, even unconsciously, at the time he quits this life, is certainly washed immediately of the sins of many, many births and attains Him without fail.” (Bhag. [3.9.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.15))

He continues: Let me take shelter of the primary root and the complete tree of material existence, who as time ultimately destroys the plans of the fruitive workers. By Your will You incarnate in various species and perform transcendental pastimes. I offer You my obeisances because You have manifest in these different forms.

## Texts 20-26: Part Five, Request for Empowerment to Create

Brahma has surrendered to the Lord through his prayers. Now he requests the Lord for the power to create the universe as it was before the devastation: “O object of my worship . . . All these planets of the universe were stationed within Your transcendental abdomen while You were enjoying sleep. Now, Your sleep having ended, Your eyes are open like blossoming lotuses in the morning. Let the Supreme Lord be merciful towards me. . . . May He be merciful towards me so that I, as before, may be empowered with the introspection to create, for I am also one of the surrendered souls who are dear to the Lord. \[You are\] always the benefactor of the surrendered souls. \[Your\] activities are always enacted through \[Your\] internal potency, Rama, or the goddess of fortune. I pray only to engage in \[Your\] service in the creation of the material world, and I pray that I not be materially affected by my works, for thus I may be able to give up the false prestige of being the creator. ... I am now engaged in manifesting \[Your\] diverse energies in the form of the cosmic manifestation. I therefore pray that in the course of my material activities I may not be deviated from the vibration of the Vedic hymns.”

Brahma adds: “The Lord, who is supreme and is the oldest of all, is unlimitedly merciful. I wish that He may smilingly bestow His benediction upon me by opening His lotus eyes. He can uplift the entire cosmic creation and remove our dejection by kindly speaking His directions.” (Bhag. [3.9.21-25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.21))

Prabhupada’s purports to texts 22-24 speak of working humbly in surrender, free from the pride of our apparent achievements and completely focused on Krsna consciousness: “Brahma prayed to the Lord because He is very much dear to the surrendered soul. The surrendered soul knows nothing but the Lord, and therefore the Lord is very affectionate towards him.” (Bhag. [3.9.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.22), purport)

From the purport to text 23:

**Brahma, who is only an assistant in the modes of creation, wanted to remain in his actual position as an instrument of the Lord instead of becoming puffed up by the false prestige of thinking himself the creator. That is the way of becoming dear to the Supreme Lord and receiving His benediction. Foolish men want to take credit for all creations made by them, but intelligent persons know very well that not a blade of grass can move without the will of the Lord; thus all the credit for wonderful creations must go to Him. By spiritual consciousness only can one be free from the contamination of material affection and receive the benedictions offered by the Lord.**

From the purport to text 24:

**Every person engaged in the transcendental loving service of the Lord in this material world is prone to so many material activi-ties, and if one is not strong enough to protect himself against the onslaught of material affection, he may be diverted from the spiritual energy. In the material creation Brahma has to create all kinds of living entities with bodies suitable to their material conditions. Brahma wants to be protected by the Lord because he has to contact many, many vicious living entities. An ordinary brahmana may fall from the brahma-tejas, or the power of brahminical excellence, due to his association with many fallen, conditioned souls. Brahma, as the supermost brahmana, is afraid of such a falldown, and therefore he prays to the Lord for protection. This is a warning for one and all in the spiritual advancement of life. Unless one is sufficiently protected by the Lord, he may fall down from his spiritual position; therefore one has to pray constantly to the Lord for protection and the blessing to carry out one’s duty. Lord Caitanya also entrusted His missionary work to His devotees and assured them of His protection against the onslaught of material affection. The path of spiritual life is stated in the Vedas to be like the edge of a sharpened razor. A little inattentiveness may at once create havoc and bloodshed, but one who is a completely surrendered soul, always seeking protection from the Lord in the discharge of his entrusted duties, has no fear of falling into material contamination.**

“The sage Maitreya said: О Vidura, after observing the source of his appearance, namely the Personality of Godhead, Brahma prayed for His mercy as far as his mind and words would permit him. Thus having prayed, he became silent, as if tired from his activities of penance, knowledge and mental concentration.” (Bhag. [3.9.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.26))

## Texts 27-44: The Lord Responds to Brahma’s Prayers

Brahma is afraid of the waters of devastation surrounding him and anxious about his ability to create the universe. Knowing this, the Lord replies to Brahma’s prayers with deep, thoughtful, reassuring words: “O Brahma, О depth of Vedic wisdom, be neither depressed nor anxious about the execution of creation. What you are begging from Me has already been granted before. О Brahma, situate yourself in penance and meditation and follow the principles of knowledge to receive My favor. By these actions you will be able to understand everything from within your heart.” (Bhag. [3.9.29-30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.29)) The Lord tells Brahma that when he absorbs himself in devotional service, he will see Him within himself, in all living entities, and throughout the universe, because He is situated in all those places just as fire is contained within wood. Brahma will also see that the universe, all living entities, and he himself are within the Lord. “Only in that state of transcendental vision will you be able to be free from all kinds of illusion.” (Bhag. [3.9.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.32))

Srila Prabhupada’s purports to texts 29-32 contain both instructions and reassurance for those entrusted with the Lord’s service. From the purport to text 29:

**Any person authorized by either the Lord or by His bona fide representative is already blessed, as is the work entrusted to him. Of course, the person entrusted with such a responsibility should always be aware of his incapability and must always look for the mercy of the Lord for the successful execution of his duty. One should not be puffed up because he is entrusted with certain executive work. Fortunate is he who is so entrusted, and if he is always fixed in the sense of being subordinate to the will of the Supreme, he is sure to come out successful in the discharge of his work. . . . Anyone who takes pride in doing responsible work but does not give credit to the Supreme Lord is certainly falsely proud and cannot execute anything nicely. Brahma and persons in the line of his disciplic succession who follow in his footsteps are always successful in the discharge of loving transcendental service to the Supreme Lord.**

From the purport to text 30:

**The mercy the Lord bestows upon a particular person engaged in executing the responsible work entrusted unto him is beyond imagination. But His mercy is received due to our penance and perseverance in executing devotional service. Brahma was entrusted with the work of creating the planetary systems. The Lord instructed him that when he meditated he would very easily know where and how the planetary systems must be arranged. The directions were to come from within, and there was no necessity for anxiety in that task. Such instructions of buddhi-yoga are directly imparted by the Lord from within, as confirmed in Bhagavad-gita (**[**10.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.10)**).**

From the purport to text 31:

**It is cited herein by the Lord that during his daytime Brahma would see Him as Lord Sri Krsna. He would appreciate how the Lord expanded Himself into all the calves during His childhood at Vrndavana, he would know how Yasodamayi saw all the universes and planetary systems within the mouth of Krsna during His playful childhood pastimes, and he would also see that there are many millions of Brahmas during the appearance of Lord Krsna in Brahma’s daytime. But all these manifestations of the Lord, appearing everywhere in His eternal, transcendental forms, cannot be understood by anyone but the pure devotees, who are always engaged in devotional service to the Lord and are fully absorbed in the Lord. The high qualifications of Brahma are also indicated herein.**

From the purport to text 32:

**Brahma prayed that he might not forget his eternal relationship with the Lord during the course of his material activities. In answer to that prayer, the Lord said that he should not think of existing without a relationship with His omnipotency. The example is given of the fire in wood. The fire kindled in wood is always the same, although the wood may be of different types. Similarly, the bodies within the material creation may be specifically different according to shape and quality, but the spirit souls within them are not different from one another. The quality of fire, warmth, is the same everywhere, and the spiritual spark, or part and parcel of the Supreme Spirit, is the same in every living being; thus the potency of the Lord is distributed all over His creation. This transcendental knowledge alone can save one from the contamination of material illusion. Since the Lord’s potency is distributed everywhere, a pure soul, or devotee of the Lord, can see everything in relationship with the Lord, and therefore he has no affection for the outer coverings. That pure spiritual conception makes him immune to all contamination of material association. The pure devotee never forgets the touch of the Lord in all circumstances.**

The Lord continues His instructions: By attaining transcendence, you will remain free from illusion as well as from the gross and subtle coverings that encase your true self. You will thus be established in natural, pure, spontaneous loving service. You desired to recreate the universe and increase the population, but you feared you would think yourself the doer and thus become covered by passion and illusion. This will never happen. “My causeless mercy upon you will always increase for all time. You are the original rsi, and because your mind is always fixed on Me, even though you will be engaged in generating various progeny, the vicious mode of passion will never encroach upon you.” (Bhag. [3.9.34-35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.34))

It is worth noting that the Lord has blessed Brahma to be able to see Him everywhere and in all things (Bhag. [3.9.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.31)). Krsna previously defined this vision as the goal of sadhana-bhakti in the third catuh-sloki text (Bhag. [2.9.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/9.35)). In text 35, Krsna has also assured Brahma that He will protect him from becoming influenced by the mode of passion. According to one’s position, one may be requested to perform Brahmasized service or something less significant. Still, the art of service rests not on the size of the endeavor but on one’s learning to perform it with devotion. While serving, humility—the awareness of one’s inability— gives birth to conscious dependence on Krsna. This is the secret of success. Krsna states: “In all activities just depend upon Me and work always under My protection. In such devotional service, be fully conscious of Me.” (Bg. [18.57](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.57)) In his purport to that verse, Prabhupada adds some practical guidelines: “\[O\]ne has no goal in life save and except acting in Krsna consciousness just to satisfy Krsna. And while working in that way, one should think of Krsna only: ‘I have been appointed to discharge this particular duty by Krsna.’ While acting in such a way, one naturally has to think of Krsna. This is perfect Krsna consciousness.”

The Lord tells Brahma that His form is folly spiritual and that the conditioned souls cannot know Him but that He has nevertheless revealed Himself to Brahma because He is pleased by his devotion offered in the form of austerities. Srila Prabhupada indirectly explains that the Lord considered Brahma’s penances devotional service because they were performed for His pleasure. He thus revealed Himself to Brahma, not exactly because of Brahma’s austerities, but because of the devotion the austerities represented. “Such spiritual perfection is not limited by material qualifications but is developed by dint of one’s sincere endeavor to render transcendental service. Voluntary endeavor is the only qualification for spiritual perfection. Material acquisitions of wealth or education are not considered.” (Bhag. [3.9.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.38), purport) Thus the Lord confirms that everything Brahma has offered—his penance as well as his prayers—has actually sprung from Him. Krsna is pleased with Brahma’s prayers and blesses his attempt to create the universe. “Any human being who prays like Brahma, and who thus worships Me, shall very soon be blessed with the fulfillment of all his desires, for I am the Lord of all benediction. It is the opinion of expert transcendentalists that the ultimate goal of performing all traditional good works, penances, sacrifices, charities, mystic activities, trances, etc., is to invoke My satisfaction. I am the Supersoul of every individual. I am the supreme director and the dearest. People are wrongly attached to the gross and subtle bodies, but they should be attached to Me only.” (Bhag. [3.9.40-42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.40))

Srila Jiva Gosvami cites text 41 in Priti-sandarbha, anuccheda 33, to show that love of God is the ultimate result obtained by following the spiritual practices described in the Vedas. “Persons who do not know tattva (atattva'Vidam), the actual truth, think other results are more important than satisfying Me (by developing priti or loving service for), the Supreme Personality of Godhead. These persons think of devotional service only as a means to other ends.”

In anuccheda 34 he comments that text 42 means “1 am supremely pure. 1 am the dearest (presthah) of all dear things (preyasam).
