People are wrongly attached to gross and subtle bodies (dehadir yat-krte priyah), but they should be attached only to Me.” And he presents another meaning: “Those who have the fault of not understanding Me do not do everything for Me. They do not understand that I (aham) am the Supersoul (atma). I am like the sun, and the individual souls (atmandtn) are like the rays of My sunlight.” The last sentence of Prabhupada’s purport to text 42 summarizes the Lord’s message to Brahma and indeed the conclusion of all sastra: “In all circumstances one should try to develop love of Godhead, and that will solve all contending problems.”

The Lord completed His reply with these words: “By following My instructions you can now generate the living entities as before, by dint of your complete Vedic wisdom and the body you have directly received from Me, the supreme cause of everything.” (Bhag. [3.9.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/9.43)) Then the Lord, in His Narayana form, disappeared.

## Chapter 10 - Divisions of the Creation

## Texts 1-9: Brahma Acts After the Lord Departs

Hearing the Lord’s response to Brahma’s prayers prompted Vidura to ask another question: How did Brahma proceed with the creation after receiving the Lord’s blessing? Suta Gosvami, who has been relating the conversation between Maitreya and Vidura to the sages at Naimisaranya, now continues the narration.

Brahma followed the Lord’s instructions and began to meditate. After one hundred celestial years, the lotus on which Brahma sat, along with the waters of devastation, began to rock violently due to a furious wind. But now Brahma possessed the power and practical wisdom accrued from his devotional austerities and was prepared to act. By Krsna’s empowerment Brahma quickly drank up both water and wind. He could then see that the lotus on which he was seated had spread throughout the universe. Within the lotus Brahma could see all planets and living entities in “seedling form,” for the Lord had generated them previously. Brahma then entered the lotus and began his service by disseminating those “same seedlings” throughout the universe.

One might ask: “If Krsna is the supreme controller and Brahma was engaged in His service, why should Brahma undergo so much trouble?” Srila Prabhupada responds to this query in his purport to text 5: “The material world is called illusory because it is a place of forgetfulness of the transcendental service of the Lord. Thus one engaged in the Lord’s devotional service in the material world may sometimes be very much disturbed by awkward circumstances. There is a declaration of war between the two parties, the illusory energy and the devotee, and sometimes the weak devotees fall victim to the onslaught of the powerful illusory energy. Lord Brahma, however, was sufficiently strong, by the causeless mercy of the Lord, and he could not be victimized by the material energy, although it gave him cause for anxiety when it managed to totter the existence of his position.”

Srila Prabhupada also explains (in his purport to text 7) why Brahma’s creation is considered secondary: “The seeds of all the planets in the universe were impregnated in the lotus on which Brahma was situated. All the planets were already generated by the Lord, and all the living entities were also bom in Brahma. The material world and the living entities were all already generated in seedling forms by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and Brahma was to disseminate the same seedlings all over the universe. The real creation is therefore called sarga, and, later on, the manifestation by Brahma is called visarga.”

Thus in answering Vidura’s questions about creation, Maitreya Muni confirmed what Brahma explained to Narada Muni. When Narada inquired about the identity of the creator, Brahma replied, “Inspired by Him only, I discover what is already created by Him \[Narayana\] under His vision as the all-pervading Supersoul, and I also am created by Him only.” (Bhag. [2.5.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.17)) In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada states the truth about the creator and His creation in a similar way: “Even Brahma, the creator of the universe, admits that he is not the actual creator but is simply inspired by the Lord Narayana and therefore creates under His superintendence those things already created by Him, the Supersoul of all living entities.”

Exalted Lord Brahma, blessed and empowered by the Lord, performed his service of creating the fourteen planetary systems so that they could be inhabited by living entities of various degrees of piety.

## Dialogue Three - Time, Destruction, and the Secondary Creation of Brahma

## Chapter 10 (Continued)

## Texts 10-13: Divisions of the Creation, Time

After hearing from Maitreya about the Lord’s primal creation (sarga) and His discussion with Brahma, Vidura inquires about time, another of the Lord’s potencies. Time is subtle; it cannot be observed directly. Only its effects reveal its existence. Days turn into nights, summers change into autumns, and years turn into centuries. Time is the energy of Krsna that moves the creation forward; time is eternal and irreversible. Maitreya begins by explaining that time is the source of the interaction between the modes of nature. It is the Supreme Lord’s catalyst in the material world, and through time He imposes the cycles of creation, maintenance, and dissolution.

Srila Prabhupada defines time in terms of its functional relationship with the Supreme Lord: “The impersonal time factor is the background of the material manifestation as the instrument of the Supreme Lord. It is the ingredient of assistance offered to material nature. No one knows where time began and where it ends, and it is time only which can keep a record of the creation, maintenance and destruction of the material manifestation. This time factor is the material cause of creation and is therefore a self-expansion of the Personality of Godhead. Time is considered the impersonal feature of the Lord.” (Bhag. [3.10.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/10.11), purport) In his purport to text 12, Srila Prabhupada also indicates that time is inextricable from maya; they are interwoven and separate the living entity from the Supreme Lord: “This unmanifested world is the self-same Personality of Godhead, but it appears to be something else beyond or besides the Lord. It appears so because of its being separated from the Lord by means of kala. It is something like the tape-recorded voice of a person who is now separated from the voice. As the tape recording is situated on the tape, so the whole cosmic manifestation is situated on the material energy and appears separate by means of kala.”

## Texts 14-30: Time’s Effects—The Ten Creations

Time effects change in the material energy. Maitreya therefore first describes nine varieties (plus a tenth) of creation and three types of annihilation (scheduled universal destruction, destruction caused by the fire emanating from Ananta Sesa’s mouth, and destruction caused by our own actions and reactions). Of the nine creations, the first six are categorized as sarga, for they are created directly by the Lord. Each of these creations moves from subtle to gross, gradually creating a material prison suitable for the prisoner-souls to inhabit. By interacting with the material energy, the prisoners either make spiritual advancement or add to their sentence by selfishly trying to enjoy the creation.

The sarga creations include 1. the mahat-tattva, 2. false ego, 3. sense perception (made of false ego combined with the mode of ignorance), 4. knowledge and the capacity to work (false ego combined with the mode of passion), 5. the mind and the controlling demigods (false ego combined with the mode of goodness), and 6. the darkness of ignorance: attachment, hatred, pride, ignorance, and false identification—the five kinds of illusion that cause material bondage, by which the living entities are illusioned and “act like fools.” The remaining three creations (visarga, or secondary creations) are the work of Lord Brahma, whom the Lord has infused with His material creative potency, the mode of passion. These creations use as ingredients everything that was produced by the Lord in His sarga creation.

Brahma’s creations are 7. the immovable entities, 8. the lower species of life, and 9. human beings. Of these, his seventh creation, the immovable entities—the varieties of trees and plants—are identified by beings that seek subsistence upward. These beings are almost unconscious, but can still experience pain. The eighth creation, the twentyeight varieties of lower life forms—including animals and birds— consists of ignorant beings. These beings detect their desirables by smell and have little memory. Human beings, Brahma’s ninth creation, are passionate. They are characterized by their ability to stock food in their bellies, their busyness, and their perpetual condition of suffering, although they consider themselves always happy. In his tenth creation, Brahma forms the eight varieties of superior beings.

## Chapter 11 - Calculation of Time, from the Atom

## Texts 1-15: Creating a Perspective of Time

Maitreya Muni moves from describing the effects of time as one sees them during creation and annihilation to defining how one can measure time. No one can measure time directly, because one can perceive it only by its effect on material objects. Maitreya Muni therefore begins his calculations from the indivisible and most minute material object, the atom. Maitreya uses as the primary unit of measurement a specific movement of atoms in space. This is similar to the way we may define a year or month by measuring the movements of the sun or moon. He terms that primal unit of time a truti, the length of time needed for three pairs of double atoms to combine. One hundred trutis make a vedha, and three vedhas make one lava. Maitreya Muni’s calculations gradually build from these minute measurements to increasingly larger units of time until he establishes the units for days, fortnights, months, years, and the length of a full day of the demigods (equal to one year of our time).

Through these measurements Maitreya notes that the lifespan of human beings has been fixed at one hundred years.

Maitreya then underscores time’s inevitable influence by stating: “Influential stars, planets, luminaries and atoms all over the universe are rotating in their respective orbits under the direction of the Supreme, represented by eternal kala.” (Bhag. [3.11.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/11.13)) Maitreya thus establishes a frame of reference by which we can understand that everything—regardless of its range of movement—remains under the control of kala, which is Krsna’s energy. Prabhupada provides us with the essence of this technical subject in his purport to text 14: “The subject matters of physics, chemistry, mathematics, astronomy, time and space dealt with in the above verses of Srimad-Bhagavatam are certainly very interesting to students of the particular subject, but as far as we are concerned, we cannot explain them very thoroughly in terms of technical knowledge. The subject is summarized by the statement that above all the different branches of knowledge is the supreme control of kala, the plenary representation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Nothing exists without Him, and therefore everything, however wonderful it may appear to our meager knowledge, is but the work of the magical wand of the Supreme Lord.”

## Texts 16-28: Still Longer Durations of Time

Vidura respectfully inquires further about the more lengthy time spans, spans beyond the range of one kalpa, one of Lord Brahma’s days. Maitreya Muni therefore continues to expand our concept of time by defining increasingly larger time measurements based on those he has already named. After determining that the time periods covered by the four yugas (Satya, Treta, Dvapara, and Kali) are equal to 12,000 years of the demigods, he denotes the effect of each of these yugas on religious tendencies: “O Vidura, in the Satya millennium mankind properly and completely maintained the principles of religion, but in other millenniums religion gradually decreased by one part as irreligion was proportionately admitted.” (Bhag. [3.11.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/11.21)) Srila Prabhupada comments: “In the Satya millennium, complete execution of religious principles prevailed. Gradually, the principles of religion decreased by one part in each of the subsequent millenniums. In other words, at present there is one part religion and three parts irreligion. Therefore people in this age are not very happy.”

The four yugas multiplied by one thousand equal one day on Lord Brahma’s planet, Maitreya tells Vidura, and a similar period comprises his night. The universes are sustained for the length of Brahma’s day, and in each of those days, fourteen Manus rule in succession, each reigning for his entire lifespan. Every Manu’s life continues for a little more than seventy-one sets of four millenniums (306,720,000 years), and a smaller devastation occurs at each Manu’s death. “After the dissolution of each and every Manu, the next Manu comes in order, along with his descendants, who rule over the different planets; but the seven famous sages, and demigods like Indra and their followers, such as the Gandharvas, all appear simultaneously with Manu. . . . In each and every change of Manu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead appears by manifesting His internal potency in different incarnations, as Manu and others.” (Bhag. [3.11.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/11.25), [27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/11.27)) Throughout the creation and the changing Manus, the Lord continues to maintain the universe.

During Brahma’s night, Maitreya explains, time causes the universe to merge fully with darkness. During that dissolution, neither the sun nor moon provide light. Prabhupada offers a dramatic description: “The innumerable living entities merge into that dissolution, which appears to be the dropping of the curtain of the scene of the Supreme Lord’s energy, and so everything becomes silent.” (Bhag. [3.11.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/11.28), purport)

## Texts 29-38: Devastations

Maitreya Muni tells more about the subsequent devastation: “When the night of Brahma ensues, all the three worlds are out of sight, and the sun and the moon are without glare, just as in the due course of an ordinary night.” (Bhag. [3.11.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/11.29)) A fire emanates from Sahkarsana and rages throughout most of the universe. Being distressed by the heat, great sages like Bhrgu transport themselves to Janaloka. The fire rages for one hundred years of the demigods, or 36,000 human years. Then during the next 36,000 years, torrents of rain accompanied by violent winds and high waves cause the seas and oceans to overflow. The three worlds fill with water. At that time, the Lord lies down to rest on Ananta Sesa, and closes His eyes in mystic slumber. The inhabitants of Janaloka then approach Him, and with folded hands, glorify Him with prayers. Maitreya presses toward his conclusion: “Thus the process of the exhaustion of the duration of life exists for every one of the living beings, including Lord Brahma. One’s life endures for only one hundred years, in terms of the times in the different planets.” (Bhag. [3.11.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/11.33))

In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada calls it madness to refuse to face inevitable death: “This is the madness of human society. The madman has no responsibility in life. Similarly, a human being who does not develop a sense of responsibility before he dies is no better than the madman who tries to enjoy material life very happily without concern for the future. It is necessary that every human being be responsible in preparing himself for the next life, even if he has a duration of life like that of Brahma, the greatest of all living creatures within the universe.”

Maitreya next explains that the one hundred years of Brahma’s life—and we will also hear of the devastation that follows them— are divided into two 50-year parts. Brahma is now in the second half of his lifetime. Death is inevitable, then, even for Brahma. “In the beginning of the first half of Brahma’s life, there was a millennium called Brahma-kalpa, wherein Lord Brahma appeared. The birth of the Vedas was simultaneous with Brahma’s birth. The millennium which followed the first Brahma millennium is known as the Padma-kalpa because in that millennium the universal lotus flower grew out of the navel reservoir of water of the Personality of Godhead, Hari. О descendant of Bharata, the first millennium in the second half of the life of Brahma is also known as the Varaha millennium because the Personality of Godhead appeared in that millennium as the hog incarnation.” (Bhag. [3.11.35-37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/11.35))

Brahma has already mentioned his birth on a lotus flower in Bhagavatam [2.6.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/6.23), and Maitreya Muni has also recently described it in Bhagavatam [3.8.15-16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/8.15). The birth of the Vedas from Brahma will be described in Bhagavatam [3.12.35-39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.35), and Varahadeva’s appearance will be described in the thirteenth chapter of the Third Canto. The killing of Hiranyaksa will be described later in the Third Canto, chapters Eighteen and Nineteen.

Srila Sridhara Svami discusses Varahadeva’s birth in his commentary on text 35: “Lord Varaha appeared in the first manvantara, when the earth was plunged in the water. At that time Varaha, bom from the demigod Brahma’s nostril, rescued the earth and fought with Hiran-yaksa. That is one description of Varahadeva. Lord Varahadeva also appeared during the sixth manvantara. At that time He was bom from Diti, the daughter of Prajapati Daksa. Because in both appearances Lord Varaha rescued the earth when it was plunged in water, the two appearances are described in a single narration.”

After describing Brahma’s seemingly unending lifespan, Maitreya expands our perspective: “The duration of the two parts of Brahma’s life, as above mentioned, is calculated to be equal to one nimesa \[less than a second\] for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is unchanging and unlimited and is the cause of all causes of the universe.” (Bhag. [3.11.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/11.38))

Brahma’s interminably long life of trillions of years appears insignificant when compared to eternity. Indeed, Srila Prabhupada states: “By these calculations the life of Brahma seems fantastic and interminable, but from the viewpoint of eternity it is as brief as a lightning flash. In the Causal Ocean there are innumerable Brahmas rising and disappearing like bubbles in the Atlantic. Brahma and his creation are all part of the material universe, and therefore they are in constant flux.” (Bg. [8.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/8.17), purport)

Accepting Maitreya Muni’s perspective on time—in which even Lord Brahma’s lifespan is insignificant—should alter our view of life. Vaisnavas maintain that greater perspective, and they view the lifespan of Indra as a speck of time spent in an eternity. They also view misery from the same perspective. Both pain and pleasure—all problems, losses, acquisitions, and conquests—when seen from the vantage point of eternal time, diminish in importance. If we wish to seriously practice spiritual life, we must learn to develop this “long” conception of time, and Maitreya Muni is helping us to develop this vision.

## Texts 39-42: The Limit of Time’s Control

Maitreya Muni then places eternal time itself in perspective: Time controls everything, from the atom to the divisions of Brahma’s life, yet time is controlled by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. “Time can control only those who are body conscious, even up to the Satyaloka or the other higher planets of the universe.” (Bhag. [3.11.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/11.39)) And into perspective goes the universe in which we live, as well as all the created universes. The diameter of this universe is four billion miles.

The layers or elements covering the universes are each ten times thicker than the one before, and all the universes clustered together appear like atoms in a huge combination.

Finally Maitreya Muni offers the ultimate frame of reference, the perspective into which all else fits: “The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, is therefore said to be the original cause of all causes. Thus the spiritual abode of Visnu is eternal without a doubt, and it is also the abode of Maha-Visnu, the origin of all manifestations.” (Bhag. [3.11.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/11.42))

Srila Prabhupada quotes the Brahma-samhita ([5.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/1)) in his purport: “The Supreme Lord is Krsna, the original Personality of Godhead known as Govinda. His form is eternal, foil of bliss and knowledge, and He is the original cause of all causes.” Maitreya Muni’s conclusion cannot be avoided: the Lord is unlimitedly powerful. We tiny souls, controlled by His time energy and living in an insignificant part of space—in one house, in one city, in one country, on one planet, in one of many universes—are not the center of existence. We are simply insignificant.

## Chapter 12 - Creation of the Kumaras and Others

## Texts 1-27: Brahma Creates The Four Kumaras, Rudra, and the Ten Sages

Next, Maitreya will discuss visarga, the secondary creation. The purpose of the creation is to house souls who have rejected their identity as Krsna’s servants and who wish to live as if they existed independently of their Lord. Brahma’s first work, then, was to create the required ignorance and illusion that allows these souls to live with a false sense of identity (false ego). Brahma thus created self-deception, the sense of death, anger after frustration, the sense of false ownership, and the illusory bodily conception. All these cover a soul’s true identity.

Srila Prabhupada describes the purpose behind Brahma’s primary creative acts in his purport to Bhagavatam [3.12.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.2): “Before the factual creation of the living entities in different varieties of species, the conditions under which a living being in the material world has to live were created by Brahma. Unless a living entity forgets his real identity, it is impossible for him to live in the material conditions of life. Therefore the first condition of material existence is forgetfulness of one’s real identity. And by forgetting one’s real identity, one is sure to be afraid of death, although a pure living soul is deathless and birthless.

This false identification with material nature is the cause of false ownership of things which are offered by the arrangement of superior control. All material resources are offered to the living entity for his peaceful living and for the discharge of the duties of self-realization in conditioned life. But due to false identification, the conditioned soul becomes entrapped by the sense of false ownership of the property of the Supreme Lord.”

As necessary as these forms of ignorance are, Brahma still felt dissatisfied after creating them. As Srila Prabhupada states in his purport to the next text, “he had to do it because most of the conditioned souls wanted it to be so.” Srila Prabhupada’s interesting purport continues to describe how Krsna deals with the living entity’s independence: “Anyone who has some independence may sometimes misuse it due to ignorance. When the living entity prefers to misuse his independence and glide down towards nescience, the all-merciful Lord first of all tries to protect him from the trap, but when the living entity persists in gliding down to hell, the Lord helps him to forget his real position. The Lord helps the falling living entity glide down to the lowest point, just to give him the chance to see if he is happy by misusing his independence.”

Despite his dissatisfaction, however, and wishing to continue his service, Brahma purified himself by meditating on the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He then began the second step of the visarga creation. This creation is based not on ignorance but knowledge, and thereafter the four Kumaras—Sanaka, Sananda, Sanatana and Sanat-kumara—appeared from Brahma.

In his purport to text 4, Srila Prabhupada describes the principles of knowledge these sages possessed: “ . . . sankhya, or empirical philosophy for the analytical study of material conditions; yoga, or mysticism for liberation of the pure soul from material bondage; vairagya, the acceptance of complete detachment from material enjoyment in life to elevate oneself to the highest spiritual understanding; and tapas, or the various kinds of voluntary austerities performed for spiritual perfection.”

Brahma attempted to enlist the Kumaras to assist him in expanding the creation: ‘“My dear sons,’ he said, ‘now generate progeny.’ But due to their being attached to Vasudeva, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, they aimed at liberation, and therefore they expressed their unwillingness.” (Bhag. [3.12.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.5)) Upon hearing their refusal, Brahma became angry. Srila Prabhupada writes: “Brahma, being absorbed in the mode of passion, could not check his passionate anger. He did not express it, however, because he knew that his sons were far enlightened in spiritual advancement and thus he should not express his anger before them.” (Bhag. [3.12.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.6), purport) Despite his attempt to control his anger, it forced its way “out from between his eyebrows, and a child mixed blue and red was immediately generated.” (Bhag. [3.12.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.7)) Srila Prabhupada states: “Such anger in its true color came from between the eyebrows of Brahma as Rudra, in a mixed color of blue (ignorance) and red (passion), because anger is the product of passion and ignorance.” (Bhag. [3.12.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.7), purport)

Rudra immediately began to cry: “O destiny maker, teacher of the universe, kindly designate my name and place.” (Bhag. [3.12.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.8)) Lord Brahma pacified the boy with gentle words and fulfilled his request: “Do not cry. I shall certainly do as you desire.” (Bhag. [3.12.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.9)) Brahma then awarded the child twelve names: Rudra, Manyu, Manu, Mahinasa, Mahan, Siva, Rtadhvaja, Ugrareta, Bhava, Kala, Vamadeva, and Dhrtavrata. He also awarded him places of residence—the heart, senses, life air, sky, air, fire, water, earth, sun, moon, and austerity—and provided him with wives, the Rudranis, named Dhi, Dhrti, Rasala, Uma, Niyut, Sarpi, Ila, Ambika, Iravati, Svadha, and Diksa. Brahma then requested him: “My dear boy, you may now accept all the names and places designated for you and your different wives, and since you are now one of the masters of the living entities, you may increase the population on a large scale.” (Bhag. [3.12.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.14))

Rudra’s nature was different from that of the Kumaras, who were bom of knowledge, and he accepted Brahma’s order. But the many offspring he created resembled him exactly in features, strength, and fury. He created so many entities that when they assembled to devour the universe they seemed unlimited in number. Brahma became afraid and spoke to Rudra: “O best among the demigods, there is no need for you to generate living entities of this nature. They have begun to devastate everything on all sides with the fiery flames from their eyes, and they have even attacked me. My dear son, you had better situate yourself in penance, which is auspicious for all living entities and which will bring all benediction upon you.” (Bhag. [3.12.17-18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.17)) Thus Brahma intelligently inspired Rudra and his offspring to turn to peaceful meditation, assuring Rudra that when it was time to dissolve the universe, his services would be required and Brahma would call for him. Rudra assented to Brahma’s order, circumambulated his father respectfully, and left for the forest to perform penance.Lord Brahma’s guiding Rudra toward peaceful meditation and the selective use of his furious anger hint at the danger of anger as well as two of its immediate causes, lust and greed. Krsna Himself issues a strong warning about lust, anger, and greed: “There are three gates leading to this hell—lust, anger and greed. Every sane man should give these up, for they lead to the degradation of the soul.” (Bg. [16.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/16.21)) In his Prema-bhakti-candrika (Song 2), Narottama dasa Thakura counsels devotees to purify themselves of the contaminating effects of these three enemies—along with bewilderment and madness—by enlisting them in Krsna’s service while never forgetting the Lord:

**Lust I will engage in offering the fruits of my work to Lord Krsna. Anger I will direct toward the enemies of the devotees. Greed I will engage by being greedy to hear the topics of Lord Hari in the association of the saintly devotees. Bewilderment will be manifest because I cannot immediately attain my worshipable Lord. Madness will appear when I madly glorify Lord Krsna’s transcendental attributes. In this way I will engage each of these in Lord Krsna’s service.**

**If lust is not controlled, then it becomes the breeding ground for a host of vices and checks one’s advancement on the path of devotional service. However, if one stays in the association of the saintly devotees, then that association will carry him beyond the influence of lust, anger, and their friends. I shall not become angry. I shall renounce anger. I shall become free from my six enemies, such as greed and bewilderment. I shall control my mind and always remember Lord Krsnacandra. When lust and his friends hear the word “Govinda,” they immediately begin to flee, as a herd of elephants flees when it hears a lion’s roar. If one engages in singlepointed devotional service to Lord Krsna, then the worshiper attains transcendental bliss, and all kinds of calamities flee from him.**

Brahma next generated ten great sages. Nine of these (Marici, Atri, Angira, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Bhrgu, Vasistha, and Daksa) were inclined to fruitive activities, and therefore the tenth sage, Sri Narada Muni, born of Brahma’s deliberation, is considered best. Narada Muni embodies pure devotional service, and Srila Prabhupada glorifies Narada in his purport to text 23: “Narada was bom from the best deliberation of Brahma because Narada was able to deliver the Supreme Lord to anyone he liked. The Supreme Personality of Godhead cannot be realized by any amount of Vedic knowledge or by any number of penances. But a pure devotee of the Lord like Narada can deliver the Supreme Lord by his good will. The very name Narada suggests that he can deliver the Supreme Lord. Nara means the ‘Supreme Lord,’ and da means ‘one who can deliver.’”

Brahma then manifested states of consciousness to accommodate the varieties of living entities and their individual desires. He created religion from his breast, irreligion from his back, lust and desire from his heart, anger from between his eyebrows, greed from his lips, the power of speaking from his mouth, the ocean from his penis, low and abominable activities from his anus, and the great sage Kardama Muni, the husband of the great Devahtiti, from his shadow. Brahma manifested all of these creations directly from either his body or his mind.

## Texts 28-48: The Secondary Creation Continues

Brahma created a daughter, Vak (speech), but then fell under the influence of ignorance and became inappropriately attracted to her. The sages headed by Marici respectfully brought to Brahma’s attention the disturbance to religious principles his attraction would cause, and Brahma immediately desisted. His shame caused him to renounce his body (mentality), which later appeared as dangerous fog.

Srila Prabhupada places this unique incident in perspective in his purport to text 29: “\[The sages\] knew very well that even though their father committed a mistake, there must have been some great purpose behind the show, otherwise such a great personality could not have committed such a mistake. It might be that Brahma wanted to warn his subordinates about human frailties in their dealings with women. This is always very dangerous for persons who are on the path of selfrealization.”

It is interesting to note that even during Brahma’s creation the inherent nature of matter did not allow it to proceed smoothly. Practically speaking, as we have seen exemplified in Brahma’s deeds, ignorance and goodness, good and bad, creation and destruction naturally and unavoidably occur one after another.

After accepting a more suitable body, Brahma considered how to best continue the creation. From this deliberation appeared the four Vedas (Rg, Yajur, Sama, and Atharva), further Vedic knowledge (medical science, military art, music, and architecture), the fifth Veda (the Puranas and histories), the processes of fire sacrifice, the four legs of religion (truth, austerity, mercy, and cleanliness), the four asrama orders of life (brahmacarya, grhastha, vanaprastha, and sannyasa), and the four varnas (brahmana, ksatriya, vaisya, and sudra) along with their divisions and duties. Further, Maitreya explains, “The science of logical argument, the Vedic goals of life, and also law and order, moral codes, and the celebrated hymns bhuh, bhuvah and svah all became manifested from the mouths of Brahma, and the pranava orhkara was manifested from his heart.” (Bhag. [3.12.44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.44))

Brahma then generated varieties of modes of expression, including poetic meter and the various letters of the alphabet, as well as the notes of the musical scale.

## Texts 49-57: Brahma Creates Svayambhuva Manu and Satarupa

Brahma then accepted another body, for he noted that despite the presence of great, potent sages the population hadn’t increased quickly enough. Brahma thought, “There is no other cause for this misfortune but destiny.” (Bhag. [3.12.51](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.51)) As he became absorbed in his contemplation, two forms—one male and one female—were generated from his body. The male became known as Svayambhuva Manu and the female as Satarupa, Manu’s queen.

Manu begot in Satarupa three daughters (Akuti, Devahuti, and Prasuti) and two sons (Priyavrata and Uttanapada). Manu gave his first daughter, Akuti, to the sage Ruci. The middle daughter, Devahuti, was given to the sage Kardama, and the youngest, Prasuti, was given to the great prajapati Daksa.

The Srimad-Bhagavatam, Canto Three, Chapter Twenty, discusses Brahma’s visarga creation in similar detail to Chapter Twelve. Chapter Twenty opens by describing the Lord’s sarga creation, but quickly moves to describing Brahma’s creation of illusion and ignorance. It then proceeds to describe his creation of night and day, demons and demigods, Apsaras and Gandharvas, moonlight, ghosts and fiends, Sadhyas and Pitas, Siddhas and Vidyadharas, Kimpurusas and Kin-naras, snakes and serpents, and in his own likeness, Svayambhuva Manu and Satarupa. Finally, Chapter Twenty describes Brahma’s creation of great sages. To each of them he, the unborn creator of the universe, offered a part of his own body.

Taking either Chapter Twelve or Twenty for reference, one knows that the descendants of Svayambhuva Manu and Satarupa gradually populated the universe. The Bhagavatam will narrate the histories of a number of these descendants, especially in the Third, Fourth, and Fifth Cantos. Chapters Twenty-one through Thirty-three of the Third Canto will describe Devahuti’s marriage to Kardama Muni and the teachings of their glorious son, Kapila Muni Chapters One through Four of the Fourth Canto will describe Prasuti and Prajapati Daksa’s descendants. These chapters will also describe the unfortunate suicide of Prasuti’s daughter Sati after Sati’s marriage to Lord Siva. In the first chapter of the Fourth Canto, Kardama Muni’s daughter, Anasuya, and her husband Atri Muni, are described, along with their three sons, who were partial representations of Visnu, Brahma, and Siva. Chapters Eight through Thirty-one of the Fourth Canto will describe the descendants of Svayambhuva Manu’s youngest son, Uttanapada, and Chapters One through Fifteen of the Fifth Canto will narrate the history and descendants of Manu’s eldest son, Priyavrata.

## Dialogue Four - The Appearance of Lord Varaha and Killing of Hiranyaksa

## Chapter 13 - The Appearance of Lord Varahadeva

## Texts 1-17: Svayambhuva Manu’s Desire to Serve

Hearing how Lord Brahma had manifest Svayambhuva Manu and Manu’s beloved wife, Satariipa, from his own body (Bhag. [3.12.52-55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/12.52)), Vidura inquired about the great devotee Manu’s activities. Srila Prabhupada recommends such hearing about the Lord’s devotees in his purport to Bhagavatam [3.13.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.4):

**Transcendental students are those who undergo great penance in being trained by hearing the Vedas from a bona fide spiritual master. Not only must they hear about the activities of the Lord, but they must also hear about the transcendental qualities of the devotees who are constantly thinking of the lotus feet of the Lord within their hearts. A pure devotee of the Lord cannot be separated from the lotus feet of the Lord for even a moment. Undoubtedly the Lord is always within the hearts of all living creatures, but they hardly know about it because they are deluded by the illusory material energy. The devotees, however, realize the presence of the Lord, and therefore they can always see the lotus feet of the Lord within their hearts. Such pure devotees of the Lord are as glorious as the Lord; they are, in fact, recommended by the Lord as more worshipable than He Himself is. Worship of the devotee is more potent than worship of the Lord. It is therefore the duty of the transcendental students to hear of pure devotees, as explained by similar devotees of the Lord, because one cannot explain about the Lord or His devotee unless one happens to be a pure devotee himself.**

Hearing is the means by which one acquires the same intense devotional taste the advanced devotees possess and comes to understand the method by which such devotional inclination was ignited in their hearts. Suta Gosvami has already presented the essence of this: “O twice-born sages, by serving those devotees who are completely freed from all vice, great service is done. By such service, one gains affinity for hearing the messages of Vasudeva.” (Bhag. [1.2.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.16))

Enlivened by Vidura’s eagerness to hear about Krsna, Maitreya Muni tells Vidura about the humble request Manu made of Lord Brahma, his father: “Please order us how we may be able to render service unto you.” (Bhag. [3.13.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.7)) Brahma was pleased with his son’s affectionate but respectful submission and requested three things of him: “My dear son, О lord of the world, I am very pleased with you, and I desire all blessings for both you and your wife. You have without reservation surrendered yourself unto me with your heart for my instructions. . . . Since you are my very obedient son, I ask you to beget children qualified like yourself in the womb of your wife. Rule the world in pursuance of the principles of devotional service unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and thus worship the Lord by performances of yajna.” (Bhag. [3.13.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.9), [11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.11)) Brahma also told Manu that he could please the Lord by protecting the conditioned souls in his charge.

Srila Prabhupada guides the reader to examine several important points, such as independence, obedience, and the ideal relationship between father and son: “The relationship between the father and the son is always sublime. The father is naturally disposed with good will towards the son, and he is always ready to help the son in his progress in life. But in spite of the father’s good will, the son is sometimes misguided because of his misuse of personal independence. Every living entity, however small or big he may be, has the choice of independence. If the son is unreservedly willing to be guided by the father, the father is ten times more eager to instruct and guide him by all means. The father and son relationship as exhibited here in the dealings of Brahma and Manu is excellent. Both the father and the son are well qualified, and their example should be followed by all humankind.” (Bhag. [3.13.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.9), purport)

Manu accepted Lord Brahma’s words but foresaw a problem: The earth lay submerged in the Garbhodaka Ocean. Where would he perform his appointed service? Where would those under his protection live? Manu petitioned Brahma for help: “O master of the demigods, please attempt to lift the earth, which is merged in the great water, because it is the dwelling place for all the living entities. It can be done by your endeavor and by the mercy of the Lord.” (Bhag. [3.13.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.15)) Brahma looked and saw that the earth had indeed fallen into the water. How could such a huge planet be lifted? “While I have been engaged in the process of creation, the earth has been inundated by a deluge and has gone down into the depths of the ocean.” (Bhag. [3.13.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.17)) Despite his power, Brahma, master of the demigods and the secondary creator of the material universe, was mindful of his position: What can I do? It is best to allow Him from whose heart I was bom direct me.

The Lord reciprocates with devotees as they render service: “The devotees of the Lord, who are all confidential servitors, are sometimes perplexed in the discharge of their respective duties, but they are never discouraged. They have full faith in the Lord, and He paves the way for the smooth progress of the devotee’s duty.” (Bhag. [3.13.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.17), purport)

## Texts 18-33: The Birth and Deeds of Lord Varahadeva

As Brahma immersed himself in thought, a small boar, no bigger than the upper portion of a thumb, suddenly flew from Brahma’s nostril into the sky. The boar then expanded Himself until He was as large as an elephant. Brahma and his brahmana sons gazed at the boar in wonder. “He appeared from my nose as a small entity but instantaneously expanded. Who is this extraordinary entity? Is it the Supreme Lord?”

Were people asked to nominate graceful, beautiful, or elegant creatures, the boar would be unlikely to gamer many votes. Nevertheless, whatever form the Lord assumes is most wonderful, fully spiritual, and endowed with all transcendental qualities. Thus Krsna appeared as Varahadeva, a transcendental boar, and as a boar the Lord would rescue the earth in a most amazing and creative way.

As Brahma and his sons deliberated on the boar’s identity, Varaha raised His splendid voice and roared tumultuously. Then He roared again, and His uncommon voice, echoing in all directions, enlivened Brahma and the other elevated brahmanas. The Lord’s roar actually confirmed for Brahma that this was the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and hearing the Lord’s roar, the sages on the higher planets also recognized Him and responded with praise from the three Vedas. Varahadeva roared again in response to their prayers, then flew into the sky and slashed His tail back and forth. His hard hairs quivered, His glance was luminous, and He scattered the clouds with His hooves and glittering white tusks.

Although the Lord had appeared as a boar, He was not a boar; He was the Personality of Godhead. Therefore the sages glorified Him with Vedic hymns. Through this pastime, the Lord asserts that regardless of what form He assumes or activities He performs, He is always the fully transcendental Lord, the supreme object of Vedic worship. Varahadeva was gigantic, and His pastime of lifting the earth with His white tusks is beyond anything anyone but the Lord could accomplish. Although Lord Varaha’s boarlike form and superhuman activities are difficult to understand, still more difficult to understand are Krsna’s own form and activities, for they are nara, humanlike.

Thus Srimad-Bhagavatam systematically establishes the concepts required if one is to understand Lord Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who will be revealed in Canto Ten.

Srila Prabhupada expands on the nature of the Lord’s form and activities: “The Lord can assume any form He likes, and in all circumstances He is the cause of all causes. Since His form is transcendental, He is always the Supreme Personality of Godhead, as He is in the Causal Ocean in the form of Maha-Visnu. Innumerable universes generate from the holes of His bodily hairs, and thus His transcendental body is the Vedas personified. He is the enjoyer of all sacrifices, and He is the unconquerable Supreme Personality of Godhead. He is never to be misunderstood to be other than the Supreme Lord because of His assuming the form of a boar to lift the earth. That is the clear understanding of sages and great personalities like Brahma and other residents of the higher planetary systems.” (Bhag. [3.13.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.34), purport)

Varahadeva, the Lord and beneficiary of all Vedic sacrifices, glanced at the devotee'brahmanas offering prayers and immediately entered the Garbhodaka Ocean, piercing the surface of the water with His sharp hooves. Though omniscient, Lord Varaha sought the earth through the power of scent, just as if He were a hog of this world. Varahadeva located the earth and lifted it from the water on His mighty tusks.

Maitreya Muni tells Vidura that as the Lord was performing this wonderful pastime, He killed the powerful demon Hiranyaksa. When He arose from the water, the Lord, “playing like an elephant, suspended the earth on the edge of His curved white tusks. He assumed a bluish complexion like that of a tamala tree, and thus the sages, headed by Brahma, could understand Him to be the Supreme Personality of Godhead and offered respectful obeisances unto the Lord.” (Bhag. [3.13.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.33))

## Texts 34-45: The Sages Further Glorify Lord Boar

Seeing Lord Varaha, the sages glorified Him as the personified Vedas and as the one whose form is worshiped through Vedic sacrifice. How can the Lord be realized? Their answer was clear: The Lord can be realized only when one’s mind is purified of material contamination. It is purity that allows one to understand God, regardless of the form in which the Lord chooses to appear. It is purity that allows one His merciful association. Therefore one should offer Krsna service with a pure heart—with sincerity, affection, and freedom from selfish motivation. Such pure service will inspire Krsna to supply one with the intelligence and ability to make further progress in devotion.

The sages then described the Lord’s beauty as He stood with the earth upon His tusks, comparing His splendor to the splendor of a great mountain decorated with clouds. The sages also described Lord Varaha as the Lord of Vedic sacrifices, the purpose of which are to worship and please God. “Who else but You, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, could deliver the earth from within the water? It is not very wonderful for You, however, because You acted most wonderfully in the creation of the universe. By Your energy You have created this wonderful cosmic manifestation. О Supreme Lord, undoubtedly we are inhabitants of the most pious planets—the Jana, Tapas and Satya lokas—but still we have been purified by the drops of water sprinkled from Your shoulder hairs by the shaking of Your body.” (Bhag. [3.13.43-44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.43))

It is interesting to note that the sages, including Brahma, were perfect brahmanas, yet they considered themselves purified by the water sprinkled on them when the Lord shook His body. Ordinarily, when a hog shakes its wet body, everyone quickly moves aside in disgust.

Yet these pure brahmanas again present their willingness to accept and venerate the Lord in His current form, considering His body and actions fully transcendental. Srila Prabhupada states: “Ordinarily the body of a hog is considered impure, but one should not consider that the hog incarnation assumed by the Lord is also impure. That form of the Lord is the personified Vedas and is transcendental. The inhabitants of the Jana, Tapas and Satya lokas are the most pious persons in the material world, but because those planets are situated in the material world, there are so many material impurities there also. Therefore, when the drops of water from the tips of the Lord’s shoulder hairs were sprinkled upon the bodies of the inhabitants of the higher planets, they felt purified.” (Bhag. [3.13.44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.44), purport)

The sages, learned and powerful, accepted their inability to fathom the limits of the unlimited Lord’s deeds. They conclude their prayers by requesting Lord Varaha to bless them with the ability to worship Him with devotion. Srila Prabhupada paraphrases the sages’ prayers (Bhag. [3.13.34-45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.34)) in his purport to text 45: “Both worlds \[the material and spiritual\] are bewildered by Your different energies. Those who are in the spiritual world are absorbed in Your loving service, forgetting themselves and You also, and those in the material world are absorbed in material sense gratification and therefore also forget You. No one can know You, because You are unlimited. It is best not to try to know You by unnecessary mental speculation. Rather, kindly bless us so that we can worship You with causeless devotional service.”

## Texts 46-50: Varahadeva Returns to His Own Abode, and Maitreya Muni Offers Benedictions

After being worshiped by the sages, the Lord touched the earth with His hooves and placed it on the water, where by His potency it remained afloat. He then returned to His own abode. Maitreya Muni concludes his narration: “If one hears and describes in a devotional attitude this auspicious narration of Lord Boar, which is worthy of description, the Lord, who is within the heart of everyone, is very pleased. Nothing remains unachieved when the Supreme Personality of Godhead is pleased with someone. By transcendental achievement one understands everything else to be insignificant. One who engages in transcendental loving service is elevated to the highest perfectional stage by the Lord Himself, who is seated in everyone’s heart. Who, other than one who is not a human being, can exist in this world and not be interested in the ultimate goal of life? Who can refuse the nectar of narrations about the Personality of Godhead’s activities, which by itself can deliver one from all material pangs?” (Bhag. [3.13.48-50](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.48))Srila Prabhupada’s purports to these final texts of the chapter can inspire readers to hear faithfully about the Lord and to seek His shelter. Here is a selection from these purports:

**Intelligent persons should therefore hear personally and cause others to hear the descriptive narrations of the Lord’s activities, for that will destroy the pangs of material existence. Out of His causeless mercy only, the Lord comes to this earth and leaves behind His merciful activities so that the devotees may derive transcendental benefit. (Bhag.** [**3.13.48**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.48)**, purport)**

**There are many books of stories and histories in the world, but except for the histories or narrations on the topics of the Personality of Godhead, none are capable of diminishing the burden of material pangs. Therefore one who is serious about eliminating material existence must chant and hear of the transcendental activities of the Personality of Godhead. (Bhag.** [**3.13.50**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.50)**, purport)**

In his purport to text 49, Srila Prabhupada describes the help the Lord offers His pure devotees:

**As stated in Bhagavad-gita (**[**10.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.10)**), the Lord gives intelligence to the pure devotees so that they may be elevated to the highest perfectional stage. It is confirmed herein that a pure devotee, who constantly engages in the loving service of the Lord, is awarded all knowledge necessary to reach the Supreme Personality of Godhead. For such a devotee there is nothing valuable to be achieved but the Lord’s service. If one serves faithfully, there is no possibility of frustration because the Lord Himself takes charge of the devotee’s advancement. The Lord is seated in everyone’s heart, and He knows the devotee’s motive and arranges everything achievable. In other words, the pseudo devotee, who is anxious to achieve material gains, cannot attain the highest perfectional stage because the Lord is in knowledge of his motive. One merely has to become sincere in his purpose, and then the Lord is there to help in every way.**

## Chapter 14 - Pregnancy of Diti in the Evening

## Texts 1-7: Vidura Inquires about the Lord’s Fight with Hiranyaksa

Listening carefully, Vidura noted that Varahadeva killed the demon Hiranyaksa while lifting the earth (stated in Bhag. [3.13.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.31)). He now asks Maitreya why Varahadeva was inimical to this demon and to describe the battle. In response, Maitreya Muni takes us back to the time before Hiranyaksa’s birth.

## Texts 8-31: Diti’s Inappropriate Desire

Diti was overcome by desire and wanted to immediately unite with her husband to produce a child. Therefore she broke his meditation and pleaded with him to fulfill her desire. After all, Diti begged, he was a compassionate sage and a great soul. Kasyapa agreed, but warned that the time was inauspicious.

Kasyapa Muni explained: This sandhya \[juncture between day and night\] is ill-omened because it is at this time that the glorious Lord Siva wanders about with his ghastly followers. Only a soul illusioned with a dreadful consciousness could be attracted at this time to enter your womb as your son.

Although the sage implored Diti to remain fixed in religious action, Diti could not overcome her desire. She caught hold of the great brahmana’s clothing and obliged him to lay with her in a secluded place. Kasyapa Muni, deferring to fate, conceived a child with his wife at the forbidden and inauspicious time.

## Texts 32-51: Kasyapa Muni Foretells the Birth of Demonic Progeny

Thereafter the sage purified himself by bathing and chanting Vedic mantras. Diti, ashamed of her impropriety, approached Kasyapa with lowered eyes. Trembling and afraid that Lord Siva, in his wrath, might destroy her child, she offered Siva obeisances and begged her powerful husband to protect the embryo. Prabhupada paraphrases Diti’s prayers: “The lord can cause me to cry, but if he likes he can also stop my crying because he is Asutosa. He is so great that if he likes he can immediately destroy my pregnancy, but by his mercy he can also fulfill my desire that my pregnancy not be spoiled. Because he is all-auspicious, it is not difficult for him to excuse me from being punished, although he is now ready to punish me because I have moved his great anger. He appears like a man, but he is the lord of all men.” (Bhag. [3.14.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/14.35), purport)

Kasyapa Muni was disdainful: “Because of your mind’s being polluted, because of your defiling that particular time, because of your negligence of my directions, and because of your being apathetic to the demigods, everything was inauspicious. О haughty one, you will have two contemptuous sons born of your condemned womb. Unlucky woman, they will cause constant lamentation to all the three worlds! They will kill poor, faultless living entities, torture women and enrage the great souls. At that time, the Lord of the universe, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the well-wisher of all living entities, will descend and kill them, just as Indra smashes the mountains with his thunderbolts.” (Bhag. [3.14.38-41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/14.38))

Aggrieved, humbled, and contrite, Diti felt content to hear that at least her sons would be killed by the merciful Lord Visnu Himself: “It is very good that my sons will be magnanimously killed by the arms of the Personality of Godhead with His Sudarsana weapon. О my husband, may they never be killed by the wrath of the brahmana-devotees.” (Bhag. [3.14.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/14.42)) In his purport, Srila Prabhupada explains the legitimacy of Diti’s satisfaction: “If someone is killed by the wheel of the Lord and is thus fortunate enough to see the arms of the Lord, that is sufficient for his liberation. Such good fortune is not achieved even by the great sages.” While those killed by the Lord are glorious, those killed by brahmanas' curses are condemned. Brahma himself will later marvel at the fortunate death of Diti’s son Hiranyaksa: “Oh, who could meet such blessed death?” (Bhag. [3.19.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/19.27))

Kasyapa Muni was touched both by Diti’s repentance and by her faith. He softened, then offered her a benediction: Although your sons will be demons, your grandson will become the topmost, most glorious and exalted devotee of the Lord. Hiranyakasipu’s son will be named Prahlada Maharaja. He will have great intelligence and influence, and he will be the greatest of great souls. Prahlada will always be ecstatic, and at the end of his life he will enter the spiritual world. He will be jolly to see others’ happiness and distressed by their distress. He will consider no one his enemy. Like the pleasant moon that follows the blazing summer sun, Prahlada will remove the lamentation of the universe. He will be able to see the Supreme Personality of Godhead everywhere, both within and without.

Anticipating the birth of her glorious grandson and knowing that her sons would be killed by Lord Visnu, Diti was pleased.

## Chapter 15 - Description of the Kingdom of God

## Texts 1-10: The Universe is Covered by Darkness

Diti understood that her unborn sons were demonic and would cause the demigods incredible disturbances. Therefore, she held them in her womb for one hundred years. Still, by the brothers’ potency, the sun dimmed and the universe fell into darkness. The demigods, sensing danger behind the darkness, approached Lord Brahma in fear. They sought to understand how these demons, still unborn, could possess the power to cause such tremendous universal catastrophe. Brahma smiled and explained the identity of Diti’s children. He began by recounting the journey his own sons, the Kumaras, had undertaken to Vaikuntha.

## Texts 11-22: The Four Kumaras Travel to Vaikuntha

Pure and fixed in the Absolute Truth, the four Kumaras traveled throughout the universe by their own will and entered Vaikuntha. Witnessing the natural purity and beauty of the Vaikuntha forests, flowers, and fruits, the sages noted that nothing was contaminated by matter but was fully spiritual. The residents were glorious, similar in form to the Lord, and exquisitely beautiful. The entire land was fragrant with blossoming flowers and alive with buzzing bees. Despite the fact that Vaikuntha possessed unlimited opulence, including the opulence of the most beautiful women, the residents did not become attracted to it but remained fixed in their service to Lord Narayana. Because of their ever-blossoming love for the Lord, they had no desire to enjoy separately from Him but remained blissfully absorbed in His service.

The pure love and one-pointed desire to please Krsna that all residents of Vaikuntha experience is the essence of the spiritual world. Indeed, the women in Vaikuntha sweep and dust the palace marble, although dust does not exist in Vaikuntha. Prabhupada explains: “Thus there is no need to sweep the stone in Vaikuntha, for there is hardly any dust on it, but still, in order to satisfy the Lord, the ladies there always engage in dusting the marble walls. Why? The reason is that they are eager to achieve the grace of the Lord by doing so.” (Bhag. [3.15.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.21), purport) The women therefore clean and simultaneously remember their Lord.

Although the flowers in Vaikuntha are unimaginably beautiful and fragrant, they nevertheless acknowledge the superiority of Tulasi-devi because the Lord prefers tulasi flowers to all other flowers. In his purport to text 19, Prabhupada speaks of Tulasi and then continues to describe “the most important thing about the spiritual world”: “Tulasi plants and their leaves are very important in devotional service. Devotees are recommended to water the tulasi tree every day and collect the leaves to worship the Lord. . . . The most important thing about the spiritual world is that there is no envy among the devotees there. This is true even among the flowers, which are all conscious of the greatness of tulasi. In the Vaikuntha world entered by the four Kumaras, even the birds and flowers are conscious of service to the Lord.”

## Texts 23-25: Lord Brahma Glorifies Vaikuntha

As if unable to contain his enthusiasm about Vaikuntha, Lord Brahma interrupted his narration to praise the wonder of human life, saying that even the demigods desire it because it affords one the opportunity to bypass illusion and attain the Lord’s abode. Lord Brahma then proclaims the fortune of those who even discuss Vaikuntha, and comments on the misfortune of those who refrain from speaking of such topics: “Those who give up the topics of Vaikuntha and take to talk of the material world are thrown into the darkest region of ignorance. My dear demigods, the human form of life is of such importance that we also desire to have such life, for in the human form one can attain perfect religious truth and knowledge.” (Bhag. [3.15.23-24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.23))

Prabhupada further defines fortune and misfortune for human beings in his purport to text 23: “They hold many conventions, meetings and discussions to solve the problems of this worldly situation, where they can remain for only a few years, but they are not interested in understanding the spiritual situation of the Vaikuntha world. If they are at all fortunate, they become interested in going back home, back to Godhead, but unless they understand the spiritual world, they rot in this material darkness continuously.”

In his purport to the next text, Srila Prabhupada offers further impetus for us to use our human life to return to the spiritual world: “Brahmaji condemns very vehemently the condition of the human being who does not take interest in the Personality of Godhead and His transcendental abode, Vaikuntha. The human form of life is desired even by Brahmaji. Brahma and other demigods have much better material bodies than human beings, yet the demigods, including Brahma, nevertheless desire to attain the human form of life because it is specifically meant for the living entity who can attain transcendental knowledge and religious perfection. . . . The human being who does not take advantage of all these facilities in this life is committing suicide. Therefore one who does not begin Krsna consciousness in the human form of life loses his life to the influence of the illusory energy. Brahma regrets the situation of such a human being.”

Hearing in ecstasy about the Lord’s glories carries us to Vaikuntha. Brahma continues: “Persons whose bodily features change in ecstasy and who breathe heavily and perspire due to hearing the glories of the Lord are promoted to the kingdom of God, even though they do not care for meditation and other austerities. The kingdom of God is above the material universes, and it is desired by Brahma and other demigods.” (Bhag. [3.15.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.25)) Considering the potency of hearing the Lord’s names and glories, one may wonder why he doesn’t experience ecstasy when he chants. Prabhupada answers this essential question in his purport to text 25: “When one is free from all ten of these offenses in chanting the holy name of God, he develops the ecstatic bodily features called pulakasru. Pulaka means ‘symptoms of happiness,’ and asru means ‘tears in the eyes.’ The symptoms of happiness and tears in the eyes must appear in a person who has chanted the holy name offenselessly.”

Can one do something to counteract his offenses and thus help himself gain the result of chanting? Prabhupada continues: “Caitanya-caritamrta suggests a nice remedy in this connection. There it is said in verse 31, Chapter 8, of Adi-lila, that if anyone takes shelter of Lord Caitanya and just chants the holy name of the Lord, Hare Krsna, he becomes freed from all offenses.”

## Texts 26-37: The Sages Are Obstructed and Curse the Gatekeepers

Returning to his narration, Brahma related the unprecedented happiness the four Kumaras felt on entering the spiritual world, for the Lord’s internal potency, yogamdyd, not His illusory energy, prevails in that land. Gate by gate, the Kumaras passed through the six entrances leading to the Lord’s residence. At the seventh gate, however, they saw two shining beings—guards armed with clubs—protecting the palace in which the Lord was resting. They were adorned with valuable jewelry and fresh flower garlands swarming with bees. These guards appeared disturbed, and they arched their eyebrows and flared their nostrils as the Kumaras approached. Although the Kumaras appeared as small, naked children, the Vaikuntha doormen blocked them from entering the Lord’s palace.

As wandering children become angry when prohibited from freely entering a place, so the innocent, saintly devotees felt both sorrow and anger when forbidden to pass through the seventh gate. Because they were checked from seeing the Lord of Vaikuntha, their eyes reddened. Srila Prabhupada calls their anger spiritual: “Here we can mark that even great saintly persons like the Kumaras were also angry, but they were not angry for their personal interests. They were angry because they were forbidden to enter the palace to see the Personality of Godhead. Therefore the theory that in the perfectional stage one should not have anger is not supported in this verse. Anger will continue even in the liberated stage.” (Bhag. [3.15.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.31), purport)

We saw Srila Prabhupada himself become angry at times. One such occasion was during a festival at the Gita Bhavan in Indore, which he attended with his disciples in 1970. The event is recalled in Srila. Prabhupada'lilamrta (Vol. 1, p. 908):

**During the kirtana one of the members of the Gita Bhavan gestured to the devotees to jump down into the crowd as they had done on the preceding night. But what had been a spontaneous event the night before could not be artificially staged simply as a crowdpleaser. The man, however, was insistent. He came forward to the edge of the stage, reached up, and began grabbing at the feet of the dancing devotees, trying to pull them into the audience. The devotees became annoyed. Grabbing indiscriminately, the man pulled at one of the women’s saris. Srila Prabhupada was also dancing, but when he saw this he rushed to the edge of the stage, swinging his karatdlas toward the man’s face and shouting, “Stop this!” The man retreated, and Prabhupada and his disciples continued their kirtana. Although little noticed by the crowd, Prabhupada’s burst of lionlike ferocity had amazed his disciples.**

The four Kumaras spoke sharply: “Who are these two persons who have developed such a discordant mentality even though they are posted in the service of the Lord in the highest position and are expected to have developed the same qualities as the Lord? How are these two persons living in Vaikuntha? Where is the possibility of an enemy’s coming into this kingdom of God? The Supreme Personality of Godhead has no enemy. Who could be envious of Him? Probably these two persons are imposters; therefore they suspect others to be like themselves.” (Bhag. [3.15.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.32)) The Kumaras accused the doorkeepers of being imposters because they perceived a dichotomy between friends and enemies in a world where no such dualities exist. Thus they considered their mentality discordant with the mood of the Lord and His pure associates. Srila Prabhupada comments on this text: “The sages . . . were surprised to see that the two doormen who checked them from entering the palace were not exactly like the residents of Vaikunthaloka. It may be said that a doorman’s duty is to determine who should be allowed to enter the palace and who should not. But that is not relevant in this matter because no one is allowed to enter the Vaikuntha planets unless he has developed one hundred percent his mentality of devotional service to the Supreme Lord. No enemy of the Lord can enter Vaikunthaloka.”

In his purport to text 33, Prabhupada confirms that harmony— oneness in desire with the Lord—is indeed the essence of Vaikuntha life: “In the Vaikuntha world there is no disharmony between the Lord and the residents. Therefore God’s creation in the Vaikuntha world is perfect. There is no cause of fear. The entire kingdom of God is such a completely harmonious unit that there is no possibility of enmity. Everything there is absolute. Just as there are many physiological constructions within the body yet they work in one order for the satisfaction of the stomach, and just as in a machine there are hundreds and thousands of parts yet they run in harmony to fulfill the function of the machine, in the Vaikuntha planets the Lord is perfect, and the inhabitants also perfectly engage in the service of the Lord.”

Srila Prabhupada also discusses what type of mentality breaks the harmony one has with the Lord as well as what prohibits “criminals” from entering Vaikuntha: “Since the basic principles of criminality are sense gratification, anger and unnecessary lust, persons conducted by these three enemies of the living entity are never promoted to Vaikunthaloka. People should learn Bhagavad-gita and accept the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Krsna, as the Lord of everything; they should practice satisfying the senses of the Supreme Lord instead of trying to satisfy their own senses.” (Bhag. [3.15.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.34), purport)

Krsna conscious religious principles bring harmony. If we can adopt the same principles in our own society, whether “wholly or partially,” then we will turn our society into Vaikuntha. “If the members of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness, putting faith in Krsna as the center, live in harmony according to the order and principles of Bhagavad-gita, then they are living in Vaikuntha, not in this material world.” (Bhag. [3.15.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.33), purport)

Considering Jaya and Vijaya unfit to reside in the spiritual world, the four boy-sages cursed them to leave Vaikuntha and fall to the material realm. Terrified, the doorkeepers fell at the Kumaras’ feet. Even while doing so, however, they accepted their fate, considering the curse appropriate punishment for their own show of disrespect. Nevertheless, they begged the sages to mitigate the harshness of their curse: “We pray that due to your compassion at our repentance, the illusion of forgetting the Supreme Personality of Godhead will not come upon us as we go progressively downward.” (Bhag. [3.15.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.36)) Srila Prabhupada explains the relevance of their plea: “To a devotee, any heavy punishment is tolerable but the one which effects forgetfulness of the Supreme Lord.” (Bhag. [3.15.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.36), purport)

## Texts 38-45: The Lord Arrives

The moment Lord Narayana heard of the curse, He and Laksmidevi rushed to the seventh gate. Fearing that His keepers might be vanquished by the brahmanas’ fiery anger, and knowing that the anger was caused by a thwarted desire to see Him, the Lord immediately appeared before the four Kumaras. Thus within moments of uttering the curse, the sages saw Lord Narayana standing before them.

Srila Jiva Gosvami writes in his Bhagavatsandarbha, anuccheda 78, about Lord Narayana’s immediate appearance on the scene: “The Lord thought, ‘I will pacify the anger caused by their being prevented from seeing My feet by showing them My feet.’ He thus went there on foot as a way of showing His haste. He was accompanied by the goddess Sri to secure their forgiveness by showering them with opulence, even though they were free from desire.”

Previously, the sages had observed Him only in the ecstatic trance of their yogic meditation, but now He stood directly in front of them. They were awe-struck. “As He came forward, accompanied by His own associates bearing all paraphernalia, such as an umbrella and a camara fan, the white bunches of hair moved very gently, like two swans, and due to their favorable breeze the pearls garlanding the umbrella also moved, like drops of nectar falling from the white full moon or ice melting due to a gust of wind. The Lord is the reservoir of all pleasure. His auspicious presence is meant for everyone’s benediction, and His affectionate smiling and glancing touch the core of the heart. The Lord’s beautiful bodily color is blackish, and His broad chest is the resting place of the goddess of fortune, who glorifies the entire spiritual world, the summit of all heavenly planets. Thus it appeared that the Lord was personally spreading the beauty and good fortune of the spiritual world.” (Bhag. [3.15.38-39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.38))

The Kumaras saw that Lord Narayana’s wrists were graced with bracelets, and despite the fact that He had run to protect His gatekeepers, He was casually resting one hand on Garuda’s shoulder and twirling a lotus flower in the other. The sages gazed at the Lord’s face with “unsated” eyes, then bowed their heads at His feet (Bhag. [3.15.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.42)).

That the four Kumaras stared at the Lord’s form but felt no satiation confirms that the Lord’s form is transcendental, because the sages, who were transcendental and beyond the lure of matter, were so struck by the Lord’s beauty. They were so captivated that although they had previously been fixed in meditation on the formless Brahman, they now wished to gaze forever at this beautiful form.

In Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 78, Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on text 38 as follows: The sages now saw the Lord directly before them. Formerly, He had only been visible in their hearts. This text affirms that it is possible to directly perceive the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and refutes the following ideas: 1. the Lord’s form is a superfluous appearance imposed on the formless Brahman; 2. the goodness of which the Lord’s form is composed is mixed with other modes and is material; 3. the Lord’s form is a transformation of the material mode of goodness; and 4. the Lord’s form is primarily filled with the mode of goodness.

Prabhupada describes the Lord’s beauty in his purport to text 42:

**In the words of Vaisnava poets, it is said that the Lord’s beauty is so enchanting that it defeats hundreds of thousands of Cupids. He is therefore called Madana-mohana. It is also described that the Lord sometimes becomes mad after the beauty of Radharani. Poets describe that under those circumstances, although Lord Krsna is Madana-mohana, He becomes Madana-daha, or enchanted by the beauty of Radharani. Actually the Lord’s beauty is superexcellent, surpassing even the beauty of Laksmi in Vaikuntha. The devotees of the Lord in the Vaikuntha planets want to see the Lord as the most beautiful, but the devotees in Gokula or Krsnaloka want to see Radharani as more beautiful than Krsna. The adjustment is that the Lord, being bhakta-vatsala, or one who wants to please His devotees, assumes such features so that devotees like Lord Brahma, Lord Siva and other demigods may be pleased. Here also, for the devotee-sages, the Kumaras, the Lord appeared in His most beautiful feature, and they continued to see Him without satiation and wanted to continue seeing Him more and more.**

It is interesting to note that the Lord is neither aloof nor neutral in His dealings. As Bhagavatam [3.15.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.39) asserts, the Lord’s “affectionate smiling and glancing touch the core of the heart.”

Just as the Kumaras were beholding the Lord, a breeze carrying the aroma of the tulasi leaves decorating His lotus feet entered their nostrils. These sages were attached to the impersonal Brahman aspect of the Lord, but when they smelled that spiritual fragrance, their minds and bodies became affected. The four Kumaras were beyond matter— even beyond the mode of goodness—but the transcendental aroma of tulasi transformed them. Rather than desiring to become one with the Lord, they now desired to serve Him. The four sages had traveled freely and had fully experienced the material world, but the fragrance of tulasi on the Lord’s feet was a new transcendental experience. From it they understood that everything connected with the Lord—from the fragrance of His lotus feet to the unparalleled sweetness of His beauty— was beyond matter and was completely spiritual. Their new attraction brought ecstatic transformations to body and mind, and they became devotees.

Referring to text 43, Srila Sridhara Svami analyzes their ecstatic transformations: This wind carried the fragrance of tulasi leaves mixed with saffron particles and entered their nostrils. Aksarajusam means “even though they relished the bliss of Brahman, they nevertheless experienced ‘agitation’ or ‘elation’ in their consciousness, and ‘horripilation,’ the standing on end of the bodily hairs.” Thus the bliss they experienced in devotional service was greater than the bliss caused by simply realizing their spiritual nature.

What other feelings did the Kumaras experience when they saw the Lord? “The Lord’s beautiful face appeared to them like the inside of a blue lotus, and the Lord’s smile appeared to be a blossoming jasmine flower. After seeing the face of the Lord, the sages were fully satisfied, and when they wanted to see Him further, they looked upon the nails of His lotus feet, which resembled rubies. Thus they viewed the Lord’s transcendental body again and again, and so they finally achieved meditation on the Lord’s personal feature.” (Bhag. [3.15.44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.44))

To what in this world can the Lord’s beauty be compared? Of course, the Lord’s beauty is transcendental, beyond this world’s dull matter, but as one can glimpse the moon by being directed where to look—“just above that tree branch”—one can be afforded a distant glimpse of Krsna’s beauty by drawing comparisons to beautiful things in this world. One should know, however, that all words and analogies fall short of the actual truth.
