In his book Madhurya-kadambini, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura repeats the words of an exalted prema^bhakta whose love has attracted Krsna to appear before his eyes for the first time:

**Just yesterday I was rudely comparing Your dark limbs to the fresh monsoon cloud, the blue lotus, and the sapphire, Your beautiful face to the moon, and the tenderness of Your feet to newly sprouted leaves. Seeing Your real beauty, I realize that I was offending You by my poor intelligence. I was trying to compare half a useless mustard seed to golden Mount Meru, a chickpea to a touchstone, a jackal to a lion, and a mosquito to Garuda. I was thinking, “I am praising the Lord,” and my inept poetry became famous among common people, but now for one moment I behold the splend-orous beauty of Your form before my eyes and I have become ashamed. My words of comparison are like the teeth of a restless cow trying to defile the desire creeper of Your beauty. But they are unable to do so.**

The Kumaras, who were accomplished yogis and the gurus of all impersonalists, had now achieved the full perfection of their practice by directly beholding the Lord’s exquisite form. Prabhupada’s lengthy purport to text 45, a segment of which is included below, explains the relationship between yoga and the practice of Krsna consciousness:

**In this age, people in general are short-living and very slow to understand self-realization or spiritual life; they are mostly unfortunate, and therefore if someone is a little bit interested in selfrealization he is likely to be misguided by so many frauds. The only way to realize the perfect stage of yoga is to follow the principles of Bhagavad-gita as practiced by Lord Caitanya. This is the simplest and highest perfection of yoga practice. Lord Caitanya demonstrated this Krsna consciousness yoga system in a practical manner simply by chanting the holy name of Krsna, as prescribed in the Vedanta, Srimad-Bhagavatam, Bhagavad-gita, and many important Puranas. ... It is very easy and practical for this age, especially for those who are serious about success in yoga. No other process of yoga can be successful in this age. The meditation process was possible in the golden age, Satya-yuga, because people in that age used to live for hundreds of thousands of years. If one wants success in practical yoga practice, it is advised that he take to the chanting of Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare, and he will actually feel himself making progress.**

## Texts 46-50: The Four Kumaras Offer Prayers to Lord Narayana

The Kumaras began to offer the Lord prayers: “Our dear Lord, You are not manifested to rascals, even though You are seated within the heart of everyone. But as far as we are concerned, we see You face to face, although You are unlimited. The statements we have heard about You from our father, Brahma, through the ears have now been actually realized by Your kind appearance.” (Bhag. [3.15.46](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.46))

Priti-sandarbha, anuccheda 203, cites this verse to illustrate the sthayi-bhava of a jnana-bhakta who had been attached to the impersonal Brahman. This indicates that the Kumaras’ association with the Lord elevated them from impersonalists to bhaktas in santa-rasa. Srila Prabhupada states in his purport to this verse that “because they were sincerely searching for the Lord, they finally saw His personal feature directly, which corresponded with the description given by their father. They thus became fully satisfied.” The Lord’s mercy combined with the sages’ purity and sincerity allowed them to see Narayana, who although unlimited, possesses a form of eternity, bliss, and knowledge. His form is free of bone, muscle, and mucus; it is fully spiritual. Those of us who possess impure desires (duratmana) remain unable to see it.

What did these sages realize about Lord Narayana’s form? “We know that You are the Supreme Absolute Truth, the Personality of Godhead, who manifests His transcendental form in the uncontaminated mode of pure goodness. This transcendental, eternal form of Your personality can be understood only by Your mercy, through unflinching devotional service, by great sages whose hearts have been purified in the devotional way.” (Bhag. [3.15.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.47))

Srila Prabhupada offers the essential message of the two prayers contained in texts 46 and 47, and explores the relationship between mercy and qualification, in his purport to text 47: “It is said that one can understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead when one is even slightly favored by Him; otherwise, without His mercy, a man may speculate for thousands of years and not understand what is actually the Absolute Truth. This mercy can be perceived by the devotee when he is completely freed from contamination. It is stated, therefore, that only when all contamination is rooted out and the devotee is completely detached from material attractions can he receive this mercy of the Lord.”

Prior to seeing the Lord, the Kumaras had realized only His Brahman feature and had only heard from Brahma of His existence—the existence of a transcendental person who was the source of Brahman. Now by the Lord’s mercy they were actually seeing the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Thus they expressed their gratitude to Him and confirmed that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the highest and most complete revelation of the Absolute Truth.

It is rare to achieve darsana of the Lord’s personal form. Ordinary people cannot see powerful kings; such persons may deal only with the king’s power—his delegates and government. Few people can visit a king when he is relaxing in his quarters with his family, yet the king may invite a qualified citizen into his chambers at any time. Whoever is invited has received the king’s mercy. That same path of mercy allows us Krsna’s intimate association in Vrndavana.

But who is qualified to receive such mercy? The scriptures teach that the qualification to receive mercy is complete sincerity, defined as the unmixed, deep eagerness to serve. As Srila Prabhupada states in his purport to Bhagavatam [7.15.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/15.20): “If one is very greedy to enhance his Krsna consciousness, this is a great boon. Tatra laulyam ekalam mulam. This is the best path available.” One possessing such a jewel can attract Krsna’s mercy. One cannot force Krsna to invite him.In Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 78, Srila Jiva Gosvami adds some details to the exchange between the Kumaras and the Lord as recorded in texts 46 and 47. A paraphrase follows:

**At this point Lord Narayana may object, “Has not your father taught you that the Absolute Truth is invisible and secret? Because I, Narayana, am now openly visible before your eyes, I therefore cannot be that Absolute Truth. I must be something else.”**

**The Kumaras reject the idea that Lord Narayana is different from the Absolute Truth. They say \[in text 47\], “O Supreme Personality of Godhead (bhagavdn), we know (vidama) that You are the same Supreme Absolute Truth (param atma-tattvam), whose form is spiritual.”**

**Lord Narayana may then ask, “How do you know?”**

**The Kumaras may then reply, “We know because You have now (samprati) manifest Your transcendental form before us in the uncontaminated mode of pure goodness (sattvena). Until this moment we did not understand You, but now that we can see You directly, we have concluded that You are the Supreme. You are visible to our eyes just as Brahman appears in the functioning of a pure heart. In other words, You are not perceived as a \[material\] object of vision.”**

**The Kumaras continue, “You are not known through transcendental knowledge \[devoid of love for You\]. You have created (racayantam) our love (ratim) for You, for otherwise we could not love You. You are better than Brahman because by Your appearance we have attained ratim, attachment to You. We could not be attached to Your form if it were material.”**

The Kumaras then describe how the Lord’s spiritual form becomes manifest by His mercy (anutapa-viditair): by practicing unflinching devotional service (drdha-bhakti-yogaih) one understands the Lord’s spiritual form. The way of attaining His mercy includes genuine humility, by which one comes to understand unflinching pure devotional service.

What qualities characterize those who have rejected the impersonal as the highest realization and who understand Bhagavan as supreme? The four Kumaras continue: “Persons who are very expert and most intelligent in understanding things as they are engage in hearing narrations of the auspicious activities and pastimes of the Lord, which are worth chanting and worth hearing. Such persons do not care even for the highest material benediction, namely liberation, to say nothing of other less important benedictions like the material happiness of the heavenly kingdom. О Lord, we pray that You let us be born in any hellish condition of life, just as long as our hearts and minds are always engaged in the service of Your lotus feet, our words are made beautiful \[by speaking of Your activities\] just as tulasl leaves are beautified when offered unto Your lotus feet, and as long as our ears are always filled with the chanting of Your transcendental qualities.” (Bhag. [3.15.48-49](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.48))

The Kumaras, who had once desired freedom from birth and death, now cared neither for liberation nor an auspicious birth. Even if they were to take birth in hell because of their offense, they desired simply that their hearts and minds be engaged in the Lord’s service. They prayed to speak of His activities and fill their ears with accounts of His transcendental qualities. Srila Prabhupada underscores these essential points: “Pure devotional service is sravanam kirtanam. Pure devotees, who take transcendental pleasure in hearing and chanting the glories of the Lord, do not care for any kind of liberation . . .” (Bhag. [3.15.48](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.48), purport) Earlier in the same purport Prabhupada states, “The transcendental bliss enjoyed by the devotees of the Lord is completely different from the material happiness enjoyed by less intelligent persons.”

Expressing their change of heart, the Kumaras offered the prayer in text 49 and saw value only in serving Krsna. They now began to understand the fault in their having cursed the two gatekeepers. Sri Jiva, in Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 78, comments: “And now, alluding to their offense, they pray for devotional service in the verse beginning kamam. О Lord, before this we had no distress, but now all distress has arisen because we cursed Your two devotees. Therefore let our existence, our birth, be with that distress and in various hells.”

In his purport to text 49, Srila Prabhupada describes the mood in which the Kumaras offered their prayer: “The four sages now offer their humility to the Personality of Godhead because of their having been haughty in cursing two other devotees of the Lord. Jaya and Vijaya, the two doorkeepers who checked them from entering the Vaikuntha planet, were certainly offenders, but as Vaisnavas, the four sages should not have cursed them in anger. After the incident, they became conscious that they had done wrong by cursing the devotees of the Lord, and they prayed to the Lord that even in the hellish condition of life their minds might not be distracted from the engagement of service to the lotus feet of Lord Narayana.”

The Kumaras thus reveal that what one should really fear is not hell but forgetfulness of Krsna and His service. After being cursed, Jaya and Vijaya had a similar fear: “the illusion of forgetting the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [3.15.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.36)) That neither heaven nor hell is preferable to a devotee rapt in remembrance of Krsna will later be explained by Maharaja Citraketu in Bhagavatam [6.17.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-6/17.28): “Devotees solely engaged in the devotional service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Narayana, never fear any condition of life. For them the heavenly planets, liberation and the hellish planets are all the same, for such devotees are interested only in the service of the Lord.”

Srila Prabhupada brings the Kumaras’ mood to a practical conclusion in a later section of his purport to text 49: “A devotee is not afraid of going to hell if he has the opportunity to hear the glories of the Lord constantly. This is the advantage of chanting Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare. One may be put in any condition, but God gives him the prerogative to chant Hare Krsna. In any condition of life, if one goes on chanting he will never be unhappy.” These statements allow readers to glimpse the actual value of devotional service. Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 48: “When Lord Caitanya was talking with Ramananda Raya, there were varieties of suggestions offered by Ramananda regarding spiritual realization, but Lord Caitanya rejected all but one—that one should hear the glories of the Lord in association with pure devotees. That is acceptable for everyone, especially in this age. One should engage himself in hearing from pure devotees about the activities of the Lord. That is considered the supreme benediction for mankind.”

In addition, Jiva Gosvami’s comments on these texts in Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 78, demonstrate that personalism is superior to impersonalism. “And, ‘Oh,’ they pray with pitiful cries, ‘Let these hellish sufferings occur, for we have no fear of them. But please do not let us obtain the ultimate undesirable consequence of enmity toward the Personality of Godhead. Let our hearts take pleasure at Your feet and become like bees who are interested only in tasting their sweetness. This is what we desire, instead of desiring to experience Brahman and the self.’ . . . From the sense of these two verses it can be inferred that ‘For we who only desire devotional service to You, even hell is better than impersonal merging. All the same, it is most astonishing how our lives have become successful in this way.’” To this Sri Jiva adds: “Here we should understand that the Supreme Lord forgave the offense to His devotees because it was only a shadow, an imitation of an offense, for it had originated in anger created merely by His own desire.”

The Kumaras then offer their final prayer to the Lord in text 50:

“O Lord, we therefore offer our respectful obeisances unto Your eternal form as the Personality of Godhead, which You have so kindly manifested before us. Your supreme, eternal form cannot be seen by unfortunate, less intelligent persons, but we are so much satisfied in our mind and vision to see it.”

Jiva Gosvami also comments on this text (Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 78). He paraphrases the Kumaras as follows: “You do not appear before those who do not have unalloyed devotion for You, but now You have appeared before us (pratitah) and we offer (vidhema) our respectful obeisances (namah) to You (tasmai).”

Further on in the same anuccheda, Jiva Gosvami cites a quotation from Bhagavatam [12.12.69](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-12/12.69) that glorifies another self-satisfied imper-sonalist who became attracted to the Supreme Person: “Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto my spiritual master, the son of Vyasadeva, Sukadeva Gosvami. It is he who defeats all inauspicious things within this universe. Although in the beginning he was absorbed in the happiness of Brahman realization and was living in a secluded place, giving up all other kinds of consciousness, he became attracted by the most melodious pastimes of Lord Krsna. He therefore mercifully spoke the supreme Purana, known as Srimad-Bhagavatam, which is the light of the Absolute Truth and which describes the activities of Lord Krsna.”

The Kumaras have concluded their prayers by offering their respectful obeisances to the Lord’s form, whom neither the unfortunate nor the less intelligent can see, but which He has so mercifully manifest before them. Seeing this form, they were now folly satisfied in both eyes and mind.

## Chapter 16 - The Two Doorkeepers of Vaikuntha, Jaya and Vijaya, Cursed by the Sages

## Texts 1-12: The Lord Replies to the Four Kumaras—The Lord Expresses His Love for His Devotees

By now the sages have both recognized and acknowledged their fault in cursing Jaya and Vijaya. They have also expressed their new appreciation for Lord Narayana’s form, which they had come to understand as completely spiritual.

How will the Lord respond to their supplication? Astoundingly, His first words were “These attendants of Mine, Jaya and Vijaya by name, have committed a great offense against you because of ignoring Me. О great sages, I approve of the punishment that you who are devoted to Me have meted out to them.... The disrespect shown by My attendants has actually been displayed by Me because the doormen are My servitors. I take this to be an offense by Myself; therefore I seek your forgiveness for the incident that has arisen.” (Bhag. [3.16.2-4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.2))

The weight of the “offense” supposedly committed by the doorkeepers was accepted by their master, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Srila Prabhupada uses this example in his purport to text 2 to illustrate the reciprocation between the Lord and His devotees: “Even when a living entity is promoted to Vaikuntha, there is still the chance that he may commit offenses, but the difference is that when one is in a Vaikuntha planet, even if by chance one commits an offense, he is protected by the Lord. This is the remarkable fact in the dealings of the Lord and the servitor ... The Lord understood that the trouble was due to His lotus feet not being seen by the sages, and therefore He wanted to please them by personally going there. The Lord is so merciful that even if there is some impediment for the devotee, He Himself manages matters in such a way that the devotee is not bereft of having audience at His lotus feet.”

But in his purport to text 5, Srila Prabhupada cautions us to act with care: “A devotee should always see that his Vaisnava qualities increase with the advancement of his Krsna consciousness. A devotee should be blameless because any offense by the devotee is a scar on the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The devotee’s duty is to be always conscious in his dealings with others, especially with another devotee of the Lord.”

Continuing to describe His full dedication to His devotees, the Lord said: “Anyone in the entire world, even down to the candala, who lives by cooking and eating the flesh of the dog, is immediately purified if he takes bath in hearing through the ear the glorification of My name, fame, etc. Now you have realized Me without doubt; therefore I will not hesitate to lop off My own arm if its conduct is found hostile to you.” (Bhag. [3.16.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.6))

The Lord expressed His gratitude to the Kumaras, who had recently become His devotees. How obliged He must have felt to His gatekeepers, who had been directly serving Him for so much longer. The Lord, the greatest of teachers, was indirectly instructing the Kumaras and sparking their realization about the depth of the love He feels for His devotees. Again they became aware of the offense they had committed toward the Lord’s gatekeepers; by hearing Lord Narayana glorify Jaya and Vijaya, the sages felt even more remorseful.Lord Narayana then credited the sacredness of His feet to the fact that He serves His devotees: “Because I am the servitor of My devotees, My lotus feet have become so sacred that they immediately wipe out all sin, and I have acquired such a disposition that the goddess of fortune does not leave Me, even though I have no attachment for her and others praise her beauty and observe sacred vows to secure from her even a slight favor.” (Bhag. [3.16.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.7)) Srila Prabhupada’s purports to texts 6 and 7 enter the heart of the Lord’s mood:

**If one takes to Krsna consciousness with all seriousness, he is to be understood as already purified, and Krsna is ready to give him protection by all means. The Lord assures herein that He is ready to give protection to His devotee even if there is need to cut off part of His own body. (Bhag.** [**3.16.6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.6)**, purport)**

**The Lord admits herein that although He certainly has the quality that anyone who receives a slight particle of the dust of His lotus feet becomes at once a great personality, this greatness is due to His affection for His devotee. It is because of this affection that the goddess of fortune does not leave Him and that not only one but many thousands of goddesses of fortune engage in His service.. .. He is therefore famous as bhakta-vatsala. (Bhag.** [**3.16.7**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.7)**, purport)**

In Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya [24.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/24.42), Srila Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami glorifies the Lord’s qualities: “Krsna’s transcendental qualities of opulence, sweetness and mercy are perfect and full. As far as Krsna’s affectionate leaning toward His devotees is concerned, He is so magnanimous that He can give Himself to His devotees.”

After revealing His pleasure at seeing Vaisnavas and brahmanas fed, the Lord declared: “If I can take the dust of the feet of the Vaisnavas on My head, who will refuse to do the same?” (Bhag. [3.16.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.9)) Srila Prabhupada explains the conclusion one should reach after hearing the above statement: “(If one can feed a brahmana or Vaisnava, it is better than performing hundreds of thousands of sacrifices. In this age, therefore, it is recommended that harer nama—chanting the holy name of God—and pleasing the Vaisnava are the only means to elevate oneself to spiritual life.” (Bhag. [3.16.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.8), purport)

Expressing the natural love He felt for His servants, the Lord then begged the Kumaras that these “servants of Mine . . . may return to My presence soon and the time of their exile from My abode may expire before long.\*’ (Bhag. [3.16.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.12)) Srila Prabhupada’s purport to this text highlights an important point: “It is to be assumed that there is no possibility of a misunderstanding between the Lord and the devotees, but when there are discrepancies or disruptions between one devotee and another, one has to suffer the consequences, although that suffering is temporary.”

## Texts 13-25: The Four Kumaras Remain Submissive

On hearing the Lord’s words, which were both sweet and profound, the Kumaras found that they could not understand whether the Lord was pleased or displeased with them. Srila Prabhupada expresses their mind: “The sages tried with wide-open ears to understand the words from the lips of the Supreme Lord, but although His speech was very concise and meaningful, the sages could not completely comprehend what He was saying. They could not even comprehend the purport of the speech or what the Supreme Lord wanted to do. Nor could they understand whether the Lord was angry or pleased with them.” (Bhag. [3.16.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.14), purport)

But despite being almost too puzzled to speak, the sages’ hair stood on end in ecstasy. They expressed their confusion: “O Supreme Personality of Godhead, we are unable to know what You intend for us to do, for even though You are the supreme ruler of all, You speak in our favor as if we had done something good for You.” (Bhag. [3.16.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.16)) The Kumaras stated that the Lord teaches by His humble words that everyone should honor brahmanas: You Yourself are the supreme objective of religious principles. You are eternally inexhaustible and unchangeable! Your words and acts protect religion. Everyone—both mystics and other transcendentalists—depend on Your mercy to cross beyond the ocean of ignorance. Clearly, no one is in a position to bestow their favor on You.

Then the Kumaras poetically glorified the Lord’s unique, independent position: “The goddess of fortune, Laksmi, the dust of whose feet is worn on the head by others, waits upon You, as appointed, for she is anxious to secure a place in the abode of the king of bees, who hovers on the fresh wreath of tulasi leaves offered at Your feet by some blessed devotee.” (Bhag. [3.16.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.20))

Srila Prabhupada emphasizes the Lord’s unequaled position in his purport to text 20: “As previously described, tulasi has attained all superior qualities due to being placed at the lotus feet of the Lord. The comparison made here is very nice. As the king of bees hovers over the tulasi leaves offered to the lotus feet of the Lord, so Laksmi, the goddess who is sought by the demigods, brahmanas, Vaisnavas and everyone else, always engages in rendering service to the lotus feet of the Lord. The conclusion is that no one can be the benefactor of the Lord; everyone is actually the servant of the servant of the Lord.”

The Kumaras next expressed wonder at the supremely independent Lord’s humble actions and words: О Lord, You are very attached to the activities of Your pure devotees, yet You are never attached to the goddesses of fortune who constantly serve You with loving devotion. How can You be purified, therefore, by the dust of the path traversed by the brahmanas, and how can You be glorified or made fortunate by the marks of Srivatsa on Your chest?

Then they repeated their acknowledgment of the Lord’s humble words and His ability to illuminate the proper path: О Lord, You personify religion! You protect the universe! You bestow all blessing! And You protect religion and set the proper example by respecting the twice-born brahmanas, speaking to them with gentle words. Thus You protect the path of auspiciousness for the benefit of the people in general. You own the three creations and maintain the entire universe. Therefore Your potency is not reduced by Your submissive behavior. Rather, by submission You exhibit Your transcendental pastimes.

Witnessing the Lord’s humility and submission, the Kumaras again rejected their curse as rash: “O Lord, whatever punishment You wish to award to these two innocent persons or also to us we shall accept without duplicity. We understand that we have cursed two faultless persons.” (Bhag. [3.16.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.25)) The Kumaras realized that they had made a grave mistake.

Srila Prabhupada describes the care with which we should deal with devotees: “In general, when dealing with devotees, we should not try to find faults. In Bhagavad-gita also it is confirmed that the devotee who faithfully serves the Supreme Lord, even if found to commit a gross mistake, should be considered a sadhu, or saintly person. Due to former habits he may commit some wrong, but because he is engaged in the service of the Lord, that wrong should not be taken very seriously.” (Bhag. [3.16.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.25), purport)

## Texts 26-34: Who was Actually at Fault, the Gatekeepers or the Four Kumaras?

The gatekeepers, the Kumaras, and the Lord Himself each took the blame for the curse uttered by the Kumaras. After being cursed, Jaya and Vijaya thought themselves in error and liable for punishment. They asked only that they never forget the Lord (Bhag. [3.15.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.36)). Similarly, after seeing the Lord and hearing of His dedication to His devotees, the Kumaras understood the supremacy of devotional service. They then viewed themselves as at fault and liable for punishment. Like Jaya and Vijaya, they requested that even if they were sent to hell they would remain ever able to serve the Lord with heart and mind (Bhag. [3.15.49](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.49)). Lord Narayana also took responsibility for His devotee-gatekeepers’ actions (Bhag. [3.16.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.4)). Now the Lord reveals the truth: this entire episode was a pastime He had preordained. Therefore, Jaya and Vijaya “will fall to a birth in a demoniac family. But they will be firmly united with Me in thought through mental concentration intensified by anger, and they will return to My presence shortly.” (Bhag. [3.16.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.26)) Prabhupada gives an extensive explanation of the Lord’s purpose in arranging for the cursing of Jaya and Vijaya:

**The Lord stated that the punishment inflicted by the sages upon the doorkeepers Jaya and Vijaya was conceived by the Lord Himself. Without the Lord’s sanction, nothing can happen. It is to be understood that there was a plan in the cursing of the Lord’s devotees in Vaikuntha, and His plan is explained by many stalwart authorities. The Lord sometimes desires to fight. The fighting spirit also exists in the Supreme Lord, otherwise how could fighting be manifested at all? Because the Lord is the source of everything, anger and fighting are also inherent in His personality. When He desires to fight with someone, He has to find an enemy, but in the Vaikuntha world there is no enemy because everyone is engaged fully in His service. Therefore He sometimes comes to the material world as an incarnation in order to manifest His fighting spirit. . .. Thus Jaya and Vijaya were selected by the Lord to fight with Him in the material world, and that was the reason the sages came to see Him and accidentally the doorkeepers were cursed.**

Thereafter, the sages, experiencing the delight of contemplating Lord Narayana’s supreme position, and understanding the position of His devotees and the spiritual world, circumambulated the Lord and left His presence. The Supreme Lord then encouraged Jaya and Vijaya by openly revealing that everything had occurred by His merciful desire: “Depart this place, but fear not. All glories unto you. Though I am capable of nullifying the brahmanas’ curse, I would not do so. On the contrary, it has My approval.” (Bhag. [3.16.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.29))

In anuccheda 92 of the Priti-sandarbha, Srila Jiva Gosvami indicates that the devotional intimacy between the Lord and His gatekeepers was greater than that between the Lord and the Kumaras. Sri Jiva explains that specific Bhagavatam texts ([3.15.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.37), [3.16.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.4), [3.16.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.25), and [3.16.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.29)) make it clear that Jaya and Vijaya were the Supreme Lord’s personal associates and had achieved the special mercy of His close service. The Kumaras, on the other hand, were more distantly associated with the Lord in the mood of awe and reverence. Also, Lord Narayana told Jaya and Vijaya, their “departure from Vaikuntha was foretold by Laksmi, the goddess of fortune. She was very angry because when she left My abode and then returned, you stopped her at the gate while I was sleeping.” (Bhag. [3.16.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.30)) Assured by the Lord that they would soon return to Vaikuntha, Jaya and Vijaya fell to the material world and entered Diti’s womb.

## Texts 35-37: Brahma’s Concluding Words to the Demigods

By narrating how Lord Narayana allowed the four Kumaras to curse His two gatekeepers, Brahma revealed to the demigods the history of Diti’s sons: the two had originated in Vaikuntha. Therefore, even though they were still in the womb of their mother, their almost unlimited power rendered them capable of causing the darkness now enveloping the universe. He concluded: “There is no remedy within my power, however, for it is the Lord Himself who desires to do all this.... That most ancient person, the Personality of Godhead, will alone come to our rescue. What purpose can we serve on His behalf by deliberating on this subject?” (Bhag. [3.16.36-37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/16.36)) Maharaja Pariksit, Maharaja Ambarisa, Maharaja Rantideva, the Pandavas, Maharaja Citreketu, and countless other exalted devotees have undergone tribulation that to ordinary vision would seem unnecessary. Why should Krsna’s devotees suffer so severely? It is natural to ask this.

On seeing the extent of the Pandavas’ suffering, Bhismadeva, on his deathbed, answered the question with simple words: “O King, no one can know the plan of the Lord \[Sri Krsna\]. Even though great philosophers inquire exhaustively, they are bewildered.” (Bhag. [1.9.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/9.16))

Devotees accept everything as Krsna’s plan, and they teach others by acting for His pleasure in all circumstances. They do not see any event as happening separately from His mercy. This vision qualifies them to enter the kingdom of God: “My dear Lord, one who earnestly waits for You to bestow Your causeless mercy upon him, all the while patiently suffering the reactions of his past misdeeds and offering You respectful obeisances with his heart, words and body, is surely eligible for liberation, for it has become his rightful claim.” (Bhag. [10.14.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.8)) Srila Prabhupada’s final purport to this chapter (text 37) explains how we must all be fully dependent on Krsna and bow to His plan, even if we are unable to comprehend it:

**When something is arranged by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one should not be disturbed by it, even if it appears to be a reverse according to one’s calculations. For example, sometimes we see that a powerful preacher is killed, or sometimes he is put into difficulty, just as Haridasa Thakura was. He was a great devotee who came into this material world to execute the will of the Lord by preaching the Lord’s glories. But Haridasa was punished at the hands of the Kazi by being beaten in twenty-two marketplaces. Similarly, Lord Jesus Christ was crucified, and Prahlada Maharaja was put through so many tribulations. The Pandavas, who were direct friends of Krsna, lost their kingdom, their wife was insulted, and they had to undergo many severe tribulations. Seeing all these reverses affect devotees, one should not be disturbed; one should simply understand that in these matters there must be some plan of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Bhagavatam's conclusion is that a devotee is never disturbed by such reverses. He accepts even reverse conditions as the grace of the Lord. One who continues to serve the Lord even in reverse conditions is assured that he will go back to Godhead, back to the Vaikuntha planets. Lord Brahma assured the demigods that there was no use in talking about how the disturbing situation of darkness was taking place, since the actual fact was that it was ordered by the Supreme Lord. Brahma knew this because he was a great devotee; it was possible for him to understand the plan of the Lord.**

Hearing from Brahma that the ultimate solution was to take shelter of Krsna, the demigods experienced peace, their fear having vanished. Srila Prabhupada offers a “conclusive instruction of this incident” in his purport to Bhagavatam [3.17.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/17.1): “We may be disturbed by some material condition, but if we approach the authority who can actually explain the matter, then our problem is solved. The demigods approached Brahma for the meaning of the disturbance, and after hearing from him they were satisfied and returned home peacefully.”

Thus by Krsna’s arrangement, the gatekeepers would taste the fortune of serving the Lord with focused remembrance, the Lord would relish the pleasure of fighting, and the Kumaras’ bliss would increase, for they had become pure devotees. Not only that, but the countless persons who would hear this pastime in Srimad-Bhagavatam would benefit because topics about Krsna have great spiritual potency. The Vraja gopis state: “The nectar of Your words and the descriptions of Your activities are the life and soul of those suffering in this material world. These narrations, transmitted by learned sages, eradicate one’s sinful reactions and bestow good fortune upon whoever hears them. These narrations are broadcast all over the world and are filled with spiritual power. Certainly those who spread the message of Godhead are most munificent.” (Bhag. 10.31.9)

## Chapter 17 - The Victory of Hiranyaksa Over All the Directions of the Universe (Texts 1-31)

Maitreya Muni now returns to the fight between Varahadeva and Hiranyaksa, since he had mentioned it only briefly in Bhagavatam [3.13.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.31).

Diti gave birth to twin sons after a full one hundred years of pregnancy. At their birth, inauspicious signs appeared throughout the universe. Srila Prabhupada describes the ominous import of natural catastrophes: “When there are natural disturbances like blowing cyclones, too much heat or snowfall, and uprooting of trees by hurricanes, it is to be understood that the demoniac population is increasing and so the natural disturbance is also taking place. There are many countries on the globe, even at the present moment, where all these disturbances are current. This is true all over the world. There is insufficient sunshine, and there are always clouds in the sky, snowfall and severe cold. These assure that such places are inhabited by demoniac people who are accustomed to all kinds of forbidden, sinful activity.” (Bhag. [3.17.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/17.5), purport)

Kasyapa Muni named his firstborn son Hiranyaksa and the second Hiranyakasipu. Kasyapa considered Hiranyakasipu the elder twin because he was bom last, which meant he had been conceived first. The two demons grew quickly. Their bodies became as hard as steel and they assumed mountainlike proportions. Hiranyaksa, his temper flaring, traveled throughout the universe and challenged every demigod to fight with him. Varuna, however, warned Hiranyaksa: Lord Visnu Himself will meet you in battle and remove your pride.

## Chapters 18-19 - The Battle Between Lord Boar and Hiranyaksa, and the Killing of Hiranyaksa

**The Meeting of Hiranyaksa and Lord Varahadeva**

On hearing Varuna’s warning, Hiranyaksa immediately sought out Lord Visnu. The demon came upon the Lord as He was bearing the earth upward from the bottom of the Garbhodaka Ocean. Hiranyaksa laughed to see the Lord in the water. He cried out, “Oh, Visnu is an amphibious beast!” He then insulted and challenged Lord Varahadeva. The demon’s abusive, shaftlike words pained the Lord.

In his purport to Bhagavatam [3.18.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/18.6), Srila Prabhupada emphasizes God’s personality: “In this case, although the Lord felt sorrow from the piercing words of the demon, He delivered the earth for the satisfaction of the demigods, who are ever His devotees. The conclusion is that God is as sentient as we are. He is satisfied by our prayers and dissatisfied by our harsh words against Him.”

Yet despite Hiranyaksa’s words, Lord Varaha neglected his challenge and first set the earth in a safe place in His sight. By His potency, He caused the earth to float, and then, while the enemy looked on, Brahma extolled the Lord and the demigods showered Him with flowers. Lord Varaha then turned to face Hiranyaksa, who was dressed in golden armor and who had chased Him from behind. Roaring like thunder, Hiranyaksa continued to hurl abuses: Are You not ashamed of running away before a challenging adversary? Nothing is reproachable for shameless creatures!

The Lord said: “Indeed, We are creatures of the jungle, and We are searching after hunting dogs like you. One who is freed from the entanglement of death has no fear from the loose talk in which you are indulging, for you are bound up by the laws of death. . . . Give up all your foolish talk and wipe out the cares of your kith and kin by slaying Us. One may be proud, yet he does not deserve a seat in an assembly if he fails to fulfill his promised word.” (Bhag. [3.18.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/18.10), [12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/18.12)) Hiranyaksa trembled like a cobra when he heard these words. He then attempted to hit the Lord with his mace. The Lord moved slightly and dodged the violent blow aimed at His chest. While protecting Himself with His own mace, Varahadeva then struck His enemy to the right of his brow.

As the rivals fought on and on, Lord Brahma begged the Lord to play with this arrogant demon no longer: Kill him quickly! Nighttime approaches and in darkness his power will increase! Kill this formidable foe and win victory for the demigods! Kill him now! The Lord laughed heartily and accepted Brahma’s prayer with a glance laden with love. Before long, in the midst of their tumultuous battle, even as Hiranyaksa fearlessly stalked Him, Varahadeva invoked His Sudarsana cakra. “As the discus began to revolve in the Lord’s hands and the Lord contended at close quarters with the chief of His Vaikuntha attendants, who had been born as Hiranyaksa, a vile son of Diti, there issued from every direction strange expressions uttered by those who were witnessing from airplanes. They had no knowledge of the Lord’s reality, and they cried, ‘May victory attend You! Pray dispatch him. Play no more with him.’” (Bhag. [3.19.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/19.6))

Hiranyaksa hissed like a serpent and bit his lip in resentment. He stared at the Personality of Godhead as though to bum Him. Springing into the air, he aimed his mace at the Lord, yelling, “You are slain!” But the Lord playfully knocked down Hiranyaksa’s mace with His left foot, even as it came on Him with the force of a tempest. The Lord then said, “Pick up your weapon and try again, eager as you are to conquer Me.” Challenged, Hiranyaksa aimed his mace again and roared. When the Lord saw the mace coming toward Him, He stood His ground and caught it with the same ease as Garuda seizes a serpent.

Hiranyaksa’s valor was frustrated. Humiliated, he refused to accept the mace when Lord Varahadeva attempted to return it. Instead, the demon attacked the Lord with his trident, which was as threatening as raging fire. But the Lord’s Sudarsana cakra ripped the trident to pieces. After failing in his next attempt to harm the Lord by striking Him with his fists, Hiranyaksa attacked Varahadeva with magic, causing the sky to rain pus, hair, blood, stool, urine, and bones. Mountains discharged weapons, naked demonesses armed with tridents attacked along with loudly chanting Yaksas and Raksasas, but the Lord’s beloved cakra dispelled the demon’s conjured forces. “At that very moment, a shudder suddenly ran through the heart of Diti, the mother of Hiranyaksa. She recalled the words of her husband, Kasyapa, and blood flowed from her breasts.” (Bhag. [3.19.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/19.23))

Hiranyaksa saw his attacks fail and his weapons repelled. He then tried to crush Varahadeva in a powerful embrace. To his amazement, the Lord remained outside the circle of his arms, for no one devoid of devotion can capture the Lord. Finally, Varaha slapped Hiranyaksa indifferently at the root of his ear. The demon’s arms and legs broke and his hair scattered. Hiranyaksa fell dead like a gigantic tree uprooted by the wind.

Glancing at the dead demon, Brahma wondered aloud, “Oh, who could meet such blessed death?” (Bhag. [3.19.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/19.27)) Diti’s son, he thought, having cast off his mortal body, would soon return to his position as doorkeeper in the spiritual sky.

The demigods were joyous, and they offered their obeisances to Lord Varahadeva, who, although in the shape of a boar, possesses a transcendental form of pure goodness and is the enjoyer of Vedic sacrifices. The demigods thanked the Lord for removing their anxiety by killing this formidable demon. After hearing their praise, Lord Hari, the origin of the boar species, returned to His own abode.

Thus Maitreya Muni described to Vidura the extraordinary way in which Lord Varaha saved the earth and killed Hiranyaksa. While narrating this account to the sages at Naimisaranya, Suta Gosvami also described the ecstasy Vidura felt while hearing about the Supreme Lord’s transcendental pastimes: “People may take transcendental pleasure even in hearing of the works and deeds of the devotees, whose fame is immortal. . . . What grateful soul is there who would not render his loving service to such a great master as the Personality of Godhead? The Lord can be easily pleased by spotless devotees who resort exclusively to Him for protection, though the unrighteous man finds it difficult to propitiate Him.” (Bhag. [3.19.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/19.34), [36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/19.36))

Suta Gosvami ends this chapter by offering a phala-sruti, a benediction to its hearers: “O brahmanas, anyone who hears, chants, or takes pleasure in the wonderful narration of the killing of the Hiranyaksa demon by the Lord, who appeared as the first boar in order to deliver the world, is at once relieved of the results of sinful activities, even the killing of a brahmana. This most sacred narrative confers extraordinary merit, wealth, fame, longevity, and all the objects of one’s desire. On the field of battle it promotes the strength of one’s vital organs and organs of action. One who listens to it at the last moment of his life is transferred to the supreme abode of the Lord, О dear Saunaka.” (Bhag. [3.19.37-38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/19.37))

In his commentary on this section, Srila Jiva Gosvami explains that Lord Visnu was not actually angry with Jaya and Vijaya when they were playing the parts of demons. He then cites Bhagavatam [3.18.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/18.9), which describes Varahadeva as having “expressed His terrible anger,” which seems to contradict his previous statement. To support his point, however, he offers Srila Sridhara Svami’s commentary on this text: “The Lord’s terrible anger is here only an external show, a show intended to relieve the fears of the demigods, who were frightened by the demon’s insults. The Lord did not really become angry by hearing those insults.”

Sri Jiva also cites Sridhara Svami’s commentary on Bhagavatam [3.19.8-9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/19.8) (“The enjoyer of all sacrificial offerings playfully knocked down the mace with His left foot, even as it came upon Him with the force of a tempest”) to illustrate that the Lord was not actually angry.

Srila Prabhupada’s concluding purport to this chapter (written for text 38) prescribes “sparing some time” to attentively hear the Lord’s pastimes:

**Devotees are generally attracted by the narratives of the pastimes of the Lord, and even though they do not prosecute austerities or meditation, this very process of hearing attentively about the pastimes of the Lord will endow them with innumerable benefits, such as wealth, fame, longevity and other desirable aims of life. If one continues to hear Srimad-Bhagavatam, which is full of narratives of the pastimes of the Lord, at the end of this life, one is sure to be transferred to the eternal, transcendental abode of the Lord. Thus hearers are benefited both ultimately and for as long as they are in the material world. That is the supreme, sublime result of engaging in devotional service. The beginning of devotional service is to spare some time and listen to Srimad-Bhagavatam from the right source. Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu also recommended five items of devotional service, namely to serve the devotees of the Lord, to chant Hare Krsna, to hear Srimad-Bhagavatam, to worship the Deity of the Lord and to live in a place of pilgrimage. Just performing these five activities can deliver one from the miserable condition of material life.**

## Dialogue Five - The Marriage and Renunciation of Kardama Muni

## Chapter 20 - Conversation Between Maitreya and Vidura

## Texts 1-6: Further Questions from Vidura

Saunaka Rsi’s desire to hear krsna-katha increases after he hears about Varahadeva killing Hiranyaksa, so he eagerly asks Suta Gosvami to narrate how Svayambhuva Manu revealed “the path of liberation to persons who were to take birth later on.” (Bhag. [3.20.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/20.1)) He also wants to know whether Vidura asked Maitreya any other questions.

## Texts 7-53: The Creation Continues

Suta’s reply restates one of Vidura’s questions: “How did the Prajapatis \[such progenitors of living entities as Marici and Svayambhuva Manu\] create according to the instruction of Brahma, and how did they evolve this manifested universe?” (Bhag. [3.20.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/20.10)) Suta then repeats Maitreya’s response by again describing creation, beginning with Maha-Visnu, the origin, who glanced at the material energy and impregnated it.

If one were to look at an object in this world—say, a skyscraper— one may wonder how it could have been constructed. One would also want to know who built it. One would discover that no one person built the skyscraper; rather, its construction was the work of many people, including financiers, architects, engineers, suppliers, bricklayers, carpenters, and other laborers. One can consider such persons the building’s co-creators. But without access to the building’s ingredients—steel, cement, glass, wood, etc.—what could they have created? Therefore one would be forced to conclude that the person who had created the ingredients, the primary creator, was more important than those who had simply assembled them. Without Krsna, the ultimate creator and supplier of all ingredients, no secondary creation could exist. Krsna is the cause of all causes and the only independent entity. Everything rests on Him. When Krsna is in the mood of creation, He is known as Maha-Visnu.

Maitreya then describes that after Maha-Visnu glances at the material energy He causes its step-by-step evolution by injecting it with His time potency. Maha-Visnu then expands into Garbhodakasayi Visnu and enters each universe. From the lotus sprouting from Garbhodakasayi Visnu’s navel, Brahma takes birth and continues the process of creating the universe “as it was before.”

Brahma creates darkness first. From his own shadow he manifests five kinds of ignorance to cover, engage, and bewilder the conditioned souls. These may be understood as follows: The soul’s illusory attempt to compete with the Lord is known as tamisra (“darkness”). Such a mood dictates that he must forget his eternal relationship with Krsna, otherwise it would be impossible to compete with the Lord. Trapped by that ignorance, he then acquires a material body and identifies himself with it. This is called andha-tamisra (“complete blindness that leaves the soul in darkness”), a form of ignorance based on tamas, ignorance of his true identity. Bodily identification leads to physical and mental attachments, and therefore moha, illusion, increases, which in turn causes him both to make materialistic endeavor and to view others either as friends or enemies. This only increases his desire to enjoy matter, and he gradually becomes mad after such enjoyment. To maintain the spirit that life is meant for his own pleasure, he requires all the forgetfulness that ignorance can supply, including forgetfulness of impending physical death, forgetfulness of his previous failed attempts to enjoy and the frustration he felt in their wake, and forgetfulness of all the failed attempts of the countless souls before him. He must especially forget his own insignificance. This form of ignorance is called maha-moha (“great illusion”). These five forms of ignorance are necessary prerequisites for material life. No soul can approach the idea of enjoying independently from Krsna without them.

The description Maitreya Muni offers in this chapter of the Bhag-avatam is quite similar to previous descriptions offered in chapters Five, Six, and Eight of the Third Canto. In this Chapter Twenty description, however, Maitreya describes how Brahma created demons, who subsequently approached him with lust. In fear of these demons, Brahma sought shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In his purport to text 28, Srila Prabhupada directs all those in distress to seek the Lord’s shelter: “If anyone can completely perceive another’s distress without doubt, it is the Lord Himself. If someone is in distress and wants to get relief from his friend, sometimes it so happens that his friend does not appreciate the volume of distress he is suffering. But for the Supreme Lord it is not difficult. The Supreme Lord, as Paramatma, is sitting within the heart of every living entity, and He directly perceives the exact causes of distress. In Bhagavad-gita the Lord says, sarvasya caham hrdi sannivistah: ‘I am sitting in everyone’s heart, and because of Me one’s remembrance and forgetfulness occur.’ Thus whenever one fully surrenders unto the Supreme Lord, one finds that He is sitting within one’s heart. He can give us direction how to get out of dangers or how to approach Him in devotional service.”

Upon receiving the Lord’s order, Brahma cast off his body, which took the form of evening twilight, the juncture between day and night and the time that kindles passion. The demonic, who are controlled by passion, mistook the twilight to be a beautiful woman and approached her with flattering words, their minds overwhelmed by lust. In his purport to text 31 Srila Prabhupada advises how to avoid passionate attraction: “The real beauty is Krsna and Radha. One who is attracted by the beauty of Radha and Krsna cannot be attracted by the false beauty of this material world. That is the difference between a demon and a godly person or devotee.”

Thus by the Lord’s grace, Brahma escaped his fearful situation and, “with a laugh full of deep significance,” continued the creation. Brahma created Gandharvas and Apsaras from his loveliness, ghosts and fiends from his sloth, Sadhyas and Pitas from his navel, and Siddhas and Vidyadharas from his ability to remain invisible. He created Kimpurusas and Kinnaras from his reflection and ferocious serpents and Nagas from one of his hairs. Finally, he became satisfied by his own work and evolved from his mind the humanlike forms of Manu and his wife, Satarupa, who were similar to his own form. Lord Brahma next caused the appearance of beloved sons, great sages who each became an exemplar of a particular spiritual discipline.

## Chapter 21 - Conversation Between Manu and Kardama

## Texts 1-6: Vidura Inquires about the Lineage Descending from Svayambhuva Manu

Vidura is aware that the powerful incarnation Kapiladeva had appeared in Svayambhuva Manu’s line as the son of Kardama Muni (one of Brahma’s direct sons) and Devahuti (one of Svayambhuva Manu’s three daughters). Wishing to hear about Kapila Muni, Vidura requests Maitreya to describe Svayambhuva Manu’s descendants in more detail, specifically those bom during the marriage of Kardama Muni and Manu’s dear daughter Devahuti.

## Texts 7-12: Kardama Muni’s Devotional Austerities Evoke the Lord’s Appearance

Maitreya speaks first of how Kardama Muni prepared himself to fulfill his father’s order to produce children and increase the universal population. Since Kardama was a sage, he decided to purify his consciousness before entering household life. He engaged in austere yoga practices to train himself to reject material pleasure; he knew the quality of his consciousness would attract souls of similar consciousness to become his children. The parents’ consciousness at the time of conception attracts a specific soul with a corresponding consciousness to take birth in their family. Sages desired offspring with holy tendencies, so they were extremely careful about the mentality with which they conceived their children.

Kardama practiced his austerities near what would later become Bindu-sarovara, an area circled by the Sarasvati River. There, he spent ten thousand years in devotional trance, his mind and heart focused on his worshipful Lord Hari. Attracted by Kardama’s pure devotion, the Lord, clad in effulgent yellow silk, beautifully garlanded with white lotuses, His pinkish lotus feet on Garuda’s shoulders, revealed His eternal form to the sage. Kardama fell to the ground in respectful obeisance, then arose, fully satisfied, and with folded hands, offered prayers.

## Texts 13-21: Kardama Muni Offers the Lord Prayers

Kardama first glorified the shelter of the Lord’s splendid lotus feet: “O supreme worshipful Lord, my power of sight is now fulfilled, having attained the greatest perfection of the sight of You, who are the reservoir of all existences. Through many successive births of deep meditation, advanced yogis aspire to see Your transcendental form.” (Bhag. [3.21.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.13))

Srila Prabhupada describes the perfection of eyesight: “Kardama Muni admits that seeing the Lord personally in bhaktLyoga is the perfection of sight. The exalted perfection of seeing the Lord is not exaggerated by Kardama Muni. He gives evidence that those who are actually elevated in yoga aspire in life after life to see this form of the Personality of Godhead. He was not a fictitious yogi. Those who are actually on the advanced path aspire only to see the eternal form of the Lord.” (Bhag. [3.21.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.13), purport)

Later, the gopis of Vrndavana describe the highest perfection of eyesight (Bhag. [10.21.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/21.7)): “O friends, those eyes that see the beautiful faces of the sons of Maharaja Nanda are certainly fortunate. As these two sons enter the forest, surrounded by Their friends, driving the cows before Them, They hold Their flutes to Their mouths and glance lovingly upon the residents of Vrndavana. For those who have eyes, we think there is no greater object of vision.”

Kardama Muni humbly continues his prayers: “Your lotus feet are the true vessel to take one across the ocean of mundane nescience. Only persons deprived of their intelligence by the spell of the deluding energy will worship those feet with a view to attain the trivial and momentary pleasures of the senses, which even persons rotting in hell can attain. However, О my Lord, You are so kind that You bestow mercy even upon them. Therefore, desiring to marry a girl of like disposition who may prove to be a veritable cow of plenty in my married life, to satisfy my lustful desire I too have sought the shelter of Your lotus feet, which are the source of everything, for You are like a desire tree.” (Bhag. [3.21.14-15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.14))

Kardama Muni was in an awkward position, as Srila Prabhupada describes in his purport to text 15: “In spite of his condemning persons who approach the Lord for material advantages, Kardama Muni expressed his material inability and desire before the Lord by saying, ‘Although I know that nothing material should be asked from You, I nevertheless desire to marry a girl of like disposition.’”

In that same purport, Srila Prabhupada also explains that the “advantage of worshiping the Supreme Person is that even if one has desires for material enjoyment, if he worships Krsna he will gradually become a pure devotee and have no more material hankering.” Both Prabhupada’s words and Kardama Muni’s actions confirm Sukadeva Gosvami’s instruction in Bhagavatam [2.3.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/3.10): “A person who has broader intelligence, whether he be full of all material desire, without any material desire, or desiring liberation, must by all means worship the supreme whole, the Personality of Godhead.”

What activity on the devotional path raises us to purity? Kardama Muni continues: О Lord and master, leader of all living entities, О embodiment of religion, О eternal time, those who have “taken shelter of the umbrella of Your lotus feet by drinking the intoxicating nectar of Your qualities and activities in discussions with one another, can be freed from the primary necessities of the material body.” (Bhag. [3.21.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.17)) Taking shelter of Krsna’s lotus feet is the ultimate process of purification. Srila Prabhupada explains this process in his purport to text 17:

**Samsara, or the repetition of birth and death, is compared to a forest fire. A forest fire takes place automatically, without anyone’s endeavor, by the friction of dried wood, and no fire department or sympathetic person can extinguish it. The raging forest fire can be extinguished only when there is a constant downpour of water from a cloud. The cloud is compared to the mercy of the spiritual master. By the grace of the spiritual master the cloud of the mercy of the Personality of Godhead is brought in, and then only, when the rains of Krsna consciousness fall, can the fire of material existence be extinguished. This is also explained here. In order to find freedom from the stereotyped conditional life of material existence, one has to take shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord, not in the manner in which the impersonalists indulge, but in devotional service, chanting and hearing of the activities of the Lord. Only then can one be freed from the actions and reactions of material existence. . . . Only by drinking the nectar of chanting and hearing the pastimes of the Lord can one forget the intoxication of material existence.**

In this Canto, Maitreya has thrice described the process of creation. On one level, creation facilitates the conditioned souls’ attempts to fulfill their desires. Why, then, does sastra insist that everyone, whether they are happy or sad, healthy or ill, wealthy or impoverished, ultimately strive for freedom from material desire and long for purity? Why does sastra even insist that we become “freed from the primary necessities of the material body”?

Kardama Muni answers this question by describing time, the Lord’s rotating cakra, and how it foils one’s plans and devours one’s life. Time crushes to dust all attempts to enjoy matter in this world. Yet, Kardama explains, even time cannot affect a bhakta’s lifespan. “Just as a spider creates a cobweb by its own energy and again winds it up,” (Bhag. [3.21.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.19)) the Lord creates, maintains, and destroys the universes through His own energy. Although it is not His desire to see the living entities suffer in illusion, He manifests the universes containing both subtle and gross elements so that the living entities can fulfill their sensual desires in the material realm. The Lord is sentient; He has heard and answered His devotees’ prayer. “Let Your causeless mercy be upon us, for You have appeared before us in Your eternal form, adorned with a splendid wreath of tulasi leaves.” (Bhag. [3.21.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.20))

In the purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada further describes Krsna’s actual desire for those living in the material world: “Elsewhere in the Srimad-Bhagavatam it is stated that for those who have taken shelter of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, this material world is useless; because this material world is full of danger at every step, it is not meant for the devotees but for living entities who want to lord it over the material energy at their own risk. Krsna is so kind that He allows the sense-enjoying living entities a separate world created by Him to enjoy as they like, yet at the same time He appears in His personal form. The Lord unwillingly creates this material world, but He descends in His personal form or sends one of His reliable sons or a servant or a reliable author like Vyasadeva to give instruction. He Himself also instructs in His speeches of Bhagavad-gita. This propaganda work goes on side by side with the creation to convince the misguided living entities who are rotting in this material world to come back to Him and surrender unto Him. Therefore the last instruction of Bhagavad-gita is this: ‘Give up all your manufactured engagements in the material world and just surrender unto Me. I shall protect you from all sinful reactions.’”

Kardama Muni concludes: “I continuously offer my respectful obeisances unto Your lotus feet, of which it is worthy to take shelter, because You shower all benedictions on the insignificant. To give all living entities detachment from fruitive activity by realizing You, You have expanded these material worlds by Your own energy.” (Bhag. [3.21.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.21)) Srila Prabhupada advises us to take advantage of He who “showers all benedictions on the insignificant”: “Everyone, therefore, whether he desires material enjoyment, liberation or the transcendental loving service of the Lord, should engage himself, offering obeisances unto the Supreme Lord, because the Lord can award everyone his desired benediction. In Bhagavad-gita the Lord affirms, ye yatha mam prapadyante: anyone who desires to be a successful enjoyer in this material world is awarded that benediction by the Lord ...” (Bhag. [3.21.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.21), purport)

But what of those who, despite their Krsna conscious desires, also possess material desires? Srila Prabhupada continues: “The conclusion is that one should worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead for any benediction. The word kdma'Varsam is very significant, for it indicates that He satisfies the desires of anyone who approaches Him. But one who sincerely loves Krsna and yet wants material enjoyment is in perplexity. Krsna, being very kind toward him, gives him an opportunity to engage in the transcendental loving service of the Lord, and so he gradually forgets the hallucination.”

## Texts 22-33: The Lord Responds to Kardama Muni

Lord Visnu, the beautifully effulgent Lord, replied affectionately to the muni with words as sweet as nectar: “Having come to know what was in your mind, I have already arranged for that for which you have worshiped Me well through your mental and sensory discipline. My dear rsi, О leader of the living entities, for those who serve Me in devotion by worshiping Me, especially persons like you who have given up everything unto Me, there is never any question of frustration.” (Bhag. [3.21.23-24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.23)) Krsna already knew Kardama Muni’s desire and had arranged to satisfy it! Srila Prabhupada explains that Krsna “never disappoints a sincere devotee, regardless of what he wants, but He never allows anything which will be detrimental to the individual’s devotional service.” (Bhag. [3.21.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.23), purport) We become more deeply entangled in Krsna’s illusory energy when we attempt to fulfill our desires independently. On the other hand, Krsna fulfills His devotees’ desires in such a way that they advance in spiritual life.

As the above indicates, it is not necessary to worship the omniscient, omnipotent Lord to invoke His cooperation in fulfilling our needs. Such worship is encouraged, yet not very exalted. Why? Because earnest devotional service, even if materially motivated, eventually leads one to complete purity.

It is important to note here, as Srila Jiva Gosvami mentions in Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 225, that Kardama’s devotional service was not grossly materially motivated. Rather, as a moral obligation, he dutifully desired to obey Lord Brahma’s order to create progeny. Thus the Lord was pleased by Kardama’s offering of his prescribed duty to Him. This is indicated by the Lord’s shedding a tear of delight on seeing the sage. (That tear became Bindu-sarovara.)

The Lord continued: “The day after tomorrow, О brahmana, that celebrated emperor, who is expert in religious activities, will come here with his queen, Satarupa, wishing to see you. He has a grownup daughter whose eyes are Hack. She is ready for marriage, and she has good character and all good qualities. She is also searching for a good husband. My dear sir, her parents will come to see you, who are exactly suitable for her, just to deliver their daughter as your wife.” (Bhag. [3.21.26-27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.26)) The Lord goes on to assure Kardama that Devahuti is “just the type you have been thinking of in your heart for all these long years.” (Bhag. [3.21.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.28))Many of Srila Prabhupada’s purports in this and succeeding chapters discuss essential points relating to marriage and household life, such as arranged marriages (Bhag. [3.21.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.27)), the necessity of God’s grace for attaining a good marriage partner (Bhag. [3.21.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.28)), the difference between grhamedhi and grhastha life (Bhag. [3.22.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.11)), the deciding factors in choosing a wife (Bhag. [3.22.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.15)), the duty of both householders and sannyasis to be compassionate (Bhag. [3.21.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.31)), the importance of begetting children for Lord Visnu’s service (Bhag. [3.22.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.19)), and the importance of matching the boy’s and girl’s natures before marriage (Bhag. [3.24.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/24.15)). Following are some excerpts from these important purports:

**The selection of a good husband for a good girl was always entrusted to the parents. Here it is clearly stated that Manu and his wife were coming to see Kardama Muni to offer their daughter because the daughter was well qualified and the parents were searching out a similarly qualified man. This is the duty of parents. Girls are never thrown into the public street to search out their husband, for when girls are grown up and are searching after a boy, they forget to consider whether the boy they select is actually suitable for them. Out of the urge of sex desire, a girl may accept anyone, but if the husband is chosen by the parents, they can consider who is to be selected and who is not. According to the Vedic system, therefore, the girl is given over to a suitable boy by the parents; she is never allowed to select her own husband independently. (Bhag.** [**3.21.27**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.27)**, purport)**

**Only by God’s grace can one get a nice wife just as he desires. Similarly, it is only by God’s grace that a girl gets a husband suitable to her heart. Thus it is said that if we pray to the Supreme Lord in every transaction of our material existence, everything will be done very nicely and just suitable to our heart’s desire. In other words, in all circumstances we must take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and depend completely on His decision. Man proposes, God disposes. The fulfillment of desires, therefore, should be entrusted to the Supreme Personality of Godhead; that is the nicest solution. Kardama Muni desired only a wife, but because he was a devotee of the Lord, the Lord selected a wife for him who was the Emperor’s daughter, a princess. Thus Kardama Muni got a wife beyond his expectation. If we depend on the choice of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, we will receive benedictions in greater opulence than we desire. (Bhag.** [**3.21.28**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.28)**, purport)**

**A wife should not only be equal to her husband in age, character and qualities, but must be helpful to him in his household duties. The household duty of a man is not to satisfy his sense gratification, but to remain with a wife and children and at the same time attain advancement in spiritual life. One who does not do so is not a householder but a grhamedhi. Two words are used in Sanskrit literature; one is grhastha, and the other is grhamedhi. The difference between grhamedhi and grhastha is that grhastha is also an asrama, or spiritual order, but if one simply satisfies his senses as a householder, then he is a grhamedhi. For a grhamedhi, to accept a wife means to satisfy the senses, but for a grhastha a qualified wife is an assistant in every respect for advancement in spiritual activities. It is the duty of the wife to take charge of household affairs and not to compete with the husband. A wife is meant to help, but she cannot help her husband unless he is completely equal to her in age, character and quality. (Bhag.** [**3.22.11**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.11)**, purport)**

**There were many considerations by Kardama Muni before accepting the daughter of Svayambhuva Manu. Most important is that Devahuti had first of all fixed her mind on marrying him. She did not choose to have any other man as her husband. That is a great consideration because female psychology dictates that when a woman offers her heart to a man for the first time, it is very difficult for her to take it back. Also, she had not married before; she was a virgin girl. All these considerations convinced Kardama Muni to accept her. (Bhag.** [**3.22.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.15)**, purport)**

**It is indicated here that Kardama Muni was directed by the Lord to be very compassionate and liberal in his householder life and to give assurance to the people in his renounced life. ... A person who is a householder but is initiated by a sannyasi has the duty to spread Krsna consciousness at home; as far as possible, he should call his friends and neighbors to his house and hold classes in Krsna consciousness. Holding a class means chanting the holy name of Krsna and speaking from Bhagavad-gita or Srimad-Bhagavatam. There are immense literatures for spreading Krsna consciousness, and it is the duty of each and every householder to learn about Krsna from his sannyasi spiritual master. (Bhag.** [**3.21.31**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.31)**, purport)**

**There are two kinds of children bom of good fathers: one is educated in Krsna consciousness so that he can be delivered from the clutches of maya in that very life, and the other is a ray of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and teaches the world the ultimate goal of life. . . . Great householders pray to God to send His representative so that there may be an auspicious movement in human society. This is one reason to beget a child. Another reason is that a highly enlightened parent can train a child in Krsna consciousness so that the child will not have to come back again to this miserable world. Parents should see to it that the child bom of them does not enter the womb of a mother again. Unless one can train a child for liberation in that life, there is no need to marry or produce children. If human society produces children like cats and dogs for the disturbance of social order, then the world becomes hellish, as it has in this age of Kali. ... In the same order as Kardama Muni, about one hundred years ago, Thakura Bhaktivinoda also wanted to beget a child who could preach the philosophy and teachings of Lord Caitanya to the fullest extent. By his prayers to the Lord he had as his child Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Gosvami Maharaja, who at the present moment is preaching the philosophy of Lord Caitanya throughout the entire world through his bona fide disciples. (Bhag.** [**3.22.19**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.19)**, purport)**

**Man and woman should not be united simply on the consideration of sex life. There are many other considerations, especially character and taste. If the taste and character differ between the man and woman, their combination will be unhappy. Even about forty years ago, in Indian marriages, the taste and character of the boy and girl were first of all matched, and then they were allowed to marry. This was done under the direction of the respective parents. The parents used to astrologically determine the character and tastes of the boy and girl, and when they corresponded, the match was selected: “This girl and this boy are just suitable, and they should be married.” Other considerations were less important. The same system was also advised in the beginning of the creation by Brahma: “Your daughters should be handed over to the rsis according to taste and character.” ... At the present moment, because boys and girls are not married according to quality and character, most marriages are unhappy, and there is divorce. (Bhag.** [**3.24.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/24.15)**, purport)**

Srimad-Bhagavatam is called the paramahamsa'samhita, and much of the Bhagavatam is written on a level spiritually higher than discussions about marriage and household duties. When the Bhagavatam does speak about and encourage these topics, it does so to support the soul’s spiritual journey so that a practitioner’s mind will be peaceful enough to allow him to make steady progress. Thus the Bhagavatam’s purpose in presenting these topics—and Srila Prabhupada shared this purpose as he wrote his purports—is to instruct those of us who are interested in or in need of material satisfaction that parallels our spiritual advancement. “As far as possible, a devotee is very cautious so that he does not do anything that could disrupt his wholesome condition,” Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to Bhagavad-gita [9.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.30).

Yet on another level, the Bhagavatam criticizes those who focus on marriage and household life because they are physical conditions ultimately doomed to destruction. A devotee’s true interest is to attain the ultimate necessity—the soul’s necessity. In Bhagavad-gita ([9.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.27)) Krsna Himself describes how to obtain the body’s necessities and still benefit the soul: “Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer or give away, and whatever austerities you perform—do that, О son of Kunti, as an offering to Me.” The Sanskrit word for necessity is prayojana. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu stated, prema pumartho mahan: the soul’s true necessity is love of Krsna. Although one should act practically and renounce according to one’s true capacity, one’s life should nevertheless unfailingly move toward this ultimate, spiritual goal.

The Lord next revealed to Kardama that he and Devahuti would give birth to nine daughters who would marry the nine great sages bom directly from Brahma’s body. “With your heart cleansed by properly carrying out My command, resigning to Me the fruits of all your acts, you will finally attain to Me. Showing compassion to all living entities, you will attain self-realization. Giving assurance of safety to all, you will perceive your own self as well as all the universes in Me, and Myself in you.” (Bhag. [3.21.30-31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.30)) In his purport to text 31 Srila Prabhupada points out what it means practically to realize everything in Krsna and Krsna in everything: “The real position, as explained by the Lord Himself, is that although nothing can exist without Him, it is not a fact that everything is Him. He is different from everything. So here also the Lord says: ‘You will see everything in the world to be nondifferent from Me.’ This means that everything should be considered a product of the Lord’s energy, and therefore everything should be employed in the service of the Lord. One’s energy should be utilized for one’s self-interest. That is the perfection of the energy.”
