The Lord concludes His instructions to Kardama with another prediction: “O great sage, I shall manifest My own plenary portion through your wife, Devahuti, along with your nine daughters, and I shall instruct her in the system of philosophy that deals with the ultimate principles or categories.” (Bhag. [3.21.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.32)) Having reciprocated with Kardama Muni’s devotion, austerities, and prayers, the Lord then departed.

## Texts 34-57: The Lord Fulfills His Words and Kardama Greets King Svayambhuva Manu

Kardama Muni waited at Bindu-sarovara. Several days after his darsana of the Lord, Emperor Svayambhuva Manu arrived. Manu bowed before the sage, who greeted him with honor and sweet words. Kardama, whose hair was matted and whose body was effulgent because of the Lord’s affectionate glance, offered his respects to Svayambhuva Manu and glorified him as the “protecting energy of Sri Hari.” Kardama thus demonstrated the natural, respectful relationship between Vedic brahmanas and ksatriyas. Rather than rivaling one another, cultured sages and rulers appreciated, respected, and acknowledged that they—as well as the entire society—required one another’s specialized services.

The appreciative words exchanged between the two great souls describes the duties of both qualified kings and sages. Srila Prabhupada’s purport to Bhagavatam [3.22.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.4) summarizes the purpose of this symbiosis: “The entire social structure of varna and asrama is a cooperative system meant to uplift all to the highest platform of spiritual realization. The brahmanas are intended to be protected by the ksatriyas, and the ksatriyas also are intended to be enlightened by the brahmanas. When the brahmanas and ksatriyas cooperate nicely, the other subordinate divisions, the vaisyas, or mercantile people, and the sudras, or laborer class, automatically flourish.”

Kardama Muni concludes his tribute by requesting the king to reveal the reason he had come to visit, adding respectfully, “I shall carry out your request without reservation.”

## Chapter 22 - The Marriage of Kardama Muni and Devahuti

## Texts 1-14: Manu Offers his Daughter in Marriage to the Sage

The emperor is humbled by Kardama’s praise and responds by glorifying the brahmanas and expressing his fortune at having attained Kardama’s association. In his purport to text 5, Prabhupada describes from his own experience the powerful result of meeting a sage, in particular his saintly Guru Maharaja, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura:

**Lord Caitanya says that one should always try to associate with saintly persons because if one establishes a proper association with a saintly person, even for a moment, one attains all perfection. Somehow or other, if one meets a saintly person and achieves his favor, then the entire mission of one’s human life is fulfilled. In our personal experience we have actual proof of this statement of Manu. Once we had the opportunity to meet Visnupada Sri Srimad Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Gosvami Maharaja, and on first sight he requested this humble self to preach his message in the Western countries. There was no preparation for this, but somehow or other he desired it, and by his grace we are now engaged in executing his order, which has given us a transcendental occupation and has saved and liberated us from the occupation of material activities. Thus it is actually a fact that if one meets a saintly person completely engaged in transcendental duties and achieves his favor, then one’s life mission becomes complete. What is not possible to achieve in thousands of lives can be achieved in one moment if there is an opportunity to meet a saintly person. It is therefore enjoined in Vedic literature that one should always try to associate with saintly persons and try to disassociate oneself from the common man, because by one word of a saintly person one can be liberated from material entanglement. A saintly person has the power, because of his spiritual advancement, to give immediate liberation to the conditioned soul.**

In his next purport Prabhupada states: “If one takes shelter of the lotus feet of a great soul, there is every possibility of one’s also becoming a great soul.” Further, in his purport to text 7, he describes how a spiritual master’s instructions lead us in a practical way to perfection:

**The real fact is that a bona fide spiritual master knows the nature of a particular man and what sort of duties he can perform in Krsna consciousness, and he instructs him in that way. He instructs him through the ear, not privately, but publicly. “You are fit for such and such work in Krsna consciousness. You can act in this way.” One person is advised to act in Krsna consciousness by working in the Deities’ room, another is advised to act in Krsna consciousness by performing editorial work, another is advised to do preaching work, and another is advised to carry out Krsna consciousness in the cooking department. There are different departments of activity in Krsna consciousness, and a spiritual master, knowing the particular ability of a particular man, trains him in such a way that by his tendency to act he becomes perfect. . . . One has to receive the message of the spiritual master regarding how to act in one’s capacity, for the spiritual master is expert in giving such instructions.**

This combination, the instruction of the spiritual master and the faithful execution of the instruction by the disciple, makes the entire process perfect. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura describes in his explanation of the verse in Bhagavad-gita, vyavasa-yatmika buddhih, that one who wants to be certain to achieve spiritual success must take the instruction from the spiritual master as to what his particular function is. He should faithfully try to execute that particular instruction and should consider that his life and soul. The faithful execution of the instruction, which he receives from the spiritual master is the only duty of a disciple, and that will bring him perfection. One should be very careful to receive the message from the spiritual master through the ears and execute it faithfully. That will make one’s life successful.

Svayambhuva Manu’s sweet words praising Kardama Muni are followed by a gentle request: О great sage, graciously listen to my humble prayer, for my mind is troubled by affection for my daughter.

Devahuti had heard of Kardama from Narada Muni and had fixed her mind on marrying him. “O wise man, I heard that you were prepared to marry. Please accept her hand, which is being offered to you by me, since you have not taken a vow of perpetual celibacy.” (Bhag. [3.22.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.14))

## Texts 15-21: The Sage’s Acceptance

Kardama Muni immediately agreed to accept Devahuti. “Certainly I have a desire to marry, and your daughter has not yet married or given her word to anyone. Therefore our marriage according to the Vedic system can take place. Let your daughter’s desire for marriage, which is recognized in the Vedic scriptures, be fulfilled. Who would not accept her hand? She is so beautiful that by her bodily luster alone she excels the beauty of her ornaments. . . . What wise man would not welcome her, the very ornament of womanhood, the beloved daughter of Svayambhuva Manu and sister of Uttanapada? Those who have not worshiped the gracious feet of the goddess of fortune cannot even perceive her, yet she has come of her own accord to seek my hand.” (Bhag. [3.22.15-16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.15), [18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.18))

Then Kardama added a condition: After Devahuti bears semen from my body, I will renounce household life and accept the life of a paramahamsa sannyasi to perform devotional service.

After saying this, Kardama fell silent, immersed in “thinking of his worshipable Lord, Visnu, who has a lotus on His navel” (Bhag. [3.22.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.21)) and by whom this entire exchange had been predicted. As he smiled to himself, Kardama’s handsome face captured Devahuti’s mind.

In Priti-sandarbha, anuccheda 190, Srila Jiva Gosvami notes that one should not think of the affection between Kardama and Devahuti as mundane.

## Texts 22-39: Manu Returns to his Kingdom

Anticipating separation from his daughter Devahuti, Svayambhuva Manu affectionately embraced her, tears of affection pouring from his eyes. Finally, he departed. Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 24 that a father’s responsibility is to find his daughter a suitable husband: “A father always remains in anxiety until he can hand over his grown-up daughter to a suitable boy. A father and mother’s responsibility for children continues until they marry them to suitable spouses; when the father is able to perform that duty, he is relieved of his responsibility.”

Upon returning to his opulent capital, Barhismati, Manu worshiped the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by whose grace he was ruling the world. The atmosphere in Barhismati was auspicious; because of the spiritual atmosphere the king maintained, no one experienced misery. King Manu himself lived in opulence in his city. Sitting on a kusu-grass mat, Manu worshiped the Lord with sacrifices. Previously, Brahma had guided Manu’s rule by instructing him to “beget children qualified like yourself in the womb of your wife. Rule the world in pursuance of the principles of devotional service unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and thus worship the Lord by performances of yajna.” (Bhag. [3.13.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.11)) Manu was also to “give proper protection to the living beings in the material world,” in the mood of that service being “the best service for me.” (Bhag. [3.13.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.12))

Svayambhuva Manu had followed Lord Brahma’s instructions and become successful. Despite his wealth and power he had remained an exalted devotee, living in a palace permeated by a Krsna conscious atmosphere that erased the threefold miseries of material existence.

Those who try to become Krsna conscious often wish to stop their suffering. We tell one another, “Chant Hare Krsna and your life will be sublime.” Most discover in time, however, that the path is neither smooth nor easy. Material desires surface and obstacles appear. Does one’s preordained karma hinder one’s attempt to perform devotional service? Can Krsna consciousness increase one’s happiness and remove one’s distress if one’s allotted karma is fixed? Srila Prabhupada deals with these questions: “It is not that the miseries of the material world completely vanish when one takes to Krsna consciousness, but for one who is Krsna conscious the miseries of material existence have no effect. We cannot stop the miseries of the material atmosphere, but Krsna consciousness is the antiseptic method to protect us from being affected by the miseries of material existence. For a Krsna conscious person, both living in heaven and living in hell are equal.” (Bhag. [3.22.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.32), purport)

One can then shift the question to something more practical: How can one become an actual devotee? Srila Prabhupada describes (in his purports to texts 33 and 34) Svayambhuva Manu’s mood and activities. The king lived in the world and enjoyed household life, but remained “a Krsna conscious person”:

**It is understood that Emperor Svayambhuva Manu enjoyed his household life by following these principles. It is stated here that early in the morning there were musicians who used to sing with musical instruments about the glories of the Lord, and the Emperor, with his family, personally used to hear about the pastimes of the Supreme Person. This custom is still prevalent in India in some of the royal families and temples. Professional musicians sing with sahndis, and the sleeping members of the house gradually get up from their beds in a pleasing atmosphere. During bedtime also the singers sing songs in relationship with the pastimes of the Lord, with sahnai accompaniment, and the householders gradually fall asleep remembering the glories of the Lord. In every house, in addition to the singing program, there is an arrangement for Bhagavatam lectures in the evening; family members sit down, hold Hare Krsna kirtana, hear narrations from Srimad-Bhagavatam and Bhagavad-gita and enjoy music before going to bed. The atmosphere created by this sankirtana movement lives in their hearts, and while sleeping they also dream of the singing and glorification of the Lord. In such a way, perfection of Krsna consciousness can be attained. (Bhag.** [**3.22.33**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.33)**, purport)**

From Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 34: “The kingly happiness of material enjoyment generally drags one to the lowest grade of life, namely degradation to animal life, because of unrestricted sense enjoyment. But Svayambhuva Manu was considered as good as a saintly sage because the atmosphere created in his kingdom and home was completely Krsna conscious. The case is similar with the conditioned souls in general; they have come into this material life for sense gratification, but if they are able to create a Krsna conscious atmosphere, as depicted here or as prescribed in revealed scriptures, by temple worship and household Deity worship, then in spite of their material enjoyment they can make advancement in pure Krsna consciousness without a doubt. At the present moment, modem civilization is too much attached to the material way of life, or sense gratification. Therefore, the Krsna consciousness movement can give the people in general the best opportunity to utilize their human life in the midst of material enjoyment. Krsna consciousness does not stop them in their propensity for material enjoyment, but simply regulates their habits in the life of sense enjoyment. In spite of their enjoying the material advantages, they can be liberated in this very life by practicing Krsna consciousness by the simple method of chanting the holy names of the Lord—Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare.”

After years of pleasing the Lord by following Lord Brahma’s instructions, Svayambhuva Manu became old. Maitreya Muni tells Vidura: “Consequently, although his duration of life gradually came to an end, his long life, consisting of a Manvantara era, was not spent in vain, since he ever engaged in hearing, contemplating, writing down and chanting the pastimes of the Lord.” (Bhag. [3.22.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.35))

Srila Prabhupada depicts the miseries of old age in his purport to this text: “As freshly prepared food is very tasteful but if kept for three or four hours becomes stale and tasteless, so the existence of material enjoyment can endure as long as life is fresh, but at the fag end of life everything becomes tasteless, and everything appears to be vain and painful. The life of Emperor Svayambhuva Manu, however, was not tasteless; as he grew older, his life remained as fresh as in the beginning because of his continued Krsna consciousness.”

During his extremely long life, Manu proved that Krsna consciousness can be executed perfectly by those who either by inclination or by order live and work in the greater society, “away from the monastery.”

By following Svayambhuva Manu’s example, anyone can fearlessly avoid the alluring yet virulent web created by materialistic life.

## Chapter 23 - Devahuti’s Lamentation

## Texts 1-11: Devahuti Serves Kardama Muni

After Svayambhuva Manu departed for his capital, Devahuti began the life of a married woman and cared for her husband with intimacy, respect, love, and sweet words. “Working sanely and diligently, she pleased her very powerful husband, giving up all lust, pride, envy, greed, sinful activities and vanity.” (Bhag. [3.23.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/23.3))Srila Prabhupada’s purports to texts 2-5 of this chapter instruct wives in their duty. Indirectly, he also instructs husbands to become deserving of such service, as Kardama Muni was deserving:

**Here two words are very significant. Devahuti served her husband in two ways, visrambhena and gauravena. These are two important processes in serving the husband or the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Visrambhena means “with intimacy,” and gauravena means “with great reverence.” The husband is a very intimate friend; therefore, the wife must render service just like an intimate friend, and at the same time she must understand that the husband is superior in position, and thus she must offer him all respect. A man’s psychology and woman’s psychology are different. As constituted by bodily frame, a man always wants to be superior to his wife, and a woman, as bodily constituted, is naturally inferior to her husband. Thus the natural instinct is that the husband wants to post himself as superior to the wife, and this must be observed. Even if there is some wrong on the part of the husband, the wife must tolerate it, and thus there will be no misunderstanding between husband and wife. (Bhag.** [**3.23.2**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/23.2)**, purport)**

**Here are some of the qualities of a great husband’s great wife. Kardama Muni is great by spiritual qualification. Such a husband is called tejiyamsam, most powerful. Although a wife may be equal to her husband in advancement in spiritual consciousness, she should not be vainly proud. Sometimes it happens that the wife comes from a very rich family, as did Devahuti, the daughter of Emperor Svayambhuva Manu. She could have been very proud of her parentage, but that is forbidden. The wife should not be proud of her parental position. She must always be submissive to the husband and must give up all vanity. As soon as the wife becomes proud of her parentage, her pride creates great misunderstanding between the husband and wife, and their nuptial life is ruined. Devahuti was very careful about that, and therefore it is said here that she gave up pride completely. Devahuti was not unfaithful. The most sinful activity for a wife is to accept another husband or another lover.... A chaste and faithful woman must not practice adultery—that is a greatly sinful act. (Bhag.** [**3.23.3**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/23.3)**, purport)**

**The wife is expected to be of the same category as the husband. She must be prepared to follow the principles of the husband, and then there will be happy life. If the husband is a devotee and the wife is materialistic, there cannot be any peace in the home. The wife must see the tendencies of the husband and must be prepared to follow him. From Mahabharata we learn that when Gandhari understood that her would-be husband, Dhrtarastra, was blind, she immediately began to practice blindness herself. Thus she covered her eyes and played the part of a blind woman. She decided that since her husband was blind, she must also act like a blind woman, otherwise she would be proud of her eyes, and her husband would be seen as inferior. (Bhag.** [**3.23.4-5**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/23.4)**, purport)**

Devahuti willingly accepted the difficulties inherent in serving a renounced sage. In time she grew physically thin and weak, and soon Kardama was overcome with compassion and love for her and said, “Since the body is so dear to embodied beings, I am astonished that you have neglected your own body to use it on my behalf.” (Bhag. [3.23.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/23.6)) Kardama then blessed Devahuti by offering her the pious results of his own religiosity, austerity, meditation, and Krsna consciousness. Thus by the grace of her great husband, Devahuti received the Lord’s blessings. Prabhupada describes the potency of blessings in his purport to text 7: “By the grace of Kardama Muni, Devahuti experienced actual realization simply by serving. . . . For spiritual achievement the easiest path is to take shelter of a bona fide spiritual master and to serve him with heart and soul. That is the secret of success. As stated by Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura in his eight stanzas of prayer to the spiritual master, yasya prasadad bhagavat-prasadah: by serving or receiving the grace of the spiritual master, one receives the grace of the Supreme Lord. By serving her devotee husband, Kardama Muni, Devahuti shared in his achievements. Similarly, a sincere disciple, simply by serving a bona fide spiritual master, can achieve all the mercy of the Lord and the spiritual master simultaneously.”

Hearing Kardama’s kind words, Devahuti smiled shyly and reminded him of his promise to give her a child. As she spoke, her voice became choked and her heart filled with modesty and love. Considering her emaciated body and her meager dwelling, the sage’s humble cottage, which was enriched by the mode of goodness, she first begged Kardama to use his mystic power to remake her body and provide her with a suitable home—one in which his passion would be sufficiently aroused to produce a son.

It is interesting to contrast Diti’s union with Kasyapa with Deva-huti’s union with Kardama. Both women served their husbands, but Diti was impurely motivated by her desire that her husband immediately impregnate her. Because of her inappropriate attitude, she did not even consider the inauspiciousness of the time. As a result of Diti’s union with her husband, two demons were bom. On the other hand, Devahuti served Kardama with a simple heart. When he expressed his pleasure with her, she requested a child. The child that would take birth from this auspicious union of a humble, chaste wife and a powerful devotee husband would be an incarnation of Godhead, Lord Kapila.

## Texts 12-48: Kardama Creates an Aerial Mansion

On hearing his wife’s request, Kardama Muni used his mystic power to create a gold-and-jewel-bedecked seven-story aerial mansion. The mansion was adorned with pillars of precious stones and equipped with comfortable furniture. Flags, festoons, fine linen tapestries, silks, and other fabrics hung from the walls and pillars. The diamond-studded walls were set with the choicest rubies. Here and there, ponds and gardens were established and stocked with both real and artificial swans.

Kardama’s prowess thrilled Devahuti, but she was too shy to enter the mansion because her dress and body were dirty and her hair matted. Seeing her hesitation and understanding her heart, Kardama Muni pointed her toward Bindu-sarovara, which was also filled with the sacred waters of the Sarasvati River.

Devahuti entered the lake and saw in the waters the thousand youthful maidservants Kardama Muni had created to rejuvenate and restore her to her former beauty. The maidservants bathed Devahuti’s body and then decorated her with excellent clothes, necklaces, bangles, and anklets of gold. Her adornment complete, Devahuti thought of her great husband, who was extremely dear to her, and at once appeared before him. The sage looked at his beautiful wife, her countenance shining, her teeth beautiful, her eyes moistened at their comers, and her face surrounded by dark curling tresses, and his fondness for her increased. He took her into the aerial mansion, and together they toured for many years the pleasure valleys of the universe, which were decorated with cool, gentle, fragrant breezes.

One may wonder how the sage created such a mansion. Text 42 answers this question with a rhetorical question: “What is difficult to achieve for determined men who have taken refuge of the Supreme Personality of Godhead’s lotus feet? His feet are the source of sacred rivers like the Ganges, which put an end to the dangers of mundane life.” Prabhupada underscores this point in his purport to this text: “Kardama Muni is special not because he was a great mystic, but because he was a great devotee. Therefore it is said here that for a great devotee like Kardama Muni, nothing is impossible.”

Kardama Muni then returned with Devahuti to his hermitage and divided himself into nine persons, impregnating Devahuti with nine discharges of semen.

## Texts 49-57: Kardama Muni Prepares to Leave Home

On the same day she became pregnant, Devahuti gave birth to nine charming daughters, each fragrant with the scent of red lotus flowers. Suddenly Devahuti noticed that her husband was preparing to leave home, just as he had promised Svayambhuva Manu he would (Bhag. [3.22.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/22.19)).

“When she saw her husband about to leave home, she smiled externally, hut at heart she was agitated and distressed. She stood and scratched the ground with her foot, which was radiant with the luster of her gemlike nails. Her head bent down, she spoke in slow yet charming accents, suppressing her tears. Sri Devahuti said: ‘My lord, you have fulfilled all the promises you gave me, yet because I am your surrendered soul, you should give me fearlessness too.’” (Bhag. [3.23.49-51](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/23.49)) Devahuti explained that her daughters would eventually marry and leave home and she would then be alone. “But who will give me solace after your departure as a sannyasi? (Bhag. [3.23.52](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/23.52)) Indirectly, Devahuti was asking her husband for a son. She also regretted that she had loved her great husband but had not accepted spiritual guidance from him. They had produced nine daughters and enjoyed touring in the aerial mansion, savoring material life by his grace, but these had simply been acts of sense gratification. Now Devahuti wanted something to help her progress spiritually. It would be such a loss if her saintly husband left, because what is more important in developing spiritual consciousness than a saint’s association? Devahuti now lamented that while serving her husband she had been unaware of his potency, a hint of which she obtained when he had created the aerial mansion. She said: Despite having served you, my toil has proved useless, for it has failed to generate devotional service toward the Supreme Lord.

Feeling cheated, she regretted having asked only for children and not for liberation. Thus Devahuti, having followed a religious path for her material satisfaction, had attained both material detachment and spiritual desire.

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 57 summarizes the materialistic attitude that leads one not to seek spiritual rewards from spiritual association: “An intelligent man should utilize good opportunities. The first opportunity is the human form of life, and the second opportunity is to take birth in a suitable family where there is cultivation of spiritual knowledge; this is rarely obtained. The greatest opportunity is to have the association of a saintly person. Devahuti was conscious that she was bom as the daughter of an emperor. She was sufficiently educated and cultured, and at last she got Kardama Muni, a saintly person and a great yogi, as her husband. Still, if she did not get liberation from the entanglement of material energy, then certainly she would be cheated by the insurmountable illusory energy.”

## Chapter 24 - The Renunciation of Kardama Muni

## Texts 1-6: Kardama Pacifies Devahuti

Kardama’s response was definitive: Engage in devotional service with austerity and sense control, follow religious principles, and give in charity. Then the Supreme Lord will be pleased with you and will appear as your son. “The Personality of Godhead, being worshiped by you ... will vanquish the knot of your heart by becoming your son and teaching knowledge of Brahman.” (Bhag. [3.24.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/24.4))

A tightly knotted rope ties one thing to another just as maya uses a three-stranded rope made of self-centered desire to tie conditioned souls to material existence. Kapiladeva’s teachings will soon cut that knot in Devahuti’s heart. Srila Prabhupada offers a glimpse of Kapila’s teachings in his purport to this text: “The explanation was given by Lord Rsabha to His sons that this material world is an atmosphere of attraction between male and female. That attraction takes the shape of a knot in the heart, and by material affection it becomes still more tight. For people who hanker after material possessions, society, friendship and love, this knot of affection becomes very strong. It is only by brahma-bhavana—the instruction by which spiritual knowledge is enhanced—that the knot in the heart is cut to pieces. No material weapon is needed to cut this knot, but it requires bona fide spiritual instruction. Kardama Muni instructed his wife, Devahuti, that the Lord would appear as her son and disseminate spiritual knowledge to cut the knot of material identification.”

Following Kardama’s instructions, Devahuti began to worship the Lord situated in everyone’s heart. Maitreya Muni explains: “Devahuti was fully faithful and respectful toward the direction of her husband, Kardama, who was one of the Prajapatis, or generators of human beings in the universe. О great sage, she thus began to worship the master of the universe, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is situated in everyone’s heart. After many, many years, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Madhusudana, the killer of the demon Madhu, having entered the semen of Kardama, appeared in Devahuti just as fire comes from wood in a sacrifice.” (Bhag. [3.24.5-6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/24.5))

Krsna is both all-pervading and independent, and therefore it is not difficult for Him to manifest in either the semen or the womb of His devotee. Srila Prabhupada states in his purport to text 6: “Lord Nrsimha appeared from the pillar of Hiranyakasipu’s palace, Lord Varaha appeared from the nostril of Brahma, and Lord Kapila appeared from the semen of Kardama, but this does not mean that the nostril of Brahma or the pillar of Hiranyakasipu’s palace or the semen of Kardama Muni is the source of the appearance of the Lord. The Lord is always the Lord. Bhagavdn madhusudanah—He is the killer of all kinds of demons, and He always remains the Lord, even if He appears as the son of a particular devotee.”

## Texts 7-25: The Appearance of Lord Kapiladeva

When Kapila Muni appeared, the atmosphere became joyous and the demigods showered flowers. Brahma, Brahma’s nine sons, and the other demigods hurried to Kardama Muni’s hermitage. Kardama Muni had faithfully followed Brahma’s order to increase the population, and Brahma was pleased with the sage. In his purport to text 13 Prabhupada asserts that the disciple must accept the spiritual master’s order: “Whatever the father and the spiritual master order should be taken without argument: ‘Yes.’ There should be no instance in which the disciple or the son says, ‘This is not correct. I cannot carry it out.’ When he says that, he is fallen.... In any case, the order of the father or the order of the spiritual master must be carried out without hesitation, with an immediate yes. There should be no argument. That is real service to the father and to the spiritual master. Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura has stated that the order of the spiritual master is the life and soul of the disciples. As a man cannot separate his life from his body, a disciple cannot separate the order of the spiritual master from his life. If a disciple follows the instruction of the spiritual master in that way, he is sure to become perfect. This is confirmed in the Upanisads: the import of Vedic instruction is revealed automatically only to one who has implicit faith in the Supreme Personality of Godhead and in his spiritual master. One may be materially considered an illiterate man, but if he has faith in the spiritual master as well as in the Supreme Personality of Godhead, then the meaning of scriptural revelation is immediately manifested before him.”

After requesting Kardama and Devahuti to offer their nine daughters to his nine sons, Brahma then revealed the purpose of Kapiladeva’s advent: “By mystic yoga and the practical application of knowledge from the scriptures, Kapila Muni, who is characterized by His golden hair, His eyes just like lotus petals and His lotus feet, which bear the marks of lotus flowers, will uproot the deep-rooted desire for work in this material world.” (Bhag. [3.24.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/24.17))

Srila Prabhupada outlines in simple fashion the knowledge underpinning Kapila Muni’s Sankhya philosophy: “A man tries to be happy by achieving the fruits of his own honest labor, but actually he becomes more and more entangled. One cannot get out of this entanglement unless he has perfect knowledge, or devotional service.”

Finally, Brahma addressed DevahOti, telling her that Kapila Muni, who was within her womb, would remove her fear, ignorance, and doubt. After enlightening her, Kapiladeva, famous as Devahuti’s son, would preach throughout the world. Then Brahma departed, leaving the nine great sages who accompanied him to marry Kardama Muni’s nine daughters.

## Texts 26-34: Kardama’s Prayers to Kapila Muni

Just after Kapila Muni’s birth, Kardama approached him in a secluded place. Kardama was Kapila’s father, so he naturally loved his son. That love expanded and became perfect, however, because Kapiladeva was the Personality of Godhead. After offering his obeisances, Kardama thanked the Lord for His kindness: You have descended to alleviate the living entities’ suffering. How fortunate I am to see You, who are so rarely seen even by yogis in trance. You have incarnated Yourself by Your mercy in my home as my son. You have done this to keep true the words You spoke to me \[Bhag. [3.21.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.32)\] and to spread true knowledge. You have no material form but only a spiritual form, which You accept to please Your devotees.

In his purport to text 29, Srila Prabhupada glorifies the potency of devotional service: “Devotional service is such a powerful transcendental method that it surpasses all other methods of transcendental realization. The Lord says, therefore, that He lives neither in Vaikuntha nor in the heart of a yogi, but He lives where His pure devotees are always chanting and glorifying Him. The Supreme Personality of Godhead is known as bhakta-vatsala. He is never described as jnani-vatsala or yogi-vatsala. He is always described as bhakta-vatsala because He is more inclined toward His devotees than toward other transcendentalists. In Bhagavad-gita it is confirmed that only a devotee can understand Him as He is. Bhaktya mam abhijanati: ‘One can understand Me only by devotional service, not otherwise.’”

After surrendering himself to the all-opulent Supreme Personality of Godhead, the independent Lord and creator, powerful Kardama Muni begged the Lord to fulfill his desire: “Today I have something to ask from You, who are the Lord of all living entities. Since I have now been liberated by You from my debts to my father, and since all my desires are fulfilled, I wish to accept the order of an itinerant mendicant. Renouncing this family life, I wish to wander about, free from lamentation, thinking always of You in my heart.” (Bhag. [3.24.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/24.34)) Kardama Muni wanted to renounce the temporary for the eternal. In his purport to the next verse, Srila Prabhupada will discuss why Kardama was choosing to leave home despite the Lord’s advent there, but in his purport to this verse, he defines the renunciant’s duty.

**Actually, sannyasa, or renunciation of material household life, necessitates complete absorption in Krsna consciousness and immersion in the self. One does not take sannyasa, freedom from family responsibility in the renounced order of life, to make another family or to create an embarrassing transcendental fraud in the name of sannyasa. The sannyasi’s business is not to become proprietor of so many things and amass money from the innocent public. A sannyasi is proud that he is always thinking of Krsna within himself. Of course, there are two kinds of devotees of the Lord. One is called gosthy'dnandi, which means those who are preachers and have many followers for preaching the glories of the Lord and who live among those many, many followers just to organize missionary activities. Other devotees are atmanandi, or self-satisfied, and do not take the risk of preaching work. They remain, therefore, alone with God. In this classification was Kardama Muni. He wanted to be free from all anxieties and remain alone within his heart with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Parivraja means “an itinerant mendicant.” A mendicant sannyasi should not live anywhere for more than three days. He must be always moving because his duty is to move from door to door and enlighten people about Krsna consciousness.**

## Texts 35-40: Kapila Muni Replies

Now Srila Prabhupada answers an interesting question: If the Supreme Lord had advented in Kardama’s home as his son, why did Kardama want to leave home to seek self- or God-realization? Why leave home when God is already present in your home? In Krsna’s pastimes, as in life, the actual significance of an event is often more easily understood in retrospect. Krsna accomplishes many purposes through His pastimes, and thus “the will of Krsna” ultimately answers the question as to why Kardama Muni now, with Lord Kapiladeva as his son, desired to renounce his home. Srila Prabhupada addresses one purpose Krsna fulfilled through Kardama Muni’s renunciation in his purport to text 35: it underscored the importance of a householder’s duty to leave home after he has turned fifty. Thus even though the Supreme Personality of Godhead appeared as his son, Kardama Muni was duty-bound to respect Vedic authority. “This is a very important lesson,” Srila Prabhupada writes.

**Kardama Muni’s example is very instructive, for in spite of having the Supreme Personality of Godhead as his son, he left home just to obey the authority of the Vedic injunction. Kardama Muni states here the main purpose of his leaving home: while traveling all over the world as a mendicant, he would always remember the Supreme Personality of Godhead within his heart and thereby be freed from all the anxieties of material existence.... In Kali-yuga the injunction is that no one should accept sannyasa. Of course, those who actually follow the rules and regulations must take sannyasa. Generally, however, people are unable to accept sannyasa life, and therefore Caitanya Mahaprabhu stressed, kalau nasty eva nasty eva nasty eva gatir anyatha. In this age there is no other alternative, no other alternative, no other alternative than to chant the holy name of the Lord: Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare. The main purpose of sannyasa life is to be in constant companionship with the Supreme Lord, either by thinking of Him within the heart or hearing of Him through aural reception. In this age, hearing is more important than thinking because one’s thinking may be disturbed by mental agitation, but if one concentrates on hearing, he will be forced to associate with the sound vibration of Krsna. Krsna and the sound vibration “Krsna” are nondifferent, so if one loudly vibrates Hare Krsna, he will be able to think of Krsna immediately. This process of chanting is the best process of self-realization in this age; therefore Lord Caitanya preached it so nicely for the benefit of all humanity.**

Kapila Muni, the Personality of Godhead, replied to both Kardama’s prayers and to his request: “O Muni, because I told you before that I would become your son, I have descended to fulfill this truth. My appearance in this world is especially to explain the philosophy of Sankhya, which is highly esteemed for self-realization by those desiring freedom from the entanglement of unnecessary material desires.” (Bhag. [3.24.35-36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/24.35))

Common people aspire for happiness by satisfying their material desires without understanding that the attempt to satisfy material desires, which are themselves bom from passion, simply gives birth to a multiplicity of desires. “O chief of the Bharatas, when there is an increase in the mode of passion the symptoms of great attachment, fruitive activity, intense endeavor, and uncontrollable desire and hankering develop.” (Bg. [14.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/14.12)) And, “The mode of passion is bom of unlimited desires and longings, О son of Kunti, and because of this the embodied living entity is bound to material fruitive actions.” (Bg. [14.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/14.7)) A living entity in passion will be possessed by an ever-increasing number of desires. Yet his capacity to fulfill those desires is limited by his karma regardless of the ability or facility one thinks he has. Thus by increasing one’s association with the mode of passion, one necessarily lessens the percentage of desires he can actually fulfill. Frustration and distress must follow; they are the natural companions of passion. Bhagavad-gita ([14.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/14.16)) therefore warns: “action done in the mode of passion results in misery.”

The Bhagavad-gita therefore favors the mode of goodness over passion, because the mode of goodness encourages one to simplify and lessen one’s material desires. “O sinless one, the mode of goodness, being purer than the others, is illuminating, and it frees one from all sinful reactions. Those situated in that mode become conditioned by a sense of happiness and knowledge.” (Bg. [14.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/14.6)) Obtaining freedom from all material desires, including those bom of goodness, by worshiping the Lord, forms the basis of Kapiladeva’s teachings.

Sanctioning Kardama Muni’s renunciation, Kapiladeva offered him instruction: “Go as you desire, surrendering all your activities to Me. Conquering insurmountable death, worship Me for eternal life. In your own heart, through your intellect, you will always see Me, the supreme self-effulgent soul dwelling within the hearts of all living entities. Thus you will achieve the state of eternal life, free from all lamentation and fear.” (Bhag. [3.24.38-39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/24.38))

In text 34 of this chapter, Kardama Muni asked Kapiladeva to bless him with the strength to follow the sannyasa path and to “wander about, free from lamentation, thinking always of You in my heart.” Here, in text 39, Kapiladeva confirms that the process Kardama had suggested would award him the desired result.

In Bhagavatam [3.23.51-57](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/23.51), Devahuti requested Kardama to award her fearlessness and spiritual knowledge, for she felt she had not taken actual advantage of his association. Kardama’s reply (Bhag. [3.24.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/24.2)) repeated the Lord’s promise (Bhag. [3.21.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/21.32)) that He would appear as Devahuti’s son and instruct her. Kapiladeva’s final words to Kardama (Bhag. [3.24.40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/24.40)) confirm this mission: “I shall also describe this sublime knowledge, which is the door to spiritual life, to My mother, so that she also can attain perfection and self-realization, ending all reactions to fruitive activities. Thus she also will be freed from all material fear.”

## Texts 41-47: Kardama Muni’s Renunciation

Kardama’s responsibility to his faithful wife had now been fulfilled. He circumambulated his son, and with a peaceful mind left for the forest to take shelter of Krsna. Kardama then accepted mauna-vrata, the vow of silence, which can ultimately mean that one spends one’s life speaking only the Lord’s glories. He thus focused his mind on the Supreme Personality of Godhead and gradually became free of all material identification. With his mind turned inward and perfectly calm, Kardama attained full liberation and saw the Supreme Lord in the heart of every living entity. Understanding that every soul exists in Him, the Supersoul, Kardama Muni performed pure devotional service and “ultimately attained the path back to Godhead.” (Bhag. [3.24.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/24.47))

## Dialogue Six - Lord Kapha’s Teaching of Sankhya-yoga

## Chapter 25 - The Glories of Devotional Service

## Texts 1-11: Devahuti Inquires from Her Son, Kapila Muni

Kardama Muni had taken sannyasa, and Saunaka Rsi now inquires from Suta Gosvami about Lord Kapila’s activities after that event. Suta’s reply repeats what Maitreya told Vidura. In his purport to Bhagavatam 3.25.2, Srila Prabhupada glorifies the result of such inquiries, because hearing from and about Krsna offers the sweet taste of His association: “To hear from Krsna is the real pleasure of the senses; therefore He is known as Govinda, for by His words, by His teachings, by His instruction—by everything connected with Him—He enlivens the senses. Whatever He instructs is from the transcendental platform, and His instructions, being absolute, are nondifferent from Him. Hearing from Krsna or His expansion or plenary expansion like Kapila is very pleasing to the senses. Bhagavad-gita can be read or heard many times, but because it gives great pleasure, the more one reads Bhagavad-gita the more he gets the appetite to read and understand it, and each time he gets new enlightenment. That is the nature of the transcendental message. Similarly, we find that transcendental happiness in the Srimad-Bhagavatam. The more we hear and chant the glories of the Lord, the more we become happy.”

Suta Gosvami begins: Once as Kapila Muni was sitting leisurely, Devahuti remembered that Brahma had predicted that her divine son would cut the knots of her ignorance and doubt. She then approached her son and expressed her weariness with material existence. “I am very sick of the disturbance caused by my material senses, for because of this sense disturbance, my Lord, I have fallen into the abyss of ignorance. Your Lordship is my only means of getting out of this darkest region of ignorance because You are my transcendental eye, which, by Your mercy only, I have attained after many, many births.” (Bhag. 3.25.7-8) Devahuti’s cynical attitude about material life is healthy for her spiritual advancement. Understanding her son’s actual position, she begged Him to dispel her illusion. “You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the origin and Supreme Lord of all living entities. You have arisen to disseminate the rays of the sun in order to dissipate the darkness of the ignorance of the universe. ... I have taken shelter of Your lotus feet because You are the only person of whom to take shelter. You are the ax which can cut the tree of material existence. I therefore offer my obeisances unto You, who are the greatest of all transcendentalists, and I inquire from You as to the relationship between man and woman and between spirit and matter.” (Bhag. [3.25.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.9), [11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.11))Prabhupada describes both how a living entity is bound by matter and then released by Krsna’s grace:

**The Lord is merciful; if anyone wants to forget Him and enjoy this material world, He gives him full facility, not directly but through the agency of His material potency. Therefore, since the material potency is the Lord’s energy, indirectly it is the Lord who gives the facility to forget Him. Devahuti therefore said, “My engagement in sense gratification was also due to You. Now kindly get me free from this entanglement.”**

**By the grace of the Lord one is allowed to enjoy this material world, but when one is disgusted with material enjoyment and is frustrated, and when one sincerely surrenders unto the lotus feet of the Lord, then the Lord is so kind that He frees one from entanglement. Krsna says, therefore, in Bhagavad-gita, “First of all surrender, and then I will take charge of you and free you from all reactions of sinful activities.” (Bhag.** [**3.25.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.10)**, purport)**

## Texts 12-20: Kapila Muni’s Introduction of the Sankhya-yoga System

Satisfied by her sincere inquiries, Kapila thanks His mother, and smiling, introduces Devahuti to an ancient path. “The yoga system which relates to the Lord and the individual soul, which is meant for the ultimate benefit of the living entity, and which causes detachment from all happiness and distress in the material world, is the highest yoga system.” (Bhag. 3.25.13) Kapila assures His mother that he will explain it to her, just as He has explained it to great sages in the past “because they were also anxious to hear about it.” Misery and suffering is at the heart of material experience; it is the inherent nature of this world and cannot be avoided. Ironically, what fixes an eternal soul to this world is his desire to enjoy matter. Ignorant of his true identity, and identifying with his body, he searches out material objects for his pleasure as if his consciousness were a searchlight. He thinks, “I am the enjoyer, and the world is meant for me to exploit.”

But even apparently successful enjoyment is temporary. The frustrated eternal soul continues to long for true happiness. Devahuti understood this and therefore wished to cut her material existence at the root. She wanted to stop trying to exploit matter for her own pleasure.

Kapila Muni first instructs her in the essence of His teachings, which He begins by differentiating between the soul’s restricted, conditioned life and its natural, liberated life: “The stage in which the consciousness of the living entity is attracted by the three modes of material nature is called conditional life. But when that same consciousness is attached to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one is situated in the consciousness of liberation.” (Bhag. [3.25.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.15)) As conditioned souls, we view ourselves as if we were the center of existence. Choosing to live in this illusion allows the three modes of material nature to control us, just as when we break the government’s laws we become controlled by its prison system. Our attempt to exploit what has been produced by the modes traps us under the modes’ control. When our attachment honestly shifts to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, we become liberated, free. The searchlight of our consciousness then seeks means by which we can please Krsna instead of seeking self-centered pleasure.

To untie the ropes of illusion, Kapiladeva explains, one must eradicate the lust and greed produced when one misidentifies himself with the body and becomes attached to everything connected to it as if it were his own. When one drops the illusion of “I” and “mine,” he becomes pure and no longer experiences material happiness and distress. Srila Prabhupada briefly describes how one can attain this freedom: “One’s senses must be engaged in devotional service to the Lord. That is the process. The mind must have some engagement. One cannot make the mind vacant. Of course there are some foolish attempts to try to make the mind vacant or void, but that is not possible. The only process that will purify the mind is to engage it in Krsna. The mind must be engaged. If we engage our mind in Krsna, naturally the consciousness becomes fully purified, and there is no chance of the entrance of material desire and greed.” (Bhag. [3.25.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.16), purport)

Once one has become attached to Krsna by focusing his mind on Him, what will one then perceive as reality? Lord Kapila tells His mother that such a pure soul will see himself as eternal and transcendental, as minute yet self-effulgent. His perception of everything in existence will be accurate because he will be complete in knowledge and devotional renunciation. In this way, he will remain indifferent to matter.

In well-staged dramatic performances, the audience is manipulated into identifying with specific characters. Creating characters with whom one can identify is one of the arts of stagecraft. If a playwright is successful and the audience manages to empathize with one or more of the characters, he can lead them to feel the same emotions the characters feel—emotions that actually have nothing to do with them personally. They will become elated with the hero when he is triumphant and dejected with him in his losses. In truth, the audience has neither triumphed nor lost, so there is no real reason for the audience to become happy or sad. They have simply experienced an illusion. Similarly, by identifying with the well-staged drama of maya, one comes to identify with feelings and events that actually have nothing to do with him.

Therefore the Bhagavad-gita ([2.69](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.69)) mysteriously describes that the perceptions and actions of those in illusion are antithetical to the perceptions and actions of realized souls: “What is night for all beings is the time of awakening for the self-controlled; and the time of awakening for all beings is night for the introspective sage.” Those in illusion remain indifferent to their actual identities and, like members of an audience, identify only with the drama before their eyes. A soul who has realized his true identity by practicing devotional service sees beyond this world’s dramatic performance. His perception is accurate; he sees truth. Instead of identifying with illusory characters and events, he identifies with the real character, the Absolute Truth, Krsna, and perceives himself in his true identity as Krsna’s eternal servant. It is therefore natural for him to be materially detached because he is genuinely beyond the material experience. This full freedom from illusion, Kapila Muni explains, is brought about only when we practice devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Bhakti-yoga is therefore the only auspicious path.

After hearing of the value of devotional service, Devahuti naturally seeks instruction on how to practice it. Kapiladeva therefore explains its root cause: All men of learning recognize that material attachment entraps and entangles the soul. It is natural for a soul to be attached to something, but persons should be discriminating with their attachments. Better than material attachment is attachment to self-realized devotees, sadhus, because such attachment opens the door of liberation. Srila Prabhupada amplifies this foundational principle:

**Here it is clearly stated that attachment for one thing is the cause of bondage in conditioned life, and the same attachment, when applied to something else, opens the door of liberation. Attachment cannot be killed; it has simply to be transferred. Attachment for material things is called material consciousness, and attachment for Krsna or His devotee is called Krsna consciousness. Consciousness, therefore, is the platform of attachment. It is clearly stated here that when we simply purify the consciousness from material consciousness to Krsna consciousness, we attain liberation. ... Here it is recommended that attachment should be transferred to the self-realized devotees, the sadhus. And who is a sadhu? A sadhu is not just an ordinary man with a saffron robe or long beard. A sadhu is described in Bhagavad-gita as one who unflinchingly engages in devotional service. . . . Attachment to a devotee is attachment to the service of the Lord because if one associates with a sadhu, the result will be that the sadhu will teach him how to become a devotee, a worshiper and a sincere servitor of the Lord. . . . That is the result of associating with a sadhu. Kapila Muni first of all instructs that the path of liberation begins with such association. (Bhag.** [**3.25.20**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.20)**, purport)**

## Texts 21-24 and 25-27: Recognizing a Sadhu and The Highest Yoga—Results of Associating with a Sadhu

Understanding the qualities that decorate a sadhu allows one to recognize him and make him an object of one’s affection. Kapila Muni therefore defines the characteristics by which a sadhu may be known. Sadhus are tolerant, merciful, and friendly to everyone. They have no enemies, are peaceful, and abide by the scriptures. Sadhus engage in devotional service and do not deviate from the bhakti-marga. They renounce everything, including their own comforts, to serve the Lord. For Krsna’s service they may even renounce family and friends. Sadhus always chant and hear about Krsna, and thus they transcend material misery.

Attachment to such sadhus—devotees free from material attachment—“counteracts the pernicious effects of material attachment.” (Bhag. [3.25.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.24)) A sadhu is holy because he serves Krsna so faithfully. Because of a sadhu’s faithful serving mood, Krsna remains present in his consciousness. If one hears from such a sadhu even for a moment —especially as the sadhu opens his heart and speaks about Krsna— the taste for Krsna consciousness enters one’s ear and makes an impression on one’s heart. One actually glimpses Krsna through that brief association.

Citing the Caitanya-caritamrta in his purport to Bhagavatam [3.2.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/2.6), Srila Prabhupada defines the bhakti-lata-bija as “taste”: “The living entities all over the universes are enjoying the effects of the respective fruitive results of their own work, life after life. Out of all of them, some may be influenced by the association of pure devotees and thus get the chance to execute devotional service by attainment of taste. This taste is the seed of devotional service, and one who is fortunate enough to have received such a seed is advised to sow it in the core of his heart.”

I remember being with Prabhupada and being painfully aware of my own insincerity. Or perhaps I was simply distracted or in a terrible mood. Then Srila Prabhupada would ask, “So, everything is all right?” That question forced me to bathe in the compassionate, moonlike rays of his pure heart, and miraculously I would find that everything really was all right. This was neither a mystical trick nor some form of material charisma on Prabhupada’s part. Rather, his openhearted association offered me a taste of Goloka Vrndavana. And the full flavor of his own taste planted a seed of the same flavor in his disciples’ hearts.

Although sadhu'sanga is a foundational principle in spiritual life, it is based on a still more general principle. That is, association transfers the contents of one person’s heart into another’s heart. The heart is like a crystal, and it naturally becomes colored by whatever is around it. If one associates with materialists, one becomes tinged with materialism; if one associates with drunkards, one will become a drunkard. Association with sincere devotees turns one into a sincere devotee. Therefore, association with advanced devotees is essential for those seeking to advance in Krsna consciousness.In his purports to texts 21-24, Srila Prabhupada expands on a sadhu's qualities as well as the benefits of his holy association. Here is a sampling from those purports:

**A sadhu, as described above, is a devotee of the Lord. His concern, therefore, is to enlighten people in devotional service to the Lord. That is his mercy. He knows that without devotional service to the Lord, human life is spoiled. A devotee travels all over the country, from door to door, preaching, “Be Krsna conscious. Be a devotee of Lord Krsna. Don’t spoil your life in simply fulfilling your animal propensities. Human life is meant for self-realization, or Krsna consciousness.” These are the preachings of a sadhu. He is not satisfied with his own liberation. He always thinks about others. He is the most compassionate personality towards all the fallen souls. One of his qualifications, therefore, is karunika, great mercy to the fallen souls. While engaged in preaching work, he has to meet with so many opposing elements, and therefore the sadhu, or devotee of the Lord, has to be very tolerant. (Bhag.** [**3.25.21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.21)**, purport)**

**A sadhu is one who has given up all responsibility to society, family and worldly humanitarianism, simply for the service of the Lord. As soon as he takes his birth in the world, a person has so many responsibilities and obligations—to the public, to the demigods, to the great sages, to the general living beings, to his parents, to the family forefathers and to many others. When he gives up all such obligations for the sake of the service of the Supreme Lord, he is not punished for such renunciation of obligation. But if for sense gratification a person renounces all such obligations, he is punished by the law of nature. (Bhag.** [**3.25.22**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.22)**, purport)**

**There are multifarious miseries in material existence—those pertaining to the body and the mind, those imposed by other living entities and those imposed by natural disturbances. But a sadhu is not disturbed by such miserable conditions because his mind is always filled with Krsna consciousness, and thus he does not like to talk about anything but the activities of the Lord. Maharaja Ambarisa did not speak of anything but the pastimes of the Lord. Vacamsi vaikuntha-gunanuvarnane (Bhag.** [**9.4.18**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/4.18)**). He engaged his words only in glorification of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Sadhus are always interested in hearing about the activities of the Lord or His devotees. Since they are filled with Krsna consciousness, they are forgetful of the material miseries. Ordinary conditioned souls, being forgetful of the activities of the Lord, are always full of anxieties and material tribulations. On the other hand, since the devotees always engage in the topics of the Lord, they are forgetful of the miseries of material existence. (Bhag.** [**3.25.23**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.23)**, purport)**

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to Bhagavatam [3.25.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.24) describes sadhus in relation to his founding of ISKCON:

**Kapila Muni herein advises His mother, Devahuti, that if she wants to be free from material attachment, she should increase her attachment for the sadhus, or devotees who are completely freed from all material attachment.... We have to seek the association of such devotees. For this reason we have begun the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. There are many mercantile, scientific and other associations in human society to develop a particular type of education or consciousness, but there is no association which helps one to get free from all material association. If anyone has reached the stage where he must become free from this material contamination, then he has to seek the association of devotees, wherein Krsna consciousness is exclusively cultured. One can thereby become freed from all material association . . . One should therefore give up the association of materialistic persons and seek the association of persons engaged in Krsna consciousness, and by such association he will benefit in spiritual advancement. By their words and instructions, he will be able to cut off his attachment to material existence.**

What occurs naturally in a sadhu’s association? Kapiladeva continues: “In the association of pure devotees, discussion of the pastimes and activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very pleasing and satisfying to the ear and the heart. By cultivating such knowledge one gradually becomes advanced on the path of liberation, and thereafter he is freed, and his attraction becomes fixed. Then real devotion and devotional service begin.” (Bhag. [3.25.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.25)) In his purport Srila Prabhupada again underscores why association with sadhus is essential: “Association with devotees means association with the Lord. The devotee who makes this association develops the consciousness for rendering service to the Lord, and then, being situated in the transcendental position of devotional service, he gradually becomes perfect.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami states in Priti-sandarbha, anuccheda 61, that the word bhakti in text 25 (sraddha ratir bhaktir anukramisyati) refers to prema-bhakti, bhakti where the deepest priti (love) is present.

Kapila Muni then further describes devotional service, the highest yoga process: Through constant engagement in devotional service in the association of devotees, and by constantly thinking of the Lord’s activities, a person gains a complete distaste for sense gratification. One on that path is able to fully control his mind. By fixing his controlled mind beyond the modes of nature—that is, on the Lord— one achieves the Lord’s association. One can contact the Supreme Personality of Godhead by practicing the kind of yoga “in which the mind is always fixed in devotional service unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead ...” (Bhag. [3.25.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.27))

Srila Prabhupada emphasizes the power of practicing bhakti-yoga in his purport to text 27: “Lord Caitanya, therefore, approved the process of hearing from realized devotees about the pastimes of the Lord. It does not matter to what category of this world the audience belongs. If one meekly and submissively hears about the activities of the Lord from a realized soul, he will be able to conquer the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is unconquerable by any other process. Hearing or associating with devotees is the most important function for self-realization.”

## Texts 28-40: Devahuti Again Questions Kapila Muni, and Kapila Replies

Devahuti now asks her son to describe bhakti-yoga in more depth, because so far, the Lord has only explained its essence. She wants to know what specific practices she should perform to “easily and immedi' ately attain the service of Your lotus feet.” (Bhag. [3.25.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.28)) She also inquires into the various parts of the mystic yoga system. Realizing her limitations, Devahuti fears her inability to understand the Absolute Truth. Therefore she requests Kapila Muni: “My dear son, Kapila, after all, I am a woman. It is very difficult for me to understand the Absolute Truth because my intelligence is not very great. But if You will kindly explain it to me, even though I am not very intelligent, I can understand it and thereby feel transcendental happiness.” (Bhag. [3.25.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.30)) Kapiladeva’s heart is melted by her unassuming estimation of herself, and out of compassion He offers a more detailed explanation of the Sankhya system, “which is a combination of devotional service and mystic realization . . .” (Bhag. [3.25.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.31)) He begins: The senses have a natural inclination to work toward a goal; the mind is the center of the senses. It is the natural tendency of the mind to serve. “When that service spirit is engaged in devotional service to the Personality of Godhead, without any motive, that is far better even than salvation.” (Bhag. [3.25.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.32))

In The Nectar of Devotion (p. 15), Srila Prabhupada highlights the superiority of bhakti over liberation by summarizing Srila Rupa Gosvami’s words: “If brahmananda, or the happiness of becoming one with the Supreme, is multiplied by one trillionfold, it still cannot compare to an atomic fraction of the happiness derived from the ocean of devotional service.” The Nectar of Devotion then quotes Prahlada Maharaja in Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya. There, Prahlada compares liberation to “the water in the impression left by a cow’s hoof in the earth” and praises “this ocean of bliss” afforded by his devotion to Lord Nrsimhadeva. The Nectar of Devotion follows with a quotation from Srila Sridhara Svami’s commentary on Srimad-Bhagavatam, Bhavartha-dipika, in which Sridhara Svami compares devotional service to the happiness of religiosity, economic development, sense gratification, and liberation: “A transcendental devotee regards any kind of happiness other than devotional service as no better than straw in the street.”

Kapila Muni next explains the superior attainments possible when serving the Personality of Godhead: “Bhakti, devotional service, dissolves the subtle body of the living entity without separate effort, just as fire in the stomach digests all that we eat. A pure devotee, who is attached to the activities of devotional service and who always engages in the service of My lotus feet, never desires to become one with Me. Such a devotee, who is unflinchingly engaged, always glorifies My pastimes and activities.” (Bhag. [3.25.33-34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.33))

The first endeavor of jnana-yogis and monistic astanga-yogis is to quiet and ultimately remove the fluctuations of the wayward and obstinate mind. The initial instruction of Patanjali’s Yoga Sutras is yogarh citta-vrtti nirodhah: yoga is defined as the cessation of movements of consciousness. This essentially means that the purpose of yoga is to stop or annihilate the mind. Having accomplished that, the impersonalists contend, one will automatically realize his undifferentiated oneness with the Absolute Truth. The incredible endeavor to subdue the mind can be accomplished automatically, Lord Kapila explains, by practicing devotional service.

Devotional service removes the problem at its root. The cause of material bondage is the soul’s aversion to Krsna and its consequent absorption in false ego. By training the mind to become attached to Krsna and to serve Him with devotion, the subtle material body—mind, intelligence, and false ego—is automatically dissolved. The soul then becomes situated in its unfettered true glory as servant of Krsna. Thus Sri Vrndavana dasa Thakura states in Caitanya-bhagavata (Adi [13.178](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-adi/13.178)), sei se vidyara phala janiha niscaya ‘krsna-pada-padme yadi citta-vrtti raya’: “The perfect result of an education is the fixing of the mind on Krsna’s lotus feet.”

Then Kapila reveals further exalted attainments of pure devotees: “O My mother, My devotees always see the smiling face of My form, with eyes like the rising morning sun. They like to see My various transcendental forms, which are all benevolent, and they also talk favorably with Me. Upon seeing the charming forms of the Lord, smiling and attractive, and hearing His very pleasing words, the pure devotee almost loses all other consciousness. His senses are freed from all other engagements, and he becomes absorbed in devotional service. Thus in spite of his unwillingness, he attains liberation without separate endeavor.” (Bhag. [3.25.35-36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.35))Kapila Muni will later describe the Lord’s beauty in more detail, but the Lord’s beauty is also described in many places in scripture. Here are three particularly sweet texts:

**The women of the palace thought He was Lord Krsna when they saw His dark-blue complexion the color of a rain cloud, His yellow silk garments, His long arms and red-tinged eyes, His charming lotus face adorned with a pleasing smile, His fine ornaments and His thick, curly blue hair. Thus the women became bashful and hid themselves here and there. (Bhag.** [**10.55.27-28**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/55.27)**)**

**I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who is adept in playing on His flute, with blooming eyes like lotus petals, with head decked with peacock feather, with the figure of beauty tinged with the hue of blue clouds, and His unique loveliness charming millions of Cupids. (Bs.** [**5.30**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bs/30)**)**

**My dear friend, the luster of Krsna’s body is more brilliant than that of a newly formed cloud, and His yellow dress is more attractive than newly arrived lightning. A peacock feather decorates His head, and on His neck hangs a lovely necklace of brilliant pearls. As He holds His charming flute to His lips, His face looks as beautiful as the full autumn moon. By such beauty, Madana-mohana, the enchanter of Cupid, is increasing the desire of My eyes to see Him. (Cc. Antya** [**15.63**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/15.63)**)**

During a lecture on Bhagavatam [3.25.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.35) (Bombay, December 4, 1974), Srila Prabhupada wonderfully directed his audience to meditate on the beautiful deity form of Krsna:

**It is not idol worship. The atheist class may say so, but it is not so. Those who have got eyes, they can see. Just like when Caitanya Mahaprabhu entered the temple of Jagannatha, immediately He fainted, “Oh, here is My Lord. Here is My Lord.” . . . When you develop that love for Krsna, then you will see immediately and you will faint, “Oh, here is my Lord.” Somebody was saying to me that “It is just like your deity here is trying to talk with me.” Yes. He is here to talk with you, but He is waiting whether you’re interested to talk with Him. That’s all. Krsna says that tesarh satata-yuktanam, bhajatam priti-purvakam buddhi-yogam dadami tam. He talks, but with whom? One who is twenty-four hours engaged with love and faith in the service of the Lord. To whom? ... Krsna is ready to talk with you. He has come. He has descended in arcd-murti to talk with you, to be visible by you. Now you make yourself ready and fit to talk with Krsna. Then He will exchange conversation. This is possible.**

Prabhupada also notes the importance of deity worship in his purport to text 35 and discusses the sweet, loving exchanges the Lord in His deity form and the devotee share. In his purport to text 36, Srila Prabhupada strongly directs us to hearing sastra in addition to our performance of deity worship: “It is a prescribed duty in temple worship that not only should one visit the temple to see the Deity nicely decorated, but at the same time he should hear the recitation of Srimad-Bhagavatam, Bhagavad-gita or some similar literature, which is regularly recited in the temple. It is the system in Vrndavana that in every temple there is recitation of the sastras. Even third-class devotees who have no literary knowledge or no time to read Srimad-Bhagavatam or Bhagavadgita get the opportunity to hear about the pastimes of the Lord. In this way their minds may remain always absorbed in the thought of the Lord—His form, His activities and His transcendental nature. This state of Krsna consciousness is a liberated stage. Lord Caitanya, therefore, recommended five important processes in the discharge of devotional service: (1) to chant the holy names of the Lord, Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare, (2) to associate with devotees and serve them as far as possible, (3) to hear Srimad-Bhagavatam, (4) to see the decorated temple and the Deity and, if possible, (5) to live in a place like Vrndavana or Mathura. These five items alone can help a devotee achieve the highest perfectional stage.”

When devotees think constantly of the Lord, they lose their desire for both heavenly and earthly pleasure, for mystic perfection (siddhi), and for liberation. Still, by Krsna’s grace, the devotees enjoy all benedictions. As they advance, devotees are naturally blessed by Krsna with powerful abilities to use in His service. Indeed, when by their advancement “the seed of fruitive activity is burned by the fire of knowledge, the spiritual properties and mystic powers are automatically manifest,” as Srila Prabhupada explains in his summary of Canto Five, Chapter Six. Sukadeva Gosvami answers the question of why one does not see exalted devotees exhibiting such mystic powers in Bhagavatam [5.6.2-5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/6.2), where he warns even advanced souls to remain vigilant, protecting themselves from lust, anger, and greed. It is important, he stresses, that yogis control their mind and not allow themselves to become tempted by opulence, mystic or otherwise. Yet as Srila Prabhupada notes in his purport to Bhagavatam [5.6.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/6.1): “If, by the grace of the Supreme Lord, a devotee achieves extraordinary opulence, he utilizes the opportunity for the Lord’s service. He is not disturbed by the opulence.”

It is also important to note that when Srila Prabhupada speaks about the opulence a devotee might attain, even in this life, he is referring to the opulence of Vaikuntha: “Devotees enjoy all the benefits of the higher planets and the Vaikuntha planets also.” A devotee “enjoys all the facilities of the material and spiritual worlds, even during the present life-span.” (Bhag. [3.25.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.37), purport) What does it mean for a pure Krsna conscious devotee to possess the opulences “of the higher planets” and “all the facilities of the material and spiritual worlds”? A pure devotee, living only to serve Krsna, understands that everything is Krsna’s and is to be used in His service. Therefore Kapila Muni (Bhag. [3.25.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.38)) will next state that time destroys neither a devotee’s opulence nor his possessions, for a devotee ultimately sees only the Lord as his “opulence” and “possessions.”

The Lord continues: “My dear mother, devotees who receive such transcendental opulences are never bereft of them; neither weapons nor the change of time can destroy such opulences. Because the devotees accept Me as their friend, their relative, their son, preceptor, benefactor and Supreme Deity, they cannot be deprived of their possessions at any time.” (Bhag. [3.25.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.38))

In his purport to texts 39-40, Srila Prabhupada describes the reason behind the Lord’s causeless mercy by describing the devotee’s exalted selfless mentality:

For a devotee there is no concern for this life or the next life because in any life he does not desire elevation in material prosperity or a high-grade or low-grade life. He prays to the Lord, “My dear Lord, it does not matter where I am bom, but let me be bom, even as an ant, in the house of a devotee.” A pure devotee does not pray to the Lord for liberation from this material bondage. Actually, the pure devotee never thinks that he is fit for liberation. Considering his past life and his mischievous activities, he thinks that he is fit to be sent to the lowest region of hell. If in this life I am trying to become a devotee, this does not mean that in my many past lives 1 was one-hundred-percent pious. That is not possible. A devotee, therefore, is always conscious of his real position. Only by his full surrender to the Lord, by the Lord’s grace, are his sufferings made shorter. As stated in Bhagavad-gita, “Surrender unto Me, and 1 will give you protection from all kinds of sinful reaction.” That is His mercy. But this does not mean that one who has surrendered to the lotus feet of the Lord has committed no misdeeds in his past life. A devotee always prays, “For my misdeeds, may I be bom again and again, but my only prayer is that 1 may not forget Your service.” The devotee has that much mental strength, and he prays to the Lord: “May I be born again and again, but let me be bom in the home of Your pure devotee so that I may again get a chance to develop myself.”

Srila Prabhupada continues to explain the full focus of a devotee’s life: “A pure devotee is not anxious to elevate himself in his next birth. He has already given up that sort of hope.... He is satisfied with whatever is obtainable by God’s grace. He is not at all attached to improving his social status or improving the status of education of his children.
