Srila Prabhupada describes the importance of meditating on the Lord’s wonderful laughter, smile, and beauty: “The exceptional beauty of the laughter of Lord Visnu is that when He smiles His small teeth, which resemble the buds of jasmine flowers, at once become reddish, reflecting His rosy lips. If the yogi is able to place the beautiful face of the Lord in the core of his heart, he will be completely satisfied. In other words, when one is absorbed in seeing the beauty of the Lord within himself, the material attraction can no longer disturb him.” (Bhag. [3.28.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/28.33), purport)

From the same purport: “It is recommended that the yogi visualize the laughter of the Lord after studying His smile very carefully. These particular descriptions of meditation on the smile, laughter, face, lips and teeth all indicate conclusively that God is not impersonal. It is described herein that one should meditate on the laughter or smiling of Visnu. There is no other activity that can completely cleanse the heart of the devotee.”

## Texts 34-44: Results of Fixed Yogic Meditation on the Lord

## Text 34: The Yogi’s Experience

The yogis successive practices and realizations, which increase as he advances in devotion, gradually award him ecstatic love and its symptoms. Kapila Muni describes the yogi’s perfection: “By following this course, the yogi gradually develops pure love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari. In the course of his progress in devotional service, the hairs on his body stand erect through excessive joy, and he is constantly bathed in a stream of tears occasioned by intense love. Gradually, even the mind, which he used as a means to attract the Lord, as one attracts a fish to a hook, withdraws from material activity.” (Bhag. [3.28.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/28.34))

Srila Prabhupada describes the perfect state of yoga in his purport to this text: “When one’s love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead in devotional service is fully developed, one always sees the Lord, even without artificially meditating on His form. His vision is divine because he has no other engagement. At this stage of spiritual realization it is not necessary to engage the mind artificially. Since the meditation recommended in the lower stages is a means to come to the platform of devotional service, those already engaged in the transcendental loving service of the Lord are above such meditation. This stage of perfection is called Krsna consciousness.” When a yogi becomes attracted to the Lord, he can withdraw himself from material activities.

## Texts 35-39: The Yogi Views His Body

In these five verses, Kapila continues to respond to Devahuti’s question (Bhag. [3.27.17-20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/27.17)) about how the soul is bound and freed. Here He explains that the perfect yogi’s mind, retracted from matter, is still, peaceful, and naturally absorbed in the Lord. His thoughts are fixed in the Lord’s service. Fully purified by his love for God, his false ego dissolved, free from the modes of nature, with great devotion he desires only to serve his Lord. Although a conditioned soul remains unable to truly understand the actions of a liberated soul, Kapila Muni will now describe this difficult subject. The yogi, free of all material influence and situated in his true identity, sees everything he has previously experienced as the product of false ego—ignorance. “Because he has achieved his real identity, the perfectly realized soul has no conception of how the material body is moving or acting, just as an intoxicated person cannot understand whether or not he has clothing on his body. The body of such a liberated yogi, along with the senses, is taken charge of by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and it functions until its destined activities are finished.” (Bhag. [3.28.37-38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/28.37)) The yogi remains fully detached, considering everything connected to his body a dream. Thus the liberated soul clearly understands that he and his body, family, possessions, and wealth are not synonymous.Srila Prabhupada’s purports to this section are interesting. Here are several excerpts:

**When the mind is completely purified in love of Godhead, the mind becomes the mind of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The mind at that time does not act separately, nor does it act without inspiration to fulfill the desire of the Lord. (Bhag.** [**3.28.35**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/28.35)**, purport)**

**By yoga practice one can eradicate this ignorance of thinking oneself independent of the Supreme Lord. One’s actual relationship is eternally that of love. The living entity is meant to render transcendental loving service to the Lord. Forgetfulness of that sweet relationship is called ignorance, and in ignorance one is impelled by the three material modes of nature to think himself the enjoyer. (Bhag.** [**3.28.36**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/28.36)**, purport)**

**Even after being switched off, an electric fan moves for some time. That movement is not due to the electric current, but is a continuation of the last movement; similarly, although a liberated soul appears to be acting just like an ordinary man, his actions are to be accepted as the continuation of past activities. (Bhag.** [**3.28.38**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/28.38)**, purport)**

## Texts 40-44: Because He Views Everything in Relationship to the Supreme, the Yogi Never Falls

Blazing firewood is simultaneously one with and different from its products—smoke, flames, and heat. Similarly, Krsna, the independent source of everything, is both different and nondifferent from everything. This is Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s philosophy of acintya-bhedabheda'tattva. From mountains to planets to universes, everything is His energy, nondifferent from Him yet separately manifest. The infinitesimal individual souls that fill the various bodies with life in this world are also one of His energies. They are like sparks of fire whose potency appears to manifest differently depending on the wood they ignite. Srila Prabhupada writes: “As stated in the previous verse, fire, flame, smoke and firewood are combined together. Here the living entity, the material elements and the Supreme Personality of Godhead are combined together. The exact position of the living entities is just like that of the sparks of a fire; they are part and parcel. The material energy is compared to the smoke. The fire is also part and parcel of the Supreme Lord.” (Bhag. [3.28.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/28.41), purport)

The yogi thus realizes that the Lord, not His illusory energy, is both the cause and effect of everything, and surrenders to Him to conquer maya’s insurmountable spell.

Kapiladeva concludes that the Lord has an acintya-bhedabheda relationship with all existence. This is true Brahman realization; it is a oneness that inspires, not prohibits, the soul’s activity. Srila Prabhupada explains this in his purport to text 44: “After Brahman realization, one can engage in the activities of Brahman. As long as one is not self-realized, he engages in activities based on false identification with the body. When one is situated in his real self, then the activities of Brahman realization begin. The Mayavadi philosophers say that after Brahman realization, all activities stop, but that is not actually so. If the soul is so active in its abnormal condition, existing under the covering of matter, how can one deny its activity when free?... It may be said that the activities of Brahman realization are different from those of conditional life, but that does not stop activity. This is indicated in Bhagavad-gita ([18.54](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.54)): after one realizes oneself to be Brahman, devotional service begins. Mad'bhaktim labhate param: after Brahman realization, one can engage in the devotional service of the Lord. Therefore devotional service of the Lord is activity in Brahman realization.” And in the same purport: This realization “is possible, by the grace of the Lord, when God reveals Himself to the surrendered soul.”

Thus the perfected yogi renounces all mundane activity to actively serve Krsna with devotion on the spiritual, Brahman platform. Kapila Muni has now completed his response to Devahuti’s question about the process of forever separating the soul from matter.

## Chapter 29 - Explanation of Devotional Service by Lord Kapila

## Texts 1-5: Devahuti’s Further Questions

After hearing Kapila Muni’s words, Devahuti asks her divine son further questions: You have scientifically described the symptoms of the total material nature and the characteristics of spirit according to Sankhya philosophy. Now please explain the path of devotional service, which is the ultimate end of all philosophical systems. Please also describe the path of birth and death, because “by hearing of such calamities we may become detached from the activities of this material world.” (Bhag. [3.29.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.3)) Devahuti then asks Kapila Muni to describe eternal time, which is a representation of His form and by whose influence people perform pious activities. Thus Devahuti desires that her son’s words illuminate the darkened, ignorant lives of those struggling with the “pleasant” and “unpleasant” karma of their material existence.

## Texts 6-14: Kapila Muni’s Description of Devotional Service

Pleased with His glorious mother’s compassion for others, Kapila Muni also becomes filled with compassion. He begins: “O noble lady, there are multifarious paths of devotional service in terms of the different qualities of the executor.” (Bhag. [3.29.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.7))

In Bhagavatam [3.29.8-10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.8), Kapila Muni describes devotional service rendered in each of the three modes of nature. In texts 11 and 12 He describes devotional service transcendental to the modes. Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 10 presents an overview of devotional service under the modes of nature: “Devotional service in the modes of ignorance, passion and goodness can be divided into eighty-one categories. There are different devotional activities, such as hearing, chanting, remembering, worshiping, offering prayer, rendering service and surrendering everything, and each of them can be divided into three qualitative categories. There is hearing in the mode of passion, in the mode of ignorance and in the mode of goodness. Similarly, there is chanting in the mode of ignorance, passion and goodness, etc. Three multiplied by nine equals twenty-seven, and when again multiplied by three it becomes eighty-one. One has to transcend all such mixed materialistic devotional service in order to reach the standard of pure devotional service...”

First, Kapila Muni defines devotional service performed by one in ignorance: “Devotional service executed by a person who is envious, proud, violent and angry, and who is a separatist, is considered to be in the mode of darkness.” (Bhag. [3.29.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.8)) Srila Prabhupada writes: “One who approaches the Supreme Lord to render devotional service, but who is proud of his personality, envious of others or vengeful, is in the mode of anger. He thinks that he is the best devotee. Devotional service executed in this way is not pure; it is mixed and is of the lowest grade, tamasah. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura advises that a Vaisnava who is not of good character should be avoided. A Vaisnava is one who has taken the Supreme Personality of Godhead as the ultimate goal of life, but if one is not pure and still has motives, then he is not a Vaisnava of the first order of good character. One may offer his respects to such a Vaisnava because he has accepted the Supreme Lord as the ultimate goal of life, but one should not keep company with a Vaisnava who is in the mode of ignorance.” (Bhag. [3.29.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.8), purport)

Devotional service in passion: “The worship of Deities in the temple by a separatist, with a motive for material enjoyment, fame and opulence, is devotion in the mode of passion.” (Bhag. [3.29.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.9)) Srila Prabhupada defines “separatist” in his purport: “A separatist is one who sees his interest as separate from that of the Supreme Lord. Mixed devotees, or devotees in the modes of passion and ignorance, think that the interest of the Supreme Lord is supplying the orders of the devotee; the interest of such devotees is to draw from the Lord as much as possible for their sense gratification. This is the separatist mentality. Actually, pure devotion is explained in the previous chapter: the mind of the Supreme Lord and the mind of the devotee should be dovetailed. A devotee should not wish anything but to execute the desire of the Supreme. That is oneness. When the devotee has an interest or will different from the interest of the Supreme Lord, his mentality is that of a separatist. When the so-called devotee desires material enjoyment, without reference to the interest of the Supreme Lord, or he wants to become famous or opulent by utilizing the mercy or grace of the Supreme Lord, he is in the mode of passion.” (Bhag. [3.29.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.9), purport)

Devotional service in goodness: “When a devotee worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead and offers the results of his activities in order to free himself from the inebrieties of fruitive activities, his devotion is in the mode of goodness.” (Bhag. [3.29.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.10)) Prabhupada writes: “The four asramas and four varnas act for some benefit in accordance with their personal interests. Therefore such activities are in the mode of goodness; they cannot be counted in the category of pure devotion. Pure devotional service as described by Rupa Gosvami is free from all material desires. Anyabhilasita-sunyam. There can be no excuse for personal or material interest.” (Bhag. [3.29.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.10), purport)

Kapila Muni has described devotees practicing devotional service in the three modes of material nature as “separatists.” He has termed practitoners in ignorance as bhinna-drg bhavam (Bhag. [3.29.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.8)) and practitioners in both passion and ignorance as prthag-bhavah (Bhag. [3.29.9-10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.9)). Both terms indicate “separatists,” those who maintain interests separate from the Lord’s interests. “Separate interest” indicates the presence of false ego, a consciousness that remains situated in the mahat-tattva, the material world. The cure for false ego is surrender, a return to the soul’s natural consciousness as Krsna’s loving servant. Thereafter, beginning in texts 11-12, Kapila Muni defines pure devotional service, service free from false ego and the binding ropes of the three modes of material nature: “The manifestation of unadulterated devotional service is exhibited when one’s mind is at once attracted to hearing the transcendental name and qualities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is residing in everyone’s heart. Just as the water of the Ganges flows naturally down towards the ocean, such devotional ecstasy, uninterrupted by any material condition, flows towards the Supreme Lord.” (Bhag. [3.29.11-12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.11))From excerpts to Srila Prabhupada’s purports to texts 11-13:

**The word ahaituki means “without reason.” A pure devotee does not render loving service to the Personality of Godhead for any cause or for any benefit, material or spiritual. This is the first symptom of unalloyed devotion. . . . Avyavahita means “without cessation.” A pure devotee must engage in the service of the Lord twenty-four hours a day, without cessation; his life is so molded that at every minute and every second he engages in some sort of devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Another meaning of the word avyavahita is that the interest of the devotee and the interest of the Supreme Lord are on the same level. The devotee has no interest but to fulfill the transcendental desire of the Supreme Lord. Such spontaneous service unto the Supreme Lord is transcendental and is never contaminated by the material modes of nature. These are the symptoms of pure devotional service, which is free from all contamination of material nature. (Bhag.** [**3.29.11-12**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.11)**, purport)**

**Lord Caitanya teaches us how to execute pure devotional service out of spontaneous love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In the Siksastaka, He prays to the Lord: “O Lord, I do not wish to gain from You any wealth, nor do I wish to have a beautiful wife, nor do I wish to have many followers. All I want from You is that in life after life I may remain a pure devotee at Your lotus feet.” There is a similarity between the prayers of Lord Caitanya and the statements of Srimad-Bhagavatam. Lord Caitanya prays, “in life after life,” indicating that a devotee does not even desire the cessation of birth and death. The yogis and empiric philosophers desire cessation of the process of birth and death, but a devotee is satisfied to remain even in this material world and execute devotional service. (Bhag.** [**3.29.13**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.13)**, purport)**

## Texts 15-18: Devotional Practices

Kapila next describes how devotional service is practiced: Regardless of the nature of one’s duties, one should perform them regularly. As one works, one should remain free from desires for material profit and think only of Krsna’s pleasure. Srila Prabhupada encourages the devotees in his purport to text 15 as he guides them to serve Krsna from whatever position fate has awarded them: “Everyone’s prescribed duty is glorious if it is performed in devotional service of the Lord, without desire for profit. Such loving service must be performed without reason, without impediment, and spontaneously. Krsna is lovable, and one has to serve Him in whatever capacity one can. That is pure devotional service.”

Kapila continues: Devotees should regularly worship the deity and see every living entity as spiritual. “The pure devotee should execute devotional service by giving the greatest respect to the spiritual master and the acaryas. He should be compassionate to the poor and make friendship with persons who are his equals, but all his activities should be executed under regulation and with control of the senses. A devotee should always try to hear about spiritual matters and should always utilize his time in chanting the holy name of the Lord. His behavior should always be straightforward and simple, and although he is not envious but friendly to everyone, he should avoid the company of persons who are not spiritually advanced.” (Bhag. [3.29.17-18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.17))

Prabhupada’s purports to texts 16-18 stress many of these essential practices. Nine excerpts have been selected and presented here:

Deity worship: “An advanced devotee accepts the Deity in the temple as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He does not see any difference between the original form of the Lord and the statue, or area form of the Lord, in the temple. This is the vision of a devotee whose devotional service is in the highest stage of bhava, or love of Godhead, whereas a neophyte’s worship in the temple is a matter of routine duty.” (Bhag. [3.29.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.16), purport)

Vaisnava association: “We should befriend and offer special respect to persons who are developed in Krsna consciousness. Other living entities are undoubtedly part and parcel of the Supreme Lord, but because their consciousness is still covered and not developed in Krsna consciousness, we should renounce their association. It is said by Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura that even if one is a Vaisnava, if he is not of good character his company should be avoided, although he may be offered the respect of a Vaisnava. Anyone who accepts Visnu as the Supreme Personality of Godhead is accepted as a Vaisnava, but a Vaisnava is expected to develop all the good qualities of the demigods.” (Bhag. [3.29.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.16), purport)

Patience and determination: “The exact meaning of the word sattvena is given by Sridhara Svami as being synonymous with dhairyena, or patience. One must perform devotional service with great patience. One should not give up the execution of devotional service because one or two attempts have not been successful. One must continue. Sri Rupa Gosvami also confirms that one should be very enthusiastic and execute devotional service with patience and confidence. Patience is necessary for developing the confidence that ‘Krsna will certainly accept me because I am engaging in devotional service.’ One has only to execute service according to the rules and regulations to insure success.” (Bhag. [3.29.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.16), purport)

Compassion for the poor: “A man may be very rich materially, but if he is not Krsna conscious, he is considered poor. On the other hand, many acaryas, such as Rupa Gosvami and Sanatana Gosvami, used to live beneath trees every night. Superficially it appeared that they were poverty-stricken, but from their writings we can understand that in spiritual life they were the richest personalities. A devotee shows compassion to those poor souls who are wanting in spiritual knowledge by enlightening them in order to elevate them to Krsna consciousness. That is one of the duties of a devotee.” (Bhag. [3.29.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.17), purport)

Respecting holy teachers: “Acaryopasanam: one should worship an acarya, a spiritual master who knows things as they are. The spiritual master must be in the disciplic succession from Krsna. The predecessors of the spiritual master are his spiritual master, his grand spiritual master, his great-grand spiritual master and so on, who form the disciplic succession of acaryas. It is recommended herewith that all the acaryas be given the highest respect.” (Bhag. [3.29.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.17), purport)

Friendship among devotees: “He should also make friendship with persons who are on an equal level with himself or who have the same understanding that he does. For a devotee, there is no point in making friendships with ordinary persons; he should make friendship with other devotees so that by discussing among themselves, they may elevate one another on the path of spiritual understanding. This is called ista-gosthi.

“In Bhagavad-gita there is reference to bodhayantah parasparam, ‘discussing among themselves.’ Generally pure devotees utilize their valuable time in chanting and discussing various activities of Lord Krsna or Lord Caitanya amongst themselves. There are innumerable books, such as the Puranas, Mahabharata, Bhagavatam, Bhagavad-gita and Upanisads, which contain countless subjects for discussion among two devotees or more. Friendship should be cemented between persons with mutual interests and understanding. Such persons are said to be svajdti, ‘of the same caste.’” (Bhag. [3.29.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.17), purport)

Chanting Hare Krsna: “It is especially mentioned here . . . one should chant the holy names of the Lord—Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare—either individually or with others. Lord Caitanya has given special stress to chanting of these holy names of the Lord as the basic principle of spiritual advancement.” (Bhag. [3.29.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.18), purport)

Avoiding bad association: “Lord Caitanya advised, asat-sanga-tyaga: one should avoid persons who are attached to the temporary. Asat is one who is too materially attached, who is not a devotee of the Lord and who is too attached to women or enjoyable material things. Such a person, according to Vaisnava philosophy, is a persona non grata." (Bhag. [3.29.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.18), purport)

Humility: “A devotee should not be proud of his acquisitions. The symptoms of a devotee are meekness and humility. Although spiritually very advanced, he will always remain meek and humble, as Kaviraja Gosvami and all the other Vaisnavas have taught us by personal example. Caitanya Mahaprabhu taught that one should be humbler than the grass on the street and more tolerant than the tree. One should not be proud or falsely puffed up. In this way one will surely advance in spiritual life.” (Bhag. [3.29.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.18), purport)

## Texts 19-20: The Results of Performing These Devotional Practices

Kapila Muni states, “When one is fully qualified with all these transcendental attributes and his consciousness is thus completely purified, he is immediately attracted simply by hearing My name or hearing of My transcendental quality. As the chariot of air carries an aroma from its source and immediately catches the sense of smell, similarly, one who constantly engages in devotional service, in Krsna consciousness, can catch the Supreme Soul, who is equally present everywhere.” (Bhag. [3.29.19-20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.19))

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 20 is sweet, describing how a qualified devotee captures Krsna: “As a breeze carrying a pleasant fragrance from a garden of flowers at once captures the organ of smell, so one’s consciousness, saturated with devotion, can at once capture the transcendental existence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who, in His Paramatma feature, is present everywhere, even in the heart of every living being.” A nondevotee fails to see God anywhere; a devotee sees Krsna everywhere because his consciousness is saturated with devotion.

## Texts 21-27: A Devotee’s Dealings with Others

The Lord is present in everything that exists, including each living entity’s heart. Kapila Muni thus next stresses the importance of respecting everything in existence. How? Srila Prabhupada provides guidance: “A devotee should try to understand everything in relationship with Krsna and try to serve everything in that spirit. To serve everything means to engage everything in the service of Krsna. If a person is innocent and does not know his relationship with Krsna, an advanced devotee should try to engage him in the service of Krsna. One who is advanced in Krsna consciousness can engage not only the living being but everything in the service of Krsna.” (Bhag. [3.29.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.21), purport) One should respect all living entities regardless of their bodily designation simply because they are all parts of the Lord and He is present in their hearts as the indwelling Supersoul. Srila Prabhupada expands Kapiladeva’s instructions in this regard: “\[A\] devotee should not ignore any living entity. The devotee must know that in every living entity, however insignificant he may be, even in an ant, God is present, and therefore every living entity should be kindly treated and should not be subjected to any violence. In modem civilized society, slaughterhouses are regularly maintained and supported by a certain type of religious principle. But without knowledge of the presence of God in every living entity, any so-called advancement of human civilization, either spiritual or material, is to be understood as being in the mode of ignorance.” (Bhag. [3.29.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.22), purport)

Kapila Muni thus criticizes those who worship the deity but who simultaneously neglect and disrespect the Lord in other living entities’ hearts. Such disrespect is symptomatic of devotees on the lowest stage of devotion, of prakrta-bhaktas. Even if one performs deity worship according to the rules and regulations, Krsna will nevertheless be displeased if one fails to perceive His presence in other living entities. After all, the real purpose of deity worship is to exhibit one’s love for the Lord—a love that should extend to His parts and parcels. Srila Prabhupada writes: “The offerings themselves are secondary.... Real love and devotion is accepted by the Lord. Many valuable foodstuffs may be presented to a person, but if the person is not hungry, all such offerings are useless for him. Similarly, we may offer many valuable items to the Deity, but if we have no real sense of devotion and no real sense of the Lord’s presence everywhere, then we are lacking in devotional service; in such a state of ignorance, we cannot offer anything acceptable to the Lord.” (Bhag. [3.29.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.24), purport)

One should perform his prescribed duties, Kapila Muni instructs, while worshiping the deity as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He should sustain that worship until he realizes the Lord’s presence in his own heart as well as in the hearts of all others. A devotee should not be satisfied simply to have properly discharged his duties. Perhaps one will have thought such dutifulness is sufficient after reading Kapila’s instruction in text 15: “A devotee must execute his prescribed duties, which are glorious, without material profit. Without excessive violence, one should regularly perform one’s devotional activities.” However, “he must,” as Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 25, “realize his relationship and the relationship of all other living entities with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. If he does not understand this, then even though he discharges his prescribed duties properly, it is to be understood that he is simply laboring without profit.”

## Texts 28-33: Varieties of Living Entities

Kapila Muni has spoken strongly in the previous section about seeing the Supersoul in the heart of every living entity and thus seeing their commonality, their oneness: “Therefore, through charitable gifts and attention, as well as through friendly behavior and by viewing all to be alike, one should propitiate Me, who abide in all creatures as their very Self.” (Bhag. [3.29.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.27)) Indeed, He warns: “As the blazing fire of death, I cause great fear to whoever makes the least discrimination between himself and other living entities because of a differential outlook.” (Bhag. [3.29.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.26)) Yet this principle, important as it is, needs to be applied with a practical spirit. To confirm and assist one’s practical actions as one views all living entities with equality, Kapila Muni now describes the progression of species. Although every living entity from the ant to the tiger to the prostitute to the pure devotee is a soul with Krsna in its heart, one should not indiscriminately embrace every living being. Therefore, understanding both the spiritual essence of other beings and how to treat them while working practically in this world is vital to spiritual and material development.

Prabhupada already noted this point in his purport to text 16: Although devotees see all living entities on the level of spiritual existence, they are not interested in associating with everyone. Simply because a tiger is part and parcel of the Supreme Lord does not mean that we embrace it because of its spiritual relationship with the Supreme Lord. Prabhupada expands the point fully in his purport to text 28:

**In the previous verse it was explained that living entities should be honored by charitable gifts and friendly behavior, and in this verse and in the following verses, the description of different grades of living entities is given so that one can know when to behave friendly and when to give charity. For example, a tiger is a living entity, part and parcel of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and the Supreme Lord is living in the heart of the tiger as Supersoul. But does this mean that we have to treat the tiger in a friendly manner? Certainly not. We have to treat him differently, giving him charity in the form of prasada. The many saintly persons in the jungles do not treat the tigers in a friendly way, but they supply prasada foodstuffs to them. The tigers come, take the food and go away, just as a dog does. According to the Vedic system, a dog is not allowed to enter the house. Because of their uncleanliness, cats and dogs are not allowed within the apartment of a gentleman, but are so trained that they stand outside. The compassionate householder will supply prasada to the dogs and cats, who eat outside and then go away. We must treat the lower living entities compassionately, but this does not mean that we have to treat them in the same way we treat other human beings. The feeling of equality must be there, but the treatment should be discriminating. Just how discrimination should be maintained is given in the following six verses concerning the different grades of living conditions.**

Thus Kapila Muni classifies living beings into an ascending set of categories: inanimate objects, living entities displaying life symptoms, and animals with increasing stages of developed consciousness. Better than animals are human beings, and the best of all human beings are the pure Vaisnava brahmanas who execute devotional service without expectation of reward. “I do not find a greater person than he who has no interest outside of Mine,” Kapila Muni concludes in text 33, “and who therefore engages and dedicates all his activities and all his life—everything—unto Me without cessation.” Association with such a soul is best of all.

## Texts 34-36: Kapila Muni’s Conclusion

Pure devotees act without self-interest and only to serve Krsna. Because they are firmly convinced that the Supreme Lord is in everyone’s heart, they respect all living entities. Those who practice bhakti' yoga as Kapila Muni has described it will achieve the Lord’s supreme abode by the power of their service.

And who is that Supreme Lord one should approach and serve? Kapila Muni describes Him: “This purusa whom the individual soul must approach is the eternal form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is known as Brahman and Paramatma. He is the transcendental chief personality, and His activities are all spiritual.” (Bhag. [3.29.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.36)) Thus Kapila Muni confirms that bhakti is the heart of Sankhya-yoga, and that the goal of bhakti is to approach, love, and serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

Devahuti inquired about bhakti-yoga at the beginning of Chapter Twenty-nine and Kapila Muni has now completed His response. She also inquired about time and how it inspires a soul to perform either fruitive or pious activities. She asked these questions specifically to awaken detachment, which is essential to the practice of Sankhya-yoga (Bhag. [3.26.72](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/26.72)). She thus asked her son in Bhagavatam [3.29.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.3): “My dear Lord, please also describe in detail, both for me and for people in general, the continual process of birth and death, for by hearing of such calamities we may become detached from the activities of the material world.” In texts 37-45 Kapila Muni begins to answer his mother’s question from Bhagavatam [3.29.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.4) about the Lord’s time potency by describing the devastating effects of unstoppable time.

To answer her question from text 3 of the same chapter about fruitive actions, which cause the calamity of repeated birth and death, Kapila Muni will speak Chapters Thirty and Thirty-one. He will then return to complete his answer to Devahuti’s question in text 4, which will also complete His teachings, by describing in Chapter Thirty-three the effects of materially pious, sastric action.

## Dialogue Seven - Lord Kapila Concludes His Instructions

## Chapter 29 (continued) - Explanation of Devotional Service by Lord Kapila

## Texts 37-45: The Devastating Effect of Time

In Bhagavatam [3.29.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.2), Devahuti asked Kapila Muni to describe bhaktiyoga in detail. In Bhagavatam [3.29.5-36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.5), Kapila Muni responded. Devahuti had also requested (Bhag. [3.29.3-4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.3)) that He explain the effects of “eternal time” and “the continual process of birth and death.” Kapila Muni will now respond so powerfully that it will awaken renunciation in our heart.

Time is an energy of the Supersoul. It forces matter to change continuously. If we see time as separate from the Lord, we become afraid, because time crushes everything in the material realm. Time is actually “the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the enjoyer of all sacrifices . . . the master of all masters.” (Bhag. [3.29.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.38)) Time is nondifferent from the Lord, who enters everyone’s heart as the neutral witness. “. . . He is the support of everyone, and He causes every being to be annihilated by another. No one is dear to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, nor is anyone His enemy or friend. But He gives inspiration to those who have not forgotten Him and destroys those who have.” (Bhag. [3.29.38-39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.38))

Kapila has spoken of truths about which most people are already aware: Time is unstoppable, an energy of the Supersoul, and acts neutrally, destroying all without bias.

Time annihilates everything in the material realm. Still, a conditioned soul both laments and becomes terror-stricken when these truths penetrate his heart. After all, he has conferred on ever-shifting matter his natural soul-bom longing for a tangible, secure, concrete reality. Yet this unstoppable, all-crushing force, time, is simply one of Krsna’s energies.

Knowing this awards a faithful devotee both peace and security. Indeed, trusting all-powerful, dear Krsna is what Prabhupada calls the “peace formula”: “A person in full consciousness of Me, knowing Me to be the ultimate beneficiary of all sacrifices and austerities, the Supreme Lord of all planets and demigods, and the benefactor and well-wisher of all living entities, attains peace from the pangs of material miseries.” (Bg. [5.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/5.29))

Kapila Muni assures us that Krsna, the ultimate controller, is at work behind unstoppable time. In the material and spiritual realms, everything is under the Lord’s control. The rain falls and the sun shines out of fear of Him; trees grow tall and the oceans do not flood the earth out of fear of Him; fire gives off heat and the earth remains in its orbit out of fear of Him. Time is eternal; it has neither beginning nor end. It carries all living entities into existence and moves the creation forward. Ultimately, time dissolves the universe. Srila Prabhupada is clear in his purport to text 45: “No one can live within this material world eternally. The phenomenal world is created, maintained and destroyed by the finger signal of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore a devotee does not desire anything in this material world. A devotee desires only to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This servitude exists eternally; the Lord exists eternally, His servitor exists eternally, and the service exists eternally.”

Kapila Muni prods His devotees to leave this temporary world for the eternal, spiritual realm. He continues to prod them in the next chapter.

## Chapter 30 - Description of Adverse Fruitive Activities

## Texts 1-5: Time’s Deluding Effect

Lord Kapila further explains the ramifications of time’s actions: Although time and its consequences are powerful and obvious, consciously or unconsciously we seem to choose to remain blind to its devastating effects. “Whatever is produced by the materialist with great pain and labor for so-called happiness, the Supreme Personality, as the time factor, destroys, and for this reason the conditioned soul laments. The misguided materialist does not know that his very body is impermanent and that the attractions of home, land and wealth, which are in relationship to that body, are also temporary. Out of ignorance only, he thinks that everything is permanent.” (Bhag. [3.30.2-3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.2)) Kapila Muni provides a metaphor in text 1: As clouds remain unaware of the wind that pushes them across the sky, a conditioned soul remains unaware that it is the time factor mixed with his karma, not his free choice, that determines his actions. Srila Prabhupada notes in his purport that “unfortunately, those who are not in Krsna consciousness are carried away by the strong power of time without their knowledge, as clouds are carried by the wind.”

Kapila Muni is speaking such strong words to Devahuti to inspire detachment because the materially attached are unable to become attached to Krsna’s lotus feet. Prahlada Maharaja makes the same point: “Because of their uncontrolled senses, persons too addicted to materialistic life make progress toward hellish conditions and repeatedly chew that which has already been chewed. Their inclinations toward Krsna are never aroused, either by the instructions of others, by their own efforts, or by a combination of both.” (Bhag. [7.5.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/5.30)) Still, whether or not one is attached to matter, the Lord in His form as time will crush and destroy everything material one has accumulated by his hard work and good fortune. The material world is truly a holocaust. Nothing survives—neither the king nor his kingdom.

The Lord’s time energy combines with maya to cause one to mistake the temporary for the permanent. One then foolishly becomes overwhelmed by and entangled in the temporary. Srila Prabhupada writes: “\[O\]ut of illusion only does the materialist accept his home, his land and his money as permanent. Out of this illusion, the family life, national life and economic development, which are very important factors in modem civilization, have grown. A Krsna conscious person knows that this economic development of human society is but temporary illusion.” (Bhag. [3.30.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.3), purport)

In his purport to text 2, Srila Prabhupada summarizes the crushing effect of time: “The main function of the time factor, which is a representative of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is to destroy everything. The materialists, in material consciousness, are engaged in producing so many things in the name of economic development. They think that by advancing in satisfying the material needs of man they will be happy, but they forget that everything they have produced will be destroyed in due course of time. From history we can see that there were many powerful empires on the surface of the globe that were constructed with great pain and great perseverance, but in due course of time they have all been destroyed. Still the foolish materialists cannot understand that they are simply wasting time in producing material necessities, which are destined to be vanquished in due course of time.”

Kapila Muni next explains that a soul relishes the specific type of happiness offered by his body, regardless of the quality of that body or even the species he inhabits. A human, for example, attempts to obtain pleasure by means suitable to his culture and status. An ant’s attempt parallels the human experience, although it lives in a vastly different body. Every embodied soul identifies with the body it inhabits and endeavors to maintain happiness. Deluded by maya, each entity aims both to be satisfied and to avoid casting off its body. Even the residents of hell delight in the specific pleasures of that realm. That one experiences satisfaction in any species even though one’s life is objectively abominable is proof that he is illusioned. In the material world, the illusion of identifying with the body is unassailable.

One should remember, however, that it is not the objects in this world that are maya. Rather, illusion bewitches the conditioned souls into viewing temporary objects both as if they were permanent and as if they existed simply for their pleasure. In addition, due to maya’s potent spell, the conditioned souls imagine that the objects themselves bring happiness. Souls in maya’s kingdom therefore continue their frustrating attempts to combine their senses with the sense objects that compel them. Regardless of the specific nature of particular bodies, all embodied souls remain addicted to petty, self-centered “pleasure.”

Srila Prabhupada describes the mystifying effect of maya: “Lord Krsna is personally canvassing, ‘Give up everything in this material world. Come to Me, and I shall give you all protection,’ but we are not agreeable. We think, ‘We are quite all right. Why should we surrender unto Krsna and go back to His kingdom?’ This is called illusion, or maya. Everyone is satisfied with his standard of living, however abominable it may be.” (Bhag. [3.30.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.5), purport) In his purport to text 4, Srila Prabhupada also speaks on this theme: “In any condition of life, the materialistic person or animal will be satisfied because his knowledge is covered by the influence of maya. In the lower grade or lower species of life, the development of consciousness is so poor that one cannot understand whether he is happy or distressed. This is called avaranatmika. Even a hog, who lives by eating stool, finds himself happy, although a person in a higher mode of life sees that the hog is eating stool. How abominable that life is!”

## Texts 6-19: Time As Portrayed in the Life of an Illusioned Human

Kapila Muni continues to describe the imperceptible effects of time as it acts to move a human from one stage of life to the next: Souls in human bodies tend to think themselves “quite perfect” because they possess “deep-rooted attraction for body, wife, home, children, animals, wealth and friends.” (Bhag. [3.30.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.6)) Just hearing Kapila’s description of materialistic human life fills one with fear.

He continues: The materialistic householder bums with anxiety bom of his attachment to his family and the opposite sex. He experiences the anxiety that accompanies his vain attempts to counteract misery as well and his unending attempt to collect sufficient money. “The attached householder remains in his family life, which is full of diplomacy and politics. Always spreading miseries and controlled by acts of sense gratification, he acts just to counteract the reactions of all his miseries, and if he can successfully counteract such miseries, he thinks that he is happy.” (Bhag. [3.30.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.9))

Two short sentences in Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 7 work to undermine the “nuclear family”—husband, wife, and children—as an unquestionable central principle of civilization: “As we change bodies, our family relationships also change. Sometimes we are in a family of human beings, sometimes in a family of demigods, sometimes a family of cats, or sometimes a family of dogs.” And in three sentences in his purport to text 9, he challenges the core of capitalism: “Human society competes nationally or individually, and in the attempt to be successful the entire human society becomes full of diplomacy. We should always remember that in spite of all diplomacy and all intelligence in the struggle for our existence, everything will end in a second by the supreme will. Therefore, all our attempts to become happy in this material world are simply a delusion offered by maya.”

Yet despite all endeavors, Kapiladeva explains, a materialist remains unable to satisfy his family members. He grieves his failure deeply and suffers reversals at work. He is disrespected by others and tortured by greed. He “tries again and again to improve himself, but when he is baffled in all attempts and is ruined, he accepts money from others because of excessive greed.” (Bhag. [3.30.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.11)) Gradually he loses his beauty and becomes deformed and invalid in his old age. “Thus he remains at home just like a pet dog and eats whatever is so negligently given to him. Afflicted with many illnesses, such as dyspepsia and loss of appetite, he eats only very small morsels of food, and he becomes an invalid, who cannot work any more.” (Bhag. [3.30.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.15)) Thus he prepares to meet death. In his old age, his throat rattles and his lungs are congested with mucus. He can breathe only with difficulty. “In this way he comes under the clutches of death and lies down, surrounded by lamenting friends and relatives, and although he wants to speak with them, he no longer can because he is under the control of time.” (Bhag. [3.30.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.17)) Soon he will be forced to die and leave his family members behind.

In his purport to text 13 Srila Prabhupada offers the practical advice to seek shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead: “It is judicious, therefore, to give up family attachment before one attains old age and take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. One should employ himself in the Lord’s service so that the Supreme Lord can take charge of him, and he will not be neglected by his so-called kinsmen.” Prabhupada takes the point further in his purport to text 14: “After preparing himself fully, he should become a sannyasi to distribute the knowledge of spiritual life to each and every home.”

“Thus the man, who engaged with uncontrolled senses in maintaining a family, dies in great grief, seeing his relatives crying. He dies most pathetically, in great pain and without consciousness. At death, he sees the messengers of the lord of death come before him, their eyes full of wrath, and in great fear he passes stool and urine.” (Bhag. [3.30.18-19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.18)) Srila Prabhupada’s purports to these texts are unsentimental and stark: “For formality’s sake, when a man is lying on his deathbed, his relatives come to him, and sometimes they cry very loudly, addressing the dying man: ‘Oh, my father!’ ‘Oh, my friend!’ or ‘Oh, my husband!’ In that pitiable condition the dying man wants to speak with them and instruct them of his desires, but because he is fully under the control of the time factor, death, he cannot express himself, and that causes him inconceivable pain. He is already in a painful condition because of disease, and his glands and throat are choked up with mucus. He is already in a very difficult position, and when he is addressed by his relatives in that way, his grief increases.” (Bhag. [3.30.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.17), purport)

And: “Sometimes a dying man entrusts the family affairs to either his son or some relative, saying, ‘I am going. Please look after the family.’ He does not know where he is going, but even at the time of death he is anxious about how his family will be maintained. Sometimes it is seen that a dying man requests the physician to increase his life at least for a few years so that the family maintenance plan which he has begun can be completed. These are the material diseases of the conditioned soul. He completely forgets his real engagement—to become Krsna conscious—and is always serious about planning to maintain his family, although he changes families one after another.” (Bhag. [3.30.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.18), purport)

## Texts 20-34: Beyond Death to Hell and Rebirth

Kapila Muni now describes a materialist’s after-death experience, and there are no harps, fluffy clouds, or soothing white lights: “As a criminal is arrested for punishment by the constables of the state, a person engaged in criminal sense gratification is similarly arrested by the Yamadutas, who bind him by the neck with strong rope and cover his subtle body so that he may undergo severe punishment. While carried by the constables of Yamaraja, he is overwhelmed and trembles in their hands. While passing on the road he is bitten by dogs, and he can remember the sinful activities of his life. He is thus terribly distressed.” (Bhag. [3.30.20-21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.20)) Arrested for his criminality—his unrestricted sense gratification—he is overwhelmed and begins to tremble. He receives horrendous punishments. He is tired and thirsty, he falls unconscious, and he is whipped, burnt, bitten, and tormented by serpents and scorpions. He is an unwilling captive and thus suffers hell. “The money he acquired by envying other living entities is the passage money with which he leaves this world.” (Bhag. [3.30.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.31))

Srila Prabhupada explains the great and dangerous fault in contemporary life in his purport to text 30: “The mistake of modem civilization is that man does not believe in the next life. But whether he believes or not, the next life is there, and one has to suffer if one does not lead a responsible life in terms of the injunctions of authoritative scriptures like the Vedas and Puranas.” In his purport to text 31 he explains the results of maintaining one’s family with improperly earned money: “When a man earns money by unfair means and maintains his family and himself with that money, the money is enjoyed by many members of the family, but he alone goes to hell. A person who enjoys life by earning money or by envying another’s life, and who enjoys with family and friends, will have to enjoy alone the resultant sinful reactions accrued from such violent and illicit life. For example, if a man secures some money by killing someone and with that money maintains his family, those who enjoy the black money earned by him are also partially responsible and are also sent to hell, but he who is the leader is especially punished. The result of material enjoyment is that one takes with him the sinful reaction only, and not the money. The money he earned is left in this world, and he takes only the reaction.”Having considered only the welfare of his family and not worried about the honesty of his means of livelihood, a man leaves behind the wealth he has earned and takes only the pain-filled reactions accrued when performing dishonest deeds. Srila Prabhupada describes how a human being may maintain his family, yet be saved from sinful reaction:

**Maintaining one’s family is certainly the duty of a householder, but one should be eager to earn his livelihood by the prescribed method, as stated in the scriptures. In Bhagavad-gita it is described that the Lord has divided the social system into four classifications of castes, or varnas, according to quality and work. Apart from Bhagavad-gita, in every society a man is known according to his quality and work. For example, when a man is constructing wooden furniture, he is called a carpenter, and a man who works with an anvil and iron is called a blacksmith. Similarly, a man who is engaged in the medical or engineering fields has a particular duty and designation. All these human activities have been divided by the Supreme Lord into four varnas, namely brahmana, ksatriya, vaisya and sudra. In Bhagavad-gita and in other Vedic literatures, the specific duties of the brahmana, ksatriya, vaisya and sudra are mentioned.**

**One should work honestly according to his qualification. He should not earn his livelihood unfairly, by means for which he is not qualified. If a brahmana who works as a priest so that he may enlighten his followers with the spiritual way of life is not qualified as a priest, then he is cheating the public. One should not earn by such unfair means. The same is applicable to a ksatriya or to a vaisya. It is especially mentioned that the means of livelihood of those who are trying to advance in Krsna consciousness must be very fair and uncomplicated. Here it is mentioned that he who earns his livelihood by unfair means (kevalena) is sent to the darkest hellish region. Otherwise, if one maintains his family by prescribed methods and honest means, there is no objection to one’s being a family man. (Bhag.** [**3.30.33**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.33)**, purport)**

Kapila Muni further describes the soul’s progress: In due course, having “gone through all the miserable, hellish conditions”—their purpose being to train his subtle body to tolerate hellish sufferings of his next animal births—“and having passed in a regular order through the lowest forms of animal life prior to human birth, and having thus been purged of his sins, one is reborn again as a human being on this earth.” (Bhag. [3.30.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/30.34)) Srila Prabhupada explains: “Even if one is unable to attain complete Krsna consciousness in this life, he is guaranteed at least to take his next birth in a human family. He cannot be sent into a hellish condition. Krsna consciousness is the purest life, and it protects all human beings from gliding down to hell to take birth in a family of dogs or hogs.”

## Chapter 31 - Lord Kapila’s Instructions On the Movements of the Living Entity

## Texts 1-10: The Soul Further Suffers As a Human Embryo

For the most part, Srimad-Bhagavatam does not encourage bhakti by engendering fear. The point is not to pursue devotional service because one wants to avoid the “fire and brimstone” of hell. Still, a little fear can help one cut through the material attachments that hinder one from becoming attached to Krsna. Even if a devotee’s wealth of attachment to Krsna already pales his material attachment, a pinch of fear infused in his devotional service may add wisdom to his dealings with the powerful material energy. Sukadeva Gosvami confirms the need for such caution even for advanced devotees. In Bhagavatam [5.6.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/6.1) Maharaja Pariksit asks Sukadeva why Rsabhadeva neglected to use his mystic powers. Sukadeva replies in Bhagavatam [5.6.2-3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/6.2): “ . . . after capturing animals, a cunning hunter does not put faith in them, for they might run away. Similarly, those who are advanced in spiritual life do not put faith in the mind. Indeed, they always remain vigilant and watch the mind’s action. All the learned scholars have given their opinion. The mind is by nature very restless, and one should not make friends with it. If we place full confidence in the mind, it may cheat us at any moment.”

One should take care in his dealings with the material energy, because the stakes are so high. It may take one thousands of births to expunge reactions from a moment of sensory happiness. For example, if one eats cow’s flesh, it will yield a severe karmic reaction: One will have to take one animal birth for each hair on the cow’s body. A person who eats cow’s flesh regularly and who lives to the age of seventy may have accumulated millions of years worth of karmic debt. Perhaps he will have to begin as a worm and know only how to live deep in the moist earth. Perhaps he will experience birth as a weed, in which he will seek only sunlight, water, and the drive to reproduce his species. Perhaps he will take birth as a jackal, seeking only the taste of blood. Does the soul ever escape? Does he benefit from his ordeal? After many births of such untold suffering, the Supersoul finally sanctions another human body.

Kapila Muni now explains the continuation of the cycle: “Under the supervision of the Supreme Lord and according to the result of his work, the living entity, the soul, is made to enter into the womb of a woman through the particle of male semen to assume a particular type of body.” (Bhag. [3.31.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.1)) The child lies helpless in the womb as his body develops. He is surrounded by foul stool and urine, bitten by worms, and experiencing agony. He falls unconscious because of the pain. When his mother eats foods that are overly bitter, pungent, spicy, salty, or sour, they burn his sensitive skin, causing him incessant, intolerable pain. If fortunate, “he can remember all the troubles of his past one hundred births, and he grieves wretchedly.” (Bhag. [3.31.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.9))

In his purport to text 9, Srila Prabhupada advises his readers to become determined to cross the ocean of material ignorance: “After birth the child may forget about the difficulties of his past lives, but when we are grown up we can at least understand the grievous tortures undergone at birth and death by reading the authorized scriptures like Srimad-Bhagavatam. If we do not believe in the scriptures, that is a different question, but if we have faith in the authority of such descriptions, then we must prepare for our freedom in the next life; that is possible in this human form of life. One who does not take heed of these indications of suffering in human existence is said to be undoubtedly committing suicide. It is said that this human form of life is the only means for crossing over the nescience of maya, or material existence. We have a very efficient boat in this human form of body, and there is a very expert captain, the spiritual master; the scriptural injunctions are like favorable winds. If we do not cross over the ocean of the nescience of material existence in spite of all these facilities, then certainly we are all intentionally committing suicide.”

## Texts 11-21: The Prayers of a Soul Embodied in a Human Embryo

In this frightful, painful womb-bound condition, the soul, like a bird trapped in a cage, prayerfully folds his hands and appeals to the Lord. Srila Prabhupada addresses a doubt in his purport to text 18: “This prayer of the child in the womb may be questioned by some atheistic people. How can a child pray in such a nice way in the womb of his mother? Everything is possible by the grace of the Lord. The child is put into such a precarious condition externally, but internally he is the same, and the Lord is there. By the transcendental energy of the Lord, everything is possible.”

Kapila Muni describes to Devahuti the mood and words of a fearful yet fortunate soul begging the Supersoul for relief: “I take shelter of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who appears in His various eternal forms and walks on the surface of the world. I take shelter of Him only, because He can give me relief from all fear and from Him I have received this condition of life, which is just befitting my impious activities.” (Bhag. [3.31.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.12)) Able to perceive the Lord in his heart due to his repentant spirit, he understands that the Lord, although near, is nevertheless transcendental and beyond all suffering. He therefore seeks His shelter: “To Him I offer my respectful obeisances. I am separated from the Supreme Lord because of my being in this material body, which is made of five elements, and therefore my qualities and senses are being misused, although I am essentially spiritual. Because the Supreme Personality of Godhead is transcendental to material nature and the living entities, because He is devoid of such a material body, and because He is always glorious in His spiritual qualities, I offer my obeisances unto Him.” (Bhag. [3.31.13-14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.13))

Clearly, although the soul and the Supersoul are neighbors, they are nevertheless separate individuals. While the living entity is bound, the Supersoul is forever free. The living entity offers the Lord his obeisances again and again, willing to accept whatever suffering he deserves for his past impious deeds. He accepts that the ultimate cause of his suffering is that he has forgotten the Lord. He thus prays for the Lord’s mercy, something he needs if he is to achieve loving devotional service to the Lord. In his purport to text 15, Srila Prabhupada outlines how one can become free of illusion: “Maya is so strong that the Lord says that it is very difficult to surmount her influence. But one can do so very easily ‘if he surrenders unto Me.’ Mam eva ye prapad-yante: anyone who surrenders unto Him can overcome the influence of the stringent laws of material nature. It is clearly said here that a living entity is put under the influence of maya by His will, and if anyone wants to get out of this entanglement, this can be made possible simply by His mercy.” Krsna is the supreme controller. To become free from the miseries of conditioned life one need only surrender to Him.

Then, in his purport to text 16, Srila Prabhupada defines both the need to surrender and the method to achieve it: “. . . Krsna as the Supersoul is seated within the heart of the living entity, and when the living entity is serious, the Lord directs him to take shelter of His representative, a bona fide spiritual master. Directed from within and guided externally by the spiritual master, one attains the path of Krsna consciousness, which is the way out of the material clutches. . . . The seed of Krsna consciousness is sown within the heart of the conditioned soul, and when one hears instruction from the spiritual master, the seed fructifies, and one’s life is blessed.”

Kapila Muni continues to describe the misery the soul experiences in the womb: “Fallen into a pool of blood, stool and urine within the abdomen of his mother, his own body scorched by the mother’s gastric fire, the embodied soul, anxious to get out, counts his months and prays, ‘O my Lord, when shall I, a wretched soul, be released from this confinement?”’ (Bhag. [3.31.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.17)) Although suffering tremendously, the soul nevertheless appreciates his good fortune: “My dear Lord, by Your causeless mercy I am awakened to consciousness, although I am only ten months old. For this causeless mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the friend of all fallen souls, there is no way to express my gratitude but to pray with folded hands. . . . I offer my respectful obeisances to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by whom I have been blessed with this body and by whose grace I can see Him within and without.” (Bhag. [3.31.18-19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.18))

Thus the embryonic living entity amazingly accepts his suffering without complaint, grateful for his awareness. One should consider awareness of one’s own suffering a gift from Krsna and superior to superficial happiness, because it may impel one to root out the ultimate cause of suffering, aversion to Krsna, and inspire him to attain true surrender and devotion.

But the conscious soul is also legitimately afraid: “Therefore, my Lord, although I am living in a terrible condition, I do not wish to depart from my mother’s abdomen to fall again into the blind well of materialistic life.” (Bhag. [3.31.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.20)) The soul thinks, “I am suffering now, but when I take birth I will immediately begin to identify with my body due to maya’s plan. I will then become a materialist and further extend my suffering. Better that I remain in this womb, despite my present misery.”

Srila Prabhupada illustrates the soul’s plight in his purport to text 20: “By the influence of maya only, one forgets his eternal relationship with Krsna and identifies himself with his body and the by-products of the body—namely wife, children, society, friendship and love. Thus he becomes a victim of the influence of maya, and his materialistic life of continued birth and death becomes still more stringent.”

The living entity concludes his prayers by expressing determination: “Therefore, without being agitated any more, I shall deliver myself from the darkness of nescience with the help of my friend, clear consciousness. Simply by keeping the lotus feet of Lord Visnu in my mind, I shall be saved from entering into the wombs of many mothers for repeated birth and death.” (Bhag. [3.31.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.21)) The fortunate soul thus places the responsibility to take shelter of Krsna on himself.

In his purport to text 21, Srila Prabhupada describes the essence of the conditioned soul’s dilemma: “The child prays that it is better to remain within the womb of darkness and be constantly absorbed in Krsna consciousness than to get out and again fall a victim to the illusory energy. The illusory energy acts within the abdomen as well as outside the abdomen, but the trick is that one should remain Krsna conscious, and then the effect of such a horrible condition cannot act unfavorably upon him.”

But despite assistance from the pain of material life, can one practically speaking remain Krsna conscious—whether within the womb or at work? Prabhupada explains the most effective means to escape material existence regardless of one’s external situation: “One does not need any material arrangement to cultivate Krsna consciousness. One can cultivate Krsna consciousness anywhere and everywhere, provided he can always think of Krsna. The maha-mantra, Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare, can be chanted even within the abdomen of one’s mother. One can chant while sleeping, while working, while imprisoned in the womb or while outside. Krsna consciousness cannot be checked in any circumstance. The conclusion of the child’s prayer is: ‘Let me remain in this condition; although it is very miserable, it is better not to fall a victim to maya again by going outside.’” (Bhag. [3.31.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.21), purport)

In his Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 151, Srila Jiva Gosvami explains that only those souls who are fortunate prayerfully seek the Lord’s shelter while they are still in the womb. Sri Jiva describes that a living entity must only pray in this way to the Lord for one birth, and that by Krsna’s grace his prayers will award him liberation from birth and death. Actually, Sri Jiva continues, such a fortunate living entity is rare, for most souls remain unaware of the merciful nature of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Thus only those in the womb who neglect to pray suffer.

Sri Jiva then offers an example from Sridhara Svami’s commentary on Bhagavatam [3.13.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/13.35) (the appearance of Lord Varahadeva) to illustrate that, as in the above case of the unborn child in the womb, one event (the soul’s prayers) and a second event (Kapila Muni’s subsequent descriptions of suffering), although narrated sequentially, may actually not be sequential but “temporally disconnected.”

## Texts 22-33: Kapila Muni Describes the Child’s Expulsion from the Womb and His Forgetfulness

The embryo’s time to be expelled from the womb arrives. With great difficulty the child takes birth, his head down. He is breathless and loses his memory because of the severe pain. He “falls on the ground, smeared with stool and blood, and plays just like a worm germinated from the stool. He loses his superior knowledge and cries under the spell of maya.” (Bhag. [3.31.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.24)) Crying, surrounded by family members, able to eat only what others offer him, and unable to communicate his needs, he is placed in a bed infested with sweat and germs. He is unable to sit, stand, or move on his own. His body itches, and his tender skin is bitten again and again by germs and insects. He cries bitterly, deprived of his wisdom, his consciousness compressed.

In his purport to text 27, Srila Prabhupada uses the information provided about the unfavorable circumstances in which newborns find themselves to preach to all devotees: “Not only children but also elderly persons should be very careful to protect their sense of Krsna consciousness and avoid unfavorable circumstances so that they may not forget their prime duty.”

In Chapter Thirty, Lord Kapila narrated the history of the soul in a human body from birth to death. Now after suffering death and untold punishments over countless births, that soul has again taken birth in a human family and received another chance for spiritual awakening. Yet his tendencies remain unchanged and his sufferings continue. Kapila continues: Passing through his childhood, he suffers distress and attains boyhood. “In boyhood also he suffers pain over desires to get things he can never achieve. And thus, due to ignorance, he becomes angry and sorry.” (Bhag. [3.31.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.28)) His body grows and so does his false prestige and anger, which incite him to create enmity with other lusty persons. Thus the soul trapped in a material body accepts nonpermanent things as if they were his own. Because he identifies his body with himself, his ignorance increases. To benefit his body, as well as to assist those attached to his body, he acts in such a way that he becomes further entangled in ignorance. “If, therefore, the living entity again associates with the path of unrighteousness, influenced by sensually minded people engaged in the pursuit of sexual enjoyment and the gratification of the palate, he again goes to hell as before. He becomes devoid of truthfulness, cleanliness, mercy, gravity, spiritual intelligence, shyness, austerity, fame, forgiveness, control of the mind, control of the senses, fortune and all such opportunities.” (Bhag. [3.31.32-33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.32))

A living entity absorbed in false ego attempts to increase the prestige of his temporary identity. While his successes bring him pleasure, they also increase his lust and greed. His inevitable failures cause him to taste the bitterness of his insignificance. This makes him angry, which contracts his consciousness even more than lust contracts it.Humility is a much different experience than the feeling of material insignificance, although both require that one dwell on his own rottenness. A humble person considers himself an insignificant servant of God and understands how much he must rely on God’s mercy. He attempts to serve and please Krsna with devotion, knowing that any identity other than devotional servanthood is incomplete. Material feelings of insignificance are self-indulgent and paralyzing. They lead not to devotion but to further self-absorption. Srila Prabhupada offers practical advice on how one can avoid the suffering caused by misidentifying the self:

**It is said that a living entity is eternal, and, as such, qualitatively one with the Supreme Lord. Then what is the reason he falls prey to the material and commits so many sinful activities by the influence of the material energy? In reply to this question, Lord Krsna said that it is lust which causes a living entity to glide down from his exalted position to the abominable condition of material existence. This lust circumstantially changes into anger. Both lust and anger stand on the platform of the mode of passion. Lust is actually the product of the mode of passion, and in the absence of satisfaction of lust, the same desire transforms into anger on the platform of ignorance. When ignorance covers the soul, it is the source of his degradation to the most abominable condition of hellish life.**

**To raise oneself from hellish life to the highest position of spiritual understanding is to transform this lust into love of Krsna. Sri Narottama dasa Thakura, a great acarya of the Vaisnava sum-pradaya, said, kama krsna'karmarpane: due to our lust, we want many things for our sense gratification, but the same lust can be transformed in a purified way so that we want everything for the satisfaction of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Anger also can be utilized towards a person who is atheistic or who is envious of the Personality of Godhead. As we have fallen into this material existence because of our lust and anger, the same two qualities can be utilized for the purpose of advancing in Krsna consciousness, and one can elevate himself again to his former pure, spiritual position. (Bhag.** [**3.31.29**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.29)**, purport)**

Srila Prabhupada continues to discuss the soul’s becoming covered by ignorance in his purport to text 30: “The expansion of ignorance is explained in this verse. The first ignorance is to identify one’s material body, which is made of five elements, as the self, and the second is to accept something as one’s own due to a bodily connection. In this way, ignorance expands. The living entity is eternal, but because of his accepting nonpermanent things, misidentifying his interest, he is put into ignorance, and therefore he suffers material pangs.”

## Texts 34-42: Beware of Bad Association

Kapila Muni now offers a grave warning: “One should not associate with a coarse fool who is bereft of the knowledge of selfrealization and who is no more than a dancing dog in the hands of a woman. The infatuation and bondage which accrue to a man from attachment to any other object is not as complete as that resulting from attachment to a woman or to the fellowship of men who are fond of women.” (Bhag. [3.31.34-35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.34)) Fearing materialistic association, sages in ancient times chose to reside in the forest, for one consciously or unconsciously adopts the characteristics of those with whom one associates. Kapila Muni warns Devahuti about association with those absorbed in sensuality, especially in relation to the opposite sex. Srila Prabhupada echoes Kapiladeva’s mood in his purport to text 35: “In Kali-yuga, association with women is very strong. In every step of life, there is association with women. If a person goes to purchase something, the advertisements are full of pictures of women. The physiological attraction for women is very great, and therefore people are very slack in spiritual understanding. The Vedic civilization, being based on spiritual understanding, arranges association with women very cautiously. ... In other words, attraction for woman’s association is the cause of the material conditional life, and anyone interested in being freed from this conditional life must detach himself from the association of women.”

The texts in this section stress the danger of men associating with women, especially attractive women, because in such association the spirit of enjoyment tends to become inflamed. The more one fortifies his spirit of enjoyment, the more he fortifies the core of his material existence. Therefore, those who wish to make spiritual advancement reject loose association with members of the opposite sex. Laxity in this regard could prove itself “the gateway to hell for the advancing devotee.” (Bhag. [3.31.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.39)) For a man, Kapila Muni explains, woman “is the representation of maya” (Bhag. [3.31.40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.40)), and for a woman, her house, husband, and children should be viewed as arrangements by the external energy to carry her closer to death.

Srila Prabhupada notes in his purport to text 38 that Sri Sri Radha and Krsna are the ultimate attractive beauty: “Instead of being attracted by material beauty, if one is accustomed to be attracted by the beauty of Radharani and Krsna, then the statement of Bhagavadgita, param drstva nivartate holds true. When one is attracted by the transcendental beauty of Radha and Krsna, he is no longer attracted by material feminine beauty. That is the special significance of Radha-Krsna worship. That is testified to by Yamunacarya.
