He says, ‘Since I have become attracted by the beauty of Radha and Krsna, when there is attraction for a woman or a memory of sex life with a woman, I at once spit on it, and my face turns in disgust.’ When we are attracted by Madana-mohana and the beauty of Krsna and His consorts, then the shackles of conditioned life, namely the beauty of a material woman, cannot attract us.”

Srila Prabhupada speaks of these truths as they apply to devotees:

**In these instructions of Lord Kapiladeva it is explained that not only is woman the gateway to hell for man, but man is also the gateway to hell for woman. It is a question of attachment. A man becomes attached to a woman because of her service, her beauty and many other assets, and similarly a woman becomes attached to a man for his giving her a nice place to live, ornaments, dress and children. It is a question of attachment for one another. As long as either is attached to the other for such material enjoyment, the woman is dangerous for the man, and the man is also dangerous for the woman. But if the attachment is transferred to Krsna, both of them become Krsna conscious, and then marriage is very nice. ... Man and woman should live together as householders in relationship with Krsna, only for the purpose of discharging duties in the service of Krsna. Engage the children, engage the wife and engage the husband, all in Krsna conscious duties, and then all these bodily or material attachments will disappear. Since the via medium is Krsna, the consciousness is pure, and there is no possibility of degradation at any time. (Bhag.** [**3.31.42**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.42)**, purport)**

## Texts 43-48: Reclaiming One’s Eternal Nature

As if he were the Lord’s competitor, the eternal living entity adopts a spirit of enjoyment and wanders from body to body, planet to planet. He is actually the cause of his own incessant births and deaths through an endless succession of bodies. Still, it can be said that materialistic association causes repeated birth and death, because it fills one’s heart with material desire. Good spiritual association, on the other hand, fills the heart with pure spiritual desires; it brings about the cessation of repeated birth and death.

Srila Prabhupada defines both birth and death in his purport to texts 45-46: “When one’s instrument of action is broken and cannot function, that is called death. Again, when one gets a new instrument for action, that is called birth.” The term death refers to when a soul in a specific body’s loses his ability to perceive; birth is the onset of a soul’s new bodily identification.

“Therefore,” Kapila Muni concludes, “one should not view death with horror, nor have recourse to defining the body as soul, nor give way to exaggeration in enjoying the bodily necessities of life. Realizing the true nature of the living entity, one should move about in the world free from attachment and steadfast in purpose.” (Bhag. [3.31.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.47)) Prabhupada’s purport to this text is a powerful and complete statement on renunciation:

**While discharging devotional service in full Krsna consciousness, one should not be miserly. He should not unnecessarily show that he has renounced this world. Actually, renunciation is not possible. If one renounces his palatial building and goes to a forest, there is actually no renunciation, for the palatial building is the property of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the forest is also the property of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. If he changes from one property to another, that does not mean that he renounces; he was never the proprietor of either the palace or the forest. Renunciation necessitates renouncing the false understanding that one can lord it over material nature. When one renounces this false attitude and renounces the puffed-up position that he is also God, that is real renunciation. Otherwise, there is no meaning of renunciation. Rupa Gosvami advises that if one renounces anything which could be applied in the service of the Lord and does not use it for that purpose, that is called phalgu-vairagya, insufficient or false renunciation. Everything belongs to the Supreme Personality of Godhead; therefore everything can be engaged in the service of the Lord; nothing should be used for one’s sense gratification. That is real renunciation. Nor should one unnecessarily increase the necessities of the body. We should be satisfied with whatever is offered and supplied by Krsna without much personal endeavor. We should spend our time executing devotional service in Krsna consciousness. That is the solution to the problem of life and death.**

Kapila Muni concludes this section of his instructions as follows: “Endowed with right vision and strengthened by devotional service and a pessimistic attitude towards material identity, one should relegate his body to this illusory world through his reason. Thus one can be unconcerned with this material world.” (Bhag. [3.31.48](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.48)) In the final texts of this chapter, Kapila Muni has summarized essential spiritual truths. First, one should be extremely careful about one’s association, because association plants desire in the heart, and desire is the seed of action. Material actions cause reactions, which cause birth and death. In addition, one should become fixed philosophically. One should know that all living entities are eternal souls. One should therefore avoid accruing karma, because it causes further entanglement in material life. The attempt to renounce the world is both incorrect and impossible. One can hardly renounce eating, breathing, and taking shelter from the elements. What one needs to do, however, is renounce the idea that the world is meant for one’s own pleasure.

As Kapila Muni described in Chapter Twenty-six, the material world issues from Krsna and is His energy. One should therefore replace one’s enjoying spirit with neutrality toward matter and a spirit of devotional service to Krsna.

## Chapter 32 - Entanglement in Fruitive Activities

## Levels of Work in Accordance with Sastra

Although in Chapter Thirty-one Kapila Muni implanted fear in the hearts of His listeners by describing the horrific results brought by the attempt to enjoy contrary to sastric regulations, one may nevertheless wonder if one can be happy and avoid suffering and rebirth through pious, nondevotional following of sastra. By delineating the results obtained by followers of various paths of karma, Kapila Muni will answer that question.

## Texts 1-4: Attached Workers

“The person who lives in the center of household life derives material benefits by performing religious rituals, and thereby he fulfills his desire for economic development and sense gratification. Again and again he acts the same way.” (Bhag. [3.32.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.1)) Although these persons follow sastra, they are nevertheless condemned. They are labeled grhamedhis, materialistic householders, because their motives are selfish, centered only on gratifying the false ego.

Because they have no spiritual goal, their pious actions and vows to worship the demigods may carry them to the heavenly planets, specifically the moon, but when their piety is exhausted, they will return to the cycle of birth and death on earth.

Srila Prabhupada differentiates between these grhamedhis and the grhasthas in his purport: “A grhastha is a person who lives with family, wife, children and relatives but has no attachment for them. He prefers to live in family life rather than as a mendicant or sannyasi, but his chief aim is to achieve self-realization, or to come to the standard of Krsna consciousness.” (Bhag. [3.32.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.1), purport)

It is interesting to note that Kapila Muni’s first instruction on the performance of devotional service (Bhag. [3.29.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.15)) is as follows: A devotee must execute his prescribed duties, which are glorious, without material profit. The word animittena, which Prabhupada translated in the text as “without material profit,” appears in the word-for-word translation as “without attachment to the result.” Prabhupada continues this theme after Kapila’s strong warning to men against associating with women, and to women against associating with men: “The relationship between man and woman is very complicated, but the substance is that one who aspires to ascend to the transcendental stage of spiritual realization should be very careful in accepting the association of a woman. In the stage of Krsna consciousness, however, such restriction of association may be slackened because if a man’s and woman’s attachment is not to each other but to Krsna, then both of them are equally eligible to get out of the material entanglement and reach the abode of Krsna. As it is confirmed in Bhagavad-gita, anyone who seriously takes to Krsna consciousness—whether in the lowest species of life or a woman or of the less intelligent classes, such as the mercantile or laborer class—will go back home, back to Godhead, and reach the abode of Krsna. A man should not be attached to a woman, nor should a woman be attached to a man. Both man and woman should be attached to the service of the Lord. Then there is the possibility of liberation from material entanglement for both of them.” (Bhag. [3.31.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/31.41), purport) Thus both Kapila and Prabhupada have provided ample warnings, guidance, balance, and encouragement.

## Texts 5-7: Detached Workers

Superior to the grhamedhis are those who perform their work with detachment, dutifully, in purified consciousness, free from a sense of proprietorship, and not swayed by sensual desires. Such persons gradually approach the Supreme Personality of Godhead by the path of illumination, and by first attaining the sun planet.

Thus Kapila Muni has described three kinds of householders: those who work selfishly against the principles of sastra (chapters Thirty and Thirty-one), those who work selfishly according to the principles of sastra (Bhag. [3.32.1-3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.1), [16-21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.16)), and those who perform detached work according to the principles of sastra (Bhag. [3.32.5-7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.5)). Lord Kapila has also described the various results each of these workers will attain: attached impious materialists go to hell, attached pious materialists go to heaven but later fall back to earth, and detached dutiful householders become purified and attain the spiritual realm.

Bhagavad-gita [18.26-27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.26) notes that those who perform detached work are in the mode of goodness; they are superior to those who are in passion and ignorance and who work with attachment. Such detached workers can be divided into two categories. One group includes those who are detached and dutiful, but who are not devotees. These souls neglect to offer the fruits of their activities to the Lord and only gradually progress toward the spiritual realm, as indicated (in text 7) by the words surya-dvdrena, “through the sun planet.” The second group, the devotees, are also detached and dutiful, but they work for Krsna and offer the results of their work to Him. The spiritual results they attain are immediate. Srila Prabhupada describes these devoted, detached workers as follows: “Nyasta-karmdna/i indicates that the results of their activities are given to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Such persons appear to be acting on the platform of their respective duties, but such activities are not performed for personal sense gratification; rather, they are performed for the Supreme Person. Such devotees are called prasantah, which means ‘completely satisfied.’” (Bhag. [3.32.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.5), purport)

Krsna Himself describes the actions of those who work for His pleasure in Bhagavad-gita ([18.46](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.46)): “By worship of the Lord, who is the source of all beings and who is all-pervading, a man can attain perfection through performing his own work.” One thus situated considers himself the Lord’s servant and worships Him with folded hands: “By this work, О Lord, may You be pleased.”

## Texts 8-11: Perfect Yogis, Worshipers of the Hiranyagarbha, and Taking Shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead

Kapila Muni now describes other followers of sastra: Worshipers of the Hiranyagarbha (Garbhodakasayi Visnu) do not gain a direct approach to the Supreme Personality of Godhead in Vaikuntha. Rather, they remain in this universe on the higher planets up to Satyaloka (Brahmaloka). At the end of Brahma’s life, such pious souls, free of maya’s contamination, are transferred along with Brahma to the spiritual kingdom.

Perfected yogis also attain Brahma’s planet and are unable to directly attain Vaikuntha or to directly merge into the Lord’s impersonal effulgence, should that be their desire. Because they remain in the material atmosphere, all of these exalted souls risk taking birth again in the material world.

Thus after having delineated various pious paths and their results, Kapila Muni advises Devahuti: “My dear mother, by devotional service take direct shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is seated in everyone’s heart.” (Bhag. [3.32.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.11))

' The translations for sruta-anubhdvam (“whose glories you have heard”) and bhamini (“My dear mother”) indicate Kapila Muni’s desire that His mother focus her attention on Him, the Supersoul. Srila Prabhupada comments on Kapila Muni’s purpose in comparing direct Krsna consciousness to other pious paths (Bhag. [3.32.1-21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.1)) in his purport to text 11: “Lord Kapila advised His mother that she did not need any indirect process. She was already situated in that direct process because the Supreme Lord had taken birth as her son. Actually, she did not need any further instruction because she was already in the perfectional stage. Kapiladeva advised her to continue in the same way. He therefore addressed His mother as bhamini to indicate that she was already thinking of the Lord as her son.”

## Texts 12-21: More Pious Paths—Demigods, Sages, Impersonalists, and Other Attached Sastric Workers

All those who maintain self-interest, Kapila Muni explains, are forced by time to return to the material world. Even “demigods such as Lord Brahma, great sages such as Sanat-kumara and great munis such as Marici have to come back to the material world again at the time of creation. When the interaction of the three modes of material nature begins, Brahma, who is the creator of this cosmic manifestation and who is full of Vedic knowledge, and the great sages, who are the authors of the spiritual path and the yoga system, come back under the influence of the time factor. They are liberated by their nonfruitive activities and they attain the first incarnation of the purusa, but at the time of creation they come back in exactly the same forms and positions as they had previously.” (Bhag. [3.32.12-15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.12)) In his purport Srila Prabhupada explains why great sages and even Lord Brahma may have to again return to the material world: “Brahma and the great rsis and the great master of yoga (Siva) are not ordinary living entities; they are very powerful and have all the perfections of mystic yoga. But still they have an inclination to try to become one with the Supreme, and therefore they have to come back. In the Srimad-Bhagavatam it is accepted that as long as one thinks that he is equal with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he is not completely purified or knowledgeable. In spite of going up to the first purusa-avatar a, Maha-Visnu, after the dissolution of this material creation, such personalities again fall down or come back to the material creation.”

Karmis, pious but fruitive workers who base their work on sastra, are addicted to material enjoyment. Because of their addiction, they enact their prescribed duties faithfully, knowing that by following the scriptural order, they will gain sense pleasure. “They worship the forefathers and are busy day and night improving the economic condition of their family, social or national life.” (Bhag. [3.32.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.17)) They are impelled by passion and lust, desiring only to satisfy their senses. Despite their apparent religiosity, they are selfish and thus do not develop attraction to hearing the Lord’s pastimes. Kapila Muni condemns such aversion to hearing “the nectar of the activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead” and their indulgence in “hearing of the abominable activities of materialistic persons,” (Bhag. [3.32.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.19)) comparing such pious materialists to “stool-eating hogs.” He states that such persons may attain Pitrloka, but asserts that when their piety is exhausted they will return to earth and to rebirth in the same families in which they once lived.

In his purport to text 19, Srila Prabhupada presents the essential fault of all materialists: “Materialistic persons are considered condemned because they are interested in hellish activities and not in transcendental activities. The message of the Lord’s activities is nectar, and besides that message, any information in which we may be interested is actually hellish.”

## Texts 22-26: The Conclusion of Kapila Muni’s Teachings

After having analyzed and compared the processes of a variety of practitioners, Kapila Muni concludes His instructions to Devahuti: “My dear mother, I therefore advise that you take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for His lotus feet are worth worshiping. Accept this with all devotion and love, for thus you can be situated in transcendental devotional service.” (Bhag. [3.32.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.22)) Kapila Muni advises His mother to take full shelter of Krsna with great devotion. Nothing else has value. Dependence on one’s limited abilities constricts one’s spiritual advancement, but taking shelter of Krsna shifts one’s capacity to advance from oneself to Krsna, who possesses both unlimited power and unlimited mercy.

In his purport to text 22, Srila Prabhupada glorifies Krsna’s kindness and liberality: “His behavior with the devotees is so exalted that a devotee need not try to divert his attention to any other worship. It is said that the demoniac Putana came to kill Krsna by poisoning Him, but because Krsna was pleased to suck her breast, she was given the same position as His mother. Devotees pray, therefore, that if a demon who wanted to kill Krsna gets such an exalted position, why should they go to anyone other than Krsna for their worshipful attachment? There are two kinds of religious activities: one for material advancement and one for spiritual advancement. By taking shelter under the lotus feet of Krsna, one is endowed with both kinds of prosperity, material and spiritual. Why then should one go to any demigod?”

One should take shelter of Krsna and try to please Him. As Krsna is composed of sac-cid-ananda, eternity, knowledge, and bliss, matter does not even tinge His existence, and nothing material—nothing of lesser quality than His spiritual energy—can please Him. Krsna describes the simple, devotional essence of pleasing Him in Bhagavad-gita [9.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.26): “If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, 1 will accept it.” Obviously, as He is the Supreme Lord of countless universes, Krsna needs neither leaves nor fruits, yet He is truly eager to accept these things in proportion to the devotion with which they are offered. Indeed, devotion is the element that transforms an offering made of material elements and makes it acceptable to Krsna. Therefore, there is nothing else we need to do but worship Krsna with devotion and humbly depend on His mercy.

In Hyderabad on April 12, 1975, Srila Prabhupada described the process of pleasing Krsna:

**You should submit, and you should feel that “I am worthless. My Guru Maharaja has given this chance to serve Krsna, to offer Krsna. My Lord, I am worthless. I have no capacity to serve You. But on the order of my Guru Maharaja, I am trying to serve You. Please do not take any offense. Accept whatever I can do. That’s all. That is my request.” That mantra is sufficient. Krsna says in the Bhagavad-gita, у о me bhaktya prayacchati. Krsna never said that “One who offers Me with Sanskrit mantra.” Yo me bhaktya prayacchati. The real thing is bhakti, feeling: “How can I serve Krsna? How can I please Him?” That is wanted. The process is not to become a very good scholar in speaking in Sanskrit or English. Always feel that “1 am worthless, but I have been given a chance to serve by the grace of my Guru Maharaja. So kindly accept whatever little service I can give. I am offensive. So kindly excuse me.” In this way be humble, meek, and offer your feeling, and Krsna will be satisfied. Not that you have to show how you can speak in the Sanskrit language.**

Comparing the results of bhakti with the achievements of other spiritual practices, Kapila Muni makes it clear that those who surrender to Krsna automatically achieve the results of jnana (knowledge) and vairagya (renunciation). In addition, a devotee never again returns to the material world. Even while in this world, a pure devotee remains detached from matter, purified, and free from bad habits, because his attention is fixed on the spiritual platform and on serving Krsna. Material gains and losses neither excite nor trouble him any more than the gain or loss of a single dollar excites or troubles a billionaire. In addition, despite the existence of many systems of worship and paths for spiritual advancement, Krsna is the ultimate goal. It is He alone who is realized, albeit differently, through every practice.

In his purport to text 33, Srila Prabhupada offers an example to illustrate how different paths reveal differing aspects of the same Truth: “... it is stated here that both bhakti-yoga and jnana-yoga are meant for reaching the same destination—the Personality of Godhead. By the process of jnana-yoga the same Personality of Godhead appears to be impersonal. As the same object appears to be different when perceived by different senses, the same Supreme Lord appears to be impersonal by mental speculation. A hill appears cloudy from a distance, and one who does not know may speculate that the hill is a cloud. Actually, it is not a cloud; it is a big hill. One has to learn from authority that the sight of a cloud is not actually a cloud but a hill. If one makes a little more progress, then instead of a cloud he sees the hill and something green. When one actually approaches the hill, he will see many varieties.... Similarly, those who are trying to find the Supreme Godhead by mental speculation may approach the bodily effulgence, or the impersonal Brahman, and those who are trying to find the Supreme Godhead by yoga practice may find Him as the localized Supersoul, but those who are directly trying to approach the Supreme Truth by practice of bhakti-yoga can see Him face to face as the Supreme Person.”

Despite common elements in all paths, as Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 26, devotional service awards results unavailable to practitioners of other processes. A practitioner of other paths must necessarily perform devotional service to attain his goal, but a devotee’s only desire is to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead. That, in turn—far different from the desires of jndnis and many yogis—fixes his destination as the spiritual world, the Vaikuntha planets: “The devotee can see the Supreme Lord face to face, but the jnani, the empiric philosopher or yogi cannot. They cannot be elevated to the positions of associates of the Lord. There is no evidence in the scriptures stating that by cultivating knowledge or worshiping the impersonal Brahman one can become a personal associate of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. . . . One has to make one’s destination the supreme abode of the Lord.”

## Summary of Kapila’s Teaching on Astanga-yoga, Jnana-yoga, and Bhakti-yoga (Chapters 25-29)

## Texts 27-36: Attaining Bhagavan Realization is the Ultimate Goal of All Vedic Practices

All types of yogis desire to escape material entrapment. Detachment from fleeting material pleasure is thus common to all yogic practices. Those yogis who are actually averse to the transcendence conclude through their limited intellectual abilities that everything in existence is relative, limited, and false. This is not true. Kapiladeva states (reiterating what He has already explained) that everything rests on Him: “From the total energy, the mahat-tattva, I have manifested the false ego, the three modes of material nature, the five material elements, the individual consciousness, the eleven senses and the material body. Similarly, the entire universe has come from the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [3.32.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.29))

In texts 27-29 of this thirty-second chapter, Kapiladeva comments on the position of yogis and jnanis. In his purport to text 28, Srila Prabhupada explains how we may understand Krsna’s position through the intellectual process of jnana: “When uncontaminated pure knowledge is uncovered from the modes of material nature, the actual identity of the living entity is discovered: he is eternally a servitor of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The process of uncovering is like this: the rays of sunshine are luminous, and the sun itself is also luminous. In the presence of the sun, the rays illuminate just like the sun, but when the sunshine is covered by the spell of a cloud, or by maya, then darkness, the imperfection of perception, begins. Therefore, to get out of the entanglement of the spell of nescience, one has to awaken his spiritual consciousness, or Krsna consciousness, in terms of the authorized scriptures.” The steady, faithful, detached devotee, absorbed in thinking of the Supreme, achieves perfect knowledge. Kapiladeva has already explained the ultimate path, devotional service, “by which one can come to understand the real truth of matter and spirit and their relationship.” (Bhag. [3.32.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.31))

“Philosophical research culminates in understanding the Supreme Personality of Godhead. After achieving this understanding, when one becomes free from the material modes of nature, he attains the stage of devotional service. Either by devotional service directly or by philosophical research, one has to find the same destination, which is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. A single object is appreciated differently by different senses due to its having different qualities. Similarly, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is one, but according to different scriptural injunctions He appears to be different.” (Bhag. [3.32.32-33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.32)) By progressing to perfection by other paths—including the path of jnana-yoga—one can, through proper association and an adjustment in both one’s method and one’s goal, achieve the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the perfection achieved by devotees. Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is the complete manifestation of the Absolute Truth, but He is realized differently according to one’s path and is therefore described differently in various scriptures. To fully realize the Absolute Truth, however, as He is manifest both in matter and in transcendence, one must take to His devotional service.

Srila Prabhupada, Srila Jiva Gosvami, and Srila Sridhara Svami have all commented on texts 32 and 33. Srila Prabhupada states: “Bhaktya mam abhijanati \[Bg. [18.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.55)\]: if one wants to understand the Absolute Truth in perfection, he must take to devotional service. Of course, no one can understand the Absolute Truth in all perfection. That is not possible for the infinitesimal living entities. But the highest point of understanding by the living entity is reached by discharge of devotional service, not otherwise.” (Bhag. [3.32.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.33), purport)

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on these texts in his Bhagavat' sandarbha, anuccheda 86, explaining that the ultimate destination of jndnis should not be the Brahman feature of Bhagavan but service to the Lord’s personal form, a fact that is further described by Lord Krsna in Bhagavad-gita [12.3-4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/12.3): “But those who fully worship the unmanifested, that which lies beyond the perception of the senses, the all-pervading, inconceivable, unchanging, fixed and immovable— the impersonal conception of the Absolute Truth—by controlling the various senses and being equally disposed to everyone, such persons, engaged in the welfare of all, at last achieve Me.”

Srila Sridhara Svami comments: Text 32 states that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is attained by jnana-yoga. However, the jndna' yoga described here is like bhakti-yoga. This text notes that “philosophical research fjnana-yoga\] ends in understanding the Supreme Personality of Godhead. After achieving this understanding, when one becomes free from the material modes of nature, he attains the stage of devotional service. Either directly by devotional service or by philosophical research, one has to reach the same destination, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. How are jnana-yoga and bhakti-yoga the same? The answer is hinted at by the phrase “Either by direct devotional service or by philosophical research, one has to find the same destination, which is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

In his purport to Bhagavad-gita [12.3-4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/12.3), Srila Prabhupada further clarifies how one following the impersonal path who remains an imper-sonalist neglects to surrender to Krsna, although such surrender is the ultimate goal of every path, including the impersonal path: “Those who do not directly worship the Supreme Godhead, Krsna, but who attempt to achieve the same goal by an indirect process, also ultimately achieve the same goal, Sri Krsna. ‘After many births the man of wisdom seeks refuge in Me, knowing that Vasudeva is all.’ When a person comes to full knowledge after many births, he surrenders unto Lord Krsna. If one approaches the Godhead by the method mentioned in this verse, he has to control the senses, render service to everyone and engage in the welfare of all beings. It is inferred that one has to approach Lord Krsna, otherwise there is no perfect realization. Often there is much penance involved before one fully surrenders unto Him.”

Kapila Muni has thus compared and contrasted the methods and achievements of devotees, fruitive workers, yogis, tapasvis, and jnanis. He underlines His conclusion by instructing His mother to devotedly serve and worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Ending His instructions, Kapila Muni again confirms that the object of devotional service as well as the final realization of all processes is to know and serve Krsna: “By performing fruitive activities and sacrifices, by distributing charity, by performing austerities, by studying various literatures, by conducting philosophical research, by controlling the mind, by subduing the senses, by accepting the renounced order of life and by performing the prescribed duties of one’s social order; by performing the different divisions of yoga practice, by performing devotional service and by exhibiting the process of devotional service containing the symptoms of both attachment and detachment; by understanding the science of self-realization and by developing a strong sense of detachment, one who is expert in understanding the different processes of self-realization realizes the Supreme Personality of Godhead as He is represented in the material world as well as in transcendence.” (Bhag. [3.32.34-36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.34))

In his purport to these texts, Srila Prabhupada restates the conclusion concisely—that the goal of all processes is to attain Krsna: “. . . when one is able to see his real constitutional position, he sees all other processes and becomes situated in the stage of pure devotional service. At that time he can understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Bhagavan.”

## Texts 37-38: Summary of Time and Fruitive Activities (Chapters 29-32)

Kapila Muni continues to summarize his teachings from this and previous chapters by again noting the four kinds of devotional service, three practiced under the modes of material nature and one practiced beyond them. Only pure, transcendental devotional service can carry one to Krsna in the spiritual world. Neglecting devotional service to act in ignorance, warns Kapila, places us under the influence of time. Once one has entered “that forgetfulness, he is unable to understand where his movements will end.” (Bhag. [3.32.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.38)) In his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada describes the prime element in having our ignorance removed and becoming free to leave the material world: “Unless the living entity receives the mercy of the saintly persons, the spiritual master or Krsna, it is not possible for him to get out of the darkness of material existence; by his own endeavor it is not possible.”

## Texts 39-42: Who Should and Should Not Be Instructed in Sankhya

Kapila Muni now offers a caveat to His teachings: “This instruction is not meant for the envious, for the agnostics or for persons who are unclean in their behavior. Nor is it for hypocrites or for persons who are proud of material possessions. It is not to be instructed to persons who are too greedy and too attached to family life, nor to persons who are nondevotees and who are envious of the devotees and of the Personality of Godhead. Instruction should be given to the faithful devotee who is respectful to the spiritual master, nonenvious, and friendly to all kinds of living entities and eager to render service with faith and sincerity This instruction should be imparted by the spiritual master to persons who have taken the Supreme Personality of Godhead to be more dear than anything, who are not envious of anyone, who are perfectly cleansed and who have developed detachment for that which is outside the purview of Krsna consciousness.” (Bhag. [3.32.39-42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/32.39))Srila Prabhupada’s extensive purport to text 42 explains how we can advance in Krsna consciousness. Six excerpts follow:

**To serve a devotee, to chant the holy name according to a certain counting method, to worship the Deity, to hear Srimad-Bhagavatam or Bhagavad-gita from a realized person and to live in a sacred place where devotional service is not disturbed are the first out of sixty-four devotional activities for making progress in devotional service. One who has accepted these five chief activities is called a devotee.**

**One must be prepared to offer the necessary respect and honor to the spiritual master. He should not be unnecessarily envious of his Godbrothers. Rather, if a Godbrother is more enlightened and advanced in Krsna consciousness, one should accept him as almost equal to the spiritual master, and one should be happy to see such Godbrothers advance in Krsna consciousness.**

**A devotee should always be very kind to the general public in instructing Krsna consciousness because that is the only solution for getting out of the clutches of maya. That is really humanitarian work, for it is the way to show mercy to other people who need it very badly.**

**Not only is \[a devotee\] detached from activities which are not connected to Krsna consciousness, but he should be internally averse to the material way of life.**

**To become actually cleansed externally and internally, one should chant the holy name of the Lord, Hare Krsna, or Visnu, constantly.**

**The spiritual master should train his disciple in such a way so that in the future only the Supreme Personality of Godhead will be the dearmost goal of his life.**

## Text 43: Phala-sruti—Kapila Muni Ends

Kapila Muni’s concludes with a benediction: “Anyone who once meditates upon Me with faith and affection, who hears and chants about Me, surely goes back home, back to Godhead.”

## Chapter 33 - The Activities of Kapila Muni

## Texts 1-8: The Prayers of Devahuti

Devahuti’s questions have all been answered by Kapila Muni’s explanation of Sankhya philosophy. She has understood that the Lord, her son, is the source of all and that devotional service to Him is both the means to attain Him and the goal. The burning fire of Devahuti’s ignorance has been extinguished. Devahuti now offers Kapila her obeisances, as well as prayers in which she expresses her realizations, all of which satisfy Kapiladeva.

Devahuti says: Unborn Brahma has taken birth from the lotus flower growing from Your navel, and that powerful entity then meditated on You, the source of unlimited universes. Although You personally are not doing anything, Your determination is absolute. There is no question of Your fulfilling Your will with the help of anyone besides Yourself. You are, in the end, the Supreme Soul and the supreme controller. Your will, therefore, cannot be checked by anyone else.

Devahuti then expresses amazement: Yet “You have taken birth from my abdomen. О my Lord, how is that possible for the supreme one, who has in His belly all the cosmic manifestation? The answer is that it is possible, for at the end of the millennium You lie down on a leaf of a banyan tree, and just like a small baby, You lick the toe of Your lotus foot.” (Bhag. [3.33.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.4))Srila Prabhupada’s purport to this text is sweet:

**At the time of dissolution the Lord sometimes appears as a small baby lying on a leaf of a banyan tree, floating on the devastating water. Therefore Devahuti suggests, “Your lying down within the abdomen of a common woman like me is not so astonishing. You can lie down on the leaf of a banyan tree and float on the water of devastation as a small baby. It is not very wonderful, therefore, that You can lie down in the abdomen of my body. You teach us that those who are very fond of children within this material world and who therefore enter into marriage to enjoy family life with children can also have the Supreme Personality of Godhead as their child, and the most wonderful thing is that the Lord Himself licks His toe.”**

**Since all the great sages and devotees apply all energy and all activities in the service of the lotus feet of the Lord, there must be some transcendental pleasure in the toes of His lotus feet. The Lord licks His toe to taste the nectar for which the devotees always aspire. Sometimes the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself wonders how much transcendental pleasure is within Himself, and in order to taste His own potency, He sometimes takes the position of tasting Himself. Lord Caitanya is Krsna Himself, but He appears as a devotee to taste the sweetness of the transcendental mellow in Himself which is tasted by Srimati Radharani, the greatest of all devotees.**

Why does the Lord, as Kapiladeva or other incarnations, descend to this world? Devahuti continues: You appear in all Your incarnations to diminish the sinful activities of the fallen as well as to enrich their knowledge and devotion. Not only are Your potencies and activities wonderful, but even Your names possess incredible power. “To say nothing of the spiritual advancement of persons who see the Supreme Person face to face, even a person born in a family of dogeaters immediately becomes eligible to perform Vedic sacrifices if he once utters the holy name of the Supreme Personality of Godhead or chants about Him, hears about His pastimes, offers Him obeisances or even remembers Him.” (Bhag. [3.33.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.6))

In furthur glorification, Devahuti exclaims: “Oh, how glorious are they whose tongues are chanting Your holy name! Even if born in the families of dog-eaters, such persons are worshipable. Persons who chant the holy name of Your Lordship must have executed all kinds of austerities and fire sacrifices and achieved all the good manners of the Aryans. To be chanting the holy name of Your Lordship, they must have bathed at holy places of pilgrimage, studied the Vedas and fulfilled everything required.” (Bhag. [3.33.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.7))

Krsna has kindly come in the form of His names. Srila Prabhupada’s important purport to text 6 describes Krsna’s potent holy names: “Sridhara Svami especially remarks in this connection, anena piijya-tvam laksyate. Some caste brahmanas remark that by chanting Hare Krsna, purification begins. Of course, that depends on the individual process of chanting, but this remark of Sridhara Svami’s is completely applicable if one chants the holy name of the Lord without offense, for he immediately becomes more than a brahmana. As Sridhara Svami says, pujyawam: he immediately becomes as respectable as a most learned brahmana and can be allowed to perform Vedic sacrifices. If simply by chanting the holy name of the Lord one becomes sanctified instantly, then what can be said of those persons who see the Supreme Lord face to face and who understand the descent of the Lord, as Devahuti understands Kapiladeva.”Prabhupada also discusses the qualification we need to successfully chant the holy name. And in his purport to text 7, he discusses which names we should chant:

**Just as a student in a law class is to be understood to have already graduated from general education, anyone who is engaged in the chanting of the holy name of the Lord—Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare—must have already passed all lower stages. It is said that those who simply chant the holy name with the tip of the tongue are glorious. One does not even have to chant the holy name and understand the whole procedure, namely the offensive stage, offenseless stage and pure stage; if the holy name is sounded on the tip of the tongue, that is also sufficient. It is said herein that nama, a singular number, one name, Krsna or Rama, is sufficient. It is not that one has to chant all the holy names of the Lord. The holy names of the Lord are innumerable, and one does not have to chant all the names to prove that he has already undergone all the processes of Vedic ritualistic ceremonies. If one chants once only, it is to be understood that he has already passed all the examinations, not to speak of those who are chanting always, twenty-four hours a day....**

**The holy name has to be chanted to please the Supreme Lord, and not for any sense gratification or professional purpose. If this pure mentality is there, then even though a person is bom of a low family, such as a dog-eater’s, he is so glorious that not only has he purified himself, but he is quite competent to deliver others. He is competent to speak on the importance of the transcendental name, just as Thakura Haridasa did.**

Srila Prabhupada continues in the same purport: “There are many Vedic statements in different places saying that anyone who chants the holy name of the Lord becomes immediately freed from conditional life and that anyone who hears the holy name of the Lord, even though bom of a family of dog-eaters, also becomes liberated from the clutches of material entanglement.” As the respect offered a government minister implies that he has the power and facility to carry out his office—respect without facility is meaningless—being respected as a brahmana also entails being offered the full facility to function as a brahmana without waiting for another birth. The Vedic culture offered this opportunity for social mobility. A person’s status depended on qualification, not birth. This is confirmed in Bhagavatam [7.11.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/11.35) by Narada Muni: “If one shows the symptoms of being a brahmana, ksatriya, vaisya or sudra, even if he has appeared in a different class, he should be accepted according to those symptoms of classification.”The Srimad-Bhagavatam refers to instances in which someone was bom in a non-brahmana family but was accepted as a brahmana without awaiting a future birth. Here are three examples:

**In addition to these nineteen sons mentioned above, there were eighty-one younger ones, all bom of Rsabhadeva and Jayanti. According to the order of their father, they became well cultured, well behaved, very pure in their activities and expert in Vedic knowledge and the performance of Vedic rituals. Thus they all became perfectly qualified brahmanas. (Bhag.** [**5.4.13**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/4.13)**)**

**From Karilsa, another son of Manu, came the Karilsa dynasty, a family of ksatriyas. The Karilsa ksatriyas were the kings of the northern direction. They were celebrated protectors of brahminical culture and were all firmly religious. From the son of Manu named Dhrsta came a ksatriya caste called Dharsta, whose members achieved the position of brahmanas in this world. (Bhag.** [**9.2.16-17**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/2.16)**)**

**Visvamitra, the son of Maharaja Gadhi, was as powerful as the flames of fire. From the position of a ksatriya, he achieved the position of a powerful brahmana by undergoing penances and austerities. (Bhag.** [**9.16.28**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/16.28)**)**

Srila Jiva Gosvami has also commented extensively on these important texts (Bhag. [3.33.6-7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.6)) in Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 128. Sri Jiva refers to these texts to explain that devotional service removes the results of past sins, even one’s prarabdha-karma, the karma that affects his current body. He explains that the word svadah means “a member of a caste of dog-eaters.” He then says that according to its grammatical derivation the word svadah means “a person who presently eats dog’s flesh, as carnivorous animals eat the flesh of various creatures.” Although other meanings of the word are possible, the rule riidhir у ogam apaharad (customary usage takes precedence over etymology) here eclipses all other definitions. Srila Sridhara Svami has used the word svapaca, “one who cooks dog meat,” as a synonym for svadah, to specify that this verse is referring to a person from a lower class who habitually eats dog meat.

Sri Jiva next explains that savanaya refers to the soma-yajna. Thus by any of the activities of devotion, such as hearing the name of the Lord, the dog-eater’s prarabdha-karma is destroyed. This means that the karma by which such persons have obtained their low birth is destroyed, and they are given the respect offered to one qualified to perform the soma-yajna. So we can understand that bhakti destroys prarabdha sins. If this is true even for those bom in families of dogeaters, then how much more true is it for devotees who are pious and of faultless character? The Srimad-Bhagavatam ([11.14.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/14.21)) thus explains, “Only by practicing unalloyed devotional service with full faith in Me can one obtain Me, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. I am naturally dear to My devotees, who take Me as the only goal of their loving service. By engaging in such pure devotional service, even the dog-eaters can purify themselves from the contamination of their low birth.”

Sri Jiva adds: By engaging in devotional service, a dog-eater becomes purified of the contamination brought about by his past sins. Then through further training he can actually attain the remaining qualities needed to perform the yajna. This is similar to a boy bom in a brahmana family, for he too is not automatically qualified to perform yajna; he is qualified only when he attains the proper training and initiation.. This is confirmed by Srila Sridhara Svami, who comments here, “This statement declares that a devotee of the Lord is supremely worthy of receiving worship.” In this way it is clearly seen that the performance of devotional service removes all the disadvantages created by past sins, as confirmed in Bhagavatam [3.33.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.7), wherein the word aho indicates a sense of being struck with wonder.

Sri Jiva continues: The text states, “Even a dog-eater is glorious if Your holy name stays on his tongue.” How is that possible? The answer is given: “He must have already executed all kinds of austerities.” The meaning here is that a person who chants Your holy name, О Lord, is the most pious of persons. Thus it is clear that engagement in devotional service to the Lord removes the diseases and sufferings caused by past sins. The Skanda Purana describes this as well: “I offer my respectful obeisances to the limitless Supreme Personality of Godhead. When one remembers His holy name, all one’s sufferings and diseases perish.” Sri Nama-kaumudi also explains that according to the worshiper’s desire, chanting the Lord’s holy name can remove the chanter’s prdrabdha-karma.

That qualified persons bom in non-brahmana families can perform the function of brahmanas is stressed by Sri Narada Muni in the Bhagavatam [7.11.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/11.35): “If one shows the symptoms of being a brahmana, ksatriya, vaisya or sudra . . . even if he has appeared in a different class, he should be accepted according to those symptoms of classification.”

And again by Narada Muni in Bhagavatam [7.11.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/11.17): “Except in a time of emergency, lower persons should not accept the occupational duties of those who are higher. When there is such an emergency, of course, everyone but the ksatriya may accept the means of livelihood of others.”

Srila Prabhupada comments as follows on the current emergency state of the world: “Sometimes brahmanas protest against our Krsna consciousness movement for creating brahmanas from Europeans, or, in other words, from mlecchas and yavanas. This movement, however, is here supported in Srimad-Bhagavatam. At the present moment, society is in a chaotic condition, and everyone has given up the cultivation of spiritual life, which is especially meant for the brahmanas. Because spiritual culture has been stopped all over the world, there is now an emergency, and therefore it is now time to train those who are considered lower and condemned, so that they may become brahmanas and take up the work of spiritual progress. The spiritual progress of human society has been stopped, and this should be considered an emergency. Here is solid support from Narada Muni of the movement known as Krsna consciousness.” (Bhag. [7.11.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/11.17), purport)

Additionally, in the Mahabharata Yudhisthira replies to a question posed by Nahusa: “One is not considered a brahmana or sudra simply because of birth. It is the actual possession of brahminical qualities that makes one a genuine brahmana, and the lack of them that qualifies one as a sudra.” To this Nahusa responds: “O King, if one’s varna is to be determined by qualities alone and not by birth, then no distinction could be made between persons until their qualities become manifest by their activities.” Yudhisthira’s response is again clear: “Yes, that is a fact. Thus until they are initiated by a bona fide acarya, everyone should be considered a sudra no matter how exalted their birth. Actually, in human society (especially in Kali-yuga) people engage in promiscuous sexual intercourse with members of any social order. Therefore it is very difficult to ascertain the real nature of one’s birth. For this reason also, one’s personal qualities must be the determining factor for ascertaining a person’s social status. Anyone who displays the proper qualifications should be accepted as a genuine brahmana.”

In his purport to Bhagavatam [1.8.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/8.26), Srila Prabhupada clarifies the potency of chanting Krsna’s holy names: “It is said in the sastras that by once uttering the holy name of the Lord, the sinner gets rid of a quantity of sins that he is unable to commit. Such is the power of uttering the holy name of the Lord. There is not the least exaggeration in this statement. Actually the Lord’s holy name has such powerful potency. But there is a quality to such utterances also. It depends on the quality of feeling. A helpless man can feelingly utter the holy name of the Lord, whereas a man who utters the same holy name in great material satisfaction cannot be so sincere. A materially puffed up person may utter the holy name of the Lord occasionally, but he is incapable of uttering the name in quality. Therefore, the four principles of material advancement, namely (1) high parentage, (2) good wealth, (3) high education and (4) attractive beauty, are, so to speak, disqualifications for progress on the path of spiritual advancement.”

Devahuti has thus glorified the Lord, who has descended as her son, by glorifying the potency of His holy names. Instead of prolonging her prayers, she concludes them with a summary of her divine son’s position: “I believe, my Lord, that You are Lord Visnu Himself under the name of Kapila, and You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Supreme Brahman! The saints and sages, being freed from all the disturbances of the senses and mind, meditate upon You, for by Your mercy only can one become free from the clutches of the three modes of material nature. At the time of dissolution, all the Vedas are sustained in You only.” (Bhag. [3.33.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.8))

## Texts 9-11: Kapila Muni’s Reply

Kapila Muni, satisfied by His mother’s prayers, replies with gravity, affection, and respect, encouraging Devahuti to follow the system of self-realization He has just described: “You can execute this system without difficulty, and by following it you shall very soon be liberated, even within your present body. My dear mother, those who are actually transcendentalists certainly follow My instructions, as I have given them to you.” (Bhag. [3.33.10-11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.10)) By following these instructions, Kapiladeva promises Devahuti that she will attain perfect self-realization, become free of “fearful material contamination,” and ultimately reach Him. “Mother, persons who are not conversant with this method of devotional service certainly cannot get out of the cycle of birth and death.” (Bhag. [3.33.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.11))

In his purport to text 10, Srila Prabhupada describes how a disciple attains liberation: “Devotional service is so perfect that simply by following the rules and regulations and executing them under the direction of the spiritual master, one is liberated, as it is said herein, from the clutches of maya, even in this body. In other yogic processes, or in empiric philosophical speculation, one is never certain whether or not he is at the perfectional stage. But in the discharge of devotional service, if one has unflinching faith in the instruction of the bona fide spiritual master and follows the rules and regulations, he is sure to be liberated, even within this present body.”

From the same purport, further details about liberation: “Sometimes doubts arise in the minds of neophytes about whether or not the spiritual master is liberated, and sometimes neophytes are doubtful about the bodily affairs of the spiritual master. The point of liberation, however, is not to see the bodily symptoms of the spiritual master. One has to see the spiritual symptoms of the spiritual master. Jivan-mukta means that even though one is in the material body (there are still some material necessities, since the body is material), because one is fully situated in the service of the Lord, he should be understood to be liberated.”

Then Srila Prabhupada explains the true meaning of liberation: “Liberation entails being situated in one’s own position. That is the definition in the Srimod-Bfidgavatam: muktir. . . svarupena vyavasthitih. The svarupa, or actual identity of the living entity, is described by Lord Caitanya. Jivera ‘svariipa’ haya—krsnera ‘nitya-dasa’-. the real identity of the living entity is that he is eternally a servitor of the Supreme Lord. If someone is one-hundred-percent engaged in the service of the Lord, he is to be understood as liberated. One must understand whether or not he is liberated by his activities in devotional service, not by other symptoms.”

## Texts 12-32: Devahuti Achieves Perfection

Kapila Muni’s responsibility toward His mother is now complete. After asking her permission, He leaves home. Devahuti remains behind in her husband’s asrama, detached despite the surrounding opulence. Her son had been her only shelter. Now that he has left her, she feels sorrow at His separation, “aggrieved at the loss of her son, just as a cow is affected when her calf dies.” (Bhag. [3.33.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.21)) Srila Prabhupada’s sweet purport to this text describes how to attain the perfection of love Devahuti attained:

**The example given here is that Devahuti became just like a cow who has lost her calf. A cow bereft of her calf cries day and night. Similarly, Devahuti was aggrieved, and she always cried and requested her friends and relatives, “Please bring my son home so that I may live. Otherwise, I shall die.” This intense affection for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, although manifested as affection for one’s son, is spiritually beneficial. Attachment for a material son obliges one to remain in material existence, but the same attachment, when transferred to the Supreme Lord, brings one elevation to the spiritual world in the association of the Lord.**

**Every woman can qualify herself as much as Devahuti and then can also have the Supreme Godhead as her son. If the Supreme Personality of Godhead can appear as the son of Devahuti, He can also appear as the son of any other woman, provided that woman is qualified. If one gets the Supreme Lord as a son, one can have the benefit of bringing up a nice son in this world and at the same time get promotion to the spiritual world to become the face-to-face associate of the Personality of Godhead.**

Srila Prabhupada comments further on Devahuti’s love for Kapila Muni in his purport to text 22:

**Here is a practical example of how one can elevate oneself in spiritual advancement by Krsna consciousness. Kapiladeva is Krsna, and He appeared as the son of Devahuti. After Kapiladeva left home, Devahuti was absorbed in thought of Him, and thus she was always Krsna conscious. Her constant situation in Krsna consciousness enabled her to be detached from hearth and home.**

**Unless we are able to transfer our attachment to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, there is no possibility of becoming freed from material attachment....**

**The devotees adopt the devotional process, hearing about the Supreme Lord’s pastimes and glorifying His activities and thereby always remembering His beautiful eternal form. By rendering service, becoming His friend or His servant and offering Him everything that one possesses, one is able to enter into the kingdom of God. As it is said in Bhagavad-gita, tato mam tattvato jndtva: after discharging pure devotional service, one can understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead in fact, and thus one becomes eligible to enter into His association in one of the spiritual planets.**

It is interesting to note that the culmination of Devahuti’s having heard Kapila Muni’s teachings on bhakti mixed with jnana-yoga and astanga'yoga was that she simply became fully absorbed in love for her son, the Personality of Godhead. Srila Jiva Gosvami has commented on text 21 in anuccheda 84 of Pnti'Sandarbha. The quality of a devotee’s love for the Lord in which he wishes to give the Lord his mercy and thinks “The Lord is my son” is called vatsalya. The word vatsalya is derived from the word vatsa, calf. As a cow is affectionate toward her calf, so parents may be affectionate toward their children and hug them, holding them to their chests. This kind of love-filled relationship is called vatsalya, parental love.

This state, and this derivation of the word vatsalya, are seen in these words describing Devahuti when she was separated from her son: vatse gaur iva vatsala.

Devahuti’s grief in her separation from her son was true spiritual love, and it carried her to the Lord’s presence. Srila Prabhupada discusses the importance of spiritual separation in Krsna book: “When Krsna went to the forest with His cowherd boyfriends and cows, the gopis did not physically take part, but their hearts went with Him. And because their hearts went, they were able to enjoy His company through strong feelings of separation. To acquire this strong feeling of separation is the teaching of Lord Caitanya and His direct disciplic succession of Gosvamis. When we are not in physical contact with Krsna, we can associate with Him like the gopis, through feelings of separation. Krsna’s transcendental form, qualities, pastimes and entourage are all identical with Him. . . . Those who are in the disciplic succession of the Madhva-Gaudiya-sampradaya should always feel separation from Krsna, worship His transcendental form and discuss His transcendental teachings, His pastimes, His qualities and His entourage. That will enrich the devotees to the highest devotional perfection. Feeling constant separation while engaged in the service of the Lord is the perfection of Krsna consciousness.” (pp. 332-33)

For a nondevotee, practically nothing is auspicious, whereas for a devotee, every situation—even separation from his beloved Lord—is auspicious.

Devahuti felt great love as she continually meditated on her son, Kapiladeva. As she carefully followed His instructions on devotional service, her heart became purified and she became situated in full knowledge. Gradually the modes of material nature ceased to act on her, and she became liberated, achieving the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. “Situated in eternal trance and freed from illusion impelled by the modes of material nature, she forgot her material body, just as one forgets his different bodies in a dream.” (Bhag. [3.33.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.27)) Thus Devahuti achieved the same success through her love for her son, Kapila Muni, as achieved by the practitioner of yoga by meditating on the Supersoul: “The liberated devotee, being awake to his constitutional position and thus situated in samadhi, the highest perfectional stage of yoga, does not accept the by-products of the material body as his own. Thus he considers his bodily activities to be like the activities of a body in a dream.” (Bhag. [3.28.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/28.38))

## Texts 33-37: Maitreya Muni Offers a Benediction

Kapila Muni headed northeast and finally came to the place called Gaiiga-sagara-tirtha, where the Ganges River meets the sea at the Bay of Bengal. Srila Prabhupada gives us information about His journey in his purport to Bhagavatam [3.33.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.34): “It is understood that Kapila Muni first went towards the Himalayas and traced the course of the river Ganges, and He again came to the delta of the Ganges at the sea now known as the Bay of Bengal. The ocean gave Him residence at a place still known as Ganga-sagara, where the River Ganges meets the sea. That place is called Ganga-sagara-tirtha, and even today people gather there to offer respects to Kapiladeva, the original author of the Sankhya system of philosophy. Unfortunately, this Sankhya system has been misrepresented by an imposter who is also named Kapila, but that other system of philosophy does not tally with anything described in the Sankhya of Kapila in the Srimad-Bhagavatam.”

Even today, Lord Kapila remains in trance at Ganga-sagara for the benefit of the world. Maitreya Muni concludes his words to Vidura on Kapila Muni’s teachings with the following: “The description of the dealings of Kapiladeva and His mother is very confidential, and anyone who hears or reads this narration becomes a devotee of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is carried by Garuda, and he thereafter enters into the abode of the Supreme Lord to engage in the transcendental loving service of the Lord.” (Bhag. [3.33.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/33.37))

## CANTO FOUR

## Dialogue One - Lord Siva, Sati, and Daksa

## Chapter 1 - Genealogical Table of the Daughters of Manu

## Texts 1-10: The Descendants of Akuti

Canto Three ends with Maitreya’s description of Lord Kapila’s teachings, and Canto Four begins with Maitreya describing Svayambhuva Manu’s descendants other than Devahuti and her children. Manu had three daughters—Devahuti, Akuti, and Prasuti—and two sons—Priyavrata and Uttanapada. Maitreya Muni’s descriptions will now center on Manu’s daughters and their children and further descendants.

When Manu gave his daughter Akuti in marriage to Prajapati Ruci, it was on the condition that their firstborn son would be given to Manu to be brought up as his son. Manu knew that the Supreme Lord, Yajna, along with Yajna’s eternal consort, Laksmidevi, would take birth as his grandchildren. Yajna, who indeed was an incarnation of the Lord, later assumed the position of Indra, and His children served Him as the demigods known as the Tusitas.

## Texts 11-47: Further Descendants of Devahuti and Kardama Muni

Devahuti and Kardama Muni’s nine daughters married nine sages. Anasuya, the first daughter, married the great sage Atri Muni, and gave birth to partial incarnations of Lord Brahma (Soma), Lord Siva (Durvasa), and Lord Visnu (Dattatreya). A second daughter, Sraddha, married Arigira, and among their children was the learned scholar Brhaspati. Havirbhu, a third daughter, married the sage Pulastya. They had two sons. One of them, the saint Visrava, was the father of Ravana, Kumbhakarna, and Vibhisana. Markandeya Muni was descended from Bhrgu Muni and his wife, who was Kardama Muni’s seventh daughter. Also descending from Bhrgu was Sukracarya, the priest who led the demons. Many other exalted sages resulted from these marriages, and thus the population of the universe increased through the exalted descendants of the sage-sons of Lord Brahma and the daughters of Kardama Muni.

In text 47 Maitreya Muni offers the following benediction: “Anyone who hears the descriptions of this dynasty with faith will be relieved from all sinful reactions.”

## Texts 48-66: The Descendants of Prasuti and Daksa

Having described the descendants of both Akuti and Devahuti, two of Manu’s three daughters, Maitreya Muni next describes the descendants of the sixteen daughters of Daksa and Prasuti, Manu’s third daughter. After concluding his description of the marriages of fifteen of their daughters, Maitreya describes Sati, the youngest daughter, who was married to Lord Siva. Sati, Maitreya says, died without issue, leaving her body in the flames of a mystic trance after her father had rebuked her faultless husband.

## Chapter 2 - Daksa Curses Lord Siva

## Texts 1-19: Daksa Storms from the Sacrificial Assembly

When Vidura inquires about Satis astonishing death, Maitreya begins his reply, narrating the events of a sacrifice held in a millennium long past. Srila Prabhupada’s purport to Bhagavatam [4.2.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/2.4) offers several details: It was “a great sacrifice performed by the leaders of the universal creation, namely Marici, Daksa and Vasistha. These great personalities arranged for a great sacrifice, for which demigods like Indra and the fire-gods assembled with their followers. Lord Brahma and Lord Siva were also present.”

After they had gathered, Daksa entered the sacrificial arena. He was powerful and as effulgent as the sun. All those present—sages, demigods, philosophers, and fire-gods—immediately stood in respect. Brahma, Daksa’s father and the assembly’s president, greeted Daksa and invited him to accept a seat of honor.

Lord Siva was also present, but he was absorbed in a meditative trance when Daksa entered and therefore did not rise. One would think that etiquette would not require Siva to stand in Daksa’s honor, but because Siva had married Daksa’s daughter Sati, he had become Daksa’s son-in-law and was therefore required to offer Daksa respect.

Daksa noticed Lord Siva’s apparent neglect. Feeling the sting of insult and disrespect, his eyes glowing with anger, he said: “All sages, brahmanas and fire-gods present, please hear me with attention, for I speak about the manners of gentle persons. I do not speak out of ignorance or envy. Siva has spoiled the name and fame of the governors of the universe and has polluted the path of gentle manners. Because he is shameless, he does not know how to act. He has already accepted himself as my subordinate by marrying my daughter in the presence of fire and brahmanas. He has married my daughter, who is equal to Gayatri, and has pretended to be just like an honest person. He has eyes like a monkey’s, yet he has married my daughter, whose eyes are just like those of a deer cub. Nevertheless he did not stand up to receive me, nor did he think it fit to welcome me with sweet words.” (Bhag. [4.2.9-12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/2.9))

Daksa considered Lord Siva unqualified as a son-in-law, even though he is an empowered gund'avatara. He thought him disrespectful, poorly dressed, ignorant, impure, and shameless for not respecting him. Daksa even dared to criticize Lord Siva’s eyes, comparing them to those of a monkey. “Thus Daksa, seeing Lord Siva sitting as if against him, washed his hands and mouth and cursed him in the following words: ‘The demigods are eligible to share in the oblations of sacrifice, but Lord Siva, who is the lowest of all the demigods, should not have a share.’” (Bhag. [4.2.17-18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/2.17)) Proud, outraged, and indignant, Daksa then stormed from the assembly with the fury of lightning bolting from a rain cloud.

In his purport to text 19 Prabhupada warns readers not to succumb to anger: “Anger is so detrimental that even a great personality like Daksa, out of anger, left the arena where Brahma was presiding and all the great sages and pious and saintly persons were assembled. All of them requested him not to leave, but, infuriated, he left, thinking that the auspicious place was not fit for him. Puffed up by his exalted position, he thought that no one was greater than he in argument. It appears that all the members of the assembly, including Lord Brahma, requested him not to be angry and leave their company, but in spite of all these requests, he left. That is the effect of cruel anger.”

## Texts 20-35: The Cursing and Counter-Cursing Begin

Nandisvara, one of Lord Siva’s principal associates, heard Daksa’s curse and grew furious. With angry red eyes he pronounced a countercurse aimed not only at Daksa but at the brahmanas who had heard Daksa’s verbal attack on Lord Siva without protest. Nandisvara cried: The followers of Daksa study Vedic literature but foolishly neglect Lord Siva. They will lose their transcendental knowledge! Yes, they will be firmly fixed in their pursuits, but their pursuits will all be material. They will follow the Vedas in name only!

Thus Nandisvara cursed the brahmanas to lose their knowledge of the soul and the Supreme Personality of Godhead. His words have fructified in the appearance of the smdrta-brahmanas, those who follow the Vedas but do not understand their true purpose. Nandisvara then uttered a further curse: Daksa accepts his body as his self. He has forgotten life’s goal and is attached only to sex. In a short time he will acquire the face of a goat!

And then another: May these dull, so-called brahmanas, who have cultivated materialism, continue their cycle of birth and death! They have purposely insulted Lord Siva. Let them remain ever attached to materialistic activities. Their only goal is to maintain their bodies. “They shall be devoid of discrimination between what to eat and what not to eat. They will acquire money, begging from door to door, simply for the satisfaction of the body.” (Bhag. [4.2.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/2.26))

Hearing these curses against the brahminical class, powerful Bhrgu Muni reacted with his own strong curse: Persons vowing to satisfy Lord Siva will certainly become atheists. They will be diverted from transcendental scriptural injunctions. These persons will imitate Lord Siva. Acting in ignorance, they will grow their hair and allow it to mat, decorate their bodies with ashes, and wear bones as ornaments. They will eat flesh and drink wine. For blaspheming the brahmanas and Vedas, they have already become atheists!

In his purport to text 28 Srila Prabhupada points out that Bhrgu Muni’s curse has come true: “In the Siva Purana it is stated that Lord Siva said to Parvati that in the Kali-yuga, in the body of a brahmana, he would preach the Mayavada philosophy. Thus it is generally found that the worshipers of Lord Siva are Mayavadi followers. . . . Bhrgu Muni cursed that persons who worshiped Lord Siva would become followers of this Mayavada asat-sastra, which attempts to establish that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is impersonal. Besides that, among the worshipers of Lord Siva there is a section who live a devilish life.”

Jiva Gosvami comments (Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 106) that those who worship Lord Siva as the independent Supreme Personality of Godhead cannot surmount the influence of Bhrgu Muni’s curse.

In the midst of the cursing and counter-cursing, Lord Siva sat silent and morose. Finally, without speaking, he rose and swiftly left the sacrificial arena, followed by his disciples.

When the tumult of curses had ended, the one-thousand-year sacrifice was completed and the remaining participants returned home. It is interesting to note Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comment, cited in Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 18: “. . . Lord Siva was saved from the calamity of taking part with other demigods, who were all materialistic. Lord Siva is the greatest devotee of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and it is not fitting for him to eat or sit with materialistic persons like the demigods. Thus the curse of Daksa was indirectly a blessing, for Siva would not have to eat or sit with other demigods, who were too materialistic. . . . The conclusion is that Lord Siva behaved in his own way to avoid materialistic persons who might disturb him in his prosecution of devotional service.”

## Chapter 3 - Talks Between Lord Siva and Sati

## Texts 1-14: Daksa’s Next Sacrifice—Sati Wishes to Attend

Daksa, proud of his position as chief progenitor of the universe, planned another sacrifice, but this time refused to invite Lord Siva.

Sati, Daksa’s daughter, however, longed to attend the sacrifice; her mother and sisters would be there along with many powerful demigods and a host of brahmarsis and sages and their wives. Sati requested Lord Siva’s permission to dress up in her finery and attend the auspicious event, despite her father’s continuing offensive attitude toward her husband: “O best of the demigods, how can the body of a daughter remain undisturbed when she hears that some festive event is taking place in her father’s house? Even though you may be considering that I have not been invited, there is no harm if one goes to the house of one’s friend, husband, spiritual master or father without invitation. О immortal Siva, please be kind towards me and fulfill my desire. You have accepted me as half of your body; therefore please show kindness towards me and accept my request.” (Bhag. [4.3.13-14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/3.13))

## Texts 15-25: Lord Siva Replies to Sati

Lord Siva smiled, yet the malicious, heart-piercing curses Daksa had uttered at the previous sacrifice continued to reverberate in him. In his purport to text 15 Srila Prabhupada explains why the great, liberated Lord Siva felt unhappiness because of Daksa’s words:

**The question may now be raised why a liberated personality like Lord Siva was so unhappy because of the words of Daksa. The answer is given by Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura. Lord Siva is atmarama, or situated in complete self-realization, but because he is the incarnation in charge of the material mode of ignorance, tamo'guna, he is sometimes affected by the pleasure and pain of the material world. The difference between the pleasure and pain of this material world and that of the spiritual world is that in the spiritual world the effect is qualitatively absolute. Therefore one may feel sorry in the absolute world, but the manifestation of so-called pain is always full of bliss. For instance, once Lord Krsna, in His childhood, was chastised by His mother, Yasoda, and Lord Krsna cried. But although He shed tears from His eyes, this is not to be considered a reaction of the mode of ignorance, for the incident was full of transcendental pleasure. When Krsna was playing in so many ways, sometimes it appeared that He caused distress to the gopis, but actually such dealings were full of transcendental bliss. That is the difference between the material and spiritual worlds.**

Lord Siva’s reply forebodes calamity: Should you attend, your own father’s insults, caused by his envy, pride, and anger, will pierce your heart more deeply than an enemy’s arrow. You are my wife, and because of that your father will neither welcome nor honor you. When you are shamed because of your relationship with me, your beloved husband, your heart will be tom by grief. Going will cause only regret.

Lord Siva then spoke of his own position, explaining why he seemed to disrespect Daksa: “I am always engaged in offering obeisances to Lord Vasudeva in pure Krsna consciousness, in which the Supreme Personality of Godhead, known as Vasudeva, is revealed without any covering.” (Bhag. [4.3.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/3.23))

Srila Jiva Gosvami quotes this text (sattvarh visuddham vasudeva-sabditam) in Prti-sandarbha, anuccheda 110, to illustrate that a soul’s connection with pure spiritual goodness allows him to taste spiritual rasa. Sri Jiva also cites this text in Bhagavat-sandarbha, anuccheda 98, to illustrate that the Lord is only revealed by and within His own spiritual potency, pure goodness, sattvam visuddham.

Lord Siva continued: Although I have committed no fault in dealing with your father, he has enviously and cruelly cursed me. Do not attend the sacrifice. If you neglect my instruction and attend, you too will be insulted. You are most respectable, and when you are insulted by your father, the insult will be equal to death.

Srila Prabhupada’s purports to texts 21-23 answer several questions that typically arise:

1\. What causes anger? Why did Daksa become angry and subsequently criticize and curse Lord Siva? Srila Prabhupada explains that anger is caused by enmity. Here is an excerpt from the purport to text 21:

**Daksa was envious of Lord Siva because of Siva’s high position as an incarnation of a quality of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and because Siva was directly in contact with the Supersoul and was therefore honored and given a better sitting place than he. There were many other reasons also.
