Daksa, being materially puffed up, could not tolerate the high position of Lord Siva, so his anger at Lord Siva’s not standing up in his presence was only the final manifestation of his envy. Lord Siva is always in meditation and always perceives the Supersoul, as expressed here by the words purusa-buddhisaksinam. The position of one whose intelligence is always absorbed in meditation upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very great and cannot be imitated by anyone, especially an ordinary person. When Daksa entered the arena of yajna, Lord Siva was in meditation and might not have seen Daksa enter, but Daksa took the opportunity to curse him because Daksa had maintained an envious attitude towards Lord Siva for a long time.**

2\. To whom should one offer obeisances? Why didn’t Lord Siva stand up or offer obeisances to Daksa, his father-in-law, when Daksa entered the sacrificial arena? Srila Prabhupada writes that obeisances should be offered to the Supersoul. From Prabhupada’s purport to text 21:

**When one offers respect to the body, it is not to the material body but to the presence of the Supreme Lord. Thus one who is always in meditation upon the Supreme Lord is always offering Him obeisances. But since Daksa was not very elevated, he thought that obeisances were offered to the material body, and because Lord Siva did not offer respect to his material body, Daksa became envious. Such persons, being unable to rise to the standard of self-realized souls like Lord Siva, are always envious.**

And from earlier in the same purport: “Those who are actually selfrealized see every individual body as a temple of the Supreme Personality of Godhead because the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in His Paramatma feature, is residing in everyone’s body.”

From Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 22:

**It may be argued that since Daksa was the father-in-law of Lord Siva, it was certainly the duty of Lord Siva to offer him respect. In answer to that argument it is explained here that when a learned person stands up or offers obeisances in welcome, he offers respect to the Supersoul, who is sitting within everyone’s heart. It is seen, therefore, among Vaisnavas, that even when a disciple offers obeisances to his spiritual master, the spiritual master immediately returns the obeisances because they are mutually offered not to the body but to the Supersoul. Therefore the spiritual master also offers respect to the Supersoul situated in the body of the disciple. The Lord says in Srimad-Bhagavatam that offering respect to His devotee is more valuable than offering respect to Him. Devotees do not identify with the body, so offering respect to a Vaisnava means offering respect to Visnu. It is stated also that as a matter of etiquette as soon as one sees a Vaisnava one must immedi-ately offer him respect, indicating the Supersoul sitting within. A Vaisnava sees the body as a temple of Visnu. Since Lord Siva had already offered respect to the Supersoul in Krsna consciousness, offering respect to Daksa, who identified with his body, was already performed. There was no need to offer respect to his body, for that is not directed by any Vedic injunction.**

3\. Is it actually possible for someone situated in transcendence to disrespect any living entity? Did Siva’s failure to offer obeisances to Daksa, who was a superior in terms of their family relationship, indicate disrespect? Srila Prabhupada writes that one fixed in transcendence constantly meditates on, offers obeisances to, and serves the Supersoul in the heart of every living entity. Lord Siva was in pure consciousness, fixed in the vasudeva state, in samadhi. As he was already fixed in meditation on the Supersoul when Daksa entered the sacrificial arena, there was no need for him to separately offer respects to the Supersoul in Daksa’s heart. From Srila Prabhupada’s purport to text 23:

**Lord Siva said that since his heart was always filled with the conception of Vasudeva, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, because of the Supreme Lord’s presence within his mind and heart, he was always offering obeisances unto that Supreme Godhead. In other words, Lord Siva is always in trance, samadhi.**

## Chapter 4 - Sati Quits Her Body

## Texts 1-10: Sati Attends the Sacrifice and Becomes Offended

Hearing her husband’s words, which ran contrary to her desire, Sati became unsettled, tom between wanting to attend the sacrifice and wanting to obey her exalted husband. Srila Prabhupada describes Sati’s torment in his purport to Bhagavatam [4.4.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/4.1): “Sati’s mind was divided about whether to go to her father’s house or obey the orders of Lord Siva. The struggle between the two decisions was so strong that she was pushed from one side of the room to another, and she began to move just like the pendulum of a clock.” In his next purport Srila Prabhupada characterizes Sati’s response as typical: “Since Lord Siva could not be persuaded to give her permission, Sati took shelter of a woman’s last weapon, weeping, which forces a husband to agree to the proposal of his wife.”

Although anxious, shivering, and breathing heavily, Sati decided to attend her father’s sacrifice. She left quickly, accompanied by some of Lord Siva’s followers, who placed her on the back of Siva’s bull Nandi and covered her with a great canopy. They sang and played drums, conchshells, and bugles, making their procession resemble a royal parade. When Sati arrived at her father’s house, she entered the sacrificial arena, which was surcharged with the sound vibration of the Vedic hymns typically chanted before a sacrifice.

Prabhupada describes the auspicious scene and recommends creating similar auspiciousness by congregationally chanting Krsna’s names:

**When learned sages and brahmanas assemble to chant Vedic mantras, some of them also engage in arguing about the conclusion of the scriptures. Thus some of the sages and brahmanas were arguing, and some of them were chanting the Vedic mantras, so the entire atmosphere was surcharged with transcendental sound vibration. This transcendental sound vibration has been simplified in the transcendental vibration Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare. In this age, no one is expected to be highly educated in the Vedic ways of understanding because people are very slow, lazy and unfortunate. Therefore Lord Caitanya has recommended the sound vibration Hare Krsna, and in the Srimad-Bhagavatam (**[**11.5.32**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/5.32)**) it is also recommended: yajnaih sanldrtana'prayair yajanti hi sume' dhasah. At the present moment it is impossible to gather sacrificial necessities because of the poverty of the population and their lack of knowledge in Vedic mantras. Therefore for this age it is recommended that people gather together and chant the Hare Krsna mantra to satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is accompanied by His associates. Indirectly this indicates Lord Caitanya, who is accompanied by His associates Nityananda, Advaita and others. That is the process of performing yajna in this age. (Bhag.** [**4.4.6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/4.6)**, purport)**

Upon her arrival, however, Sati was neither greeted nor welcomed, but ignored. The other guests were afraid of Daksa; only her mother and sisters received her at all. Daksa himself offered no welcome other than his silence and his angry face. In his purport to text 7 Srila Prabhupada describes the scene: “Due to natural affection, they immediately embraced her with tears in their eyes and with loving

feelings. This shows that women as a class are very softhearted; their natural affection and love cannot be checked by artificial means. Although the men present were very learned brahmanas and demigods, they were afraid of their superior, Daksa, and because they knew that their welcoming Sati would displease him, although in their minds they wanted to receive her, they could not do so. Women are naturally softhearted, but men are sometimes very hardhearted.”

Then Sati noticed that no sacrificial oblations were being offered to her husband. Although she prohibited Siva’s followers from disrupting the sacrifice or killing Daksa, Sati decided to condemn her father before the entire assembly, her eyes aflame. Srila Prabhupada considers Sati’s reaction appropriate:

**One may prosecute the Vedic injunctions of offering sacrifices and other fruitive activities, but if by such activities one does not develop attraction for Visnu, they are useless labors. One who has developed love for Visnu must develop love and respect for Visnu’s devotees. Lord Siva is considered the foremost personality amongst the Vaisnavas. Vaisnavanam yatha sambhuh. Thus when Sati saw that her father was performing great sacrifices but had no respect for the greatest devotee, Lord Siva, she was very angry. This is fitting; when Visnu or a Vaisnava is insulted, one should be angry. Lord Caitanya, who always preached nonviolence, meekness and humility, also became angry when Nityananda was offended by Jagai and Madhai, and He wanted to kill them. When Visnu or a Vaisnava is blasphemed or dishonored, one should be very angry. Narottama dasa Thakura said, krodha bhakta-dvesi jane. We have anger, and that anger can be a great quality when directed against a person who is envious of the Supreme Personality of Godhead or His devotee. One should not be tolerant when a person is offensive towards Visnu or a Vaisnava. The anger of Sati towards her father was not objectionable, for although he was her father, he was trying to insult the greatest Vaisnava. Thus Sati’s anger against her father was quite applaudable. (Bhag.** [**4.4.10**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/4.10)**, purport)**

## Texts 11-23: Sati Angrily Speaks to Daksa

Sati’s words defending her husband were strong: “Lord Siva is the most beloved of all living entities. He has no rival. No one is very dear to him, and no one is his enemy. No one but you could be envi-ous of such a universal being, who is free from all enmity.” Sati added: Lord Siva sees and magnifies the good qualities of everyone, but you, seeing only faults, find fault with him! Because you have offended Lord Siva you will fall down, “diminished by the dust of the feet of great personalities.” (Bhag. [4.4.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/4.11), 13)

In his purport to text 12 Srila Prabhupada explains Sati’s accusations against her father. First, Sati states that Lord Siva judges the bad qualities in others as good. Srila Prabhupada writes in Sati’s voice: “You are just the opposite. Although Lord Siva has so many good qualities and no bad qualities at all, you have accepted him as bad and found fault with him. Because of your accepting his good qualities to be bad, instead of your becoming the most exalted soul you have become the most fallen. A man becomes the greatest soul by accepting the goodness of others’ qualities, but by unnecessarily considering others’ good qualities to be bad, you have become the lowest of the fallen souls.”In his purport to text 15 Prabhupada glorifies Lord Siva, and in his purport to text 13 warns against offending any great personality:

**Even Vaisnavas, who are above both the ordinary and the elevated men in this world, also worship Lord Siva as the greatest Vaisnava. Thus he is the friend of everyone—the common men, the elevated men and the devotees of the Lord—so no one should disrespect or create enmity towards Lord Siva. (Bhag.** [**4.4.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/4.15)**, purport)**

**Everything depends on the strength of the recipient. For example, due to the scorching sunshine many vegetables and flowers dry up, and many grow luxuriantly. Thus it is the recipient that causes growth and dwindling. Similarly, mahiyasam pada-rajo-bhisekam: the dust of the lotus feet of great personalities offers all good to the recipient, but the same dust can also do harm. Those who are offenders at the lotus feet of a great personality dry up; their godly qualities diminish. A great soul may forgive offenses, but Krsna does not excuse offenses to the dust of that great soul’s feet, just as one can tolerate the scorching sunshine on one’s head but cannot tolerate the scorching sunshine on one’s feet. An offender glides down more and more; therefore he naturally continues to commit offenses at the feet of the great soul. Offenses are generally committed by persons who falsely identify with the impermanent body. (Bhag.** [**4.4.13**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/4.13)**, purport)**

Sati continued her criticisms of Daksa: Even Lord Siva’s name means auspicious. No one but you envy him, as his kindness flows to both those who want material rewards and those materially frustrated souls who want liberation. Even Lord Brahma honors the flowers offered to his lotus feet. One who vilifies such a great personality is the lowest among men. My father, “the opulence we possess is impossible for either you or your flatterers to imagine . . . We can exhibit our opulences simply by desiring to do so.” (Bhag. [4.4.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/4.21)) I am ashamed of being known as Daksayani, and I therefore condemn my body, bom of you, and vow to give up my life!

In his purport to text 16 Prabhupada reveals Sati’s internal reason for wanting to attend the sacrifice: “She did not actually come to her father’s house to participate in the function, although before coming she pleaded with her husband that she wanted to see her sisters and mother. That was a plea only, for actually at heart she maintained the idea that she would convince her father, Daksa, that it was useless to continue being envious of Lord Siva. That was her main purpose.”

## Texts 24-27: Sati Quits Her Body

Sati then sat on the ground facing north. She absorbed herself in a mystic trance and raised her life airs to the cakra between her eyebrows. Becoming purified by meditating on the holy lotus feet of her husband, she renounced her self-conception as Daksayani, daughter of Prajapati Daksa. Then, filled with anger at her father, she began to meditate on the fiery air within her body. Her body then burst into flames.

Srila Prabhupada writes about Sati’s process of purification: “Sati at once thought of the lotus feet of her husband, Lord Siva, who is one of the three great personalities of Godhead in charge of the management of the material world, and simply by meditating on his lotus feet she derived such great pleasure that she forgot everything in relationship with her body.” (Bhag. [4.4.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/4.27), purport)

In the same purport Srila Prabhupada also draws a parallel between Sati’s purification and the purification undergone by devotees: “Simply by chanting the holy name of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, simply by remembering the lotus feet of Krsna, simply by offering prayers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one is immediately freed from material contamination, the material bodily concept, by the blazing fire of ecstasy. This effect takes place immediately, without a second’s delay.”

The purport continues: “According to Sri Jiva Gosvami, that Sati quit her body means that she gave up within her heart her relationship with Daksa. Sri Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura also comments that since Sati is the superintendent deity of the external potency, when she quit her body she did not get a spiritual body but simply transferred from the body she had received from Daksa. Other commentators also say that she immediately transferred herself into the womb of Menaka, her future mother. She gave up the body she had received from Daksa and immediately transferred herself to another, better body, but this does not mean that she got a spiritual body.”

## Texts 28-37: Lord Siva’s Followers Attempt to Disrupt the Sacrifice

After Sati’s dramatic death the members of the sacrifice were thrown into tumult. The attendees began to condemn Daksa, predicting that he would attain infamy because of his hard-heartedness: Envy of Lord Siva was the root cause of this calamity. Daksa had not stopped his own daughter from committing suicide. Therefore, his infamy would certainly increase.

The persons attending the sacrifice were amazed at Sati’s suicide, while Lord Siva’s followers readied themselves to kill Daksa. Bhrgu Muni saw the danger and uttered hymns from the Yajur Veda. Suddenly, from the sacrificial fire appeared thousands of Rbhu demigods. Armed with brahminical potency and half-burned wood from the fire, they attacked Sati’s attendants, causing them to disperse.

## Chapter 5 - Frustration of Daksa’s Sacrifice

## Texts 1-26: The Destruction of the Sacrifice and the Killing of Daksa

Lord Siva was outraged when he heard from Narada Muni that his wife had committed suicide and his followers had been driven from the sacrificial arena. He pressed his lips against his teeth and in fury snatched a strand of hair from his head. The hair blazed like fire. He stood up, laughing like a madman, and dashed it to the ground. The hair immediately transformed into a fearful black demon named Virabhadra. The demon stood before Lord Siva with folded hands and asked him for orders. Lord Siva commanded Virabhadra to go along with his soldiers to the arena and kill Daksa and his soldiers.

Meanwhile, at the arena the sacrifice had continued despite Sati’s death. As Virabhadra and the others came on, however, the participants noticed a great dust storm approaching. Dangerous omens appeared both on earth and in the sky. Although Daksa had remained steady and unshaken even as his beloved daughter killed herself, he became afraid to see the disturbance. Prasuti, Daksa’s wife and the mother of Sati, predicted disaster, knowing how seriously Daksa’s insults had pained Sati. She knew Daksa would die for failing to save his own daughter from suicide.

On reaching the sacrificial arena, Virabhadra bared his teeth. When he moved his eyebrows, “he scattered the luminaries all over the sky, and he covered them with his strong, piercing effulgence.” (Bhag. [4.5.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/5.11)) Armies of Lord Siva’s followers, who resembled black and yellow sharks, joined Virabhadra in surrounding the sacrificial arena. All were filled with anger and bent on destruction. “Some of the soldiers pulled down the pillars which were supporting the pandal of sacrifice, some of them entered the female quarters, some began destroying the sacrificial arena, and some entered the kitchen and the residential quarters.” (Bhag. [4.5.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/5.14)) They broke pots made for the sacrifice and began to extinguish the sacrificial fire. “Some tore down the boundary line of the sacrificial arena, and some passed urine on the arena. Some blocked the way of the fleeing sages, some threatened the women assembled there, and some arrested the demigods who were fleeing the pandal.” (Bhag. [4.5.15-16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/5.15)) They showered stones on the arena. Fearing for their lives, the priests and other participants attempted to flee.

Virabhadra ripped off Bhrgu Muni’s moustache as he attempted to offer sacrificial oblations to the fire. He grabbed Bhaga, who had moved his eyebrows during Daksa’s cursing of Lord Siva, and in anger forced him to the ground and put out his eyes.

Virabhadra then knocked out the teeth of both Daksa, who had shown them while cursing Lord Siva, and Pusa, who had smiled sympathetically and also shown his teeth. That giantlike personality then sat on Daksa’s chest and tried unsuccessfully to cut Daksa’s head from his body with sharp weapons and hymns. Frustrated, Virabhadra saw the wooden device used to behead sacrificial animals and used it to behead Daksa. “Upon seeing the action of Virabhadra, the party of Lord Siva was pleased and cried out joyfully, and all the bhutas, ghosts and demons that had come made a tumultuous sound. On the other hand, the brahmanas in charge of the sacrifice cried out in grief at the death of Daksa.” (Bhag. [4.5.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/5.25)) Then, after throwing Daksa’s head into the southern side of the sacrificial fire, and after setting the entire arena ablaze, Lord Siva’s followers returned to their master’s abode, Kailasa.

## Chapter 6 - Brahma Satisfies Lord Siva

## Texts 1-41: The Demigods and Lord Brahma Journey to Mount Kailasa in an Attempt to Satisfy Lord Siva

Defeated and dejected, the priests, demigods, and other participants fearfully approached Lord Brahma. The unborn son of Visnu consoled them, explaining that happiness flees from those who offend and blaspheme great personalities: Lord Brahma also advised them that Lord Siva was so powerful that by his anger all the planets and their chief controllers could immediately be destroyed. Also, he said, Lord Siva was grieving for his lost wife and was also afflicted by Daksa’s unkind words. Brahma continued: Yet although you have offended him and excluded him from his share of the sacrifice, Lord Siva will nevertheless become pleased if you surrender to his lotus feet and beg his pardon.

In his purport to text 5 Srila Prabhupada explains Lord Siva’s magnanimous nature: “Lord Siva is also called Asutosa. Asu means ‘very soon,’ and tosa means ‘to become satisfied.’ The demigods were advised to go to Lord Siva and beg his pardon, and because he is very easily pleased, it was certain that their purpose would be served. Lord Brahma knew the mind of Lord Siva very well, and he was confident that the demigods, who were offenders at his lotus feet, could mitigate their offenses by going to him and surrendering without reservation.”

How horrible and destructive are the reactions to offending powerful devotees! The Padma Purana states, satarh ninda ndmnah paramam aparadham vitanute, yatah khyatirh yatarh katham и sahate tad-vigarham: To blaspheme great saintly persons is the worst offense at Nama Prabhu’s lotus feet. Sastra warns again and again against committing Vaisnava aparadha. In Caitanya-caritamrta Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami likens offenses against Vaisnavas to a had mata, a mad elephant. As a mad elephant on the loose destroys a garden, offending a Vaisnava destroys the growth of the creeper of devotion. In his Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 153, Srila Jiva Gosvami lists five obstacles to pure devotional service that result from offenses:

1. crookedness
2. faithlessness
3. attachment to things that destroy faith in the Lord
4. slackness in devotional service
5. pride in being devotionally advanced

Sri Jiva adds that if one has these symptoms, it indicates that one has committed offenses either in this life or in previous lives. Krsna will not accept the service of one who possesses the fault of crookedness, Sri Jiva explains, even if that person offers him many valuable items. He gives Duryodhana as an example: Duryodhana once made sumptuous arrangements for Krsna’s meal when Krsna was visiting as Yudhisthira’s peace messenger, but Krsna only laughed at Duryodhana’s attempt at diplomacy and would not eat. He preferred to eat with His devotee Vidura, even though the meal consisted of nothing but bananas. Thus by His actions, Krsna showed His unwillingness to accept service from those possessing an offensive attitude toward His devotees.Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu gives two strict warnings about committing Vaisnava aparadha in the Caitanya-bhagavata, Antya-khanda, [3.444-63](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-antya/3.444). After Lord Caitanya accepted sannyasa and had lived for some time in Jagannatha Puri, He visited Kuliya-grama near Navadvipa. Thousands came to see the Lord, and all were delivered. A brahmana approached Mahaprabhu and tightly embraced His feet, saying, “Unaware of the glory of devotional service, I committed many sins. I blasphemed many Vaisnavas. I would say, ‘How, in Kali-yuga is it possible for anyone to be a true Vaisnava? How can anyone truly sing kirtana?’ Moment after moment I blasphemed many Vaisnavas in this way. Moment after moment, remembering these sins, my heart bums with grief. О lion who delivers all the worlds, please tell me how I can break my sins into pieces.”

**Hearing the brahmana's sincere words, Lord Caitanya smiled and spoke this remedy: “O brahmana, please listen. If with his own mouth a person drinks poison, and then with the same mouth drinks the nectar of immortality, then the poison will wither and the nectar will make that person’s body immortal. Please hear this explanation.**

**“Not knowing what was happening, you blasphemed Vaisnavas. In this way you drank poison. Now with your mouth you should always drink the nectar of Lord Krsna’s holy names and qualities. The same mouth that once blasphemed Vaisnavas should now sing their praises. О brahmana, in poetry and song you should sing the devotees’ glories.**

**“What I say is the truth. If a person who unwittingly commits blasphemy stops blaspheming others and instead praises Lord Visnu and the Vaisnavas, then that person will destroy all his sins. That is the right way to destroy them. Millions of rituals of atonement will not destroy them. О brahmana, go and sing the glories of the devotees. Then you will become free of all sins.”**

**Hearing these words from the Lord’s graceful mouth, the Vaisnavas called out, “Jaya! Jaya! Hari!” In this way Lord Caitanya described the best atonement for the sin of blasphemy. Any sinner who, not honoring Lord Caitanya’s order, blasphemes the Vaisnavas will be plunged in an ocean of suffering. Anyone who honors Lord Caitanya’s order as the essence of the Vedas will become happy. He will cross the ocean of repeated birth and death.**

A second grave warning issued from the lips of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu when a leper came before Him and offered dandavat obeisances as he wept in pain (CB Antya [4.346-385](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/4.346)):

**“O merciful Lord,” the leper said. “You descended to deliver the world and are unable to tolerate the sufferings of others. I have therefore come before You. I am tormented by leprosy. My body bums with pain. Please tell me how I may be cured.”**

**Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu angrily replied, “Die, sinner! When people see you, sin takes birth in them. Even saintly persons must suffer the moment they set eyes on you. You have blasphemed a Vaisnava. How much more suffering awaits you! Even the word Vaisnava purifies the world. Brahma and the demigods sing the Vaisnavas’ glories. One who worships Vaisnavas attains Lord Krsna. Nothing is greater than worshiping Vaisnavas. Anyone who blasphemes a Vaisnava will suffer in life and after death. Those who blaspheme Vaisnavas are sinners. Such persons’ education, noble family, austerities, and other virtues are fruitless. Lord Krsna will not accept the worship of such persons.**

**“Srivasa Pandita is a great Vaisnava, but you blasphemed his character. These flames of leprosy are only the beginning of your punishment; Yamaraja will punish you far more in the future. You are not worthy for Me to look upon. It will not be I who delivers you.”**

**Upon hearing the Lord’s words, the leper placed a blade of grass between his teeth and said pitifully, “1 do not know anything. I went mad and blasphemed a Vaisnava, so it is right that I am punished. Still, You are the Supreme Controller. Please think of my welfare also. It is the nature of a saint to rescue those who suffer. A saintly person will be merciful even to a blasphemer. Therefore I surrender at Your feet. If You reject me, who will deliver me? You know everything about atonement. Please tell me how I can atone for my sin.”**

**Lord Caitanya replied, “Sastra reveals that those who blaspheme Vaisnavas will contract leprosy, yet that is only their present punishment. How many torments will follow at Yamaraja’s hands? Those who blaspheme Vaisnavas again and again will suffer fourteen thousand tortures in Yamaraja’s kingdom. Leper, run to Srivasa Pandita and fall at his feet to beg forgiveness. You blasphemed him, so only his mercy can deliver you. Go, and he will forgive and deliver you.”**

**Hearing the Lord’s words, the devotees present loudly called, “Jaya! Jaya!" After again offering dandavat obeisances before the Lord, the leper left at once to take shelter of Srivasa Pandita. He attained the Pandita’s mercy and was delivered, his offenses broken into pieces.**

The priests, demigods, and others who attended Daksa’s sacrifices also feared their participation in the blasphemy of Siva, a Vaisnava. Fearing Lord Siva’s wrath they accepted Lord Brahma’s advice and journeyed along with him to opulent Mount Kailasa, where they found Lord Siva sitting beneath a banyan tree, calm and as grave as eternal time. He was surrounded by the four Kumaras and other saints, and he sat on a deerskin, his body smeared with ashes. His countenance reminded them of an evening cloud. Sitting in virasana, his left leg placed on his right thigh, Lord Siva held his right hand in the tarka-mudra to impress on his audience, which included Narada Muni, the point he was making about the Absolute Truth.

The demigods and sages approached Lord Siva and immediately offered their respectful obeisances in worship of his lotus feet. As they did so, Lord Siva rose to offer his own respects to Lord Brahma, who with a smile reciprocated by glorifying Lord Siva’s power.

Srila Prabhupada explains the reason for Lord Brahma’s smile in his purport to text 41: “Lord Brahma was smiling because he knew that Lord Siva is not only easily satisfied but easily irritated as well. He was afraid that Lord Siva might be in an angry mood because he had lost his wife and had been insulted by Daksa. In order to conceal this fear, he smiled and addressed Lord Siva as follows.”

## Texts 42-53: Brahma’s Words to Lord Siva

Brahma honored Lord Siva as both different and nondifferent from Lord Visnu, the transcendental controller of the cosmos. Brahma said: “My dear lord, you create this cosmic manifestation, maintain it, and annihilate it by expansion of your personality, exactly as a spider creates, maintains and winds up its web. My dear lord, Your Lordship has introduced the system of sacrifices through the agency of Daksa, and thus one may derive the benefits of religious activities and economic development.” (Bhag. [4.6.43-44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/6.43)) Generally all souls attain their just rewards—the pious are rewarded and the sinful punished. “Yet sometimes it is found that their destinations are just the opposite. It is very difficult to ascertain the cause of this.” (Bhag. [4.6.45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/6.45))

Srila Prabhupada describes how a devotee considers this seeming anomaly: “The Supreme Personality of Godhead is called the supreme will. It is by the supreme will that everything is happening. It is said, therefore, that not a blade of grass moves without the supreme will. . . . The conclusion is . . . that the supreme will is the ultimate judgment; no one can argue upon this. A pure devotee therefore submits in all circumstances to the supreme will of the Lord, accepting it as all-auspicious.” (Bhag. [4.6.45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/6.45), purport)

Brahma continued: Pure souls, devotees, never become angry, for they recognize the Lord as the sanction-giver, the Paramatma in the heart of each living entity. Providence demands that the envious, the materially attached, and those who cause others distress by uttering harsh or piercing words die. There is no need for them to be killed again by an exalted personality like you. Knowing the Lord’s position as the ultimate giver of sanction, and the conditioned soul’s position as always overpowered by the Lord’s maya, saintly persons do not take seriously the offenses of materialists.

Lord Brahma’s point is easy to understand, but to act on it demands pure devotion. Therefore, one should not attempt to imitate a realization one does not yet possess. Rather, one should walk the path the great souls have prescribed both in their instructions and by their example, and gradually come to the proper vision. Lord Brahma has spoken a great truth: one should see Krsna’s hand in everything that occurs, even when it is obvious that the modes of material nature are simultaneously at work. We have noted this point in Prabhupada’s purport to Bhagavatam [3.1.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/1.16): “In spite of being very strongly insulted by Duryodhana’s words, Vidura could see that Duryodhana, under the influence of maya, the external energy, was making progress on the path toward his own ruination. He therefore considered the acts of the external energy to be supreme, yet he also saw how the internal energy of the Lord helped him in that particular situation. . . . Maya, the supreme energy of the Lord, acted here both internally and externally.”

Lord Brahma told Lord Siva that although Daksa’s actions were full of pride and envy, Lord Siva’s purity had awarded him the vision to see Krsna’s will in all events. Saints like Lord Siva do not need to counteract envious persons. “My dear lord, you are never bewildered by the formidable influence of the illusory energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore you are omniscient and should be merciful and compassionate toward those who are bewildered by the same illusory energy and are very much attached to fruitive activities.” (Bhag. [4.6.49](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/6.49))

Brahma then humbly placed before Lord Siva the following requests (texts 50-53): That he undo the destruction his followers had caused during Daksa’s sacrifice; that he allow King Daksa to regain his life, Bhaga his eyes, Bhrgu his mustache, and Pilsa his teeth; that he allow the demigods and priests injured during the sacrifice to recover; and that he please accept his portion of the sacrifice. “Let the sacrifice be completed by your grace.”

## Chapter 7 - The Sacrifice Performed by Daksa

## Texts 1-5: Lord Siva Replies to Lord Brahma

By killing Daksa and ruining the sacrifice, Lord Siva appeared angry and vengeful, but Brahma’s sweet words pacified him and he then revealed his actual mood and intent: “My dear father, Brahma, I do not mind the offenses created by the demigods. Because these demigods are childish and less intelligent, I do not take a serious view of their offenses, and I have punished them only in order to right them.” (Bhag. [4.7.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.2))

In his purport to this text, Prabhupada explains further: “There are two types of punishment. One is that which a conqueror imposes on an enemy, and the other is like that a father imposes on his son. There is a gulf of difference between these two kinds of punishment. Lord Siva is by nature a Vaisnava, a great devotee, and his name in this connection is Asutosa. He is always satisfied, and therefore he did not become angry as if he were an enemy. He is not inimical to any living entity; rather, he always wishes the welfare of all. Whenever he chastises a person, it is just like a father’s punishment of his son. Lord Siva is like a father because he never takes seriously any offense by any living entities, especially the demigods.”

Just as a scar may cover a deep wound, Lord Siva agreed to mitigate his punishments but leave a “scar” to remind those who were punished not to commit the same mistake again. Lord Siva said: “Since the head of Daksa has already been burned to ashes, he will have the head of a goat. The demigod known as Bhaga will be able to see his share of sacrifice through the eyes of Mitra. The demigod Piisa will be able to chew only through the teeth of his disciples, and if alone, he will have to satisfy himself by eating dough made from chickpea flour. But the demigods who have agreed to give me my share of the sacrifice will recover from all their injuries. Those who have had their arms cut off will have to work with the arms of Asvini-kumara, and those whose hands were cut off will have to do their work with the hands of Pusa. The priests will also have to act in that manner. As for Bhrgu, he will have the beard from the goat’s head.” (Bhag. [4.7.3-5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.3))

## Texts 6-12: Daksa Regains His Life and Apologizes to Lord Siva

Returning with the demigods to the sacrificial arena, Lord Siva directed Daksa’s body to be joined with the head of the goat intended for the sacrifice. The demigods carefully followed Siva’s instructions. Then Daksa, as if awakening from sleep, returned to consciousness and saw Lord Siva before him. Daksa’s first response was reverential; his heart, polluted by envy, had obviously been cleansed.

Srila Prabhupada describes Lord Siva’s auspiciousness in his purport to text 10: “Here is an example of why Lord Siva is called auspicious. If anyone sees Lord Siva with devotion and reverence, his heart is immediately cleansed. King Daksa was polluted by envy of Lord Siva, and yet by seeing him with a little love and devotion, his heart immediately became cleansed. In the rainy season, the reservoirs of water become dirty and muddy, but as soon as the autumn rain comes, all the water immediately becomes clear and transparent. Similarly, although Daksa’s heart was impure because of his having slandered Lord Siva, for which he was severely punished, Daksa now came to consciousness, and just by seeing Lord Siva with veneration and respect, he became immediately purified.”

At once King Daksa wished to offer Lord Siva prayers, but as he remembered the ill-fated death of his daughter Sati, his eyes filled with tears and his voice choked in bereavement. With great endeavor, he pacified his mind, checked his feelings, and with pure consciousness began to offer prayers to Lord Siva.

## Texts 13-15: Daksa Speaks to Lord Siva

Daksa said: О Lord Siva, you have kindly purified me by punishing me. Despite my offenses you have not neglected me. Both you and Lord Visnu always protect brahmanas, and as the “protector of the brahmanas, you always protect the regulative principles they follow, just as a cowherd boy keeps a stick in his hand to give protection to the cows. I did not know your full glories. For this reason, I threw arrows of sharp words at you in the open assembly, although you did not take them into account. I was going down to hell because of my disobedience to you, who are the most respectable personality, but you took compassion upon me and saved me by awarding punishment. I request that you be pleased by your own mercy, since I cannot satisfy you by my words.” (Bhag. [4.7.14-15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.14))Thus Daksa admitted his faults to Lord Siva and begged to be excused. Prabhupada describes that Daksa accepted his punishment as Krsna’s mercy on him:

**As usual, a devotee in an adverse condition of life accepts such a condition to be the mercy of the Lord. Factually, the insulting words used by Daksa against Lord Siva were enough to have him thrown perpetually into a hellish life. But Lord Siva, being kind toward him, awarded him punishment to neutralize the offense. King Daksa realized this and, feeing obliged for Lord Siva’s magnanimous behavior, wanted to show his gratitude. Sometimes a father punishes his child, and when the child is grown up and comes to his senses, he understands that the father’s punishment was not actually punishment but mercy. Similarly, Daksa appreciated that the punishment offered to him by Lord Siva was a manifestation of Lord Siva’s mercy. That is the symptom of a person making progress on the path of Krsna consciousness. It is said that a devotee in Krsna consciousness never takes any miserable condition of life to be condemnation by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He accepts the miserable condition to be the grace of the Lord. He thinks, “1 would have been punished or put into a more dangerous condition of life due to my past misdeeds, but the Lord has protected me. Thus I have received only a little punishment as token execution of the law of karma.” Thinking of His grace in that way, a devotee always surrenders to the Supreme Personality of Godhead more and more seriously and is not disturbed by such so-called punishment. (Bhag.** [**4.7.15**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.15)**, purport)**

## Texts 16-25: Lord Visnu Appears in the Sacrificial Arena

Pardoned by Lord Siva, and with Lord Brahma’s permission, Daksa resumed the yajna. The brahmanas first purified the arena and then offered the oblation known as purodasa into the fire. As soon as King Daksa offered the clarified butter with Yajur Veda mantras in sanctified meditation, Lord Visnu appeared in His original form as Narayana. The area was illuminated by the Lord’s beauty, and all the others present seemed suddenly insignificant. Even Lord Brahma’s luster was overpowered. Lord Visnu had a beautiful blackish complexion and bluish hair. His body resembled a blossoming tree decorated with fragrant flowers. Lord Brahma, Lord Siva, Daksa, and everyone else fell like rods to offer their respects. Filled with awe, no one spoke, because no one, not even Lord Brahma, could fully understand the Lord’s limitless glories.

Krsna Himself states in Bhagavad-gita ([10.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.2)) that it is impossible to know Him fully: “Neither the hosts of demigods nor the great sages know My origin or opulences, for, in every respect, I am the source of the demigods and sages.” One can only appreciate the Lord according to the depth of his realization of Him, and that realization is based on the purity of one’s consciousness.

According to the purity of their realization, therefore, theists appreciate God as angry, fearful, loving, the creator, the all-powerful, the all-merciful, the all-intelligent, the lawmaker, the provider, as He who awards material wealth, or as the supreme problem solver. Each of these views is correct but incomplete, because all realizations of the Supreme Lord are simply manifestations of Krsna’s reciprocation with an individual’s mentality. Srila Prabhupada summarizes this point in his purport to text 24: “The Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead, is always unlimited, and His glories cannot be completely enumerated by anyone, even by a personality like Lord Brahma. It is said that Ananta, a direct incarnation of the Lord, has unlimited mouths, and with each mouth He has been trying to describe the glories of the Lord for an unlimited span of time, yet the glories of the Lord remain unlimited, and He therefore never finishes. It is not possible for any ordinary living entity to understand or to glorify the unlimited Personality of Godhead, but one can offer prayers or service to the Lord according to one’s particular capacity. This capacity is increased by the service spirit.”

Srila Prabhupada also explained this point in a lecture delivered in Sri Mayapur-dhama in 1976: “Ye yathd mam prapadyante tarns tathaiva bhajamy aham: It is up to you too. If you surrender cent percent, then Krsna is also fully cent percent for you. But if you have got discrimination—certain percentage for my wife, certain percentage for my children, certain percentage for my country, certain percent. . ., so on, so on, so on, so on, ultimately, ‘Zero for God,’ then God is also zero. It is up to you. But if you take God—‘You are my everything’—then He is also for you, everything.”

To understand how individual souls view the Supreme Lord differently, one can think of how a king is seen by his citizens. A prisoner sees the king as his greatest enemy, whereas the king’s loyal subjects see him as their hero. The members of the court see the king as someone to impress, but the king’s intimate friends will treat him as an equal. The king’s parents may still view him as their small son despite his displays of power. His children, wife, and other family members tend to forget his position and deal with him in intimacy.

One may naturally inquire what Krsna is like when He is fully realized and thus fully uncovered. The Bhagavatam’s Tenth Canto reveals the Absolute Truth in that most complete aspect as Sri Krsna in Vrndavana. There, Krsna acts with His intimate devotees as He desires. He is present in His all-beautiful feature and wanders around His favorite places engaging in pastimes with His closest devotees. Here in the Fourth Canto, however, we will hear about the Lord as He is seen through the realizations of those present and fortunate enough to see Him at Daksa’s sacrifice.

## Texts 26-47: Each Person in the Assembly Glorifies Lord Visnu According to His Own Realization

With great pleasure at the Lord’s arrival, Prajapati Daksa first offered his respectful obeisances: “My dear Lord, You are transcendental to all speculative positions. You are completely spiritual, devoid of all fear, and You are always in control of the material energy.

Even though You appear in the material energy, You are situated transcendentally. You are always free from material contamination because You are completely self-sufficient.” (Bhag. [4.7.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.26)) Thus Daksa expressed his realization that the Lord was free from material contamination, self-sufficient, and transcendental (beyond matter).

The sacrificial priests next offered their prayer: “O Lord, transcendental to material contamination, by the curse offered by Lord Siva’s men we have become attached to fruitive activities, and thus we are now fallen and therefore do not know anything about You. On the contrary, we are now involved in the injunctions of the three departments of the Vedic knowledge under the plea of executing rituals in the name of yajna.” (Bhag. [4.7.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.27)) Thus the priests confirmed by their own experience that those who are selfishly engaged lose their ability to know the Lord.

The members of the assembly explained to the Lord that time, like a snake, awaits its chance to strike the conditioned souls. These suffering souls, tom between seeking happiness and avoiding distress, feeling the heat of the blazing fire of lamentation and the alluring mirages of happiness from which they cannot escape, and feeling overburdened by so-called duties, are unable to gain shelter at His lotus feet. Srila Prabhupada describes the benediction the Krsna consciousness movement may offer such troubled souls: “Persons who are not in Krsna consciousness are living a very precarious life, as described in this verse, but all these circumstantial conditions are due to forgetfulness of Krsna. The Krsna consciousness movement is meant to give relief to all these bewildered and distressed persons; therefore it is the greatest relief work for all human society, and the workers thereof are the greatest well-wishers, for they follow in the footsteps of Lord Caitanya, who is the greatest friend to all living entities.” (Bhag. [4.7.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.28), purport)

What happens when one focuses fully on the Lord? Lord Siva prays: “My dear Lord, my mind and consciousness are always fixed on Your lotus feet, which, as the source of all benediction and the fulfillment of all desires, are worshiped by all liberated great sages ... With my mind fixed on Your lotus feet, I am no longer disturbed by persons who blaspheme me, claiming that my activities are not purified. I do not mind their accusations, and I excuse them out of compassion, just as You exhibit compassion toward all living entities.” (Bhag. [4.7.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.29))

In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada explains that Lord Siva regretted his anger: “Lord Siva expresses herein his regret at having been angry and having disturbed the sacrificial activities of Daksa. King Daksa had insulted him in many ways, and thus he had become angry and had frustrated the entire sacrificial ceremony. Later, when he was pleased, the yajna performances were reinstituted, and therefore he regretted his activities. Now he says that because his mind is fixed on the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord, Visnu, he is no longer disturbed by the ordinary critics of his way of life. From this statement by Lord Siva it is understood that as long as one is on the material platform one is affected by the three modes of material nature. As soon as one is in Krsna consciousness, however, one is no longer affected by such material activities. One should therefore always be fixed in Krsna consciousness, busy in the transcendental loving service of the Lord. It is guaranteed that such a devotee will never be affected by the actions and reactions of the three modes of material nature.”

Sri Bhrgu Muni then described those in need of the Lord’s instructions and mercy: “My dear Lord, all living entities, beginning from the highest, namely Lord Brahma, down to the ordinary ant, are under the influence of the insurmountable spell of illusory energy, and thus they are ignorant of their constitutional position. Everyone believes in the concept of the body, and all are thus submerged in the darkness of illusion. They are actually unable to understand how You live in every living entity as the Supersoul, nor can they understand Your absolute position. But You are the eternal friend and protector of all surrendered souls. Therefore, please be kind toward us and forgive all our offenses.” (Bhag. [4.7.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.30))

Srila Prabhupada gives a poignant explanation of the living entity’s forgotten relationship with the Lord: “Ignorant personalities, or conditioned souls, have no choice but to accept their precarious condition under material nature. The only remedy is to surrender to Visnu and always pray to be excused. One should depend only on the causeless mercy of the Lord for deliverance and not even slightly on one’s own strength. That is the perfect position of a Krsna conscious person. The Lord is everyone’s friend, but He is especially friendly to the surrendered soul. The simple process, therefore, is that a conditioned soul should remain surrendered to the Lord, and the Lord will give him all protection to keep him out of the clutches of material contamination.” (Bhag. [4.7.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.30), purport)

Lord Brahma, the most intelligent person in the universe, spoke next. He first acknowledged his own limitations in knowing the transcendental Lord, who is unknowable by the empiric process. The Lord may only be understood by His mercy by perfecting one’s service attitude. Otherwise, Srila Prabhupada writes in his purport to text 31, “the Supreme Lord cannot be understood by materialistic persons even though He is present before them.”

Indra, the chief demigod, then described the appearance of the unknowable Lord, who was inconceivably standing before him: “My dear Lord, Your transcendental form with eight hands and weapons in each of them appears for the welfare of the entire universe, and it is very pleasing to the mind and eyes. In such a form, Your Lordship is always prepared to punish the demons, who are envious of Your devotees.” (Bhag. [4.7.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.32)) Indra’s prayer clarifies Brahma’s prayer by adding that although one cannot perceive the Lord’s activities or form through the power of his material senses, he may nevertheless understand something about the Unknowable. Prabhupada writes: “As Lord Brahma had said, to realize the transcendental form of the Lord is beyond the power of the senses. In reply to that statement by Brahma, King Indra said that even though the transcendental form of the Lord is not perceivable by the material senses, His activities and His transcendental form can be understood. The Lord’s uncommon features, uncommon activities and uncommon beauty can be perceived even by an ordinary man. For example, when Lord Krsna appeared just like a six- or seven-year-old boy in Vrndavana, He was approached by the residents there. There were torrents of rain, and the Lord saved the residents of Vrndavana by lifting Govardhana Hill and resting it on the little finger of His left hand for seven days. This uncommon feature of the Lord should convince even materialistic persons who want to speculate to the limit of their material senses.”

One by one the wives of the performers of the sacrifice, the sages, Siddhas, Daksa’s wife, the universal protectors, mystics, personified Vedas, fire-god, demigods, Gandharvas, Vidyadharas, and brahmanas —each according to their experience and realization—offered prayers and glorified the Lord by describing His qualities and position.

## Texts 48-54: The Sacrifice Begins and Lord Visnu Instructs Daksa

When all present had glorified Lord Visnu, Daksa again began to perform the same yajna that had been devastated by Lord Siva’s followers. Maitreya Muni tells Vidura that Lord Visnu, although the supreme proprietor, the Supersoul, and the ultimate enjoyer of the results of all sacrifices, was nevertheless satisfied simply with His allotted share. The Lord then addressed Daksa, explaining to him the philosophy of acintya-bhedabheda, simultaneous difference and non-difference between Himself and all things: “Brahma, Lord Siva and I are the supreme cause of the material manifestation. I am the Supersoul, the self-sufficient witness.... I am the original Personality of Godhead, but in order to create, maintain and annihilate this cosmic manifestation, I act through My material energy, and according to the different grades of activity, My representations are differently named. . . . One who is not in proper knowledge thinks that demigods like Brahma and Siva are independent, or he even thinks that the living entities are independent. A person with average intelligence does not think the head and other parts of the body to be separate. Similarly, My devotee does not differentiate Visnu, the all-pervading Personality of Godhead, from any thing or any living entity. . . . One who does not consider Brahma, Visnu, Siva or the living entities in general to be separate from the Supreme, and who knows Brahman, actually realizes peace; others do not.” (Bhag. [4.7.50-54](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.50))

Thus Lord Visnu explained Himself as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Supersoul, and the creator, maintainer, and destroyer of the material world. As He is the Supersoul on which everything in existence rests, no difference exists between Him and Lord Brahma or Lord Siva. On the absolute level of Brahman, nothing is different from the Lord because everything comes from Him. It is He alone who is acting through different levels of material energy during creation, maintenance, and destruction. No one is independent or equal to Him. Devotees understand that nothing and no one—not even Brahma or Siva—are separate from Lord Visnu. One who sees everything as nondifferent from Lord Visnu actually realizes peace.

Srila Prabhupada writes about acintya-bhedabheda-tattva in his purport to text 54: “Two words are very significant in this verse. Trayanam indicates ‘three,’ namely Lord Brahma, Lord Siva and Lord Visnu. Bhidam means ‘different.’ They are three, and therefore they are separate, but at the same time they are one. This is the philosophy of simultaneous oneness and difference, which is called acintya-bheda.' bheda-tattva. The example given in the Brahma-samhitd is that milk and yogurt are simultaneously one and different; both are milk, but the yogurt has become changed. In order to achieve real peace, one should see everything and every living entity, including Lord Brahma and Lord Siva, as nondifferent from the Supreme Personality of Godhead. No one is independent. Every one of us is an expansion of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This accounts for unity in diversity. There are diverse manifestations, but, at the same time, they are one in Visnu. Everything is an expansion of Visnu’s energy.”

On a separate level, the jivas too are nondifferent from the Lord, also being expansions of His potencies. Srila Prabhupada explained this in a 1974 lecture in Mayapur: “There are many potencies of God, Krsna. Parasya saktir vividhaiva sruyate. Many millions. So they have been summarized into three. What is that? The external potency, the internal potency, and third, the marginal potency. The marginal potency and internal potency are of the same quality.”

The jivas, the Lord’s marginal potency, are thus also eternally Krsna’s energy, His parts and parcels. As such, each jiva has an individual unbreakable relationship with Him. Yet despite the fact that such a relationship is at the foundation of a jiva’s existence, conditioned souls suffer like elephants unable to escape a forest fire.

On the other hand, awakening their relationship with Krsna can bring them peace, because Krsna is everyone’s dearest friend: “The source of satisfaction is Krsna. Santi. Suhrdarh sarva-bhutanam jnatva mam santim rcchati. When you know Krsna as the friend of everyone, at that time you get satisfaction. How nice. Everything is so nice.” (Conversation, San Diego, 1972)

In his Paramatma-sandarbha, anuccheda 17, Srila Jiva Gosvami supports Lord Visnu’s statement that He Himself is the Supreme, while maintaining that no one, not even Lord Brahma and Lord Siva, is different from Him. He presents a skeptical response from a hypothetical reader of text 54 who believes that Visnu, Brahma, and Siva are equally supreme. Sri Jiva writes, “We do not propound that they are different.” Sri Jiva explains that all three are forms of the one parama-purusa. Lord Siva and Lord Brahma are seen as different from Lord Visnu in nature, but in their engagement in creation and destruction they are not independent of Him and should not be confused with Him. Lord Visnu is supreme and is the source of both Brahma and Siva.

Sri Jiva further explains that although some Puranas do proclaim Siva as supreme, the statements of the Puranas in the mode of goodness are more authoritative. Not all Puranas are on the same level: those in goodness glorify Visnu, those in passion glorify Brahma, and those in ignorance glorify Siva. In Bhagavad-gita Krsna says that knowledge

is bom of goodness. If one wants actual knowledge, one must receive information from Puranas in the mode of goodness.

## Texts 55-57: Daksa Completes the Yajna and Satisfies All Who Participated

After hearing Lord Visnu’s instructions Daksa worshiped the Lord, then separately worshiped Lord Brahma and Lord Siva. With full respect he offered Lord Siva his share of the sacrificial remnants. Fully satisfied, purified, and again situated in religiosity, Daksa was blessed by all the demigods. Thus the great sacrifice conducted by Daksa ended in harmony and peace.

## Texts 58-61: Maitreya Offers Benedictions to Those Who Hear and Narrate this Pastime

Maitreya concludes by telling Vidura that Sati was later reborn as the daughter of Menaka in the Himalayas and again accepted Lord Siva as her husband. Completing his narration, Maitreya offers a benediction: “If one who hears and again narrates, with faith and devotion, this story of the Daksa yajna as it was conducted by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Visnu, then certainly one is cleared of all contamination of material existence, О son of Kuru.” (Bhag. [4.7.61](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/7.61))

## Dialogue Two - Dhruva Maharaja Attains the Lord

## Chapter 8 - Dhruva Maharaja Leaves Home for the Forest

## Texts 1-7: Descendants of Svayambhuva Manu

Maitreya Muni has already narrated the histories of Svayambhuva Manu’s descendants, and in that context described the Daksa-yajna, which intimately affected Svayambhuva Manu’s granddaughter Sati. At the beginning of this eighth chapter he first describes the causes of devastation, and then tells Vidura that he will discuss Manu’s two sons, Uttanapada and Priyavrata, both of whom were “competent to rule the universe.” (Bhag. [4.8.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.7)) In his purport to text 8 Prabhupada explains why Maitreya Muni in his narration suddenly turns to a description of Dhruva Maharaja’s life: “Priyavrata was the first son of Svayambhuva Manu, and Uttanapada was the second, but the great sage Maitreya immediately began to speak of Dhruva Maharaja, the son of Uttanapada, because Maitreya was very eager to describe pious activities. The incidents in the life of Dhruva Maharaja are very attractive for devotees. From his pious actions, one can learn how one can detach himself from material possessions and how one can enhance one’s devotional service by severe austerities and penances. By hearing the activities of pious Dhruva, one can enhance one’s faith in God and can directly connect with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and thus one can very soon be elevated to the transcendental platform of devotional service. The example of Dhruva Maharaja’s austerities can immediately generate a feeling of devotional service in the hearts of the hearers.”

Srila Vrndavana dasa Thakura makes a similar point in the tenth chapter of the Caitanya-bhagavata (Antya [10.32-35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-antya/10.32)) when describing Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu: “In this way the Lord would happily spend His days hearing Bhagavatam from Gadadhara. Whenever Gadadhara would recite Bhagavatam, the Lord would manifest symptoms of love. The Lord would carefully hear the glories of Prahlada and Dhruva hundreds of times. He had no time for any other activity, but would always hear and chant the names and qualities of Krsna and His devotees.”

The remainder of Canto Four therefore discusses Dhruva Maharaja and Maharaja Uttanapada’s other descendants, while much of Canto Five delineates the descendants of Maharaja Priyavrata.

## Texts 8-23: Suruci Insults Dhruva Maharaja and He Leaves Home

Maharaja Uttanapada had two queens, Suruci and Suniti. Suruci was the younger queen and was the King’s favorite. Each of the queens had one son; Dhruva was Suniti’s son, and Uttama, Suruci’s son. Dhruva, who was only five years old, came into the throne room to see his father taking Suruci’s son Uttama on his lap and patting him. Dhruva Maharaja tried to join his brother by climbing on his father’s lap, but Dhruva was neither welcomed nor shown affection. Suruci said aloud for the King to hear: Dhruva, you deserve to sit neither on the throne nor on the King’s lap. Surely you are also the King’s son, but as you did not take birth from my womb, you should not hope to ascend the throne. My dear child, you may not realize it, but you were bom of a different mother. Your attempt, therefore, to climb on your father’s throne is doomed. It is impossible to fulfill your desire. Do you want to sit on the King’s throne? Then go and perform tapasya. Satisfy the Supreme Lord, Narayana, and if He finds favor with you, ask Him to allow you to die and be reborn in my womb.

Hearing her proud, envious words, Dhruva Maharaja began to breathe heavily. He ran from the throne room and rushed to the shelter of his mother’s arms. Dhruva’s tears were hot with anger and he was trembling. It especially disturbed him that his father had remained silent while his stepmother had spoken so cruelly. Suniti took her aggrieved son on her lap, and as she tried to pacify him, asked the palace residents what was wrong. Hearing of her со-wife’s harsh words, her bright, lotuslike eyes filled with tears. She too began to breathe heavily. Unable to ease her son’s pain, she first tried to soothe any sense of vengeance he might be feeling: “My dear son, don’t wish for anything inauspicious for others. Anyone who inflicts pain upon others suffers himself from that pain.” (Bhag. [4.8.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.17))

But Suniti had to admit the agonizing truth: Suruci’s harsh words were accurate. She said: “My dear boy, whatever has been spoken by Suruci, your stepmother, although very harsh to hear, is factual. Therefore, if you desire at all to sit on the same throne as your stepbrother, Uttama, then give up your envious attitude and immediately try to execute the instructions of your stepmother. Without further delay, you must engage yourself in worshiping the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [4.8.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.19))

In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada writes: “The harsh words used by Suruci to her stepson were true because unless one is favored by the Supreme Personality of Godhead one cannot achieve any success in life. Man proposes, God disposes. Suniti, the mother of Dhruva Maharaja, agreed with her со-wife’s advice that Dhruva engage himself in the worship of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Indirectly, the words of Suruci were a benediction for Dhruva Maharaja, for because of the influence of his stepmother’s words, he became a great devotee.”

Citing examples of Dhruva’s grandfather and great-grandfather, Suniti impressed on Dhruva that success is possible only by worshiping the Supreme Lord without deviation. She implored Dhruva to seek His shelter; Suniti had strong faith in the Lord’s kindness to His devotees.

Suniti continued: “You came to me crying, having been insulted by your stepmother, but I am unable to do any good for you. But Krsna is so kind to His devotees that if you go to Him, then the combined kindness of millions of mothers like me will be surpassed by His affectionate and tender dealings. When everyone else fails to mitigate one’s misery, Krsna is able to help the devotee.”

Srila Prabhupada adds: “Even a child less than five years old, or anyone of any age, can be purified. That is the special significance of bhakti-yoga. Therefore she advised him not to accept worship of the demigods or any other process, but simply to take to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and the result would be all perfection. As soon as one places the Supreme Personality of Godhead within one’s heart, everything becomes easy and successful.”

Hearing his mother’s words, young Dhruva, fixed and determined as befits a ksatriya, left his father’s house to seek the Supreme Personality of Godhead in the forest. Regarding Dhruva’s decision, Srila Prabhupada advises all devotees how to deal with misfortunes in his purport to text 24: “Both the mother and the son were lamenting Dhruva Maharaja’s having been insulted by his stepmother and his father’s not having taken any step on this issue. But mere lamentation is useless—one should find out the means to mitigate one’s lamentation. Thus both mother and son decided to take shelter of the lotus feet of the Lord because that is the only solution to all material problems. It is indicated in this connection that Dhruva Maharaja left his father’s capital city to go to a secluded place to search out the Supreme Personality of Godhead. It is the instruction of Prahlada Maharaja also that if one is seeking peace of mind he should free himself from all contamination of family life and take shelter of the Supreme Godhead by going to the forest. To the Gaudiya Vaisnava this forest is the forest of Vrnda, or Vrndavana. If one takes shelter of Vrndavana under Vrndavanesvari, Srimati Radharani, certainly all the problems of his life are solved very easily.”

Srila Prabhupada echoes the “best” instruction offered by another boy-devotee, Prahlada Maharaja, to his demoniac father: “O best of the asuras, King of the demons, as far as I have learned from my spiritual master, any person who has accepted a temporary body and temporary household life is certainly embarrassed by anxiety because of having fallen in a dark well where there is no water but only suffering. One should give up this position and go to the forest \[vana\]. More clearly, one should go to Vrndavana, where only Krsna consciousness is prevalent, and should thus take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [7.5.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/5.5))

## Texts 25-38: Dhruva Maharaja Meets Narada Muni, His Spiritual Master

When the great Narada Muni heard of young Dhruva’s determined attempt to find the Lord, he was struck with wonder. In his purport to text 25, Srila Prabhupada describes how Narada, who was not present to witness all these events, nevertheless knew of them: “When Dhruva Maharaja was talking with his mother, Suniti, of all the incidents that had taken place in the palace, Narada was not present. Thus the question may be raised how Narada overheard all these topics. The answer is that Narada is trikala-jna; he is so powerful that he can understand the past, future and present of everyone’s heart, just like the Supersoul, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore, after understanding the strong determination of Dhruva Maharaja, Narada came to help him.”

Does this mean that powerful devotees like Narada are equal in knowing to the Supersoul? Srila Prabhupada’s indicates that even the most powerful devotee’s knowledge of events is inspired by the Supersoul, who knows all: “The Supreme Personality of Godhead is present in everyone’s heart, and as soon as He understands that a living entity is serious about entering devotional service, He sends His representative. In this way Narada was sent to Dhruva Maharaja. . . . Because of Dhruva Maharaja’s determination, Krsna, the Supersoul, immediately sent His representative, Narada, to initiate him.”

Narada marveled at Dhruva’s ksatriya spirit, for it was his natural ksatriya pride that did not allow him, even at such a young age, to tolerate an insult. Deciding to test Dhruva further, Narada approached the fearless young prince after he entered the forest, which was teeming with ferocious beasts and reptiles: You are only a boy. Why have you taken your stepmother’s insults so seriously? After all, the sufferings we experience in this life stem from our previous karma.

Why did Narada Muni insist that Dhruva Maharaja’s sufferings were caused not by his stepmother’s arrogant words but by his own karma—by himself? In his purport to text 28, Srila Prabhupada explains Narada’s insights: “Narada Rsi first of all wanted to impress upon Dhruva Maharaja that he was only a child; he should not have been affected by words of insult or honor. And if he were so developed as to understand honor and insult, then this understanding should have been applied in his own life; he should have known that honor and dishonor are both destined only by one’s previous actions; therefore one should not be sorry or happy under any circumstances.” If Dhruva was old enough to feel an insult to his honor, he should have been old enough to understand the workings of maya, karma, and Krsna’s mercy.

Narada Muni next instructed Dhruva Maharaja to see everything that happens as Krsna’s kindness: “The process of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very wonderful. One who is intelligent should accept that process and be satisfied with whatever comes, favorable or unfavorable, by His supreme will.” (Bhag. [4.8.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.29))

Srila Prabhupada explains the import of these instructions in his purport to this text: “The great sage Narada instructed Dhruva Maharaja that one should be satisfied in all circumstances. Everyone who is intelligent should know that because of our concept of bodily existence, we are subjected to suffering and enjoyment. One who is in the transcendental position, beyond the concept of bodily life, is considered to be intelligent. One who is a devotee especially accepts all reverses as gifts of the Supreme Lord. When a devotee is put into distress, he accepts this as God’s mercy and offers Him repeated obeisances with his body, mind and intellect. An intelligent person, therefore, should be always satisfied, depending on the mercy of the Lord.”

Later, in his purport to text 33, Srila Prabhupada advises readers to adopt a Krsna conscious vision when looking at life’s reverses: “Material existence consists of pious and impious fruitive activities. As long as one is engaged in any kind of activity other than devotional service, it will result in the happiness and distress of this material world. When we enjoy life in so-called material happiness, it is to be understood that we are diminishing the resultant actions of our pious activities. And when we are put into suffering, it is to be understood that we are diminishing the resultant actions of our impious activities. Instead of being attached to the circumstantial happiness and distress resulting from pious or impious activities, if we want to get out of the clutches of this nescience, then whatever position we are put in by the will of the Lord we should accept. Thus if we simply surrender unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, we shall get out of the clutches of this material existence.”

Narada decided to test Dhruva’s determination: You are just a child, and the process is arduous. Come back when you’re older and more mature. Perhaps then, by the Lord’s mercy, you will be able to attain perfection. You’ll fail if you try for it now. Better that you simply become satisfied with whatever the Lord has already offered you.

Dhruva listened respectfully, then said: “My dear Lord Naradaji, for a person whose heart is disturbed by the material conditions of happiness and distress, whatever you have so kindly explained for attainment of peace of mind is certainly a very good instruction. But as far as I am concerned, I am covered by ignorance, and this kind of philosophy does not touch my heart. My dear lord, I am very impudent for not accepting your instructions, but this is not my fault. It is due to my having been born in a ksatriya family. My stepmother, Suruci, has pierced my heart with her harsh words. Therefore your valuable instruction does not stand in my heart.” (Bhag. [4.8.35-36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.35))

Dhruva then told Narada what he wanted: “O learned brahmana, I want to occupy a position more exalted than any yet achieved within the three worlds by anyone, even by my fathers and grandfathers. If you will oblige, kindly advise me of an honest path to follow by which I can achieve the goal of my life.” (Bhag. [4.8.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.37))

Srila Prabhupada explains Dhruva’s mood: “It is said that the heart or mind is just like an earthen pot,3 once broken, it cannot be repaired by any means. Dhruva Maharaja gave this example to Narada Muni. He said that his heart, having been pierced by the arrows of his stepmother’s harsh words, felt so broken that nothing seemed valuable but his desire to counteract her insult. His stepmother had said that because he was bom from the womb of Suniti, a neglected queen of Maharaja Uttanapada, Dhruva Maharaja was not fit to sit either on the throne or on his father’s lap. In other words, according to his stepmother, he could not be declared king. Dhruva’s determination, therefore, was to become king of a planet exalted even beyond that possessed by Lord Brahma, the greatest of all the demigods.” (Bhag. [4.8.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.36), purport)

Dhruva’s father ruled the world, and his great-grandfather, Lord Brahma, ruled the universe. Dhruva wanted a kingdom greater than both of theirs, and solicited Narada’s blessings to achieve this unreachable desire. Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 37 that “This was practically an impossible proposition, but by pleasing the Supreme Personality of Godhead a devotee can achieve even the impossible.”

In his purport to text 35, Srila Prabhupada tells us what we should leam from Dhruva Maharaja: “The question raised here is whether or not a person afflicted by material desires is fit to worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The answer is that everyone is fit to worship Him. Even if one has many material desires to fulfill, he should take to Krsna consciousness and worship the Supreme Lord Krsna, who is so merciful that He fulfills everyone’s desires. Through this narration it will become very clear that no one is barred from worshiping the Supreme Personality of Godhead, even if one has many material desires.”One need only be as determined as Dhruva was, a point Srila Prabhupada notes in his purport to text 72:

**Dhruva Maharaja is an acarya, and by undergoing severe austerities and penances he teaches us how one should execute devotional service. We must carefully know the process of Dhruva Maharaja’s service; how severely he passed his days will be shown in later verses. We should always remember that to become a bona fide devotee of the Lord is not an easy task, but in this age, by the mercy of Lord Caitanya, it has been made very easy. But if we do not follow even the liberal instructions of Lord Caitanya, how can we expect to discharge our regular duties in devotional service? It is not possible in this age to follow Dhruva Maharaja in his austerity, but the principles must be followed; we should not disregard the regulative principles given by our spiritual master, for they make it easier for the conditioned soul. As far as our ISKCON movement is concerned, we simply ask that one observe the four prohibitive rules, chant sixteen rounds and, instead of indulging in luxurious eating for the tongue, simply accept prasada offered to the Lord....**

**It is our duty to remember always that in comparison to Dhruva Maharaja we are insignificant. We cannot do anything like what Dhruva Maharaja did for self-realization because we are absolutely incompetent to execute such service. But by Lord Caitanya’s mercy we have been given all concessions possible for this age, so at least we should always remember that neglect of our prescribed duties in devotional service will not make us successful in the mission we have undertaken. It is our duty to follow in the footsteps of Dhruva Maharaja, for he was very determined. We should also be determined to finish our duties in executing devotional service in this life; we should not wait for another life to finish our job.**

## Texts 39-62: Narada’s Instructions to Dhruva

Dhruva’s desire was material, yet Narada knew that Dhruva would soon attain the Lord, fulfill his desire for worldly benediction, and lose that desire in the Lord’s soothing, fully satisfying presence. Seeking to truly bless Dhruva, Narada Muni therefore took advantage of Dhruva’s determination and instructed him to completely absorb himself in devotional service. To attain his desire, Dhruva should control his senses and worship with devotion the Supreme Personality of Godhead alone.

In his purport to text 40, Srila Prabhupada reveals an interesting facet of the relationship between Narada Muni, a great spiritual master, and his disciple Dhruva: “Narada Muni is referred to here as bhaga-van because he can bless any person just as the Supreme Personality of Godhead can. He was very pleased with Dhruva Maharaja, and he could have at once personally given whatever he wanted, but that is not the duty of the spiritual master. His duty is to engage the disciple in proper devotional service as prescribed in the sastras. Krsna was similarly present before Arjuna, and even though He could have given him all facilities for victory over the opposing party without a fight, He did not do so; instead He asked Arjuna to fight. In the same way, Narada Muni asked Dhruva Maharaja to undergo devotional discipline in order to achieve the desired result.”

It is wise to note that the process—selfless devotional service—not a product—attaining the spiritual world—is the essence of Krsna consciousness.
