Although one may tend to view “the process” as a means to achieve residence in Vaikuntha, both the process and the goal are the same. It is natural that a devotee wishes to serve Krsna in the spiritual world, but a devotee’s deepest desire is more simply to give Krsna pleasure wherever the devotee may be. A devotee is always satisfied to allow Krsna to choose the field of service. Mature devotees who possess hearts free of envy and false ego are already living in the spiritual world even as they appear to live in this world.

The love of immature devotees is tinged with selfishness; it is their own consciousness that prohibits them from entering Goloka Vrndavana. Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami illustrates the pure quality of spiritual love by describing Srimati Radharani’s mood in serving Krsna as “a highly advanced ecstasy. All Her dealings are completely pure and devoid of material tinge. Indeed, Her dealings are ten times purer than gold.” (Cc. Madhya [14.165](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/14.165)) In Sri Prema-bhakti-candrika (song 7, verse 1) Narottama dasa Thakura compares the love of Radha and Krsna to prema laksa-bana yena hema, gold purified millions of times. Clearly, such love cannot manifest in an impure heart.

It is the guru’s duty to instruct his disciple in how to perform pure devotional service and to engage the disciple in activities and attitudes that will ever deepen the process, because that is how the disciple will gradually develop a real desire to engage in Krsna’s loving service. Such service will blossom in the disciple’s heart. There is no difference between devotional service rendered in this world and devotional service rendered in Goloka Vrndavana. As Prabhupada later explains (in his purport to Bhagavatam [4.9.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.11)): “By devotional service only is one elevated to the transcendental planet Goloka Vrndavana, and there also there is only devotional service, for the activities of devotional service both in this world and in the spiritual world are one and the same. Devotional service does not change. The example of a mango can be given here. If one gets an unripe mango, it is still a mango, and when it is ripe it remains the same mango, but it has become more tasteful and relishable. Similarly, there is devotional service performed according to the direction of the spiritual master and the injunctions and regulative principles of sastra, and there is devotional service in the spiritual world, rendered directly in association with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. But they are both the same. There is no change. The difference is that one stage is unripe and the other is ripe and more relishable.”

Prabhupada also emphasizes process over product in his purport to Caitanya-caritamrta, Adi [7.91](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/7.91): “According to the revealed scriptures, if a spiritual master can convert even one soul into a perfectly pure devotee, his mission in life is fulfilled. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura always used to say, ‘Even at the expense of all the properties, temples and mathas that I have, if I could convert even one person into a pure devotee, my mission would be fulfilled.’ It is very difficult, however, to understand the science of Krsna, what to speak of developing love of Godhead. Therefore if by the grace of Lord Caitanya and the spiritual master a disciple attains the standard of pure devotional service, the spiritual master is very happy. The spiritual master is not actually happy if the disciple brings him money, but when he sees a disciple is following the regulative principles and advancing in spiritual life, he is very glad and feels obliged to such an advanced disciple.”

Understanding Dhruva’s exalted qualities, Narada blessed him by giving him specific instructions: “My dear boy, I therefore wish all good fortune for you. You should go to the bank of the Yamuna, where there is a virtuous forest named Madhuvana, and there be purified. Just by going there, one draws nearer to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who always lives there.” (Bhag. [4.8.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.42))

In his purport to this text, Prabhupada underscores the importance of residing in a holy place: “Unless one is very advanced in spiritual life, it is recommended that he live in such holy places and execute devotional service there. But an advanced devotee like Narada Muni who is engaged in preaching work can serve the Supreme Lord anywhere. Sometimes he even goes to the hellish planets. Hellish conditions do not affect Narada Muni because he is engaged in greatly responsible activities in devotional service. According to the statement of Narada Muni, Madhuvana, which is still existing in the Vrndavana area, in the district of Mathura, is a most sacred place. Many saintly persons still live there and engage in the devotional service of the Lord.”

Sri Narada continued: Bathe three times daily in the Yamuna River and practice astanga'yoga. Meditate on the Supreme Personality of Godhead’s beautiful youthful form. He is in everyone’s heart. If you focus your consciousness on the bodily features of the Lord, who bestows all benedictions, you will never fall into material consciousness.

Narada then instructed Dhruva to perform mantra-japa along with his meditation, prescribing the mantra от namo bhagavate vasudevaya. Sri Narada told Dhruva that this twelve-syllable mantra was intended for Krsna’s worship. He told him to install the Lord’s physical form (deity) and, while chanting the mantra, to offer flowers and fruits and other foods in strict adherence to authoritative rules and regulations. He should, of course, do this while considering time, place, and attendant conveniences and inconveniences.

Srila Prabhupada explains how to simultaneously chant Hare Krsna and meditate on the Lord’s form: “Another point established in this verse is that meditation should be carried on with the chanting of a mantra. Chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra is the easiest process of meditation in this age. As soon as one chants the Hare Krsna mantra, he sees the forms of Krsna, Rama and Their energies, and that is the perfect stage of trance. One should not artificially try to see the form of the Lord while chanting Hare Krsna, but when the chanting is performed offenselessly the Lord will automatically reveal Himself to the view of the chanter. The chanter, therefore, has to concentrate on hearing the vibration, and without extra endeavor on his part, the Lord will automatically appear.” (Bhag. [4.8.53](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.53), purport)In his purport to text 54, Srila Prabhupada reveals a parallel between Narada’s instructions to Dhruva and both the practices he himself established and the obstacles he encountered while spreading Krsna consciousness throughout the world:

**The method of worship—chanting the mantra and preparing the forms of the Lord—is not stereotyped, nor is it exactly the same everywhere. It is specifically mentioned in this verse that one should take consideration of the time, place and available conveniences. Our Krsna consciousness movement is going on throughout the entire world, and we also install Deities in different centers. Sometimes our Indian friends, puffed up with concocted notions, criticize, “This has not been done. That has not been done.” But they forget this instruction of Narada Muni to one of the greatest Vaisnavas, Dhruva Maharaja. One has to consider the particular time, country and conveniences. What is convenient in India may not be convenient in the Western countries. Those who are not actually in the line of acaryas, or who personally have no knowledge of how to act in the role of acarya, unnecessarily criticize the activities of the ISKCON movement in countries outside of India. The fact is that such critics cannot do anything personally to spread Krsna consciousness. If someone does go and preach, taking all risks and allowing all considerations for time and place, it might be that there are changes in the manner of worship, but that is not at all faulty according to sastra. Srimad Viraraghava Acarya, an acarya in the disciplic succession of the Ramanuja-sampradaya, has remarked in his commentary that candalas, or conditioned souls who are bom in lower than sudra families, can also be initiated according to circumstances. The formalities may be slightly changed here and there to make them Vaisnavas.**

**Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu recommends that His name should be heard in every nook and comer of the world. How is this possible unless one preaches everywhere?**

Srila Prabhupada and his Guru Maharaja both struggled mightily to establish the above principle, one that allows people from all conditions of life to become elevated to the position of brahmanas and Vaisnavas. Yet the weight of this work rests on all their followers; we must complete the process of purification, a point Srila Prabhupada noted during a morning walk in Los Angeles in 1975. Prabhupada explained that he was creating brahmanas by awarding the “sacred thread on the pancaratriki-vidhi, the same principle.”

**Prabhupada: There is a little spot, fire. Fan it. The process of fanning. But if the farming is stopped, then the small spot of fire also will be extinguished. It will have no effect because the small fire cannot do anything. It must become a blazing fire. So this is our process. We are accepting souls from the most fallen condition. Because he has little spark of fire—he wants to get Krsna consciousness—so our process is fan it, and it must become a blazing fire. But if you say, “Now that small fire is sufficient,” that will not act \[sufficiently\]. It must be a blazing fire. A small fire has the potential, but that potential should be brought to . . . Just like in wood there is fire. That everyone knows. But that will not serve your purpose. Fuel wood has to become fire, and then it has to be increased. First of all set fire. Then there will be smoke. The smoke is also not fire. Smoke is another condition, a symptom of fire, but smoke is not fire. The smoke must come into blazing fire. Then it can act.**

**Devotee: The fanning, that is the devotional practices.**

**Prabhupada: Yes.**

**Brahmananda: If that stops ...**

**Prabhupada: Then it is finished.**

Narada Muni continued: “My dear Dhruva, besides worshiping the Deity and chanting the mantra three times a day, you should meditate upon the transcendental activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead in His different incarnations, as exhibited by His supreme will and personal potencies.” (Bhag. [4.8.57](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.57))

In his purport to text 58, Srila Prabhupada describes the versatility of meditation: “It is recommended here that even if one cannot arrange to worship the forms of the Lord with all recommended paraphernalia, one can simply think about the form of the Lord and mentally offer everything recommended in the sdstras, including flowers, candana pulp, conchshell, umbrella, fan and carnara. One can meditate upon offering and chant the twelve-syllable mantra, orh namo bhagavate vasudevaya. Since the mantra and the Supreme Personality of Godhead are nondifferent, one can worship the form of the Lord with the mantra in the absence of physical paraphernalia.”

In his purport to text 57, Srila Prabhupada compares meditating on the Lord’s pastimes and chanting Krsna’s names: “Narada advises Dhruva to meditate on the pastimes of the Lord, which is as good as the meditation of concentrating one’s mind on the form of the Lord. As meditation on any form of the Lord is valuable, so is chanting of different names of the Lord, such as Hari, Govinda and Narayana. But in this age we are especially advised to chant the Hare Krsna mantra as enunciated in the sastra: Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare.”

By pleasing the Lord, one will be blessed by the Lord according to one’s desire. But, as Narada pointed out, should one wish to attain liberation from matter, one must become aloof from sense enjoyment and lovingly serve the Lord with ecstasy twenty-four hours a day.

When Narada finished speaking, Dhruva circumambulated his spiritual master and offered obeisances. “Then he started for Madhuvana, which is always imprinted with the lotus footprints of Lord Krsna and which is therefore especially auspicious.” (Bhag. [4.8.62](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.62))

It is interesting to note that text 62 mentions Hari, not Krsna, although Srila Prabhupada translates the word as “Krsna.” Many people consider Hari a name of Visnu, not Krsna, but Srila Sanatana Gosvami comments on Bhagavatam 10.21.10 that in Vrndavana, Krsna goes barefoot and thus marks the earth with the symbols of His lotus feet. Therefore that transcendental land is even more glorious than Vaikuntha, where Visnu wears slippers. That Lord who is marking the land of Vrndavana with His lotus footprints can only be Krsna, as Srila Prabhupada has noted. It is interesting that Krsna’s eternal presence in Vrndavana was known even during the time of Dhruva Maharaja.

## Texts 63-70: Narada Visits King Uttanapada

Narada Muni decided to visit Dhruva’s father, King Uttanapada. On being received and comfortably seated by the King, Narada, fully aware of the answer, asked the King why his face appeared withered and he seemed depressed. Maharaja Uttanapada told Narada of his fear for his young son’s safety and of his own role in Dhruva’s leaving home. The King said: Alas, just see how I allowed myself to be conquered by my wife! Imagine my cruelty. Out of affection the boy was trying to climb on my lap, but I would not receive him. Nor did I embrace him even for a moment. Just imagine how hardhearted I am.

Narada then assured Uttanapada that Dhruva, although apparently alone in the forest, had surrendered to the Supreme Personality of Godhead and was therefore fully under the Lord’s protection. Srila Prabhupada describes the protection that those on Dhruva’s path, the fearless path of surrender, receive from the Lord: “Sometimes when we hear that great sages and devotees go to the forest and engage themselves in devotional service or meditation, we become surprised: how can one live in the forest and not be taken care of by anyone? But the answer, given by a great authority, Narada Muni, is that such persons are well protected by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Saranagati, or surrender, means acceptance or firm belief that wherever the surrendered soul lives he is always protected by the Supreme Personality of Godhead; he is never alone or unprotected. Dhruva Maharaja’s affectionate father thought his young boy, only five years old, to be in a very precarious position in the jungle, but Narada Muni assured him, ‘You do not have sufficient information about the influence of your son.’ Anyone who engages in devotional service, anywhere within this universe, is never unprotected.” (Bhag. [4.8.68](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.68), purport)

Narada then told Uttanapada of Dhruva’s glorious determination to attain the Lord. In his purport to text 69, Prabhupada stresses the importance of determination: “What was the task that Dhruva Maharaja undertook? The most difficult task in life is to satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and Dhruva would be able to do that. We must remember that Dhruva Maharaja was not fickle; he was determined to execute his service and then come back. Every devotee, therefore, should be determined that in this life he will be able to satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead and by that process go back home, back to Godhead. That is the perfection of the highest mission of life.”

Srila Prabhupada continues to implore his readers in his purport to text 72: “It is our duty to remember always that in comparison to Dhruva Maharaja we are insignificant. We cannot do anything like what Dhruva did for self-realization because we are absolutely incompetent to execute such service. But by Lord Caitanya’s mercy we have been given all concessions possible for this age, so at least we should always remember that neglect of our prescribed duties in devotional service will not make us successful in the mission we have undertaken. It is our duty to follow in the footsteps of Dhruva Maharaja, for he was very determined. We should also be determined to finish our duties in executing devotional service in this life; we should not wait for another life to finish our job.”

After Narada’s visit, Uttanapada lost interest in his kingdom and thought only of his son Dhruva.

## Texts 71 -82: Dhruva Successfully Executes Narada’s Instructions

After arriving in Madhuvana, Dhruva began to apply Narada’s instructions. Srila Prabhupada advises: “Dhruva Maharaja acted exactly according to the advice of his spiritual master, the great sage Narada. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti also advises that if we want to be successful in our attempt to go back to Godhead, we must very seriously act according to the instruction of the spiritual master. That is the way of perfection. There need be no anxiety over attaining perfection because if one follows the instruction given by the spiritual master he is sure to attain perfection. Our only concern should be how to execute the order of the spiritual master. A spiritual master is expert in giving special instructions to each of his disciples, and if the disciple executes the order of the spiritual master, that is the way of his perfection.” (Bhag. [4.8.71](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.71), purport)

Step by step, day by day, month by month, Dhruva practiced devotional service. As Narada had instructed him, he first controlled his senses. Then he freed his mind from all diversions and fixed it on the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Having captured the master of all living entities and the refuge of the creation in his heart, Dhruva became heavier than the heaviest, causing both the material and spiritual planets to tremble.

Dhruva, the child-devotee whose stepmother had denied him a place on his father’s lap, now had enough power to destabilize the universe. Srila Prabhupada writes of Dhruva’s incredible power in his purport to text 78: “By associating constantly with the Supreme Personality in his heart, Dhruva Maharaja naturally became equal to the greatest, Brahman, by His association, and thus became the heaviest, and the entire universe trembled. In conclusion, a person who always concentrates on the transcendental form of Krsna within his heart can very easily strike the whole world with wonder at his activities.... Or-dinary yogis can exhibit wonderful material activities, known as asta-siddhi, eight kinds of yogic perfection, but a pure devotee of the Lord can surpass these perfections by performing activities which can make the whole universe tremble.”

Dhruva Maharaja stood steadily on one leg. With the pressure of his big toe, he moved the earth “just as an elephant being carried on a boat rocks the boat left and right with his every step.” (Bhag. [4.8.79](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.79)) Because of Dhruva’s full concentration, his weight became one with Lord Visnu’s weight. When in his practice Dhruva closed off the holes in his body, he choked the total universal breathing. The demigods, suffocating and distressed, took shelter of the Supreme Lord.

In his purport to text 80, Srila Prabhupada relates Dhruva Maharaja’s power to the power of a preacher: “This example of Dhruva Maharaja’s closing the holes of his personal body and thereby closing the breathing holes of the total universe clearly indicates that a devotee, by his personal devotional service, can influence all the people of the whole world to become devotees of the Lord. If there is only one pure devotee in pure Krsna consciousness, he can change the total consciousness of the world into Krsna consciousness. This is not very difficult to understand if we study the behavior of Dhruva Maharaja.” Srila Prabhupada successfully changed the world; his powerful preaching caused both materialists and aspiring devotees to tremble. He accomplished such an impossible task without anxiety. Because of Prabhupada’s intense, unalloyed desire to please his spiritual master and Krsna, Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu gave Prabhupada, His dear devotee who had sacrificed everything, His own potency.

After listening to the demigods’ fears, the Lord assured them that Dhruva’s intentions were not malevolent: Young Dhruva Maharaja is causing your suffering, for he is “now fully absorbed in thought of Me.

. . . You can safely return to your respective homes. I shall stop this boy in his severe acts of austerities, and you will be saved from this situation.” (Bhag. [4.8.82](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/8.82))

## Chapter 9 - Dhruva Maharaja Returns Home

## Texts 1-5: The Lord Reveals His Form to Dhruva Maharaja

Having reassured the demigods, the Lord, even as Dhruva Maharaja was meditating on Him, rode to Madhuvana on His carrier, Garuda.  Suddenly, the brilliant, lightning-like form of the Lord vanished from Dhruva’s heart. Dhruva’s meditation broke and he opened his eyes. The Supreme Personality of Godhead was standing before him. Dhruva fell to the ground in obeisance, falling before the Lord like a wooden rod.

Absorbed in ecstatic love, Dhruva felt as if he were drinking the Lord with his eyes, kissing His lotus feet with his mouth, and embracing Him with his arms.

## Texts 6-17: Dhruva Offers Prayers

Dhruva wanted to greet the Lord with prayerful words, but he hesitated, feeling too young and inexperienced to speak eloquently. Knowing Dhruva’s awkwardness, the Lord touched the boy’s forehead with His conchshell, empowering Dhruva to have full awareness of the Absolute Truth. Dhruva instantly thanked Him, and as he comprehended the Absolute Truth by the Lord’s causeless mercy, he understood that the Lord’s blessings would grace his words.

Srila Prabhupada notes that the Lord’s blessing empowers a devotee to glorify Him: “Every devotee wants to chant the transcendental qualities of the Lord. Devotees are always interested in hearing about the Lord’s transcendental qualities, and they are always eager to glorify these qualities, but sometimes they feel inconvenienced by humbleness. The Personality of Godhead, being situated in everyone’s heart, specifically gives a devotee intelligence to describe Him. It is therefore understood that when a devotee writes or speaks about the Supreme Personality of Godhead, his words are dictated by the Lord from within. This is confirmed in Bhagavad-gita, Tenth Chapter: to those who constantly engage in the transcendental loving service of the Lord, the Lord, from within, dictates what to do next in order to serve Him.” (Bhag. [4.9.4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.4), purport)

Krsna is transcendental, beyond the material world, and this implies that nothing in this world can please Him. Whatever devotees offer, therefore, including their words, is made of bhakti, the Lord’s internal, spiritual energy. It is the bhakti-sakti added to the devotees’ sincere desire to glorify Krsna that empowers their words and brings Krsna pleasure. This is also the secret of successful preaching. Vallabha Bhatta states, kali-kalera dharma—krsna-nama-sankirtana, krsna-sakti vina nahe tdra pravartana: “The fundamental religious system in the age of Kali is the chanting of the holy name of Krsna. Unless empowered by Krsna, one cannot propagate the sankirtana movement.” (Cc. Antya [7.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/7.11)) Prabhupada explains: “Spiritual enlightenment is possible by the mercy of the spiritual energy of the Lord. The chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra is first addressed to the spiritual energy of the Lord, Hare. This energy acts when a living entity folly surrenders and accepts his position as an eternal servitor. When a person places himself at the disposal or order of the Supreme Lord, that is called sevon-mukha; at that time the spiritual energy gradually reveals the Lord to him.” (Bhag. [4.9.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.6), purport) Full surrender brings enlightenment.

Seeing that the Lord’s internal energy had changed him, Dhruva first acknowledged the unlimitedly potent nature of that Person whom he now saw before him: “My dear Lord, You are all-powerful. After entering within me, You have enlivened all my sleeping senses—my hands, legs, ears, touch sensation, life force and especially my power of speech. Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto You.” (Bhag. [4.9.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.6)) Dhruva continued: You are the Supreme, and no one is either equal to or higher than You. You are both the source and the maintainer of the material world. Indeed, You are spread throughout the cosmic manifestation by Your energy. You give knowledge and liberation, and You are the friend of all who are distressed. How, therefore, can one—knowing You as all this—ever forget You?

In his purport to text 8, Srila Prabhupada describes a devotee’s constant remembrance of Krsna: “The Supreme Personality of Godhead cannot be forgotten even for a moment by His surrendered devotees.

The devotee understands that the Lord’s causeless mercy is beyond his estimation; he cannot know how much he is benefited by the grace of the Lord. The more a devotee engages himself in the devotional service of the Lord, the more encouragement is supplied by the energy of the Lord. In the Bhagavad-gita the Lord says that to those who are constantly engaged in devotional service with love and affection, the Supreme Personality of Godhead gives intelligence from within, and thus they may make further progress. Being so encouraged, the devotee can never forget, at any moment, the Personality of Godhead. He always feels obliged to Him for having achieved increased power in devotional service by His grace.”

Confronted with the merciful Lord’s appearance before him, Dhruva then lamented his desire for a kingdom: I performed my austerities simply to gain the greatest kingdom. Now I understand that only a fool would worship You to attain sense gratification. “Persons who worship You simply for the sense gratification of this bag of skin are certainly influenced by Your illusory energy. In spite of having You, who are like a desire tree and are the cause of liberation from birth and death, foolish persons, such as me, desire benedictions from You for sense gratification, which is available even for those who live in hellish conditions.” (Bhag. [4.9.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.9)) Thus Dhruva repented approaching the Lord with his petty, material ambitions.

Dhruva next minimized the value of both karma and jnana while hinting at proper aspiration: The greatest bliss comes from meditating on Your lotus feet and hearing Your glories from pure devotees. That bliss is far above the bliss of impersonal realization, which is itself beyond the happiness of the material world.

But how can one learn to aspire in a pure-hearted, devotional way? How does devotional service appear in the heart? Dhruva explains that the boat for crossing the dangerous ocean of material existence is constructed of drinking through one’s ears the Lord’s nectarean pastimes and qualities: “O unlimited Lord, kindly bless me so that I may associate with great devotees who engage in Your transcendental loving service constantly, as the waves of a river constantly flow. Such . . . devotees are completely situated in an uncontaminated state of life. By the process of devotional service I shall surely be able to cross the nescient ocean of material existence, which is filled with the waves of blazing, firelike dangers. It will be very easy for me, for I am becoming mad to hear about Your transcendental qualities and pastimes, which are eternally existent.” (Bhag. [4.9.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.11))In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada emphasizes the importance of Vaisnava association:

**The significant point in Dhruva Maharaja’s statement is that he wanted the association of pure devotees. Transcendental devotional service cannot be complete and cannot be relishable without the association of devotees. We have therefore established the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. Anyone who is trying to be aloof from this Krishna Consciousness Society and yet engage in Krsna consciousness is living in a great hallucination, for this is not possible. From this statement by Dhruva Maharaja it is clear that unless one is associated with devotees, his devotional service does not mature; it does not become distinct from material activities. The Lord says, satdm prasangan mama viryasamvido bha-vanti hrt'karna-rasayanah (Bhag.** [**3.25.25**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/25.25)**). Only in the association of pure devotees can the words of Lord Krsna be fully potent and relishable to the heart and ear. Dhruva Maharaja explicitly wanted the association of devotees....**

**A Mayavadi philosopher may question us, “You may be very happy in the association of devotees, but what is your plan for crossing the ocean of material existence?” Dhruva Maharaja’s answer is that it is not very difficult. He clearly says that this ocean can be crossed very easily if one simply becomes mad to hear the glories of the Lord. Bhavad-guna-katha: for anyone who persistently engages in hearing the topics of the Lord from Srlmad Bhagavad-gita, Srimad-Bhagavatam and Caitanya-caritamrta and who is actually addicted to this process, just as one becomes addicted to intoxicants, it is very easy to cross the nescience of material existence. The ocean of material nescience is compared to a blazing fire, but to a devotee this blazing fire is insignificant because he is completely absorbed in devotional service. Although the material world is blazing fire, to a devotee it appears full of pleasure (visvam purna-sukhayate).**

**The purport of this statement by Dhruva Maharaja is that devotional service in the association of devotees is the cause of the development of further devotional service.... It is possible to mature in devotional service only in the association of devotees.**

Dhruva Maharaja next commented on the transcendental nature of the Lord’s unlimited and attractive form: Attachment to You automatically evokes detachment from the material world. Your form, when compared to any other form in the totality of material existence, is transcendental and wonderful. You are Lord Garbhodakasayi Visnu, the source of universal manifestations, and Karanadakasayi Visnu, the Supersoul of the entire material existence. You are nondifferent from Brahman, which contains both knowledge and ignorance and is the source of the material manifestation.

Understanding the Lord’s position by His mercy, Dhruva Maharaja repeatedly offered obeisances.

In his purport to text 16, Srila Prabhupada compares different realizations of the Lord: “Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura describes that this impersonal feature, or Brahman manifestation, of the Supreme Lord is meant for persons who are essentially very advanced but still not able to understand the personal features or variegatedness of the spiritual world.... An example is given in this connection by Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura of a person proceeding towards a destination. As he approaches, he sees the destination from a distant place, just as we see a city from a distance. At that time he simply understands that the city is situated at a distance. When, however, he comes still nearer, he sees the domes and flags. But as soon as he enters the city, he sees various paths, gardens, lakes, and marketplaces with shops, and persons buying. He sees varieties of cinema houses, and he sees dancing and jubilation. When a person actually enters the city and personally sees the activities of the city, he becomes satisfied.”

Dhruva knew that it was the Lord in His personal form, the Supreme Person, who awards all realization and benedition to seekers. He then experienced Him as the personified form of benediction. Understanding this clarified for Dhruva the nature of the topmost desire: to become a devotee with no other desire but to please Krsna.

Dhruva concluded in text 17 by explaining that although he had worshiped the Lord to gain material benediction, the worship itself was the greatest benediction: “My Lord, О Supreme Lord, You are the supreme personified form of all benediction. Therefore, for one who abides in Your devotional service with no other desire, worshiping Your lotus feet is better than becoming king and lording it over a kingdom. That is the benediction of worshiping Your lotus feet. To ignorant devotees like me, You are the causelessly merciful maintainer, just like a cow, who takes care of the newly born calf by supplying milk and giving it protection from attack.”

Sridhara Svami breaks this text down in his commentary: “O Supreme Personality of Godhead (bhagavan), Your form (murteh) is the supreme bliss and the highest goal of life (purusartha). Your lotus feet (pada-padmam) are the true benediction (satyasiso), and are a benediction far greater than other benedictions (rsis), such as ruling over a kingdom. This is the right conclusion (hi). Why? It is like this (tatha): For the devotees who worship You (anubhajatah) without ulterior motive, You are the highest goal of life. О master (arya), even though this is so, You still maintain and protect poor (dinan) people like us (’sman).”

Srila Prabhupada details Dhruva Maharaja’s realization in his purport to this text: “Dhruva Maharaja was cognizant of the defective nature of his own devotional service. Pure devotional service is without material form and is not covered by mental speculation or fruitive activities. Pure devotional service is therefore called ahaituki, unmotivated. Dhruva Maharaja knew that he had come to worship the Lord in devotional service with a motive—to get the kingdom of his father. Such an adulterated devotee can never see the Supreme Personality of Godhead face to face. He therefore felt very grateful for the causeless mercy of the Lord. The Lord is so merciful that not only does He fulfill the desires of a devotee who is driven by ignorance and desires for material benefit, but He also gives such a devotee all protection, just as a cow gives milk to a newly bom calf. In the Bhagavad-gita it is said that the Lord gives intelligence to the constantly engaged devotee so that he may gradually approach the Lord without difficulty. A devotee must be very sincere in his devotional service; then, although there may be many things wrong on the devotee’s part, Krsna will guide him and gradually elevate him to the highest position of devotional service. ... Lord Caitanya therefore taught us not to ask from the Supreme Personality any benediction such as material wealth, popularity or a good wife. One should simply pray to the Lord to be constantly engaged in His transcendental loving service. Dhruva Maharaja, being cognizant of his desire for material benefit, wanted protection from the Lord so that he might not be misled or deviated from the path of devotional service by material desires.”

## Texts 18-26: The Lord Replies to Dhruva

After hearing Dhruva’s prayers, the bhakta-vatsala Lord first assured the determined young prince: “My dear Dhruva, son of the King, you have executed pious vows, and I also know the desire within your heart. Although your desire is very ambitious and very difficult to fulfill, I shall favor you with its fulfillment. All good fortune unto you.” (Bhag. [4.9.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.19))

Additionally, as Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 19, “The Lord assured Dhruva Maharaja that Dhruva would not be bereft of the Lord’s love. He encouraged Dhruva not to be worried that he childishly had material desires and at the same time had the pure aspiration to be a great devotee. Generally, the Lord does not award a pure devotee material opulence, even though he may desire it. But Dhruva Maharaja’s case was different. The Lord knew that he was such a great devotee that in spite of having material opulence he would never be deviated from love of God.”

The Lord then awarded Dhruva the polestar, a planet that no one had previously ruled and that would remain even during the partial universal devastations. In Bhagavatsandarbha, anuccheda 71, Srila Jiva Gosvami refers to Dhruvaloka as an eternal Vaikuntha planet, quoting texts [5.22.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/22.17) and [5.23.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-5/23.1) from the Srimad-Bhagavatam. In his purport to text 29, Srila Prabhupada confirms the unique and exalted benediction Dhruva was offered: “Dhruva Maharaja was offered Dhruvaloka, a planet that was never resided upon by any conditioned soul. Even Brahma, although the topmost living creature within this universe, was not allowed to enter the Dhruvaloka. Whenever there is a crisis within this universe, the demigods go to see the Supreme Personality of Godhead Ksirodakasayi Visnu, and they stand on the beach of the Milk Ocean. So the fulfillment of Dhruva Maharaja’s demand—a position more exalted than that of even his great-grandfather, Brahma —was offered to him.”

But even before attaining Dhruvaloka, the Lord continued, Dhruva would remain strong and rule the earth for 36,000 years without aging. The Lord then predicted the future: Dhruva’s stepmother, Suruci, would suffer a reaction for her insult and would lose her only son, Uttama, when he went hunting in the forest. Suruci would also die, burnt to death in a forest fire.

It is worth noting that Suruci’s offense to Dhruva was committed before he had attained the Lord’s darsana. One should take care when dealing with devotees, even if they do not appear advanced at the moment. In his purport to text 23, Srila Prabhupada underlines the danger of offending or insulting Vaisnavas—or anyone: “Dhruva Maharaja came to the forest to search out the Supreme Personality of Godhead with a revenging spirit against his stepmother. His stepmother had insulted Dhruva, who was not an ordinary person, but a great Vaisnava. An offense at the lotus feet of a Vaisnava is the greatest offense in this world. Because of having insulted Dhruva Maharaja, Suruci would become mad upon the death of her son and would enter a forest fire, and thus her life would be ended. This was specifically mentioned by the Lord to Dhruva because he was determined for revenge against her. From this we should take the lesson that we should never try to insult a Vaisnava. Not only should we not insult a Vaisnava, but we should not insult anyone unnecessarily. When Suruci insulted Dhruva Maharaja, he was just a child. She of course did not know that Dhruva was a great recognized Vaisnava, and so her offense was committed unknowingly. When one serves a Vaisnava unknowingly, one still gets the good result, and if one unknowingly insults a Vaisnava, one suffers the bad result.”

The Lord then awarded Dhruva the ability to remember Him fully at death, despite his having ruled as a king surrounded by material opulence for thousands of years. “I am the heart of all sacrifices. You will be able to perform many great sacrifices and also give great charities. In this way you will be able to enjoy the blessings of material happiness in this life, and at the time of your death you will be able to remember Me. . . . My dear Dhruva, after your material life in this body, you will go to My planet, which is always offered obeisances by the residents of all other planetary systems \[polestar\]. It is situated above the planets of the seven rsis, and having gone there you will never have to come back again to this material world.” (Bhag. [4.9.24-25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.24))

We too can attain the benediction of remembering Krsna at the time of death: “In this age of Kali . . . the great sacrifice is the performance of sankirtana-yajha. Our Krsna consciousness movement is designed to teach people (and to learn ourselves) the exact instruction of the Personality of Godhead. In this way we shall continuously perform the sahkirtana^yajria and continuously chant the Hare Krsna mantra. Then at the end of our lives we shall certainly be able to remember Krsna, and our program of life will be successful.” (Bhag. [4.9.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.24), purport)

Hearing the Lord’s benedictions, Dhruva reciprocated by offering the Lord honor and worship. Then as Dhruva looked on, the Lord returned to His own abode.

## Texts 27-36: Dhruva’s Lamentation

Under Narada Muni’s guidance, Dhruva Maharaja had transformed powerful anger to focused determination. Now he had reaped the fruit of his devotion and seen the Lord. His desire had also been fulfilled: he would now rule a kingdom greater than his father’s and grandfather’s. By the Lord’s mercy, Dhruva had achieved the impossible. Yet Dhruva was dissatisfied. He was ashamed of the selfishness that had motivated his worship. He remembered his stepmother’s sharp words and how they had penetrated so deeply that he had lost sight of the actual goal of life. The Lord certainly could have immediately taken Dhruva back to Godhead, but He didn’t. Dhruva’s desire for revenge and a vast material kingdom had earned him those benedictions. He would have to rule on earth for 36,000 years. Dhruva was not overjoyed at this apparent fortune. He considered himself a fool.Srila Prabhupada describes (Bhag. [4.9.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.29), purport) how a pure devotee approaches the Lord:

**A pure devotee has no demand from the Lord. His only concern is to serve the Lord sincerely and seriously, and he is not at all concerned about what will happen in the future. In the Mukunda' malastotra, King Kulasekhara, author of the book, states in his prayer: “My dear Lord, I don’t want any position of sense gratification within this material world. I simply want to engage in Your service perpetually.” Similarly, Lord Caitanya, in His Siksastaka, also prayed, “My Lord, I do not want any amount of material wealth, I do not want any number of materialistic followers, nor do I want any attractive wife to enjoy. The only thing I want is that I may engage life after life in Your service.” Lord Caitanya did not pray even for mukti, or liberation.**

**In this verse Maitreya replied to Vidura that Dhruva Maharaja, influenced by a revengeful attitude towards his insulting stepmother, did not think of mukti, nor did he know what mukti was. Therefore he failed to aim for mukti as his goal in life. But a pure devotee also does not want liberation. He is a soul completely surrendered to the Supreme Lord, and he does not demand anything from the Lord. This position was realized by Dhruva Maharaja when he saw the Supreme Personality of Godhead present personally before him because he was elevated to the vasudeva platform. (Bhag.** [**4.9.29**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.29)**, purport)**

In the same purport, Srila Prabhupada continues, describing the Lord’s kindness to Dhruva:

**Dhruva Maharaja’s demand was for a position so exalted that it was never enjoyed even by Lord Brahma, his great-grandfather. Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is so affectionate and kind towards His devotee, especially to a devotee like Dhruva Maharaja, who went to render devotional service in the forest alone at the age of only five years, that although the motive might be impure, the Lord does not consider the motive; He is concerned with the service. But if a devotee has a particular motive, the Lord directly or indirectly knows it, and therefore He does not leave the devotee’s material desires unfulfilled. These are some of the special favors by the Lord to a devotee.**

According to text 32, Dhruva decided that the demigods must have conspired against him to pollute his intelligence, for although he was the disciple of a great Vaisnava, he was unable to accept his spiritual master’s first instructions and renounce his material ambition. In his purport to text 32, Srila Prabhupada notes: “Dhruva Maharaja regretted very much that he could not take seriously the instruction of his spiritual master and that his consciousness was therefore contaminated. Still, the Lord is so merciful that due to Dhruva’s execution of devotional service He offered Dhruva the ultimate Vaisnava goal.”

And Srila Prabhupada ends his purport to text 31: “In other words, every one of us who is engaged in devotional service in Krsna consciousness should be completely free from all material aspirations. Otherwise we will have to lament like Dhruva Maharaja.”

In text 33 Dhruva Maharaja decided not to blame the demigods. Still, he lamented how tightly he had been gripped by maya: “I was under the influence of the illusory energy; being ignorant of the actual facts, I was sleeping on her lap. Under a vision of duality, I saw my brother as my enemy, and falsely I lamented within my heart, thinking, ‘They are my enemies.’”

Dhruva offered a final lamentation: “Because of my state of complete foolishness and paucity of pious activities, although the Lord offered me His personal service, I wanted material name, fame and prosperity. My case is just like that of the poor man who, when he satisfied a great emperor who wanted to give him anything he might ask, out of ignorance asked only a few broken grains of husked rice.” (Bhag. [4.9.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.35))

Srila Prabhupada explains the misfortune of a devotee who cultivates a materialistic mentality: “The conclusion is that anyone who is engaged in the loving service of the Lord should never ask for material prosperity from the Lord. The awarding of material prosperity simply depends on the stringent rules and regulations of the external energy. Pure devotees ask the Lord only for the privilege of serving Him. This is our real independence. If we want anything else, it is a sign of our misfortune.” (Bhag. [4.9.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.35), purport)

Maitreya Muni concludes this discussion by describing to Vidura Dhruva Maharaja’s unique achievements. He characterizes a pure devotee’s equipoised attitude as “always attached to the honey of His lotus feet,” and says, “In any condition of life, such persons remain satisfied, and thus they never ask the Lord for material prosperity.” (Bhag. [4.9.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.36))

In Priti-sandarbha, anuccheda 45, Srila Jiva Gosvami explains that the words yadrcchaya labdha-manah-samrddhayah in text 36 indicate that devotees, without effort, attain great spiritual wealth, for even the briefest of the Lord’s merciful glances fulfills all their desires. Such is the potency of devotional service.

In his purport to text 36, Srila Prabhupada writes of a devotee’s fixedness in devotional service: “The Lord’s feet are compared to the lotus, wherein there is saffron dust. A devotee is always engaged in drinking the honey from the lotus feet of the Lord. Unless one is freed from all material desires, he cannot actually taste the honey from the Lord’s lotus feet. One has to discharge his devotional duties without being disturbed by the coming and going of material circumstances.”

## Texts 37-67: Dhruva Maharaja Returns to His Father’s Kingdom

Five-year-old Dhruva had braved the forest and had been missing for months. When Maharaja Uttanapada learned from a messenger of his son’s imminent arrival, he feared he had disqualified himself from being able to see Dhruva by his own sinful neglect. Yet as Narada Muni had previously insisted that Dhruva would return, the King eagerly gathered a procession to greet the young prince. Drums and flutes played and brahmanas chanted Vedic mantras. Both of Uttana-pada’s queens accompanied Dhruva’s brother. When Uttanapada saw Dhruva approaching, his heart filled with emotion. He got down from his chariot and affectionately embraced his son with his powerful arms. He immediately saw that Dhruva had changed, sanctified by the Lord’s touch, but nevertheless he bathed his son in torrents of cool tears.

Dhruva offered his obeisances to his father and bowed his head at the feet of both his mothers. Suruci, touched by Dhruva’s noble spirit, said: “My dear boy, long may you live!” (Bhag. [4.9.46](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.46)) Uttama and Dhruva then embraced one another with affection. When Suniti, Dhruva’s natural mother, embraced her son’s tender body, she forgot all her grief. Milk flowed from her breasts and she felt proud to be the mother of such a hero. All the palace residents praised both Dhruva and Suniti. Dhruva then mounted an elephant with Uttama, and the entire procession returned to the capital, which for Dhruva’s home-coming had been decorated with trees, fruits, flowers, auspicious leaves, branches, gates, and lamps.

Dhruva lived in his father’s palace for many years, and Maharaja Uttanapada became fully satisfied both by hearing of his deeds and witnessing his power and influence. Eventually, Maharaja Uttanapada began to feel the warning hand of time. Noting Dhruva’s maturity, he consulted with his ministers and installed Dhruva as world emperor. King Uttanapada then renounced all worldly affairs and went to the forest to perfect his Krsna consciousness.

## Dialogue Three - Dhruva Maharaja’s Reign and Departure

## Chapter 10 - Dhruva Maharaja’s Fight with the Yaksas

### Texts 1-30

King Uttanapada enthroned his son Dhruva, renounced his kingdom, and left for the forest without waiting to arrange Dhruva’s marriage. Prabhupada states in his purport to Bhagavatam [4.10.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/10.1): “Maharaja Uttanapada knew very well that to get his son Dhruva Maharaja married was not so important that it should take preference to his going away to the forest for self-realization.” Shortly after Dhruva Maharaja ascended the throne he married and his wife bore him two sons. He married again, and his second wife gave birth to a son and a beautiful daughter. Life seemed peaceful. Then one day Uttama decided to go hunting in the Himalayas. The Lord had predicted Uttama’s death, and it came to pass as the Lord had said: Uttama was killed by a powerful Yaksa. Suruci went to search for her beloved son, but died in a forest fire. Thus the Lord’s second prediction (Bhag. [4.9.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/9.23)) also came true.

Dhruva Maharaja was outraged at his brother’s death, and for one Yaksa’s crime, the entire Yaksa race would suffer. Dhruva Maharaja’s grief and anger drove him to ferocity. He vowed revenge against the Yaksas, mounted his chariot, and headed north to the Himalayas. Traveling alone through the mountain passes, Dhruva eventually came to Alakapuri, the Yaksa capital, which was located in a valley in the mountains and was populated by Lord Siva’s ghostly followers. Dhruva sounded his conchshell in challenge. Unable to tolerate the challenge, the Yaksas rushed forward, weapons in hand. Heroic Dhruva was both a great charioteer and a bowman. He released volleys of arrows, three at a time, and one Yaksa after another fell. The Yaksas, however, although appreciating Dhruva’s prowess, were valiant, each Yaksa soldier releasing six arrows at a time. The Yaksa army consisted of 130,000 soldiers, and it engulfed Dhruva in a shower of feathered arrows, sharp swords, razor-sharp tridents, pointed lances, and spears. This shower of weapons covered Dhruva Maharaja just as incessant rain obscures a mountain peak. Siddhas from the higher planetary system who were observing the fight from the sky were afraid that Dhruva Maharaja was about to set like the sun in the ocean of the Yaksa army.

In his purport to text 13, Srila Prabhupada cites Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “The example of a mountain peak’s being covered by incessant rain is just suitable, for when a mountain is covered by incessant rain, all dirty things are washed from the body of the mountain. Similarly, the incessant shower of arrows from the enemy gave Dhruva Maharaja new vigor to defeat them. In other words, whatever incompetency he might have had was washed away.”

Indomitable Dhruva, neither discouraged nor defeated, reappeared like the sun burning through a dense fog. Dhruva Maharaja’s bow and arrows twanged as he shot incessant arrows at his enemies and shattered their weapons. The heads of those cut to pieces by Dhruva Maharaja’s arrows were decorated with beautiful earrings and turbans. Their legs were as beautiful as golden palm trees, their arms were decorated with golden jewelry. Valuable helmets bedecked with gold were scattered around the battlefield.

The surviving Yaksas began to flee. “Dhruva Maharaja, the best of human beings, observed that in that great battlefield not one of the opposing soldiers was left standing with proper weapons. He then desired to see the city of Alakapuri, but he thought to himself, ‘No one knows the plans of the mystic Yaksas.’” (Bhag. [4.10.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/10.21)) Suddenly, Dhruva heard a roaring that resembled the roar of the ocean, and a great dust storm appeared to descend from the sky. Lightning and thunder crashed. Blood, stool, urine, pus, mucus, and bodily parts began raining down on Dhruva Maharaja. Dhruva saw serpents, lions, and tigers coming to devour him. “Then, as if it were the time of the dissolution of the whole world, the fierce sea with foaming waves and great roaring sounds came forward before him.” (Bhag. [4.10.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/10.27))

Observing Dhruva’s predicament, great sages sought to encourage him by assembling and praying that the Lord relieve His devotee’s distress. The sages then advised Dhruva: “The holy name of the Lord is as powerful as the Lord Himself. Therefore, simply by chanting and hearing the holy name of the Lord, many men can be fully protected from fierce death without difficulty. Thus a devotee is saved.” (Bhag. [4.10.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/10.30))

Chanting Krsna’s names brings a devotee into Krsna’s association and under His protection. What difficulty can befall one sheltered by Krsna? And where else but Krsna can true shelter be found? The typical material shelters—family, intelligence, money—prove as substantial as clouds. At death, will our consciousness cling to a parting secret that we’ve neglected to communicate to a loved one, or will we have become practiced enough to cling without flinching to Krsna’s names? The difficulties we each face are the tests that allow us to assess our own consciousness. Each day we see ourselves seeking shelter whenever we face trouble, perplexity, or hardship. These tests show where we perceive our shelter to be while simultaneously suggesting whether we need to take remedial measures in our spiritual life.

It is truly in our self-interest to become deeply attached to and sheltered by Krsna. This is more important than cultivating detachment from matter. Positive attachment to Krsna is perfection. Thus the sages instructed Dhruva to surpass the Yaksas’ illusory warfare by chanting Krsna’s holy names, a point Srila Prabhupada expands on in his purport to text 30: “The great rsis approached Dhruva Maharaja at a time when his mind was very perplexed due to the magical feats exhibited by the Yaksas. A devotee is always protected by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. By His inspiration only, the sages came to encourage Dhruva Maharaja and assure him that there was no danger because he was a soul fully surrendered to the Supreme Lord. By the grace of the Lord, if a devotee, at the time of death, can simply chant His holy name—Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare / Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare—simply by chanting this maha-mantra, he immediately surpasses the great ocean of the material sky and enters the spiritual sky. He never has to come back for repetition of birth and death. Simply by chanting the holy name of the Lord, one can surpass the ocean of death, so Dhruva Maharaja was certainly able to surpass the illusory magical feats of the Yaksas, which for the time being disturbed his mind.”

Thus Krsna had kindly sent the sages to Dhruva in his time of need to guide him in finding His merciful shelter and protection. This then —the gift of Vaisnava sanga—is Krsna’s central method of offering mercy in this world.

## Chapter 11 - Svayambhuva Manu Advises Dhruva Maharaja to Stop Fighting

## Texts 1-5: Dhruva Maharaja Slays the Yaksas

Encouraged by the sages’ words, Dhruva fixed to his bow the arrow Lord Narayana had once given him. When the arrow touched the bow, “the illusion created by the Yaksas was immediately vanquished, just as all material pains and pleasures are vanquished when one becomes fully cognizant of the self.” (Bhag. [4.11.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.2))

Srila Prabhupada explains in his purports to texts 1 and 2 that as Lord Narayana’s astra dispelled the Yaksas’ illusions, so the “weapon” given by Lord Caitanya dispels the illusions of Kali-yuga: “Without Narayana, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, no one is able to overcome the action of the illusory energy. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu has also given us a nice weapon for this age, as stated in the Bhagavatam: sangopangastra—in this age, the narayanastra, or weapon to drive away maya, is the chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra in pursuance of the associates of Lord Caitanya, such as Advaita Prabhu, Nityananda, Gadadhara and Srivasa.” (Bhag. [4.11.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.1), purport)

“Krsna is like the sun, and maya, or the illusory energy of Krsna, is like darkness. Darkness means absence of light; similarly, maya means absence of Krsna consciousness. Krsna consciousness and maya are always there, side by side. As soon as there is awakening of Krsna consciousness, all the illusory pains and pleasures of material existence are vanquished. Mayam etam taranti te: constant chanting of the maha-mantra will keep us always aloof from the illusory energy of maya.” (Bhag. [4.11.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.2), purport)

Krsna and maya can no more coexist than light and darkness. As darkness flees from light, so maya departs when a soul attains Krsna’s shelter. However, it is worth noting that both the quality and the quantity of the light is important. A fragile flame may offer some light, even though flickering, but darkness lurks nearby; the light is too dim to drive away darkness completely. Similarly, weak, inconsistent surrender at Krsna’s feet may hold maya back, but it will not drive maya away completely. The conditioned soul tends toward wavering surrender, but Srila Prabhupada offers a beacon for souls hoping to move toward more complete shelter at Krsna’s feet: constant chanting of Krsna’s names keeps maya away permanently, just as the constant and brilliant presence of the sun causes darkness to vanish.

“Even as Dhruva Maharaja fixed the weapon made by Narayana Rsi onto his bow, arrows with golden shafts and feathers like the wings of a swan flew out from it. They entered the enemy soldiers with a great hissing sound, just as peacocks enter a forest with tumultuous crowing. Those sharp arrows dismayed the enemy soldiers, who became almost unconscious, but various Yaksas on the battlefield, in a rage against Dhruva Maharaja, somehow or other collected their weapons and attacked. Just as serpents agitated by Garuda rush towards Garuda with upraised hoods, all the Yaksa soldiers prepared to overcome Dhruva Maharaja with their upraised weapons.” (Bhag. [4.11.3-4](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.3)) Dhruva cut the enemy to pieces with his arrows. Separating their arms, legs, heads, and bellies from their bodies, he killed them, delivering them to an exalted destination above the sun globe ordinarily reserved only for pure brahmacaris. Thus Dhruva Maharaja slew any Yaksa who continued fighting.

## Texts 6-14: Svayambhuva Manu Instructs Dhruva Maharaja—One Should Act to Satisfy the Lord

Svayambhuva Manu, Dhruva’s grandfather, saw Dhruva killing Yaksas who had had nothing to do with Uttama’s death. He approached Dhruva and asked him to stop killing the sinless. So many innocent persons had died to avenge one death, and Dhruva had certainly already proven his affection for Uttama. Because one person was killed, so many died as a consequence. Manu is the great lawgiver, and he disapproves of unnecessary violence: “One should not accept the body as the self and thus, like the animals, kill the bodies of others. This is especially forbidden by saintly persons, who follow the path of devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [4.11.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.10)) О Dhruva, to achieve Vaikuntha, the abode of Hari, is difficult, but your Lord has already planned your journey to that holy abode because you have worshiped Him. Please do not forget that He resides in the heart of every living entity. Do not unnecessarily kill any living entity, even your enemy, for all living entities are souls inhabiting different bodies. Do not cause them suffering. You are a pure devotee and are always thinking of your Lord, as He is also thinking of you. Everyone recognizes you as His confidential devotee. Therefore you should live an exemplary life. “I am therefore surprised—why have you undertaken such an abominable task?” (Bhag. [4.11.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.12))

Srila Prabhupada describes the responsibility pure devotees accept: “Dhruva Maharaja was a pure devotee and was accustomed to always thinking of the Lord. Reciprocally, the Lord always thinks of those pure devotees who think of Him only, twenty-four hours a day. As a pure devotee does not know anything beyond the Lord, so the Lord does not know anything beyond His pure devotee. Svayambhuva Manu pointed out this fact to Dhruva Maharaja: ‘Not only are you a pure devotee, but you are recognized by all pure devotees of the Lord. You should always act in such an exemplary way that others may learn from you. Under the circumstances, it is surprising that you have killed so many faultless Yaksas.’” (Bhag. [4.11.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.12), purport)

Instead of avenging his brother by killing Yaksas, what should Dhruva have done? How should he have responded to his brother’s death? We ourselves may never have to decide how to deal with a family member’s murder, but it is important to understand the criteria that determine proper action in difficult situations. Svayambhuva Manu now describes an essential principle: “The Lord is very satisfied with His devotee when the devotee greets other people with tolerance, mercy, friendship and equality.” (Bhag. [4.11.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.13)) In other words, one should act only to please Krsna. Svayambhuva Manu asks Dhruva to decide whether or not his actions were pleasing to the Lord. Was he treating the Yaksas with tolerance, mercy, friendship, and equality? Srila Prabhupada writes: “It is the duty of an advanced devotee in the second stage of devotional perfection to act in accordance with this verse.. .. His general view should be to see every living entity as part of the Supreme Lord. Different living entities appear in different forms of dress, but according to the instruction of the Bhagavad-gita, a learned person sees all living entities equally. Such treatment by the devotee is very much appreciated by the Supreme Lord.” (Bhag. [4.11.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.13), purport)

In his purport to text 14, Srila Prabhupada describes the difference between how a devotee thinks and how karmis (gross sense gratifiers), jndnis (subtle sense gratifiers), and yogis (those aspiring for mystic perfection) think: “Only devotees try to satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” Earlier in the same purport he writes, “A person should act in such a way that the Lord is satisfied by the activity; it is not that he himself is to be satisfied. Of course, when the Lord is satisfied, the devotee automatically becomes satisfied. This is the secret of the process of bhakti-yoga.”

To meditate consistently on pleasing Krsna and then to act accordingly is the definition of selfless, surrendered, divine consciousness. What will the result of such behavior be? Manu says: One who actually satisfies the Supreme Lord becomes liberated. Thus being freed from material bondage, he achieves unlimited spiritual bliss.

Why should acting for Krsna’s pleasure bring such a wonderful result? Can one achieve the same result while motivated by either the desire to escape material misery or to attain devotional bliss? And even if one is not selfishly motivated, why should one serve Krsna? Svayambhuva Manu will respond to these questions by describing the relationship between the Lord, the living entities, and everything that happens in the world.

## Texts 15-27: Svayambhuva Manu Instructs Dhruva Maharaja—The Lord Is the Cause of Everything, so Surrender to His Will

First, one must understand who actually killed Dhruva’s brother: “The creation of the material world begins with the five elements, and thus everything, including the body of a man or a woman, is created of these elements. By the sexual life of man and woman, the number of men and women in this material world is further increased. . . . My dear King Dhruva, it is simply by the illusory, material energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and by the interaction of the three modes of material nature that creation, maintenance and annihilation take place.” (Bhag. [4.11.15-16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.15))

In his purport to text 15, Prabhupada delineates Manu’s line of reasoning: “When Svayambhuva Manu saw that Dhruva Maharaja understood the philosophy of Vaisnavism and yet was still dissatisfied because of his brother’s death, he gave him an explanation of how this material body is created by the five elements of material nature. ... In the background, of course, there is the direction of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is also confirmed in Bhagavad-gita (mayadhyaksena). In the Ninth Chapter, Krsna says, ‘Under My superintendence material nature is acting.’ Svayambhuva Manu wanted to impress on Dhruva Maharaja that the death of the material body of his brother was not actually the Yaksas’ fault; it was an act of the material nature.”

The ultimate cause behind everything in material nature, Srila Prabhupada writes, is Dhruva’s worshipful Lord: “The potter’s wheel rotates, and several varieties of earthen pots come out. There are many causes for the earthen pots, but the original cause is the potter, who sets a force on the wheel. That force comes by his superintendence. The same idea is explained in Bhagavad-gita—behind all material action and reaction there is Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [4.11.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.17), purport)

Manu continues: “My dear Dhruva, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is uncontaminated by the material modes of nature. He is the remote cause of the creation of this material cosmic manifestation. When He gives the impetus, many other causes and effects are produced, and thus the whole universe moves, just as iron moves by the integrated force of a magnet.” (Bhag. [4.11.17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.17))

Does this mean that Dhruva should hold the Lord responsible for his brother’s death? Manu explains further how the Lord is simultaneously active and inactive in the creation: Everything that occurs happens by His inconceivable, supreme energy time. Time causes the three modes to interact. The Lord manifests all His energies in the form of time. “It appears that He is acting, but He is not the actor. He is killing, but He is not the killer. Thus it is understood that only by His inconceivable power is everything happening.” (Bhag. [4.11.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.18))

Despite His being aloof from matter, the Lord is the ultimate controller and cause of everything. By His impetus all other causes and effects are produced. Nothing occurs without His sanction, yet He Himself does nothing. Prabhupada calls the Lord’s actions acintya-bhedabheda in his purport to text 18: He does everything, but simultaneously does nothing. Therefore He cannot be held responsible for what occurs. “It is incorrect to argue ... that because energy issues from the Supreme Personality of Godhead, He is the actor. In the previous verse, the word nimitta'matram indicates that the Supreme Lord is completely aloof from the action and reaction of this material world. How is everything being done? The word ‘inconceivable’ has been used. It is not within the power of one’s small brain to comprehend; unless one accepts the inconceivable power and energy of the Lord, one cannot make any progress. The forces which act are certainly set up by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but He is always aloof from their action and reaction. The varieties of energies produced by the interaction of material nature produce the varieties of species of life and their resultant happiness and unhappiness.”

Manu says further: “My dear Dhruva, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is ever existing, but in the form of time, He is the killer of everything.” (Bhag. [4.11.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.19)) By time He destroys, crushing and killing everything in existence. Time, the Lord’s potent energy, dominates the material world. Time causes everything in creation to progress, and it disrupts all stability. Time, moving and unstoppable, pushes onward forever. People hope that unpleasant situations will end and they fear the end of pleasant situations, but time is indiscriminate and relentless, crushing everything and everyone in its path. All-powerful time is an energy of the Supersoul, but is only an expansion of an expansion of the Lord. How powerful, then, is svayam-bhagavan Krsna?

Svayambhuva Manu asked Dhruva: Who has ultimately killed your brother? Manu’s own understanding was clear: The world’s events are neither indicative of the Lord’s specific will nor His doing. Dhruva should know that the Lord was not his killer, for whatever occurs in the material world is neither directly the Lord’s will nor His doing. The Lord had not killed Dhruva’s brother; He is aloof and only impartially sanctions the continuous flow of karma, the material actions and their reactions, through the time factor. Although it is Krsna who sanctions and who is therefore the ultimate cause of everything, everyone is suffering and enjoying only according to his or her own karma. The Lord only awards the reactions through the time factor. Everyone, therefore, suffers and enjoys according to his or her own deeds.

“The differentiation among varieties of life and their suffering and enjoyment is explained by some to be the result of karma. Others say it is due to nature, others due to time, others due to fate, and still others say that it is due to desire.” (Bhag. [4.11.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.22))

Krsna has created a system in which much suffering exists. How, then, can we say that He is not ultimately responsible for everyone’s suffering? Can He be accused of cruelty? Srila Prabhupada compares the material world to a state in which maintaining law and order is in the hands of the police: “A government state is always supposed to be merciful, but sometimes, in order to keep law and order, the government employs its police force, and thus punishment is meted out to the rebellious citizens. Similarly, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is always merciful and full of transcendental qualities, but certain individual souls have forgotten their relationship with Krsna and have endeavored to lord it over material nature.” (Bhag. [4.11.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.18), purport)

After setting up the laws, the Lord, like a king, remains neutral. Individuals then decide whether to maintain the law or to break it. Those who misuse their free will and break the law go to prison. Although a prisoner may say he is suffering because of the king, we know he is not speaking factually. The criminal has caused his own suffering.We must ask: Can the living entities, even the convicted criminals, truly be held responsible for their actions in the presence of a supreme controller? Do they truly have the power of free will required for them to accept responsibility for their actions? Srila Prabhupada addressed these questions on a morning walk in Mayapur in 1976:

**Ramesvara: I spoke with one man who argued that “Krsna is very cruel because He knows everything past, present, and future, so He knew that we would all fall down from the spiritual sky. Still, He gave us the independence to fall down.**

**Prabhupada: Hmm?**

**Ramesvara: Even though He knew we would fall, because He knows everything ...**

**Acyutananda: That’s a common question.**

**Prabhupada: That is another foolish question. Unless you have independence, what is your life? Then you are a dead stone. You want to become a dead stone? That is not Krsna’s concern. Krsna does not give such perfection that you become a dead stone.**

In his purport to text 22 Srila Prabhupada clarifies that it is indeed the living entities’ freely chosen unlawful desires and subsequent actions that cause their suffering. They must therefore accept responsibility for themselves. The “curse” of free will is simultaneously Krsna’s greatest blessing: “The living entity is not a dead stone; he has different varieties of desire, or kama. .. . This kama, or desire, cannot be annihilated. There are some philosophers who say that if one gives up his desires, he again becomes liberated. But it is not at all possible to give up desire, for desire is a symptom of the living entity. If there were no desire, then the living entity would be a dead stone. Srila Narottama dasa Thakura, therefore, advises that one turn his desire towards serving the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Then desire becomes purified. And when one’s desires are purified, one becomes liberated from all material contamination. The conclusion is that the different philosophers’ theories to explain the varieties of life and their pleasure and pain are all imperfect. The real explanation is that we are eternal servants of God and that as soon as we forget this relationship we are thrown into the material world, where we create our different activities and suffer or enjoy the result. We are drawn into this material world by desire, but the same desire must be purified and employed in the devotional service of the Lord. Then our disease of wandering in the universe under different forms and conditions will end.”

Who, then, is this all-powerful cause of everything? And how can one know that mysterious Absolute Truth, Krsna, who grants the living entities their free will and who simultaneously does everything yet does nothing? How can a living entity under the Lord’s control know the Person who controls him? Manu’s answer is clear: No one can understand Him by his own power. That Truth can only be known when the Lord reveals Himself. Those following the ascending process will forever fail to find Him.

In his purport to text 23 Srila Prabhupada describes bhakti, the process of descending grace through which Krsna may be known: “The bhakti-yoga process ... is completely different from so-called scientific advancement of knowledge. A devotee completely surrenders unto the Supreme, who reveals Himself by His causeless mercy. As stated in Bhagavad-gita, dadami buddhi-yogam tarn. The Lord says, ‘I give him intelligence.’ What is that intelligence? Yena mam upa-yanti te. The Lord gives one the intelligence to cross over the ocean of nescience and come back home, back to Godhead. In conclusion, the cause of all causes, the Absolute Truth, or Supreme Brahman, cannot be understood by philosophical speculation, but He reveals Himself to His devotee because the devotee fully surrenders unto His lotus feet. Bhagavad-gita is therefore to be accepted as a revealed scripture spoken by the Absolute Truth Himself when He descended to this planet. If any intelligent man wants to know what God is, he should study this transcendental literature under the guidance of a bona fide spiritual master. Then it is very easy to understand Krsna as He is.”

Manu continued: Every living being’s birth and death are ultimately caused by the Supreme, the cause of all causes. It was He, not these Yaksas, who actually killed your brother. He is the ultimate killer of everyone, for He is the ultimate annihilator of the material cosmos. Yet He remains ever unaffected by reactions to His deeds.

As described in Srimad-Bhagavatam [2.5.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/5.24), [3.5.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/5.28), [3.26.23-24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/26.23), and other Bhagavatam texts, ahahkara is the foundation of material existence. Ahahkara is the soul’s false, selfish, self-absorbed, selfconception—his viewing himself as independent of Krsna. Under the spell of ahahkara persons act for their own pleasure, accrue reactions, and find themselves entangled in matter. Thus their material existence lengthens. In his purport to text 25 of this chapter Srila Prabhupada clarifies why living entities are affected by their actions while Krsna remains unaffected: “In this verse the word anahahkara means ‘without ego.’ The conditioned soul has a false ego, and as a result of his karma he gets different types of bodies in this material world.” As Krsna possesses no false ego, His work does not bind Him. “Krsna has no false ego, for He does not identify Himself with the false and temporary body. His body is always eternal; He descends to this world in His own original, spiritual body.”

Krsna is the ultimate controller and maintainer of everything in the material and spiritual worlds, which include both His external and internal energies. Therefore, Manu requested: “Please surrender unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the ultimate goal of the progress of the world. Everyone, including the demigods headed by Lord Brahma, is working under His control, just as a bull, prompted by a rope in its nose, is controlled by its owner.” (Bhag. [4.11.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.27))

In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada reveals Manu’s hopes in offering instructions to Dhruva: “Dhruva Maharaja was advised to stop fighting by his grandfather, who was concerned that Dhruva was adhering to a personal ambition to fight to annihilate the whole race of Yaksas. In this verse, therefore, Svayambhuva Manu seeks to eradicate the last tinge of false ambition in Dhruva by explaining the position of the supreme controller.”

Actions performed as surrender are enacted for Krsna’s pleasure. They are based on the soul’s real ego, its actual identity, for it is every soul’s nature to serve Krsna. Actions impelled by motives other than pleasing Krsna are unnatural, impelled by false ego. They therefore bind a soul to illusion.

Svayambhuva Manu now speaks further on surrendered service.

## Texts 28-34: Svayambhuva Manu Instructs Dhruva to Surrender to the Lord and Give up His Anger

To add further weight to his argument, Manu reminded Dhruva how as a child he had surrendered to the Lord and come under His protection. As a result, Manu explained, within six months you achieved the topmost position in the material world and were able to see the Lord face to face.
