Thus Manu expressed his pride in Dhruva, his descendant.

Factually, as Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 28: “. . . Dhruva Maharaja is the glory of the Manu dynasty, or the human family. . . . Not only is Dhruva Maharaja the glory of the family of Svayambhuva Manu, but he is the glory of the entire human society. Because Dhruva Maharaja had already surrendered to the Supreme Godhead, he was especially requested not to do anything unbefitting a surrendered soul.”

Manu continued: Turn your attention to the Supreme Person once more. Face the Lord from your natural position as His surrendered servant and you will find this material differentiation (between yourself and the Yaksas) as unimportant as the flickering of a candle flame.

Srila Prabhupada explains that Manu wanted Dhruva to surpass the understanding of an ordinary man when he looked at the Yaksas: “Indirectly Manu pointed out to Dhruva Maharaja that out of material affection Dhruva thought of his brother as his kin and the Yaksas as his enemies. Such observation of differentiation subsides as soon as one is situated in his original position as an eternal servant of the Lord.” (Bhag. [4.11.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.29), purport) Brothers are not eternally brothers, nor are Yaksas eternally Yaksas. A learned devotee recognizes that in each body, regardless of the bodily type, is a soul and the Supersoul. “The humble sages, by virtue of true knowledge, see with equal vision a learned and gentle brahmana, a cow, an elephant, a dog and a dogeater \[outcaste\].” (Bg. [5.18](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/5.18)) Dhruva’s lamenting his brother’s death by angrily retaliating and killing thousands of Yaksas was based on material vision, a vision that would bring him a severe reaction as well as displease the Lord. Kapila Muni describes (Bhag. [3.29.22-24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/29.22)) the fruitless result of worshiping the Lord while maintaining enmity with living entities, who are part of Him: “One who worships the Deity of Godhead in the temples but does not know that the Supreme Lord, as Paramatma, is situated in every living entity’s heart, must be in ignorance and is compared to one who offers oblations into ashes. One who offers Me respect but is envious of the bodies of others and is therefore a separatist never attains peace of mind, because of his inimical behavior towards other living entities. My dear Mother, even if he worships with proper rituals and paraphernalia, a person who is ignorant of My presence in all living entities never pleases Me by the worship of My Deities in the temple.”

Manu said: Regaining your natural surrendered relationship to the Lord and His service will vanquish your misunderstandings. “My dear King, just consider what I have said to you, which will act as medicinal treatment upon disease. Control your anger, for anger is the foremost enemy on the path of spiritual realization. I wish all good fortune for you. Please follow my instructions. A person who desires liberation from this material world should not fall under the control of anger because when bewildered by anger one becomes a source of dread for all others.” (Bhag. [4.11.31-32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.31))

Those wishing to make spiritual advancement must give up anger. Srila Prabhupada advises: “Dhruva Maharaja was a liberated soul, and actually he was not angry with anyone. But because he was the ruler, it was his duty to become angry for some time in order to keep law and order in the state. His brother, Uttama, was without fault, yet he was killed by one of the Yaksas. It was the duty of Dhruva Maharaja to kill the offender (life for life) because Dhruva was the king. When the challenge came, Dhruva Maharaja fought vehemently and punished the Yaksas sufficiently. But anger is such that if one increases it, it increases unlimitedly. In order that Dhruva Maharaja’s kingly anger not exceed the limit, Manu was kind enough to check his grandson. Dhruva Maharaja could understand the purpose of his grandfather, and he immediately stopped the fighting.” (Bhag. [4.11.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.31), purport)

How can one check anger? Prabhupada continues: “The words srutena bhuyasd, ‘by constantly hearing,’ are very important in this verse. By constantly hearing about devotional service, one can check the force of anger, which is detrimental to the process of devotional service. Pariksit Maharaja said that the constant hearing of the pastimes of the Lord is the panacea for all material diseases. Everyone, therefore, should hear about the Supreme Personality of Godhead constantly. By hearing one can always remain in equilibrium, and thus his progress in spiritual life will not be hampered.”

Is it sensible to renounce anger, which may be required to instill fear or keep enemies at bay? Prabhupada explains in the same purport:

**Dhruva Maharaja’s becoming angry with the miscreants was quite appropriate. There is a short story in this connection about a snake who became a devotee upon instruction by Narada, who instructed him not to bite anymore. Since ordinarily a snake’s business is to fatally bite other living entities, as a devotee he was forbidden to do so. Unfortunately, people took advantage of this nonviolence on the part of the snake, especially the children, who began to throw stones at him. He did not bite anyone, however, because it was the instruction of his spiritual master. After a while, when the snake met his spiritual master, Narada, he complained, “I have given up the bad habit of biting innocent living entities, but they are mistreating me by throwing stones at me.” Upon hearing this, Narada Muni instructed him, “Don’t bite, but do not forget to expand your hood as if you were going to bite. Then they will go away.” Similarly, a devotee is always nonviolent; he is qualified with all good characteristics. But, in the common world, when there is mischief made by others, he should not forget to become angry, at least for the time being, in order to drive away the miscreants.**

Manu concluded his instructions with an admonition: You have retaliated against the Yaksa race because a single Yaksa killed your brother. You have thus disrespected Kuvera, because the Yaksas belong to his family. Pacify Kuvera with gentle words and prayers so that his wrath does not affect our family.

After saying this and receiving Dhruva’s respects, Manu returned home.

## Chapter 12 - Dhruva Maharaja Goes Back to Godhead

## Texts 1-9: The Instructions and Benedictions of Kuvera to Dhruva Maharaja

Manu’s instructions assuaged Dhruva Maharaja’s anger, and he stopped his belligerence. Kuvera was satisfied to hear that Dhruva’s enmity toward the Yaksas had ended. Speaking as Manu had but from a different vantage point, Kuvera graciously pointed out that Dhruva had not ultimately killed the Yaksas, because the Supreme Lord is the final cause in this world in His feature as eternal time. Thus both Manu and Kuvera instructed Dhruva to increase his awareness of the ultimate doer. Srila Prabhupada writes: “When the master of the treasury addressed him as sinless, Dhruva Maharaja, considering himself responsible for killing so many Yaksas, might have thought himself otherwise. Kuvera, however, assured him that factually he had not killed any of the Yaksas; therefore, he was not at all sinful. He did his duty as a king, as it is ordered by the laws of nature. ‘Nor should you think that your brother was killed by the Yaksas,’ said Kuvera. ‘He died or was killed in due course of time by the laws of nature. Eternal time, one of the features of the Lord, is ultimately responsible for annihilation and generation. You are not responsible for such actions.”’ (Bhag. [4.12.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.3), purport)

Again, with concepts similar to Manu’s, Kuvera further advised Dhruva: Do not see bodily differences. Everyone should be seen in oneness because we are all the Lord’s servants. Even so, all entities are distinct individuals. Everything is nondifferent from the Lord, but at the same time, only the Lord is Lord. He is beyond our sense perception and is the Supersoul. As He is the greatest on whom all of us depend, we are each insignificant and should serve Him with great devotion. Although everything in the material world occurs by His acintya-sakti, the Lord is nevertheless aloof from the influence of His material energy. By serving Him one can also remain aloof from material actions and reactions. Nondevotees fail to serve the Lord, and therefore they become further entangled through each action they perform.

Kuvera, pleased with Dhruva, spoke sweetly. “My dear Dhruva Maharaja, son of Maharaja Uttanapada, we have heard that you are constantly engaged in transcendental loving service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is known for His lotus navel. You are therefore worthy to take all benedictions from us. Please, therefore, ask without hesitation whatever benediction you want from me.” (Bhag. [4.12.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.7))

Dhruva, who as a boy had gone to the jungle and performed arduous austerities to gain an unparalleled kingdom, now begged Kuvera, treasurer of the demigods, “that he might have unflinching faith in and remembrance of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for thus a person can cross over the ocean of nescience very easily, although it is very difficult for others to cross.” (Bhag. [4.12.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.8))

How radically Dhruva’s mentality had changed! As a child he had desired material benediction. Now his devotion had matured and he wanted only increased service to the Lord. In text 8, Maitreya Muni refers to Dhruva as maha-bhagavato maha-matih, a first-class pure devotee and most intelligent. Dhruva revealed his intelligence in declining any material benediction from Kuvera. By Krsna’s grace he had fully realized the worthlessness of worldly benediction and now desired only wealth of spiritual significance. Dhruva had truly come to understand the meaning of his life. Kuvera appreciated Dhruva’s devotion and awarded him his request. Then Dhruva Maharaja returned to his capital.

How could Kuvera, who is not an unalloyed bhakta, have the power to bless Dhruva with unflinching faith and remembrance of the Supreme Lord? Srila Jiva Gosvami explains, mahabhagavato 'pi acalam smrtim, vavra iti na yavanmahatam teja, ity adipita-mahavakyad bhagavat-smaranadau vighnamasankyeti bhavah: The great mahabhagavata asked for unbroken remembrance because Manu’s words \[in [4.11.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/11.34), pacifying Kuvera\] warning him that the wrath of great personalities might befall “our family” made him apprehensive about encountering obstacles in his remembrance of the Lord \[because of his offense toward Kuvera\]. In other words, Dhruva Maharaja’s request to Kuvera would naturally remove any lingering resentment on Kuvera’s part that might act as an obstacle to Dhruva’s krsna-smaranam.

## Texts 10-16: Dhruva Maharaja Rules with Renunciation

Dhruva returned home and, fulfilling his kingly duties, performed many sacrifices for the Supreme Lord’s pleasure. In his purport to text 10 Srila Prabhupada speaks about the sacrifices Dhruva performed: “Although Dhruva Maharaja was a great devotee and had nothing to do with these sacrifices, to set an example to his people he performed many sacrifices and gave all his wealth in charity. For as long as he lived as a householder, he never spent a farthing for his sense gratification.” It was Dhruva’s duty to act as an exemplary king, and he “rendered devotional service unto the Supreme, the reservoir of everything, with unrelenting force.” He saw that “everything is situated in Him only and that He is situated in all living entities.” He realized that the Lord is called Acyuta “because He never fails in His prime duty, to give protection to His devotees.” (Bhag. [4.12.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.11))

The instructions of Svayambhuva Manu and Kuvera had fructified, and Dhruva’s vision had cleared. Srila Prabhupada describes Dhruva Maharaja’s pure vision: “Ordinary persons cannot understand how the Supreme Lord is situated in everyone’s heart, but a devotee can actually see Him. Not only can the devotee see Him outwardly, but he can see, with spiritual vision, that everything is resting in the Supreme Personality of Godhead, as described in Bhagavad-gita (mat' sthani sarva-bhutani). That is the vision of a maha-bhagavata. He sees everything others see, but instead of seeing merely the trees, the mountains, the cities or the sky, he sees only his worshipable Supreme Personality of Godhead in everything because everything is resting in Him only. This is the vision of the maha-bhagavata. In summary, a mahd' bhagavata, a highly elevated pure devotee, sees the Lord everywhere, as well as within the heart of everyone. This is possible for devotees who have developed elevated devotional service to the Lord. As stated in the Brahma-samhita (5.38), premanjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena: only those who have smeared their eyes with the ointment of love of Godhead can see everywhere the Supreme Lord face to face ...” (Bhag. [4.12.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.11), purport)

Exalted Maharaja Dhruva protected his citizens, considering them like his own children. Fixed in devotional service he was unaffected by the material world. He “diminished the reactions of pious activities by enjoyment, and by practicing austerities he diminished inauspicious reactions.” (Bhag. [4.12.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.13)) Thus internally renounced, Dhruva dutifully ruled throughout his long life. Viewing the material world as a dream, he remained interested only in reality. As his life drew to a close, Dhruva left his kingdom, wives, children, friends, army, and treasury and retired to holy Badarikasrama, high in the Himalayas.

Srila Prabhupada explains the path of detachment in a materialistic milieu: “Since he ruled over the world for thirty-six thousand years, naturally one may conclude that he became very, very old, but factually his senses were very young—and yet he was not interested in sense gratification. In other words, he remained self-controlled. He performed his duties perfectly according to the materialistic way. That is the way of behavior of great devotees. Srila Raghunatha dasa Gosvami, one of the direct disciples of Lord Caitanya, was the son of a very rich man. Although he had no interest in enjoying material happiness, when he was entrusted with doing something in managing the state, he did it perfectly. Srila Gaurasundara advised him, ‘From within, keep yourself and your mind completely aloof, but externally execute the material duties just as they need to be done.’ This transcendental position can be achieved by devotees only, as described in the Bhagavad-gita: while others, such as yogis, try to control their senses by force, devotees, even though possessing full sensory powers, do not use them because they engage in higher, transcendental activities.” (Bhag. [4.12.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.14), purport)

## Texts 17-39: Dhruva Maharaja Remains at Badarikasrama and then Returns to the Spiritual World

While at Badarikasrama Dhruva perfected the yoga practices and remained in trance, focusing his mind wholly on the Lord’s arca-vigraha. He was overwhelmed with bliss; tears flowed from his eyes and his heart melted. Rapt in meditation on the Lord, he was liberated, experiencing a life beyond his bodily existence. In his purport to text 18 Srila Prabhupada speaks of liberation: “When a devotee completely forgets his bodily existence, he should be understood to be liberated. He is no longer encaged in the body. The example is given that when a coconut becomes completely dry, the coconut pulp within the coconut shell separates from the bondage of the shell and the outer covering. By moving the dry coconut, one can hear that the pulp within is no longer attached to the shell or to the covering. Similarly, when one is fully absorbed in devotional service, he is completely disconnected from the two material coverings, the subtle and gross bodies. ... Of course, from the beginning of devotional service the path of liberation immediately opens, just as the coconut taken from the tree immediately begins to dry; it simply takes some time for the shell and pulp to separate from one another.”

“As soon as the symptoms of his liberation were manifest, he saw a very beautiful airplane coming down from the sky, as if the brilliant full moon were coming down, illuminating all the ten directions.” (Bhag. [4.12.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.19)) Dhruva saw two lustrous persons standing on the plane, and he could tell they were associates of the Lord. They were youthful, and their eyes were as red as lotus flowers. “They held clubs in their hands, and they were dressed in very attractive garments with helmets and were decorated with necklaces, bracelets and earrings.” (Bhag. [4.12.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.20)) These uncommon personalities were the Lord’s servants, yet Dhruva, in his eagerness, forgot to receive them properly. He simply offered obeisances with folded hands and chanted the Lord’s holy names.

Srila Prabhupada glorifies the appropriateness of always chanting the Lord’s holy names: “When Dhruva Maharaja saw the Visnudutas, the direct associates of Lord Visnu, four-handed and nicely decorated, he could understand who they were, but for the time being he was puzzled. But simply by chanting the holy name of the Lord, the Hare Krsna mantra, he could satisfy the uncommon guests who had all of a sudden arrived before him. The chanting of the holy name of the Lord is perfect; even though one does not know how to please Lord Visnu or His associates, simply by sincerely chanting the holy name of the Lord, everything becomes perfect. A devotee, therefore, either in danger or in happiness, constantly chants the Hare Krsna mantra. When he is in danger he is immediately relieved, and when he is in a position to see Lord Visnu or His associates directly, by chanting this maha-mantra he can please the Lord. This is the absolute nature of the maha-mantra. Either in danger or in happiness, it can be chanted without limitation.” (Bhag. [4.12.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.21), purport)

“Dhruva Maharaja was always absorbed in thinking of the lotus feet of Lord Krsna. His heart was full with Krsna. When the two confidential servants of the Supreme Lord, who were named Nanda and Sunanda, approached him, smiling happily, Dhruva stood with folded hands, bowing humbly.” (Bhag. [4.12.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.22)) The Lord’s servants blessed him while repeating his life history. They glorified Dhruva’s severe austerities and said that as a small child he had satisfied the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In his purport to text 22 Srila Prabhupada comments on the universality of Dhruva’s achievement: “What was possible for Dhruva Maharaja is possible for everyone. Anyone who very seriously engages in devotional service can obtain, in due course of time, the same perfection of the human form of life.”

In his purport to text 23 Srila Prabhupada emphasizes that giving children a proper education will help them attain life’s perfection: “What was possible for Dhruva Maharaja is possible for anyone. Any five-year-old child can be trained, and within a very short time his life will become successful by realization of Krsna consciousness. Unfortunately, this training is lacking all over the world. It is necessary for the leaders of the Krsna consciousness movement to start educational institutions in different parts of the world to train children, starting at the age of five years. Thus such children will not become hippies or spoiled children of society; rather, they can all become devotees of the Lord. The face of the world will then change automatically.”

In his purport to text 34 Srila Prabhupada makes a similar point, underlining the responsibility of parents: “It should be noted also that while Suniti was going to Vaikunthaloka she also changed her body into spiritual form. Like Sri Suniti, every mother should train her child to become a devotee like Dhruva Maharaja. Suniti instructed her son, even at the age of five years, to be unattached to worldly affairs and to go to the forest to search out the Supreme Lord. She never desired that her son remain at home comfortably without ever undertaking austerities and penances to achieve the favor of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Every mother, like Suniti, must take care of her son and train him to become a brahmacari from the age of five years and to undergo austerities and penances for spiritual realization. The benefit will be that if her son becomes a strong devotee like Dhruva, certainly not only will he be transferred back home, back to Godhead, but she will also be transferred with him to the spiritual world, even though she may be unable to undergo austerities and penances in executing devotional service.”

Thereafter, the Visnudutas, whose forms resembled the Lord’s, informed Dhruva that the Lord now desired that he go to the polestar, the Visnuloka within the universe. They first reminded Dhruva that he had attained a kingdom greater than that of his fathers and grandfathers, then said: “Now please come; you are welcome to go there. . . . Please come with us and live there eternally. . . You are quite worthy to board such a plane.” (Bhag. [4.12.25-27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.25))

Dhruva Maharaja, whose body was now fully spiritualized, first worshiped the airplane, which was as huge as a house. Then as he prepared to enter the plane, death personified approached him. Not caring for death, Dhruva placed his feet on death’s head and boarded. “At that time drums and kettledrums resounded from the sky, the chief Gandharvas began to sing, and other demigods showered flowers like torrents of rain upon Dhruva Maharaja.” (Bhag. [4.12.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.31))

Prabhupada describes Dhruva Maharaja’s death: “Instead of death’s giving him trouble, Dhruva Maharaja took advantage of death’s presence and put his feet on the head of death. People with a poor fund of knowledge do not know the difference between the death of a devotee and the death of a nondevotee. In this connection, an example can be given: a cat carries its kittens in its mouth, and it also catches a rat in its mouth. Superficially, the catching of the rat and the kitten appear to be one and the same, but actually they are not. When the cat catches the rat in its mouth it means death for the rat, whereas when the cat catches the kitten, the kitten enjoys it. When Dhruva Maharaja boarded the airplane, he took advantage of the arrival of death personified, who came to offer him obeisances . . .” (Bhag. [4.12.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.30), purport)

In his purport to text 29 Srila Prabhupada describes the nature of the spiritual realm: “As Lord Visnu is worshipable, so also are His associates, His paraphernalia, His airplane and His abode, for everything of Visnu’s is as good as Lord Visnu. Dhruva Maharaja knew all this very well, as a pure Vaisnava, and he offered his respects to the associates and to the plane before riding in it. But in the meantime, his body changed into spiritual existence, and therefore it was illuminating like molten gold. In this way he also became one with the other paraphernalia of Visnuloka.”

“Dhruva was seated in the transcendental airplane, which was just about to start, when he remembered his poor mother, Suniti. He thought to himself, ‘How shall I go alone to the Vaikuntha planet and leave behind my poor mother?’” (Bhag. [4.12.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.32)) His mother was his siksa-guru, because she had directed him to Krsna in his childhood. The Lord’s associates then pointed, and Dhruva saw his mother also heading toward Vaikuntha in another plane.

Srila Prabhupada gives powerful instructions on diksa- and siksa-gurus in his purports to texts 32 and 33. From the purport to text 32:

**Dhruva had a feeling of obligation to his mother, Suniti. It was Suniti who had given him the clue which had now enabled him to be personally carried to the Vaikuntha planet by the associates of Lord Visnu. He now remembered her and wanted to take her with him. Actually, Dhruva Maharaja’s mother, Suniti, was his patha-pradarsaka-guru. Patha-pradarsaka-guru means “the guru, or the spiritual master, who shows the way.” Such a guru is sometimes called siksa-guru. Although Narada Muni was his diksa-guru (initiating spiritual master), Suniti, his mother, was the first who gave him instruction on how to achieve the favor of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. It is the duty of the siksa-guru or diksa-guru to instruct the disciple in the right way, and it depends on the disciple to execute the process. According to sastric injunctions, there is no difference between siksa-guru and diksa-guru, and generally the siksa-guru later on becomes the diksa-guru. Suniti, however, being a woman, and specifically his mother, could not become Dhruva Maharaja’s diksa-guru. Still, he was not less obliged to Suniti. There was no question of carrying Narada Muni to Vaikunthaloka, but Dhruva Maharaja thought of his mother.**

According to this purport, a disciple’s spiritual advancement remains his responsibility. It is obviously the guru’s duty to represent Krsna properly by instructing his students with clear Krsna consciousness, but as Srila Prabhupada indicates, it “depends on the disciple to execute the process.”

In his purport to text 33 Srila Prabhupada speaks further about the relationship between guru and disciple, and humbly comments on the power of a pure disciple:

**This incident proves that the siksa or diksa-guru who has a disciple who strongly executes devotional service like Dhruva Maharaja can be carried by the disciple even though the instructor is not as advanced. Although Suniti was an instructor to Dhruva Maharaja, she could not go to the forest because she was a woman, nor could she execute austerities and penances as Dhruva Maharaja did. Still, Dhruva Maharaja was able to take his mother with him. Similarly, Prahlada Maharaja also delivered his atheistic father, Hiranyakasipu. The conclusion is that a disciple or an offspring who is a very strong devotee can carry with him to Vaikunthaloka either his father, mother or siksd' or diksa-guru. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura used to say, “If I could perfectly deliver even one soul back home, back to Godhead, I would think my mission—propagating Krsna consciousness—to be successful.” The Krsna consciousness movement is spreading now all over the world, and sometimes I think that even though I am crippled in many ways, if one of my disciples becomes as strong as Dhruva Maharaja, then he will be able to carry me with him to Vaikunthaloka.**

In his purport to Bhagavatam [4.12.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.32), revealing the devotee’s mood of full dependence on and surrender to Krsna, Srila Prabhupada further describes how responsive the Lord is to His devotee’s desires: “Dhruva Maharaja had thought that he was going alone to Vaikunthaloka, leaving behind his mother, which was not very auspicious because people would criticize him for going alone to Vaikunthaloka and not carrying with him Suniti, who had given him so much. But Dhruva also considered that he was not personally the Supreme. Therefore, if Krsna fulfilled his desires, only then would it be possible. Krsna could immediately understand his mind, and He told Dhruva that his mother was also going with him. This incident proves that a pure devotee like Dhruva Maharaja can fulfill all his desires; by the grace of the Lord, he becomes exactly like the Lord, and thus whenever he thinks of anything, his wish is immediately fulfilled.”

“While Dhruva Maharaja was passing through space, he gradually saw all the planets of the solar system, and on the path he saw all the demigods in their airplanes showering flowers upon him like rain. Dhruva Maharaja thus surpassed the seven planetary systems of the great sages who are known as saptarsi. Beyond that region, he achieved the transcendental situation of permanent life in the planet where Lord Visnu lives.” (Bhag. [4.12.34-35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.34))

Texts 36 and 37 note the process that carries everyone to the spiritual world: “The self-effulgent Vaikuntha planets, by whose illumination alone all the illuminating planets within this material world give off reflected light, cannot be reached by those who are not merciful to other living entities. Only persons who constantly engage in welfare activities for other living entities can reach the Vaikuntha planets. Persons who are peaceful, equipoised, cleansed and purified, and who know the art of pleasing all other living entities, keep friendship only with devotees of the Lord; they alone can very easily achieve the perfection of going back home, back to Godhead.”

Persons bom in the iron age of Kali-yuga suffer physical and mental debilities and are overcome by countless desires. Quite naturally they tend to be absorbed in trying to solve their problems and fulfill their desires. The essential practices of spiritual life tend to be relegated to “later,” after problems are solved and needs met. Yet experience shows that our karmic reactions—the desires, the problems—don’t dissipate so quickly. Rather, we find ourselves further entangled in life’s complexities. In his purport to text 36, Prabhupada doesn’t directly address the perplexity of life in Kali-yuga; instead he stresses that devotees wishing to go back to Godhead, rather than solving their own distress, should spend their time helping others become spiritually fortunate: “From this material world . . . people can be transferred to the Vaikunthaloka, if they incessantly engage in welfare activities for all other living entities. Such incessant welfare activities can really be performed only in Krsna consciousness. There is no philanthropic work within this material world but Krsna consciousness that can engage a person twenty-four hours a day.”

And later in the same purport: “A Krsna conscious being is always engaged in planning how to take all of suffering humanity back home, back to Godhead. Even if one is not successful in reclaiming all the fallen souls back to Godhead, still, because he is Krsna conscious, his path to Vaikunthaloka is open. He personally becomes qualified to enter the Vaikunthalokas, and if anyone follows such a devotee, he also enters into Vaikunthaloka. . . . Vaisnavas, who are servants of the Lord, come forward in the actual field of work in Krsna consciousness to reclaim fallen souls. Only Krsna conscious persons are eligible to enter into the spiritual world. That is clearly stated in this verse and is confirmed in Bhagavad-gita, wherein the Lord says that there is no one dearer to Him than those who preach the gospel of Bhagavad-gita to the world.”

That distributing Krsna consciousness helps one’s own Krsna consciousness is noted both by Srila Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami in Caitanya-caritamrta, Adi [7.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/7.24), and by Srila Prabhupada in his purport to that text. Krsnadasa Kaviraja writes: “Although the members of the Panca-tattva plundered the storehouse of love of Godhead and ate and distributed its contents, there was no scarcity, for this wonderful storehouse is so complete that as the love is distributed, the supply increases hundreds of times.”

What is true for the storehouse is true for the individual, as Srila Prabhupada indicates in his purport: “A pseudo incarnation of Krsna once told his disciple that he had emptied himself by giving him all knowledge and was thus spiritually bankrupt. Such bluffers speak in this way to cheat the public, but actual spiritual consciousness is so perfect that the more it is distributed, the more it increases.”

In preaching, as in life, a devotee can remain always dependent on Krsna and thus find peace. In his purport to text 37 Srila Prabhupada describes the reason for a devotee’s peacefulness, a quality mentioned in that text as a prerequisite for attaining the spiritual world: “A devotee is peaceful because he is fully surrendered to the Supreme Personality of Godhead and thinks of himself as completely helpless; just as a child feels complete peace in depending on the parent, so a devotee is completely peaceful, for he depends on the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

## Texts 40-52: Narada Muni Glorifies Dhruva Maharaja

Narada Muni noted his disciple Dhruva’s exalted achievements and in three verses praised Dhruva in the sacrificial arena of Dhruva’s descendants, the Pracetas. Narada’s first verse glorifies Dhruva’s determined devotional austerities, which allowed him to achieve a result unachievable by “so-called Vedantists or strict followers of the Vedic principles, not to speak of ordinary human beings.” (Bhag. [4.12.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.41)) Narada then glorified Dhruva because at five years old, aggrieved by his stepmother’s harsh words, he performed austerities to satisfy the Lord. Finally, Narada glorified Dhruva because by Dhruva’s devotion he had defeated the unconquerable Lord.

In his purport to text 42 Prabhupada describes what it was about the Lord that made it possible for Dhruva Maharaja to conquer Him: “The Supreme Godhead is unconquerable; no one can conquer the Lord. But He voluntarily accepts subordination to the devotional qualities of His devotees. For example, Lord Krsna accepted subordination to the control of mother Yasoda because she was a great devotee. The Lord likes to be under the control of His devotees. In the Caitanya-caritamrta it is said that everyone comes before the Lord and offers Him exalted prayers, but the Lord does not feel as pleased when offered such prayers as He does when a devotee, out of pure love, chastises Him as a subordinate. The Lord forgets His exalted position and willingly submits to His pure devotee. . . . This unalloyed love for Krsna can be achieved simply by hearing about Krsna. Lord Caitanya accepted this principle—that if one in any position submissively hears the transcendental message spoken by Krsna or about Krsna, then gradually he develops the quality of unalloyed love, and by that love only he can conquer the unconquerable. . . . Arjuna also, by his devotional service, made Lord Krsna his chariot driver; he ordered the Lord, ‘Put my chariot here,’ and the Lord executed his order. These are some examples of how a devotee can acquire the exalted position of conquering the unconquerable.”

Narada’s third verse recounts how it took Dhruva only six months to conquer the unconquerable. This revealed Dhruva’s determination to do everything required to achieve the Lord’s darsana. Prabhupada presents Dhruva’s success as a lesson for his own followers: “The lesson from the life of Dhruva Maharaja is that if one likes, one can attain Vaikunthaloka in one life, without waiting for many other lives. My Guru Maharaja, Sri Srimad Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Gosvami Prabhupada, used to say that every one of his disciples could attain Vaikunthaloka in this life, without waiting for another life to execute devotional service. One simply has to become as serious and sincere as Dhruva; then it is quite possible to attain Vaikunthaloka and go back home, back to Godhead, in one life.” (Bhag. [4.12.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.43), purport)

After completing his narration of Dhruva Maharaja’s activities to Vidura, Maitreya offers powerful benedictions to those who have heard the pastime: “Anyone who hears the narration of Dhruva Maharaja, and who repeatedly tries with faith and devotion to understand his pure character, attains the pure devotional platform and executes pure devotional service. By such activities one can diminish the threefold miserable conditions of material life. Anyone who hears this narration of Dhruva Maharaja acquires exalted qualities like him. For anyone who desires greatness, prowess or influence, here is the process by which to acquire them, and for thoughtful men who want adoration, here is the proper means.” (Bhag. [4.12.46-47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.46))

Maitreya Muni next emphasizes the power of hearing about Dhruva Maharaja in the association of pure Vaisnavas, which parallels Srila Prabhupada’s description of the purpose of the Krsna consciousness movement. Srila Prabhupada writes: “The Krsna consciousness movement has been started especially to create qualified brahmanas to broadcast spiritual knowledge all over the world, for thus people may become very happy.” (Bhag. [4.12.48](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.48), purport)

The Srimad-Bhagavatam has tremendous potency. In his purport to text 49-50 Srila Prabhupada instructs us how to be sure we are connected to that power when we are hearing the Bhagavatam: “Only one who is completely surrendered at the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, depending fully on Him for personal maintenance or even for maintenance of his family, can attain perfection by recitation of Srimad-Bhagavatam, which is full of narrations of the pastimes of the Lord and His devotees. The process can be summarized as follows: The audience must be faithfully receptive to the Bhagavata message, and the reciter should completely depend on the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Bhagavata recitation must not be a business. If done in the right way, not only does the reciter achieve perfect satisfaction, but the Lord also is very satisfied with the reciter and the audience, and thus both are liberated from material bondage simply by the process of hearing.”

There is great need for the Bhagavatam in such an age as the present one. Therefore, in his purport to text 51, Prabhupada stresses the importance of preaching the Bhagavatam: “Materialists are very proud of their advancement in education, in philosophical speculation and in scientific knowledge, but no one actually knows what the Absolute Truth is. The great sage Maitreya, therefore, recommends that to enlighten people about the Absolute Truth (tattva), devotees should preach the teachings of Srimad-Bhagavatam throughout the entire world.”

Maitreya Muni continues to glorify the power of hearing about Dhruva Maharaja, for such hearing awards the desires cherished by karmis, jnanis, and yogis. But Maitreya encourages the practitioners of other paths to practice bhakti: “The narration of Dhruva Maharaja is sublime knowledge for the attainment of immortality. Persons unaware of the Absolute Truth can be led to the path of truth. Those who out of transcendental kindness take on the responsibility of becoming master-protectors of the poor living entities automatically gain the interest and blessings of the demigods.” (Bhag. [4.12.51](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.51))

Maitreya concludes his narration with the following words: “The transcendental activities of Dhruva Maharaja are well known all over the world, and they are very pure. In childhood Dhruva Maharaja rejected all kinds of toys and playthings, left the protection of his mother and seriously took shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Visnu. My dear Vidura, I therefore conclude this narration, for I have described to you all its details.” (Bhag. [4.12.52](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.52))

And Srila Prabhupada concludes this chapter’s purports with a further glorification of Dhruva Maharaja: “It is said by Canakya Pandita that life is certainly short for everyone, but if one acts properly, his reputation will remain for a generation. As the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Krsna, is everlastingly famous, so the reputation of Lord Krsna’s devotee is also everlasting. . . . Dhruva Maharaja’s leaving home at a tender age and taking shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead in the forest is a unique example in this world.”

## Dialogue Four - The Advent of Prthu Maharaja and His Maintenance of Earth

## Chapter 13 - Description of the Descendants of Dhruva Maharaja

## Texts 1-20: The Lord Appears as a Descendant of Dhruva Maharaja

At the end of the last chapter (Bhag. [4.12.41-43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/12.41)) Maitreya Muni repeats three verses spoken by Narada Muni in praise of Dhruva Maharaja. The Bhagavatam tells us that on hearing about Dhruva Maharaja, Vidura became “much enlightened in devotional emotion.” (Bhag. [4.13.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/13.1)) Fascinated by the topic, he inquires: “O greatly advanced devotee, who were the Pracetas? To which family did they belong? Whose sons were they, and where did they perform the great sacrifices? . . . My dear brahmana, how did Narada Muni glorify the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and what pastimes were described in that meeting? I am very eager to hear of them. Kindly explain fully about that glorification of the Lord.” (Bhag. [4.13.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/13.2), [5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/13.5))

Vidura’s unflagging eagerness to hear about Krsna and His devotees indicates the spiritual potency of krsna-katha when properly spoken and heard.

Srila Prabhupada notes this in his purport to text 1: “As evidenced in the topics between Vidura and Maitreya, the activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the devotees are so fascinating that neither the devotee who is describing them nor the devotee who is hearing is at all fatigued by the inquiries and answers. Transcendental subject matter is so nice that no one becomes tired of hearing or speaking. Others, who are not devotees, may think, ‘How can people devote so much time simply to talks of God?’ But devotees are never satisfied or satiated in hearing and speaking about the Supreme Personality of Godhead or about His devotees. The more they hear and talk, the more they become enthusiastic to hear. The chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra is simply the repetition of three words, Hare, Krsna and Rama, but still devotees can go on chanting this Hare Krsna mantra twenty-four hours a day without feeling fatigued.”

The inspiration of realized devotees who, due to absorption in hearing and chanting, have lost the taste for eating and sleeping, offers one a glimpse of the potency of full immersion in the spiritual atmosphere. For example, the six Gosvamis and their immediate followers were so absorbed in krsna-katha that they cast off material life as insignificant. Srila Prabhupada did the same in his inspiration to translate Srimad-Bhagavatam and spread Krsna consciousness throughout the world. One cannot imitate such great personalities, but their example points one to the happiness of transcending the material realm for eternal life in Vrndavana.

Maitreya next describes what happened after Dhruva renounced his kingdom and went to the forest. Dhruva’s son Utkala was a maha-bhagavata. Since birth, Utkala was fully satisfied and materially detached. He was equipoised because he could see that everything rested in the Supersoul and that the Supersoul was present in everyone’s heart. Thus Utkala saw nothing but the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He refused to reveal his devotional consciousness to others because he wanted to avoid all materialistic interactions and entanglements.

Thus he remained silent, as if foolish, blind, dumb, and deaf. “For this reason the ministers and all the elderly members of the family thought Utkala to be without intelligence and, in fact, mad. Thus his younger brother, named Vatsara, the son of Bhrami, was elevated to the royal throne, and he became king of the world.” (Bhag. [4.13.11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/13.11))

Maitreya Muni quickly describes Dhruva Maharaja’s descendants one after another, but when he describes the seventh and eighth generations after Dhruva, he provides more information, telling the story of Maharaja Ariga and his son, Vena. Bitterly disappointed with Vena’s character, Maitreya tells Vidura, King Ariga renounced his kingdom and went to the forest. Cruel Vena then reigned until struck down by the curse of great sages.

With Vena dead and leaving no heir, the kingdom fell into chaos. “On seeing this, the great sages took the right hand of Vena as a churning rod, and as a result of their churning, Lord Visnu in His partial representation made His advent as King Prthu, the original emperor of the world.” (Bhag. [4.13.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/13.20))

## Texts 21-49: King Vena, Maharaja Anga’s Irreligious Son

It was natural for Vidura to wonder how a gentle king like Ariga, who was both saintly and deeply respectful of brahminical culture, could father a cruel child. Vidura is shocked that Vena’s actions could have been so grievous that they drove his father from his home and later caused the naturally tolerant sages to curse and kill Vena. Through his deliberations and inquiries, Vidura inspires Maitreya Muni to recount the history.

Maitreya Muni begins with the description of a sacrifice Maharaja Ariga had performed, which although flawless in execution produced no result. The demigods did not appear, nor would they accept the sacrificial offerings.

In his purport to text 25 Srila Prabhupada notes that discrepancies in the performance of a sacrifice can cause a sacrifice to fail. Therefore, he writes, “In this age . . . the only practical yajna is sankirtana-yajna, or chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra twenty-four hours a day.” In his purport to text 27, Srila Prabhupada stresses why the sankirtana'yajna is alone recommended: “Even if the Hare Krsna mantra is not chanted properly, it still has so much potency that the chanter gains the effect.”

With the priests’ permission, Maharaja Ariga broke the silence required while performing a sacrifice to ask why the sacrifice had failed. The head priests responded: “O King, in this life we do not find any sinful activity, even within your mind, so you are not in the least offensive. But we can see that in your previous life you performed sinful activities due to which, in spite of your having all qualifications, you have no son.” (Bhag. [4.13.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/13.31)) The head priests suggested that the king stop performing the asvamedha sacrifice, for no demigods would appear and the sacrifice would end in failure. Then they said: You planned to first satisfy the demigods to evoke their presence. Then, with the demigods present, you planned to call the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Instead you should simply perform a sacrifice for the Supreme Lord’s pleasure. “If you pray at once to the Supreme Lord and ask for a son, and if you execute the sacrifice for that purpose, the enjoyer of the sacrifice, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, will fulfill your desire. When Hari, the supreme enjoyer of all sacrifices, is invited to fulfill your desire for a son, all the demigods will come with Him and take their shares in the sacrifice.” (Bhag. [4.13.32-33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/13.32))

Maharaja Anga then began a second sacrifice, this time intended to please only Lord Visnu and thus gain a son. The sacrifice began, and as soon as the first oblation was offered, the yajna'purusa appeared wearing a golden garland and dressed in white. “He was carrying a golden pot filled with rice boiled in milk.” (Bhag. 4.13.36) The King took permission from his priests, and after smelling the rice, offered a portion to his wife. Anga’s wife, whose father was death personified, soon became pregnant and bore a child, whom they named Vena.

The boy took on his grandfather’s inauspicious qualities and grew up as an irreligious person. Even as a child Vena displayed unabashed cruelty. “After fixing his bow and arrow, the cruel boy used to go to the forest and unnecessarily kill innocent deer, and as soon as he came all the people would cry, ‘Here comes cruel Vena! Here comes cruel Vena!’ The boy was so cruel that while playing with young boys of his age he would kill them very mercilessly, as if they were animals meant for slaughter.” (Bhag. [4.13.40-41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/13.40))

King Anga punished Vena in various ways in an attempt to reform his character, but he was unable to make him gentle. Aggrieved, he mused: “Persons who have no son are certainly fortunate. They must have worshiped the Lord in their previous lives so that they would not have to suffer the unbearable unhappiness caused by a bad son. A sinful son causes a person’s reputation to vanish. His irreligious activities at home cause irreligion and quarrel among everyone, and this creates only endless anxiety. Who, if he is considerate and intelligent, would desire such a worthless son? Such a son is nothing but a bond of illusion for the living entity, and he makes one’s home miserable.” (Bhag. [4.13.43-45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/13.43))

Maharaja Anga, however, came to recognize the fortune hidden in his misfortune: A bad son is better than a good son because a good son makes one attached to his home, whereas a bad son does not. When there is a bad son, home life is hellish and it is easy to become detached. In his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada appreciates Anga’s realization: “King Anga . . . considered his bad son his friend since he was helping him become detached from his home. Ultimately one has to learn how to detach oneself from attachment to material life; therefore, if a bad son, by his bad behavior, helps a householder to go away from home, it is a boon.”

And in his purport to text 37 Srila Prabhupada confirms that Vena’s birth was specifically the Supreme Lord’s mercy on Anga: “Since the King was very liberal, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in order to increase his detachment from this material world, willed that a cruel son be bom of the Queen so that the King would have to leave home. As stated above, Lord Visnu fulfills the desires of the karmis as they desire, but the Lord fulfills the desire of a devotee in a different way so that the devotee may gradually come to Him.”

Maharaja Anga is not unique in receiving the Lord’s mercy in the form of suffering. The prostitute Pingala’s wise words (Bhag. [11.8.37-39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-11/8.37)) demonstrate the mood that transforms suffering into disappointment, detachment, and then surrender: “Although I most stub bomly hoped to enjoy the material world, somehow or other detachment has arisen in my heart, and it is making me very happy. Therefore the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Visnu, must be pleased with me. Without even knowing it, I must have performed some activity satisfying to Him. A person who has developed detachment can give up the bondage of material society, friendship and love, and a person who undergoes great suffering gradually becomes, out of hopelessness, detached and indifferent to the material world. Thus, due to my great suffering, such detachment awoke in my heart; yet how could I have undergone such merciful suffering if I were actually unfortunate? Therefore, I am in fact fortunate and have received the mercy of the Lord. He must somehow or other be pleased with me. With devotion 1 accept the great benefit that the Lord has bestowed upon me. Having given up my sinful desires for ordinary sense gratification, 1 now take shelter of Him, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

King Anga could not sleep. Gradually he became indifferent to both family and kingdom. “Once, therefore, in the dead of night, he got up from bed and left Vena’s mother \[his wife\], who was sleeping deeply. He gave up all attraction for his greatly opulent kingdom, and, unseen by anyone, he very silently gave up his home and opulence and proceeded towards the forest.” (Bhag. [4.13.47](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/13.47)) Finding their king absent the next morning, the ministers, citizens, priests, and other friends became distraught. Who would rule in his stead? How would order be maintained? The citizens made a wide search, but they could not find Anga, and in sorrow, they returned to the city. All the country’s great sages assembled to help the citizens in the king’s absence. With tears in their eyes the citizens offered the sages their respectful obeisances and informed them that they were unable to find the king.

## Chapter 14 - The Story of King Vena

## Texts 1-35: The Sages Install Cruel Vena as King and Later Kill Him

Maitreya next tells Vidura that the sages, headed by Bhrgu, are always thinking of the welfare of the people. Srila Prabhupada explains the magnanimous spirit of sages: “In this verse the significant word is ksema-darsinah, which refers to those who are always looking after the welfare of the people in general. All the great sages headed by Bhrgu were always thinking of how to elevate all the people of the universe to the spiritual platform. Indeed, they advised the kings of every planet to rule the people with that ultimate goal of life in mind. The great sages used to advise the head of the state, or the king, and he used to rule the populace in accordance with their instruction.”

The sages upheld their duty to society but feared becoming entangled in the mode of passion should they rule directly. They therefore chose to advise the ruler rather than to personally govern the people. They understood that without a proper ruler to uphold the law, the citizens would become degraded; at worst they would become animalistic, and at best, act morally but without a higher purpose.

The sages’ goal in advising the king was to ensure that the ruler himself maintained a higher purpose and could thus govern his citizens with that purpose in mind. “In the absence of King Ariga there was no one to protect the interests of the people ...” (Bhag. [4.14.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.1)) To protect the people from becoming independent and unregulated, the sages installed Vena on the throne. The ministers, however, disagreed with this. They were too aware of Vena’s irreligious nature to consider him fit to rule. Still, “It was already known that Vena was very severe and cruel; therefore, as soon as all the thieves and rogues in the state heard of his ascendance to the royal throne, they became very much afraid of him. Indeed, they hid themselves here and there as rats hide themselves from snakes.” (Bhag. [4.14.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.3))

As soon as he ascended the throne, Vena became proud of his power. Considering himself great, he began to insult and even terrify others, including the powerful sages who had installed him as king. “When he became overly blind due to his opulences, King Vena mounted a chariot and, like an uncontrolled elephant, began to travel through the kingdom, causing the sky and earth to tremble wherever he went.” (Bhag. [4.14.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.5)) Thinking of himself as the supreme and only object of worship, Vena forbid the performance of religious rituals and stopped the brahmanas from performing sacrifices. He forbade the offering of charity as well as the sacrificial offerings of ghee, demanding that in the future everything be offered to him. The same sages who had enthroned him were now prohibited from performing sacrifices! They feared catastrophe. They felt compassion for Vena’s citizens, likening their position to ants in the middle of a log that was burning at both ends—on one side they had an inresponsible king, and on the other thieves and rogues. The sages were also afraid that they would be implicated by Vena’s atrocious behavior. After all, it was they who had enthroned him. They decided to try counseling him. Concealing their anger, which burned like fire due to Vena’s evil actions, they attempted to pacify King Vena with sweet words: Dear King, we have come to give you good advice. Please listen carefully. If you hear our words, your life span, opulence, strength, and reputation will all increase.

The sages then instructed Vena about a king’s duties, requesting him to avoid hampering his citizens’ spiritual advancement. “If their spiritual life is spoiled because of your activities, you will certainly fall down from your opulent and royal position. ... О noble one, if the king sees that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the original cause of the cosmic manifestation and the Supersoul within everyone, is worshiped, the Lord will be satisfied.” (Bhag. [4.14.16](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.16), [19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.19))

Srila Prabhupada points readers to their own happiness by encouraging them to do everything to satisfy Krsna: “People do not know that the ultimate goal of life is to approach Lord Visnu and satisfy Him. They have taken this materialistic way of life as everything and have become captivated by materialistic activities. Indeed, their leaders are always encouraging them to follow this path, and the general populace, being ignorant of the laws of God, are following their blind leaders down the path of unhappiness. In order to rectify this world situation, all people should be trained in Krsna consciousness and act in accordance with the varnasrama system. The state should also see that the people are engaged in satisfying the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is the primary duty of the state. The Krsna consciousness movement was started to convince the general populace to adopt the best process by which to satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead and thus solve all problems.” (Bhag. [4.14.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.20), purport)

Please remember, continued the sages, that the Supreme Personality of Godhead “is the enjoyer of the results of all sacrifices in all planets. The Supreme Lord is the sum total of the three Vedas, the owner of everything, and the ultimate goal of all austerity. Therefore your countrymen should engage in performing various sacrifices for your elevation. Indeed, you should always direct them towards the offering of sacrifices. ... О hero, do not stop the sacrificial performances. If you stop them, you will disrespect the demigods.” (Bhag. [4.14.21-22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.21))

Maharaja Vena’s reply was sharp: You are as inexperienced as small children. You are as foolish as an unchaste wife who, for a paramour, neglects the husband who maintains her. Why should anyone worship the demigods when I am present? “Those who, out of gross ignorance, do not worship the king, who is actually the Supreme Personality of Godhead, experience happiness neither in this world nor in the world after death.” (Bhag. [4.14.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.24)) Vena then accused the sages of envy, explaining that as king he was the greatest of living beings: All sacrifices should be offered to me. Why worship the demigods when they are simply manifestations of my body?

The illusion of mistaking himself for the Lord rather than the Lord’s servant overwhelmed Vena, and he lost sight of his true insignificance. How opposed to Krsna’s desire is such pride! Vena thought himself the center of existence. Srila Prabhupada writes: “There are many demons who think of themselves as the Supreme and present themselves as the directors of the sun, moon and other planets. This is all due to false pride. Similarly, King Vena developed the demonic mentality and presented himself as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Such demons are numerous in this age of Kali, and all of them are condemned by great sages and saintly persons.” (Bhag. [4.14.26-27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.26), purport)

In contrast to Vena’s mood stands the mentality Prabhupada ascribes to a true king: “The kings of all planets are especially meant for the protection of the inhabitants, and therefore the royal order should understand the science of Bhagavad-gita in order to be able to rule the citizens and protect them from material bondage to lust. Human life is meant for the cultivation of spiritual knowledge, in eternal relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and the executive heads of all states and all planets are obliged to impart this lesson to the citizens by education, culture and devotion. In other words, the executive heads of all states are intended to spread the science of Krsna consciousness so that the people may take advantage of this great science and pursue a successful path, utilizing the opportunity of the human form of life.” (Bg. [4.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/4.1), purport)

Although the sages spoke humbly, Vena was unwilling to hear their message. Brokenhearted but enraged, they heard his arrogant, insulting, and blasphemous words and condemned him: “Kill him! Kill him! He is the most dreadful, sinful person. If he lives, he will certainly turn the whole world into ashes in no time.... This impious, impudent man does not deserve to sit on the throne at all. He is so shameless that he even dared insult the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Visnu.” (Bhag. [4.14.31-32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.31)) The sages already considered Vena as good as dead because of his blasphemy; they manifested their covered anger and killed him with a powerful curse and no other weapon. Then they returned to their hermitages. Vena’s mother, Sunitha, grief-stricken, used herbs and mantras to embalm her son’s body.

## Texts 36-46: The Sages Churn Vena’s Body

Sometime later, those same sages bathed in the Sarasvati River and began to perform their daily duties by offering oblations into the sacrificial fires. Then, sitting on the river bank they began to talk about the Lord and His pastimes. Despite feeling the natural satisfaction that comes from engaging in sadhana, it was nevertheless clear to them that there was trouble in the kingdom.

The citizens were in danger and were beginning to panic. With neither king nor government, “the state was devoid of law and order, and consequently there was a great uprising of murderous thieves and rogues, who were plundering the riches of the people in general. Although the great sages could subdue the disturbance by their powers—just as they could kill the King—they considered it improper on their part to do so. Thus they did not attempt to stop the disturbance.” (Bhag. [4.14.39-40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.39)) Still, they felt obliged to correct the unfortunate situation.

Srila Prabhupada advises contemporary sages in his purport to text 37: “The conclusion is that even though saintly persons have no business in political affairs, they are always compassionate upon the people in general. Thus even though they are always aloof from society, out of mercy and compassion they consider how the citizens can peacefully execute their rituals and follow the rules and regulations of varnasrama-dharma. That was the concern of these sages. In this age of Kali, everything is disturbed. Therefore saintly persons should take to the chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra, as recommended in the sastras: harerndmaharernamaharernamaivakevalam, kalaunasty evanasty eva nasty eva gatir anyatha (Cc. Adi [17.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-adi/17.21)). Both for spiritual and material prosperity, everyone should devotedly chant the Hare Krsna mantra.”

The sages considered: We are renounced and fear entanglement in political affairs, but how can we watch the citizens suffer? Although brahmanas are peaceful and impartial, being equal to everyone, we should not neglect people who are suffering. “By such neglect, a brahmana’s spiritual power diminishes, just as water kept in a cracked pot leaks out.” (Bhag. [4.14.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.41)) The sages decided to correct the situation and reestablish Maharaja Anga’s dynasty. After all, the sages thought, the semen in Dhruva Maharaja’s dynasty is powerful, and Dhruva’s descendants are prone to serve the Lord. The saintly persons then churned the thighs of King Vena’s dead body “with great force and according to a specific method.” As a result, a dwarflike person was bom from King Vena’s body. His complexion was as black as a crow’s, his limbs short, and his jaw large. His nose was flat, his eyes reddish, and his hair copper-colored. The sages named him Bahuka, and knew him to be the extirpation of all Vena’s sins.

In his purport to text 43, Srila Prabhupada discusses how this sinful person was produced from King Vena’s dead body: “Although dead, the body of King Vena was preserved by drugs and mantras chanted by King Vena’s mother. In this way the ingredients for the production of another body were there. When the body of the person named Bahuka came out of the dead body of King Vena, it was really not very astonishing. It was simply a question of knowing how to do it. From the semen of one body, another body is produced, and the life symptoms are visible due to the soul’s taking shelter of this body. One should not think that it was impossible for another body to come out of the dead body of Maharaja Vena. This was performed by the skillful action of the sages.”

Bahuka was submissive and meek, and “immediately after his birth he bowed down and inquired, ‘Sirs, what shall I do?’ The great sages replied, ‘Please sit down \[nisida\].’ Thus Nisada, the father of the Naisada race, was born.” (Bhag. [4.14.45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/14.45)) Bahuka immediately took charge of the resultant actions of King Vena’s sinful activities and went to live in the distant hills and forests.

## Chapter 15 - King Prthu’s Appearance and Coronation

### Texts 1-26

The sages continued to chum Vena’s body, and soon a male and female couple appeared from his arms. The sages recognized the male as the Lord’s partial incarnation, an expansion of the Personality of Godhead, and named him Maharaja Prthu, considering him first among kings. The female was King Prthu’s queen and a partial incarnation of the goddess of fortune. She was named Arci.

One may wonder how an avatar a of Visnu could appear from sinful King Vena’s body. Srila Prabhupada writes: “The method adopted by the great sages and scholars, who were learned in Vedic knowledge, was perfect. They removed all the reactions of King Vena’s sinful activities by seeing that King Vena first gave birth to Bahuka, described in the previous chapter. After King Vena’s body was thus purified, a male and female came out of it, and the great sages could understand that this was an expansion of Lord Visnu.” (Bhag. [4.15.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/15.2), purport)

The sages were pleased to see Maharaja Prthu and his queen, and they immediately predicted their glorious activities. As if to confirm their words, “the best singers of Gandharvaloka chanted his glories. The inhabitants of Siddhaloka showered flowers, and the beautiful women in the heavenly planets danced in ecstasy. Conchshells, bugles, drums and kettledrums vibrated in outer space. Great sages, forefathers and personalities from the heavenly planets all came to earth from various planetary systems.” (Bhag. [4.15.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/15.7)) Lord Brahma himself arrived, and noting “the lines of Lord Visnu’s palm on King Prthu’s right hand and impressions of lotus flowers on the soles of his feet . . . could understand that King Prthu was a partial representation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [4.15.9-10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/15.9)) The learned brahmanas, who were attached to Vedic ritualistic ceremonies, began to prepare for the King’s coronation.

Maharaja Prthu was offered a throne, and both the King and his Queen were dressed in exquisite garments and ornaments as brilliant as fire. Demigods such as Kuvera, Varuna, Vayu, Dharma, Indra, and Yamaraja made valuable presentations to increase the King’s wealth, power, and prestige. Lord Brahma presented him with a protective garment made of spiritual knowledge. Sarasvati, Lord Brahma’s wife, gave him a transcendental necklace. Lord Visnu gave him a Sudarsana disc, and the goddess of fortune gave him undying wealth. Lord Siva presented him with a sword in a sheath marked with ten moons, and Durgadevi presented him with a shield marked with one hundred moons. The moon-god presented him with horses made of nectar, and Visvakarma presented him with a very beautiful chariot.

Agni, the sun-god, and the predominating deity of Bhurloka offered presentations, and demigods from outer space showered offerings of flowers again and again. The seas, mountains, and rivers presented him with space to drive his chariot without impediment, and professional reciters—a siita, a magadha, and a vandi—offered prayers and praises. As these reciters sang of the King’s future glories, however, he gently asked them to stop: О gentle reciters, please offer your prayers when the qualities of which you speak have appeared in me. “The gentle who offer prayers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead do not attribute such qualities to a human being, who does not actually have them.” (Bhag. [4.15.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/15.23)) In this way Prthu Maharaja cautioned everyone not to cheaply accept an ordinary jiva as the Personality of Godhead, and he also exhibited his humility, showing that “a person who is very famous and powerful does not like to hear himself praised.” (Bhag. [4.15.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/15.25))

King Prthu said: How could an intelligent man allow his followers to praise him for qualities he does not yet possess? To praise a man by saying that if he were educated he might have become a great scholar is insulting. A foolish person who agrees to accept such praise does not recognize the insult. I have done nothing praiseworthy. If I were to accept such praise, it would be like taking seriously praise spoken by a child.

## Chapter 16 - King Prthu Praised by the Professional Reciters

### Texts 1-27

Prthu Maharaja’s nectarean words gave pleasure to those who heard them, but despite his request that his future glories remain unspoken, the reciters, encouraged by the sages, neglected the King’s order and honored him with praise.

Srila Prabhupada explains their inspiration: “Although the King denied such praise because he was not at that time exhibiting his godly qualities, the reciters did not stop praising him. Rather, they were very pleased with the King, who, although actually an incarnation of God, was so humble and delightful in his dealings with devotees. . . . The King’s behavior was very pleasing to the reciters, and consequently the reciters continued their praise and even foretold the King’s future activities, as they had been instructed by the sadhus and sages.” (Bhag. [4.16.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/16.1), purport)

But the reciters felt unqualified to properly express the King’s glories. Although they feared that their words would be insufficient and would in fact minimize him, still they continued, knowing that they would be purified by the attempt. Srila Prabhupada writes: “By glorifying the Lord with exalted verses, one becomes purified. Although we are unable to offer prayers to the Lord in an adequate fashion, our duty is to make the attempt in order to purify ourselves. It is not that we should stop our glorification because demigods like Lord Brahma and Lord Siva cannot adequately glorify the Lord. Rather, as stated by Prahlada Maharaja, everyone should glorify the Lord according to his own ability. If we are serious and sincere devotees, the Lord will give us the intelligence to offer prayers properly.” (Bhag. [4.16.2](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/16.2), purport)

The reciters discovered that their attempt to glorify Prthu Maharaja, lacking as it may have been, filled them with bliss. In his purport to text 3 Srila Prabhupada carries the concept of speaking the Lord’s glories into the realm of preaching: “However expert one may be, he can never describe the glories of the Lord adequately. Nonetheless, those engaged in glorifying the activities of the Lord should try to do so as far as possible. Such an attempt will please the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Lord Caitanya has advised all His followers to go everywhere and preach the message of Lord Krsna. Since this message is essentially Bhagavad-gita, the preacher’s duty is to study Bhagavad-gita as it is understood by disciplic succession and explained by great sages and learned devotees. One should speak to the general populace in accordance with one’s predecessors—sadhu, guru and sastras. This simple process is the easiest method by which one can glorify the Lord. Devotional service, however, is the real method, for by devotional service one can satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead with just a few words. Without devotional service, volumes of books cannot satisfy the Lord. Even though preachers of the Krsna consciousness movement may be unable to describe the glories of the Lord, they can nonetheless go everywhere and request people to chant Hare Krsna.”

The reciters adored Prthu Maharaja: “This King alone, in his own body, will be able in due course of time to maintain all living entities and keep them in a pleasant condition by manifesting himself as different demigods to perform various departmental activities.” (Bhag. [4.16.5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/16.5)) Prthu Maharaja, they foretold, will be as powerful as the sun in reclaiming land and making it fertile. He will care for the comforts of his citizens, even at the cost of his own convenience, and he will supply the rain that protects his citizens from drought. His affectionate glances will enhance people’s lives. He will govern with the unfathomable gravity of an expert diplomat, yet when required, will act like fire in repulsing his enemies. He will be aware of everything that occurs in his kingdom, but will remain neutral in his dealings. To all—be they son or enemy—he will be fair and equal. Prthu Maharaja’s influence will expand unchecked throughout his kingdom, and the citizens will be satisfied with him as their king. He will be a determined, truthful lover of brahminical culture, and he will respect every woman as if she were his own mother, while treating each citizen as his son.

Prthu Maharaja will associate intimately with liberated persons and will consider all embodied living entities dear to him. He is an empowered incarnation, a saktyavesa-avatara, and sees the material world in a different way than the conditioned souls see it. He will be uniquely powerful and heroic, and all other kings will offer him respect and also sing his glories.

“This King, this protector of the citizens, is an extraordinary king and is equal to the Prajapati demigods. For the living facility of all citizens, he will milk the earth, which is like a cow. Not only that, but he will level the surface of the earth with the pointed ends of his bow, breaking all the hills exactly as King Indra, the heavenly King, breaks mountains with his powerful thunderbolt.” (Bhag. [4.16.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/16.22)) Prthu Maharaja will travel through the kingdom, and rogues and thieves will hide. He will attempt to perform one hundred asvamedha'yajnas at the source of the Sarasvati River, but Indradeva will stop the one hundredth sacrifice by stealing the sacrificial horse. In addition, Prthu Maharaja will meet Sanat-kumara and accept instructions from the great boy-sage. No one will disobey Prthu Maharaja’s orders, and everyone, both suras and asuras, will glorify his activities. He will uproot the miseries of his citizens.

In his purport to text 27, Srila Prabhupada describes the qualifications required if one is to rule the world: “Persons or nations anxious to spread their influence all over the world should consider this point. If one is able to eradicate completely the threefold miseries of the citizens, he should aspire to rule the world. One should not aspire to rule for any political or diplomatic consideration.”

Srila Prabhupada presents an additional prediction in his purport to Bhagavatam [2.7.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-2/7.9): “In the Vamana Purana the history of Maharaja Vena and his degradation are fully described. When Maharaja Prthu heard about the hellish condition of his father, Vena, who was suffering from leprosy in the family of a mleccha, he at once brought the former king to Kuruksetra for his purification and relieved him of all sufferings.”

## Chapter 17 - Maharaja Prthu Becomes Angry at the Earth

## Texts 1-7: Vidura Questions Maitreya Muni about Prthu Maharaja

When the professional reciters finished speaking, the King worshiped and rewarded them. He then satisfied and offered his respects to the leaders of the brahmanas and other castes, his servants, ministers, and to the priests, citizens, his countrymen, people from other communities, his admirers, and others. Everyone became pleased at heart. After hearing of Prthu Maharaja’s birth and future qualities and activities, Vidura asked Maitreya five questions: (1) Why did the earth take the shape of a cow? (2) When Maharaja Prthu milked her, who became the earth’s calf? What was used as the milking pot? (3) How did Maharaja Prthu level the surface of the earth? (4) Why did Indra, king of heaven, steal the horse meant for Prthu Maharaja’s one hundredth horse sacrifice? (5) After receiving instructions from Sanat-kumara, the greatest Vedic scholar, how did Maharaja Prthu apply that knowledge and attain his desired destination?

## Texts 8-17: The Earth in the Form of a Cotv Fearfully Surrenders to Prthu Maharaja

Maitreya Muni begins his reply by narrating the story of Prthu Maharaja’s milking the earth in the form of a cow, because this naturally answers the questions, Who became the calf? and, What kind of pot was used to contain the milk? Maitreya Muni continues: “My dear Vidura, at the time King Prthu was enthroned by the great sages and brahmanas and declared to be the protector of the citizens, there was a scarcity of food grains. The citizens actually became skinny due to starvation. Therefore they came before the King and informed him of their real situation. Dear King, just as a tree with a fire burning in the hollow of the trunk gradually dries up, we are drying up due to the fire of hunger in our stomachs. You are the protector of surrendered souls, and you have been appointed to give employment to us. Therefore we have all come to you for protection. You are not only a king, but the incarnation of God as well. Indeed, you are the king of all kings. You can give us all kinds of occupational engage' ments, for you are the master of our livelihood. Therefore, О king of all kings, please arrange to satisfy our hunger by the proper distribution of food grains. Please take care of us, lest we soon die for want of food.” (Bhag. [4.17.9-11](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/17.9))

The head of a state naturally assumes both material and spiritual responsibility for the citizens. He is bound to guide them in the development of proper values, ethics, prescribed duties, and spiritual advancement. Because the Bhagavad-gita teaches these processes in a practical fashion, Krsna directed the disciplic succession, which carries the teachings of the Bhagavad-gita, through a line of saintly kings.
