О Lord, may Your millions of transcendental qualities dance on those tongues. What is the use of a soul that does not have millions of bodies? What is the use of a body that does not have millions of mouths? What is the use of a mouth that does not have millions of tongues? What is the use of a tongue that does not chant Your millions of names? О Lord, may I perpetually have hundreds of bodies and may each body have thousands of mouths. May each mouth have millions of tongues, and may each tongue chant millions of Your Holy Names. О Madhava, wherever and whenever anyone chants Your names and pastimes at any time, there may I with millions of ears eternally drink Your nectar. May I have millions of ears and millions upon millions of tongues. Then, О Lord, I will eternally and happily hear and chant Your pastimes. May I have millions of ears, millions of eyes, millions of hearts and minds, and millions of tongues. Hearing about, seeing, and embracing the ocean of Your handsomeness, I will drink its sweetness. May I have millions of eyes, ears, noses, tongues, and chests so that I may continually taste the nectar of Your handsomeness, Your sweet sounds, Your sweet fragrance, and Your embrace. May I have millions of feet to go to Your side. May I have millions of hands to serve You. May 1 have millions of intelligences to teach that service. О Lord, please grant me these boons.**

In his purport to text 24, Srila Prabhupada emphasizes the sweet (and essential) activity of hearing about Krsna from pure devotees (and not from Mayavadis): “Maharaja Prthu wanted to have a million ears to hear the glories of the lotus feet of the Lord. He specifically mentioned that the glories of the Lord should emanate from the mouths of pure devotees, who speak from the cores of their hearts. It is stated in the beginning of Srimad-Bhagavatam ([1.1.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/1.3)), suka-mukhad amrta-drava-samyutam: the nectar of Srimad-Bhagavatam became more relishable because it emanated from the mouth of Srila Sukadeva Gosvami. One might think that these glories of the Lord can be heard from anywhere, from the mouths of either devotees or nondevotees, but here it is specifically mentioned that the glories of the Lord must emanate from the mouths of pure devotees. Sri Sanatana Gosvami has strictly prohibited hearing from the mouth of a nondevotee. There are many professional reciters of Srimad-Bhagavatam who speak the narrations very ornamentally, but a pure devotee does not like to hear from them because such glorification of the Lord is simply a vibration of material sound. But when heard from the mouth of a pure devotee, glorification of the Lord is immediately effective.... Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu said that if anyone hears from a Mayavadi philosopher preaching about the activities of the Lord, even if it is a description from the Vedic literature, he is ultimately doomed. By hearing such Mayavada philosophy one cannot come to the destination of spiritual perfection of life.”

Prthu Maharaja continued: “My dear Lord, You are glorified by the selected verses uttered by great personalities. Such glorification of Your lotus feet is just like saffron particles. When the transcendental vibration from the mouths of great devotees carries the aroma of the saffron dust of Your lotus feet, the forgetful living entity gradually remembers his eternal relationship with You. Devotees thus gradually come to the right conclusion about the value of life. My dear Lord, I therefore do not need any other benediction but the opportunity to hear from the mouth of Your pure devotee.” (Bhag. [4.20.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/20.25))

In his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada again explains the potency of hearing about Krsna from a pure devotee: “The transcendental vibration from the mouth of a pure devotee is so powerful that it can revive the living entity’s memory of his eternal relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In our material existence, under the influence of illusory maya, we have almost forgotten our eternal relationship with the Lord, exactly like a man sleeping very deeply who forgets his duties. In the Vedas it is said that every one of us is sleeping under the influence of maya. We must get up from this slumber and engage in the right service, for thus we can properly utilize the facility of this human form of life. As expressed in a song by Thakura Bhaktivinoda, Lord Caitanya says, jivajaga, jivajaga. The Lord asks every sleeping living entity to get up and engage in devotional service so that his mission in this human form of life may be fulfilled. This awakening voice comes through the mouth of a pure devotee.”

What is the source of this “awakening” potency in a pure devotee’s voice? Srila Prabhupada continues: “A pure devotee always engages in the service of the Lord, taking shelter of His lotus feet, and therefore he has a direct connection with the saffron mercy-particles that are strewn over the lotus feet of the Lord. Although when a pure devotee speaks the articulation of his voice may resemble the sound of this material sky, the voice is spiritually very powerful because it touches the particles of saffron dust on the lotus feet of the Lord. As soon as a sleeping living entity hears the powerful voice emanating from the mouth of a pure devotee, he immediately remembers his eternal relationship with the Lord, although up until that moment he had forgotten everything.”

What is the result of such hearing? “The process of hearing from a pure devotee is recommended in all Vedic scriptures, especially by Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu. One may stay in his position of life—it does not matter what it is—but if one hears from the mouth of a pure devotee, he gradually comes to the understanding of his relationship with the Lord and thus engages in His loving service, and his life becomes completely perfect. Therefore, this process of hearing from the mouth of a pure devotee is very important for making progress in the line of spiritual understanding.”

Prthu Maharaja further praised hearing the Lord’s glories: If one even once hears the glories of the Lord in the association of devotees, one cannot give up that association. Even Laksmidevi, the goddess of fortune, desires to hear of the Lord’s unlimited activities and transcendental glories. But, Prthu wondered, what if hearing about Krsna gives birth to such desires for service that I begin to compete with the goddess of fortune for the privilege of serving the Lord’s lotus feet? Despite Laksmidevi’s superior position, power, and opulence, King Prthu said, I nevertheless aspire to serve Your feet. And if Laksmidevi and I quarrel, my dear Lord, “I am hopeful that... You will take my part, for You are very much inclined to the poor and You always magnify even insignificant service unto You. Therefore even though she becomes angry, I think that there is no harm for You, because You are so self-sufficient that You can do without her.” (Bhag. [4.20.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/20.28))

Srila Prabhupada writes in his purport to this text: “The goddess of fortune is called cancala (‘restless’) because she is very restless and is always coming and going. So Prthu Maharaja indicated that even though she might go away out of anger \[if the Lord grants him the service of His lotus feet over Srimati Laksmidevi’s claim\] there would be no harm for Lord Visnu, because He is self-sufficient and can do anything and everything without the help of Laksmiji.”

In Priti-sandarbha, anuccheda 175, Srila Jiva Gosvami clarifies the difference between Prthu Maharaja’s relationship with the Lord and that of Laksmidevi: Maharaja Prthu desires to serve the Lord in dasya-rasa, not in srngara-rasa, which is the mood of Goddess Laksmi. This is clear when one examines the examples Prthu offers as the types of services he would like to render, for these services are clearly in dasya-rasa. Thus his apparent rivalry with Goddess Laksmi is not actually inappropriate. Sri Jiva adds that others say that Maharaja Prthu’s words show only his great love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is merciful to the poor and fallen, and do not show any true feelings of rivalry with Goddess Laksmi.

Prthu Maharaja’s words do show great appreciation for the Lord’s mercy, however, as he presents the Lord as more merciful to His devotee than His mercy even to Goddess Laksmi. Sri Jiva then offers Prahlada Maharaja’s words in Bhagavatam [8.23.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-8/23.6) and [7.9.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/9.26) to confirm the point: “O Supreme Personality of Godhead, You are universally worshiped; even Lord Brahma and Lord Siva worship Your lotus feet. Yet although You are such a great personality, You have kindly promised to protect us, the demons. I think that such kindness has never been achieved even by Lord Brahma, Lord Siva or the goddess of fortune, Laksmi, what to speak of other demigods or common people.” (Bhag. [8.23.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-8/23.6)) And, “O my Lord, О Supreme, because I was bom in a family full of the hellish material qualities of passion and ignorance, what is my position? And what is to be said of your causeless mercy, which was never offered even to Lord Brahma, Lord Siva, or the goddess of fortune, Laksmi? You never put Your lotus hand upon their heads, but You have put it upon mine.” (Bhag. [7.9.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/9.26))

It is not astounding that Prthu Maharaja aspires to serve the Lord’s lotus feet. Even liberated saints desire full absorption in such service, because practically speaking, offering service is natural to all living entities; it is an activity that transcends liberation. Prthu Maharaja therefore said: “Great saintly persons who are always liberated take to Your devotional service because only by devotional service can one be relieved from the illusions of material existence. О my Lord, there is no reason for the liberated souls to take shelter at Your lotus feet except that such souls are constantly thinking of Your feet.” (Bhag. [4.20.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/20.29))

Srila Prabhupada expresses Prthu Maharaja’s conclusion in his purport to this text: “Prthu Maharaja therefore concluded that he would simply hear of the glories of the Lord constantly and thus engage his mind upon the lotus feet of the Lord. That is the highest perfection of life.”

In his commentary on text 29, Srila Sridhara Svami explains that the text shows that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is kind and affectionate to the poor and fallen, and that the devotees (sadhavah) who have no material desires and who worship (bhajanti) and attain Him are those who have turned away from impersonal speculation. That Lord is characterized by freedom from all the bewildering material activities inspired by the modes of material nature. The devotees worship Him because, as the verse explains, they think about nothing but His lotus feet (bhavat-padanusmaranad rte satam).

After having stated the superiority of bhakti over liberation, Prthu Maharaja next expresses his greatest fear: If he were to accept a material benediction from the Lord, he might have to become entangled in the complexities of this world. Thus Prthu considers even the lofty benedictions offered in the Vedas unsuitable for him and again prays for the opportunity to perform surrendered devotional service.

Earlier in this chapter Lord Visnu instructed Prthu Maharaja how to use karma and jnana to serve his bhakti. Now Prthu expresses his attraction to bhakti—to hearing and chanting about the Lord in the association of devotees—and denounces liberation and sense enjoyment, the false fruits of the jnana- and karrna-margas. Later, in his guiding words for his citizens in Chapter Twenty-one, Prthu Maharaja expands on Lord Visnu’s instructions on how to convert karma (the performance of prescribed duties) into bhakti. Still later, in Chapter Twenty-two, Sanat-kumara will further illuminate the Lord’s instructions on carrying jnana to its perfection by leading the soul to bhakti.

Prthu Maharaja concluded: Please, therefore, “do not ask me to take some material benefits from You, but as a father, not waiting for the son’s demand, does everything for the benefit of the son, please bestow upon me whatever You think best for me.” (Bhag. [4.20.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/20.31)) Thus Prthu Maharaja fully surrendered, placing himself at the Lord’s lotus feet.Srila Prabhupada expands on Prthu Maharaja’s reply in his purport to text 31:

**Prthu Maharaja therefore tells the Lord that, as the supreme fathser, He may elect to bestow whatever He considers beneficial for Prthu Maharaja. That is the perfect position of the living entity. Therefore Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu teaches us in His Siksastaka: na dhanam na janam na sundarim kavitam va jagad-isa kdmaye, mama janmani janmanisvare bhavatad bhaktir ahaitukl tvayi (Siksastaka 4): О Almighty Lord! I have no desire to accumulate wealth, nor have I any desire to enjoy beautiful women, nor do I want any number of followers. I only want Your causeless devotional service in my life, birth after birth.**

**The conclusion is that the pure devotee should not aspire after any material benefit from devotional service, nor should he be enamored by fruitive activities or philosophical speculation. He should always be engaged favorably in the service of the Lord. That is the highest perfection of life.**

## Texts 32-38: The Lord Responds to Prthu Maharaja’s Prayers

The Lord’s inspiring words confirmed that He would award the King his desired benediction: “My dear King, may you always be blessed by engaging in My devotional service. Only by such purity of purpose, as you yourself very intelligently express, can one cross over the insurmountable illusory energy of maya.” (Bhag. [4.20.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/20.32))

The purity of purpose to which the Lord refers is one-pointed attention on devotional service. Srila Prabhupada writes: “If one wants to cross over the ocean of material existence, there is no alternative than to take to devotional service. A devotee, therefore, should not care for any material position, whether in heaven or in hell. A pure devotee should always engage in the service of the Lord, for that is his real occupation. Simply by sticking to that position, one can overcome the stringent laws of material nature.” (Bhag. [4.20.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/20.32), purport)

The Lord then requested Prthu Maharaja to accept the essence of religious activity—to please Him by following His instructions: “My dear King, О protector of the citizens, henceforward be very careful to execute My orders and not be misled by anything. Anyone who lives in that way, simply carrying out My orders faithfully, will always find good fortune all over the world.” (Bhag. [4.20.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/20.33)) Prthu Maharaja thus received both the Lord’s blessings and His instructions. He then worshiped the Lord and then the demigods, as well as all others present. Everyone was satisfied by Prthu Maharaja’s pleasing words and generous gifts. Then the Supreme Personality of Godhead, having captivated the minds of the King and the priests, returned to the spiritual sky. King Prthu offered his obeisances to the Supreme Lord, who although not an object of material vision, had revealed Himself to Maharaja Prthu.

## Chapter 21 - Instructions by Prthu Maharaja

## Texts 1-13: Prthu Maharaja Prepares to Perform a Sacrifice

Prthu Maharaja then entered his city, which was “beautifully decorated to receive him with pearls, flower garlands, beautiful cloth and golden gates, and the entire city was perfumed with highly fragrant incense. Fragrant water distilled from sandalwood and aguru herb was sprinkled everywhere on the lanes, roads and small parks throughout the city, and everywhere were decorations of unbroken fruits, flowers, wetted grains, varied minerals, and lamps, all presented as auspicious paraphernalia. At the street crossings there were bunches of fruits and flowers, as well as pillars of banana trees and betel nut branches. All these combined decorations everywhere looked very attractive. . . . When the King entered the palace, conchshells and kettledrums were sounded, priests chanted Vedic mantras, and professional reciters offered different prayers. But in spite of all this ceremony to welcome him, the King was not the least bit affected.” (Bhag. [4.21.1-3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.1), [5](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.5))

That Prthu Maharaja “was not the least bit affected” indicates that he remained humble despite the opulent worship he received at the hands of his citizens. In his purport to text 5, Srila Prabhupada draws our attention to Prthu Maharaja’s character: “The reception given to the King was full of opulence, yet he did not become proud. It is said, therefore, that great personalities of power and opulence never become proud, and the example is given that a tree which is full of fruits and flowers does not stand erect in pride but instead bends downwards to show submissiveness. This is a sign of the wonderful character of great personalities.”

Prthu Maharaja ruled for years, responsibly, according to the Lord’s instructions. He was especially attentive to ensure that he and his citizens performed sacrifices to please the Lord and that each citizen was well fed and working according to his prescribed duty. Srila Prabhupada lectured on these aspects of a king’s duty: “Formerly the king used to see whether a brahmana is acting like a brahmana. Otherwise he will be stopped. Then he will be designated as he is working. This was the duty of the king to see that everyone is employed according to his profession. It was the duty of the king. Everyone must be employed: a brahmana must be working like a brahmana, a ksatriya must be working like a ksatriya.” (Lecture on Bg. [1.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/1.20), London, July 17, 1973)

Listening to Maitreya Muni speak of Prthu Maharaja’s glories inspires Vidura to inquire further. He asks: Prthu Maharaja performed such great activities and was so magnanimous in his rule that all other kings, and even the demigods, still follow in his footsteps. Who wouldn’t be interested in hearing more about him? Please tell me more of his glories, because his activities are so pious and auspicious.

In his purport to text 10 Srila Prabhupada notes the importance of hearing about Prthu Maharaja: “Saint Vidura’s purpose in hearing about Prthu Maharaja over and over again was to set an example for ordinary kings and executive heads, who should all be inclined to hear repeatedly about Prthu Maharaja’s activities in order to also be able to rule over their kingdoms or states very faithfully for the peace and prosperity of the people in general. Unfortunately, at the present moment no one cares to hear about Prthu Maharaja or to follow in his footsteps; therefore no nation in the world is either happy or progressive in spiritual understanding, although that is the sole aim and objective of human life.”

Saintly Maitreya responds: “My dear Vidura, King Prthu lived in the tract of land between the two great rivers Ganges and Yamuna. Because he was very opulent, it appeared that he was enjoying his destined fortune in order to diminish the results of his past pious activities. Maharaja Prthu was an unrivaled king and possessed the scepter for ruling all the seven islands on the surface of the globe. No one could disobey his irrevocable orders but the saintly persons, the brahmanas and the descendants of the Supreme Personality of Godhead \[the Vaisnavas\].” (Bhag. [4.21.11-12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.11))

Text 12 states that although Prthu Maharaja’s order was supreme in his kingdom, the saintly persons, the brahmanas and Vaisnavas were so pure that they were allowed to remain independent. In Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 247, Srila Jiva Gosvami delineates the qualities of worshipable, advanced Vaisnavas, offering evidence from the Garuda Purana, where the Lord lists His pure devotees’ qualities. They (1) have love for My devotees, (2) are pleased to worship Me, (3) take pleasure in hearing My glories, (4) manifest a choked voice, tears in the eyes, and other symptoms of ecstatic love after hearing My glories, (5) dance in ecstatic love for Me, (6) are free of false ego, (7) personally worship Me, and (8) do not worship Me professionally, as a means of livelihood. The Garuda Purana considers these eight traits symptoms that one is practicing pure devotional service. If these traits are manifest in someone—even in one bom in a mleccha family—one should accept that person as the king of brahmanas, the best of sages, wise, and truly learned. Gifts should be given to such a person, and one should accept whatever that person offers. As one worships Lord Hari, so one should worship such a pure devotee.

Sri Jiva then offers support for this point from Srila Sanatana Gosvami’s Hari-bhakti-vilasa ([10.127](https://vedarama.com/en/books/hbv/10.127)): “\[Lord Krsna said:\] Even though a person is a very learned scholar of the Sanskrit Vedic literature, he is not accepted as My devotee unless he is pure in devotional service. Even though a person is bom in a family of dog-eaters, he is very dear to Me if he is a pure devotee who has no motive to enjoy fruitive activities or mental speculation. Indeed, all respects should be given to him, and whatever he offers should be accepted. Such devotees are as worshipable as I am.” (quoted in Cc. Madhya [19.50](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.50))

## Texts 14-26: Prthu Maharaja Instructs His Citizens

**Part One: Perform Your Duties According to Varnasrama**

Once while beginning another sacrifice, one in which Brahma and other demigods, sages, and saintly kings assembled to participate, Prthu Maharaja worshiped his exalted guests. Standing in their midst he appeared like the full moon rising among the stars. Prthu Maharaja’s body was beautiful and strong. His teeth were beautifully set in his smiling face. Preparing for the sacrifice, he donned a black deerskin and wore a ring of kusa grass on his finger. He was initiated as the performer of the sacrifice and then spoke to his citizens, glancing as he spoke over the members of the assembly. His beautiful eyes seemed like stars in the sky or as if they were wet with dew. He spoke beautifully, yet his words were grave and certain, full of his realization of the Absolute Truth He first greeted everyone present. Then humbly and honestly he explained that he had received the king’s scepter by the Supreme Lord’s grace.

He said: As king, my duty is to rule and protect my subjects from danger as well as to ensure that they act according to their social position under the varnasrama system. Even my actions are prescribed, and Krsna is pleased when I do my duty. Doing so guarantees my future fortune. “Any king who does not teach his citizens about their respective duties in terms of varna and asrama but who simply exacts tolls and taxes from them is liable to suffer for the impious activities which have been performed by the citizens. In addition to such degradation, the king also loses his own fortune.... Therefore, my dear citizens, for the welfare of your king after his death, you should execute your duties properly in terms of your positions of varna and asrama and should always think of the Supreme Personality of Godhead within your hearts. By doing so, you will protect your own interests, and you will bestow mercy upon your king for his welfare after death. I request all the pure-hearted demigods, forefathers and saintly persons to support my proposal, for after death the result of an action is equally shared by its doer, its director and its supporter.” (Bhag. [4.21.24-26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.24))

Lord Visnu had already instructed Prthu Maharaja (Bhag. [4.20.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/20.9)) that one who worships Krsna through his occupational duty, without desiring material gain, becomes fully satisfied. Now Prthu Maharaja passed that instruction on to his subjects. Because his citizens felt such deep affection for him, they did not want him to suffer due to their misdeeds. Lord Visnu had predicted that Prthu Maharaja’s citizens would love him if he executed his prescribed duty properly (Bhag. [4.20.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/20.15)), and their affection proved an additional impetus for them to perform their occupational duties with care.

## Texts 27-33: Prthu Maharaja Instructs His Citizens

**Part Two: Perform Prescribed Duties for Lord Visnu’s Pleasure**

Prthu Maharaja next explained a basic principle of the Vedic system: Sastra teaches that there is a supreme authority who, according to our past actions, awards us either pleasure or misery, fortune or misfortune. There is no other way to coherently explain why some individuals are bom fortunate and others unfortunate.

In his purport to text 27, Srila Prabhupada criticizes the atheistic idea that the world functions without the benefit of a supreme authority: “Prthu Maharaja suggested that theistic men will solidly reject the views of the atheists on the grounds that there cannot be many varieties of existence without the plan of a superior intelligence.”

Prthu Maharaja continued: A supreme authority, one who bestows benedictions, must exist. The Vedas confirm God’s existence, and the Vedic conclusion is supported by many great souls. Therefore we too should accept God’s existence.

The idea that everything came about by chance is not a reasonable alternative to theism. Common sense dictates that order left to chance would result in chaos. By definition, order is “ordered,” not a chance combination or interaction of elements. Srila Prabhupada explains the theory of “chance” in a unique way in his purport to text 27. There he refers to “chance” as the opportunity God gives the living entities to perform activities that will bring them to Him. “Chance” used in this way implies free will. The proper use of free will—taking advantage of the “chance” afforded by human life—will allow one to return to the spiritual world. But even that “chance” is not random; rather it is ordered by the Supreme Lord. Prabhupada writes:

**The theory of chance can best be explained in the Vedic literature by the words ajnata'Sukrti, which refer to pious activities performed without the actor’s knowledge. But these are also planned. For example, Krsna comes like an ordinary human being, He comes as a devotee like Lord Caitanya, or He sends His representative, the spiritual master, or pure devotee. This is also the planned activity of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. They come to canvass and educate, and thus a person in the illusory energy of the Supreme Lord gets a chance to mix with them, talk with them and take lessons from them, and somehow or other if a conditioned soul surrenders to such personalities and by intimate association with them chances to become Krsna conscious, he is saved from the material conditions of life. Krsna therefore instructs: sarva-dharman parityajya mam ekam saranam vraja, aham tvam sarva-papebhyo moksayisyami ma sucah— “Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reaction. Do not fear.” (Bg.** [**18.66**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.66)**) The word sarva-papebhyah means “from all sinful activities.” A person who surrenders unto Him by utilizing the chance to associate with the pure devotee, spiritual master or other authorized incarnations of Godhead, like Prthu Maharaja, is saved by Krsna. Then his life becomes successful.**

After establishing the Supreme Lord’s existence, Prthu Maharaja continues to encourage his citizens to perform the fruitive, ritualistic Vedic sacrifices bom of their prescribed duties. How will the performance of such sacrifices, designed for material gain, actually help them? After all, aren’t his citizens eternal souls whose constitutional nature is to exclusively serve Krsna? In Bhagavad-gita Krsna Himself decries Vedic fruitive activities, considering them separate from true spiritual consciousness: “When your mind is no longer disturbed by the flowery language of the Vedas, and when it remains fixed in the trance of self-realization, then you will have attained the divine consciousness.” (Bg. [2.53](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.53)) How would Vedic actions, such as the ones Prthu Maharaja is recommending to his citizens, help his citizens make spiritual advancement?

The answer is straightforward: The sastric injunctions on which the Vedic culture rests emanate from the Lord, who is the supreme authority. Those injunctions define sacrifice and proper and improper actions. One who fails to accept sastric direction suffers reactions from material nature, and ultimately one is forced to cycle through the 8,400,000 species of life. Since it was the Lord who recommended Vedic activities, even those that are materialistic, performing them means following His desire. Bhakti is defined as performing actions solely for the Lord’s pleasure. Those who adhere to the Vedic processes to give the Lord pleasure as they follow His instructions are practicing bhakti.

In addition, even within the karma-kanda sacrifices, Lord Visnu is given the central position. Thus followers of the Vedic system, even if not motivated by pure devotion, naturally and gradually advance to engagement in the Lord’s transcendental loving service. This advancement is what King Prthu wants for his citizens, and therefore he is encouraging the Visnu worship so inherent in the Vedic processes.

In his purport to text 34 Srila Prabhupada establishes this point: “Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments that these karma-kanda ritualistic ceremonies, although contaminated, contain touches of devotional service because whenever there is a performance of any yajna, Lord Visnu is given a central position. This is very important because even a little endeavor to please Lord Visnu is bhakti and is of great value. A tinge of bhakti purifies the material nature of the performances, which by devotional service gradually come to the transcendental position. Therefore although such yajnas are superficially material activities, the results are transcendental.”

Therefore, Prthu Maharaja explained, atheists like his father, King Vena, were condemned for stopping Vedic sacrifices—sacrifices meant to please the Lord. Ultimately it is the Supreme Lord alone who bestows the benedictions offered through the various Vedic sacrifices, not the individual demigods.

Srila Prabhupada offers a working definition of “humanistic materialists” in his purport to text 30 and then points to flaws in their reasoning: “According to them \[the atheists\], dharma, or religious principles, are meant to establish an imaginary God to encourage one to become moral, honest and just so that the social orders may be maintained in peace and tranquility. Furthermore, they say that actually there is no need to accept God for this purpose, for if one follows the principles of morality and honesty, that is sufficient. Similarly, if one makes nice plans and works very hard for economic development, automatically the result of economic development will come. Similarly, sense gratification also does not depend on the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for if one earns enough money by any process, one will have sufficient opportunity for sense gratification. Insofar as liberation is concerned, they say that there is no need to talk of liberation because after death everything is finished.”

Srila Prabhupada continues, explaining the insufficiency of the materialistic viewpoint:

**If one does not accept the authority of the Supreme Godhead in matters of religion and morality, one must explain why two persons of the same moral standard achieve different results. It is generally found that even if two men have the same moral standards of ethics, honesty and morality, their positions are still not the same. Similarly, in economic development it is seen that if two men work very hard day and night, still the results are not the same. One person may enjoy great opulence without even working, whereas another person, although working very hard, does not even get two sufficient meals a day. Similarly, in the matter of sense gratification, sometimes one who has sufficient food is still not happy in his family affairs or sometimes is not even married, whereas another person, even though not economically well off, has the greatest opportunity for sense gratification. Even an animal like a hog or a dog may have greater opportunities for sense gratification than a human being. Aside from liberation, even if we consider only the preliminary necessities of life—dharma, artha and kama (religion, economic development and sense gratification)— we will see that they are not the same for everyone. Therefore it must be accepted that there is someone who determines the different standards. In conclusion, not only for liberation must one depend on the Lord, but even for ordinary necessities in this material world. Prthu Maharaja therefore indicated that in spite of having rich parents, children are sometimes not happy. Similarly, in spite of valuable medicine administered by a competent physician, sometimes a patient dies; or in spite of having a big safe boat, sometimes a man drowns. We may thus struggle to counteract impediments offered by material nature, but our attempts cannot be successful unless we are favored by the Supreme Personality of Godhead.**

The natural inclination and taste that people possess to serve a superior, especially the Supreme Lord, should be encouraged, even if the desire to serve is motivated by selfishness. Why? Because rather than discouraging service simply because it is materially motivated, one should encourage and purify it so it can bear its proper fruit. “By the inclination to serve the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, suffering humanity can immediately cleanse the dirt which has accumulated in their minds during innumerable births. Like the Ganges water, which emanates from the toes of the lotus feet of the Lord, such a process immediately cleanses the mind, and thus spiritual or Krsna consciousness gradually increases.” (Bhag. [4.21.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.31))Due to contact with the Lord’s lotus feet, Ganges water purifies those who bathe in it. Similarly, the Lord’s lotus feet, the source of the Ganges’ purity, cleanses all who take shelter of them. In his purport to text 31 Srila Prabhupada explains how practicing Krsna consciousness “immediately cleanses the mind”:

**If one takes to the service of the lotus feet of the Lord, or takes to Krsna consciousness, he is immediately cleansed of the many dirty things which have accumulated in his innumerable births. We have seen that in spite of the very black record of their past lives, persons who take to Krsna consciousness become perfectly cleansed of all dirty things and make spiritual progress very swiftly. Therefore Prthu Maharaja advises that without the benediction of the Supreme Lord, one cannot make advancement—either in so-called morality, economic development or sense gratification. One should therefore take to the service of the Lord, or Krsna consciousness, and thus very soon become a perfect man, as confirmed in Bhagavad-gita (ksipram bhavati dharmatma sasvac chantim nigacchati). Being a responsible king, Prthu Maharaja recommends that everyone take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and thus be immediately purified. Lord Sri Krsna also says in Bhagavad-gita that simply by surrendering unto Him one is immediately relieved of all sinful reactions. As Krsna takes away all the sinful reactions of a person immediately upon his surrender unto Him, similarly the external manifestation of Krsna, the representative of Krsna who acts as the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, takes all the resultant actions of the sinful life of the disciple immediately after the disciple’s initiation. Thus if the disciple follows the principles instructed by the spiritual master, he remains purified and is not contaminated by the material infection.**

**Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu therefore stated that the spiritual master who plays the part of Krsna’s representative has to consume all the sinful reactions of his disciple. Sometimes a spiritual master takes the risk of being overwhelmed by the sinful reactions of the disciples and undergoes a sort of tribulation due to their acceptance. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu therefore advised that one not accept many disciples.**

When compared to the shelter Sri Krsna’s lotus feet offer, all other shelters—body, family, wealth—prove false and insufficient. Krsna’s lotus feet are the root from which everything in existence has sprung. Prthu Maharaja continued: Taking shelter of the Lord’s lotus feet removes misunderstandings and gradually causes renunciation to manifest. These gains are “possible only when one is strengthened by practicing bhakti-yoga. Once having taken shelter at the root of the lotus feet of the Lord, a devotee never comes back to this material existence, which is full of the threefold miseries.” (Bhag. [4.21.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.32))

Srila Prabhupada describes the potency of chanting Hare Krsna and practicing bhakti-yoga: “As stated by Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu in His Siksastaka instructions, by the chanting of the holy name of the Lord—Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare—or by the process of hearing and chanting of the glories of the Lord, one’s mind is gradually cleansed of all dirt. Due to our material association since time immemorial, we have accumulated heaps of dirty things in our minds. The total effect of this takes place when a living entity identifies himself with his body and is thus entrapped by the stringent laws of material nature and put into the cycle of repeated birth and death under the false impression of bodily identification. When one is strengthened by practicing bhakti' yoga, his mind is cleansed of this misunderstanding, and he is no longer interested in material existence or in sense gratification.

“. . . By practicing bhakti-yoga, one can directly perceive his advancement in spiritual life. In other practices—like karma-yoga, jnana-yoga and dhyana-yoga—one may not be confident about his progress, but in bhakti-yoga one can become directly aware of his progress in spiritual life, just as a person who eats can understand that his hunger is satisfied. Our false appetite for enjoyment and lordship of the material world is due to a prominence of passion and ignorance. By bhakti-yoga these two qualities are diminished, and one becomes situated in the mode of goodness. Gradually surpassing the mode of goodness, one is situated in pure goodness, which is not contaminated by the material qualities. When thus situated, a devotee no longer has any doubts; he knows that he will not come back to this material world.” (Bhag. [4.21.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.32), purport)

Prthu Maharaja therefore strongly advised his citizens to confidently serve the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead with body, mind, words, and the results of their work. Success in bhakti is not dependent on a particular occupation or on any other material designation. One should use whatever one does and has to offer service. In this way, there can be full cooperation between all the parts of society, just as the various parts of the body cooperate to serve the whole. Those who followed Maharaja Prthu’s instructions will “surely be successful in achieving the final objective” of their lives.Srila Prabhupada explains unity in the Lord’s service in his purport to text 33:

**In executing the prescribed duties of life, no one is higher or lower; there are such divisions as “higher” and “lower,” but since there is actually a common interest—to satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead—there are no distinctions between them.**

**The question may be raised that since the Lord is supposed to be worshiped by great demigods like Lord Brahma, Lord Siva and others, how can an ordinary human being on this planet serve Him? This is clearly explained by Prthu Maharaja by the use of the word yathadhikara, “according to one’s ability.” If one sincerely executes his occupational duty, that will be sufficient. One does not need to become like Lord Brahma, Lord Siva, Indra, Lord Caitanya or Ramanuj acarya, whose capabilities are certainly far above ours. Even a sudra, who is in the lowest stage of life according to the material qualities, can achieve the same success. Anyone can become successful in devotional service provided he displays no duplicity. It is explained here that one must be very frank and open-minded (amayinah). To be situated in a lower status of life is not a disqualification for success in devotional service. The only qualification is that whether one is a brahmana, ksatriya, vaisya or sudra, he must be open, frank and free from reservations. Then, by performing his particular occupational duty under the guidance of a proper spiritual master, he can achieve the highest success in life.**

## Texts 34-36: Prthu Maharaja Instructs His Citizens

**Part Three: The Goal of Prescribed Varnasrama Duties**

Prthu Maharaja continued: Although Himself spiritual and in need of nothing, Krsna kindly accepts sacrifices performed with material elements to purify those who perform the sacrifices. The Lord even accepts sacrifices meant to satisfy material desires, even though those sacrifices appear to be aimed at worship of the demigods.

Both the individual soul and the Lord live in the body. Whether or not a living entity will be aware of that fact depends on the type of body it inhabits. Although occupational duties are prescribed according to the body and the degree of consciousness a particular body makes possible, the goal of all occupational duties is the same: to move each soul toward deeper surrender to Krsna. Therefore the specific nature of one’s duties is less important than the necessity to perform them steadily, because it is the Supreme Personality of Godhead who is the master of all sacrifices and the enjoyer of all results. He is also the supreme spiritual master.

Maharaja Prthu concluded: “All of you citizens on the surface of the globe who have a relationship with me and are worshiping Him by dint of your occupational duties are bestowing your mercy upon me. Therefore, О my citizens, I thank you.” (Bhag. [4.21.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.36))

Thus as Srila Prabhupada confirms in his purport to text 36, Maharaja Prthu has requested his subjects to accept the bhakti-marga by focusing their minds on the Lord as they perform their prescribed duties and by knowing the Lord as both the Paramatma in everyone’s heart and the ultimate beneficiary of all sacrificial performances. It is He who is to be pleased.

## Texts 37-44: Prthu Maharaja Instructs His Citizens

**Part Four: Becoming Fixed in Devotional Service by Serving the Brahmanas and Vaisnavas**

Maharaja Prthu’s instructions end with text 44. Up until this point we have heard the glory of performing duties for Krsna’s satisfaction. But what is the source of the soul’s tendency to please Krsna? Everyone has a tendency to act, but few people relish action purely for God’s satisfaction. What causes the seed of bhakti to appear? How does it sprout and gradually grow into pure devotional service? In reply to these questions, Maharaja Prthu emphasized the role of brahmanas and Vaisnavas in society. Srila Prabhupada’s purports stress that while the Bhagavatam’s texts refer to brahmanas, the topmost brahmana is a Vaisnava, because Vaisnavas, who have surpassed the mode of goodness, are automatically brahmanas.

To fix his citizens more securely in devotional service, Prthu Maharaja glorified the brahmanas and Vaisnavas. He began by describing their mercy, for it is by their mercy that his citizens’ inclination to serve Krsna will awaken, strengthen, and become fixed: “The brahmanas and Vaisnavas are personally glorified by their characteristic powers of tolerance, penance, knowledge and education. By dint of all these spiritual assets, Vaisnavas are more powerful than royalty. It is therefore advised that the princely order not exhibit its material prowess before these two communities and should avoid offending them. The Supreme Personality of Godhead, the ancient, eternal Godhead, who is foremost amongst all great personalities, obtained the opulence of His staunch reputation, which purifies the entire universe, by worshiping the lotus feet of those brahmanas and Vaisnavas. The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is everlastingly independent and who exists in everyone’s heart, is very pleased with those who follow in His footsteps and engage without reservation in the service of the descendants of brahmanas and Vaisnavas, for He is always dear to brahmanas and Vaisnavas and they are always dear to Him. By regular service to the brahmanas and Vaisnavas, one can clear the dirt from his heart and thus enjoy supreme peace and liberation from material attachment and be satisfied. In this world there is no fruitive activity superior to serving the brahmana class, for this can bring pleasure to the demigods, for whom the many sacrifices are recommended.” (Bhag. [4.21.37-40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.37))

In his purport to text 37 Srila Prabhupada warns against offending Vaisnavas: “Prthu Maharaja warns his citizens who are actually engaged in the devotional service of the Lord to take care against offenses to the brahmanas and Vaisnavas. Offenses at their lotus feet are so destructive that even the descendants of Yadu who were bom in the family of Lord Krsna were destroyed due to offenses at their feet. The Supreme Personality of Godhead cannot tolerate any offense at the lotus feet of brahmanas and Vaisnavas. Sometimes, due to their powerful positions, princes or government servants neglect the position of brahmanas and Vaisnavas, not knowing that because of their offense they will be ruined.”

In his purport to text 38 he emphasizes service to the Vaisnavas: “In the Bhagavad-gita it is said that the Lord does not need to work to achieve material gain. Since He is perpetually supremely perfect, He does not need to obtain anything, but still it is said that He obtained His opulences by worshiping the lotus feet of the brahmanas. These are His exemplary actions. When Lord Sri Krsna was in Dvaraka, He offered His respects by bowing down at the lotus feet of Narada. When Sudama Vipra came to His house, Lord Krsna personally washed his feet and gave him a seat on His personal bed. Although He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Sri Krsna offered His respects to Maharaja Yudhisthira and Kunti. The Lord’s exemplary behavior is to teach us.”

After glorifying brahmanas and Vaisnavas, Srila Prabhupada issues a caution: “The spiritual master is the best brahmana. At present, in the age of Kali, it is very difficult to render service to the brahmana-kula, or the brahmana class. The difficulty, according to the Varaha Purana, is that demons, taking advantage of Kali-yuga, have taken birth in brahmana families. Raksasah kalim asritya jayante brahma-yonisu (Varaha Purana). In other words, in this age there are many so-called caste brahmanas and caste Gosvamis who, taking advantage of the sastra and of the innocence of people in general, claim to be brahmanas and Vaisnavas by hereditary right. One will not derive any benefit by rendering service to such false brahmana-kulas. One must therefore take shelter of a bona fide spiritual master and his associates and render service to them, for such activity will greatly help the neophyte in attaining full satisfaction.” (Bhag. [4.21.40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.40), purport)

Prthu Maharaja explained that the Lord feels more pleasure when the brahmanas and Vaisnavas are fed than when He is offered ghee in a sacrificial fire. In his purport to text 41, Srila Prabhupada suggests the topmost service one can offer the Lord: “Fire is certainly devoid of life, but devotees and brahmanas are the living representatives of the Supreme Lord. Therefore to feed brahmanas and Vaisnavas is to feed the Supreme Personality of Godhead directly. It may be concluded that instead of offering fire sacrifices, one should offer foodstuffs to brahmanas and Vaisnavas, for that process is more effective than fire yajna.”

Why does the Lord consider the brahmanas so dear? It is because brahmanas faithfully accept the sastra, practice austerity, adhere to scriptural conclusions, fully control the mind and senses, and meditate on Him (Bhag. [4.21.37](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.37), [42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.42)). As text 42 notes, brahmanas therefore keep their consciousness clean, because “In this way the real goal of life is illuminated, just as one’s face is fully reflected in a clear mirror.” In his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada notes that a genuine Vaisnava is naturally a perfect brahmana, for by gazing into the pure mirror of his own consciousness he clearly sees his eternal identity as Krsna’s servant.

The Lord cherishes the service performed by Vaisnavas because Vaisnavas keep Krsna in their hearts by always thinking of Him in devotion: “The pure devotee is always within the core of My heart, and I am always in the heart of the pure devotee. My devotees do not know anything else but Me, and I do not know anyone else but them.” (Bhag. [9.4.68](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-9/4.68)) By the mercy of such Vaisnavas, the seed of devotional faith and taste is planted in the heart of all whom they contact.

Concluding his instructions, Prthu Maharaja begged the citizens to bless his success in perpetually carrying on his royal crown the dust of the lotus feet of brahmanas and Vaisnavas. By doing so, Prthu Maharaja prayed, I will be relieved from sinful reactions and will simultaneously develop desirable qualities. “Whoever acquires the brahminical qualifications—whose only wealth is good behavior, who is grateful and who takes shelter of experienced persons—gets all the opulence of the world. I therefore wish that the Supreme Personality of Godhead and His associates be pleased with the brahmana class, with the cows and with me.” (Bhag. [4.21.44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.44))

In his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada glorifies the qualities Prthu Maharaja mentions and uses them to define a brahmana or Vaisnava: “When one actually attains good qualities, becomes grateful for the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and takes shelter of a bona fide spiritual master, he is endowed with all opulence. Such a person is a brahmana or Vaisnava.”

## Texts 45-52: The Citizens, Demigods, and Residents of Pitrloka Reply

The citizens heard Prthu Maharaja’s words and, pleased with his guidance and Vaisnava humility, congratulated him. They expressed their goodwill and agreement by calling out, “Sadhu! Sadhu!” Offering the example of Prahlada Maharaja, whose glorious activities saved his demoniac father, Hiranyakasipu, the citizens glorified Prthu Maharaja, who also saved his sinful father by his own purity. The brahmanas blessed Prthu Maharaja for his devotion to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and said they saw him as God’s representative.

Srila Prabhupada accepts the citizens’ viewpoint in his purport to text 49 and explains that Prthu Maharaja both preached and followed the Lord’s instructions, thus setting an example that inspired his followers to act in a similar way.

The citizens expressed their appreciation for Prthu Maharaja’s affection and for his compassion in overseeing their welfare. They acknowledged that his words had opened their eyes and taught them how to cross the ocean of fruitive entanglement: “Dear lord, you are situated in your pure existential position of goodness; therefore you are the perfect representative of the Supreme Lord. You are glorified by your own prowess, and thus you are maintaining the entire world by introducing brahminical culture and protecting everyone in your line of duty as a ksatriya.” (Bhag. [4.21.52](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/21.52))

## Chapter 22 - Prthu Maharaja’s Meeting with the Four Kumaras

## Texts 1-17: The Arrival of the Four Kumaras

The Lord predicted (Bhag. [4.20.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/20.15)) that Prthu Maharaja would have the fortune of meeting the four Kumaras. Now, as the citizens prayed to their king, the four Kumaras, the powerful, ever-youthful, ancient sages, who are as effulgent as the sun, descended from the sky. Everyone recognized them immediately. Since they had just finished listening to King Prthu’s instructions on the importance of respecting brahmanas and Vaisnavas, the citizens felt anxious to receive them properly.

The Bhagavatam describes: “Seeing the four Kumaras, Prthu Maharaja was greatly anxious to receive them. Therefore the King, with all his officers, very hastily got up, as anxiously as a conditioned soul whose senses are immediately attracted by the modes of material nature.” (Bhag. [4.22.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.3)) In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada quotes the adage “Birds of a feather flock together.” He means that “In this world, everyone is attracted by a person of the same category. A drunkard is attracted to persons who are also drunkards. Similarly, a saintly person is attracted by other saintly persons. Prthu Maharaja was in the topmost position of spiritual advancement, and as such, he was attracted by the Kumaras, who were of the same category. It is said, therefore, that a man is known by his company.”

After Prthu Maharaja worshiped these renowned teachers, he sprinkled the water that had washed their lotus feet on his head. Thus he set a wonderful example to accompany the instructions he had just imparted to his citizens.

Prthu Maharaja then welcomed the Kumaras with sweet words, humbly expressing his great fortune in having attained their audience: “My dear great sages, auspiciousness personified, it is very difficult for even the mystic yogis to see you. Indeed, you are very rarely seen. I do not know what kind of pious activity I performed for you to grace me by appearing before me without difficulty.... From the beginning of your birth you strictly observed the vows of celibacy, and although you are experienced in the path of liberation, you are keeping yourselves just like small children.” (Bhag. [4.22.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.7), [12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.12))

In his purport to text 15, Srila Prabhupada describes Maharaja Prthu’s mood in greeting the Kumaras: “When saintly persons go from door to door to see those who are too much materially engaged, it is to be understood that they do not go to ask anything for their personal benefit. It is a fact that saintly persons go to materialists just to give real information of the auspicious. Maharaja Prthu was assured of this fact; therefore instead of wasting time by asking the Kumaras about their welfare, he preferred to inquire from them whether he could soon be relieved from the dangerous position of materialistic existence.”

Prthu Maharaja began with two questions: How can those entangled in material existence, such as householders, be blessed with good fortune? (Bhag. [4.22.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.13)) And, How can one make quick advancement in spiritual life? (Bhag. [4.22.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.15)) In text 14 he acknowledges that the four sages are different from residents of this world. “My dear sirs, there is no need to ask about your good and bad fortune because you are always absorbed in spiritual bliss. The mental concoction of the auspicious and inauspicious does not exist in you.” He therefore considered the sages the true friends of all living beings.

In his purport to text 15 Srila Prabhupada describes what we attain by associating with saints: “\[Wjhenever one meets a great saintly person, one should immediately surrender unto him and inquire about relief from the material pains of existence. Therefore Srila Narottama dasa Thakura says, samsara-visanale, divanisi hiyajvale, juddite nd kainu upaya: ‘We are always suffering from material pangs, and our hearts are burning, but we cannot find any way out of it.’ The materialistic person can also be called a tapasvi, which means someone who is always suffering from material pains. One can get rid of all these material pains only when he takes shelter of the chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra. This is also explained by Narottama dasa Thakura: golokera prema-dhana, harinama-sanklrtana, rati nd janmila kene tdya. Narottama dasa Thakura regretted that he did not pursue his attraction for the transcendental vibration of the Hare Krsna mantra. The conclusion is that all persons in this material world are suffering from material pains, and if one wants to get rid of them, he must associate with saintly persons, pure devotees of the Lord, and chant the maha-mantra, Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare / Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare. That is the only auspicious way for materialistic persons.”

Thus Prthu Maharaja expressed his conviction that the Lord exhibits His mercy toward a soul when He awards that soul the opportunity to associate with His devotees.

Sanat-kumara will reply on behalf of all four sages.

## Texts 18-23: Sanat-kumara’s Response—The Process of Advancement in Spiritual Life

Sanat-kumara first glorified Prthu Maharaja’s question, “How can I make quick spiritual advancement?” This question is wonderful, because although the King had asked it for the benefit of others, it nevertheless evoked krsna-katha.

Srila Prabhupada writes: “When Narada Muni questioned Lord Brahma about the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Brahma thanked Narada Muni for giving him a chance to speak about the Supreme Lord. Therefore questions put by a saintly person to another saintly person about the Supreme Personality of Godhead or about the ultimate goal of life surcharge everything spiritually. Whoever takes advantage of such discussions is benefited both in this life and in the next.” (Bhag. [4.22.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.19), purport)

Sanat-kumara continued: The unflinching, faithful heart of one who has developed a taste for hearing and speaking krsna-katha will become pure and free of lust. Then in that pure heart the soul’s natural attachment to the Lord will increase. “It has been conclusively decided in the scriptures, after due consideration, that the ultimate goal for the welfare of human society is detachment from the bodily concept of life and increased and steadfast attachment for the Supreme Lord, who is transcendental, beyond the modes of material nature.” (Bhag. [4.22.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.21)) How does one achieve this? “Attachment for the Supreme can be increased by practicing devotional service, inquiring about the Supreme Personality of Godhead, applying bhakti-yoga in life, worshiping the Yogesvara, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and by hearing and chanting about the glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. These actions are pious in themselves.” (Bhag. [4.22.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.22))

These central texts in Sanat-kumara’s instructions appear to define much of the remaining instructions in this Canto. In essence, this text declares the need in spiritual life for both detachment and attachment: one should become more detached from the body and more attached to Krsna. Of the two, Prabhupada emphasizes in his purports to this section the importance of increasing one’s attachment to Krsna. “The conclusion is that by developing a loving desire for the service of the lotus feet of the Lord, we subdue all material desires for sense gratification.” (Bhag. [4.22.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.39), purport) Sanat-kumara’s remaining instructions also emphasize these two points. Additionally, Narada Muni’s allegorical story describing King Puranj ana’s ephemeral life (Bhag. [4.25.9](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/25.9) through Bhag. [4.28.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/28.27)) powerfully increases our detachment, while the King’s next birth as Queen Vaidharbi glorifies bhakti, attached service to Krsna, and its eternal benefits (Bhag. [4.28.28-64](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/28.28)). Sections of Chapter Twenty-nine continue these two themes.

Sanat-kumara continued by listing five ways to advance in Krsna consciousness, each leading to increased attachment to Krsna. In his purport to text 22, Srila Prabhupada supports Sanat-kumara’s words and fills in several key details: “\[T\]o increase attachment for the Supreme Personality of Godhead one has to accept a bona fide spiritual master and learn from him the methods of devotional service and hear from him about the transcendental message and glorification of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In this way one has to increase his conviction about devotional service. Then it will be very easy to increase attachment for the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

Sanat-kumara then offered further instructions: One should hear about Krsna, renounce unfavorable association, and serve Krsna. Give up the association of those “simply interested in sense gratification and making money. Not only avoid such persons, but also those who associate with such persons.” Mold your life “in such a way that you cannot live in peace without drinking the nectar of the glorification of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari. One can be thus elevated by being disgusted with the taste for sense enjoyment.” (Bhag. [4.22.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.23))

One must remove anything negative—whatever it is that impedes one’s advancement. Then by following the positive process Sanat-kumara prescribed, one’s attachment to Krsna will blossom. In his purport to text 23 Srila Prabhupada decries an existence based on sensual pleasures and the necessity to earn money to support one’s sense gratification: “To advance in devotional service one should be uninterested in the materialistic way of life. That which is the subject matter of satisfaction for the devotees is of no interest to the nondevotees.”

Yet, as Srila Prabhupada notes, “Simple negation, or giving up the company of materialistic persons, will not do.” One must become fixed in devotional service in the association of devotees: “The beginning of devotional service is to hear about the glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. That is recommended in this verse: vind harer guna-piyusa-pandt. One must drink the nectar of the glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and this means that one must be always engaged in hearing and chanting the glories of the Lord. It is the prime method for advancing in spiritual life. Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu also recommends this in the Caitanya-caritamrta. If one wants to make advancement in spiritual life, by great fortune he may meet a bona fide spiritual master and from him learn about Krsna. By serving both the spiritual master and Krsna he gets the seed of devotional service (bhakti-lata-bija), and if he sows the seed within his heart and waters it by hearing and chanting, it grows into a luxuriant bhakti-lata, or bhakti creeper. The creeper is so strong that it penetrates the covering of the universe and reaches the spiritual world and continues to grow on and on until it reaches and takes shelter of the lotus feet of Krsna, just as an ordinary creeper also grows on and on until it takes a solid shelter on a roof; then it very steadily grows and produces the required fruit. The real cause of the growing of such fruit, which is here called the nectar of hearing the glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is to water the creeper of devotional service by hearing and chanting. The purport is that one cannot live outside the society of devotees; one must live in the association of devotees, where there is constant chanting and hearing of the glories of the Lord.”

Srila Prabhupada then defines ISKCON’s compassionate purpose: “The Krsna consciousness movement is started for this purpose, so that hundreds of ISKCON centers may give people a chance to hear and chant, to accept the spiritual master and to disassociate themselves from persons who are materially interested, for in this way one can make solid advancement in going back home, back to Godhead.”

## Texts 24-31: Sanat-kumara Gives Further Details about the Path of Spiritual Advancement

If one wants to make rapid spiritual advancement, one should hear about Krsna. That was Sanat-kumara’s prescription. But can other practices or qualities assist our advancement? How can we make the mind more receptive to krsna'kathd? Sanat-kumara said: A candidate wishing to advance spiritually must be nonviolent, must follow in the footsteps of great acaryas, must remember the nectar of the Lord’s pastimes, must follow the regulative principles (without material desire), and “while following the regulative principles, must not blaspheme others. A devotee should lead a very simple life and not be disturbed by the duality of opposing elements. He should learn to tolerate them.” (Bhag. [4.22.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.24))

Srila Prabhupada writes: “A devotee should be tolerant and should be very much compassionate toward others. For example, if he suffers personal injury, he should tolerate it. . . . but if someone else suffers injury, the devotee need not tolerate it. The word smrtyd is very important in spiritual life. Smrtya means remembering Krsna always. Life should be molded in such a way that one cannot remain alone without thinking of Krsna. . . . We should live in Krsna so that while eating, sleeping, walking and working we remain only in Krsna. Our Krsna consciousness society recommends that we arrange our living so that we can remember Krsna. Another feature of the devotee is ninhaya, simple living. Niriha means ‘gentle,’ ‘meek’ or ‘simple.’ A devotee should not live very gorgeously and imitate a materialistic person. Plain living and high thinking are recommended for a devotee. He should accept only so much as he needs to keep the material body fit for the execution of devotional service.” (Bhag. [4.22.24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.24), purport)

How can one become firmly fixed in these practices? “The devotee should gradually increase the culture of devotional service by constant hearing of the transcendental qualities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. These pastimes are like ornamental decorations on the ears of devotees. By rendering devotional service and transcending the material qualities, one can easily be fixed in transcendence in the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [4.22.25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.25))

In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada tells us how to advance: “This verse is especially mentioned to substantiate the devotional process of hearing the subject matter. A devotee does not like to hear anything other than subjects dealing with spiritual activities, or the pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. We can increase our propensity for devotional service by hearing Bhagavad-gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam from realized souls. The more we hear from realized souls, the more we make advancement in our devotional life. The more we advance in devotional life, the more we become detached from the material world. The more we become detached from the material world, as advised by Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu, the more we increase in attachment for the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore, a devotee who actually wants to make progress in devotional service and go back home, back to Godhead, must lose interest in sense enjoyment and associating with persons who are after money and sense gratification.”

What does one gain from being fixed on the path? “Upon becoming fixed in his attachment to the Supreme Personality of Godhead by the grace of the spiritual master and by awakening knowledge and detachment, the living entity, situated within the heart of the body and covered by the five elements, burns up his material surroundings exactly as fire, arising from wood, burns the wood itself.” (Bhag. [4.22.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.26))

But one needs a material situation in order to live in this world, even to prosecute Krsna consciousness. Devotees need the body, because without a body, how will they hear and chant? However, hearing and chanting stimulate devotion, which causes detachment from the body, the very facility allowing them to serve. Thus an advanced devotee, although in a body, remains simultaneously aloof from it. Srila Prabhupada explains this point in his purport to text 26: “An advanced devotee, therefore, does not live within the material body but within his spiritual body, just as a dry coconut lives detached from the coconut husk, even though within the husk. The pure devotee’s body is therefore called tin-maya-sarira (‘spiritualized body’). In other words, a devotee’s body is not connected with material activities, and as such, a devotee is always liberated (brahma-bhuyaya kalpate), as confirmed in Bhagavad-gita ([14.26](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/14.26)). Srila Riipa Gosvami also confirms this: ihd yasya harer dasye karmana manasa gira, nikhilasv apy avasthasu jivan-muktah sa ucyate: ‘Whatever his condition may be, one who is engaged fully with his body, mind and speech in the service of the Lord is liberated, even within this body.’”

Describing the position of liberation, Sanat-kumara said: “When a person becomes devoid of all material desires and liberated from all material qualities, he transcends distinctions between actions executed externally and internally. At that time the difference between the soul and the Supersoul, which was existing before selfrealization, is annihilated. When a dream is over, there is no longer a distinction between the dream and the dreamer.” (Bhag. [4.22.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.27))

Is this great soul suggesting an impersonal conclusion? The four Kumaras had been impersonalists on the jndna-mdrga before becoming bhaktas. Their ecstatic conversion brought about by their smelling the aroma of tulasi leaves on the Lord’s lotus feet has already been described (Bhag. [3.15.43-50](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/15.43)). Sanat-kumara is not suggesting an impersonal conclusion. Rather, Sanat-kumara spoke in a way that would appeal to jndnis. He wanted to indicate that jndna does indeed become perfect in bhakti, and he wanted to carry to the path of bhakti the many imper-sonalists practicing jndna. Srila Prabhupada clarifies: “This is the stage of oneness, or merging into the existence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This means that the individual soul, while keeping his individuality, no longer has separate interests. He is fully in the service of the Lord, and he has nothing to do for his personal sense gratification; therefore he sees only the Supreme Personality of Godhead and not himself. His personal interest completely perishes. When a person comes out of a dream, the dream vanishes. While dreaming a person may consider himself a king and see the royal paraphernalia, his soldiers, etc., but when the dream is over, he does not see anything beyond himself. Similarly, a liberated person understands that he is part and parcel of the Supreme Lord acting in accordance with the desire of the Supreme Lord, and as such there is no distinction between himself and the Supreme Lord, although both of them retain their individuality.” (Bhag. [4.22.27](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.27), purport)

Sanat-kumara next contrasted the consciousness and vision of a conditioned soul with those of a pure soul: “When the soul exists for sense gratification, he creates different desires, and for that reason he becomes subjected to designations. But when one is in the transcendental position, he is no longer interested in anything except fulfilling the desires of the Lord.” (Bhag. [4.22.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.28)) When such great souls view other beings, they see the soul—the being’s spiritual essence —regardless of the body encasing it. This perception is actually natural to every living entity.

Sanat-kumara then presented an example: We may see a man’s reflection on water, on oil, and in a mirror. Although the reflected image in each may appear different due to the quality of the reflecting substance, there is only one man. Similarly, those free of illusion see an individual soul acting even though that soul’s activities may be expressed through any one of a variety of bodies.

What prohibits one from having this universal vision? Sanat-kumara explained: The absorption of the mind and senses in seeking one’s own pleasure agitates the mind and draws it from its natural spiritual consciousness. “\[O\]ne’s real consciousness almost becomes lost, like the water in a lake that is gradually sucked up by the big grass straws on its bank.” (Bhag. 4.22.30) Just as the water in a lake is gradually consumed by the reeds on its shore, so the consciousness of one absorbed in sense gratification is similarly consumed. In his purport to text 30, Srila Prabhupada describes this further: “If a big lake is covered all around by long kusa grass, just like columns, the waters dry up. Similarly, when the big columns of material desire increase, the clear water of consciousness is dried up. Therefore these columns of kusa grass should be cut or thrown away from the very beginning. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu has instructed that if from the very beginning we do not take care of unwanted grass in the paddy fields, the fertilizing agents or water will be used by them, and the paddy plants will dry up. The material desire for sense enjoyment is the cause of our falldown in this material world, and thus we suffer the threefold miseries and continuous birth, death, old age and disease. However, if we turn our desires toward the transcendental loving service of the Lord, our desires become purified. We cannot kill desires. We have to purify them of different designations.”

If one wants to return to the spiritual world, therefore, he has to turn his desires from sense gratification toward the Lord’s transcendental loving service. As desire is a natural aspect of consciousness, one can never truly eliminate it, but one must transform his self-centered material desires into robust desires to please Krsna.

What happens when the soul loses its natural consciousness? Sanat-kumara said: “When one deviates from his original consciousness, he loses the capacity to remember his previous position or recognize his present one. When remembrance is lost, all knowledge acquired is based on a false foundation. When this occurs, learned scholars consider that the soul is lost.” (Bhag. [4.22.31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.31)) Practically speaking, the soul is dead or at the least fallen into animal consciousness; actual consciousness is absent, and all actions are performed in the deepest forgetfulness and ignorance.

## Texts 32-40: Sanat-kumara Concludes His Instructions to Prthu Maharaja by Telling Him to Take Shelter of the Lord’s Lotus Feet

Sanat-Kumara then warned Prthu Maharaja: “There is no stronger obstruction to one’s self-interest than thinking other subject matters to be more pleasing than one’s self-realization. For human society, constantly thinking of how to earn money and apply it for sense gratification brings about the destruction of everyone’s interests. When one becomes devoid of knowledge and devotional service, he enters into species of life like those of trees and stones.” (Bhag. [4.22.32-33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.32))

Srila Prabhupada explains: “If we do not properly execute our mission of life in self-realization, nature’s punishment will render us inactive by putting us in the form of trees and hills. Therefore activities directed toward sense gratification are condemned herein. One who is constantly thinking of activities to earn money and gratify the senses is following a path which is suicidal. Factually all human society is following this path. Some way or other, people are determined to earn money or get money by begging, borrowing or stealing and applying that for sense gratification. Such a civilization is the greatest obstacle in the path of self-realization.” (Bhag. [4.22.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.33), purport)

“Those who strongly desire to cross the ocean of nescience must not associate with the modes of ignorance, for hedonistic activities are the greatest obstructions to realization of religious principles, economic development, regulated sense gratification and, at last, liberation.” (Bhag. [4.22.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.34)) One should follow sastra, even when pursuing material enjoyment, and not act whimsically. One is purified by acting according to sastric injunctions, and one gradually crosses the ocean of ignorance.

One should look at life as an opportunity to achieve liberation. Dharma, artha, and kama are all material and thus subject to destruction. Srila Prabhupada’s comments on these points are practical: “In other words, it is advised that one not act in a way that will obstruct the regular process of advancement in spiritual life and liberation. The Vedic process of sense gratification is therefore planned in such a way that one can economically develop and enjoy sense gratification and yet ultimately attain liberation. Vedic civilization offers us all knowledge in the sastras, and if we live a regulated life under the direction of sastras and guru, all our material desires will be fulfilled; at the same time we will be able to go forward to liberation.” (Bhag. [4.22.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.34), purport)

Still, one should focus on the true goal of human life: “Everything should be adjusted in such a way that we attain liberation.... The conclusion is that we should not stress pious activities, economic development and sense gratification, but should concern ourselves with approaching Lord Visnu in His spiritual planets, of which the topmost is Goloka Vrndavana, where Lord Krsna lives. Therefore this Krsna consciousness movement is the greatest gift for persons who are actually desiring liberation.” (Bhag. [4.22.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/22.35) purport)

Sanat-kumara had now answered Maharaja Prthu’s first question. Thus he turned to his second question: What truly signifies a soul’s good fortune? He said: When Krsna wishes to bestow His true blessings on souls, He gives them detachment from all material goals, because regardless of the pleasures that material achievements afford, neither the pleasure nor the achievements have permanent value. Only that which is eternal is worth gaining.

Those planning careers may wonder whether they should strive to become, for example, bank tellers or bank managers.
