After offering these powerful yet indirect arguments to awaken detachment in King Pracinabarhisat, Narada Muni then concisely characterized material existence: For approximately one hundred years the embodied living entities freely choose how they wish to act; each act, whether it be in goodness, passion, or ignorance, shapes their future births. In that sense the conditioned souls are like dogs whipped by destiny and driven by hunger, searching always for the “food” that will alleviate their hunger. Despite their attempts to become happy, they struggle, unable to circumvent fate.

And what of their attempt to reduce misery? Narada continues: “A man may carry a burden on his head, and when he feels it to be too heavy, he sometimes gives relief to his head by putting the burden on his shoulder. In this way he tries to relieve himself of the burden. However, whatever process he devises to counteract the burden does nothing more than put the same burden from one place to another.” (Bhag. [4.29.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.33))

In his purport to text 32 Srila Prabhupada graphically describes humankind’s struggle to counteract misery: “Just as a dog wanders here and there for a piece of bread or punishment, the living entity perpetually wanders about trying to be happy and planning in so many ways to counteract material misery. This is called the struggle for existence. We can actually see in our daily lives how we are forced to make plans to drive away miserable conditions. To get rid of one miserable condition, we have to put ourselves in another kind of miserable condition. A poor man suffers for want of money, but if he wants to become rich, he has to struggle in so many ways. Actually that is not a valid counteracting process but a snare of the illusory energy. If one does not endeavor to counteract his situation but is satisfied with his position, knowing that he has obtained his position through past activities, he can instead engage his energy to develop Krsna consciousness.”

Improvements on the material level basically cause one to exchange one misery for another. Srila Prabhupada continues to pummel the material concept in his purport to text 33: “When one gets tired of keeping a burden on his head, he will place it on his shoulder. This does not mean that he has become freed from the strains of carrying the burden. Similarly, human society in the name of civilization is creating one kind of trouble to avoid another kind of trouble. In contemporary civilization we see that there are many automobiles manufactured to carry us swiftly from one place to another, but at the same time we have created other problems. We have to construct so many roads, and yet these roads are insufficient to cope with automobile congestion and traffic jams. There are also the problems of air pollution and fuel shortage. The conclusion is that the processes we manufacture to counteract or minimize our distresses do not actually put an end to our pains. It is all simply illusion. We simply place the burden from the head to the shoulder. The only real way we can minimize our problems is to surrender unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead and give ourselves up to His protection. The Lord, being all-powerful, can make arrangements to mitigate our painful life in material existence.”

To get to the point of deeply accepting that no situation in the material world can satisfy the eternal soul is a giant step forward in spiritual life. The alternative is to strive fruitlessly to trade material dissatisfaction for material satisfaction. The dissatisfied worker may curse his boss, thinking, “I slave day after day while he sits comfortably in his office counting his profits.” Envy, accompanied by the desire to achieve the boss’s position, is bom in the worker’s heart and is already shaping him for his next birth. In a future birth both the envy and the desire will fructify, and the worker will begin to reap a new set of experiences along with a new set of miseries—he in turn will be envied by his own workers, tormented by the rise and fall of his profits, afraid of his competition, and especially afraid of losing what he has to thieves. Perhaps he will think, “If only I was really rich—a billionaire perhaps—I wouldn’t have to worry about money.” And perhaps he will discover what it really means to be a billionaire.

Srila Prabhupada explained the next step in the worker’s development during a room conversation in Columbus, Ohio, in May 1969:

**After too much material enjoyment, the next stage is—that is natural—frustration. There is a good example in our country, one Mr. C. R. Das. He was a great leader, next to Gandhi, an important political leader. So he was the topmost lawyer, barrister, earning fifty thousand dollars monthly. A very rich man. And he was making charity, and spending like anything. He was drunkard number one, woman-hunter number one, and everything. Because he had money he could enjoy everything. But he was not happy. So one day he was sitting with his wife, and just looking in the street. So his wife asked him—his name was Chittaranjan: “Chittaranjan, you are earning so much. You are spending. People are very much fond of you. You are a great leader. Why do you always remain morose? What do you want to be? You now have got everything.” So at that time one mendicant, a sannyasi, was passing. So Chittaranjan said, “I want to be like him. Then I will be happy. I don’t want to enjoy. I want to be a beggar.”**

King Pracinabarhisat had performed innumerable pious sacrifices. Narada Muni next attacked the attempt the King was making through the performance of those sacrifices to find both happiness and relief from suffering: “No one can counteract the effects of fruitive activity simply by manufacturing a different activity devoid of Krsna consciousness. All such activity is due to our ignorance. When we have a troublesome dream, we cannot relieve it with a troublesome hallucination. One can counteract a dream only by awaking. Similarly, our material existence is due to our ignorance and illusion. Unless we awaken to Krsna consciousness, we cannot be relieved of such dreams. For the ultimate solution to all problems, we must awaken to Krsna consciousness.” (Bhag. [4.29.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.34))

Troublesome dreams—sometimes we suffer because we see a tiger or a snake in a dream when neither animal is present. The only way to relieve ourselves of such troublesome dream images is to awaken. Going back to Godhead does not merely transfer the burden of misery from one shoulder to the other; it removes it. Therefore the living entities’ real interest is to escape the ignorance that has caused them to remain in the cycle of repeated birth and death by surrendering to the Supreme Personality of Godhead through His representative. As text 37 states, unless one renders devotional service to Lord Vasudeva, one cannot possibly become completely detached from the material world nor manifest real knowledge.

Narada Muni then switched from topics meant to awaken King Pracinabarhisat’s detachment to a direct discussion of devotional service (texts 34-41), for that alone would evoke the true happiness inherent in his soul. Narada Muni told King Pracinabarhisat: “O best of kings, one who is faithful, who is always hearing the glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is always engaged in the culture of Krsna consciousness and in hearing of the Lord’s activities, very soon becomes eligible to see the Supreme Personality of Godhead face to face. My dear King, in the place where pure devotees live, following the rules and regulations and thus purely conscious and engaged with great eagerness in hearing and chanting the glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in that place if one gets a chance to hear their constant flow of nectar, which is exactly like the waves of a river, one will forget the necessities of life—namely hunger and thirst—and become immune to all kinds of fear, lamentation and illusion.” (Bhag. [4.29.38-40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.38))

Srila Prabhupada describes the simultaneous removal of material attachments and the natural blossoming of a soul’s attachment to Krsna through hearing and chanting in the association of Vaisnavas: “The cultivation of Krsna consciousness is possible where great devotees live together and constantly engage in hearing and chanting the glories of the Lord. In a holy place like Vrndavana, there are many devotees constantly engaged in chanting and hearing the glories of the Lord. If one gets the chance to hear from pure devotees in such a place, allowing the constant flow of the river of nectar to come from the mouths of pure devotees, then the cultivation of Krsna consciousness becomes very easy.” (Bhag. [4.29.39-40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.39), purport)

## Texts 42-51: Narada Ends King Pracinabarhisat’s Performance of Vedic Rituals

Narada’s next attack on the King’s ritualistic practices was to explain that his sacrifices were adverse to the development of Krsna consciousness. Narada Muni said: The Lord can never be known fully even by the great sages advanced in Vedic knowledge who perform sacrifices. Neither does demigod worship help one develop realization of the Absolute Truth, even if one chants Vedic mantras. Real spiritual realization can be attained only by practicing pure devotional service. One must therefore give up fruitive tendencies and the pursuits of the jndna'marga, even though they are prescribed in certain sections of the Vedas. Instead, one should practice bhakti-yoga, serving the Lord purely. Aspire only to please Him.

In the first part of the purport to text 46, Srila Prabhupada explains something wonderful about the pure devotee: “The significant word atma-bhavitah indicates that the Lord is awakened in one’s mind if one constantly thinks of Him. A pure devotee is always thinking of the lotus feet of the Lord (sa vai manah krsna-padaravindayoh). A pure devotee cannot remain a moment without being absorbed in thoughts of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

Srila Prabhupada continues, explaining how Krsna reciprocates with pure devotees: “This constant thinking of the Lord is described in Bhagavad-gita as satata-yuktanam, always engaging in the Lord’s service. Bhajatam priti-piirvakam: this is devotional service in love and affection. Because the Supreme Personality of Godhead dictates to the pure devotee from within, the devotee is saved from all material activities.”

In explaining a second meaning of atma-bhavitah, Srila Prabhupada describes a powerful service that only a pure devotee can render: “The word atma-bhavitah also indicates that a devotee is always engaged in preaching to deliver conditioned souls. It is said of the six Gosvamis: nana-sastra-vicaranaka-nipunau sad-dharma-samsthapakau lokanam hita-karinau. A pure devotee of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is always thinking of how fallen, conditioned souls can be delivered. The Supreme Personality of Godhead, influenced by the merciful devotees’ attempt to deliver fallen souls, enlightens the people in general from within by His causeless mercy.”

Narada Muni then forbade King Pracinabarhisat to continue performing Vedic ritualistic sacrifices, because they were not in his selfinterest: “When a person is fully engaged in devotional service, he is favored by the Lord, who bestows His causeless mercy. At such a time, the awakened devotee gives up all material activities and ritualistic performances mentioned in the Vedas. My dear King Barhisman, you should never out of ignorance take to the Vedic rituals or to fruitive activity, which may be pleasing to hear about or which may appear to be the goal of self-interest. You should never take these to be the ultimate goal of life. Those who are less intelligent accept the Vedic ritualistic ceremonies as all in all. They do not know that the purpose of the Vedas is to understand one’s own home, where the Supreme Personality of Godhead lives. Not being interested in their real home, they are illusioned and search after other homes.” (Bhag. [4.29.46-48](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.46))

Narada thus directed King Pracinabarhisat toward his real selfinterest, his return to his eternal home. In his purport to text 48, Srila Prabhupada instructs us how to become purified enough that we too can attain that home: “One can go to the supreme planet (param vrajet) simply by chanting the Hare Krsna mantra. This is especially meant for the people of this age (kaler dosa-nidhe). It is the special advantage of this age that simply by chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra one can become purified of all material contamination and return home, back to Godhead. There is no doubt about this.”

Narada continued: You have become proud of your killing animals in sacrifice. This is foolish. You can never please the Lord by such sacrifices, because He is pleased only by the performance of devotional service. Therefore direct all your activities, as well as your education, toward becoming elevated in Krsna consciousness. Sri Hari is the Supersoul and guide of all embodied living entities. He is the supreme controller of all material activities in material nature. He is also our best friend, and we should take shelter of His lotus feet and make our life auspicious. One who is engaged in devotional service has not the least fear in material existence because the Supreme Lord is the Supersoul and friend of everyone. “One who knows this secret is actually educated, and one thus educated can become the spiritual master of the world. One who is an actually bona fide spiritual master, representative of Krsna, is not different from Krsna.” (Bhag. [4.29.51](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.51))

## Texts 52-55: Narada Presents Another Allegory

In another, far briefer allegory, Narada Muni again explains the points he made in the Puranjana story. Why would Narada restate the same points? Narada used the word guhyam (text 52), “confidential,” hinting that the message he had just delivered in the Puranjana story, although easy to understand on one level, was actually difficult to accept and act on. In his purport to text 52, Srila Prabhupada explains the reason Narada decided to tell another story: “Sri Narada Muni is personally acting as the spiritual master of King Barhisman. It was Narada Muni’s intention that through his instructions the King would immediately give up all engagement in fruitive activity and take to devotional service. However, although the King understood everything, he was still not prepared to give up his engagements. . . . Narada Muni therefore decided to relate another allegory to the King so that he might be induced to give up family life within material existence.”

In the same purport Srila Prabhupada also states that “the King was contemplating sending for his sons, who were away from home executing austerities and penances. After their return, he would entrust his kingdom to them and then leave home.” But Narada’s preaching was strong; he wanted the King to leave home without waiting for his sons to return.

Should we conclude that renunciation is the ultimately goal of Narada’s preaching? No, we can hardly conclude that, since when the King’s sons, the Pracetas, complete their austerities, the Lord will instruct them to return and rule the kingdom. Narada instructed Pracinabarhisat to renounce the kingdom, and Lord Visnu will instruct Pracinabarhisat’s sons to rule. Expert spiritual physicians prescribe different medicines for different individuals.

Narada Muni began his new allegory: Seek out the deer who is eating grass in a beautiful garden with his wife. The deer is attached to his business, and he enjoys the singing of the bumblebees. Just try to understand his position. He does not notice the tiger before him or the hunter with his sharp arrows behind. “Thus the deer’s death is imminent.” (Bhag. [4.29.53](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.53))

Although the scene is superficially pleasant, two agents of death— the hunter and the tiger—are stalking the deer. If the deer should notice and flee from the tiger, it would meet the hunter’s arrows. Running from the hunter would send the deer toward the tiger. This is every human being’s position. We think ourselves happy in the midst of family members, but the tiger of time is stalking us. We are in great danger. In his purport to text 53 Srila Prabhupada notes that although we are aware that death stalks us, we prefer the illusion of safety to the anxiety of life’s precariousness: “Although threatened from all sides, the deer simply eats grass in a nice flower garden, unaware of the danger all around him. All living entities, especially human beings, think themselves very happy in the midst of families. As if living in a flower garden and hearing the sweet humming of bumblebees, everyone is centered around his wife, who is the beauty of family life. The bumblebees’ humming may be compared to the talk of children. The human being, just like the deer, enjoys his family without knowing that before him is the factor of time, which is represented by the tiger.”

Narada explained: The relationship between male and female ultimately brings little satisfaction. Family members distract our mind from the fact that our life is passing day by day. Those who choose to remain in family life should think of the future. They should renounce material desire—even the pleasures of heaven—and take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. By so doing they can override their attraction to material existence. To begin the extrication process, they must free themselves from sex life in all its forms, even as an aspect of religious householder life, because even religious sex fixes the false ego as “enjoyer” rather than as the Lord’s servant. Every single form of self-centeredness binds one to the material world. By living as Krsna’s loving servant, one can be released from material bondage and become situated in one’s eternal position.

For those engrossed in material life, the intelligence given by the mercy of the sadhus—the kind of intelligence King Pracinabarhisat received from Narada—allows one to see the future and escape samsara. Despite its glitter, material reality is desolate.

## Texts 56-59: King Pracinabarhisat Rejects Fruitive Activities and Inquires from Narada about Transmigration of the Soul

When Pracinabarhisat heard Narada’s powerful words, he wondered: My previous teachers instructed me to perform ritualistic Vedic activities and to seek temporary, heavenly pleasure. Narada’s instructions, on the other hand, are fully spiritual, based on the living entity’s eternal service to Krsna.

The King thus concluded that his previous teachers were ignorant of the confidential knowledge Narada had just explained. Coming to his senses, the King rejected his priests’ instructions and engaged fully in devotional service, recognizing it as the ultimate goal of life. Maharaja Pracinabarhisat had listened to Narada Muni’s instructions, accepted them, and then decided to act. In his purport to text 56 Srila Prabhupada describes the King’s actions: “At the present moment the churches, temples and mosques all over the world are not attracting people because foolish priests cannot elevate their followers to the platform of knowledge. Not being aware of the real goal of life, they simply keep their congregations in ignorance. Consequently, those who are well educated have become uninterested in the ritualistic ceremonies. At the same time, they are not benefited with real knowledge. This Krsna consciousness movement is therefore very important for the enlightenment of all classes.”

Pracinabarhisat next inquired about the process of transmigration. He began by asking a question based on his current understanding: Each activity one performs brings results, and one experiences those results in his next life. Yet the body that was used as an instrument in the performance of those acts is dead. So how can one enjoy or suffer reactions for work done by a body that no longer exists?

## Texts 60-69: Narada’s Reply to the King Describes Transmigration of the \<span class="footnote" data-footnote-content="Texts 60-79 provide a detailed description of transmigration. The same subject is discussed in much less detail in Bhagavad-gita, especially in Chapter Fifteen, texts 7-11." data-footnote-number="334" role="footnote"\>Soul\</span\>

Narada Muni replied: The soul gives life to the gross body. The ethereal wrapping on the soul is the subtle body and is composed of mind, intelligence, and false ego. It is through the subtle body that the soul acts in the gross body. When the soul leaves the gross body the body dies, but the soul remains wrapped in the subtle body. Karma is carried in the subtle body, and as the soul transfers to a new body along with the subtle body and the soul’s karma, the living entity feels a sense of continuity.

To illustrate that we have already experienced the existence of the subtle body as separate from the gross body, Narada provides an example: “The living entity, while dreaming, gives up the actual living body. Through the activities of his mind and intelligence, he acts in another body, either as a god or a dog. After giving up this gross body, the living entity enters either an animal body or a demigod’s body on this planet or on another planet. He thus enjoys the results of the actions of his past life.” (Bhag. [4.29.61](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.61))

Srila Prabhupada summarizes the processes of transmigration, liberation, and elevation to Krsna consciousness: “The conclusion is that the subtle body—mind, intelligence and ego—creates an atmosphere with desires and ambitions that the living entity enjoys in the subtle body. Actually the living entity is in the subtle body, even though the gross body apparently changes and even though he inhabits the gross body on various planets. All the activities performed by the living entity in the subtle body are called illusory because they are not permanent. Liberation means getting out of the clutches of the subtle body. ... If we train the subtle body in this life by always thinking about Krsna, we will transfer to Krsnaloka after leaving the gross body.” (Bhag. [4.29.61](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.61), purport)

The art of Krsna consciousness is to engage the subtle body in Krsna’s service. Of course, it is far easier to engage the gross body in service than to control the mind, and therefore the early stages of learning to practice devotional service are centered on engaging the body. Yet aspiring devotees should note that they must ultimately shift their service from merely physical engagement to deep mental, intellectual, and emotional involvement. True devotion means to replace self-centeredness with Krsna-centeredness. In such consciousness one acts only to please Krsna. When desire to please Krsna becomes natural, continuous, and full of love, one is no longer part of this world.Srila Prabhupada continues:

**Thus the change of the gross body is not very important, but the change of the subtle body is important. The Krsna consciousness movement is educating people to enlighten the subtle body. The perfect example in this regard is Ambarisa Maharaja, who always engaged his mind on the lotus feet of Lord Krsna. Sa vai manah krsna-paddravindayoh. Similarly, in this life we should always fix our mind on the lotus feet of Krsna, who is present in His arca-vigraha, the incarnation of the Deity in the temple. We should also always engage in His worship. If we engage our speech in describing the activities of the Lord and our ears in hearing about His pastimes, and if we follow the regulative principles to keep the mind intact for advancing in Krsna consciousness, we shall certainly be elevated to the spiritual platform....**

**The prescription for returning home, back to Godhead, is given by the Lord Himself in Bhagavad-gita (**[**9.34**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/9.34)**): man-mana bhava mad-bhakto, mad-yaji mam namaskuru/ mam evaiyasi yuktvaivam, atmanam mat-parayanah—“Always think of Me and become My devotee. Worship Me and offer your homage unto Me. Being completely absorbed in Me, surely you will come to Me.” (Bhag.** [**4.29.61**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.61)**, purport)**

Narada Muni then continued his example of the dream: Similarly, by the Supersoul’s grace and based on the desires one is carrying in the subtle body, a living entity attains a new gross body after the death of his previous one. One can therefore understand a person’s previous desires by examining his current mental condition, because it was his mentality that carried him from his previous life to his current birth. That same karma and those same desires are reflected in his new body and activities. Therefore, by considering someone’s physical activities, one may come to understand his mind.

Narada Muni has explained that one’s current mental state also in-dicates the nature of future births. Because the mind stores experiences both from the current life and from previous lives, those aspiring to become devotees should fill their minds with loving thoughts of Krsna. According to Narada, one should always engage body, mind, and words in Krsna consciousness and thus prepare to go back to Godhead.In his purport to text 68 Prabhupada points out the importance and method of remembering Krsna:

**The transmigration of the soul is caused by the subtle body, which is the storehouse of all kinds of material desires. Unless one is fully absorbed in Krsna consciousness, material desires will come and go. That is the nature of the mind—thinking, feeling and willing. As long as the mind is not engaged in meditation on the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Krsna, the mind will desire so many material enjoyments. Sensual images are recorded in the mind in chronological order, and they become manifest one after another; therefore the living entity has to accept one body after another. The mind plans material enjoyment, and the gross body serves as the instrument to realize such desires and plans. The mind is the platform onto which all desires come and go.**

**Srila Narottama dasa Thakura therefore sings: guru-mukha-padma-vakya, cittete kariya aikya, ara nd kariha mane asa. Narottama dasa Thakura advises everyone to stick to the principle of carrying out the orders of the spiritual master. One should not desire anything else. If the regulative principles ordered by the spiritual master are followed rigidly, the mind will gradually be trained to desire nothing but the service of Krsna. Such training is the perfection of life.**

By Sri Krsna’s grace one may be shown his entire stock of karma. And, also by Krsna’s grace, that karma—along with all future transmigrations—can then be instantaneously eradicated. Srila Prabhupada states in his purport to text 69: “No living entity is free from the cycle of birth and death unless he takes to Krsna consciousness; therefore in this verse it is clearly stated (sattvaika'nisthe) that when one is fully absorbed in Krsna consciousness, in one stroke he is freed of past and future mental desires. Then, by the grace of the Supreme Lord, everything becomes simultaneously manifest within the mind. In this regard, Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura cites the example of mother Yasoda’s seeing the whole cosmic manifestation within the mouth of Lord Krsna. By the grace of Lord Krsna, mother Yasoda saw all the universes and planets within the mouth of Krsna. Similarly, by the grace of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Krsna, a Krsna conscious person can see all his dormant desires at one time and finish all his future transmigrations. This facility is especially given to the devotee to make his path clear for returning home, back to Godhead.”

Srila Sridhara Svami has commented on text 69, and Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura has quoted this comment almost in its entirety. This commentary further explains the text’s comparison between the devotee’s perceiving the cosmic manifestation as Krsna perceives it and the manifestation of Rahu in the presence of the moon. The Lord sees the universe, and then according to His desire, His devotee can also see it—as in the case of the pastime between Krsna and Mother Yasoda. Similarly, as the presence of Rahu, which is ordinarily beyond one’s perception, can be perceived when it is conjoined with the moon during an eclipse, the perception of the universe as the Lord perceives it, which is ordinarily beyond one’s perception, can be achieved by the Lord’s desire when a devotee is Krsna conscious.

Srila Sridhara Svami adds that “in this pure mind all the objects (visaya) are revealed, which is famous as yogic direct perception.” (Visaya can also mean “objects of material hankering,” which appears to be the meaning Srila Prabhupada has taken and used in his purport.)

## Texts 70-79: Narada Muni Further Details the Mind’s Role in the Soul’s Transmigration

To help clarify the concept of transmigration, Narada Muni offers a second example that demonstrates the existence of the subtle body as separate from the gross: “When the living entity is in deep sleep, when he faints, when there is some great shock on account of severe loss, at the time of death, or when the body temperature is very high, the movement of the life air is arrested. At that time the living entity loses knowledge of identifying the body with the self.” (Bhag. [4.29.71](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.71)) That the subtle body loses its identification with the gross body indicates that the soul’s identification with the gross body is therefore neither fixed nor eternal. One of the goals of Krsna consciousness is to break the connection between the soul and both gross and subtle bodies. Pure devotional service effects that break.

Narada Muni explains: The conditioned soul is habituated to identifying with the “five sense objects, the five sense organs, the five knowledge-acquiring senses and the mind ...” (Bhag. [4.29.74](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.74)) Because of the living entity’s identification with the gross and subtle bodies, these sixteen material expansions place the living entity under the three modes’ control. “By virtue of the processes of the subtle body, the living entity develops and gives up gross bodies. This is known as the transmigration of the soul. Thus the soul becomes subjected to different types of so-called enjoyment, lamentation, fear, happiness and unhappiness.” (Bhag. [4.29.75](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.75))

In his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada describes how to end transmigration: eradicate the soul’s illusory identification with both bodies. Srila Prabhupada writes: “The process of Krsna consciousness, by which one always thinks of Krsna, is the transcendental process by which one can revert to his original, spiritual existence. Devotional service means always thinking of Krsna. Man-mana bhava mad-bhakto, mad-yaji mam namaskuru/ mam evaisyasi satyam te, pratijane priyo ’si me: ‘Always think of Me and become My devotee. Worship Me and offer your homage unto Me. Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend.’ (Bg. [18.65](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.65))”

Thus the illusioned soul, its true nature covered and after having identified with something other than the true self, is whipped by the material energy and forced to comply with the material laws. The mode of goodness forces limited happiness on the soul, passion fills the soul with desires by force, and ignorance forces the soul to lament or become angry. Then the body is driven by these internal states. Yet neither the subtle nor the gross states have anything to do with the soul. A person may watch a movie and for the movie’s duration identify with the hero. Each emotion the hero experiences, the person experiences vicariously. By the end of the movie, the person may have experienced a lifetime of emotions—an experience that affords people relief from the dullness of their own lives. Krsna’s powerful illusory energy then drags the viewer, now filled with the movie character’s fears, desires, and lamentations, to yet another movie for another experience. For the soul, who longs to taste ecstasy in Krsna’s association, each successive illusion is torture—self-torture. And in much the same way, the soul transmigrates from one body to another.

Narada Muni again provids an example: As a caterpillar transfers itself from one leaf to another by grasping the second leaf before leaving the first, so the soul grasps another body through its mental desires before giving up the body it currently inhabits.

Narada Muni presents this example in texts 76-77 and again indicates that one’s next body is based on one’s current desires, for it is the desire-filled mind that carries the soul from gross body to gross body.

Srila Prabhupada explains the “root cause” of both the soul’s attraction to its current body and its future transmigrations: “The root cause of one’s association is the mind. This great Krsna consciousness movement is the greatest boon to human society because it is teaching everyone to think always of Krsna by executing devotional service. In this way, at the end of life, one may be transferred to the association of Krsna. This is technically called nityadila'pravista, entering into the planet Goloka Vrndavana. Bhagavad-gita ([18.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.55)) explains: bhaktya mam ahhijanati, yavan yas casmi tattvatah/ tato mam tattvato jnatva, visate tad-anantaram—‘One can understand the Supreme Personality as He is only by devotional service. And when one is in full consciousness of the Supreme Lord by such devotion, he can enter into the kingdom of God.’ After the mind is completely absorbed in Krsna consciousness, one can enter the planet known as Goloka Vrndavana. To enter the association of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one has to understand Krsna. The process of understanding Krsna is devotional service.” (Bhag. [4.29.76-77](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.76), purport)

And Srila Prabhupada adds: “After understanding Krsna as He is, one can become eligible to enter Krsnaloka and associate with Him. The mind is the cause of such an exalted position. The mind can also get one a body like those of dogs and hogs. To absorb the mind always in Krsna consciousness is therefore the greatest perfection of human life.”’"

Narada Muni then explains: “As long as we desire to enjoy sense gratification, we create material activities. When the living entity acts in the material field, he enjoys the senses, and while enjoying the senses, he creates another series of material activities. In this way the living entity becomes entrapped as a conditioned soul.” (Bhag. [4.29.78](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.78))

Our specific desires create our future material bodies, which then condition and trap us, the eternal soul. Concluding his teachings Narada assures the King: The Supreme Personality of Godhead controls everything in the universe. One in perfect knowledge fearlessly engages himself in the Lord’s service. When one does so, the all-powerful Lord mercifully reveals Himself to His devotee. Therefore, as Srila Prabhupada concludes in his purport to Bhagavatam [4.29.79](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.79): “In Krsna consciousness we can understand that the entire material creation is created by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, maintained by Him, annihilated by Him and absorbed in Him. We are also part and parcel of the Lord. Everything is under the control of the Lord, and therefore our only duty is to surrender unto the Supreme and engage in His transcendental loving service.”

## Texts 80-85: Narada Muni Departs, the King Renounces his Kingdom, and Maitreya Muni Offers Benedictions

Having completed his instructions, Narada returned to Siddha-loka and saintly King Pracinabarhisat left home to undergo austerities at Kapila Muni’s asrama. According to Srila Prabhupada in his purport to text 81, Pracinabarhisat left home even though his sons had not returned from their own austerities: “It is significant that when Maharaja Pracinabarhi was convinced of the goal of life through the instructions of Narada, he did not wait even a moment to see his sons return, but left immediately. There were many things to be done upon the return of his sons, but he simply left them a message. He knew what his prime duty was. He simply left instructions for his sons and went off for the purpose of spiritual advancement. This is the system of Vedic civilization.”

After arriving in Kapilasrama the King engaged constantly in the Lord’s transcendental loving service and attained “a spiritual position qualitatively equal to that of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [4.29.82](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.82))

Maitreya Muni offers the following benedictions to those who hear Narada’s teachings to King Pracinabarhisat: Those who hear this narration and who relate it to others will be liberated from the bodily conception of life. The world will be sanctified and the individuals will attain their spiritual identity. Thus those who tell this allegory to others will be liberated from material bondage.

These instructions award both renunciation and devotional service. Maitreya continues: I heard the allegory of King Puranjana from my spiritual master and it is full of knowledge. Those who can understand the purpose of this allegory will come to understand life after death. “Although one may not understand what transmigra' tion of the soul actually is, one can fully understand it by studying this narration.” (Bhag. [4.29.85](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/29.85))

## Dialogue Seven - The Activities of the Pracetas

## Chapter 24 - Chanting the Song Sung by Lord Siva

## Texts 1-15: Descendants of Prthu Maharaja

After telling Vidura the history of Prthu Maharaja, Maitreya Muni resumes naming Prthu’s descendants—and the descendants of Svayambhuva Manu. Prthu’s son Vijitasva had protected the sacrificial horse from Indra in his father’s one hundredth sacrifice. Because Vijitasva did not kill Indra as the sages had requested, Indra gave him the name Antardhana along with the ability defined by the name —to make himself invisible. After Prthu retired, Antardhana, who was also a great devotee, assumed rulership on his father’s behalf. But Antardhana was not inclined to rule, because whenever he “had to exact taxes, punish his citizens or fine them severely, he was not willing to do so. Consequently he retired from the execution of such duties and engaged himself in the performance of different sacrifices. . . . By thus worshiping the Supreme Lord, Maharaja Antardhana, rapt in ecstasy, attained His planet very easily.” (Bhag. [4.24.6-7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.6))

Antardhana’s son Havirdhana then assumed the throne. Havir-dhana had a powerful son named Barhisat, also known as Pracinabarhisat, who later became king and increased his piety by performing continuous Vedic ritualistic sacrifices.

In his purport to text 10 Srila Prabhupada explains the glorious results of performing sankirtana'yajna throughout the world:

**. . . Maharaja Barhisat dived very deeply into the fruitive activities of sacrifice. This means that as soon as he finished one yajna in one place, he began performing another yajna in the immediate vicinity. At the present moment there is a similar need to perform sankirtana'yajna all over the world. The Krsna consciousness movement has started performing sankirtana'yajna in different places, and it has been experienced that wherever sankirtana'yajna is performed, many thousands of people gather and take part in it. Imperceptible auspiciousness achieved in this connection should be continued all over the world. The members of the Krsna consciousness movement should perform sankirtana' yajnas one after another, so much that all the people of the world will either jokingly or seriously chant Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare, and thus they will derive the benefit of cleansing the heart. The holy name of the Lord (harer nama) is so powerful that whether it is chanted jokingly or seriously the effect of vibrating this transcendental sound will be equally distributed. It is not possible at the present moment to perform repeated yajnas as Maharaja Barhisat performed, but it is within our means to perform sankirtana'yajna, which does not cost anything. One can sit down anywhere and chant Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare. If the surface of the globe is overflooded with the chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra, the people of the world will be very, very happy.**

Maharaja Pracinabarhisat’s ten sons were known as the Pracetas. The King ordered the Pracetas to marry, beget children, and rule the world. In preparation for those responsibilities, he requested them to perform tapasya and worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for whose pleasure all endeavors are meant.

It is interesting to note that the Pracetas were instructed to prepare for their responsibilities as fathers and kings by attaining purity and mental strength through the practice of austerity and devotion. If they did not strengthen the mind by practicing the tolerance tapasya demands, and if they did not purify the mind by learning to consider themselves servants of Krsna, these royal princes of a bygone age would certainly have succumbed to sensuality amid the opulence of palace life. Prabhupada offers us all hope in his purport to text 14 when he emphasizes that chanting Hare Krsna can award us the exalted results the Pracetas attained: “By the grace of Lord Caitanya, one who chants the mahd-mantra (Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare/ Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare) attains the highest perfectional stage, which had previously been attained by people who entered the ocean and executed austerities for ten thousand years. In this age of Kali, if a person does not take advantage of chanting the Hare Krsna mantra, which is offered as a great concession to the fallen human beings of this age, it is to be understood that he is very much bewildered by the illusory energy of the Lord.”

After the Pracetas left home to pursue their father’s order, Krsna, wishing to care for these sincere souls, inspired Lord Siva to give them his association and instruction. After hearing Lord Siva’s words and learning the prayer he taught them, the Pracetas chanted the prayer and ultimately achieved spiritual success.

In his purport to text 15 Srila Prabhupada emphasizes the necessity of accepting the shelter and guidance of a spiritual master: “Lord Siva actually became the spiritual master of the ten sons, and in turn his disciples took his words so seriously that simply by meditating upon his instructions (dhyayantah) they became perfect. This is the secret of success. After being initiated and receiving the orders of the spiritual master, the disciple should unhesitatingly think about the instructions or orders of the spiritual master and should not allow himself to be disturbed by anything else. This is also the verdict of Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, who, while explaining a verse of Bhagavad-gita (vyavasayatmika buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana, Bg. [2.41](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/2.41)), points out that the order of the spiritual master is the life substance of the disciple. The disciple should not consider whether he is going back home, back to Godhead; his first business should be to execute the order of his spiritual master. Thus a disciple should always meditate on the order of the spiritual master, and that is perfectional meditation. Not only should he meditate upon that order, but he should find out the means by which he can perfectly worship and execute it.”

## Texts 16-32: The Pracetas Meet Lord Siva

If one observes powerful persons speaking privately together, he naturally wishes to know the topic of their conversation. Similarly, Vidura’s interest is piqued when he hears about the meeting between Lord Siva and the Pracetas. Therefore he inquires: How did the Pracetas meet Lord Siva? Nothing occurs by chance. What, then, brought about their meeting? What did they talk about?

Maitreya Muni explains that the mood in which the Pracetas left home attracted Lord Siva to bless them: The Pracetas had “accepted the words of their father with heart and soul.” (Bhag. [4.24.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.19)) In his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada describes the seriousness with which the Pracetas accepted their father’s order: “It is the duty of the father, the spiritual master and the king to regulate their subordinates in such a way that they ultimately become fully unalloyed devotees of the Supreme Lord. That is the duty of the superiors, and it is the duty of the subordinates to obey their orders perfectly and in a disciplined way. The word sirasa (‘on their heads’) is also significant, for the Pracetas accepted the orders of their father and carried them on their heads, which means they accepted them in complete surrender.”

While traveling west the Pracetas saw a vast and beautiful reservoir of water similar to an ocean. In his purport to text 20 Srila Prabhupada suggests that the peaceful body of water that afforded them shelter was near the ocean and was most probably a bay. He then compares the mental peace the Pracetas hoped to achieve by taking shelter of this peaceful body of water to the mental peace achieved by faithful disciples who have taken foil shelter of a great soul as their spiritual master: “A devotee’s mind is always calm, quiet and desireless because he is always anyabhilasitd'Stlnyam, having no desire other than to serve Krsna as His personal servant, friend, father, mother or conjugal lover. Due to his association with Krsna, a devotee is always very calm and cool. It is also significant that within that reservoir all the aquatics were also very calm and quiet. Because the disciples of a devotee have taken shelter of a great soul, they become very calm and quiet and are not agitated by the waves of the material world.”

Maitreya Muni next describes the view: “In that great lake there were different types of lotus flowers. Some of them were bluish, and some of them were red. Some of them grew at night, some in the day and some, like the indivara lotus flower, in the evening. Combined together, the lotus flowers filled the lake so full that the lake appeared to be a great mine of such flowers. Consequently, on the shores there were swans and cranes, cakravaka, karandava and other beautiful water birds standing about. There were various trees and creepers on all sides of the lake, and there were mad bumblebees humming all about them. The trees appeared to be very jolly due to the sweet humming of the bumblebees, and the saffron, which was contained in the lotus flowers, was being thrown into the air. These all created such an atmosphere that it appeared as though a festival were taking place there.” (Bhag. [4.24.21-22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.21))

As the Pracetas walked on the secluded shoreline, they were amazed to hear the rhythmic beats of various drums and kettledrums. Then Lord Siva emerged from the water. “His bodily luster was just like molten gold, his throat was bluish, and he had three eyes, which looked very mercifully upon his devotees. He was accompanied by many musicians, who were glorifying him. As soon as the Pracetas saw Lord Siva, they immediately offered their obeisances in great amazement and fell down at the lotus feet of the lord.” (Bhag. [4.24.24-25](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.24))

How had the Pracetas attained Lord Siva’s holy darsana without even trying for it? The Bhagavatam compares the “calm water” from which Lord Siva emerged to the peaceful mind of a devotee. Why is a devotee’s mind calm? Once, when Srila Prabhupada was walking along the beach of the Pacific Ocean he asked his disciples why the ocean was peaceful. When they were unable to respond he said, “Because it is deep.” In his purport to text 20 Srila Prabhupada writes about the depth of a surrendered devotee’s Krsna consciousness: “Even if he suffers some reversals in life, a devotee is never agitated. Therefore whoever takes shelter of a great soul or a great devotee becomes pacified. In the Caitanya-caritamrta (Madhya [19.149](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/19.149)) it is stated: krsna-bhakta—niskama, ataeva ‘santa.’ A devotee of Lord Krsna is always peaceful because he has no desire, whereas the yogis, karmis and jndnis have so many desires to fulfill. One may argue that the devotees have desires, for they wish to go home, back to Godhead, but such a desire does not agitate the mind. Although he wishes to go back to Godhead, a devotee is satisfied in any condition of life. Consequently, the word mahan'Tnanah is used in this verse to indicate that the reservoir of water was as calm and quiet as the mind of a great devotee.”

It is extremely rare to attain Lord Siva’s darsana, but because Lord Siva was pleased with the pious, Vaisnava gentility of the Pracetas, he appeared before them to offer his blessings. He had come simply to show them mercy, because souls surrendered to the all-pervading Supreme Personality of Godhead are dear to him. The Pracetas were thrilled to see Lord Siva, for Lord Siva, the Lord’s guna-avatara in charge of the mode of ignorance, is naturally dear to the devotees.

Lord Siva is an exalted demigod, the best of all Vaisnavas, and a mahajana, one of the twelve great authorities whom all devotees follow. In addition, Lord Siva has his own Vaisnava sampradaya. Although on the Lord’s order he appeared as Sankaracarya to teach impersonal-ism, his final instruction was bhaja govindam, “worship Govinda.” Srila Prabhupada describes the depth of affection between Lord Siva and Krsna’s devotees: “Vaisnavanam yatha sambhuh: Lord Siva is the best of all devotees. Therefore all devotees of Lord Krsna are also devotees of Lord Siva. In Vrndavana there is Lord Siva’s temple called Gopisvara. The gopis used to worship not only Lord Siva but Katyayani, or Durga, as well, but their aim was to attain the favor of Lord Krsna. A devotee of Lord Krsna does not disrespect Lord Siva, but worships Lord Siva as the most exalted devotee of Lord Krsna. Consequently whenever a devotee worships Lord Siva, he prays to Lord Siva to achieve the favor of Krsna, and he does not request material profit.” (Bhag. [4.24.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.30), purport)

In the same purport Srila Prabhupada also glorifies Lord Siva’s love for the Vaisnavas: “Because Lord Siva is a great devotee of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he loves all the devotees of the Supreme Lord. Lord Siva told the Pracetas that because they were devotees of the Lord, he loved them very much. Lord Siva was not kind and merciful only to the Pracetas; anyone who is a devotee of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very dear to Lord Siva. . . . From this text it appears that Lord Siva blesses the asuras simply for the sake of formality. Actually he loves one who is devoted to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

Lord Siva spoke to the Pracetas with affection and respect: I wish all good fortune to you. I know what you are going to do, and so I have shown myself to you just to give you my mercy. Anyone who is surrendered to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Krsna, the supreme controller, is very dear to me. A Vaisnava is rare! “A person who executes his occupational duty properly for one hundred births becomes qualified to occupy the post of Brahma, and if he becomes more qualified, he can approach Lord Siva. A person who is directly surrendered to Lord Krsna, or Visnu, in unalloyed devotional service is immediately promoted to the spiritual planets. Lord Siva and other demigods attain these planets after the destruction of this material world. You are all devotees of the Lord, and as such I appreciate that you are as respectable as the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. I know in this way that the devotees also respect me and that I am dear to them. Thus no one can be as dear to the devotees as I am.” (Bhag. [4.24.29-30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.29))

Lord Siva spoke with gravity, for he wished to impart confidential instructions: I will chant a mantra that is not only transcendental, pure and auspicious, but is the best prayer for anyone who aspires to attain the ultimate goal of life. As I chant, please listen carefully and attentively.

As the Pracetas stood with folded hands, Lord Siva began to chant. Srila Prabhupada writes: “When a mantra is chanted by a great devotee, the mantra becomes more powerful. Although the Hare Krsna maha-mantra is powerful in itself, a disciple upon initiation receives the mantra from his spiritual master, for when the mantra is chanted by the spiritual master, it becomes more powerful. Lord Siva advised the sons of the King to hear him attentively, for inattentive hearing is offensive.” (Bhag. [4.24.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.32), purport)

## Prayers of Lord Siva, Part One

## Texts 33-43: Obeisances to the Supersoul, the Supreme Creator and Controller

With the words jitam ta, “all glories to You!” Lord Siva began his prayers. First, he offered obeisances to the all-pervading Supersoul, Vasudeva (texts 33 and 34), the fully transcendental origin of all creation, and the supreme controller of the senses and sense objects. “Since You are always auspicious for the self-realized, I wish that You be auspicious for me. You are worshipable by virtue of the all-perfect instructions You give. You are the Supersoul; therefore I offer my obeisances unto You as the supreme living being.” (Bhag. [4.24.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.32))

It is natural for a soul to seek shelter, because regardless of one’s external circumstances each soul is tiny and insignificant. Turning to Krsna requires humility; one must acknowledge His greatness and one’s own insignificance. At death all of us will certainly face our minuteness, dependence, and helplessness, but why wait until that moment to acknowledge a constant truth? Thus Lord Siva, teaching both by actions and words, assists one’s return to his relationship with Krsna. The name Siva literally means “auspicious,” but Siva confirmed that although he is auspicious, Krsna is all-auspicious—even for Lord Siva himself. And Krsna is also auspicious for the self-realized, as Lord Siva stated. This implies the etemality of a soul’s individual relationship with Krsna.

In his purport to text 34 Srila Prabhupada explains the reason Lord Siva began his Rudra-gita in this way: “By the grace and help of Lord Vasudeva, who is all-pervading, one can engage his senses in devotional service without deviation, just as the Lord acts without deviation. . . . Consequently any conditioned soul within this material universe can remain completely perfect when he is under the protection of Vasudeva, or when he is engaged in devotional service.” It is the goal of Lord Siva’s prayers to direct us to perfection by placing ourselves under the shelter of the Supersoul, the Personality of Godhead.

Lord Siva then offered his obeisances to Sankarsana, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha (texts 35-38), the masters of the senses and the mind. Thus he has offered obeisances to all four vyuha aspects of the Supreme Lord, who are all worshipable expansions of Visnu with specific functions in the universal creation. Sankarsana causes the subtle material ingredients to integrate, and His potency thus coalesces the universal parts into the universal whole. He also causes those parts to again disberse at times of destruction.

Srila Prabhupada explains this in his purport to text 35, where he calls Sankarsana “the master of integration” and “the destroyer of this world by virtue of His disintegrating energy.” Pradyumna, on the other hand, is “responsible for universal growth and maintenance.” Thus the Lord “in His different features (Vasudeva, Aniruddha, Pradyumna and Sankarsana) maintains both the gross and subtle material elements of this world.” (Bhag. [4.24.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.35), purport)

In his purport to text 36 Srila Prabhupada explains why Aniruddha is specifically respected: “The mind is the director of the senses, and Lord Aniruddha is the director of the mind. In order to execute devotional service, one has to fix his mind on the lotus feet of Krsna; therefore Lord Siva prays to the controller of the mind, Lord Aniruddha, to be pleased to help him engage his mind on the lotus feet of the Lord. It is stated in Bhagavad-gita (9.34): man-mana bhava mad-bhakto mad-yaji mam namaskuru. The mind has to be engaged in meditation on the lotus feet of the Lord in order to execute devotional service. It is also stated in Bhagavad-gita ([15.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/15.15)), mattah smrtir jnanam apohanam ca: from the Lord come remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness. Thus if Lord Aniruddha is pleased, He can help the mind engage in the service of the Lord. . . . Thus Lord Siva prays to Aniruddha to be kind upon him so that his mind will always be in the perfect state of cleanliness and will be engaged in the devotional service of the Lord. Just as fire sterilizes all unclean things, the sungod also keeps everything sterilized, especially dirty things within the mind, thus enabling one to attain elevation to the platform of spiritual understanding.”

The members of the catur-vyuha—Vasudeva, Aniruddha, Pradyumna, and Sankarsana—all have Their devotees. Such worship is legitimate. Yet Lord Siva’s prayers acknowledge these potent four as aspects of Krsna’s all-powerful position as the original Supreme Personality of Godhead (as described in Bhagavatam [1.3.28](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/3.28)). Later, in Canto Ten, readers will meet Krsna directly. He will be a cowherd boy, adorned with a peacock feather and a flute, walking shoeless as He herds His cows. Unless one has learned of His unlimited power and worshipable manifestations, one may think Him ordinary in His svayam-bhagavan feature. Thus Lord Siva, a topmost authority, points out Krsna’s powerful catur-vyuha expansions, because loving and surrendering to Krsna first require a careful understanding of His power. Indeed, Lord Siva will soon mention the supreme object of his prayers by name when he addresses the Lord as namo dharmaya brhate krsnayakuntha'medhase, “Krsna, the greatest of all religious principles, the supreme mind, . . . \[has\] a brain which is never checked by any condition.” (Bhag. [4.24.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.42))

Lord Siva continued to acknowledge the Lord’s greatness in his prayer: “My Lord, as the supreme directing Deity known as Aniruddha, You are the master of the senses and the mind. I therefore offer my obeisances unto You again and again. You are known as Ananta as well as Sankarsana because of Your ability to destroy the whole creation by the blazing fire from Your mouth.” (Bhag. [4.24.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.36))

Again and again Lord Siva offered obeisances and glorified the Lord—as He who awards birth in the higher planetary systems as well as liberation, as the predominating Deity of the moon and master of the Vedas, as He who provides for the ancestors as well as the demigods, and as “the original source of satisfaction for all living entities.” (Bhag. [4.24.38](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.38))

Then Lord Siva again offered his respects to Aniruddha, for Lord Aniruddha is in everyone’s heart and by His blessings one can become free from the material pious obligations that distract one from concentrating only on devotional service. My dear Lord, Lord Siva prayed, You are the gigantic universal form that contains all the living entities’ individual bodies. “You are the maintainer of the three worlds, and as such You maintain the mind, senses, body, and air of life within them. I therefore offer my respectful obeisances unto You.” (Bhag. [4.24.39](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.39))

In his purport to text 39 Srila Prabhupada notes that one cannot perform devotional service without the Lord’s permission: The Lord “can induce every living entity to engage in his real life’s duty with full bodily and mental strength. Thus every living entity should serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead by his prana (life), artha (wealth), intelligence and words. . . . Even though one may desire to engage in the service of the Lord, without sanction one cannot do so. Lord Siva is offering his prayers in so many different ways in order to show living entities how to engage in the devotional service of the Lord.”

Lord Siva prayed: “My dear Lord, by expanding Your transcendental vibrations, You reveal the actual meaning of everything.” (Bhag. [4.24.40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.40)) Srila Prabhupada explains: “Lord Siva is . . . praying to the Personality of Godhead to be kind to us so that simply by chanting the Hare Krsna mantra we can understand everything in both the material and spiritual worlds.” (Bhag. [4.24.40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.40), purport)

Lord Siva then glorified the Lord as the cause of a person’s inclinations and disinclinations and called Him “the topmost of all bestow-ers of benediction ...” He is the cause of all causes and “the supreme mind.” (Bhag. [4.24.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.42))

Siva, the controlling deity of false ego, next described the Lord as the source of “the Rudra principle,” or the source of false ego: “My dear Lord, You are the supreme controller of the worker, sense activities and results of sense activities \[karma\]. Therefore You are the controller of the body, mind and senses. You are also the supreme controller of egotism, known as Rudra. You are the source of knowledge and the activities of the Vedic injunctions.” (Bhag. [4.24.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.43))

Srila Prabhupada explains: “Everyone acts under the dictation of the ego. Therefore Lord Siva is trying to purify false egotism through the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Since Lord Siva, or Rudra, is himself the controller of egotism, he indirectly wants to be purified by the mercy of the Lord so that his real egotism can be awakened. Of course, Lord Rudra is always spiritually awake, but for our benefit he is praying in this way. . . . Lord Siva prays to the Supreme Personality of Godhead so that his mind, senses and words will all turn toward devotional activities only.” (Bhag. 4.24-43, purport)

## The Prayers of Lord Siva, Part Two

## Texts 44-52: Seeing and Serving the Lord’s Glorious Form

The Pracetas have just heard Lord Siva offer many obeisances to glorify God and His unlimited potencies. This clearly indicates that God is the proper object of prayer, shelter, and attainment. They have now understood from Lord Siva that they are fully dependent on God, even for their spiritual advancement. Many spiritualists desire to lose their individuality and merge into God’s greatness, and many religionists tend to stop their search for love of God short of spiritual intimacy, either because they have material desires or because they are constricted by awe. This Lord whom Lord Siva worships does have incredible qualities. But does He exist in any particular form? Can a form contain the diverse, unlimited potencies Lord Siva has just described?

Lord Siva wished to lead the Pracetas closer so that they could see God’s form. Having completed his obeisances, Lord Siva then asked the Lord: “My dear Lord, I wish to see You exactly in the form that Your very dear devotees worship. You have many other forms, but I wish to see Your form that is especially liked by the devotees. Please be merciful upon me and show me that form, for only that form worshiped by the devotees can perfectly satisfy all the demands of the senses.” (Bhag. [4.24.44](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.44))

In this text Lord Siva expresses a desire to see the Lord, but as Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport: “The conclusion is that Lord Siva wants to see Him in complete perfection and not in the impersonalist or voidist way. Although the Lord is one in His various forms (advaitam acyutam anadim), still His form as the young enjoyer of the gopis and companion of the cowherd boys (kisora'murti) is the most perfect form. Thus Vaisnavas accept the form of the Lord in His Vrndavana pastimes as the chief form.”

Krsna’s form is wonderful. His fragrance captivates and maddens, far surpassing the fragrance of the blue lotus (Cc. Antya [15.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/15.22)). His skin is so soft that even the touch of newly grown leaves causes it to change color (NOD, p. 214). To hear His sweet voice is the best use of one’s ears. Indeed, the Bhagavad-gita is a river of nectar flowing from His mouth (NOD, p. 90). To view His form, as the gopis state in Bhagavatam [10.21.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/21.7), is the perfection of the eyes.

Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu summarizes Krsna’s attractiveness to each of the five senses: “Though the hearts of the gopis are like high-standing hills, they are inundated by the waves of the nectarean ocean of Krsna’s beauty. His sweet voice enters their ears and gives them transcendental bliss. The touch of His body is cooler than millions and millions of moons together, and the nectar of His bodily fragrance overfloods the entire world. О My dear friend, that Krsna, who is the son of Nanda Maharaja and whose lips are exactly like nectar, is attracting My five senses by force.” (Cc. Antya [15.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/15.14))

Lord Siva described the form he desired to see: “The Lord’s beauty resembles a dark cloud during the rainy season. As the rainfall glistens, His bodily features also glisten. Indeed, He is the sum total of all beauty. The Lord has four arms and an exquisitely beautiful face with eyes like lotus petals, a beautiful highly raised nose, a mind-attracting smile, a beautiful forehead and equally beautiful and fully decorated ears.” (Bhag. [4.24.45-46](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.45)) The Lord’s shoulders resemble those of a lion, and His chest is marked with Srivatsa, the sign of the goddess of fortune. His abdomen is rippled in three places. His navel is deep, and His waist dark and covered with yellow garments. “My dear Lord, Your two lotus feet are so beautiful that they appear like two blossoming petals of the lotus flower which grows during the autumn season. Indeed, the nails of Your lotus feet emanate such a great effulgence that they immediately dissipate all the darkness in the heart of a conditioned soul. My dear Lord, kindly show me that form of Yours which always dissipates all kinds of darkness in the heart of a devotee. My dear Lord, You are the supreme spiritual master of everyone; therefore all conditioned souls covered with the darkness of ignorance can be enlightened by You as the spiritual master.” (Bhag. [4.24.52](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.52))

In his purport to text 52 Srila Prabhupada uses the lotus as a meta phor to describe Krsna’s feet: “The beauty of the lotus feet of the Lord is compared to the petals of a lotus flower which grows in the autumn season. By nature’s law, in autumn the dirty or muddy waters of rivers and lakes become very clean. At that time the lotus flowers growing in the lakes appear very bright and beautiful. The lotus flower itself is compared to the lotus feet of the Lord, and the petals are compared to the nails of the feet of the Lord. The nails of the feet of the Lord are very bright, as Brahmasamhita testifies. Ananda-cinmaya-sad-ujjvala-vigrahasya: every limb of the transcendental body of the Lord is made of ananda'Cinmaya'Sad'Ujjvala. Thus every limb is eternally bright.”

Although religious paintings often depict a halo around a saint’s head, Krsna’s “halo” or effulgence surrounds His entire body. Srila Prabhupada summarizes the wonderful effect of seeing Krsna’s brilliant effulgence: “As sunshine dissipates the darkness of this material world, the effulgence emanating from the body of the Lord immediately dries up the darkness in the heart of the conditioned soul. In other words, everyone serious about understanding the transcendental science and seeing the transcendental form of the Lord must first of all attempt to see the lotus feet of the Lord by studying the First and Second Cantos of Srimad-Bhagavatam. When one sees the lotus feet of the Lord, all kinds of doubts and fears within the heart are vanquished.... The Lord is the supreme spiritual master, and the bona fide representative of the Supreme Lord is also a spiritual master. The Lord from within enlightens the devotees by the effulgence of the nails of His lotus feet, and His representative, the spiritual master, enlightens from without. Only by thinking of the lotus feet of the Lord and always taking the spiritual master’s advice can one advance in spiritual life and understand Vedic knowledge.” (Bhag. [4.24.52](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.52), purport)

Although the Lord does have a formless aspect apparently devoid of qualities, Lord Siva clearly desired to see His wonderful form, on which the formless rests (brahmano hi pratisthaham). One who hears of the Lord’s form, “seeing” it with his ears through Siva’s words, becomes attracted to wonderful Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

## The Prayers of Lord Siva, Part Three

## Texts 53-59: Devotional Service is the Topmost Process; One Can Attain Devotional Service by Associating with Devotees

In texts 33-43 Lord Siva offered his obeisances in a number of ways to the all-powerful Lord, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, because He was the object of Lord Siva’s prayers. Then in texts 44-52 Lord Siva described the Lord’s form. That the Supreme Lord, the controller of everything, has a form proves that He is a person. Rather than being formless, impersonal, and without qualities, the Lord has a beautiful form and personality and is eternal and ever-attractive. After hearing Lord Siva’s words, one naturally wants to know how to find that wonderful Lord. In texts 53-59, therefore, Lord Siva will describe the glories of devotional service as well as what it is that grants one the privilege of performing it: the association of Vaisnavas.

Lord Siva prayed: “My dear Lord, those who desire to purify their existence must always engage in meditation upon Your lotus feet, as described above. Those who are serious about executing their occupational duties and who want freedom from fear must take to this process of bhakti-yoga.” (Bhag. [4.24.53](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.53))

In his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada reflects on Lord Siva’s words: “Here ... it is indicated that those who are constantly engaged in meditating on the lotus feet of the Lord are certainly purified of the material contamination of the senses and are thus able to see the Supreme Lord face to face.”Then Prabhupada refers to the conversation between Ramananda Raya and Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu as it is described in Sri Caitanya-caritamrta. He explains that after delineating many processes of spiritual advancement, Ramananda Raya ultimately describes bhakti:

**Finally Ramananda Raya referred to the process of bhakti-yoga: sthane sthitah sruti-gatam tanu-van-manobhih (Bhag.** [**10.14.3**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.3)**). Regardless of one’s condition of life, if he practices bhakti-yoga, which begins with hearing (sruti-gatam) the transcendental messages of the Lord through the mouths of devotees, he gradually conquers the unconquerable God.**

**God is known to be unconquerable, but one who submissively hears the words of a self-realized soul conquers the unconquerable. The conclusion is that if one is serious about liberation, he not only should execute the occupational duties of varnasrama-dharma but should also engage in bhakti-yoga, beginning by hearing from a realized soul. This process will help the devotee conquer the unconquerable Supreme Personality of Godhead and become His associate after giving up the material body.**

Lord Siva then explained that the Lord’s service is the most desirable attainment: “My dear Lord, the king in charge of the heavenly kingdom is also desirous of obtaining the ultimate goal of life— devotional service. Similarly, You are the ultimate destination of those who identify themselves with You \[aham brahmasmi\]. However, it is very difficult for them to attain You, whereas a devotee can very easily attain Your Lordship.” (Bhag. [4.24.54](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.54))

Lord Siva thus indicated that devotional service is the ultimate goal of karma (Lord Indra desires to serve the Lord) and jnana (serving Him is the highest destination of those who wish to identify as Brahman \[aham brahmasmi\]). In his purport to text 54 Prabhupada establishes bhakti’s supreme position along with the supreme goal attained by the bhaktas: “Generally, karmis desire elevation to heavenly planets, but King Indra desires to become perfect in bhakti-yoga. Those who identify themselves as aham brahmasmi (‘I am the Supreme Brahman, one with the Absolute Truth’) also ultimately desire to attain perfect liberation in the Vaikuntha planets or Goloka Vrndavana. In Bhagavad-gita ([18.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.55)) it is said: ‘One can understand the Supreme Personality as He is only by devotional service. And when one is in full consciousness of the Supreme Lord by such devotion, he can enter into the kingdom of God.’”

Lord Siva further glorified devotional service, because one can attain the Lord’s lotus feet only by practicing bhakti: “My dear Lord, pure devotional service is even difficult for liberated persons to discharge, but devotional service alone can satisfy You. Who will take to other processes of self-realization if he is actually serious about the perfection of life?” (Bhag. [4.24.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.55))

In his commentary on Bhagavad-gita ([18.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.55)), where Krsna says that He can be known only through devotional service, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura quotes from the Narayana Adhyatma, which indicates that only devotees can know the Lord by the mercy of devotional service, which is His own internal energy: “The Lord, who is eternal and invisible, can be seen through his own sakti. Other than by that means, who can see that Lord of the highest bliss?” Srila Prabhupada therefore writes that “the bhakta is selected as the most suitable candidate to approach the Supreme Personality of Godhead. ... It is very difficult to attain the lotus feet of the Lord by any method other than bhakti-yoga.” (Bhag. [4.24.55](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.55), purport)

Siva’s next prayer points to the Lord’s unlimited time potency, which causes the nondevotees to be afraid but gives the devotees shelter: “Simply by expansion of His eyebrows, invincible time personified can immediately vanquish the entire universe. However, formidable time does not approach the devotee who has taken complete shelter at Your lotus feet.” (Bhag. [4.24.56](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.56))

Materialists struggle to increase and maintain their material assets, yet their struggle is fruitless, because Krsna, through His time factor, effortlessly destroys everything made of matter. His power is so great. On the other hand, the gain the devotees achieve by serving Krsna is eternal, even though it too appears to have been achieved in the realm of time. Whatever the devotees achieve, even if they fall short of perfection, is theirs forever. In his purport to text 56 Srila Prabhupada describes how a devotee defeats the crushing blow of time: “The Lord in the shape of death takes away everything that is created by the conditioned soul. Everything in this material world is subject to perish in due course of time. However, all the strength of time cannot hamper the activities of a devotee, for a devotee takes complete shelter under the lotus feet of the Lord. For this reason only is a devotee free from formidable time. . . . Simply by blinking his eyes, time personified can destroy the entire cosmic manifestation, but he has nothing to do with the devotee. In other words, devotional service which is rendered by the devotee in this lifetime can never be destroyed by time. Such spiritual assets remain unchanged, being beyond the influence of time.”

Devotional service, being eternal, is one’s only true asset. How does one attain it? What causes one to become a devotee? Lord Siva’s next prayer answers that question: “If one by chance associates with a devotee, even for a fraction of a moment, he no longer is subject to attraction by the results of karma or jnana. What interest then can he have in the benedictions of the demigods, who are subject to the laws of birth and death?” (Bhag. [4.24.57](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.57))

Sri Saunaka Rsi’s comments in Bhagavatam [1.18.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/18.13) express similar thoughts to those of Lord Siva: “The value of a moment’s association with the devotee of the Lord cannot even be compared to the attainment of heavenly planets or liberation from matter, and what to speak of worldly benedictions in the form of material prosperity, which are for those who are meant for death.”

In commenting on Bhagavatam [4.24.57](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.57) Srila Sridhara Svami explains that a person who has attained the feet of a great devotee becomes free of all fear. Nothing remains for such a person to attain. Thus association with the Lord’s devotee dances on the heads of all other goals of life.

In his purport to the same text, Srila Prabhupada carries this thought further: “The devotee is in such an exalted position that he is not interested in the actions of karma or jnana. The resultant actions of karma and jnana are so insignificant to a devotee situated on the transcendental platform that he is not in the least interested in them. Bhakti-yoga is sufficient to give the bhakta all happiness. As stated in Srimad-Bhagavatam ([1.2.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.6)): yayatma suprasidati. One can be fully satisfied simply by devotional service, and that is the result of association with a devotee. Without being blessed by a pure devotee, no one can be fully satisfied, nor can anyone understand the transcendental position of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

Knowing that association with exalted devotees is the method to achieve his desired goal, devotional service, Lord Siva then prayerfully requested a blessing: “My dear Lord, Your lotus feet are the cause of all auspicious things and the destroyer of all the contamination of sin. I therefore beg Your Lordship to bless me by the association of Your devotees, who are completely purified by worshiping Your lotus feet and who are so merciful upon the conditioned souls. I think that Your real benediction will be to allow me to associate with such devotees.” (Bhag. [4.24.58](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.58))
