In Bhakti-sandarbha, anuccheda 180, Jiva Gosvami notes that text 58 demonstrates that the Lord does not give mercy to the nondevotees directly, but that He manifests His mercy through His devotees.

One may then wonder about Krsna’s direct mercy toward Arjuna. In his commentary on Bhagavad-gita [18.66](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/18.66), Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura reveals Krsna’s mind. He explains that in awarding Arjuna the required mercy to practice pure devotional service, the Lord expressly states that the qualification to practice bhakti can only be attained through His devotees’ mercy: “Though that is a rule that I Myself made, I am now giving Arjuna that mercy Myself, breaking my own vow, as I did in the fight with Bhisma.”

In the First Shower of Sri Madhurya-kadambini, Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura also discusses the nature of bhakti. He concludes that an individual’s bhakti must have been caused by a devotee’s association: “Since the Lord is subservient to His devotee, He lets His mercy follow after the mercy of His devotee, and there is no irregularity in this.”

In his purport to text 58 Srila Prabhupada delineates the glories of Vaisnavas and their power to preach: “When a person takes his bath in the Ganges, he becomes freed from all life’s contaminations. The Ganges water is celebrated in this way because it emanates from the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Similarly, those who are directly in touch with the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and who are absorbed in the chanting of His glories are freed from all material contamination. Such unalloyed devotees are able to show mercy to the common conditioned souls. Srila Vrndavana dasa Thakura has sung that the devotees of Lord Caitanya are so powerful that each one of them can deliver a universe. In other words, it is the business of devotees to preach the glories of the Lord and deliver all conditioned souls to the platform of suddha'sattva, pure goodness. Here the word su'sattva means suddhasattva, the transcendental stage beyond material goodness. By his exemplary prayers, Lord Siva teaches us that our best course is to take shelter of Lord Visnu and His Vaisnava devotees.”

What results when one attains devotional service by associating with devotees? Lord Siva continued: “The devotee whose heart has been completely cleansed by the process of devotional service and who is favored by Bhaktidevi does not become bewildered by the external energy, which is just like a dark well. Being completely cleansed of all material contamination in this way, a devotee is able to understand very happily Your name, fame, form, activities, etc.” (Bhag. [4.24.59](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.59))By the mercy of devotees one becomes purified and can attain Krsna. Srila Prabhupada further details the process in his purport to text 59:

**Simply by the association of pure devotees one can understand the transcendental name, fame, quality and activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu has repeatedly said: ‘sadhu'sanga’, ‘sadhu-sanga’—sarva-sastre kaya lava-matra sadhu-sange sarva-siddhi haya (Cc., Madhya** [**22.54**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.54)**).**

**Simply by associating with a pure devotee, one becomes wonderfully advanced in Krsna consciousness. Sadhu-sanga, or association with a devotee, means always engaging in Krsna consciousness by chanting the Hare Krsna mantra and by acting for Krsna. Specifically, chanting the Hare Krsna mantra purifies one, and this chanting is therefore recommended by Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. CetO'darpana'rnarjariaTn: by chanting the names of Krsna, the mirror of the heart is cleansed, and the devotee loses interest in everything external. When one is influenced by the external energy of the Lord, his heart is impure. When one’s heart is not pure, he cannot see how things are related to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. . . . One who is pure in heart is never attracted by the external energy, which urges the individual soul to try to dominate material nature. . . . When a devotee strictly follows the rules and regulations, Bhaktidevi becomes very much satisfied with him, and at that time he is never disturbed by anything external.**

## Prayers of Lord Siva, Part Four

## Texts 60-68: The Relationship Between the Lord and the Material Creation—The Lord is Present Everywhere as the Supersoul, as Time, and through His Energies. Thus He is the Only Object of Worship

Lord Siva next described the Lord from the viewpoint that he generally experiences Him: as He who manifests potent energies in relationship to the material world as creator, maintainer, and destroyer. Lord Siva glorified Him as the ultimate source and therefore nondifferent from the impersonal Brahman, who “spreads everywhere, like the sunshine or the sky. And that impersonal Brahman, which spreads throughout the universe and in which the entire universe is manifested, is You. My dear Lord, You have manifold energies, and these energies are manifested in manifold forms. With such energies You have also created this cosmic manifestation, and although You maintain it as if it were permanent, You ultimately annihilate it. Although You are never disturbed by such changes and alterations, the living entities are disturbed by them, and therefore they find the cosmic manifestation to be different or separated from You. My Lord, You are always independent, and I can clearly see this fact.” (Bhag. [4.24.60-61](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.60))

Impersonalists are correct when they say that all matter rests on Brahman, the spiritual energy; they are incorrect in that they misconceive the Brahman, limiting the Supreme Spirit to something impersonal. They don’t understand that it is Krsna’s impersonal effulgence on which everything is resting. In his purport to text 60 Prabhupada writes: “In Vedic literature it is said that everything is Brahman and nothing else. The whole cosmic manifestation rests on the Brahman effulgence. The impersonalists, however, cannot understand how such a huge cosmic manifestation can rest on a person.”

Everything rests on the Lord. He is independent of everything, although nothing is independent of Him. Everything in existence is His energy. Yet conditioned souls, influenced by one of His energies (the maya-sakti), fail to experience Him anywhere.

Srila Prabhupada explains that by the maya-sakti “some living entities are conditioned in this material world, and thus they think themselves separated from the Supreme Lord. Due to their contact with the material energy, their existence is always troublesome. Being always in distress, the conditioned soul considers the material energy to be very much disturbing. This fact is explained by a Vaisnava kavi, or poet: ‘krsna bhuk’ sei jiva anadi'bahirmukha, ataeva maya tare deya samsara'duhkha. When the living entity forgets the Supreme Lord and wants to enjoy himself independently, imitating the Supreme Lord, he is captured by the false notion that he is the enjoyer and is separated from the Supreme Lord. This material energy is therefore very much troublesome to the spiritual energy, the living entity . . .” (Bhag. [4.24.61](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.61), purport)

Again, on the Lord’s Brahman energy rests the totality of everchanging material forms, which ceaselessly shift and transform by the potency of the time factor. Conditioned souls, influenced by maya-sakti, seek stability and security in these shifting sands but are continually frustrated. It is interesting to note that devotees, although not so different from conditioned souls in one sense, are untouched and untroubled by the Lord’s mayd-sakti. Is this because Krsna is partial? No, the devotees are free from maya because they take shelter only of Krsna. Srila Prabhupada continues: “\[B\]ecause a Vaisnava philosopher is in full knowledge of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he finds no disturbance even in the material energy. This is because he knows how to utilize the material energy for the service of the Lord. In the government, the criminal department and civil department may appear different in the eyes of the citizens, but in the eyes of the government both departments are one and the same. The criminal department is troublesome for the criminal but not for the obedient citizen. Similarly, this material energy is troublesome for the conditioned soul, but it has nothing to do with the liberated souls who are engaged in the service of the Lord.” (Bhag. [4.24.61](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.61), purport)

Jiva Gosvami comments that Lord Siva speaks these seven verses, beginning with yatredam (text 60), to show that without the mercy of bhakti-yoga, the true principles of Brahman, Bhagavan, Paramatma, and time are extremely difficult to understand. He explains that text 60 indicates Brahman by describing that Brahman spreads everywhere and yet is unrecognizably the Lord. Text 61 indicates that people are disturbed by maya, seeing different forms, but they do not see Bhagavan. Texts 62-64 indicate that as the Paramatma, the Lord as the universal form creates the entire universe and offers “honeycombs” of pleasure to the conditioned souls, who are in turn disturbed by other “bees.” Texts 65 and 66 indicate Krsna’s form as unbearable time, for that form destroys and scatters everything. Krsna in the form of time strikes down greedy planners just as a snake seizes a mouse.

Lord Siva continued his prayers: Those who worship the universal form, Paramatma, and the demigods through sacrifices ultimately worship You alone, for You are expanded into everything. “It is stated both in the Vedas and in the sastras that are corollaries of the Vedas, and indeed everywhere, that it is only You who are to be worshiped. That is the expert version of all the Vedas. My dear Lord, You are the only Supreme Person, the cause of all causes.” (Bhag. [4.24.62-63](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.62)) Through Your energy (the three modes of material nature), You cause another energy, the total material energy, the mahan, to manifest its varieties in the material creation.

The division of Krsna’s energy into categories like matter and spirit is not a concept artificially imposed on the “oneness of existence.” Rather, as Srila Prabhupada explains in his purport to text 63, the various energies are true creations of the Lord. Still, pure devotees live beyond these distinctions, for even if they appear to be situated in the Lord’s material energy, they are always and only with Krsna by dint of their Krsna consciousness. As Srila Prabhupada explains: “There is only a material world for those who want to imitate the Lord and become enjoyers. Indeed, the material world is nothing but forgetfulness of the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, the creator of everything. The distinction between matter and spirit is created by the sleeping energy of the Lord when the Lord wants to give some facility to those living entities who want to imitate the Lord in His enjoyment. It is only for them that this material world is created by the dormant energy of the Lord.” But no matter what categories those influenced by maya see, Krsna is the ultimate cause, the origin of everything.

After creating the universe, how does the Lord exhibit His presence in it? Lord Siva answers this question in text 64 by noting His presence in the form of His energy (the four kinds of living beings), as Paramatma (the Lord who lives in the living entities’ hearts and sanctions their actions), and in text 65 as time (the unstoppable destroyer), which “scatters everything, exactly as the wind scatters clouds in the sky.” As time the Lord alertly swallows all materialistic living entities, who, acting greedily for selfish sense pleasure, try to usurp His position as the Supreme Enjoyer.

In his purports to texts 64-66, Srila Prabhupada adds details to our understanding of the Lord’s continual presence in the universe: “Remaining within the hearts of all living entities, the Lord bestows remembrance by which the living entities can enjoy certain things. Thus the living entities create their enjoyable honeycombs and then enjoy them. The example of the bees is appropriate because when bees try to enjoy their honeycomb, they have to suffer the bites of other bees. Because bees bite one another when they enjoy honey, they are not exclusively enjoying the sweetness of the honey, for there is also suffering.... Thus the Lord simply witnesses and gives the living entity sanction for sense enjoyment.” (Bhag. [4.24.64](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.64), purport)

And: “Although we do not see the hand of the Supreme Lord directly, we can feel the presence of that hand through the Lord’s process of destruction. We can see the clouds scattered by the wind, although we cannot see how this is being done because it is not possible to see the wind. Similarly, although we do not directly see the Supreme Personality of Godhead, we can see that He controls the process of destruction. The destructive process is going on fiercely under the control of the Lord, but the atheists cannot see it.” (Bhag. [4.24.65](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.65), purport)

From the purport to text 66: “Everything is enacted by the laws of nature, and these laws are under the direction of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The atheists, or unintelligent men, do not know this. They are busy making their own plans, and big nations are busy expanding their empires. And yet we know that in due course of time many empires have come into existence and been destroyed. Many aristocratic families were created by people in their extreme madness, but we can see that in the course of time those families and empires have all been destroyed. But still the foolish atheists do not accept the supreme authority of the Lord. Such foolish people unnecessarily concoct their own duties without referring to the supreme authority of the Lord. ... According to the laws of nature, which are backed by the Lord, nothing can be permanent within this material world; therefore everyone should be allowed to take shelter of the Absolute in order to be saved. ... If one wants peace of mind and tranquility in society, he must accept the fact that the real enjoyer is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Lord is the proprietor of everything all over the universe, and He is the supreme friend of all living entities as well. By understanding this, people can become happy and peaceful individually and collectively.”

Lord Siva’s prayers conclude: “My dear Lord, any learned person knows that unless he worships You, his entire life is spoiled. Knowing this, how could he give up worshiping Your lotus feet? Even our father and spiritual master, Lord Brahma, unhesitatingly worshiped You, and the fourteen Manus followed in his footsteps. My dear Lord, all actually learned persons know You as the Supreme Brahman and the Supersoul. Although the entire universe is afraid of Lord Rudra, who ultimately annihilates everything, for the learned devotees You are the fearless destination of all.” (Bhag. [4.24.67-68](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.67))

## Texts 69-79: Instructions on Reciting the Prayer, and a Description of its Glories

Having concluded his prayer, Lord Siva next suggested how the Pracetas could best take advantage of the prayer: My dear princes, execute your occupational duty as kings with a pure heart. Chant this prayer, fixing your mind on the Lord’s lotus feet. That will bring you all good fortune, for the Lord will be pleased with you. О sons of the king, Lord Hari, is situated in everyone’s heart and is also in your hearts. Therefore chant the glories of the Lord and always meditate on Him.

Srila Prabhupada’s purports to both these texts are powerful. In his purport to text 69 he describes the power of prayer:

**Simply by offering prayers to the Supreme Lord one can become perfect, even though engaged in his occupational duty. The real purpose of life is to become a devotee of the Lord. It does not matter where one is situated. Whether one is a brahmana, ksatriya, vaisya, sudra, American, Englishman, Indian, etc., one can execute devotional service anywhere and everywhere in the material existence simply by offering prayers unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Hare Krsna maha-mantra is also a prayer, for a prayer addresses the Supreme Personality of Godhead by His name and invokes good fortune by petitioning the Lord to allow one to engage in His devotional service. The Hare Krsna maha-mantra also says, “My dear Lord Krsna, my dear Lord Rama, О energy of the Lord, Hare, kindly engage me in Your service.” Although one may be situated in a lowly position, he can execute devotional service under any circumstance, as stated, ahaituky apratihata: “Devotional service cannot be checked by any material condition.” (Bhag.** [**1.2.6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.6)**) Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu also recommended this process: jnane prayasam udapasya namanta eva, jivanti san-mukharitam bhavadiya-vartam/ sthane sthitah sruti-gatam tanu-van-manobhir, ye prayaso 'jitajito ’py asi tais tri-lokyam (Bhag.** [**10.14.3**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-10/14.3)**). One may remain situated in his own place or his own occupational duty and still lend his ear to receive the message of the Lord from realized souls. The Krsna conscious movement is based on this principle, and we are opening centers all over the world to give everyone a chance to hear the message of Lord Krsna in order to go back home, back to Godhead.**

In his purport to text 70 Srila Prabhupada glorifies the continuous chanting of Krsna’s names: “The word asakrt is significant, for it means not just for a few minutes but continuously. That is the instruction given by Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu in His Siksastaka 3. Kirtaniyah sada harih: ‘The holy name of the Lord should be chanted twenty-four hours daily.’ Therefore in this Krsna consciousness movement we request the devotees to chant at least sixteen rounds on their beads daily. Actually one has to chant twenty-four hours daily, just like Thakura Haridasa, who was chanting the Hare Krsna mantra three hundred thousand times daily. Indeed, he had no other business.”

Sri Jiva Gosvami also comments on these texts in his Bhakti' sandarbha, anuccheda 50. According to Sri Jiva, Lord Siva is saying, “You should worship (pujayadhvam) Lord Hari (tarn) and not perform other things. This means that one should not perform ordinary material duties. “You should glorify (gmantah) Him and meditate on (dhyayantah) Him, the Supersoul situated in everyone’s heart (dtma-stham bhutesv avasthitam atmanam). Don’t focus your minds and words on anything but Him. Always (asakrt) worship Him, and do not interrupt your worship by engaging in any other activity. As soon as one act of worship is complete, immediately begin another.”

Lord Siva said: “All of you should take this important stotra within your minds and promise to keep it in order to become great sages.” (Bhag. [4.24.71](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.71))

Lord Siva continued: Lord Brahma first spoke these prayers to the subordinate creators of the universe to caution us, for he desired us to remain ever mindful of our relationship with the Supreme Creator as we performed our duties. We recited these prayers and have remained free from ignorance because of them.

Srila Prabhupada broadens the audience of Lord Brahma’s caution from the subordinate creators to all those with material responsibilities: “The material creation means material engagement, but material engagements can be counteracted if we always remember our relationship with the Lord as that relationship is described in these prayers recited by Lord Siva. In this way we can remain constantly in touch with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Thus despite our engagement in the creation, we cannot be deviated from the path of Krsna consciousness. The Krsna consciousness movement is especially meant for this purpose. In this material world everyone is engaged in some particular occupational duty which is prescribed in the varnasrama-dharma. Brahmanas, ksatriyas, vaisyas, siidras and everyone are engaged in their occupational duty, but if one remembers his first duty—keeping in constant contact with the Supreme Personality of Godhead— everything will be successful.” (Bhag. [4.4.72](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/4.72), purport)

Lord Siva glorified the potency of the prayer he had just spoken: “A devotee of Lord Krsna whose mind is always absorbed in Him, who with great attention and reverence chants this stotra \[prayer\], will achieve the greatest perfection of life without delay. In this material world there are different types of achievement, but of all of them the achievement of knowledge is considered to be the highest because one can cross the ocean of nescience only on the boat of knowledge.

Otherwise the ocean is impassable. Although rendering devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead and worshiping Him are very difficult, if one vibrates or simply reads this stotra composed and sung by me, he will very easily be able to invoke the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [4.24.74-76](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.74))

Lord Siva then spoke of the difficulty conditioned souls encounter while attempting to devote themselves fully to the Lord. It is as easy to understand the cause of the trouble as it is difficult to eliminate it: we are habituated to self-centeredness. We forget Krsna in our absorption in ourselves. When covered by false ego we feel separate from Krsna, our dearmost; He appears unapproachable and far away. How, then, can something so ultimate—the removal of the prime covering around the soul—become easy? In his purport to text 76 Srila Prabhupada illuminates the path: “To become a devotee of Lord Krsna, Vasudeva, is very, very difficult. The word especially used in this connection is duraradhyam. The worship of the demigods is not very difficult, but becoming a devotee of Lord Vasudeva, Krsna, is not so easy. However, if one adheres to the principles and follows in the footsteps of the higher authorities, as advised by Lord Siva, one can easily become a devotee of Lord Vasudeva. This is also confirmed by Prahlada Maharaja. Devotional service cannot be practiced by a mental speculator. Devotional service is a special attainment which can be acquired only by a person who has surrendered unto a pure devotee. As confirmed by Prahlada Maharaja, mahiyasam pada'rajo-’bhisekaTh niskincananam na vrnita yavat: ‘Unless one accepts the dust of the lotus feet of a pure devotee, who is free from all material contamination, one cannot enter into the devotional service of the Lord.’ (Bhag. [7.5.32](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/5.32))”

Lord Siva concluded: Those who sing the song I have sung can please the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Then, becoming fixed in devotional service to the Lord, such devotees can acquire whatever they want from Him. “A devotee who rises early in the morning and with folded hands chants these prayers sung by Lord Siva and gives facility to others to hear them certainly becomes free from all bondage to fruitive activities. My dear sons of the King, the prayers I have recited to you are meant for pleasing the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Supersoul. I advise you to recite these prayers, which are as effective as great austerities. In this way, when you are mature, your life will be successful, and you will certainly achieve all your desired objectives without fail.” (Bhag. [4.24.78-79](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.78))

Srila Prabhupada ends the twenty-fourth chapter with a short purport: “If we persistently engage in devotional service, certainly all our desires will be fulfilled in due course of time.” (Bhag. [4.24.79](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.79), purport)

## Chapter 30 - The Activities of the Pracetas

## Texts 1-21: The Pracetas Chant the Song Sung by Lord Siva and Attain Lord Visnu’s Darsana

After hearing the Rudra'gita, the Pracetas worshiped Lord Siva with respect and entered the calm lake waters to begin practicing austerity. There they again and again recited the prayers they had learned as they stood in the water for ten thousand years.

Srila Prabhupada speaks of their austerities: “Sometimes great sages and ascetics enter the Himalaya Mountains in order to find seclusion from the turmoil of the world. It appears, however, that all the Pracetas, the sons of Pracinabarhi, entered the depths of the ocean to perform austerity in a secluded place. Since they performed austerities for ten thousand years, this incident took place in the Satya-yuga, when people used to live for a hundred thousand years.” (Bhag. [4.24.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.14), purport)

At one point, when their father, King Pracinabarhisat, had initiated yet another Vedic sacrifice, Narada Muni compassionately instructed the King and convinced him of the real purpose of life. Without waiting for his sons to return to rule his kingdom, Pracinabarhisat renounced his throne to seek out the Absolute Truth, leaving instructions with his ministers for his sons to care for the citizens. We have already heard Narada’s powerful instructions (chapters Twenty-five through Twenty-nine); now we will hear about the Pracetas’ activities after they completed their austerities.

Chapter Thirty opens with Vidura inquiring from Maitreya Muni about what the Pracetas attained in their present and future lives by chanting the Rudra'gita. Maitreya Muni replies: “The sons of King Pracinabarhi, known as the Pracetas, underwent severe austerities within the seawater to carry out the order of their father. By chanting and repeating the mantras given by Lord Siva, they were able to satisfy Lord Visnu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [4.30.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.3))

In his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada emphasizes the power of reciting prayers composed by great devotees: “One can offer prayers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead directly, but if one repeats the prayers offered by great devotees like Lord Siva and Lord Brahma, or if one follows in the footsteps of great personalities, one can please the Supreme Personality of Godhead very easily.”

Still, rote repetition does not allow one to either understand or enter the mood of those great souls. The prayers should be recited with attention, because that allows the words of great souls to affect us.

After chanting Lord Siva’s prayers for ten thousand years, the Pracetas evoked the mercy of the Supreme Lord, who then revealed to them His pleasing form.

Tapasya is by definition difficult to practice. Even performing relatively easy service becomes austere if it must be performed day after day. Devotees should remain conscious of who they are trying to please by their devotional austerities. In his purport to text 4 Srila Prabhupada solaces those who are seriously aspiring to act for the Lord’s pleasure: “The Supreme Personality of Godhead appreciated the austerities undergone by the Pracetas, and He finally appeared before them in a pleasing form. Thus they all became satisfied and forgot the austerities they underwent. In the material world, if one is successful after hard labor, he is very pleased. Similarly, the devotee forgets all his labors and austerities as soon as he contacts the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

Because it is especially difficult to concentrate in Kali-yuga Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu suggests that devotees should accompany all their activities with chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra. Srila Prabhupada writes: “Because the people of this age are fallen, the Lord is kind enough to give them the easiest method. Simply by chanting the Hare Krsna mantra, one can attain the same results. However, as Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu points out, we are so unfortunate that we are not even attracted to chanting the maha-mantra—Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare / Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare.”

The Lord appeared before the Pracetas in His attractive yellow garments, His bodily effulgence dissipating the darkness of the universe. “The Lord’s face was very beautiful, and His head was decorated with a shining helmet and golden ornaments. The helmet was dazzling and was very beautifully situated on His head.” (Bhag. [4.30.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.6)) In each of His eight hands he held a different implement: a club, disc, conch, lotus, arrow, bow, trident, and snake. As a king does not travel alone, the Lord appeared with the demigods, great sages, and sadhus, all of whom were engaged in serving Him. “Garuda, the carrier of the Lord, glorified the Lord with Vedic hymns by flapping his wings.” (Bhag. [4.30.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.6))

In his commentary on Bhagavatam [4.30.1-7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.1), Sri Jiva Gosvami discusses the Lord’s intention in appearing with eight arms although the Pracetas had meditated on Him in His four-armed form. Sri Jiva writes: “I have not appeared at this time to bestow on you that which you desired, but I have come only to console you through My descent.”

The Lord glanced mercifully at the Pracetas, His fully surrendered devotees, and addressed them in a voice as deep as thunder: “My dear sons of the King, I am very much pleased by the friendly relationships among you. All of you are engaged in one occupation—devotional service. I am so pleased with your mutual friendship that I wish you all good fortune. Now you may ask a benediction of Me.” (Bhag. [4.30.8](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.8))

Srila Prabhupada writes in his purport to this text: “Since the sons of King Pracinabarhisat were all united in Krsna consciousness, the Lord was very pleased with them. Each and every one of the sons of King Pracinabarhisat was an individual soul, but they were united in offering transcendental service to the Lord. The unity of the individual souls attempting to satisfy the Supreme Lord or rendering service to the Lord is real unity. In the material world such unity is not possible. Even though people may officially unite, they all have different interests. In the United Nations, for instance, all the nations have their particular national ambitions, and consequently they cannot be united. Disunity between individual souls is so strong within this material world that even in a society of Krsna consciousness, members sometimes appear disunited due to their having different opinions and leaning toward material things. Actually, in Krsna consciousness there cannot be two opinions. There is only one goal: to serve Krsna to one’s best ability. If there is some disagreement over service, such disagreement is to be taken as spiritual. Those who are actually engaged in the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead cannot be disunited in any circumstance. This makes the Supreme Personality of Godhead very happy and willing to award all kinds of benediction to His devotees...”

Cooperation is one of the most difficult austerities devotees must perform in Kali-yuga, and cooperation was the subject of one of Prabhupada’s final comments before leaving this world. Tamal Krishna Goswami writes: “Prabhupada emphasized that ‘Your love for me will be tested how after my departure you maintain this institution. We have glamor and people are feeling our weight. This should be maintained. Not like Gaudiya Math. After Guru Maharaja’s departure so many acaryas came up.’” (TKG’s Diary: Prabhupada’s Final Days, p. 45)

In a Mayapur room conversation on March 16, 1976, he also spoke about cooperation: “Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu—He is God Himself, Krsna Himself—He felt alone, unable to do this task. He felt this way. So this is the position. You are cooperating; therefore I am getting the credit. Otherwise, alone what could I do? Ekaki amara nahi paya bolo. Caitanya Mahaprabhu Himself wanted our cooperation. He is God, Krsna. And therefore cooperation is a very important thing. Nobody should think that ‘I have got so great ability. I can do.’ No. It is simply by cooperation we can do a very big thing. ‘United we stand; divided we fall.’ This is our \[motto\] ... So be strong in pushing on Krsna consciousness, and Krsna will help. He is the strongest. Still, we must be combined together. Sankirtana. Sankirtana means many men combined together chanting. That is sankirtana. Otherwise kirtana. Sankirtana. Bahubhir militva kirtayatiti sankirtanam. Bahu: bahu means many combined together. That is Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s mission, combined together.”

Pleased with the Pracetas, the Lord glorified them and then blessed with a special benediction those who even think of them: “Those who remember you every evening of every day will become friendly with their brothers and with all other living entities. Those who will offer Me the prayers composed by Lord Siva, both in the morning and in the evening, will be given benedictions by Me. In this way they can both fulfill their desires and attain good intelligence.” (Bhag. [4.30.9-10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.9))

Still responding to Vidura’s inquiry in text 2 Maitreya Muni repeats the Lord’s words: “Because you have with pleasure accepted within your hearts the orders of your father and have executed those orders very faithfully, your attractive qualities will be celebrated all over the world. You will have a nice son, who will be in no way inferior to Lord Brahma. Consequently, he will be very famous all over the universe, and the sons and grandsons generated by him will fill the three worlds.” (Bhag. [4.30.11-12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.11)) Soon you will be offered beautiful Marisa as your wife. Please accept her. Through her you will populate the universe. Marisa is the daughter of the heavenly Apsara Pramloca and the sage Kandu. She was later cared for by the trees and nurtured by the moon god. Empowered by Me she will be able to satisfy and care for each of you, her ten husbands.

The Lord blessed the Pracetas further: You will rule without hindrance or loss of physical strength for one million celestial years. Then you will develop pure devotional service and attain the spiritual world.

You should understand that I am the ultimate beneficiary of all activities. Knowing this, perform your work, offering Me the results. Become absorbed in hearing krsna-katha. By living in this way, even though you are involved in family life, you will remain unaffected by the results of your actions. Due to your constant devotional service, your actions will be above the modes of material nature and you will remain free of bewilderment, in touch with the Supersoul, and focused on the brahma-bhuta platform.

In his purport to text 19 Srila Prabhupada explains how bhakti allows one to transcend the material world while living in it: “This Krsna consciousness movement is . . . the greatest boon to humanity because it keeps one always engaged in Krsna’s service. The devotees think of Krsna, act for Krsna, eat for Krsna, sleep for Krsna and work for Krsna. Thus everything is engaged in the service of Krsna. A total life in Krsna consciousness saves one from material contamination. As stated by Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Gosvami Maharaja: krsna-bhajane уaha haya anukula, visaya baliya tyage taha haya bhula. If one is so expert that he can engage everything or dovetail everything in the service of the Lord, to give up the material world would be a great blunder. One should learn how to dovetail everything in the service of the Lord, for everything is connected to Krsna. That is the real purpose of life and secret of success. ... If one is placed in material opulence due to the special mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he should not consider that opulence a cause for bondage. When a mature devotee is blessed with material opulence, he does not become affected adversely, for he knows how to employ material opulence in the service of the Lord.”

The Lord continued: By your devotional service you will automatically receive the benefits offered by the paths of karma, jnana, and yoga, and the Supersoul will both help and inspire you.

Srila Prabhupada describes how the Supersoul helps a devotee: “In Bhagavad-gita the Lord says that He is situated in everyone’s heart and that He helps the living entity forget and remember. By the grace of the Lord, the devotee gets inspiration. Tesam satata-yuktanam, bhajatam priti-purvakam/dadami buddhi-yogam tam, yena mam upayanti te: ‘To those who are constantly devoted and worship Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.’ (Bg. [10.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/10.10))... The Supersoul gives instructions to the sincere, unalloyed devotee on how he can progress more and more in approaching the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Srila Jiva Gosvami in this connection says that the Supersoul, the plenary expansion of the Personality of Godhead, exists in everyone’s heart, but in the heart of the devotee He reveals Himself as ever-increasingly new. Being inspired by Him, the devotee experiences increased transcendental bliss in the execution of his devotional service.” (Bhag. [4.30.20](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.20), purport)

When one sees an increase in bhakti or the inspiration to serve Krsna in another, one should recognize it as a result of Krsna’s mercy. The inspiration to preach is another sign of having received Krsna’s mercy. Srila Prabhupada’s words in this regard are powerful: “My Guru Maharaja used to say, prana ache yara sei hetu pracara. A person can become a preacher if he has got life. A dead man cannot become a preacher. So you must be very enthusiastic that ‘I shall preach the glories of the Lord to my best capacity.’ It is not that one has to become a very learned scholar to become a preacher. Simply it requires enthusiasm, ‘My Lord is so great, so kind, so beautiful, so wonderful. So I must speak something about my Lord.’ This is the qualification, enthusiasm. You may not know Krsna very perfectly. It is not possible to know Krsna very perfectly. Krsna is unlimited. We cannot know Krsna cent percent. That is not possible. But Krsna reveals as far as possible you can understand. So if we are sincere servant of Krsna, utsahan, and if we serve patiently, then Krsna reveals \[Himself\].” (Lecture, NOD, Vrndavana, October 1972)

Maitreya Muni then says: “After the Personality of Godhead spoke thus, the Pracetas began to offer Him prayers. The Lord is the be-stower of all success in life and is the supreme benefactor. He is also the supreme friend who takes away all miserable conditions experienced by a devotee. In a faltering voice, due to ecstasy, the Pracetas began to offer prayers. They were purified by the presence of the Lord, who was before them face to face.” (Bhag. [4.30.21](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.21))

## Texts 22-32: The Pracetas Offer Obeisances to the Lord in Prayer

In his purport to text 21 Srila Prabhupada compares the Lord’s presence before the Pracetas to Krsna’s presence before a pure devotee who is chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra: “Because the Lord appeared before them, naturally all the contaminations of the material qualities of rajas and tamas completely disappeared. Similarly, when an unalloyed devotee chants the Hare Krsna maha-mantra, he is also purified of all material contamination because the name of the Lord and the Lord are identical. . . . The holy name of the Lord is the Lord Himself. If one chants and hears, he becomes purified. Gradually all material contamination disappears. The Pracetas were already purified due to the Lord’s presence before them, and they could therefore offer the proper prayers with folded hands.”

The Pracetas said: “Dear Lord, You relieve all kinds of material distress. Your magnanimous transcendental qualities and holy name are all-auspicious. This conclusion is already settled. You can go faster than the speed of mind and words. You cannot be perceived by material senses. We therefore offer You respectful obeisances again and again.” (Bhag. [4.30.22](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.22))

Noting His transcendental form, they prayed: “When the mind is fixed upon You, the world of duality, although a place for material enjoyment, appears meaningless. Your transcendental form is full of transcendental bliss. We therefore offer our respects unto You.” (Bhag. [4.30.23](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.23)) You have appeared as Brahma, Visnu, and Siva for the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the material world. Obeisances to You, the independent Lord, who incarnates to deliver His devotees from misery. You are the Paramatma and are known as the all-pervading Vasudeva. You are also known as the son of Vasudeva and as Krsna. Obeisances to You, whose abdomen is the source of the lotus flower from which all living entities emanate. Obeisances to You as Krsna, who, like a lotus, is the source of all. You are in everyone’s heart, and You wear yellow garments that are fully spiritual. As the Supersoul You witness all the living entities’ activities. Dear Lord, we conditioned souls are always covered by ignorance and the bodily conception of life. We therefore prefer misery in the material world. To deliver us from our miserable condition You have advented in Your transcendental form. This proves Your unlimited causeless mercy on those who are suffering. What, then, of the mercy You show the devotees, to whom You are always so favorably disposed? You show Your compassion by accepting the arcd'Vigraha. Please accept us as Your eternal servants. Conditioned souls prefer material existence, which causes misery and which covers them with ignorance. Every being is immersed in the bodily concept of life. By Your causeless mercy You come to relieve our suffering and deliver us.

In his purport to text 27 Srila Prabhupada explains the Lord’s appearance in the arcd'Vigraha as His compassion: “The form of the Lord as worshiped in the temples is called arcd'Vigraha or arcavatara, the worshipable form, the Deity incarnation. This facility is offered to neophyte devotees so that they can see the real form of the Lord face to face and offer their respectful obeisances and sacrifices in the form of area. Through such facilities the neophytes gradually invoke their original Krsna consciousness. Deity worship in the form of temple worship is the most valuable benediction given by the Lord to beginners. All neophytes must therefore engage in the worship of the Lord by keeping the arca-vigraha (arcavatara) at home or in the temple.”

The Pracetas continued: О Lord, You kill all inauspiciousness. You show compassion to Your poor devotees through Your arca-vigraha expansion. Please consider us Your eternal servants. Situated in the hearts of everyone, You know everything, including our desires. Therefore although You have asked us to request a benediction from You, You already know our desires despite our insignificance. Why, then, should we ask?

Srila Prabhupada speaks of the Lord’s kindness to everyone, but especially to His devotees: “Whatever a living entity desires, however insignificant he may be, is noted by the Lord, who gives him a chance to fulfill his desires. If the desires of the nondevotees are fulfilled, why not those of the devotee? A pure devotee simply wants to engage in the service of the Lord without material desire, and if he wants this within the core of his heart, where the Lord is situated, and if he is without ulterior motive, why should the Lord not understand? If a sincere devotee renders service to the Lord or to the arcd'Vigraha ... all his activities prove successful because the Lord is present within his heart and understands his sincerity. Thus if a devotee, with all confidence, goes on discharging the prescribed duties of devotional service, he will ultimately attain success.” (Bhag. [4.30.29](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.29), purport)

Earlier in this chapter (text 8), the Lord expressed His pleasure with the Pracetas and requested them to ask for a benediction. The Pracetas first glorified the Lord and offered Him their obeisances (texts 22-26). They then described the predicament of souls trapped in matter as well as the Lord’s mercy toward those souls (texts 27-32). Next they placed a request at the Lord’s lotus feet (texts 33-37) after first stating their true desire: “O Lord of the universe, You are the actual teacher of the science of devotional service. We are satisfied that Your Lordship is the ultimate goal of our lives, and we pray that You will be satisfied with us. That is our benediction. We do not desire anything other than Your full satisfaction.” (Bhag. [4.30.30](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.30))

Thus the Pracetas, fully satisfied in the Lord’s presence, had no desire to ask any further benediction. As a bee gets unlimited honey from the parijata tree and therefore never leaves that tree, the Pracetas, having approached and taken shelter of the Lord’s lotus feet, could think of no more worthy benediction than the one they had already achieved.

## Texts 33-46: The Pracetas Request Benedictions

Yet, the Pracetas continued, “As long as we have to remain within this material world due to our material contamination and wander from one type of body to another and from one planet to another, we pray that we may associate with those who are engaged in discussing Your pastimes. We pray for this benediction life after life, in different bodily forms and on different planets.” (Bhag. [4.30.33](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.33))

The two gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya, when cursed to fall to the material world, requested only that “the illusion of forgetting the Supreme Personality of Godhead will not come upon us.” (Bhag. [3.15.36](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.36)) The Kumaras, thinking that they may also be forced to fall to the material world because they cursed the gatekeepers, prayed, “Let us be bom in any hellish condition of life, just as long as our hearts and minds are always engaged in the service of Your lotus feet, our words are made beautiful \[by speaking of Your activities\] just as tulasi leaves are beautified when offered unto Your lotus feet, and as long as our ears are always filled with the chanting of Your transcendental qualities.” (Bhag. [3.15.49](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-3/15.49)) The prayers of Jaya and Vijaya and the Kumaras were fulfilled in the association of pure devotees. Lord Siva taught the Pracetas that Vaisnava sanga is the best of benedictions (Bhag. [4.24.57-59](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.57)), and the Pracetas are now experiencing the result of Lord Siva’s association: by his blessing they have received the Lord’s personal darsana.

In his purport to text 33 Srila Prabhupada also describes the benediction the Pracetas request as “the best benediction”: “One may be in one position or another according to destiny, but in any case one must continue to hear about the activities and pastimes of the Supreme Lord, regardless of circumstances. A pure devotee does not pray for liberation or for cessation of the cycle of birth and death because he does not consider that important. The most important thing for a devotee is getting a chance to hear about the pastimes and glories of the Lord. The devotees who engage in the service of the Lord in this world will have the same opportunity in the spiritual world also. Thus for a devotee, everything is in the spiritual world, for as long as he can hear about the pastimes of the Lord, or wherever he can chant, the Lord is personally present. Tatra tisthdmi narada yatra gay anti mad' bhaktah. When the pure devotees assemble to chant, hear and talk about the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the place where they assemble becomes Vaikuntha. For the devotee there is no need to pray to the Lord for transferal to the Vaikuntha world. A pure devotee can create Vaikuntha or Vrndavana anywhere simply by chanting the glories of the Lord without offense.”

Great devotees like the Pracetas humbly consider themselves too fallen to attain the spiritual world, but still, they strongly desire to hear and chant about Krsna in the association of Vaisnavas. The Pracetas continued: “Even a moment’s association with a pure devotee cannot be compared to being transferred to heavenly planets or even merging into the Brahman effulgence in complete liberation. For living entities who are destined to give up the body and die, association with pure devotees is the highest benediction.” (Bhag. [4.30.34](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.34))

In his purport to this text, Srila Prabhupada describes the value a pure devotee places on Vaisnava sanga: “A pure devotee considers a moment’s association with another pure devotee to be far superior to residing in a heavenly planet or merging in the Brahman effulgence. The topmost benediction for those who are living in this material world and are subjected to the repetition of birth and death (transmigration) is association with pure devotees. One should search out such pure devotees and remain with them. That will make one completely happy, even though living within the material world. This Krsna consciousness movement is started for that purpose. A person who is overly affected materially may take advantage of this movement and become intimately associated with it. In this way the confused and frustrated inhabitants of this material world may find the highest happiness in association with devotees.”

In his Priti-sandarbha, anuccheda 31, Srila Jiva Gosvami cites texts 33 and 34 of this chapter to illustrate the glories of associating with devotees. Sri Jiva writes that devotees pray for such association, fearing that they will turn away from the Lord and become nondevotees. Thus their prayer for Vaisnava sanga is an attempt to protect themselves from becoming nondevotees. These texts, Sri Jiva writes, describe the limitless glories of devotees, for only they desire to love and stay near the Lord’s lotus feet and have no desire for any type of liberation.

What transpires in the association of devotees? The Pracetas say that in that association nothing but krsna-katha is spoken: “Whenever pure topics of the transcendental world are discussed, the members of the audience forget all kinds of material hankerings, at least for the time being. Not only that, but they are no longer envious of one another, nor do they suffer from anxiety or fear.” (Bhag. [4.30.35](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.35))

Srila Prabhupada glorifies the anxiety-free Vaikuntha atmosphere created by the sankirtana movement:

**The living entities who have accepted this material world as a residence are full of anxiety. A place immediately becomes Vaikuntha whenever the holy topics of the Personality of Godhead are discussed by pure devotees. This is the process of sravanam kirtanam visnoh, chanting and hearing about the Supreme Lord Visnu. As the Supreme Lord Himself confirms . . . “My dear Narada, actually 1 do not reside in My abode, Vaikuntha, nor do I reside within the hearts of the yogis, but I reside in that place where My pure devotees chant My holy name and discuss My form, pastimes and qualities.” Because of the presence of the Lord in the form of the transcendental vibration, the Vaikuntha atmosphere is evoked. This atmosphere is without fear and anxiety. One living entity does not fear another. By hearing the holy names and glories of the Lord, a person executes pious activities. Srnvatam sva-kathah krsnah punya-sravana-kirtanah (Bhag.** [**1.2.17**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/2.17)**). Thus his material hankerings immediately stop. This sankirtana movement started by the Society for Krishna Consciousness is meant for creating Vaikuntha, the transcendental world that is without anxiety, even in this material world. The method is the propagation of the sravanam kirtanam process throughout the world. In the material world everyone is envious of his fellow man. Animalistic envy exists in human society as long as there is no performance of sahkirtana-yajna, the chanting of the holy names—Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare / Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare. The Pracetas therefore decided to remain always in the society of devotees, and they considered that to be the highest benediction possible in human life. (Bhag.** [**4.30.35**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.35)**, purport)**

The Pracetas continued: The Lord Himself is present among the devotees who hear and chant His holy names. He is the ultimate goal of sannyasis, and is worshiped through the sankirtana movement by liberated souls who recite the holy name again and again.

In his purport to text 36 Srila Prabhupada explains that one result of chanting and discussing krsna'kathd is that one “immediately becomes nonenvious”: “In this material world everyone is envious of everyone else, but by vibrating or discussing the holy name of the Lord, one becomes nonenvious and devoid of material hankering. Because of our envy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, we have become envious of all other living entities. When we are no longer envious of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, there will be real peace, unity and fraternity in human society. Without Narayana or sankirtana'yajna there cannot be peace in this material world.”

Because devotees who travel throughout the world speaking krsna' katha bring relief to those who are afraid of material existence, they are glorious. The Pracetas glorified even a moment’s association with such devotees, for they themselves had direct experience of the power of such association. “Dear Lord, we have studied the Vedas, accepted a spiritual master and offered respect to brahmanas, advanced devotees and aged personalities who are spiritually very advanced. We have offered our respects to them, and we have not been envious of any brother, friends or anyone else. We have also undergone severe austerities within the water and have not taken food for a long time. All these spiritual assets of ours are simply offered for Your satisfaction. We pray for this benediction only, and nothing more.” (Bhag. [4.30.39-40](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.39)) Although no one can fully understand You, we may nevertheless offer You prayers according to our capacity. Although our capability is small, we have offered our prayers to You.

In his purport to text 41 Srila Prabhupada writes that offering prayers to the Lord is one of the living entity’s constitutional rights: “Nonetheless, everyone in devotional service can offer essential prayers to the Lord. Everyone is situated in a relative position, and no one is perfect in glorifying the Lord. Beginning with Lord Brahma and Lord Siva down to ourselves, everyone is the servant of the Supreme Lord. We are all situated in relative positions according to our own karma. Yet every one of us can offer prayers with heart and soul as far as we can appreciate the Lord’s glories. That is our perfection. Even when one is in the darkest region of existence, he is allowed to offer prayers to the Lord according to his own capacity.”

The Pracetas humbly completed their offering: You are the allpervading, transcendental Supreme Personality of Godhead who is present everywhere in all existence. “You are consequently known as Vasudeva. We offer You our respectful obeisances.” (Bhag. [4.30.42](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.42)) The Pracetas wished to be free of all material desire and to focus themselves only on giving Krsna pleasure. To long only to please Krsna without any material return is bhagavata^dharma, true religion. It is love.

The Lord gave a simple reply: “May whatever you have prayed for be fulfilled.” (Bhag. [4.30.43](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.43)) ТЪеп, although the Pracetas had hoped He would stay longer, the Lord departed.

## Texts 47-51: The Pracetas Emerge from the Sea

King Pracinabarhisat had left home after assimilating Narada Muni’s teachings, but the Pracetas had not yet returned to assume the throne. Because there was no ruler, the trees had become tall and overgrown and were beginning to take over farmland. Without agriculture, no food grains were being produced.

It is significant that through His messenger Narada, Krsna, had guided Pracinabarhisat to immediately leave his kingdom before the instructed the King in a way that left his kingdom neglected.

A conditioned soul’s vision is limited to tens of years and a small portion of reality while Krsna’s plan stretches to eternity. When confronted with an “unfortunate” or incomprehensible piece of reality, a soul’s responsibility is to faithfully accept what has occurred as Krsna’s beneficent will. During difficult times, Bhismadeva’s words (Bhag. [1.9.14-17](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/9.14)) may both offer solace and help one discern and perform his duty in response to the event. Bhismadeva, on his deathbed, told Yudhisthira: “In my opinion, this is all due to inevitable time, under whose control everyone in every planet is carried, just as the clouds are carried by the wind. Oh, how wonderful is the influence of inevitable time. It is irreversible—otherwise, how can there be reverses in the presence of King Yudhisthira, the son of the demigod controlling religion; Bhima, the great fighter with a club; the great bowman Arjuna with his mighty weapon Gandiva; and above all, the Lord, the direct well-wisher of the Pandavas? О King, no one can know the plan of the Lord \[Sri Krsna\]. Even though great philosophers inquire exhaustively, they are bewildered. О best among the descendants of Bharata \[Yudhisthira\], I maintain, therefore, that all this is within the plan of the Lord. Accepting the inconceivable plan of the Lord, you must follow it. You are now the appointed administrative head, and, my lord, you should now take care of those subjects who are now rendered helpless.”

As the Pracetas emerged from the sea after many years of austerities, they noted the overgrowth of the trees and became hot with anger. Using the power they had gained by their austerities, they breathed fire and began to bum the trees to ashes.

Suddenly, Lord Brahma arrived to pacify the Pracetas, and then, as Lord Visnu had predicted, the trees, fearing the princes’ anger, soothed them by offering them their beautiful daughter, Marisa.

In his purport to text 47 Srila Prabhupada explains how Marisa could be the daughter of the trees: “In this connection, Srila Jiva Gosvami Prabhupada states, vrksah tad-adhisthatr-devatah: ‘The “trees” means the controlling deity of those trees.’ In Vedic literatures we find that there is a controlling deity of the water; similarly, there is a controlling deity of the trees. The Pracetas were engaged in burning all the trees to ashes, and they considered the trees their enemies. To pacify the Pracetas, the predominating deity of the trees, under the advice of Lord Brahma, delivered the daughter Marisa.”

From the Pracetas’ marriage with Marisa, Daksa, who was one of Brahma’s original sons, took birth again. Because he had disrespected Lord Siva, he had to take birth from a woman’s womb, although in his previous birth he had been one of Brahma’s mind-born sons.

In his purport to text 48 Srila Prabhupada provides more detail about the reason behind Daksa’s second birth: “King Daksa was the son of Lord Brahma; therefore in a previous birth he was a brahmana, but because of his behaving like a non-brahmam (abrahmana) by insulting or disrespecting Lord Mahadeva, he had to take birth within the semen of a ksatriya. That is to say, he became the son of the Pracetas. Not only that, but because of his disrespecting Lord Siva, he had to undergo the tribulation of taking birth from within the womb of a woman. In the Daksa-yajna arena, he was once killed by Lord Siva’s servant, Virabhadra. Because that was not sufficient, he again took birth, from the womb of Marisa. At the end of the Daksa-yajna and the disastrous incidents there, Daksa offered his prayer to Lord Siva. Although he had to give up his body and take birth from a woman impregnated by the semen of a ksatriya, he received all opulence by the grace of Lord Siva.”

Srila Prabhupada explains the time frame in which these events occurred: “The controversy of the Daksa-yajna took place in the Svayambhuva manvantara period. As a result, Daksa was punished by Lord Siva, but by virtue of his prayers to Lord Siva he became eligible to regain his former opulence. According to Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, Daksa underwent severe penances up to the fifth manvantara. Thus at the beginning of the sixth manvantara, known as the Caksusa manvantara, Daksa regained his former opulence by the blessings of Lord Siva.” (Bhag. [4.30.49](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/30.49), purport)

Although his previous body had been destroyed, that same Daksa, by the supreme will, continued creating living entities. His powerful bodily luster minimized all others, and His expertise at fruitive sacrifices caused him to again be known as Daksa, “expert.” As before, Lord Brahma engaged Daksa in generating living entities, and in due course of time, Daksa also engaged other Prajapatis (progenitors) in the ongoing process of generation and maintenance.

Thus the Pracetas returned home and accepted the throne vacated by Pracinabarhisat. Due to the Lord’s benedictions (given in texts 17-18) they remained pure even as they pursued household life.

The Bhagavatam does not describe much of their rule, but in the first chapter of Canto Five, Maharaja Priyavrata, Uttanapada’s elder brother and a son of Svayambhuva Manu, will demonstrate how to remain pure while performing one’s occupational duty as king.

## Chapter 31 - Narada Instructs the Pracetas

## Texts 1-7: The Pracetas Renounce Their Kingdom and Meet Narada Muni

The Pracetas ruled their father’s kingdom for thousands of years. Using them as an example in his purport to Bhagavatam [4.31.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/31.1), Srila Prabhupada points out that at the beginning of one’s life one should become the student of a spiritual master and learn the art of spiritual life. At that time one should study and practice austerities. Then when one is older, one may marry and participate in household life. Having firmly set a spiritual foundation, at death one will remember what one has learned and the detachment one has developed from one’s training.

The great saint Maitreya continued: “The Pracetas lived at home and developed perfect knowledge in spiritual consciousness. At last they remembered the blessings of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and left home for thousands of years, putting their wife in the charge of a perfect son.” (Bhag. [4.31.1](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/31.1))

Also in his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada describes the renunciation at the end of household life: “After the Pracetas had finished their penances, they were blessed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Lord blessed them by telling them that after finishing their family life they would return home, back to Godhead, in due course of time. After finishing their family life, which lasted thousands of years according to the calculations of the demigods, the Pracetas decided to leave home, putting their wife in the charge of a son named Daksa. This is the process of Vedic civilization.... Unless one practices penances and austerities in his student life, he cannot understand the existence of God. Without realizing Krsna, one cannot make his life perfect. The conclusion is that when the children are grown, the wife should be put in the children’s charge. The husband may then leave home to develop Krsna consciousness. . . . The home is considered to be a dark well covered by grass, and if one falls within this well, he simply dies without anyone’s caring. One should therefore not be too much attached to family life, for it will spoil one’s development of Krsna consciousness.”

Upon leaving home the Pracetas traveled west to the sea. There, under the guidance of the liberated sage Jajali, they increased their spiritual knowledge by practicing austerities, yoga asanas, and pranayama. All of these helped them to concentrate their minds and reach perfection. Text 3 describes the yogic practices that helped the Pracetas become focused, and in his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada describes the object of their meditation: “Lord Siva concentrated upon the personal features of Parabrahman, described in personal terms as snigdha-pravrd-ghana-syamam (Bhag. [4.24.45](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/24.45)). Following the instructions of Lord Siva, the Pracetas also concentrated their minds on the

Syamasundara form of the Supreme Brahman. Although impersonal Brahman, Paramatma Brahman and Brahman as the Supreme Person are all on the same transcendental platform, the personal feature of the Supreme Brahman is the ultimate goal and last word in transcendence.”

In the midst of their yoga practice, Narada Muni arrived. With great respect the Pracetas glorified him and offered him a sitting place. Then they confessed their faulty consciousness: Due to having being engrossed in family affairs, we have been spiritually negligent and have almost forgotten the instructions of both Lord Siva and Lord Visnu. О Narada, please enlighten us with transcendental knowledge and help us to cross beyond the darkness of material existence.

The Pracetas sought no material benediction from Narada but humbly requested him to guide them away from matter: “Dear master, kindly enlighten us in transcendental knowledge, which may act as a torchlight by which we may cross the dark nescience of material existence.” (Bhag. [4.31.7](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/31.7))

## Narada’s Instructions, Part One

## Texts 8-14: Devotional Service Is the Goal of All Spiritual Practices

Narada Muni wanted the Pracetas to focus on something more tangible than matter. He himself is always absorbed in thoughts of the Personality of Godhead, and he wished to redirect the Pracetas to the highest goal: pleasing the Supreme Lord by performing devotional service. Narada said: Many living entities are bom in this world, but the only perfection of any birth is to achieve the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. All other achievements are useless. “Similarly, one’s activities may be mundane or spiritual, but they are useless if they are not meant for satisfying the Lord.” (Bhag. [4.31.10](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/31.10))

In his important purport to text 10 Srila Prabhupada asserts that an aspirant’s Krsna consciousness may be facilitated by awarding him the position of a brahmana: “In this age of Kali, everyone is sudra due to the absence of the garbhadhana-samskara. This is the Vedic system. According to the pancaratrika system, however, even though everyone is a siidra due to the absence of the garbhadhana-samskara, if a person has but a little tendency to become Krsna conscious, he should be given the chance to elevate himself to the transcendental platform of devotional service. Our Krsna consciousness movement adopts this pancaratrika-vidhi, as advised by Srila Sanatana Gosvami, who says . . . ‘As bell metal, when mixed with mercury, is transformed to gold, a person, even though not golden pure, can be transformed into a brahmana, or dvija, simply by the initiation process.’ (Hari-bhakti-vilasa [2.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/hbv/2.12)) Thus if one is initiated by a proper person, he can be accepted as twice-born immediately. In our Krsna consciousness movement, we therefore offer the student his first initiation and allow him to chant the Hare Krsna maha-mantra. By chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra regularly and following the regulative principles, one becomes qualified to be initiated as a brahmana, because unless one is a qualified brahmana he cannot be allowed to worship Lord Visnu.”

Narada thoroughly condemns even spiritual practices that fail to direct one to Krsna, and he again stresses that Krsna consciousness, serving Lord Hari with devotion, is the only valuable attainment. “Without devotional service, what is the meaning of severe austerities, the process of hearing, the power of speech, the power of mental speculation, elevated intelligence, strength, and the power of the senses? Transcendental practices that do not ultimately help one realize the Supreme Personality of Godhead are useless, be they mystic yoga practices, the analytical study of matter, severe austerity, the acceptance of sannyasa, or the study of Vedic literature. All these may be very important aspects of spiritual advancement, but unless one understands the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, all these processes are useless.” (Bhag. [4.31.11-12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/31.11))

Srila Prabhupada compares a man’s failure to use his abilities and talents for spiritual purposes to a vulture’s power of vision: “So the whole world, they are posing themselves as highly advanced in education—science, philosophy, this, that, politics, so many things. But, their position is this body. Just like, an example, a vulture. A vulture rises very high. Seven miles, eight miles up. Wonderful. You cannot do that. And he has got wonderful eyes also. They are small eyes, yet the vulture is so powerful that it can see from seven-mile distance where there is a carcass, a dead body. So he has got good qualification. He can rise very high; he can see from a distant place. Oh. But what is his object? A dead body, that’s all. His perfection is to find out a carcass, dead body, and to eat. That’s all. Similarly we may go up very high education, but what is our objective? What are we seeing? How to enjoy sense, this body, that’s all.” (Lecture on Bg. [6.16-24](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/6.16), Los Angeles, February 17, 1969)

Narada Muni continues: “Factually the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the original source of all self'realization. Consequently, the goal of all auspicious activities—karma, jnana, yoga and bhakti —is the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhag. [4.31.13](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/31.13))

Pursuing Narada’s mood, Srila Prabhupada insists that success in following other processes is measured only by whether or not that following increases one’s bhakti. On the other hand, to achieve success in any other process requires at least some bhakti. Devotional service is at the heart of all processes: “Impersonalists do not take to devotional service, but take to other practices, such as the analytical study of the material elements, the discrimination between matter and spirit, and the mystic yoga system. These are beneficial only insofar as they are complementary to devotional service. Caitanya Mahaprabhu therefore told Sanatana Gosvami that without a touch of devotional service, jnana, yoga and Sankhya philosophy cannot give one the desired results. The impersonalists wish to merge into the Supreme Brahman; however, merging into the Supreme Brahman also requires a touch of devotional service. The Absolute Truth is realized in three phases —impersonal Brahman, Paramatma and the Supreme Personality of Godhead. All these require a touch of devotional service. Sometimes it is actually seen that these Mayavadis also chant the Hare Krsna maha-mantra, although their motive is to merge into the Brahman effulgence of the Absolute. The yogis also at times take to chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra, but their purpose is different from that of the bhaktas. In all processes—karma, jnana or yoga—bhakti is required. That is the purport of this verse.” (Bhag. [4.31.12](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/31.12), purport)

In his commentary on text 13 Srila Sridhara Svami poses an objection: How can the results of all spiritual activities other than bhakti to Lord Hari be considered worthless? He provides Narada Muni’s response as an answer to that objection by stating that Lord Hari (harir), the Supersoul (atma), is the highest possible goal (avadhih para krstha) of all auspicious activities (sreyasam). This is the truth from the higher point of view (arthatah paramarthatah), because He is more dear (priyah) than anyone or anything. Whatever else is dear or pleasing is only such because it is dear to the Self (atma), the Supersoul.

This may lead to another objection: But even if the Self is the goal, how does Hari enter into the argument (bhavatvatmavadhir hareh kim ayatam)? Again he cites Narada’s response: He is the original source of the identity of all (sarvesam apiti). Sridhara Svami adds that another interpretation of atma-da is possible: Lord Hari appeared before Bali Maharaja and other devotees in His spiritual form as the Supreme Personality of Godhead and gave Himself to them. Thus the Lord is dear to all, because He bestows Himself even in His opulent form like an offering to His devotees.

Sri Narada Muni continued: “As pouring water on the root of a tree energizes the trunk, branches, twigs and everything else, and as supplying food to the stomach enlivens the senses and limbs of the body, simply worshiping the Supreme Personality of Godhead through devotional service automatically satisfies the demigods, who are parts of that Supreme Personality.” (Bhag. [4.31.14](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/31.14))

Devotional service offered to Krsna automatically satisfies the demigods; one need not worship them separately. In his purport to text 14 Srila Prabhupada explains that devotional service is the essence of good works: “Modem society is involved in various types of philanthropic works, humanitarian works and so on, but people do not know that these activities will never be successful unless Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is brought into the center.”

Srila Prabhupada continues: “One may ask what harm there is in worshiping Krsna and the different parts of His body, the demigods, and the answer is also given in this text. The point is that by supplying food to the stomach, the indriyas, the senses, are automatically satisfied. If one tries to feed his eyes or ears independently, the result is only havoc. Simply by supplying food to the stomach, we satisfy all of the senses. It is neither necessary nor feasible to render separate service to the individual senses. The conclusion is that by serving Krsna (krsna-seva), everything is complete. As confirmed in Caitanya-caritamrta (Madhya [22.62](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/22.62)), krsne bhakti kaile sarva-karma krta haya: if one is engaged in the devotional service of the Lord, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, everything is automatically accomplished.”

## Narada’s Instructions, Part Two: Everything Emanates from the Lord

## Texts 15-17: He is Worthy of All Worship

Narada Muni stated: “During the rainy season, water is generated from the sun, and in due course of time, during the summer season, the very same water is again absorbed by the sun.” (Bhag. [4.31.15](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/31.15)) Similarly, everything in creation emanates from the Lord, and everything ultimately returns to Him. Nothing is different from Him, because He pervades everything and is the ultimate cause of all. Even the ever-shifting modes of nature are His energies. Still, He remains aloof from all material emanations and their interactions. Therefore as you Pracetas are qualitatively nondifferent from the Lord, serve Him with great devotion.

Everything is His, everything comes from Him, everything belongs to Him, and everything rests on His energy. Srila Prabhupada addresses this topic in his purport to text 16: “This confirms the philosophy of acintya-bhedabheda-tattva (simultaneously one and different) propounded by Lord Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. The Supreme Personality of Godhead is simultaneously different and nondifferent from this cosmic manifestation. In a previous text it has been explained that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, like the root of a tree, is the original cause of everything. It was also explained how the Supreme Personality of Godhead is all-pervasive. He is present within everything in this material manifestation. Since the energy of the Supreme Lord is nondifferent from Him, this material cosmic manifestation is also nondifferent from Him, although it appears different. The sunshine is not different from the sun itself, but it is simultaneously also different. One may be in the sunshine, but he is not on the sun itself. Those who live in this material world are living on the bodily rays of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but they cannot see Him personally in the material condition.”

In his purport to text 18 Srila Prabhupada carries the point to its practical conclusion—that everything in existence should be used in Krsna’s service: “The Supreme Personality of Godhead is never affected by the material qualities, although they all emanate from His spiritual energy. Those who are really conversant with this knowledge can utilize everything for the service of the Lord because nothing in this material world is unconnected with the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

## Narada’s Instructions, Part Three

## Texts 18-22: Satisfy the All-powerful Lord by Devotional Service

In text 18 Narada concludes: atmaika-bhavena bhajadhvam addha, “You should therefore engage in His devotional service, thinking yourself qualitatively one with Him.” But how can one practically serve someone who is so inconceivably powerful? Narada next clarifies the processes of devotional service: “By showing mercy to all living entities, being satisfied somehow or other and controlling the senses from sense enjoyment, one can very quickly satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Janardana.” (Bhag. [4.31.19](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-4/31.19))In his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada writes that preaching is a way to satisfy the Lord:

**These are some of the ways in which the Supreme Personality of Godhead can be satisfied by the devotee. The first item mentioned is dayaya sarva-bhutesu, showing mercy to all conditioned souls. The best way to show mercy is to spread Krsna consciousness. The entire world is suffering for want of this knowledge. People should know that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the original cause of everything. Knowing this, everyone should directly engage in His devotional service. Those who are actually learned, advanced in spiritual understanding, should preach Krsna consciousness all over the world so that people may take to it and make their lives successful.**

**The word sarva-bhutesu is significant because it applies not only to to human beings but to all living entities appearing in the 8,400,000 species of life. The devotee can do good not only to humanity but to all living entities as well. Everyone can benefit spiritually by the chanting of the Hare Krsna maha-mantra. When the transcendental vibration of Hare Krsna is sounded, even the trees, animals and insects benefit. Thus when one chants the Hare Krsna maha-mantra loudly, he actually shows mercy to all living entities.
